title: Songs of Grace, Book VI, Volume 2

intro.title: Introduction: Thiru Arutpa
paras: Thiru Arutpa, which means Divine Songs of Grace, is a collection of poems written by Ramalinga Adigal, lovingly known as Vallalar.

The entire poetic work is divided into 6 volumes or Thirumurais. The poems narrate the spiritual journey of Vallalar. From his early days of worship into the Saiva Siddhanta doctrine, the suffering from separation from the divine, to the final realization of the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light) in his late stage of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam Sathya Sangam philosophy and way of life. The core philosophical pillars of the Thiru Arutpa include:
Active Compassion: The foundation is Jeeva Karunyam, or active compassion for all living beings as basis to spiritual life
Unity of All Beings: The Arutpa teaches Anma Neya Orumaipadu, or the Unity of Souls, asserting that every creature shares the exact same spiritual essence.
Rejection of Division: Vallalar wholly rejected caste systems, religious divisions, and sectarian hierarchies.
The Divine Light: The ultimate recognition is that ArutPerunJothi, the supreme divine light, dwells within every single soul without exception.
Ultimately, the Thiru Arutpa is a spiritual guide toward boundless compassion to all life, self-realization, and what Vallalar taught as the physical body's ability to reach a deathless state.

intro.title: Introduction: Thiru Arutpa Sixth Thirumurai
paras: The Thiru Arutpa is the collected poetry of Ramalinga Adigal, and it is arranged in six parts called Thirumurai. This is the sixth and last.

The first five volumes were written by a younger Ramalinga inside a tradition. They are temple hymns. They name places, they address deities by their local names, and they follow forms Tamil devotional poetry had used for a thousand years.

The Sixth is what came after. These are the works of his final years, written at Vadalur and at Mettukuppam, in the same period when he opened a kitchen that fed anyone who came and built a hall with no god in it.

In the earlier volumes he is a devotee. Here he is teaching something, and it has a name: Suddha Sanmarkkam, the pure true path. He describes it, he sets out what it asks, and he tells people to enter it.

He says caste, creed and sect are false. Not incomplete. False. He uses the word poy, a lie, and he says he was told so from the beginning. The man writing the Sixth Thirumurai has stopped working within the religions and has begun speaking past them.

He says the body does not have to die. The teaching on deathlessness, on the body remade by grace, appears here and nowhere earlier. It is the hardest part of his work and the part most often argued over.

He puts compassion at the gate. Jeeva Karunyam, mercy toward every living thing, is not presented as one virtue among many. It is the condition. Without it, he says, nothing else opens. This is why the free kitchen and these poems belong to the same act.
The form changes too. The temple hymn gives way to direct address. He is no longer singing about the divine from a shrine. He is speaking to it, and reporting what it said back.

A note on the arrangement. Ramalinga did not publish these works himself. He wrote as occasion demanded and left the ordering to others. His disciple Thozhuvur Velayutha Mudaliar, who had edited the earlier volumes during his lifetime, gathered the late writings after 1874 and arranged them. The six-part division is the work of the disciples, not of Ramalinga. Later editors, chiefly Ooran Adigal, reordered the volumes by date of composition, which is why some poems sit in different Thirumurai in different editions.

A note on this volume. The Sixth Thirumurai is published in three volumes, and the ArutPerunJothi Agaval, at 1,596 lines a book in itself, has a book of its own: The Hymn of the Vast Grace-Light. This is Volume Two of three, with pathigams 049 to 107. All of them are free to read at sanmarkkamlife.org.
The Tamil text follows the arrangement of Ooran Adigal, as given at thiruarutpa.org, checked against the printed editions of 1885 and 1932 where it was damaged.

works.title: The Hymn of the Vast Grace-light

blocks.html: The ArutPerunJothi Agaval, the Hymn of the Vast Grace-Light, is the greatest work of Ramalinga Adigal, the Tamil saint lovingly known as Vallalar. He wrote it in his last and most mature years, at Mettukuppam in south India. It is said that he wrote it in one unbroken session, in a single night.

It has 1,596 lines. Its subject is the ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light. The poem describes what that Light is, how everything that exists came out of it and is still held by it, and what happens inside a person when it is let in.

It begins by naming it. For 437 couplets, every second line ends in the same word. Then the naming stops, and the poem calls the same thing mother, father, friend, medicine, gold, mountain, ocean, lamp. At the end the first name returns, and the poem closes on the line it opened with.
Three things are said clearly. Caste, creed and sect are false. The path of non-violence is the path of grace. Every living thing is to be seen as your own.
More than a century later, devotees all over the world still wake up before dawn to sing these blissful lines.

sections.title: The Bliss of Praising the Lord

translit: karuṇaimā nitiyē eṉṉiru kaṇṇē kaṭavuḷē kaṭavuḷē eṉkō taruṇavāṉ amutē eṉperun tāyē tantaiyē tantaiyē eṉkō teruḷniṟai matiyē eṉkuru patiyē teyvamē teyvamē eṉkō aruḷniṟai tarumeṉ aruṭperuñ cōti āṇṭava niṉṟaṉai aṟintē.
translation: Now that I have known You, my Lord, my ArutPerunJothi who grants the fullness of grace, shall I call you a great treasure of compassion, my two eyes, God, God? Shall I call you fresh heavenly ambrosia, my great mother, father, father? Shall I call you a moon full of clarity, my Guru-Lord, Divinity, Divinity?
commentary: Having experienced the divine as ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light), the poet finds that God is everything. The divine is the treasure of compassion, the very eyes we see with, the ambrosia that nourishes, the love of a mother and father, and the wisdom of a guru (spiritual teacher). This cascade of names shows how knowing God personally reveals the divine presence in every aspect of life.

translit: oṭṭiyē eṉṉuḷ uṟumoḷi eṉkō oḷielām nirampiya nilaikkōr veṭṭiyē eṉkō veṭṭiyileṉakku viḷaṅkuṟak kiṭaittaōr vayirap peṭṭiyē eṉkō peṭṭiyiṉ naṭuvē periyavar vaittatōr taṅkak kaṭṭiyē eṉkō ampalat tāṭum karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭavuḷniṉ ṟaṉaiyē.
translation: O compassionate God, You who dance in the sacred space, shall I call You the light that cleaves to and abides within me? Shall I call you the open expanse that is the state filled with all light? Shall I call you a diamond casket I received, shining brightly for me in that expanse? Shall I call you a block of gold placed inside that casket by the Great One?
commentary: God is described here using a powerful nested metaphor. First, God is the "open expanse" of pure awareness, the sacred space where the divine dances. Then, within that space, God is also the precious "diamond casket" and the "block of gold" it contains. This reveals a deep truth: the ultimate reality is both the infinite field of consciousness and the priceless treasure of grace discovered within it.

translit: tuṉpelām tavirtta tuṇaivaṉē eṉkō cōtiyuṭ cōtiyē eṉkō aṉpelām aḷitta aṉpaṉē eṉkō ammaiyē appaṉē eṉkō iṉpelām purinta iṟaivaṉē eṉkō eṉuyirk kiṉṉamu teṉkō eṉpolā maṇiyē eṉkaṇē eṉkō eṉṉuyir nātaniṉ ṟaṉaiyē.
translation: O Lord of my life, shall I call you the companion who averted all suffering? Shall I call you Light within light? The loving one who bestowed all love? Mother and father? The Lord who wrought all bliss? The sweet ambrosia for my life? My flawless gem, my very eye?
commentary: Vallalar searches for a name great enough for God, and each one falls short. Companion who removed all suffering, Light within light, Mother and Father, sweet nectar of his life, his flawless gem, his very eye: he offers them one by one, as questions. The joy of the verse is in the search itself. Praising God is its own bliss.

translit: karuttaṉē eṉatu karuttiṉuk kicainta kaṇavaṉē kaṇavaṉē eṉkō oruttaṉē ellām uṭaiyanā yakaṉē orutaṉip periyaṉē eṉkō tiruttaṉē eṉatu celvamē ellām ceyavalla cittaṉē eṉkō niruttaṉē eṉakkup poruttaṉē eṉkō niṟaiaruṭ cōtiniṉ ṟaṉaiyē.
translation: O Jothi of abundant grace, shall I call You the Creator, the husband, husband!, who is pleasing to my mind? Shall I call You the singular one, the master who possesses everything, the uniquely great one? Shall I call You the perfect one, my own wealth, the Siddha who can accomplish all things? Shall I call You the dancer, the one who is perfect for me?
commentary: The search for names continues: Creator, beloved husband, the One who owns all, the uniquely great, the Siddha who can do all things, the Dancer who is perfect for him. The bridal image (kaṇavaṉ, husband) expresses the closest union a human life knows. Each name is true, and none is enough for the Jothi of abundant grace.

translit: tāyaṉē eṉatu tātaiyē orumait talaivaṉē talaivaṉē eṉkō pēyaṉēṉ piḻaiyaip poṟuttaruḷ purinta peruntakaip perumpati eṉkō cēyaṉēṉ peṟṟa civapatam eṉkō cittelām vallacit teṉkō tūyaṉē eṉatu nēyaṉē eṉkō cōtiyuṭ cōtiniṉ ṟaṉaiyē.
translation: O Light within light, shall I call You mother, my father, the singular Lord, the Lord? Shall I call You the great magnanimous one, the supreme Master who graciously forgave the errors of this demonic one? Shall I call You the state of Siva that I, your child, received? Shall I call you the all-powerful supreme consciousness? Shall I call You the pure one, my beloved?
commentary: The divine cannot be captured by any single name or relationship. Vallalar lists many possibilities: a mother, a father, a master, a lover, and even the ultimate state of consciousness he has achieved. He feels unworthy, calling himself ‘demonic’, yet this forgiving God has granted him the highest spiritual attainment, the state of union with Siva (Sivapatam).

translit: arumpilē malarvuṟ ṟaruḷmaṇam vīcum āṉantat taṉimalar eṉkō karumpilē eṭutta cuvaittiraḷ eṉkō kaṭaiyaṉēṉ uṭaiyaneñ cakamām irumpilē paḻuttup pēroḷi tatumpi ilaṅkumōr pacumpoṉē eṉkō turumpiṉēṉ peṟṟa perumpatam eṉkō cōtiyuṭ cōtiniṉ ṟaṉaiyē.
translation: Shall I call you the unique flower of bliss that bloomed from a bud, spreading the fragrance of grace? Shall I call you the condensed sweetness extracted from sugarcane? Shall I call you the pure gold that shines, brimming with great light, after being heated in my wretched iron heart? Shall I call you the great state attained by me, a mere piece of straw? You stand as Light within light.
commentary: God’s presence is an alchemical force that transforms the unworthy into something precious. Vallalar compares his ‘wretched iron heart’ to a furnace where God's presence acts like heat, turning it into shining gold. He sees himself as insignificant, a ‘mere piece of straw’, yet through grace he has attained a ‘great state’.

translit: tākamuḷ eṭutta pōtetir kiṭaitta carkkarai amutamē eṉkō mōkamvan taṭutta pōtukaip piṭitta mukanakaik kaṇavaṉē eṉkō pōkamuḷ virumpum pōtilē valintu puṇarntaōr pūvaiyē eṉkō ākamuṭ pukunteṉ uyiriṉuṭ kalanta ampalat tāṭiniṉ ṟaṉaiyē.
translation: Shall I call you the sugary nectar that appeared when thirst arose? Shall I call you the smiling husband who took my hand when infatuation came? Shall I call you the woman who forcefully united with me when I desired blissful union? You, the Dancer in the Hall, have entered my body and mingled with my very life.
commentary: The divine responds perfectly to every kind of human yearning. To the thirsty, God is nectar; to the infatuated, a loving husband. In a bold and intimate metaphor, Vallalar also describes the divine as a forceful female lover who initiated a union during his life. This presence, the ‘Dancer in the Hall’ (Ampalattāṭi, a name for Siva), is not distant but has entered his very body and life.

translit: tattuvam aṉaittum tavirttunāṉ taṉitta taruṇattil kiṭaittatoṉ ṟeṉkō cattuva nirampum cuttacaṉ mārkkan taṉiluṟum aṉupavam eṉkō ottuvan teṉaittāṉ kalantukoṇ ṭeṉakkuḷ ōṅkiya orumaiyē eṉkō cittuvan tāṭuñ cittaṉē eṉkō tirucciṟṟam palattava niṉaiyē.
translation: Shall I call you the one thing found in the moment I stood alone, having cast off all principles? Shall I call you the experience gained in the Pure Path of Truth, which is filled with purity? Shall I call you the Oneness that rose within me after coming and mingling with me in perfect accord? Shall I call you the Siddha who plays with miraculous powers? You are the one in the Thiru Chitrambalam.
commentary: True spiritual realization happens when the mind is empty of all its usual concepts. Vallalar describes this as casting off the tattvas (the fundamental principles or categories of reality that structure our experience). In that stillness, he found God directly. This is the central experience of his path, the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure Path of Truth), and God is the perfected master, or Siddha, who resides in the Thiru Chitrambalam (the sacred hall of consciousness within).

translit: yōkameyñ ñāṉam palittapō tuḷattil ōṅkiya kāṭciyē eṉkō ēkameyñ ñāṉa yōkattiṟ kiṭaittuḷ icaintapē riṉpamē eṉkō cākalait tavirtteṉ taṉṉaivāḻ vikkac cārntacaṟ kurumaṇi eṉkō mākamum puviyum vāḻvuṟa maṇimā maṉṟilē naṭikkiṉṟōy niṉaiyē.
translation: Shall I call you the vision that arose in my mind when yoga and true wisdom bore fruit? Shall I call you the great bliss experienced within, obtained through the yoga of singular true wisdom? Shall I call you the gem-like true guru who came to make me live, saving me from death? You dance in the beautiful great hall so that heaven and earth may thrive.
commentary: The divine is both the goal of the spiritual path and the guide who leads us there. When practices like yoga and the search for wisdom bear fruit, God is the vision and bliss that result. Most importantly, God is the Satguru (the true spiritual teacher) who appears to save the seeker from physical death and grant eternal life.

translit: iravilā tiyampum pakalilā tirunta iyaṟkaiyuḷ iyaṟkaiyē eṉkō varavilā vuraikkum pōkkilā nilaiyil vayaṅkiya vāṉporuḷ eṉkō tiraiyilā tellām vallacit teṉakkē ceytatōr cittaṉē eṉkō karavilā teṉakkup pēraruṭ cōti kaḷittaḷit taruḷiya niṉaiyē.
translation: Shall I call you the Nature within nature, existing without night or proclaimed day? Shall I call you the celestial substance shining in a state without coming or going? Shall I call you the perfected one who, without any veil, performed for me the feat of all-power? You are the one who, without holding anything back, joyfully bestowed upon me the Great Grace-Light.
commentary: God is the absolute reality that underlies everything, existing beyond all dualities. This ultimate reality is a state with no night or day, no coming or going. It revealed itself to Vallalar directly, without any veil, granting him access to its unlimited power and joyfully bestowing upon him the Great Grace-Light (Pēraruṭ Cōti).
NOTES
Note 276

tamil: கெட்டியே என்கோ கெட்டியில் - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு. பதிப்பு.
translit: keṭṭiyē eṉkō keṭṭiyil - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu. patippu.
translation: keṭṭiyē eṉkō keṭṭiyil — reading of the first edition and the Po. Su. edition.
Note 277

translit: nilaikkum - mutaṟpatippu, po. cu. patippu.
translation: nilaikkum — reading of the first edition and the Po. Su. edition.

translit: patiyēem paraṉēem paramparaṉē ematu parāparaṉē āṉantap patantarumeyñ ñāṉa nitiyēmeyn niṟaivēmeyn nilaiyēmey iṉpa niruttamiṭum taṉittalaimai nipuṇamaṇi viḷakkē katiyēeṉ kaṇṇēeṉ kaṇmaṇiyē eṉatu karuttēeṉ karuttiluṟṟa kaṉivēceṅ kaṉiyē tutiyēeṉ turaiyēeṉ tōḻāeṉ uḷattē cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: O Lord, my Supreme Being, my Primordial Source, my Transcendent One! O treasure of true wisdom that bestows the state of bliss! O true fulfillment, true stability! O masterful, gem-like lamp of unique supremacy performing the dance of true bliss! O my refuge, my eye, the pupil of my eye, my very thought, the ripened sweetness within my thought, O perfectly ripe fruit! O my praise, my sovereign, my companion! O Siddha-crest-jewel performing the pure dance within my heart!
commentary: The supreme God is simultaneously the highest cosmic principle and the closest personal friend. This verse overflows with loving names, moving from the most abstract ("Primordial Source") to the most intimate ("my companion," "the pupil of my eye"). This vast, transcendent reality is finally experienced directly as a perfected being (Siddha) performing a pure dance within one's own heart.

translit: āraṇamē ākamamē āraṇaā kamattiṉ arumporuḷē arumporuḷiṉ aṉupavamē aṟivē kāraṇamē kāriyamē kāraṇakā riyaṅkaḷ kaṭantaperum patiyēeṉ karuttamarnta nitiyē pūraṇamē puṇṇiyamē potuviḷaṅkum aracē puttamutē cattiyamē poṉṉēcem poruḷē tōraṇamē viḷaṅkucitti purattiṉumeṉ uḷattum cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: You are the Āraṇam and the Āgamam! You are the rare essence of the Āraṇam and Āgamam, the direct experience of that rare essence, and knowledge itself! You are the cause and the effect, the great Lord who transcends cause and effect, the treasure settled in my thoughts. You are fullness, you are merit, the King who shines in the common space! You are fresh ambrosia, truth itself, gold, the perfect substance! You are a triumphal archway! O Siddha-crest-jewel, you perform the pure dance in the luminous City of Attainment and also within my heart!
commentary: God is more than described by the scriptures; God is the scriptures, both the Vedas (Āraṇam) and the sacred traditions (Āgamam), their hidden meaning, and the direct experience that goes beyond them. The verse presents a powerful idea: the same divine dance that takes place in a celestial "City of Attainment" also happens right inside your own heart. This makes the highest spiritual reality accessible here and now.

translit: iṇaiētum iṉṟiniṉṟa iṟaiyavaṉē maṟaicol ēkamumāy aṉēkamumāy ilaṅkuparam paraṉē aṇaiyētum iṉṟiniṟai perumpuṉalē ataṉmēl aṉalēeṉ appāeṉ avattaielām kaṭattum puṇaiyēmeyp poruḷēmeyp pukaḻēmeyp pukalē potuvēuḷ ḷatuvētaṟ pōtamilārk kutavum tuṇaiyēcat tuvamētat tuvamēeṉ ṉuḷattē cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: O God who stands without equal! O Primordial Source who shines as both the One and the Many spoken of in the scriptures! You are the great flood that fills all without a dam, the fire upon that flood! O my Father, the raft that carries me beyond all states of being! You are the true substance, true glory, true refuge! You are the common space, the one reality that is! You are the companion who helps those without ego-consciousness, you are beingness itself, the ultimate principle! O Siddha-crest-jewel performing the pure dance within my heart!
commentary: God is the one reality without a second, an infinite flood of consciousness that fills everything. For those struggling, this immense power becomes a personal raft, carrying them beyond the turbulent states of the mind (avattai). This divine help is specifically available to those who have surrendered their separate ego-consciousness (taṟpōtam).

translit: erutiṉuḻait tiruntēṉuk kiraṅkiaṭic ciṟiyēṉ irunta:iṭan taṉaittēṭi iṇaipparimāṉ īrkkum orutiruttēr ūrnteṉṉai uṭaiyavaḷō ṭaṭaintē uḷvāyil tāḻpiṭittup payattoṭuniṉ ṟēṉē varutieṉat tirukkaraṅkaḷ acaittaḻaitta patiyē maṇiyēeṉ maruntēeṉ vāḻvēeṉ varamē curutimuṭi aṭikkaṇinta turaiyēeṉ uḷattē cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: You took pity on me as I toiled like an ox. Seeking out the place where this humble servant was, you arrived with my Mistress, riding a sacred chariot drawn by a pair of swift horses. I stood at the inner gate, holding the latch, filled with fear. O Lord, you gestured with your sacred hands, beckoning me to come! O jewel, my medicine, my life, my boon! O Sovereign who wears the crest of the Sruti on your feet! O Siddha-crest-jewel performing the pure dance in my heart!
commentary: This verse tells a moving story of grace. The speaker feels lost and humbled, "toiling like an ox," but God actively seeks him out. Even when the soul is frozen with fear and feels unworthy, the divine beckons it forward with love. God is described as wearing the highest sacred texts (Sruti) as ornaments on his feet, showing that divine compassion is superior to any scripture.

translit: akavaṭivai orukaṇattē aṉakavaṭi vākki aruḷamutam uvantaḷittē aṭikkaṭieṉ uḷattē mukavaṭivan taṉaikkāṭṭi kaḷittuviyan tiṭavē muṭipaṉaittum uṇarttiōru muṉṉilaiil lātē cakavaṭivil tāṉāki nāṉāki nāṉum tāṉumoru vaṭivākit taṉittōṅkap purintē cukavaṭivan taṉaiaḷitta turaiyēeṉ uḷattē cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: In a single moment, you transformed my inner self into a flawless form. Joyfully giving me the ambrosia of grace, you repeatedly revealed your own form within my heart. Causing me to rejoice and marvel, you made me realize the entirety of the final attainment. With no sense of an 'other' before me, you became the form of the world, you became me, and then, making 'I' and 'you' into a single form, you made me flourish in uniqueness. O Sovereign who bestowed the form of bliss! O Siddha-crest-jewel performing the pure dance within my heart!
commentary: Spiritual transformation can happen in an instant through an act of grace. God purifies the inner self, reveals the divine form within the heart, and bestows the ultimate realization. The experience culminates in the dissolution of all separateness: God becomes the world, becomes the self, and finally merges the "I" and "you" into a single, blissful reality. Yet this merging does not annihilate the self; instead, it allows the soul to "flourish in uniqueness," fully realizing its true nature within the whole.

translit: uṭuttatukil aviḻttuvirit torutaraiyil taṉittē uṉṉātum uṉṉiuḷat tuṟukalakkat tōṭē paṭuttayarnta ciṟiyēṉṟaṉ arukaṇaintu makaṉē payamuṉakkeṉ eṉṟeṉṉaip parintutiruk karattāl aṭuttaṇaittuk koṇṭeṭuttup pōyppiṟitōr iṭattē amarttinakait taruḷiyaeṉ āṇṭavaṉē aracē toṭuttaṇieṉ moḻimālai aṇintukoṇṭeṉ uḷattē cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: When I, this lowly one, lay exhausted and alone on the bare ground, my clothes loosened, my heart in deep turmoil, my thoughts coming and going, you drew near. You asked, ‘My son, what is there for you to fear?’, and with your sacred hand, you compassionately embraced and lifted me. You took me to another place, seated me there, and smiled graciously. O my Master, my King, who accepts and wears the garland of my words, O Crest-jewel of consciousness, performing the pure dance within my heart.
commentary: God's presence is most felt in our moments of greatest vulnerability. Vallalar describes a scene of utter despair: lying alone, exhausted, and in deep inner turmoil. It is here that the divine appears, with the tenderness of a parent. God's response is simple and direct: a comforting question, a compassionate embrace, and a gentle smile. This is a powerful depiction of grace as an intimate, personal act of comfort when we are at our lowest.

translit: āṟṟāta aṭicciṟiyēṟ kāṟṟalmikak koṭuttē ammaiyumāy appaṉumāy ātarittaṉ puṭaṉē pōṟṟāta kuṟṟamelām poṟuttaruḷi eṉaiip pūtalattār vāṉakattār pōṟṟimatit tiṭavē ēṟṟāta uyarnilaimēl ēṟṟiellām valla iṟaimaiyumtan taruḷiyaeṉ iṟaiyavaṉē eṉakkē tōṟṟāta tōṟṟuvitta turaiyēeṉ uḷattē cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: To me, this powerless, lowly slave, you gave great strength. Becoming both my mother and father, you lovingly cherished me. You graciously forgave all my unworthy faults and elevated me to a high state never before reached, so that the people of this earth and the beings of heaven would praise and esteem me. You granted me all-powerful sovereignty itself, my Lord! O Master who made appear to me what had never appeared, O Crest-jewel of consciousness, performing the pure dance within my heart.
commentary: Grace is a power that inverts the soul's worldly condition. Vallalar begins by describing himself as a "powerless, lowly slave," but through grace, he is given great strength and cherished as if by a divine mother and father. This inner transformation brings an outer one, elevating him to a state honored by all beings. The ultimate gift is "sovereignty" itself, a spiritual mastery that reveals truths and realities previously unimaginable.

translit: paṭippaṭakkik kēḷvielām paṟṟaṟaviṭ ṭaṭakkip pārttiṭalum aṭakkiuṟum paricamelām aṭakkit taṭippuṟumūṇ cuvaiaṭakkik kantamelām aṭakkic cātimatam camayameṉum caḻakkaiyumviṭ ṭaṭakki maṭippaṭakki niṉṟālum nillēṉnāṉ eṉavē vaṉakkuraṅkum viyappaeṉṟaṉ maṉakkuraṅku kutitta tuṭippaṭakki āṭkoṇṭa turaiyēeṉ uḷattē cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: Even when I suppressed my learning, let go of all I heard, controlled my sight, my sense of touch, the taste of coarse food, and all smells; even when I abandoned the evils of caste, religion, and creed and subdued my sloth, my monkey-mind, declaring, "I will not be still!", leaped about in a way that would astonish even forest monkeys. O Master who subdued its frantic leaping and made me your own, O Crest-jewel of consciousness, performing the pure dance within my heart.
commentary: Sincere self-discipline is often not enough to quiet the mind. Vallalar describes his own rigorous efforts: controlling all five senses, abandoning the divisive evils of caste and religion, and fighting laziness. Yet, despite all this, his "monkey-mind" remained uncontrollably restless. The verse makes a plain point about spiritual life: ultimate peace is a gift of grace, which alone can subdue the mind's frantic energy and make the soul its own.

translit: paṇintaṟiyēṉ aṉpuṭaṉē pāṭutalum aṟiyēṉ paṭittaṟiyēṉ kēṭṭaṟiyēṉ pattiyilpū mālai aṇintaṟiyēṉ maṉamurukak kaṇkaḷiṉnīr peruka aḻutaṟiyēṉ toḻutaṟiyēṉ akaṅkāram ciṟitum taṇintaṟiyēṉ tayavaṟiyēṉ cattiyavā cakamum tāṉaṟiyēṉ uḻuntaṭitta taṭiyatupōl iruntēṉ tuṇinteṉakkum karuṇaiceyta turaiyēeṉ uḷattē cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: I do not know how to bow down, nor how to sing with love. I have not studied sacred texts, nor have I listened to them. I have not adorned you with flower garlands in devotion. I do not know how to weep with a melting heart and eyes overflowing with tears. I do not know how to worship. My arrogance has not subsided one bit; I do not know compassion, nor do I know truthful speech. I was as inert as a stick used for threshing black gram. O Master who boldly showed grace even to me, O Crest-jewel of consciousness, performing the pure dance within my heart.
commentary: Vallalar's self-description is strikingly blunt: he was inert, arrogant, and empty of the virtues normally considered prerequisites for spiritual life. He compares himself to an unthinking object, "a stick used for threshing." This extreme confession serves to magnify the sheer, unconditional nature of the grace he received, which was given "boldly" despite his utter lack of qualification.

translit: tāṅkātē paciperukkik kaṭaināypōl ulampit tavamviṭuttē avantoṭuttē taṉittuṇṭum vayiṟu vīṅkātēl eḻuntirukkēṉ vīṅkiveṭit tiṭalpōl vimmumeṉil eḻuntuṭaṉē veṟuntaṭipōl viḻuntē vāṅkātu tūṅkiyatōr vaḻakkamuṭai yēṉai valintaṭimai koṇṭaruḷi maṟappoḻitten nāḷum tūṅkātē viḻikkavaitta turaiyēeṉ uḷattē cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: My habit was this: unable to bear my great hunger, I would wail like a street dog. Abandoning austerity for useless deeds, I would eat alone and not rise until my stomach was swollen. If it swelled as though to burst, I would get up only to fall at once like a dead stick and sleep without stirring. Me, a man of such habits, you forcefully took as your slave, ended my forgetfulness, and made me stay awake always, never sleeping. O Master, O Crest-jewel of consciousness, performing the pure dance within my heart.
commentary: The focus here shifts from spiritual failings to a base, physical existence. Vallalar portrays his past self as enslaved by hunger and lethargy, living a life of crude instinct. God's grace is shown as a powerful interruption of this cycle, forcefully pulling him out of the "sleep" of worldly forgetfulness into a perpetual state of divine awareness.
NOTES
Note 328

tamil: தனித்துண்டு வயிறும் - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு., பி. இரா., ச. மு. க.
translit: taṉittuṇṭu vayiṟum - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu., pi. irā., ca. mu. ka.
translation: taṉittuṇṭu vayiṟum — reading of the first edition, Po. Su., P. Irā., S. Mu. Ka.

translit: āvāeṉ ṟeṉaiyāṭkoṇ ṭaruḷiyateḷ ḷamutē ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē cāvāta varameṉakkut tantaperun takaiyē tayānitiyē ciṟcapaiyil taṉittaperum patiyē ōvāteṉ uḷḷakattē ūṟṟeḻumpē raṉpē uḷḷapaṭi eṉṉaṟivil uḷḷaperuñ cukamē nīvāeṉ moḻikaḷelām nilaittapayaṉ peṟavē nittiraitīrn tēṉiravu nīṅkiviṭin tatuvē
translation: O clear nectar who graciously took me as your own, crying “Ah”! My mother, my father, my master, my king! O great benefactor who granted me the boon of immortality! O treasure of compassion, O singular great Lord in the Hall of Consciousness! O great love that ceaselessly springs from my heart! O great bliss that exists in my consciousness, just as it is! Come, You, so that all my words may attain their lasting purpose! My sleep has ended; the night has passed, it has dawned.
commentary: The dawning of the day is a powerful metaphor for spiritual enlightenment. Vallalar declares that the "night" of worldly existence is over and he is now awake, a state brought about by God's grace. This grace grants him the ultimate boon of immortality and reveals God within his own heart (Cirsabai, the Hall of Consciousness) as an endless spring of love and bliss.

translit: ārālum aṟintukoḷaṟ kariyaperum poruḷē ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē kārālum kaṉalālum kāṟṟālum kakaṉak kalaiyālum katirālum kaṭalālum kaṭalcūḻ pārālum paṭaiyālum piṟavālum taṭukkap paṭutalilāt taṉivaṭivam eṉakkaḷitta patiyē cīrālum kuṇattālum ciṟantavarcēr ñāṉa cittipurat tamutēeṉ nittiraitīrn tatuvē.
translation: O great reality, difficult for anyone to comprehend! My mother, my father, my master, my king! O Lord who bestowed on me a unique form that cannot be hindered by rain clouds, by fire, by wind, by the expanse of space, by the sun, by the sea, by the sea-girt earth, by weapons, or by anything else! O nectar of Gnana Siddhipuram, where those preeminent in honor and character gather! My sleep has ended.
commentary: This verse describes the incredible gift of a transformed, immortal body. Vallalar lists the fundamental forces of nature and humanity, from fire and wind to armies, and states that his new physical form is beyond their power to harm. He calls God the nectar of Gnana Siddhipuram, the City of Wisdom's Perfection where the noble gather, Vallalar's own name for Vadalur.

translit: ātiantam tōṟṟāta arumperuñcō tiyaṉē ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē ōtienta vakaiyālum uṇarntukoḷaṟ karitāy uḷḷapaṭi iyaṟkaiyilē uḷḷaoru poruḷē ūtiyamtan teṉaiyāṭkoṇ ṭuḷḷiṭattum puṟattum ōvāmal viḷaṅkukiṉṟa uṭaiyavaṉē intac cātiinta matameṉumvāyc caḻakkaielām tavirtta cattiyaṉē uṇkiṉṟēṉcattiyatteḷ ḷamutē.
translation: O rare and great Jothi whose beginning and end do not appear! O my mother, my father, my master, my king! O unparalleled Reality existing naturally as you truly are, hard to realize by any kind of study. O Master who gave me a great reward and took me into your service, shining unceasingly within and without! O truthful One who removed all verbal squabbles about caste and religion! I consume the clear nectar of truth.
commentary: God cannot be grasped by study of any kind; God simply is, as God is. Vallalar knows this One as Mother, Father, Master and King, shining in him and around him without pause. The same True One ended for him all the empty talk of "this caste" and "this religion." What remains is not a doctrine but a taste: he is drinking the clear nectar of Truth.

translit: accamelām tavirttaruḷi iccaielām aḷitta ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē tuccavula kācārat tuṭukkaṉaittum tavirttē cuttaneṟi vaḻaṅkuvitta cittacikā maṇiyē uccanilai naṭuviḷaṅkum orutalaimaip patiyē ulakamelām eṭuttiṭiṉum ulavāta nitiyē iccamayam eḻuntaruḷi iṟavāta varamum ellāñcey vallacittiṉ iyaṟkaiyuntan taṉaiyē.
translation: O my mother, my father, my master, my king, who graciously dispelled all fear and fulfilled all desires! O crown jewel of Siddhas who removed all the reckless and trivial worldly customs and bestowed the pure path! O one supreme Lord shining in the center of the highest state! O inexhaustible treasure even if the whole world draws from you! You manifested at this very moment and gave me the boon of deathlessness and the nature of all-powerful divine action.
commentary: Vallalar thanks God for two gifts given "at this very moment": the boon of deathlessness and the power of the Siddhi that can do all things. First God cleared the ground, removing his fears and ending the petty customs of the world so that the Pure Path could be given in their place. Deathlessness is not a hope here. He says he has received it.

translit: aṉpuṭaiya eṉṉaṟivē aruḷuṭaiya poruḷē ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē tuṉpuṭaiya ulakarelām cukamuṭaiyār ākat tuṉmārkkam tavirttaruḷic caṉmārkkam vaḻaṅka iṉpuṭaiya pēraruḷiṅ keṉaipporuḷcey taḷitta eṉamutē eṉuṟavē eṉakkiṉiya tuṇaiyē eṉpuṭainī irukkiṉṟāy uṉpuṭaināṉ makiḻntē irukkiṉṟēṉ ivvorumai yārpeṟuvār īṇṭē.
translation: O my loving knowledge! O gracious Reality! O my mother, my father, my master, my king! To make all the sorrowful people of the world joyful, you gracefully removed the evil path and bestowed Sanmarkkam. Bestowing upon me your blissful great grace here, you deemed me worthy. O my nectar, my relation, my sweet companion! You reside by my side, and I reside joyfully by your side. Who can attain such unity in this world?
commentary: The grace Vallalar received was not for himself alone. God gave it so that all who suffer in the world may become happy, turning them from the evil path (tuṉmārkkam) to the true path (Sanmarkkam). The verse ends in quiet wonder at the oneness he now lives: God beside him and he beside God, rejoicing. Who else, he asks, has received this?

translit: aṭukkiyapē raṇṭamelām aṇukkaḷeṉa viritta ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē naṭukkiyaeṉ accamelām tavirttaruḷi aḻiyā ñāṉaamu taḷittulakil nāṭṭiyapē raṟivē iṭukkiyakaip piḷḷaieṉa iruntaciṟi yēṉuk kellāñcey vallacitti īntaperun takaiyē muṭukkiyaañ ñāṉānta kāramelām tavirttu muttaruḷat tēmuḷaitta cuttaparañ cuṭarē.
translation: You who spread out all the stacked universes as mere atoms! My Mother! My Father! My Master! My King! Great Wisdom who removed all my trembling fear, gave me the ambrosia of deathless knowledge, and established me in the world! Great Being who bestowed the all-accomplishing siddhi upon this little one who was like a child held at the hip! Pure Supreme Radiance who drove away all the dense, pursuing darkness of ignorance and sprouted in the hearts of the liberated!
commentary: God is both vast enough to create universes and intimate enough to care for a single soul like a parent. Vallalar describes this dual nature: a cosmic power who sees entire universes as tiny atoms, yet also a personal protector who holds him close, like a mother holding a child at her hip. This protector grants comfort and siddhi (supernatural power) and the deathless knowledge that dispels all ignorance, sprouting like a light in the hearts of those who become free.

translit: āṅkāram tavirntavaruḷ ōṅkāniṉ ṟavaṉē ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē ōṅkāra nilaikāṭṭi ataṉmēluṟ ṟoḷirum orunilaiyum kāṭṭiappāl uyarntataṉi nilaiyil pāṅkāka ēṟṟientap patattalaiva rālum paṭaikkavoṇāc cittiyaināṉ paṭaikkavaitta patiyē tūṅkātu peruñcukamē cukittiṭa:iv vulakaic cuttacaṉmārk kantaṉilē vaittaruḷka viraintē.
translation: You who stand exalted in the grace of those who have renounced ego! My Mother! My Father! My Master! My King! Lord who showed me the state of Omkara, showed me the single state that shines above it, and then graciously elevated me to the supreme, solitary state beyond, making me attain a siddhi that no master of other high stations could create! For this world to enjoy great bliss without sleeping, please swiftly establish it in the pure Sanmarkkam.
commentary: The path to God begins with letting go of the ego. Once that is done, Vallalar says, God reveals a series of higher states of consciousness, starting with the awareness of Omkara (the primal sound 'Om') and leading to a supreme, solitary state. Having received this grace, his focus turns outward: he prays for all of humanity to be established in the Sanmarkkam (the True Path) so they too can experience this unending bliss.

translit: āṭakappoṟ capainaṭuvē nāṭakañcey taruḷum ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē ēṭakattē eḻutāta maṟaikaḷelām kaḷittē eṉuḷattē eḻutuvitta eṉurimaip patiyē pāṭakakkāl maṭantaiyarum maintarumcaṉ mārkkap payaṉpeṟanal aruḷaḷitta paramparaṉē māyaik kāṭakattai vaḷañceṟinta nāṭakamāp purinta karuṇaiyaṉē ciṟcapaiyil kaṉintanaṟuṅ kaṉiyē.
translation: You who graciously perform the dance in the center of the hall of pure gold! My Mother! My Father! My Master! My King! My own Lord, who joyfully had all the Vedas, which are unwritten on palm-leaf manuscripts, written within my heart! Supreme One who gives grace so that women with anklet-adorned feet and men may receive the benefit of Sanmarkkam! Merciful One who turned the dense forest of maya into a land rich with abundance! Ripe, fragrant fruit in the Chit Sabhai!
commentary: Divine truth is revealed directly within the heart. Vallalar describes God inscribing the "unwritten Vedas" inside him, a knowledge deeper than any scripture. In His mercy, God has turned the wild forest of maya into a fruitful land. This God, who makes the path of Sanmarkkam accessible to both women and men, is experienced as a sweet, ripe fruit within the Chit Sabhai (the inner space of pure consciousness).

translit: aṭiyāteṉ ṟaṟintukoḷaṟ karumperiya nilaiyē ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē muṭiyāteṉ ṟaṟintiṭaṟku muṭiyāteṉ ṟuṇarntōr moḻintiṭavē muṭiyātu muṭintataṉi muṭipē kaṭiyāta peruṅkaruṇaik karuttēeṉ karuttil kaṉintukaṉin tiṉikkiṉṟa kaṉiyēeṉ kaḷippē maṭiyāta vaṭiveṉakku vaḻaṅkiyanal varamē maṇimaṉṟil naṭampuriyum vāḻkkai iyaṟ poruḷē.
translation: O great state, so difficult to know as the very foundation! My Mother! My Father! My Master! My King! Unique consummation, which those who realized it is impossible to know as an end say is impossible even to speak of! Essence of great, unending compassion, you are the fruit that ripens over and over in my mind, growing ever sweeter, you are my delight! The great boon that granted me an undying form! The very substance of life, dancing in the Maṉimaṉṟam!
commentary: The ultimate reality is beyond words and even beyond intellectual understanding. Vallalar calls it a state that those who have reached it find impossible to describe. Yet, this unknowable absolute is also a deeply personal experience: a sweet fruit of compassion ripening continuously in his mind. This realization grants him an "undying form." God is the very substance of life, a joyful dance happening within the inner "hall of gems" (Maṉimaṉṟam).

translit: aṉantamaṟai ākamaṅkaḷ aḷappariya civamē ammēeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē maṉantaruvā taṉaitavirttōraṟiviṉilōr aṟivāy vayaṅkukiṉṟa kuruvēeṉ vāṭṭamelām tavirttē iṉantaḻuvi eṉṉuḷattē iruntuyiril kalanteṉ eṇṇamelām kaḷittaḷitta eṉṉurimaip patiyē ciṉantavirntev vulakamumōr caṉmārkkam aṭaintē ciṟappuṟavait taruḷkiṉṟa cittacikā maṇiyē.
translation: O Sivam, immeasurable by the infinite Vedas and Agamas! My Mother! My Father! My Master! My King! O Guru, shining as the knowledge within the knowledge of those who have rid themselves of mental vasanas, you ended all my suffering! My own Lord, you embraced me as your own, stayed in my heart, mingled with my life, and joyfully fulfilled all my thoughts! O Siddha Sigamani (crest-jewel of perfected beings) who graciously causes all worlds to renounce anger, attain the one Sanmarkkam, and flourish!
commentary: The true nature of God, called Sivam (the auspicious one), cannot be measured by the vast scriptures of the Vedas and Agamas. He is the inner Guru, the pure awareness that shines within those who have quieted their minds of latent tendencies (vasanas). This inner teacher embraces the soul, fulfills its deepest aspirations, and establishes a universal True Path (Sanmarkkam) of peace for all worlds by removing anger.

translation: tavirntōr — reading of the P. Irā. edition.

translit: aruṭperuñ cōti amutamē amutam aḷitteṉai vaḷarttiṭa aruḷām teruṭperun tāytaṉ kaiyilē koṭutta teyvamē cattiyac civamē iruṭperu nilattaik kaṭattieṉ ṟaṉaimēl ēṟṟiya iṉpamē ellāp poruṭperu neṟiyum kāṭṭiya kuruvē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O Grace-Great Jothi! O Amutham! O God who gave me into the hands of Grace, the great mother of clarity, to raise me on Amutham! O true Sivam! O Bliss that helped me cross the vast land of darkness and lifted me up! O Guru who showed me the great path to all things of substance! O Substance performing the universal dance!
commentary: God is ArutPerunJothi and the nectar (amutham) that nourishes the soul. God placed Vallalar in the hands of Grace (Arul), the great mother of clarity, to raise him on that nectar, and lifted him across the vast land of darkness. The same God is the Guru who reveals the path and the Substance performing the universal dance.

translit: cittelām valla cittaṉē ñāṉa citampara jōtiyē ciṟiyēṉ kattelām tavirttuk karuttelām aḷitta kaṭavuḷē karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalē cattelām oṉṟē cattiyam eṉaeṉ taṉakkaṟi vittatōr tayaiyē puttelām nīkkip poruḷelām kāṭṭum potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O Siddhancapable of all siddhis! O Jothi of Gnana Chidambaram! O God who removed all the clamor of this lowly one and bestowed all true understanding! O ocean of compassion! O Grace that taught me the truth that all existence is one! O Substance that removes all fabrications and reveals all realities, performing the universal dance!
commentary: God is the perfected being (Siddhan) who possesses all powers (siddhis) to bestow clarity and peace. As the Jothi of Gnana Chidambaram (the inner space of wisdom), he quiets the mind's constant noise and reveals the most fundamental truth: all of existence (sat) is a single, unified reality. This truth is the meaning behind the universal dance.

translit: kalaikaḷōr aṉantam aṉantamēl nōkkik kaṟpaṅkaḷ kaṇakkila kaṭappa nilaikaḷōr aṉantam nēṭiyuṅ kāṇā nittiya niṟkuṇaniṟaivē alaikaḷaṟ ṟuyiruk kamutaḷit taruḷum aruṭperuṅ kaṭaleṉum aracē pulaikaḷa vakaṟṟi eṉakkuḷē niṟaintu potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O eternal, attributeless fullness, which cannot be found even after seeking through infinite states, transcending countless kalpas, and looking upward through infinite arts! O King known as the great ocean of grace, which, free of waves, bestows Amutham upon souls! O Substance that removed my impurities, filled me from within, and performs the universal dance!
commentary: The divine is an eternal, formless fullness that eludes all human attempts to define it through learning, spiritual disciplines, or seeking across cosmic ages (kalpas). Yet this same transcendent reality is also a calm ocean of grace that personally bestows immortalizing nectar (amutham) upon the soul. The infinite, which is beyond all measure, becomes an intimate presence that purifies and fills one from within.

translit: taṇṇiya matiyē taṉittaceñ cuṭarē cattiya cāttiyak kaṉalē oṇṇiya oḷiyē oḷikkuḷōr oḷiyē ulakelān taḻaikkamey uḷattē naṇṇiya viḷakkē eṇṇiya paṭikkē nalkiya ñāṉapō ṉakamē puṇṇiya nitiyē kaṇṇiya nilaiyē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O cool moon! O unique crimson flame! O fire of truth and its attainment! O radiant light, O light within light! O lamp that appeared in the true heart so that all worlds may flourish! O feast of wisdom granted just as I wished! O treasure of virtue! O venerable state! O Substance performing the universal dance!
commentary: God is experienced through paradox: as both a "cool moon" of peace and a "crimson flame" of truth. This divine reality is the ultimate source of all light, a lamp that shines within the heart so the whole world can flourish. Vallalar calls this a "feast of wisdom" and a "treasure of virtue," showing that spiritual realization is an idea and a deeply nourishing and morally transforming experience.

translit: aṟputa niṟaivē caṟputaraṟivil aṟiveṉa aṟikiṉṟa aṟivē coṟpuṉai māyaik kaṟpaṉai kaṭanta turiyanal nilattilē tulaṅkum ciṟparañ cuṭarē taṟpara ñāṉac celvamē cittelām puriyum poṟpulam aḷitta naṟpulak karuttē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O wondrous fullness! O consciousness known as the consciousness within the consciousness of the virtuous! O supreme transcendent flame shining in the good state of Turiya, beyond the imaginings of word-woven māyā! O wealth of self-transcendent wisdom! O essence of the good realm that bestowed the golden realm where all siddhis are possible! O Substance performing the universal dance!
commentary: God is pure consciousness, the awareness that exists within the awareness of even the most virtuous people. This reality shines in the state of Turiya, a pure awareness beyond the ordinary states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. It is free from māyā, the illusion and limitation created by language and concepts. Attaining this state grants access to the "golden realm" where all spiritual abilities (siddhis) become possible.

translit: tattuva patiyē tattuvam kaṭanta taṉittatōr cattiya patiyē cattuva neṟiyil cārntacaṉ mārkkar tamakkuḷē cārntanaṟ cārpē pittuṟu camayap piṇakkuṟum avarkkup peṟalari tākiyapēṟē puttamu taḷitteṉ uḷattilē kalantu potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O Lord of the tattvas, O unique Lord of Truth who transcends the tattvas! O good support dwelling within the Sanmarkkis who follow the sattvic path! O blessing difficult to attain for those caught in the madness of quarreling religions! O Substance performing the universal dance, you give me fresh nectar and mingle within my heart.
commentary: God is the reality behind all the principles of existence (tattvas) and also the truth that lies beyond them. This divine support is found directly within the Sanmarkkis, those who follow the "true path" of goodness and purity (sattvic path). For those lost in the "madness of quarreling religions," this direct experience remains out of reach.

translit: mēlveḷi kāṭṭi veḷiyilē viḷainta viḷaivelām kāṭṭimey vēta nūlvaḻi kāṭṭi eṉṉuḷē viḷaṅkum nōkkamē ākkamum tiṟalum nālvakaip payaṉum aḷitteṉai vaḷarkkum nāyakak karuṇainaṟ ṟāyē pōluyirk kuyirāyp poruntiya maruntē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O vision shining within me, who shows me the supreme space, all that manifested in that space, and the path of the true scriptures! O supreme, good mother of grace who gives prosperity, power, and the four kinds of fruits to nourish me! O medicine perfectly suited to be the life of life! O Substance performing the universal dance!
commentary: God acts as an inner guide, revealing the "supreme space" of reality and the path of the true scriptures. Vallalar addresses this divine grace as a mother who lovingly nourishes him by providing prosperity, power, and the "four kinds of fruits" or goals of life. Above all, God is the "life of life," the essential medicine and animating principle at the heart of every living being.

translit: alappaṟa viḷaṅkum aruṭperu viḷakkē arumperuñ cōtiyē cuṭarē malappiṇi aṟutta vāymaiem maruntē maruntelām poruntiya maṇiyē ulappaṟu karuṇaic celvamē ellā uyirkkuḷum niṟaintatōr uṇarvē pulappakai tavirkkum pūraṇa varamē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O great lamp of grace shining immeasurably! O rare great Jothi, O flame! O our true medicine that severs the disease of mala! O gem in which all medicines are perfectly contained! O singular consciousness that fills all living beings! O perfect boon that averts the enmity of the senses! O Substance performing the universal dance!
commentary: God is the infinite Light of Grace, or Jothi, that acts as the ultimate medicine for the soul. It cures the 'disease' of mala (the soul's inherent impurity) and is the perfect remedy for all spiritual afflictions. This divine light is also the one consciousness that fills every living being, and the gift that frees us from the conflict created by our senses.

translit: parampara niṟaivē parāpara veḷiyē paramaciṟ cukantarum patiyē varampeṟu civacaṉ mārkkartam matiyil vayaṅkiya peruñcuṭar maṇiyē karampeṟu kaṉiyē kaṉivuṟu cuvaiyē karutiya karuttuṟu kaḷippē purampukaḻ nitiyē cirampukal katiyē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O fullness of the Supreme! O space of the Supreme! O Lord who gives the bliss of supreme consciousness! O great gem of light shining in the minds of the blessed Siva-Sanmarkkis! O fruit received in hand, O taste of full ripeness, O bliss at the heart of my every thought! O treasure praised by the worlds, O refuge sought with bowed head! O Substance performing the universal dance!
commentary: The divine is described as an immediate, tangible experience. For the Siva-Sanmarkkis (followers of the true path of Siva), God is a 'fruit received in hand' and the 'taste of full ripeness.' It is the fullness of being, the bliss of supreme consciousness, and the joyful core of every thought, a treasure and refuge for all.

translit: veṟpuṟu muṭiyil tampamēl ēṟṟi meynnilai amarvitta viyappē kaṟpuṟu karuttil iṉikkiṉṟa karumpē karuṇaivāṉ amutatteṇ kaṭalē aṟpuṟum aṟivil aruḷoḷi āki āṉanta māmaṉu pavamē poṟpuṟu patiyē aṟputa nitiyē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O wonder who lifted me up the pillar on the mountain peak and established me in the state of truth! O sugarcane sweet to a chaste mind! O clear ocean of the heavenly nectar of grace! O experience of bliss, becoming the light of grace within astounding wisdom! O resplendent Lord, O wondrous treasure! O Substance performing the universal dance!
commentary: Spiritual attainment is a wondrous act of grace, where the divine lifts the soul to the 'state of truth.' The image of being raised 'up the pillar on the mountain peak' refers to the ascent of consciousness to its highest point. This elevated state is an intensely sweet and blissful experience, an ocean of nectar that is the light of grace itself.

translit: taṉmaikāṇ pariya talaivaṉē ellām taravalla campuvē camayap puṉmainīt takamum puṟamumot tamainta puṇṇiyar naṇṇiya pukalē vaṉmaicēr maṉattai naṉmaicēr maṉamā vayaṅkuvit tamarntamey vāḻvē poṉmaicār kaṉakap potuvoṭu ñāṉap potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O Leader whose nature is difficult to perceive! O Sambu who can grant everything! O Refuge sought by the virtuous, who have renounced the pettiness of religions and achieved harmony between their inner and outer selves! O true Life who transformed my hard heart into a good one and settled there! O Being who performs the public dance in the golden public space and the public space of wisdom!
commentary: Though the divine's ultimate nature is hard to grasp, its effects are clear and personal. It is the refuge for virtuous people who have moved beyond religious pettiness to achieve harmony between their inner and outer lives. This God, called Sambu (bestower of good), performs the greatest transformation: it softens a hard heart into a good one and makes that heart its home.

translit: mūviru muṭipiṉ muṭintatōrmuṭipē muṭipelām kaṭantatōr mutalē tāviya mutalum kaṭaiyummēṟ kāṭṭāc cattiyat taṉinaṭu nilaiyē mēviya naṭuvil viḷaṅkiya viḷaivē viḷaivelām tarukiṉṟa veḷiyē pūviyal aḷitta puṉitacaṟ kuruvē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O ultimate Conclusion that is the end of the six philosophical systems! O Primal One who transcends all conclusions! O unique central state of Truth that reveals no beginning or end! O Fruition shining within that established center! O Space that yields all fruition! O holy Satguru who granted the nature of blossoming! O Being who performs the public dance!
commentary: God is the final truth that all philosophies try to explain, yet God also exists beyond any system or conclusion. This ultimate reality is a timeless, central state without beginning or end; it is the source from which all of life's "fruition," or results, comes. Vallalar calls God the Satguru (the true teacher), who makes it possible for the soul to blossom into its divine nature.

translit: vētamum poruḷum payaṉumōr aṭaivum viḷampiya aṉupava viḷaivum pōtamum cukamum ākiiṅ kivaikaḷ pōṉatu māyoḷir pulamē ētamuṟ ṟirunta ēḻaiyēṉ poruṭṭiv virunilat tiyalaruḷ oḷiyāl pūtanal vaṭivam kāṭṭieṉ uḷattē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: You are the Vedas, their meaning, their fruit, the path, the resulting experience, the awareness, and the bliss; you are also the shining expanse where all of these have ceased. For the sake of me, this poor one in distress, you revealed a good form of the elements on this vast earth with your light of grace, and you are the Being who performs the public dance within my heart.
commentary: God is everything on the spiritual path: the scriptures (Vedas), their meaning, the blissful experience they lead to, and the awareness itself. Yet God is also the vast, silent consciousness that exists when all these things fall away. For the sake of a suffering soul, this formless God takes on a physical form, revealing a tangible presence and performing the dance of existence within the devotee's own heart.

translit: aṭiyaṉēṉ poruṭṭiv vavaṉimēl karuṇai aruḷvaṭi veṭutteḻun taruḷi neṭiyaṉē mutalōr peṟaṟkarum citti nilaielām aḷittamā nitiyē maṭivuṟā teṉṟum cuttacaṉ mārkkam vayaṅkanal varantanta vāḻvē poṭiaṇi kaṉakap poruppoḷir neruppē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: For the sake of this devotee, you graciously took on a form of compassion and grace and arose on this earth. O great Treasure who granted all states of siddhi, which are difficult for Vishnu and others to obtain! O Life who gave the boon for the Suddha Sanmarkkam to flourish forever without decline! O Fire that glows on the golden mountain, adorned with sacred ash! O Being who performs the public dance!
commentary: God's compassion is so great that it takes on a physical form on Earth, specifically for the sake of the devoted follower. Through this grace, Vallalar receives siddhi (extraordinary spiritual powers) that are beyond the reach of even the great gods. The greatest gift, however, is the divine promise that his path, the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure Path of Truth), will thrive forever.

translit: eṉpiḻai aṉaittum poṟuttaruḷ purinteṉ itayattil irukkiṉṟa kuruvē aṉpuṭai aracē appaṉē eṉṟaṉ ammaiyē aruṭperuñ cōti iṉpuṟu nilaiyil ēṟṟiya tuṇaiyē eṉṉuyir nātaṉē eṉṉaip poṉpuṉai mālai puṉaintaōr patiyē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O Guru who graciously forgave all my faults and resides in my heart! O loving King! O Father! O my Mother! O ArutPerunJothi! O Companion who elevated me to a state of bliss! O Lord of my life! O Master who adorned me with a garland woven of gold! O Being who performs the public dance!
commentary: This verse expresses a deeply personal and intimate relationship with God. God is the forgiving teacher (Guru) in one's heart, but also a loving king, a father, and a mother. This divine companion, whom Vallalar calls ArutPerunJothi (the Vast Grace-Light), elevates the soul to a state of bliss. The image of being adorned with a golden garland symbolizes being chosen, cherished, and united with the Divine Master.

translit: cattiya patiyē cattiya nitiyē cattiya ñāṉamē vēta nittiya nilaiyē nittiya niṟaivē nittiya vāḻvaruḷ neṟiyē cittiiṉ puruvē cittiyiṉ karuvē cittiyiṟ cittiyē eṉatu puttiyiṉ teḷivē puttamu taḷittup potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O Lord of truth, O treasure of truth, O true knowledge! O eternal state of the Vedas, O eternal perfection, O path that bestows eternal life! O form of siddhi, O seed of siddhi, O siddhi within siddhi! O clarity of my intellect, O Substance that performs the universal dance, granting fresh ambrosia!
commentary: The focus here shifts from personal relationship to ultimate reality. The divine is equated with truth itself, and with siddhi (spiritual perfection) in its every aspect: its potential (seed), its expression (form), and its very essence. This perfection is a living substance that grants clarity and eternal life, described as a "fresh ambrosia."

translit: citattoḷir paramē parattoḷir patiyē civapata aṉupavac civamē matattaṭai tavirtta matimati matiyē matiniṟai amutanal vāyppē catattiru neṟiyē taṉineṟit tuṇaiyē cāmiyē tantaiyē tāyē putapperu varamē pukaṟkarun taramē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O Supreme One shining in consciousness, O Lord shining in the Supreme, O Sivam who is the experience of the state of Siva! O wisdom of the enlightened mind that has removed the barriers of dogma, O blessed fortune of ambrosia that fills the mind! O eternal sacred path, O companion on the unique path! O Master, Father, Mother! O great boon for the wise, O quality that is difficult to describe, O Substance that performs the universal dance!
commentary: God is described as both the highest transcendent reality and the light shining within your own consciousness. The path to this union is not through religious dogma, which Vallalar calls a barrier, but through direct experience. This experience of Sivam (the divine presence) is a deeply personal one, once again named as master, father, and mother, yet it is also a state of being that is ultimately beyond description.

translit: kalaivaḷar kalaiyē kalaiyiṉuṭ kalaiyē kalaielām tarumoru karuvē nilaivaḷar karuvuṭ karueṉa vayaṅkum nittiya vāṉamē ñāṉa malaivaḷar maruntē maruntuṟu palaṉē māpalam tarukiṉṟa vāḻvē pulaitavirt teṉaiyum poruḷeṉak koṇṭu potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O art that cultivates art, O art within art, O the one source that yields all arts and sciences! O eternal space, shining as the seed within the seed that develops into a stable form! O medicine growing on the mountain of wisdom, O fruit of that medicine, O life that gives great strength! O Substance that performs the universal dance, having removed my baseness and accepted even me as someone of worth!
commentary: The divine is the origin of all human creativity and knowledge, the "art within art" and the source from which all sciences flow. This creative power is also the source of life itself, from the most fundamental "seed within the seed" to the healing power of wisdom. For Vallalar, this culminates in a deep personal gratitude: this immense, universal power reached down, removed his flaws, and gave his life value.

translit: meymmaiyē kiṭaitta meymmaiyē ñāṉa viḷakkamē viḷakkattiṉ viyappē kaimmaiyē tavirttu maṅkalam aḷitta karuṇaiyē karicilāk kaḷippē aimmaiyē ataṟkuḷ atuatu ākum aṟputak kāṭciyē eṉatu poymmaiyē poruttup pukalaḷit taruḷip potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O truth that is truth itself attained! O lamp of wisdom, O wonder of that lamp! O grace that removed my widowhood and bestowed auspiciousness, O flawless delight! O wondrous vision of the fivefold reality wherein each thing becomes itself! O Substance that performs the universal dance, having tolerated my falsehood and graciously given me refuge!
commentary: Truth is not something God possesses; God is truth itself. The line about removing 'widowhood' is a powerful metaphor for ending a state of desolation and loneliness, restoring auspiciousness through grace. Finally, this perfect truth is also a forgiving presence, accepting our flaws and falsehoods.

translit: kāraṇa aruvē kāriya uruvē kāraṇa kāriyam kāṭṭi āraṇa muṭiyum ākama muṭiyum amarntoḷir aṟputac cuṭarē nāraṇa talamēnāraṇa valamē nāraṇā kārattiṉ ñāṅkarp pūraṇa oḷicey pūraṇa civamē potunaṭam purikiṉṟa poruḷē.
translation: O formless Cause, O formed Effect! O wondrous flame that reveals Cause and Effect, seated shining at the summit of the Vedas and the Agamas! O ground of Narayana, O might of Narayana! O perfect Sivam that radiates perfect light beyond the very form of Narayana! O Substance that performs the universal dance!
commentary: The divine is both the unmanifest cause of creation and the visible world of effects. It is the ultimate truth at the heart of the highest scriptures, the Vedas and Agamas. Vallalar describes this reality, Sivam, as a perfect light that shines even beyond the highest conceptions of God in other traditions, such as Narayana (a name for Vishnu).

translit: aṉpaṉē appā ammaiyē aracē aruṭperuñ cōtiyē aṭiyēṉ tuṉpelām tolaitta tuṇaivaṉē ñāṉa cukattilē tōṟṟiya cukamē iṉpaṉē ellām vallacit tāki eṉṉuḷē ilaṅkiya poruḷē vaṉpaṉēṉ piḻaikaḷ poṟuttaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: O beloved one, O father, O mother, O king, O Vast Grace-Light! O companion who destroyed all my suffering! O bliss that appeared within the bliss of wisdom! O source of joy! O substance that, as the all-powerful consciousness, shines within me! You forgave the faults of this hard-hearted one and bestowed the grace-light. Long live Your majesty!
commentary: The relationship with the divine is expressed in the most intimate human terms: beloved, parent, king, and companion. God is the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi) who personally intervenes to end suffering. Vallalar marvels that this immense power would forgive his flaws and grant him the light of grace, expressing deep gratitude.

translit: perukumā karuṇaip peruṅkaṭal iṉpap perukkamē eṉperum pēṟē urukumōr uḷḷat tuvaṭṭuṟā tiṉikkum uṇmaivāṉ amutamē eṉpāl karukumneñ cataṉait taḷirttiṭap purinta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭavuḷē viraintu varukaeṉ ṟuraittēṉ vantaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: O great ocean of swelling compassion, O flood of bliss, O my great fortune! O true heavenly ambrosia that sweetens a melting heart without ever cloying! O compassionate God who made my withering heart sprout anew! I said, "Come quickly," and You came and bestowed the grace-light. Long live Your majesty!
commentary: Grace is described here with liquid metaphors: an ocean of compassion, a flood of bliss, and ambrosia that sweetens the heart. It has the power to revive a spirit that has withered from hardship. The verse ends with a witness to the power of sincere prayer: when Vallalar called out, God came immediately and bestowed the grace-light.

translit: entaieṉ kuruvē eṉṉuyirk kuyirē eṉṉiru kaṇṇiṉuḷ maṇiyē intuṟum amutē eṉṉuyirt tuṇaiyē iṇaiyilā eṉṉuṭai aṉpē contanal uṟavē ampalat taracē cōtiyē cōtiyē viraintu vantaruḷ eṉṟēṉ vantaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: O my father, my guru! O life of my life, O pupil of my two eyes! O cool ambrosia, O companion of my soul! O my peerless love, O my own true kin! O King of the Ambalam! O Light, O Light! I said, "Come quickly and bestow grace," and You came and bestowed the grace-light. Long live Your majesty!
commentary: Here, the names for God become even more intimate: teacher (guru), the very life of one's life, the apple of one's eye. God is the very center of our being and perception. This divine presence is the king of the Ambalam, the inner space of pure consciousness, and responds instantly to the soul's call for grace.

translit: kōeṉa eṉatu kurueṉa ñāṉa kuṇameṉa oḷircivak koḻuntē pūeṉa atilē maṇameṉa vaṇattiṉ poliveṉa vayaṅkiya poṟpē tēveṉat tēva tēveṉa orumaic civameṉa viḷaṅkiya patiyē vāeṉa uraittēṉ vantaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: O radiant, tender shoot of Sivam, whom I call King and my Guru, the very quality of wisdom! O manifested beauty, whom I call the flower, the fragrance within it, and the splendor of its color! O Lord who shines as the one Sivam, whom I call God and God of gods! I said, "Come," and You came and bestowed the grace-light. Long live Your majesty!
commentary: Vallalar uses the metaphor of a flower to explain the nature of God, whom he calls Sivam (the ultimate blissful reality). God is the flower, but also the fragrance within it and the beauty of its color; the substance and its essential qualities are one. This shows that the divine is the very essence of its beauty and reality.

translit: uḷḷamē iṭaṅkoṇ ṭeṉṉaiāṭ koṇṭa oruvaṉē ulakelām aṟiyat teḷḷamu taḷittiṅ kuṉṉaivāḻ vippēm cittamañ cēleṉṟa civamē kaḷḷamē tavirtta karuṇaimā nitiyē kaṭavuḷē kaṉakaam palatteṉ vaḷḷalē eṉṟēṉ vantaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: O the one who took my heart as Your place and made me Your own! O Sivam who said, "Mind, do not fear! We will give you clear ambrosia here for all the world to know and make you flourish"! O great treasure of compassion that removed all deceit! O God! I called You "My benefactor of the golden Ambalam," and You came and bestowed the grace-light. Long live Your majesty!
commentary: The relationship with God is one of complete surrender, where God takes the heart as a dwelling place and makes the person his own. God speaks directly to the fearful mind, promising a life-giving nectar that will remove all deceit and make the soul flourish for all to see. The "golden Ambalam" refers to the luminous, sacred space of consciousness where this transformation takes place.

translit: nallavā aḷitta nallavā eṉaiyum nayantavā nāyiṉēṉ naviṉṟa collavā eṉakkut tuṇaiyavā ñāṉa cukattavā cōtiam palavā allavā aṉaittum āṉavā eṉṉai āṇṭavā tāṇṭavā ellām vallavā eṉṟēṉ vantaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: "O Giver of good things! O Good One who desired even me! O Word uttered by me, a dog! O my Companion! O Bliss of wisdom! O One of the Luminous Hall! O You who are not all things, yet became all things! O You who rule me! O Dancer! O All-powerful One!" I cried. You came and bestowed the light of grace. Long live Your greatness!
commentary: This verse expresses deep humility and wonder. Vallalar, feeling as unworthy as a dog, is amazed that the divine being accepts him and actively desires him. He touches on a deep paradox: God is the ultimate reality beyond creation ("not all things") and simultaneously the very substance of everything that exists ("became all things"). This all-powerful, dancing energy of the cosmos still comes when a single, humble soul cries out.

translit: tiṇmaiyē mutalaiṅ kuṇakkaru vāya celvamē nalvaḻi kāṭṭum kaṇmaiyē kaṇmai kalantaeṉ kaṇṇē kaṇṇuṟa iyaintanaṟ karuttē uṇmaiyē ellām uṭaiyaōr talaimai orutaṉit teyvamē ulavā vaṇmaiyē eṉṟēṉ vantaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: "O Treasure who is the source of the five qualities, beginning with solidity! O Grace that shows the good path! O my Eye, mingled with grace! O good thought, perfectly formed for perception! O true Head that possesses all! O singular, unique God! O inexhaustible Generosity!" I cried. You came and bestowed the light of grace. Long live Your greatness!
commentary: God is described as the very source of the material world, beginning with the quality of solidity. More than that, God is the grace that functions as our inner compass and the very eye through which we perceive truth. This verse identifies the divine as both the foundation of the cosmos and the core of our personal awareness.

translit: kāymaiyē tavirttuk karuṇaiyē kaṉinta kaṟpakat taṉipperun taruvē tūymaiyē viḷakkit tuṇaimaiyē aḷitta cōtiyē tūymaiil lavarkkuc cēymaiyē ellām ceyavalla ñāṉa cittiyē cuttacaṉ mārkka vāymaiyē eṉṟēṉ vantaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: "O great, singular Kalpaga tree that has cast off all harshness and ripened into pure compassion! O Jothi that reveals purity and grants companionship! O You who are distant to the impure! O Siddhi of wisdom that can do all things! O Truth of the Suddha Sanmarkkam!" I cried. You came and bestowed the light of grace. Long live Your greatness!
commentary: God's nature is pure compassion, like a mythical Kalpaga (wish-fulfilling tree) that has shed all harshness. This divine light, or Jothi, reveals purity and is the core truth of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (Path of True Purity). Proximity to God depends on one's own purity; for those who cultivate it, God becomes an accessible Siddhi, a realized power of wisdom that can accomplish anything.

translit: eṉṉavā aṉaittum īntavā eṉṉai īṉṟavā eṉṉavā vētam coṉṉavā karuṇait tūyavā periyar tutiyavā ampalat tamutam aṉṉavā aṟivāl aṟiyari vaṟivā āṉanta nāṭakam puriyum maṉṉavā eṉṟēṉ vantaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: "O my Father who gave everything! O You who gave birth to me! O my Father who uttered the Vedas! O pure One of compassion! O You who are praised by the great ones! O You who are like the Amrita of the Ambalam! O You who are wisdom itself, difficult to grasp through intellect! O King who performs the drama of bliss!" I cried. You came and bestowed the light of grace. Long live Your greatness!
commentary: God is the origin of everything: the universe, the individual soul, and the sacred scriptures. Though praised by the wise and likened to Amrita (the nectar of immortality), God as pure wisdom cannot be captured by the intellect. Instead, God is experienced directly as the blissful cosmic drama unfolding within the sacred space of consciousness, the Ambalam.

translit: viratamā tikaḷum tavirttumeyñ ñāṉa viḷakkiṉāl eṉṉuḷam viḷakki iratamā tiyanal teḷḷamu taḷittiṅ keṉkarut taṉaittaiyum purintē caratamā nilaiyil cittelām valla cattiyait tayaviṉāl taruka varataṉē eṉṟēṉ vantaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiṉai vāḻiniṉ māṇpē.
translation: "You made me abandon vows and the like, illuminating my heart with the lamp of true wisdom. You gave me the finest clear nectar, fulfilling my every thought. 'O Varadan! With Your grace, grant me now, with certainty, the Shakti that masters all realized powers!' I cried. You came and bestowed the light of grace. Long live Your greatness!"
commentary: Most religions emphasize external practices. Here, Vallalar explains that God guided him to abandon such vows, replacing them with the direct light of true inner wisdom. Having been given this clarity and spiritual nourishment, he now asks the great Varadan (Bestower of boons) for the ultimate Shakti (power) which masters all other spiritual abilities, confident that this too will be granted by grace.
NOTES
Note 322

tamil: அறியறி வறிவா - பி. இரா., ச. மு. க.
translit: aṟiyaṟi vaṟivā - pi. irā., ca. mu. ka.
translation: aṟiyaṟi vaṟivā — reading of the P. Irā. and S. Mu. Ka. Editions.

sections.title: Attaining the Rare Nectar of Grace

tamil: விரைசேர் பொன்மல ரே - அதில் - மேவிய செந்தே னே
கரைசேர் முக்கனி யே - கனி - யிற்சுவை யின்பய னே
பரைசேர் உள்ளொளி யே - பெரும் - பற்றம்ப லநடஞ் செய்
அரைசே தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: viraicēr poṉmala rē - atil - mēviya centē ṉē karaicēr mukkaṉi yē - kaṉi - yiṟcuvai yiṉpaya ṉē paraicēr uḷḷoḷi yē - perum - paṟṟampa lanaṭañ cey araicē tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O fragrant golden flower! O pure honey dwelling in it! O three ripened fruits! O benefit of the sweetness within the fruit! O inner light united with Parai! O King who performs the dance in the great hall of Perumpatrampulam, you have given yourself; you have given the rare nectar of grace.
commentary: God is experienced here as the most intimate and delightful essence of things: the fragrance in the flower, the honey within it, the sweetness within the fruit. Vallalar connects this immanent sweetness to the highest divine principles, the inner light of Parai (the supreme power) and the cosmic dancer at Perumpatrampulam (the sacred center). Grace is the taste of this divine reality present in all things.

tamil: விண்ணார் செஞ்சுட ரே - சுடர் - மேவிய உள்ளொளி யே
தண்ணார் வெண்மதி யே - அதில் - தங்கிய தண்ணமு தே
கண்ணார் மெய்க்கன லே - சிவ - காமப்பெண் காதல னே
அண்ணா தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: viṇṇār ceñcuṭa rē - cuṭar - mēviya uḷḷoḷi yē taṇṇār veṇmati yē - atil - taṅkiya taṇṇamu tē kaṇṇār meykkaṉa lē - civa - kāmappeṇ kātala ṉē aṇṇā tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O red flame filling the sky! O inner light dwelling in the flame! O cool white moon! O cool nectar abiding in it! O true fire that fills the eye! O lover of the lady Sivakami! O Great One, you have given yourself; you have given the rare nectar of grace.
commentary: This verse uses a series of powerful, complementary images: the vast, hot flame of the sun and the cool, intimate light of the moon. God is both the overwhelming cosmic fire and the gentle nectar that cools and nourishes. He is the "true fire" in the eye, meaning the very power of sight and perception, and the beloved of Sivakami (the divine feminine), showing his relational, personal nature. Grace allows one to experience God in all these forms.

tamil: துப்பார் செஞ்சடை யாய் - அருட் - சோதிச் சுகக்கட லே
செப்பா மேனிலைக் கே - சிறி - யேனைச் செலுத்திய வா
எப்பா லும்புக ழும் - பொது - இன்ப நடம்புரி யும்
அப்பா தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: tuppār ceñcaṭai yāy - aruṭ - cōtic cukakkaṭa lē ceppā mēṉilaik kē - ciṟi - yēṉaic celuttiya vā eppā lumpuka ḻum - potu - iṉpa naṭampuri yum appā tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O you with red matted locks like coral! O ocean of bliss, the Jothi of grace! Oh, how you guided this lowly one to the supreme state beyond words! O Father, praised everywhere, who performs the blissful dance in the common hall, you have given yourself; you have given the rare nectar of grace.
commentary: The devotee expresses astonishment at his own transformation. Describing himself as "lowly," he marvels that God, the ocean of blissful Jothi (divine light), has personally guided him to a spiritual state so high it is "beyond words." The "common hall" refers to God's dance being accessible to all, more than a select few. The gift of grace is this incredible, undeserved elevation.

tamil: மெய்யா மெய்யரு ளே - என்று - மேவிய மெய்ப்பொரு ளே
கையா ருங்கனி யே - நுதற் - கண்கொண்ட செங்கரும் பே
செய்யாய் வெண்ணிறத் தாய் - திருச் - சிற்றம்ப லநடஞ் செய்
ஐயா தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: meyyā meyyaru ḷē - eṉṟu - mēviya meypporu ḷē kaiyā ruṅkaṉi yē - nutaṟ - kaṇkoṇṭa ceṅkarum pē ceyyāy veṇṇiṟat tāy - tiruc - ciṟṟampa lanaṭañ cey aiyā tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O true grace that is Truth! O eternally abiding True Substance! O rare fruit in hand! O red sugarcane with an eye on your forehead! O you who are red, you who are white! O Lord who performs the dance in the sacred Chitrambalam, you have given yourself; you have given the rare nectar of grace.
commentary: Grace is God Himself. Vallalar identifies the divine with grace itself, calling it the "True Substance." The image of a "rare fruit in hand" conveys that this ultimate reality can be directly and palpably experienced. The sacred dance in Chitrambalam (the sacred space of consciousness) points to this reality as the dynamic, conscious energy at the heart of everything.

tamil: பொறிவே றின்றி நினை - நிதம் - போற்றும் புனிதரு ளே
குறிவே றின்றி நின்ற - பெருஞ் - சோதிக் கொழுஞ்சுட ரே
செறிவே தங்களெ லாம் - உரை - செய்ய நிறைந்திடும் பே
ரறிவே தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: poṟivē ṟiṉṟi niṉai - nitam - pōṟṟum puṉitaru ḷē kuṟivē ṟiṉṟi niṉṟa - peruñ - cōtik koḻuñcuṭa rē ceṟivē taṅkaḷe lām - urai - ceyya niṟaintiṭum pē raṟivē tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O grace abiding in the holy ones who praise you daily, thinking of you without sensory distraction! O rich flame of the great Jothi, which stands without any other aim! O Supreme Wisdom, pervading all that the dense Vedas proclaim, you have given yourself; you have given the rare nectar of grace.
commentary: The divine is found in those who can focus their minds completely, free from the pull of the senses. This divine Jothi is described as having no purpose other than simply to be, a pure and self-existing flame. Vallalar sees this light as the Supreme Wisdom that is the very essence of what the ancient Vedas, the sacred scriptures, try to describe.

tamil: முத்தா முத்தரு ளே - ஒளிர் - கின்ற முழுமுத லே
சித்தா சித்திஎ லாந் - தர - வல்ல செழுஞ்சுட ரே
பித்தா பித்தனெ னை - வலிந் - தாண்ட பெருந்தகை யே
அத்தா தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: muttā muttaru ḷē - oḷir - kiṉṟa muḻumuta lē cittā cittie lān - tara - valla ceḻuñcuṭa rē pittā pittaṉe ṉai - valin - tāṇṭa peruntakai yē attā tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O eternally free one, O grace for the liberated! O radiant, complete first cause! O Siddha, O rich flame capable of granting all siddhis! O divine madman! O great one who forcefully took and ruled me, another madman! O Father, you have given it, the full nectar of grace.
commentary: God is addressed as the ultimate Siddha, a perfected being who can grant all spiritual powers (siddhis). The most striking image, however, is of God as a "divine madman" who forcefully seizes Vallalar, who sees himself as another "madman" lost in worldly delusion. This is a powerful, overwhelming intervention of grace that shatters the ego and takes complete control, an act for which he is deeply grateful.

tamil: தன்னே ரில்லவ னே - எனைத் - தந்த தயாநிதி யே
மன்னே மன்றிடத் தே - நடஞ் - செய்யுமென் வாழ்முத லே
பொன்னே என்னுயி ரே - உயி - ருள்நிறை பூரண மே
அன்னே தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: taṉṉē rillava ṉē - eṉait - tanta tayāniti yē maṉṉē maṉṟiṭat tē - naṭañ - ceyyumeṉ vāḻmuta lē poṉṉē eṉṉuyi rē - uyi - ruḷniṟai pūraṇa mē aṉṉē tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O peerless one! O treasure of compassion who gave me life! O King! O source of my life who dances in the sacred hall! O my gold, my very life! O perfect fullness that fills my soul! O Mother, you have given it, the full nectar of grace.
commentary: The divine is experienced here through a flood of personal, loving relationships. God is King, compassionate life-giver, and the sacred dancer, but also something as precious as gold, as intimate as life itself, and as nurturing as a Mother. This is a complete and all-encompassing bond.

tamil: ஒளியே அவ்வொளி யின் - நடு - உள்ளொளிக் குள்ளொளி யே
வெளியே எவ்வெளி யும் - அடங் - கின்ற வெறுவெளி யே
தளியே அம்பலத் தே - நடஞ் - செய்யுந் தயாநிதி யே
அளியே தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: oḷiyē avvoḷi yiṉ - naṭu - uḷḷoḷik kuḷḷoḷi yē veḷiyē evveḷi yum - aṭaṅ - kiṉṟa veṟuveḷi yē taḷiyē ampalat tē - naṭañ - ceyyun tayāniti yē aḷiyē tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O Light! O light within the inner light, at the very center of that light! O Space! O pure, empty space in which all other spaces are contained! O sacred temple! O treasure of compassion who dances in the sacred hall! O compassionate one, you have given it, the full nectar of grace.
commentary: Vallalar uses powerful images of infinite depth to describe God. The divine is light and the light at the very heart of all inner light. It is space and the pure, empty source from which all dimensions of space emerge. God is the ultimate ground of reality, the innermost essence of everything that exists.

tamil: மருளேய் நெஞ்சக னேன் - மன - வாட்டமெ லாந்தவிர்த் தே
தெருளே யோர்வடி வாய் - உறச் - செய்த செழுஞ்சுட ரே
பொருளே சிற்சபை வாழ் - வுறு - கின்றவென் புண்ணிய னே
அருளே தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: maruḷēy neñcaka ṉēṉ - maṉa - vāṭṭame lāntavirt tē teruḷē yōrvaṭi vāy - uṟac - ceyta ceḻuñcuṭa rē poruḷē ciṟcapai vāḻ - vuṟu - kiṉṟaveṉ puṇṇiya ṉē aruḷē tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O rich flame, you removed all the mental anguish of my deluded heart and made me one with the very form of clarity! O ultimate reality! O my sacred merit who thrives in the Chit Sabhai! O Grace, you have given it, the full nectar of grace.
commentary: Grace brings a deep inner transformation. Vallalar describes how it actively removes the "mental anguish" of a confused mind and replaces it with pure clarity.
