He calls God his "sacred merit," suggesting that this transformation is the true reward of a spiritual life, experienced in the Chit Sabhai (the inner hall of consciousness).

tamil: முன்பே என்றனை யே - வலிந் - தாட்கொண்ட முன்னவ னே
இன்பே என்னுயி ரே - எனை -ஈன்ற இறையவ னே
பொன்பே ரம்பல வா - சிவ - போகஞ்செய் சிற்சபை வாழ்
அன்பே தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: muṉpē eṉṟaṉai yē - valin - tāṭkoṇṭa muṉṉava ṉē iṉpē eṉṉuyi rē - eṉai -īṉṟa iṟaiyava ṉē poṉpē rampala vā - civa - pōkañcey ciṟcapai vāḻ aṉpē tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O primal one who forcefully took and ruled me long ago! O bliss, O my life, O my creator Lord! O master of the great golden hall, who lives in the hall of consciousness creating Siva's bliss! O Love, you have given it, the full nectar of grace.
commentary: This verse returns to the theme of being "forcefully" taken by God, framing it as an act of predestined love. This divine intervention is the source of all bliss, life, and creation. The poem concludes by identifying the ultimate nature of the divine dancer in the hall of consciousness as Love, creating the bliss of Siva (the auspicious one) within the soul.

tamil: பவனே வெம்பவ நோய் - தனைத் - தீர்க்கும் பரஞ்சுட ரே
சிவனே செம்பொரு ளே - திருச் - சிற்றம் பலநடிப் பாய்
தவநே யம்பெறு வார் - தமைத் - தாங்கி யருள்செய வல்
லவனே தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: pavaṉē vempava nōy - taṉait - tīrkkum parañcuṭa rē civaṉē cemporu ḷē - tiruc - ciṟṟam palanaṭip pāy tavanē yampeṟu vār - tamait - tāṅki yaruḷceya val lavaṉē tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O Being, Supreme Light who cures the fierce disease of existence! O Sivan, Perfect Reality who dances in the sacred Chitrambalam! O powerful one, able to support and bestow grace upon those who attain love through spiritual discipline, you have given me the sweet nectar of grace.
commentary: The cycle of birth, death, and suffering is described here as a "fierce disease," and God is the supreme light that cures it. Vallalar sees the divine dance in the Chitrambalam, the inner hall of consciousness, as the active principle that heals existence. This grace also actively supports those who cultivate love for God through spiritual discipline (tavam).

tamil: தேனாய்த் தீம்பழ மாய்ச் - சுவை - சேர்கரும் பாயமு தம்
தானாய் அன்பரு ளே - இனிக் - கின்ற தனிப்பொரு ளே
வானாய்க் காலன லாய்ப் - புன - லாயதில் வாழ்புவி யாய்
ஆனாய் தந்தனை யே - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: tēṉāyt tīmpaḻa māyc - cuvai - cērkarum pāyamu tam tāṉāy aṉparu ḷē - iṉik - kiṉṟa taṉipporu ḷē vāṉāyk kālaṉa lāyp - puṉa - lāyatil vāḻpuvi yāy āṉāy tantaṉai yē - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O unique Reality that sweetens the hearts of devotees, becoming honey, sweet fruit, flavorful sugarcane, and nectar itself! You who became sky, wind, fire, water, and the earth that resides among them, you have given me the sweet nectar of grace.
commentary: God is experienced in two ways: as the most intimate, personal sweetness within the heart and as the very substance of the physical universe. By becoming everything from the five elements to the taste of honey and nectar, the divine shows that there is no place where it is not. The world is a manifestation of God.

tamil: பொடியேற் கும்புய னே - அருட் - பொன்னம் பலத்தர சே
செடியேற் கன்றளித் தாய் - திருச் - சிற்றம் பலச்சுட ரே
கடியேற் கன்னையெ னுஞ் - சிவ - காமக் கொடையுடை யாய்
அடியேற் கின்றளித் தாய் - அரு - ளாரமு தந்தனை யே.
translit: poṭiyēṟ kumpuya ṉē - aruṭ - poṉṉam palattara cē ceṭiyēṟ kaṉṟaḷit tāy - tiruc - ciṟṟam palaccuṭa rē kaṭiyēṟ kaṉṉaiye ṉuñ - civa - kāmak koṭaiyuṭai yāy aṭiyēṟ kiṉṟaḷit tāy - aru - ḷāramu tantaṉai yē.
translation: O one whose shoulders accept the sacred ash, O King of the graceful Ponnampalam! O Flame of the sacred Chitrambalam! You bestowed grace on me, a sinner, back then. O generous one whose gift is Mother Sivakami, she who accepts the marriage vow! Today you have bestowed upon me, your slave, the sweet nectar of grace.
commentary: Grace is a continuous flow from the past into the present. Vallalar recalls an earlier moment when God saved him, a "sinner," and celebrates the new gift of grace he receives "today." The reference to Ponnampalam (the golden hall) and Mother Sivakami connects his personal experience to the traditional imagery of the divine couple at the cosmic center in Chidambaram.

tamil: கண்ணே கண்மணி யே - கருத் - தேகருத் தின்கனி வே
விண்ணே விண்ணிறை வே - சிவ - மேதனி மெய்ப்பொரு ளே
தண்ணேர் ஒண்மதி யே - எனைத் - தந்த தயாநிதி யே
உண்ணேர் உள்ளொளி யே - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: kaṇṇē kaṇmaṇi yē - karut - tēkarut tiṉkaṉi vē viṇṇē viṇṇiṟai vē - civa - mētaṉi meypporu ḷē taṇṇēr oṇmati yē - eṉait - tanta tayāniti yē uṇṇēr uḷḷoḷi yē - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O my eye, the pupil of my eye! O my thought, the ripe fruit of my thought! O space, the fullness of space! O Sivam, the singular, true substance! O cool, bright moon! O treasure of compassion who gave me to myself! O inner light that is my very being, graciously tell me the truth.
commentary: This prayer addresses God as the very essence of the self: the pupil of the eye, the source of thought, the light within. The remarkable phrase "treasure of compassion who gave me to myself" suggests that our very sense of self is a gift from the divine. By invoking God in these deeply personal ways, Vallalar asks for the ultimate truth that will make this inner connection fully conscious.

tamil: வளியே வெண்ணெருப் பே - குளிர் - மாமதி யேகன லே
வெளியே மெய்ப்பொரு ளே - பொருள் - மேவிய மேனிலை யே
அளியே அற்புத மே - அமு - தேஅறி வேஅர சே
ஒளியே உத்தம னே - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: vaḷiyē veṇṇerup pē - kuḷir - māmati yēkaṉa lē veḷiyē meypporu ḷē - poruḷ - mēviya mēṉilai yē aḷiyē aṟputa mē - amu - tēaṟi vēara cē oḷiyē uttama ṉē - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O air! O white fire! O cool, great moon! O blazing heat! O expanse! O true substance! O supreme state where substance resides! O compassion! O wonder! O ambrosia! O knowledge! O king! O light! O supreme one, graciously tell me the truth.
commentary: Here, the names for God expand to encompass all of existence. God is addressed as the fundamental elements (air, fire), cosmic bodies (moon, sun), and the vastness of space itself. Vallalar then moves to the highest principles, identifying the divine with compassion, wonder, knowledge, and light. This shows a vision where every part of reality, from the material to the purely conscious, is a manifestation of the one God.

tamil: அன்பே என்னர சே - திரு - வம்பலத் தாரமு தே
என்பே உள்ளுரு கக் - கலந் - தென்னு ளிருந்தவ னே
இன்பே என்னறி வே - பர - மேசிவ மேயென வே
உன்பே ரோதுகின் றேன் - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: aṉpē eṉṉara cē - tiru - vampalat tāramu tē eṉpē uḷḷuru kak - kalan - teṉṉu ḷiruntava ṉē iṉpē eṉṉaṟi vē - para - mēciva mēyeṉa vē uṉpē rōtukiṉ ṟēṉ - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O love! O my king! O precious ambrosia of the sacred hall! O one who mingled with me, melting my very bones, and abided within me! "O bliss! O my knowledge! O Supreme One! O Sivam!" Thus I chant your names. Graciously tell me the truth.
commentary: This verse describes the overwhelming experience of divine love. The image of God mingling with the soul until the "very bones melt" signifies the complete dissolution of the ego in the presence of the divine. This is a memory of a deep mystical event. Even after such a union, the devotee continues to seek the ultimate "truth," the final word that makes sense of it all.

tamil: தனையா வென்றழைத் தே - அருட் - சத்தி யளித்தவ னே
அனையா யப்பனு மாய் - எனக் - காரிய னானவ னே
இனையா தென்னையு மேல் - நிலை - ஏற்றுவித் தாண்டவ னே
உனையான் ஏத்துகின் றேன் - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: taṉaiyā veṉṟaḻait tē - aruṭ - catti yaḷittava ṉē aṉaiyā yappaṉu māy - eṉak - kāriya ṉāṉava ṉē iṉaiyā teṉṉaiyu mēl - nilai - ēṟṟuvit tāṇṭava ṉē uṉaiyāṉ ēttukiṉ ṟēṉ - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O one who called me "My son!" and bestowed the power of grace! O one who became my mother, my father, and my master! O one who, without compare, raised me to the highest state and ruled me! I praise you. Graciously tell me the truth.
commentary: The relationship to the divine is cast in the most tender and familiar terms: God is the one who called him "son" and became his mother, father, and teacher. This portrays the spiritual path as a process of being lovingly guided and raised by a divine parent. The way to the "highest state" is presented as an act of God's grace.

tamil: துப்பார் செஞ்சுடரே - அருட் - சோதி சுகக்கட லே
அப்பா என்னர சே - திரு - வம்பலத் தாரமு தே
இப்பா ரிற்பசிக் கே - தந்த - இன்சுவை நல்லுண வே
ஒப்பாய் ஒப்பரி யாய் - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: tuppār ceñcuṭarē - aruṭ - cōti cukakkaṭa lē appā eṉṉara cē - tiru - vampalat tāramu tē ippā riṟpacik kē - tanta - iṉcuvai nalluṇa vē oppāy oppari yāy - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O perfect crimson flame! O Grace-Light! O ocean of bliss! O father! O my king! O precious ambrosia of the sacred hall! O sweet, good food given for the hunger in this world! O you who are the standard of comparison, yet beyond compare, graciously tell me the truth.
commentary: Here Vallalar invokes one of his most central names for God: ArutJothi, the Grace-Light. The divine is a vast ocean of bliss, but also something very practical: the "sweet, good food given for the hunger in this world." This refers both to spiritual nourishment and to the literal food needed to end physical suffering, a core part of Vallalar's teaching. God is described as the ultimate measure of all things, yet is simultaneously beyond any possible comparison.

tamil: என்றே யென்று ளுறுஞ் - சுட - ரேஎனை ஈன்றவ னே
நன்றே நண்பெனக் கே - மிக - நல்கிய நாயக னே
மன்றேர் மாமணி யே - சுக - வாழ்க்கையின் மெய்ப்பொரு ளே
ஒன்றே யென்றுணை யே - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: eṉṟē yeṉṟu ḷuṟuñ - cuṭa - rēeṉai īṉṟava ṉē naṉṟē naṇpeṉak kē - mika - nalkiya nāyaka ṉē maṉṟēr māmaṇi yē - cuka - vāḻkkaiyiṉ meypporu ḷē oṉṟē yeṉṟuṇai yē - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O Light that is ever within me! O You who gave birth to me! O Lord who so graciously granted me good friendship! O great Gem of the splendid Hall! O true substance of a blissful life! O the One! O my companion! Graciously speak the truth to me.
commentary: The focus here shifts from God as an external power to God as an inner presence, "the Light that is ever within me." This divine reality is experienced as a constant companion and a true friend. By calling God "The One," Vallalar points to the ultimate, unified reality that is the very substance of a blissful life.

tamil: திருவே தெள்ளமு தே - அருட் - சித்த சிகாமணி யே
கருவே ரற்றிட வே - களை - கின்றவென் கண்ணுத லே
மருவே மாமல ரே - மலர் - வாழ்கின்ற வானவ னாம்
உருவே என்குரு வே - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: tiruvē teḷḷamu tē - aruṭ - citta cikāmaṇi yē karuvē raṟṟiṭa vē - kaḷai - kiṉṟaveṉ kaṇṇuta lē maruvē māmala rē - malar - vāḻkiṉṟa vāṉava ṉām uruvē eṉkuru vē - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O Sacred Wealth! O clear Ambrosia! O crest-jewel of gracious Siddhas! O my forehead-eyed Lord who weeds out the root cause of my birth! O Fragrance! O great Flower! O Form that is the celestial one dwelling in the flower! O my Guru! Graciously speak the truth to me.
commentary: God is shown as the ultimate goal of spiritual life, the supreme among Siddhas (perfected beings). The image of the "forehead-eyed Lord" (a classic depiction of Siva) is used here to signify the power that destroys the root cause of rebirth. God is also the Guru, or true teacher, who reveals the path to this state.

tamil: தடையா வுந்தவிர்த் தே - எனைத் - தாங்கிக்கொண் டாண்டவ னே
அடையா யன்பிலர் பால் - எனக் - கன்பொடு தந்தபெ ருங்
கொடையாய் குற்றமெ லாங் - குணங் - கொண்டகு ணக்குன்ற மே
உடையாய் உத்தம னே - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: taṭaiyā vuntavirt tē - eṉait - tāṅkikkoṇ ṭāṇṭava ṉē aṭaiyā yaṉpilar pāl - eṉak - kaṉpoṭu tantape ruṅ koṭaiyāy kuṟṟame lāṅ - kuṇaṅ - koṇṭaku ṇakkuṉṟa mē uṭaiyāy uttama ṉē - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O Lord who removed all obstacles, supported me, and took me as Your own! O great Gift given to me with love, You who do not approach those without love! O mountain of virtue who accepts all my faults as virtues! O my Owner! O supreme one! Graciously speak the truth to me.
commentary: The central theme is the astonishing nature of divine love. This grace is a gift that actively removes all obstacles and is so great that it accepts the devotee's flaws as if they were virtues. There is one condition: this grace is available only to those whose hearts are filled with love, making love the essential key to connecting with God.

tamil: பெண்ணாய் ஆணுரு வாய் - எனைப் - பெற்றபெ ருந்தகை யே
அண்ணா என்னர சே - திரு - வம்பலத் தாடுகின் றோய்
எண்ணா நாயடி யேன் - களித் - திட்டவு ணவையெ லாம்
உண்ணா துண்டவ னே - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: peṇṇāy āṇuru vāy - eṉaip - peṟṟape runtakai yē aṇṇā eṉṉara cē - tiru - vampalat tāṭukiṉ ṟōy eṇṇā nāyaṭi yēṉ - kaḷit - tiṭṭavu ṇavaiye lām uṇṇā tuṇṭava ṉē - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O great noble one who, becoming both woman and man, gave birth to me! O Lord! O my King! O You who dance in the sacred Hall! O You who ate without eating all the food that I, Your worthless, dog-like devotee, offered with joy! Graciously speak the truth to me.
commentary: God transcends all limitations, including gender, becoming "both woman and man" to be the devotee's complete parent. The beautiful phrase "ate without eating" describes a mystical communion: God accepted the love and devotion behind the physical offering of food, participating in the devotee's life in a way that is beyond material laws.

tamil: நந்நா லுங்கடந் தே - ஒளிர் - ஞானச பாபதி யே
பொன்னா ருஞ்சபை யாய் - அருட் - பூரண புண்ணிய னே
என்னால் ஆவதொன் றும் - உனக் - கில்லையெ னினுமெந் தாய்
உன்னால் வாழுகின் றேன் - எனக் - குண்மை உரைத்தரு ளே.
translit: nannā luṅkaṭan tē - oḷir - ñāṉaca pāpati yē poṉṉā ruñcapai yāy - aruṭ - pūraṇa puṇṇiya ṉē eṉṉāl āvatoṉ ṟum - uṉak - killaiye ṉiṉumen tāy uṉṉāl vāḻukiṉ ṟēṉ - eṉak - kuṇmai uraittaru ḷē.
translation: O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom who shines beyond the four Vedas! O You who are the Golden Hall! O perfect Holy One, full of grace! O my Mother, though You have nothing to gain from me, I live because of You. Graciously speak the truth to me.
commentary: This verse captures the paradox of devotion: the devotee's entire existence depends on God, yet God, being perfect and complete, gains nothing from the devotee. The relationship is based entirely on one-way grace. God is described as shining beyond the ancient scriptures, found through direct experience in the inner "Hall of Wisdom" (ñāṉacapai).

sections.title: Melting in the Bliss of God

tamil: கருணை ததும்பிப் பொதுநோக்கும் கண்ணிற் கிடைத்த கண்ணேஓர்
கனியில் கனிந்தன் புருவான கருத்தில் கிடைத்த கருத்தேமெய்
அகத்தும் புறத்தும் ஒளிநிறைவித் தமர்ந்த குருவே ஐம்பூத
வருண முதலா அவைகடந்த வரைப்பாய் விளங்கு மணிமன்றில்
வயங்கு சுடரே எல்லாஞ்செய் வல்ல குருவே என்னுளத்தே
தருண நடஞ்செய் அரசேஎன் தாயே என்னைத் தந்தாயே
தனித்த தலைமைப் பதியேஇத் தருணம் வாய்த்த தருணமதே.
translit: karuṇai tatumpip potunōkkum kaṇṇiṟ kiṭaitta kaṇṇēōr kaṉiyil kaṉintaṉ puruvāṉa karuttil kiṭaitta karuttēmey aruḷnaṉ ṉilaiyilatuatuvāy aṟiviṟ kiṭaitta aṟivēeṉ akattum puṟattum oḷiniṟaivit tamarnta kuruvē aimpūta varuṇa mutalā avaikaṭanta varaippāy viḷaṅku maṇimaṉṟil vayaṅku cuṭarē ellāñcey valla kuruvē eṉṉuḷattē taruṇa naṭañcey aracēeṉ tāyē eṉṉait tantāyē taṉitta talaimaip patiyēit taruṇam vāytta taruṇamatē.
translation: O Eye obtained from the eye of universal vision, brimming with compassion! O Idea obtained from the mind that, matured with sweetness, became a form of love! O Knowledge obtained from the knowing that became this and that in the good state of true grace! O Guru who filled my inside and outside with light and took your seat there! O brilliant Flame in the jeweled hall, shining as the boundary beyond the five elements and their qualities! O Guru capable of doing everything! O King performing the timely dance in my heart! O my mother! O you who gave yourself to me! O unique, supreme Lord! This moment is the opportune moment that has arrived.
commentary: God is the very essence of perception, thought, and existence. Vallalar describes this reality as being obtained directly from the divine source: true vision from God's own vision, true knowledge from God's own knowing. This culminates in recognizing God as the inner guru (spiritual teacher) who fills his being with light, making the present moment the perfect time for realization.

tamil: கருவிற் கலந்த துணையேஎன் கனிவில் கலந்த அமுதேஎன்
கண்ணிற் கலந்த ஒளியேஎன் கருத்திற் கலந்த களிப்பேஎன்
உருவிற் கலந்த அழகேஎன் உயிரிற் கலந்த உறவேஎன்
உணர்விற் கலந்த சுகமேஎன் னுடைய ஒருமைப் பெருமானே
தெருவிற் கலந்து விளையாடுஞ் சிறியேன் தனக்கே மெய்ஞ்ஞான
சித்தி அளித்த பெருங்கருணைத் தேவே உலகத் திரளெல்லாம்
மருவிக் கலந்து வாழ்வதற்கு வாய்த்த தருணம் இதுஎன்றே
வாயே பறையாய் அறைகின்றேன் எந்தாய் கருணை வலத்தாலே.
translit: karuviṟ kalanta tuṇaiyēeṉ kaṉivil kalanta amutēeṉ kaṇṇiṟ kalanta oḷiyēeṉ karuttiṟ kalanta kaḷippēeṉ uruviṟ kalanta aḻakēeṉ uyiriṟ kalanta uṟavēeṉ uṇarviṟ kalanta cukamēeṉ ṉuṭaiya orumaip perumāṉē teruviṟ kalantu viḷaiyāṭuñ ciṟiyēṉ taṉakkē meyññāṉa citti aḷitta peruṅkaruṇait tēvē ulakat tiraḷellām maruvik kalantu vāḻvataṟku vāytta taruṇam itueṉṟē vāyē paṟaiyāy aṟaikiṉṟēṉ entāy karuṇai valattālē.
translation: O companion who mingled with me in the womb! O ambrosia that mingled with my ripened love! O light that mingled with my eyes! O delight that mingled with my thoughts! O beauty that mingled with my form! O relation that mingled with my life-breath! O bliss that mingled with my consciousness! O my great Lord of oneness! To lowly me, who wanders and plays in the streets, you are the great, compassionate God who granted the attainment of true wisdom. By the power of your compassion, O my father, I proclaim with my mouth as a drum: "This is the opportune moment for all the multitudes of the world to embrace, merge, and live."
commentary: The union with God is described with breathtaking intimacy, as a companion from the womb and the light within one's own eyes. This personal experience does not stay private. It becomes the start of a public mission to unite the world. Having received true wisdom, the devotee declares himself a town crier, announcing that the time for humanity to live in love has finally arrived.

tamil: தானே தயவால் சிறியேற்குத் தனித்த ஞான அமுதளித்த
தாயே எல்லாச் சுதந்தரமும் தந்த கருணை எந்தாயே
ஊனே விளங்க ஊனமிலா ஒளிபெற் றெல்லா உலகமும்என்
உடைமை யாக்கொண் டருள்நிலைமேல் உற்றேன் உன்றன் அருளாலே
வயங்க உனையுட் கலந்துகொண்டேன் வகுக்குந் தொழிலே முதலைந்தும்
நானே புரிகின் றேன்புரிதல் நானோ நீயோ நான்அறியேன்
நான்நீ என்னும் பேதம்இலா நடஞ்செய் கருணை நாயகனே.
translit: tāṉē tayavāl ciṟiyēṟkut taṉitta ñāṉa amutaḷitta tāyē ellāc cutantaramum tanta karuṇai entāyē ūṉē viḷaṅka ūṉamilā oḷipeṟ ṟellā ulakamumeṉ uṭaimai yākkoṇ ṭaruḷnilaimēl uṟṟēṉ uṉṟaṉ aruḷālē vāṉē matikkac cākāta varaṉāyellām vallacittē vayaṅka uṉaiyuṭ kalantukoṇṭēṉ vakukkun toḻilē mutalaintum nāṉē purikiṉ ṟēṉpurital nāṉō nīyō nāṉaṟiyēṉ nāṉnī eṉṉum pētamilā naṭañcey karuṇai nāyakaṉē.
translation: O mother who, of your own accord and by your grace, gave the unique ambrosia of wisdom to lowly me! O my compassionate father who gave me all freedoms! By your grace, I have attained the state of grace, receiving flawless light that makes my very flesh shine, and taking all worlds as my possession. Becoming one with the boon of immortality, esteemed even by the heavens, I have brightly mingled you within myself as an all-powerful realized being. I myself perform the five great cosmic functions, beginning with creation. Whether it is I who perform them or you, I do not know. O gracious Lord of the dance where the distinction between 'I' and 'you' does not exist!
commentary: At the height of mystical union, the line between the devotee and the divine disappears. Having received a deathless, light-filled body, the devotee has become a cittar (a perfected master) and now partakes in God's cosmic power. The merger is so complete that he claims to perform the five universal functions, like creation, himself, unable to tell whether it is he who acts or God acting through him.

tamil: கலைசார் முடிபு கடந்துணர்வு கடந்து நிறைவாய்க் கரிசிலதாய்க்
கருணை மயமாய் விளங்குசிதா காய நடுவில் இயற்கையுண்மைத்
தலைசார் வடிவில் இன்பநடம் புரியும் பெருமைத் தனிமுதலே
சாகாக் கல்வி பயிற்றிஎன்னுட் சார்ந்து விளங்கும் சற்குருவே
புலைசார் மனத்துச் சிறியேன்றன் குற்றம் அனைத்தும் பொறுத்தருளிப்
பொன்றா வடிவு கொடுத்தெல்லாம் புரிவல் லபந்தந் தருட்சோதி
நிலைசார் இறைமை அளித்தனைநான் பொதுவில் ஞான நீதிஎனும்
நிருத்தம் புரிகின் றேன்புரிதல் நீயோ நானோ நிகழ்த்தாயே.
translit: kalaicār muṭipu kaṭantuṇarvu kaṭantu niṟaivāyk karicilatāyk karuṇai mayamāy viḷaṅkucitā kāya naṭuvil iyaṟkaiyuṇmait talaicār vaṭivil iṉpanaṭam puriyum perumait taṉimutalē cākāk kalvi payiṟṟieṉṉuṭ cārntu viḷaṅkum caṟkuruvē pulaicār maṉattuc ciṟiyēṉṟaṉ kuṟṟam aṉaittum poṟuttaruḷip poṉṟā vaṭivu koṭuttellām purival lapantan taruṭcōti nilaicār iṟaimai aḷittaṉaināṉ potuvil ñāṉa nītieṉum niruttam purikiṉ ṟēṉpurital nīyō nāṉō nikaḻttāyē.
translation: O great, unique Source who performs the dance of bliss in the supreme form of natural Truth, in the center of the space of consciousness that shines, complete, flawless, and full of compassion, beyond the conclusions of the scriptures and beyond knowing! O true Guru who taught me the deathless learning and abides shining within me! Forgiving all the faults of lowly me with my base mind, you gave me an imperishable form, bestowed the power to do all things, and granted me the sovereignty that abides in the state of the Jothi of grace. I am performing the dance called the Justice of Wisdom in the common space. Is it you who performs it or I? Please say!
commentary: God is a dynamic, dancing reality found in the pure space of consciousness (citākāyam), a truth that lies beyond the reach of scriptures or the intellect. This ultimate reality is also the intimate, personal teacher (caṟkuruvē) who grants an imperishable form and a divine mission. For Vallalar, this mission is to perform a "dance of Justice" in the public space (potu), working for the good of all, an act he again attributes to his perfect union with the divine.

tamil: கருத்தில் கருதிக் கொண்டஎலாம் கணத்தில் புரிய எனக்கேமெய்க்
காட்சி ஞானக் கண்கொடுத்த கண்ணே விடயக் கானகத்தே
எருத்தில் திரிந்த கடையேனை எல்லா உலகும் தொழநிலைமேல்
ஏற்றி நீயும் நானும்ஒன்றாய் இருக்கப் புரிந்தாய் எந்தாயே
இருத்திக் கருத்தில் உன்தயவை எண்ணுந் தோறும் அந்தோஎன்
இதயம் உருகித் தளதளஎன் றிளகி இளகித் தண்ராய்
அருத்திப் பெருநீர் ஆற்றொடுசேர்ந் தன்புப் பெருக்கில் கலந்ததுநான்
அதுஎன் றொன்றும் தோற்றாதே அச்சோ அச்சோ அச்சோவே.
translit: karuttil karutik koṇṭaelām kaṇattil puriya eṉakkēmeyk kāṭci ñāṉak kaṇkoṭutta kaṇṇē viṭayak kāṉakattē eruttil tirinta kaṭaiyēṉai ellā ulakum toḻanilaimēl ēṟṟi nīyum nāṉumoṉṟāy irukkap purintāy entāyē iruttik karuttil uṉtayavai eṇṇun tōṟum antōeṉ itayam urukit taḷataḷaeṉ ṟiḷaki iḷakit taṇrāy aruttip perunīr āṟṟoṭucērn taṉpup perukkil kalantatunāṉ atueṉ ṟoṉṟum tōṟṟātē accō accō accōvē.
translation: O Eye that gave me the eye of wisdom of true vision, enabling me to accomplish in an instant all that I conceive in my mind! You raised me, the lowliest one, who wandered like a wild bull in the jungle of sensory objects, to a state where all worlds worship me. You made it so that you and I are one, O my father! Each time I seat your compassion in my mind and ponder it, alas, my heart melts, softens and loosens, becoming cool water. The great river of my longing joins and merges into the great flood of love, and nothing appears as 'I' or 'that'. O wonder! O wonder! O wonder!
commentary: Contemplating God's compassion is a powerful practice that leads directly to the dissolution of the self. Vallalar describes it as a tangible, overwhelming experience. His heart literally melts, his longing becomes a river, and this river merges into the flood of divine love until the very concepts of a separate 'I' and 'that' (God) completely disappear in wonder.

tamil: ஏதும் தெரியா தகங்கரித்திங் கிருந்த சிறியேன் தனைவலிந்தே
எல்லா உலகும் அதிசயிக்க எல்லாம் வல்ல சித்தெனவே
ஓதும் பொருளைக் கொடுத்தென்றும் உலவா இன்பப் பெருநிலையில்
ஓங்கி உறவைத் தனையேஎன் னுடைய ஒருமைப் பெருமானே
ஈதுன் கருணைக் கியல்போநீ என்பால் வைத்த பெருங்கருணை
தாதும் உணர்வும் உயிரும்உள்ளத் தடமும் பிறவாந் தத்துவமும்
தாமே குழைந்து தழைந்தமுத சார மயமா கின்றேனே.
translit: ētum teriyā takaṅkarittiṅ kirunta ciṟiyēṉ taṉaivalintē ellā ulakum aticayikka ellām valla citteṉavē ōtum poruḷaik koṭutteṉṟum ulavā iṉpap perunilaiyil ōṅki uṟavait taṉaiyēeṉ ṉuṭaiya orumaip perumāṉē ītuṉ karuṇaik kiyalpōnī eṉpāl vaitta peruṅkaruṇai innāṭputitē annāḷil ilaiyē itaṉai eṇṇiyanāṉ tātum uṇarvum uyirumuḷḷat taṭamum piṟavān tattuvamum tāmē kuḻaintu taḻaintamuta cāra mayamā kiṉṟēṉē.
translation: Forcefully taking me, this small one who was here full of ego, knowing nothing, you made all the worlds marvel by giving me the reality called the All-Powerful Siddhi. You established me in a great state of unending bliss and exalted me to union with yourself alone, O my great Lord of oneness! Is this the nature of your compassion? Is this great compassion you have for me new today? Did it not exist in days past? As I contemplate this, my constituent elements, consciousness, life, the space of my heart, and all other principles melt on their own and flourish, becoming the very essence of ambrosia.
commentary: Divine grace can forcefully seize and utterly transform even the most ignorant and ego-driven person. Vallalar marvels at how he, once knowing nothing, was given the "All-Powerful Siddhi" (supernatural power) and established in endless bliss. Pondering the sheer magnitude of this unearned gift causes a deep, alchemical change within him, where all the constituent principles (tattvas) of his being melt and become the essence of pure, divine ambrosia.

tamil: ஓவா துண்டு படுத்துறங்கி உணர்ந்து விழித்துக் கதைபேசி
உடம்பு நோவா துளமடக்கா தோகோ நோன்பு கும்பிட்டே
சாவா வரமும் சித்திஎலாம் தழைத்த நிலையும் சன்மார்க்க
சங்க மதிப்பும் பெற்றேன்என் சதுர்தான் பெரிதென் சரித்திரத்தை
ஆவா நினைக்கில் அதிசயம்என் அப்பா அரசே அமுதேஎன்
ஆவிக் கினிய துணையேஎன் அன்பே அறிவே அருட்சோதித்
தேவா இதுநின் செயலேஇச் செயலை நினைக்குந் தொறும்எனது
சிந்தை கனிந்து கனிந்துருகித் தெள்ளா ரமுதம் ஆனதுவே.
translit: ōvā tuṇṭu paṭuttuṟaṅki uṇarntu viḻittuk kataipēci uṭampu nōvā tuḷamaṭakkā tōkō nōṉpu kumpiṭṭē cāvā varamum cittielām taḻaitta nilaiyum caṉmārkka caṅka matippum peṟṟēṉeṉ caturtāṉ periteṉ carittirattai āvā niṉaikkil aticayameṉ appā aracē amutēeṉ āvik kiṉiya tuṇaiyēeṉ aṉpē aṟivē aruṭcōtit tēvā ituniṉ ceyalēic ceyalai niṉaikkun toṟumeṉatu cintai kaṉintu kaṉinturukit teḷḷā ramutam āṉatuvē.
translation: I incessantly ate, lay down and slept, woke up and chattered. Without disciplining my body or controlling my mind, Oho, what penance I observed!, I received the boon of deathlessness, the state where all siddhis flourish, and the esteem of the Sanmarkkam Sangam. My cleverness is great! Ah, when I think of my story, it is a marvel! My Father, King, Ambrosia, dear companion to my soul, my Love, my Wisdom, God of the Great Grace Jothi! This is your deed. Every time I think of this deed, my mind ripens and melts, becoming clear ambrosia.
commentary: Spiritual attainment is purely an act of grace, not a result of one's own efforts. With deep irony, Vallalar lists his ordinary, undisciplined life of eating, sleeping, and talking, calling it his "penance." He received the boon of deathlessness and the esteem of the Sanmarkkam Sangam (his spiritual community) not because of his "cleverness," but only because of God's action. This is a radical statement that grace is an unconditional gift.

tamil: இரவும் பகலும் தூங்கியஎன் தூக்கம் அனைத்தும் இயல்யோகத்
திசைந்த பலனாய் விளைந்ததுநான் இரண்டு பொழுதும் உண்டஎலாம்
பரவும் அமுத உணவாயிற் றந்தோ பலர்பால் பகல்இரவும்
படித்த சமயச் சாத்திரமும் பலரால் செய்த தோத்திரமும்
விரவிக் களித்து நாத்தடிக்க விளம்பி விரித்த பாட்டெல்லாம்
வேதா கமத்தின் முடிமீது விளங்கும் திருப்பாட் டாயினவே
கரவொன் றறியாப் பெருங்கருணைக் கடவுள் இதுநின் தயவிதனைக்
கருதும் தொறும்என் கருத்தலர்ந்து சுகமே மயமாக் கண்டதுவே.
translit: iravum pakalum tūṅkiyaeṉ tūkkam aṉaittum iyalyōkat ticainta palaṉāy viḷaintatunāṉ iraṇṭu poḻutum uṇṭaelām paravum amuta uṇavāyiṟ ṟantō palarpāl pakaliravum paṭitta camayac cāttiramum palarāl ceyta tōttiramum viravik kaḷittu nāttaṭikka viḷampi viritta pāṭṭellām vētā kamattiṉ muṭimītu viḷaṅkum tiruppāṭ ṭāyiṉavē karavoṉ ṟaṟiyāp peruṅkaruṇaik kaṭavuḷ ituniṉ tayavitaṉaik karutum toṟumeṉ karuttalarntu cukamē mayamāk kaṇṭatuvē.
translation: All the sleep I slept, night and day, yielded the fruit of natural yoga. The food I ate twice a day became, alas, ambrosial sustenance. The religious scriptures I studied day and night with many people, the hymns composed by many, and all the songs I mixed together, delighted in, and expansively sang until my tongue grew thick have become sacred hymns that shine upon the crown of the Vedas and Agamas. O God of great compassion who knows no concealment, this is your grace. Every time I contemplate it, my mind blossoms and becomes wholly bliss.
commentary: Through grace, every part of ordinary life becomes sacred and spiritually potent. Vallalar's sleep was transformed into yoga (spiritual union), his daily food became divine ambrosia, and even his casual songs became as holy as the highest scriptures, the Vedas and Agamas. On this path grace can make every ordinary activity holy.

tamil: ஊற்றை உடம்பில் இருட்டறைவாய் உறங்கி விழித்துக் கதைபேசி
உண்டிங் குடுத்துக் கருத்திழந்தே உதவா எருதின் ஊர்திரிந்து
நேற்றை வரையும் வீண்போது போக்கி இருந்தேன் நெறிஅறியேன்
ஆற்றை அடைந்தோர் எல்லோரும் அச்சோ என்றே அதிசயிப்ப
அமுதுண் டழியாத் திருஉருவம் அடைந்தேன் பெரிய அருட்சோதிப்
பேற்றை உரிமைப் பேறாகப் பெற்றேன் பெரிய பெருமான்நின்
பெருமை இதுவேல் இதன் இயலை யாரே துணிந்து பேசுவரே.
translit: ūṟṟai uṭampil iruṭṭaṟaivāy uṟaṅki viḻittuk kataipēci uṇṭiṅ kuṭuttuk karuttiḻantē utavā erutiṉ ūrtirintu nēṟṟai varaiyum vīṇpōtu pōkki iruntēṉ neṟiaṟiyēṉ nērēiṟṟaip pakalantō neṭuṅkā lamummeyt tavayōka āṟṟai aṭaintōr ellōrum accō eṉṟē aticayippa amutuṇ ṭaḻiyāt tiruuruvam aṭaintēṉ periya aruṭcōtip pēṟṟai urimaip pēṟākap peṟṟēṉ periya perumāṉniṉ perumai ituvēl itaṉ iyalai yārē tuṇintu pēcuvarē.
translation: In this oozing body, this dark room, I slept and woke, chattered, ate, dressed, lost my purpose, and wandered the town like a useless bull. Until yesterday, I was wasting my time, knowing no path. Yet this very day, alas, making all those who long ago attained the way of true penance and yoga exclaim "Achō!" in amazement, I have attained a deathless, sacred form by consuming ambrosia. I have received the great attainment of the Great Grace Jothi as my own rightful inheritance. Great Lord, if this is your glory, who can dare to speak of its nature?
commentary: The transformation from a lost, aimless person to an immortal being can happen in an instant as a gift of grace. Vallalar contrasts his past self, a "useless bull" wasting time in a decaying body, with his present reality. "This very day," he has received a deathless, sacred form, an attainment so direct and stunning that it amazes even those who have practiced yoga and penance for a lifetime.

tamil: புரைசேர் வினையும் கொடுமாயைப் புணர்ப்பும் இருளும் மறைப்பினொடு
புகலும் பிறவாம் தடைகளெலாம் போக்கி ஞானப் பொருள்விளங்கும்
வரைசேர்த் தருளிச் சித்தியெலாம் வழங்கிச் சாகா வரங்கொடுத்து
வலிந்தென் உளத்தில் அமர்ந்துயிரில் கலந்து மகிழ்ந்து வாழ்கின்றாய்
பரைசேர் வெளியில் பதியாய்அப் பால்மேல் வெளியில் விளங்குசித்த
பதியே சிறியேன் பாடலுக்குப் பரிசு விரைந்தே பாலித்த
அரைசே அமுதம் எனக்களித்த அம்மே உண்மை அறிவளித்த
அப்பா பெரிய அருட்சோதி அப்பா வாழி நின்அருளே.
translit: puraicēr viṉaiyum koṭumāyaip puṇarppum iruḷum maṟaippiṉoṭu pukalum piṟavām taṭaikaḷelām pōkki ñāṉap poruḷviḷaṅkum varaicērt taruḷic cittiyelām vaḻaṅkic cākā varaṅkoṭuttu valinteṉ uḷattil amarntuyiril kalantu makiḻntu vāḻkiṉṟāy paraicēr veḷiyil patiyāyap pālmēl veḷiyil viḷaṅkucitta patiyē ciṟiyēṉ pāṭalukkup paricu viraintē pālitta araicē amutam eṉakkaḷitta ammē uṇmai aṟivaḷitta appā periya aruṭcōti appā vāḻi niṉaruḷē.
translation: You have removed all obstacles: flawed karma, the grip of cruel maya, darkness, concealment, and all other impediments spoken of. You graced me by leading me to the mountain where the substance of wisdom shines, granted all siddhis, and gave the boon of deathlessness. Forcefully, you have settled in my mind, mingled with my soul, and live there rejoicing. O Master who is Lord in the space where Parai (the supreme feminine power) resides! O Lord of Siddhas who shines in the space beyond even that! O King who swiftly bestowed a reward for my humble song! O Mother who gave me ambrosia! O Father who gave me true wisdom! O Father, Great Grace Jothi! Long may your grace flourish!
commentary: The ultimate spiritual state is one where God, having removed all inner obstacles, lives intimately within the soul. Vallalar lists the barriers God cleared away: vinai (the binding effects of past actions), māyā (the illusion of separateness), and spiritual darkness. Now, God lives inside him as a complete presence: Mother, Father, King, and the supreme Lord. All of this is the work of grace alone.
NOTES
Note 318

translit: nilaiyiṉ - pi. irā. patippu.
translation: nilaiyiṉ — reading of the P. Irā. edition.
Note 319

tamil: வானாய் - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு, பி. இரா., ச. மு. க.
translit: vāṉāy - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu, pi. irā., ca. mu. ka.
translation: vāṉāy — reading of the first edition, of Po. Su., of P. Irā., and of S. Mu. Ka.

translit: nāṉceyta puṇṇiyam eṉṉuraik kēṉpotu naṇṇiyatōr vāṉceyta māmaṇi eṉkaiyil peṟṟunal vāḻvaṭaintēṉ ūṉceyta tēkam oḷivaṭi vākaniṉ ṟōṅkukiṉṟēṉ tēṉceyta teḷḷamu tuṇṭēṉkaṇ ṭēṉmeyt tirunilaiyē.
translation: What can I say of the merit I have earned? I received in my hand the great heavenly gem that reached the Common Space and attained a good life. My fleshly body now stands and soars as a form of light. I have drunk the clear, honeyed ambrosia; I have seen the true, sacred state.
commentary: He marvels at the good fortune that has led to his transformation from a physical body into a form of pure light. This is a change in consciousness and a literal, physical transmutation into a deathless state, brought about by consuming a divine ambrosia. He has now seen and experienced the ultimate reality directly.

translit: nāṉceyta puṇṇiyam eṉṉuraip pēṉpotu naṇṇiyatōr vāṉceyta meypporuḷ eṉkaiyiṟ peṟṟumey vāḻvaṭaintēṉ kōṉceyta paṟpala kōṭiaṇ ṭaṅkaḷum kūṟavaṟṟil tāṉceyta piṇṭap pakutiyum nāṉceyat tantaṉaṉē.
translation: What can I say of the merit I have earned? I received in my hand the true, heavenly substance that reached the Common Space and have attained the true life. The King made many billions of universes and the realms of individual bodies within them; He has given them to me to create.
commentary: His union with God is so complete that he has been given the divine power of creation itself. He now has the ability to create universes and all the beings within them, just as God does. His very being has changed, where he now participates in the cosmic functions of the divine.

translit: tirunilai peṟṟaṉaṉ ampalat tāṉaruḷ teḷḷamutuṇ ṭurunilai peṟṟaṉaṉ oṉṟē civameṉa ōṅkukiṉṟa perunilai peṟṟaṉaṉ cuttacaṉ mārkkam piṭittuniṉṟēṉ irunilai munnilai ellā nilaiyum eṉakkuḷavē.
translation: I have attained the sacred state. After drinking the clear ambrosia of grace from the Lord of the Ambalam, I have achieved a stable form. I have reached the great state that soars, proclaiming, "Siva is One." I stand firm, holding to Suddha Sanmarkkam. The dual state, the triple state, all states are now within me.
commentary: Having drunk the ambrosia of grace from the Lord of the Ambalam (the inner space of consciousness), he has attained a permanent, transformed body. He stands firm in his path, Suddha Sanmarkkam (the path of pure truth), and realizes the ultimate unity of God. By reaching this highest state, he finds that all other states of being, dual and triple, are now contained within him.

translit: ettaṉai nāṉkuṟṟam ceytum poṟuttaṉai eṉṉainiṉpāl vaittaṉai uḷḷam makiḻntaṉai nāṉcoṉṉa vārttaikaḷiṅ kattaṉai yumcam matittaruḷ ceytaṉai ampalattē muttaṉai yāyniṉak keṉmēl irukkiṉṟa mōkameṉṉē.
translation: However many faults I committed, you forgave them. You kept me with you and rejoiced in your heart. You consented to and graced every word I spoke here. O Perfect One in the Ambalam, what is this desire you have for me!
commentary: He marvels at the nature of God's love, which seems completely out of proportion to his own worthiness. Despite his many past faults, God has forgiven him and actively drawn him close, taking joy in his presence and honoring his words. He is left wondering at the intensity of God's desire and affection for him.

translit: iṉiyē iṟaiyum cakippaṟi yēṉeṉak kiṉpanalkum kaṉiyēeṉ taṉiru kaṇṇēmuk kaṇkoṇṭa kaṟpakamē taṉiyēeṉ aṉpuṭait tāyēciṟ ṟampalam cārtantaiyē muṉiyēl aruḷka aruḷkameyñ ñāṉam muḻutaiyumē.
translation: From now on, I cannot bear it for even a moment. O sweet fruit that gives me bliss, O my two eyes, O three-eyed, wish-fulfilling tree, O my uniquely loving mother, O father who belongs to the Chitrambalam! Do not be displeased; grace me, grace me with true wisdom in its entirety.
commentary: Having come so close to union, Vallalar finds any remaining separation unbearable. He addresses God with a stream of deeply personal and affectionate names, calling him a sweet fruit, his own eyes, a wish-fulfilling tree (karpakam), and both mother and father. His plea is urgent and emotional: now that he has tasted this bliss, he begs God to grant the fullness of wisdom immediately.

translit: puttiyañ cēlcaṟṟum eṉneñca mēciṟ potuttantaiyār nittiyañ cērnta neṟiyil celuttiṉar nīiṉinaṉ muttiyum ñāṉameyc cittiyum peṟṟu muyaṅkiṭuvāy cattiyam cattiyam cattiyam cattiyam cattiyamē.
translation: O my mind, do not fear at all. The Father of the universal space of consciousness has guided us onto the eternal path. Now you will attain good liberation and the perfection of true wisdom, and you will embrace them. This is the truth, the truth, the truth, the truth, indeed the truth.
commentary: Vallalar speaks to his own mind, telling it to cast away all fear. He affirms that God, the Father of the universal space of consciousness (cit-potu), has placed him on the irreversible path to eternity. Liberation and perfection are now a certainty, and he stresses it by repeating "truth" five times.

tamil: ஆடிய பாதம் அறியச்சொன் னேன்என தாண்ட வனே.
translit: kūṭiya nāḷitu tāṉtaru ṇameṉaik kūṭiuḷḷē vāṭiya vāṭṭamel lāntavirt tēcuka vāḻvaḷippāy nīṭiya tēliṉic caṟṟumpo ṟēṉuyir nīttiṭuvēṉ āṭiya pātam aṟiyaccoṉ ṉēṉeṉa tāṇṭa vaṉē.
translation: This is the day of union, this is the opportune moment. Unite with me, remove all the inner withering I have suffered, and grant me a life of bliss. If You delay, I cannot bear it even for a moment longer; I will give up my life. I have said this for Your dancing feet to know, O You who rule me.
commentary: The plea for union reaches its most urgent pitch. Vallalar declares that the perfect moment is now, begging God to merge with him and heal the "inner withering" caused by past separation. He makes a dramatic vow: if union is delayed any longer, he cannot live. It is a statement of absolute dependence, spoken directly to God's dancing feet to convey the depth of his loving desperation.

translit: ākkiya nāḷitu tāṉtaru ṇamaruḷā ramutam tēkkimey iṉpuṟac ceytaruḷ ceytaruḷ ceytaruḷnī nīkkiṉai yēliṉic caṟṟumpo ṟēṉuyir nīttiṭuvēṉ tūkkiya pātam aṟiyaccoṉ ṉēṉaruṭ cōtiyaṉē.
translation: This is the day You have ordained, this is the moment. Grant it, grant it, grant it: make my body fill with the precious nectar of grace and experience bliss. If You refuse, I cannot bear it even for a moment longer; I will give up my life. I have said this for Your raised foot to know, O Splendor of Grace.
commentary: Echoing the previous verse's intensity, Vallalar now frames the moment as one ordained by God Himself. The plea "grant it" is repeated three times, emphasizing his desire for a tangible experience: for his very body to be filled with the ambrosia of grace. He repeats his desperate vow that he will die without this union, directing his plea to the "raised foot" of the cosmic dancer and to God as the Splendor of Grace.

sections.title: Having Nothing to Give in Return

tamil: இழைஎலாம் விளங்கும் அம்மை இடங்கொள்நின் கருணை என்னும்
மழைஎலாம் பொழிந்தென் உள்ள மயக்கெலாம் தவிர்த்து நான்செய்
பிழைஎலாம் பொறுத்த உன்றன் பெருமைக்கென் புரிவேன் அந்தோ
உழைஎலாம் இலங்குஞ் சோதி உயர்மணி மன்று ளானே.
translit: iḻaielām viḷaṅkum ammai iṭaṅkoḷniṉ karuṇai eṉṉum maḻaielām poḻinteṉ uḷḷa mayakkelām tavirttu nāṉcey piḻaielām poṟutta uṉṟaṉ perumaikkeṉ purivēṉ antō uḻaielām ilaṅkuñ cōti uyarmaṇi maṉṟu ḷāṉē.
translation: O One in the supreme jeweled hall, who are the light shining everywhere! You, who have the Mother, radiant with every jewel, on Your left, showered down all the rain of Your compassion, dispelled all the confusion in my mind, and forgave every mistake I made. Alas, what can I do in return for Your greatness?
commentary: Struck by the magnitude of God's forgiveness, Vallalar feels a sense of helpless gratitude. He contrasts his own many mistakes with the endless "rain" of divine compassion and realizes there is nothing a human can offer that would be an adequate response to such generosity. The mention of the Mother on God's left signifies that this compassion is the active, nurturing power of the Divine.

tamil: போதுதான் வீணே போக்கிப் புலையனேன் புரிந்த பொல்லாத்
தீதுதான் பொறுத்த உன்றன் திருவருட் பெருமைக் கந்தோ
ஏதுதான் புரிவேன் ஓகோ என்என்று புகழ்வேன் ஞான
மாதுதான் இடங்கொண் டோங்க வயங்குமா மன்று ளானே.
translit: pōtutāṉ vīṇē pōkkip pulaiyaṉēṉ purinta pollāt tītutāṉ poṟutta uṉṟaṉ tiruvaruṭ perumaik kantō ētutāṉ purivēṉ ōkō eṉeṉṟu pukaḻvēṉ ñāṉa mātutāṉ iṭaṅkoṇ ṭōṅka vayaṅkumā maṉṟu ḷāṉē.
translation: O One in the great radiant hall, where the Mother of Wisdom thrives in her place! I, a base, lowly one, wasted my time, yet You forgave the wicked evils I committed. For the greatness of Your sacred grace, alas, what can I do? Oh, how shall I praise You?
commentary: This verse deepens the feeling of unworthiness in the face of grace. By calling himself a "base, lowly one" who wasted his life, Vallalar emphasizes the vast distance between human failing and divine mercy. The ultimate conclusion is that since no action can repay God, the only possible response is to simply try to praise Him, however inadequately.

tamil: சிற்றறி வுடையன் ஆகித் தினந்தொறும் திரிந்து நான்செய்
குற்றமும் குணமாக் கொண்ட குணப்பெருங் குன்றே என்னைப்
பெற்றதா யுடனுற் றோங்கும் பெருமநின் பெருமை தன்னைக்
கற்றறி வில்லேன் எந்தக் கணக்கறிந் துரைப்பேன் அந்தோ.
translit: ciṟṟaṟi vuṭaiyaṉ ākit tiṉantoṟum tirintu nāṉcey kuṟṟamum kuṇamāk koṇṭa kuṇapperuṅ kuṉṟē eṉṉaip peṟṟatā yuṭaṉuṟ ṟōṅkum perumaniṉ perumai taṉṉaik kaṟṟaṟi villēṉ entak kaṇakkaṟin turaippēṉ antō.
translation: O great mountain of virtue, who took as virtues the faults I committed, wandering daily with my petty knowledge! O Great One, who thrives with the Mother who bore me! I have no learning or wisdom; alas, by what measure can I know and describe Your greatness?
commentary: God's grace is so powerful that it does more than forgive faults, it transforms them into virtues. Faced with this alchemical power, Vallalar feels his own human knowledge is completely useless. No amount of learning can measure or comprehend a greatness that redefines the very nature of one's past errors.

tamil: மையரி நெடுங்க ணார்தம் வாழ்க்கையின் மயங்கி இங்கே
பொய்யறி வுடையேன் செய்த புன்மைகள் பொறுத்தாட் கொண்டாய்
ஐயறி வுடையார் போற்றும் அம்பலத் தரசே நின்சீர்
மெய்யறி வறியேன் எந்த விளைவறிந் துரைப்பேன் அந்தோ.
translit: maiyari neṭuṅka ṇārtam vāḻkkaiyiṉ mayaṅki iṅkē poyyaṟi vuṭaiyēṉ ceyta puṉmaikaḷ poṟuttāṭ koṇṭāy aiyaṟi vuṭaiyār pōṟṟum ampalat taracē niṉcīr meyyaṟi vaṟiyēṉ enta viḷaivaṟin turaippēṉ antō.
translation: O King of the Ambalam, praised by those who have mastered their five senses! Here I was, deluded by a life centered on women with long, kohl-lined eyes. You forgave the vile deeds that I, a man of false knowledge, committed, and You took me as Your own. I do not have the true knowledge of Your glory; alas, by what understanding could I speak of it?
commentary: A past life spent lost in worldly distractions and "false knowledge" is forgiven and redeemed by God. Vallalar contrasts his own state with those who have mastered their senses and can properly praise God in the Ambalam (the sacred hall of consciousness). He concludes that true knowledge of God's glory is a gift of grace.

tamil: பேயினும் பெரியேன் செய்த பிழைகளுக் கெல்லை இல்லை
ஆயினும் பொறுத்தாட் கொண்டாய் அம்பலத் தரசே என்றன்
தாயினும் இனிய உன்றன் தண்ணருட் பெருமை தன்னை
நாயினுங் கடையேன் எந்த நலமறிந் துரைப்பேன் அந்தோ.
translit: pēyiṉum periyēṉ ceyta piḻaikaḷuk kellai illai āyiṉum poṟuttāṭ koṇṭāy ampalat taracē eṉṟaṉ tāyiṉum iṉiya uṉṟaṉ taṇṇaruṭ perumai taṉṉai nāyiṉuṅ kaṭaiyēṉ enta nalamaṟin turaippēṉ antō.
translation: O King of the Ambalam! I am worse than a demon, and there is no limit to the wrongs I have done. Even so, You forgave me and took me as Your own. I am lower than a dog; alas, what virtue do I know that would allow me to describe the greatness of Your soothing grace, which is sweeter than my own mother?
commentary: Vallalar uses extreme language, calling himself "worse than a demon" and "lower than a dog," to emphasize a core spiritual point. It shows that divine grace is completely unconditional and does not depend on one's own merit. God's compassion is so vast that it embraces even the one who feels most unworthy, offering a comfort sweeter and deeper than a mother's love.

tamil: துரும்பினில் சிறியேன் வஞ்சம் சூழ்ந்தநெஞ் சகத்தேன் செய்த
அரும்பொருள் என்ன வேதம் ஆகமம் வழுத்து கின்ற
கரும்பினில் இனியாய் உன்றன் கருணைஎன் னென்பேன் அந்தோ.
translit: turumpiṉil ciṟiyēṉ vañcam cūḻntaneñ cakattēṉ ceyta perumpiḻai aṉaittum antō peruṅkuṇa mākakkoṇṭāy arumporuḷ eṉṉa vētam ākamam vaḻuttu kiṉṟa karumpiṉil iṉiyāy uṉṟaṉ karuṇaieṉ ṉeṉpēṉ antō.
translation: I am smaller than a speck of dust, with a heart steeped in deceit. Alas, you took all the great wrongs I committed and considered them great virtues. O you who are sweeter than sugarcane, whom the Vedas and Agamas praise as the rarest substance, alas, what can I say of your grace?
commentary: The speaker feels his inner self is deceitful and insignificant, yet he has experienced a divine alchemy where his greatest wrongs were transformed into virtues by grace. While the highest scriptures, the Vedas (ancient hymns) and Agamas (manuals of philosophy and worship), describe God as the ultimate reality, Vallalar's personal experience is one of intimate sweetness, making the grace he has received feel both supreme and deeply personal.

tamil: வரைகடந் தடியேன் செய்த வன்பிழை பொறுத்தாட் கொண்டாய்
திரைகடந் தண்ட பிண்டத் திசைஎலாம் கடந்தே அப்பால்
கரைகடந் தோங்கும் உன்றன் கருணையங் கடற்சீர் உள்ளம்
உரைகடந் ததுஎன் றால்யான் உணர்வதென் உரைப்ப தென்னே.
translit: varaikaṭan taṭiyēṉ ceyta vaṉpiḻai poṟuttāṭ koṇṭāy tiraikaṭan taṇṭa piṇṭat ticaielām kaṭantē appāl karaikaṭan tōṅkum uṉṟaṉ karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭaṟcīr uḷḷam uraikaṭan tatueṉ ṟālyāṉ uṇarvateṉ uraippa teṉṉē.
translation: You forgave the terrible wrongs I, your devotee, committed, which went beyond all bounds, and you took me as your own. Your glorious ocean of grace crosses beyond the seas, beyond the macrocosms and microcosms, beyond all directions, and swells, shoreless, even further. If it transcends thought and speech, what can I possibly perceive? What is there for me to say?
commentary: Here, the experience of grace expands from a personal feeling to a cosmic reality. Vallalar describes God's compassion as a "shoreless ocean" that is not contained by the physical universe or any human concept of space. Because this grace is infinite, it is fundamentally beyond the grasp of the mind or the power of words. Faced with something that transcends thought and speech, the only possible response is humbled silence.

tamil: நனவினும் பிழையே செய்தேன் நாயினும் கடையேன் அந்தோ
கனவினும் பிழையே செய்தேன் கருணைமா நிதியே நீதான்
நினைவினும் குறியா தாண்டாய் நின்னருட் பெருமை தன்னை
வினைவினும் சொல்வார் காணேன் என்செய்வேன் வினைய னேனே.
translit: naṉaviṉum piḻaiyē ceytēṉ nāyiṉum kaṭaiyēṉ antō kaṉaviṉum piḻaiyē ceytēṉ karuṇaimā nitiyē nītāṉ niṉaiviṉum kuṟiyā tāṇṭāy niṉṉaruṭ perumai taṉṉai viṉaiviṉum colvār kāṇēṉ eṉceyvēṉ viṉaiya ṉēṉē.
translation: I, who am lower than a dog, committed wrongs even while awake; alas, I committed wrongs even in my dreams. O great treasure of grace, you took me as your own without even giving them a thought. I find no one who can even ask about, let alone describe, the greatness of your grace. What shall I, a man of karma, do?
commentary: The speaker recognizes that his flaws are so deep they persist even in his dreams, yet God's acceptance was immediate and absolute, given "without even giving them a thought." The final question reveals a deep tension. As a "man of karma" (a person living in the world of action and consequence), he is helpless before a gift that operates outside that system. Grace has canceled a debt he could never repay, leaving him with nothing to "do" but stand in awe.

tamil: வன்செயல் பொறுத்தாட் கொண்ட வள்ளலே அடிய னேன்றன்
முன்செயல் அவைக ளோடு முடுகுபின் செயல்கள் எல்லாம்
என்செயல் ஆகக் காணேன் எனைக்கலந் தொன்றாய் நின்றோய்
நின்செயல் ஆகக் கண்டேன் கண்டபின் நிகழ்த்தல் என்னே.
translit: vaṉceyal poṟuttāṭ koṇṭa vaḷḷalē aṭiya ṉēṉṟaṉ muṉceyal avaika ḷōṭu muṭukupiṉ ceyalkaḷ ellām eṉceyal ākak kāṇēṉ eṉaikkalan toṉṟāy niṉṟōy niṉceyal ākak kaṇṭēṉ kaṇṭapiṉ nikaḻttal eṉṉē.
translation: O benefactor who forgave my harsh deeds and took me as your own! O you who have mingled with me and stand as one! I no longer see my past deeds, or all the subsequent deeds that follow, as my actions. I have seen them as your actions. Having seen this, what is there left to say?
commentary: Through union with the divine, the very idea of personal action disappears. Vallalar realizes that his past, present, and future deeds are God acting through him. This dissolves the burden of karma and the ego, replacing the sense of being an individual agent with the experience of being a vehicle for divine will.

tamil: இருமையும் ஒருமை தன்னில் ஈந்தனை எந்தாய் உன்றன்
பெருமைஎன் னென்று நான்தான் பேசுவேன் பேதம் இன்றி
உரிமையால் யானும் நீயும் ஒன்றெனக் கலந்து கொண்ட
ஒருமையை நினைக்கின் றேன்என் உள்ளகந் தழைக்கின் றேனே.
translit: irumaiyum orumai taṉṉil īntaṉai entāy uṉṟaṉ perumaieṉ ṉeṉṟu nāṉtāṉ pēcuvēṉ pētam iṉṟi urimaiyāl yāṉum nīyum oṉṟeṉak kalantu koṇṭa orumaiyai niṉaikkiṉ ṟēṉeṉ uḷḷakan taḻaikkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: You granted both this world and the next within oneness itself. My father, what can I possibly say of your greatness? I am thinking of the oneness we share, how you and I, by right, have blended into one without any distinction. As I think of it, my inner self flourishes.
commentary: God's greatest gift is the experience of oneness, where the separation between the individual and the divine dissolves. Vallalar describes it as a present reality, a union so complete that he and God have blended without distinction. Contemplating this shared identity brings his inner being to life.

tamil: உரத்தவான் அகத்தே உரத்தவா ஞான ஒளியினால் ஓங்கும்ஓர் சித்தி
புரத்தவா பெரியோர் புரத்தவா குற்றம் பொறுத்தடி யேன்தனக் களித்த
வரத்தவா உண்மை வரத்தவா ஆக மங்களும் மறைகளும் காணாத்
தரத்தவா அறிவா தரத்தவா பொதுவில் தனித்தவா இனித்தவாழ் வருளே.
translit: urattavāṉ akattē urattavā ñāṉa oḷiyiṉāl ōṅkumōr citti purattavā periyōr purattavā kuṟṟam poṟuttaṭi yēṉtaṉak kaḷitta varattavā uṇmai varattavā āka maṅkaḷum maṟaikaḷum kāṇāt tarattavā aṟivā tarattavā potuvil taṉittavā iṉittavāḻ varuḷē.
translation: O mighty One within the mighty sky! O One of Siddhipuram, which soars in the light of wisdom! O protector of the great ones! O boon, granted to me, your servant, after forgiving my faults! O true boon! O One of a nature that the Agamas and Vedas cannot see! O foundation of knowledge! O One who stands alone in the Common Space! Grant me a sweet life!
commentary: Vallalar appeals to a God whom even the Vedas and Agamas cannot see, yet who dwells in Siddhipuram, the city of attainment that soars in the light of wisdom. Siddhipuram is the name Vallalar gave to Vadalur (Uttara Gnana Siddhipuram). This God protects the great, forgives the faults of His servant, and stands alone in the universal Common Space (Potu). From Him Vallalar asks one thing: a sweet life.

tamil: முன்னவா திபர்க்கு முன்னவா வேத முடிமுடி மொழிகின்ற முதல்வா
பின்னவா திபர்க்குப் பின்னவா எவர்க்கும் பெரியவா பெரியவர் மதிக்கும்
சின்னவா சிறந்த சின்னவா ஞான சிதம்பர வெளியிலே நடிக்கும்
மன்னவா அமுதம் அன்னவா எல்லாம் வல்லவா நல்லவாழ் வருளே.
translit: muṉṉavā tiparkku muṉṉavā vēta muṭimuṭi moḻikiṉṟa mutalvā piṉṉavā tiparkkup piṉṉavā evarkkum periyavā periyavar matikkum ciṉṉavā ciṟanta ciṉṉavā ñāṉa citampara veḷiyilē naṭikkum maṉṉavā amutam aṉṉavā ellām vallavā nallavāḻ varuḷē.
translation: O You who precede the foremost! O Primal One spoken of at the very crown of the Vedas' crown! O You who come after the last! O great One to all! O subtle One esteemed by the great! O excellent subtle One! O King who dances in the space of wisdom-Chidambaram! O One like nectar! O all-powerful One! Grant me a good life!
commentary: God is timeless, existing before the first being and after the last. While vast and primary, this divine reality is also described as a subtle principle, appreciated only by the truly great. The image of the king dancing in "wisdom-Chidambaram" portrays the universe's creative energy as a joyful dance happening within the space of pure consciousness.

tamil: விடையவா தனைதீர் விடையவா சுத்த வித்தைமுன் சிவவரை கடந்த
நடையவா ஞான நடையவா இன்ப நடம்புரிந் துயிர்க்கெலாம் உதவும்
கொடையவா ஓவாக் கொடையவா எனையாட் கொண்டெனுள் அமர்ந்தரு ளியஎன்
உடையவா எல்லாம் உடையவா உணர்ந்தோர்க் குரியவா பெரியவாழ் வருளே.
translit: viṭaiyavā taṉaitīr viṭaiyavā cutta vittaimuṉ civavarai kaṭanta naṭaiyavā ñāṉa naṭaiyavā iṉpa naṭampurin tuyirkkelām utavum koṭaiyavā ōvāk koṭaiyavā eṉaiyāṭ koṇṭeṉuḷ amarntaru ḷiyaeṉ uṭaiyavā ellām uṭaiyavā uṇarntōrk kuriyavā periyavāḻ varuḷē.
translation: O Rider of the bull! O answer that resolves affliction! O One whose gait has passed beyond the mountain of Siva, which lies before pure vittai! O One of a wise gait! O generous One who helps all lives by performing the dance of bliss! O ever-generous One! O my Owner, who graciously took me as your slave and settled within me! O Owner of all! O One who belongs to those who have realized! Grant me a great life!
commentary: God is the great benefactor, whose very nature is a dance of bliss that helps all living things. Vallalar uses traditional imagery, like Siva as the rider of the bull, but emphasizes that God's reality is beyond even high spiritual knowledge (vittai). The verse culminates in a statement of personal experience: God has taken him over completely, becoming his owner and settling within him.

tamil: வலத்தவா நாத வலத்தவா சோதி மலையவா மனமுதல் கடந்த
புலத்தவா எனது புலத்தவா தவிர்த்துப் பூரண ஞானநோக் களித்த
நலத்தவா வரையா நலத்தவா மறைகள் நாடியும் காண்பதற் கரிதாம்
பலத்தவா திருஅம் பலத்தவா எல்லாம் படைத்தவா படைத்தவாழ் வருளே.
translit: valattavā nāta valattavā cōti malaiyavā maṉamutal kaṭanta pulattavā eṉatu pulattavā tavirttup pūraṇa ñāṉanōk kaḷitta nalattavā varaiyā nalattavā maṟaikaḷ nāṭiyum kāṇpataṟ karitām palattavā tiruam palattavā ellām paṭaittavā paṭaittavāḻ varuḷē.
translation: O mighty One! O One with the power of nātham! O mountain of Jothi! O One whose domain is beyond the mind and senses! O benevolent One who, removing that which was in my senses, granted me the gaze of perfect wisdom! O One of boundless benevolence! O Power that is difficult for the Vedas to find even when they search! O One of the sacred Ambalam! O Creator of all! Grant me the life that is Your creation!
commentary: God is the ultimate power, the source of primordial sound (nātham), and a mountain of Jothi (divine light). This reality cannot be reached through the mind or senses. Instead, Vallalar says God grants a "gaze of perfect wisdom," a direct, intuitive perception of truth. This vision reveals the divine as the creator of all, present in the sacred Ambalam (hall) of consciousness.

tamil: உணர்ந்தவர் உளத்தை உகந்தவா இயற்கை உண்மையே உருவதாய் இன்பம்
புணர்ந்திட எனைத்தான் புணர்ந்தவா ஞானப் பொதுவிலே பொதுநடம் புரிந்தெண்
குணந்திகழ்ந் தோங்கும் குணத்தவா குணமும் குறிகளும் கோலமும் குலமும்
தணந்தசன் மார்க்கத் தனிநிலை நிறுத்தும் தக்கவா மிக்கவாழ் வருளே.
translit: uṇarntavar uḷattai ukantavā iyaṟkai uṇmaiyē uruvatāy iṉpam puṇarntiṭa eṉaittāṉ puṇarntavā ñāṉap potuvilē potunaṭam purinteṇ kuṇantikaḻn tōṅkum kuṇattavā kuṇamum kuṟikaḷum kōlamum kulamum taṇantacaṉ mārkkat taṉinilai niṟuttum takkavā mikkavāḻ varuḷē.
translation: O One who delights in the hearts of those who have realized! O One who, taking natural truth itself as Your form, united with me so that I might unite with bliss! O One of such character that Your eight qualities shine forth and soar as You perform the universal dance in the Common Space of wisdom! O worthy One who establishes the unique state of the Sanmarkkam, which has shed qualities, signs, forms, and caste! Grant me an abundant life!
commentary: God is the very essence of natural truth, who unites with the soul to grant bliss. This union reveals the state of the Sanmarkkam, the True Path. Vallalar defines this path by what it has cast off: qualities, sectarian signs, religious forms, and caste. It is a universal path founded on realized truth alone.

tamil: தத்துவங் கடந்த தத்துவா ஞான சமரச சுத்தசன் மார்க்கச்
சத்துவ நெறியில் நடத்திஎன் தனைமேல் தனிநிலை நிறுத்திய தலைவா
சித்துவந் தாடும் சித்திமா புரத்தில் திகழ்ந்தவா திகழ்ந்தென துளத்தே
ஒத்துநின் றோங்கும் உடையவா கருணை உளத்தவா வளத்தவாழ்வருளே.
translit: tattuvaṅ kaṭanta tattuvā ñāṉa camaraca cuttacaṉ mārkkac cattuva neṟiyil naṭattieṉ taṉaimēl taṉinilai niṟuttiya talaivā cittuvan tāṭum cittimā purattil tikaḻntavā tikaḻnteṉa tuḷattē ottuniṉ ṟōṅkum uṭaiyavā karuṇai uḷattavā vaḷattavāḻvaruḷē.
translation: O Leader, who led me on the Sāttvic path of wisdom's Sama Rasa Suddha Sanmarkkam, which transcends the tattvas, and who established me in the supreme, unique state! O one who shines in Cittimā Puram, where siddhus come to dance! O Master, you who shine and, in harmony, rise high within my heart! O one with a heart of compassion, grant the grace of a flourishing life!
commentary: The spiritual path is a guided process of moving beyond all intellectual frameworks for reality, known as the tattvas. Vallalar calls his path the Sama Rasa Suddha Sanmarkkam, a way of pure (suddha) and balanced (sama rasa) wisdom. Its goal is to reach a "supreme, unique state" where the Divine, a master full of compassion, is experienced as a living presence rising within one's own heart.

tamil: மதம்புகல் முடிபு கடந்தமெய்ஞ் ஞான மன்றிலே வயங்கொள்நா டகஞ்செய்
பதம்புகல் அடியேற் கருட்பெருஞ் சோதிப் பரிசுதந் திடுதும்என் றுளத்தே
நிதம்புகல் கருணை நெறியவா இன்ப நிலையவா நித்தநிற் குணமாம்
சிதம்புகல் வேத சிரத்தவா இனித்த தேனவா ஞானவாழ் வருளே.
translit: matampukal muṭipu kaṭantameyñ ñāṉa maṉṟilē vayaṅkoḷnā ṭakañcey patampukal aṭiyēṟ karuṭperuñ cōtip paricutan tiṭutumeṉ ṟuḷattē nitampukal karuṇai neṟiyavā iṉpa nilaiyavā nittaniṟ kuṇamām citampukal vēta cirattavā iṉitta tēṉavā ñāṉavāḻ varuḷē.
translation: O one on the path of compassion, who constantly declares within my heart, "To this devotee who seeks refuge at the feet that perform the brilliant dance in the Hall of True Wisdom, which transcends the conclusions proclaimed by religions, I will grant the gift of the Vast Grace-Light!" O state of bliss! O One at the crown of the Vedas, which proclaim You as eternal Consciousness beyond all attributes! O sweet honey! Grant the grace of a life of wisdom!
commentary: Divine revelation is an intimate, personal promise whispered directly into the heart. Vallalar hears God assuring him of a great gift, the ArutPerunJothi or Vast Grace-Light. This happens not in a conventional temple, but in a "Hall of True Wisdom" that transcends the doctrines of all religions, revealing a reality that is eternal and cannot be defined by any limited human quality.

tamil: மூவிரு முடிபும் கடந்ததோர் இயற்கை முடிபிலே முடிந்தென துடம்பும்
ஆவியும் தனது மயம்பெறக் கிடைத்த அருட்பெருஞ் சோதிஅம் பலவா
ஓவுரு முதலா உரைக்கும்மெய் உருவும் உணர்ச்சியும் ஒளிபெறு செயலும்
மேவிநின் றவர்க்குள் மேவிய உணர்வுள் மேயவா தூயவாழ் வருளே.
translit: mūviru muṭipum kaṭantatōr iyaṟkai muṭipilē muṭinteṉa tuṭampum āviyum taṉatu mayampeṟak kiṭaitta aruṭperuñ cōtiam palavā ōvuru mutalā uraikkummey uruvum uṇarcciyum oḷipeṟu ceyalum mēviniṉ ṟavarkkuḷ mēviya uṇarvuḷ mēyavā tūyavāḻ varuḷē.
translation: O Vast Grace-Light of the Ambalam! You who were found so that my body and soul could be perfected into your own nature within the ultimate state of Nature, which transcends the six philosophical conclusions! O one who abides within the consciousness of those who have attained the true form spoken of, beginning with the primal form of 'Ōm', as well as the feeling and the luminous action! Grant the grace of a pure life!
commentary: The spiritual goal is to transform the body completely, along with the soul, into the very nature of God. This perfection happens in a final state that is beyond all competing philosophical systems. For those who attain it, the Divine is a living reality, experienced as a primal sound like 'Ōm', a deep feeling, and a new capacity for luminous, clear action.

tamil: பங்கமோர் அணுவும் பற்றிடா அறிவால் பற்றிய பெற்றியார் உளத்தே
தங்குமோர் சோதித்தனி ப்பெருங் கருணைத் தரந்திகழ் சத்தியத் தலைவா
துங்கமுற் றழியா நிலைதரும் இயற்கைத் தொன்மையாம் சுத்தசன் மார்க்கச்
சங்கநின் றேத்தும் சத்திய ஞான சபையவா அபயவாழ் வருளே.
translit: paṅkamōr aṇuvum paṟṟiṭā aṟivāl paṟṟiya peṟṟiyār uḷattē taṅkumōr cōtittaṉi pperuṅ karuṇait tarantikaḻ cattiyat talaivā tuṅkamuṟ ṟaḻiyā nilaitarum iyaṟkait toṉmaiyām cuttacaṉ mārkkac caṅkaniṉ ṟēttum cattiya ñāṉa capaiyavā apayavāḻ varuḷē.
translation: O Leader of Truth, whose quality of singular, great compassion shines! O Light that dwells in the hearts of the accomplished, who have grasped you with an intelligence untouched by even an atom of flaw! O one of the Satya Gnana Sabhai, praised by the assembly of the Suddha Sanmarkkam, which is the ancient nature that bestows a glorious, indestructible state! Grant the grace of a life of fearlessness!
commentary: God's most essential quality is a singular, immense compassion. This truth can be perceived by an intelligence that is perfectly pure and unclouded. This path of realization, the Suddha Sanmarkkam, leads to the Satya Gnana Sabhai (Hall of True Wisdom), where one attains an indestructible state. The final result of this attainment is abhaya, a life of complete fearlessness.

tamil: இனித்தசெங் கரும்பில் எடுத்ததீஞ் சாற்றின் இளம்பதப் பாகொடு தேனும்
கனித்ததீங் கனியின் இரதமும் கலந்து கருத்தெலாம் களித்திட உண்ட
மனித்தரும் அமுத உணவுகொண் டருந்தும் வானநாட் டவர்களும் வியக்கத்
தனித்தமெய்ஞ் ஞானஅமுதெனக் களித்த தனியவா இனியவாழ் வருளே.
translit: iṉittaceṅ karumpil eṭuttatīñ cāṟṟiṉ iḷampatap pākoṭu tēṉum kaṉittatīṅ kaṉiyiṉ iratamum kalantu karuttelām kaḷittiṭa uṇṭa maṉittarum amuta uṇavukoṇ ṭaruntum vāṉanāṭ ṭavarkaḷum viyakkat taṉittameyñ ñāṉaamuteṉak kaḷitta taṉiyavā iṉiyavāḻ varuḷē.
translation: O unique One, you gave me the singular ambrosia of true wisdom, so that both humans who have eaten the young syrup of sweet red sugarcane mixed with honey and the juice of ripe sweet fruits, delighting their whole mind, and the dwellers of heaven who feed on ambrosia, marvel at it! Grant the grace of a sweet life!
commentary: The taste of true wisdom is described as a divine nectar (amrita) far surpassing any earthly sweetness. Vallalar uses a cascade of sweet imagery, sugarcane juice, honey, ripe fruit, to suggest an experience of joy so complete that even the gods, with their own heavenly ambrosia, would be astonished by it. The experience is more than intellectual; it is a deep, all-consuming delight for the soul.

translit: karuṇāniti yēaṭi yēṉiru kaṇṇuḷāṉē teruḷnāṭumeṉ cintaiyuḷ mēviya tēvatēvē poruḷnāṭiya ciṟṟampa lattoḷir puṇṇiyāmeyt taruṇāitu tāṉtaru ṇameṉait tāṅkikkoḷḷē.
translation: O Treasury of Grace who is within my two eyes! O God of gods who dwells in my mind seeking clarity! O Virtuous One, shining in Chitrambalam, the reality I sought! O True Grace! This is the moment, embrace me.
commentary: God is intimately present within our own being, specifically in our eyes, mind, and consciousness. Vallalar refers to this inner space of awareness as Chitrambalam (the little hall). The verse is a cry of recognition and longing, a realization that the divine he sought is right here, right now, prompting an urgent plea for union.

translit: kūkāeṉak kūṭi eṭātik koṭiyaṉēṟkē cākāvaram tanta tayānitit tantaiyēniṉ mākātalaṉ ākiṉaṉ nāṉiṅku vāḻkiṉṟēṉeṉ yōkāti cayaṅkaḷ uraikka ulappuṟātē.
translation: So that no one will ever gather and lift my body away with wailing cries, you gave me, a cruel sinner, the boon of deathlessness, O Father, Treasury of Compassion! I have become your great lover and live here now. The wonders of my yoga can never be told to the end.
commentary: The highest grace, the boon of deathlessness, is given to one who calls himself a cruel sinner. Vallalar pictures the funeral that will never happen: no mourners will gather, wailing, to lift his body away. This act of pure compassion turns his relationship with the divine into one of passionate love, and the wonders of this union can never be told to the end.

translit: entāyuṉaik kaṇṭu kaḷittaṉaṉ īṇṭippōtē cintānala mumpala mumpeṟṟut tēkkukiṉṟēṉ antāmarai yāṉneṭu mālavaṉ ātivāṉōr vantāreṉai vāḻttukiṉ ṟāriṅku vāḻkaeṉṟē.
translation: O my Father! I have seen you and rejoiced, here and now. Receiving mental well-being and strength, I am filled to overflowing. He on the lovely lotus, tall Mal, and the other primordial gods have come here to bless me, saying, "Live well!"
commentary: Direct experience of God is a present reality that fills the devotee with joy and great mental strength. In a remarkable reversal of the usual order of worship, Vallalar states that his union with the divine is so complete that even the great gods like Brahma (He on the lovely lotus) and Vishnu (tall Mal) come to pay homage to him. This shows that the soul in direct communion with the supreme source attains a status beyond that of the celestial deities themselves.

translit: vāḻvēṉaru ḷāramu tuṇṭiṅku vāḻkiṉṟēṉnāṉ ēḻvētaṉai yumtavirn tēṉuṉai yēaṭaintēṉ cūḻvēṉtiruc ciṟṟampalattait tutittu vāḻttit tāḻvēṉala tiyārkkum iṉiccaṟṟum tāḻntiṭēṉē.
translation: I will live well! I am living here now, having consumed the full nectar of grace. I have escaped all suffering; I have attained you alone. I will circumambulate the sacred Chitrambalam, praising and acclaiming it. I will bow to it, but from now on, I will not bow even slightly to anyone else.
commentary: Attaining God brings an end to all suffering and fills the soul with the "nectar of grace." This experience creates an absolute and exclusive devotion. Vallalar vows to honor only the ultimate reality, symbolized as the sacred space of Chitrambalam (the Hall of Consciousness), and declares he will no longer bow to any other power, human or divine. This is a statement of complete spiritual freedom.

translit: tāḻāteṉai āṭkoṇ ṭaruḷiya tantaiyēniṉ kēḻārmaṇi ampalam pōṟṟak kiṭaittuḷēṉnāṉ ēḻānilai mēlnilai ēṟi ilaṅkukiṉṟēṉ ūḻālvanta tuṉpaṅkaḷ yāvum oḻintataṉṟē.
translation: O Father who graciously made me your own without delay! I have been granted the blessing of praising your Hall of radiant gems. I have ascended to the state beyond the seventh state, and I shine. All the sufferings that came from fate have vanished.
commentary: Grace acts instantly, lifting the soul to a level of consciousness that surpasses even the highest known spiritual states. The "state beyond the seventh state" refers to an experience beyond the traditional peaks of yoga, a state of pure divine light. In this state, the accumulated effects of past actions, which we often call fate (ūḻ), are completely dissolved.

translit: kōṭāmaṟai ākamam ātiya kūṟukiṉṟa cūṭāmaṇi yēmaṇi yuḷoḷir cōtiyēeṉ pāṭāṉavai tīrttaruḷ īntuniṉ pātameṉṉum vāṭāmalar eṉmuṭi cūṭṭiṉai vāḻinīyē.
translation: O crest-jewel proclaimed by the flawless Vedas, Agamas, and other scriptures! O Jothi that shines from within the gem! You have resolved my sufferings, bestowed grace, and placed the unfading flower of your foot upon my head. Long may you live!
commentary: God is the ultimate truth that all scriptures, like the Vedas and Agamas, attempt to describe. But this truth is more than a concept; it is a Jothi, a living light that shines from within. The "unfading flower of your foot" placed on the head is a classic image of a master's ultimate blessing, signifying the direct transmission of grace and the resolution of all worldly troubles.

translit: ellāñceya vallava ṉēeṉai īṉṟatāyiṉ nallāyciva ñāṉikaḷ peṟṟameyñ ñāṉavāḻvē kollāneṟi kāṭṭieṉ taṉṉaik kuṟippiṟkoṇṭeṉ pollāmai poṟuttaṉai vāḻkaniṉ poṟpatamē.
translation: O you who are capable of doing everything! O good one, better than the mother who bore me! O true life of wisdom attained by the sages of divine knowledge! You showed me the path of non-killing, singled me out, and forgave my wickedness. May your golden feet flourish!
commentary: The divine is portrayed here as the ultimate power, a love greater than a mother's, and the very essence of wisdom. This supreme being personally revealed the "path of non-killing" (kollā neṟi), the core ethical principle of compassion for all life. This verse connects the highest mystical experience with the most basic moral duty, showing that true spirituality is inseparable from non-violence.

translit: paramāṉa citampara ñāṉa capāpatiyē varamāṉa ellām eṉakkīntanal vaḷḷalēeṉ taramāṉatu caṟṟum kuṟittilai cāminiṉṉai uramāṉa:uḷ aṉparkaḷ ēcuvar uṇmaiītē.
translation: O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom in supreme Chidambaram! O generous patron who gave me every boon! You paid no mind at all to my standing. O Master, your staunch inner devotees will scold you. This is the truth.
commentary: God's generosity is so absolute that it overlooks all of a person's flaws and qualifications. Vallalar uses a playful, intimate tone here: he says that other, more "proper" devotees might scold God for giving such sublime grace to someone as unworthy as himself. This highlights the unconditional nature of the divine response he experiences.

translit: tāyēeṉait tanta tayānitit tantaiyēin nāyēṉpiḻai yāvaiyum koṇṭaṉai naṉmaieṉṟē kāyēkaṉi yākak karutum karuttaṉēniṉ cēyēeṉa eṉpeyar eṅkum ciṟantataṉṟē.
translation: O Mother! O Father, a treasure of compassion, who gave me life! You have taken all the faults of this dog that I am as if they were virtues. O you whose wisdom sees the unripe fruit as ripe! Is it not true that my name has become glorious everywhere as "your child"?
commentary: Divine compassion does more than forgive faults; it sees through them to a person's true, perfected nature. Vallalar uses the metaphor of seeing an unripe fruit as already ripe to describe how God perceives his potential, not his current state of imperfection. This divine perception is what transforms him and makes him known as a child of God.

translit: poyyēuraik kiṉṟaeṉ collum puṉaintukoṇṭāy meyyētiru ampalat tāṭalcey vittakaṉē eyyēṉiṉi vemmalak kūṭṭil irunteṉuḷḷam naiyēṉcutta nalluṭam peytiṉaṉ nāṉilattē.
translation: You accepted even my words, which speak only falsehood, and adorned yourself with them, O Master of Truth who performs the dance in the sacred hall! No longer will I grow weary in the harsh cage of impurity; no longer will my heart languish. I have attained a pure, good body here on this earth.
commentary: Here, devotion leads to a tangible result: the transformation of the physical body. God accepts even his imperfect praise, and in return, Vallalar is freed from the "cage of impurity," the ordinary mortal body. The attainment of a "pure, good body" on earth is a key experience in his path, signaling a victory over physical decay and suffering.

tamil: அருளே பழுத்த சிவதருவில் அளிந்த பழந்தந் தடியேனைத்
தெருளே சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
மருளே முதலாம் தடைஎல்லாம் தீர்ந்தேன் நின்பால் வளர்கின்றேன்
பொருளே இனிநின் தனைப்பாடி ஆடும் வண்ணம் புகலுகவே.
translit: aruḷē paḻutta civataruvil aḷinta paḻantan taṭiyēṉait teruḷē ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē maruḷē mutalām taṭaiellām tīrntēṉ niṉpāl vaḷarkiṉṟēṉ poruḷē iṉiniṉ taṉaippāṭi āṭum vaṇṇam pukalukavē.
translation: O embodiment of clarity! Lord of Chitrambalam! From the Siva-tree ripened with grace, you gave me the luscious fruit and made me, your servant, into your cherished child. I am free from all obstacles, starting with delusion. I am growing in you. O supreme Reality! Now, please tell me the way to sing and dance in praise of you.
commentary: The experience of grace is like being given a sweet, ripe fruit from the divine tree itself. This gift transforms the devotee from a mere servant into a beloved child, clearing away all confusion. The poem opens with this overwhelming sense of gratitude, which then naturally leads to a question: now that I have received everything, how can I serve you? The desire to sing and dance is a desire to express this boundless joy and love.

tamil: ஒருவா தடியேன் எண்ணியவா றெல்லாம் அருளி உளங்களித்தே
திருவார் சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
பெருவாழ் வடைந்தேன் பெருங்களிப்பால் பெருமான் நின்பால் வளர்கின்றேன்
உருவார் உலகில் உனைப்பாடி ஆடும் வண்ணம் உரைத்தருளே.
translit: oruvā taṭiyēṉ eṇṇiyavā ṟellām aruḷi uḷaṅkaḷittē tiruvār ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē peruvāḻ vaṭaintēṉ peruṅkaḷippāl perumāṉ niṉpāl vaḷarkiṉṟēṉ uruvār ulakil uṉaippāṭi āṭum vaṇṇam uraittaruḷē.
translation: O Lord of sacred Chitrambalam! Unfailingly granting all that I, your servant, wished for, you made my heart rejoice and made me your cherished child. I have attained the great life. O great Lord, with immense joy, I am growing in you. Please graciously tell me how to sing and dance of you in this world of forms.
commentary: This verse reinforces the previous one, emphasizing that God has fulfilled every one of the speaker's wishes, leading to a state of complete joy. This "great life" is the intimate relationship with the divine. The question of how to serve God through song and dance arises from a place of total contentment.

tamil: அவமே புரிந்தேன் தனைமீட்டுன் அருளா ரமுதம் மிகப்புகட்டிச்
சிவமே சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
பவமே தொலைத்தேன் பெருங்களிப்பால் பதியே நின்பால் வளர்கின்றேன்
நவமே அடியேன் நினைப்பாடி ஆடும் வண்ணம் நவிலுகவே.
translit: avamē purintēṉ taṉaimīṭṭuṉ aruḷā ramutam mikappukaṭṭic civamē ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē pavamē tolaittēṉ peruṅkaḷippāl patiyē niṉpāl vaḷarkiṉṟēṉ navamē aṭiyēṉ niṉaippāṭi āṭum vaṇṇam navilukavē.
translation: O embodiment of Siva! Lord of Chitrambalam! You rescued me, one who acted in futility, and fed me abundantly with your grace-filled nectar, making me your cherished child. I have destroyed the cycle of birth. O Master, with great joy, I am growing in you. O ever-new One! Please tell me how I, your servant, may sing and dance of you.
commentary: The speaker reflects on being saved from a life of futility (avam) and instead being nourished by the nectar of grace. This divine intervention has destroyed pavam (the karmic cycle of birth and death). Having achieved this ultimate liberation, he now calls on the ever-new One to tell him how to sing and dance in praise.

tamil: பல்வா தனையும் தவிர்த்தெனக்கே பரமா னந்த அமுதளித்துச்
செல்வா சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
வல்வா தனைசெய் மனச்செருக்கை மாற்றி நின்பால் வளர்கின்றேன்
நல்வாழ் வளித்தாய் நினைப்பாடி ஆடும் வண்ணம் நவிலுகவே.
translit: palvā taṉaiyum tavirtteṉakkē paramā ṉanta amutaḷittuc celvā ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē valvā taṉaicey maṉaccerukkai māṟṟi niṉpāl vaḷarkiṉṟēṉ nalvāḻ vaḷittāy niṉaippāṭi āṭum vaṇṇam navilukavē.
translation: O prosperous Lord of Chitrambalam! Removing my many latent tendencies and giving me the nectar of supreme bliss, you have made me your cherished child. Having transformed the mind's arrogance born of strong tendencies, I am growing in you. You have given me a good life. Please tell me how to sing and dance in praise of you.
commentary: The source of inner turmoil, the "latent tendencies" (vātanai) and the arrogant mind they create, have been removed by grace. In their place, he has been given supreme bliss and a "good life." It is an inner state of peace and purity. From this state of mental clarity, the natural response is to ask how to best channel his gratitude into worship.

tamil: ஓவா இன்ப மயமாகி ஓங்கும் அமுதம் உதவிஎனைத்
தேவா சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
பூவார் மணம்போல் சுகந்தருமெய்ப் பொருளே நின்பால் வளர்கின்றேன்
நாவால் அடியேன் நினைப்பாடி ஆடும் வண்ணம் நவிலுகவே.
translit: ōvā iṉpa mayamāki ōṅkum amutam utavieṉait tēvā ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē pūvār maṇampōl cukantarumeyp poruḷē niṉpāl vaḷarkiṉṟēṉ nāvāl aṭiyēṉ niṉaippāṭi āṭum vaṇṇam navilukavē.
translation: O radiant Lord of Chitrambalam! You became the form of unending bliss, bestowing the sublime nectar upon me and making me your cherished child. O true Reality who gives happiness like the fragrance of a flower, I am growing in you. Please tell me how I, your servant, may sing and dance of you with my tongue.
commentary: The divine is experienced as a constant, tangible bliss. Vallalar compares the happiness that flows from this "true Reality" (meyp-poruḷ) to the natural fragrance of a flower, something real and pervasive. In this state, he feels himself flourishing inside the divine presence itself, and asks how his very body and tongue can join in expressing this joy.

tamil: இளிவே தவிர்த்துச் சிறியேன்தன் எண்ணம் முழுதும் அளித்தருளித்
தெளிவே சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
ஒளிவேய் வடிவு பெற்றோங்கி உடையாய் உன்பால் வளர்கின்றேன்
தளிவேய் நினது புகழ்பாடி ஆடும் வண்ணம் சாற்றுகவே.
translit: iḷivē tavirttuc ciṟiyēṉtaṉ eṇṇam muḻutum aḷittaruḷit teḷivē ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē oḷivēy vaṭivu peṟṟōṅki uṭaiyāy uṉpāl vaḷarkiṉṟēṉ taḷivēy niṉatu pukaḻpāṭi āṭum vaṇṇam cāṟṟukavē.
translation: Eliminating all disgrace and granting this lowly one's every wish, O Clarity, O Lord of the Small Hall, You made me Your treasured child. I have gained a form veiled in light and am flourishing; O Master, I am growing up with You. O sheltering coolness, tell me how I am to sing Your fame and dance.
commentary: Grace has wiped away all past disgrace and fulfilled the poet's deepest wishes, making him God's child. As a result he has received a new "form veiled in light," suggesting a body transformed by spiritual realization. Now flourishing within God, he asks how to praise the one who provides this final coolness and shelter.

tamil: மறப்பே தவிர்த்திங் கெனைஎன்றும் மாளா நிலையில் தனியமர்த்திச்
சிறப்பே சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
பிறப்பே தவிர்ந்தேன் பெருங்களிப்பால் பெருமான் நின்பால் வளர்கின்றேன்
திறப்பேர் உலகில் உனைப்பாடி ஆடும் வண்ணம் செப்புகவே.
translit: maṟappē tavirttiṅ keṉaieṉṟum māḷā nilaiyil taṉiyamarttic ciṟappē ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē piṟappē tavirntēṉ peruṅkaḷippāl perumāṉ niṉpāl vaḷarkiṉṟēṉ tiṟappēr ulakil uṉaippāṭi āṭum vaṇṇam ceppukavē.
translation: Eliminating forgetfulness, You seated me here alone in an undying state; O Excellence, O Lord of the Small Hall, You made me Your treasured child. I have escaped birth; with great joy, O Great Lord, I am growing up with You. In this vast world, tell me how I am to sing of You and dance.
commentary: Grace has ended the state of "forgetfulness" (maṟappu), the soul's ordinary condition of being distracted from God.
