By being established in constant remembrance, the poet has entered an "undying state" and escaped the cycle of birth. This is the source of his great joy and the reason he now seeks to celebrate the divine through music and movement.

tamil: ஊனே புகுந்தென் உளங்கனிவித் துயிரில் கலந்தே ஒன்றாகித்
தேனே சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
நானே அழியா வாழ்வுடையேன் நானே நின்பால் வளர்கின்றேன்
தானேர் உலகில் உனைப்பாடி ஆடும் வண்ணம் சாற்றுகவே.
translit: ūṉē pukunteṉ uḷaṅkaṉivit tuyiril kalantē oṉṟākit tēṉē ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē nāṉē aḻiyā vāḻvuṭaiyēṉ nāṉē niṉpāl vaḷarkiṉṟēṉ tāṉēr ulakil uṉaippāṭi āṭum vaṇṇam cāṟṟukavē.
translation: Entering my very flesh, making my mind ripen, mingling in my life-breath and becoming one, O Honey, O Lord of the Small Hall, You have made me Your treasured child. I myself now possess immortal life; I myself am growing up with You. In this peerless world, tell me how I am to sing of You and dance.
commentary: The divine union described here is total, permeating every level of being. God enters the poet's very flesh, ripens his mind, and mingles with his life-breath until they are inseparable. As a result of this complete integration, Vallalar declares that he himself now possesses immortal life. The 'I' that speaks is one that is already growing and living within God's own being.

tamil: ஆரா அமுதம் அளித்தருளி அன்பால் இன்ப நிலைக்கேற்றிச்
சீரார் சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
ஏரார் இன்ப அனுபவங்கள் எல்லாம் பொருந்தி இருக்கின்றேன்
தீரா உலகில் அடிச்சிறியேன் செய்யும் பணியைத் தெரித்தருளே.
translit: ārā amutam aḷittaruḷi aṉpāl iṉpa nilaikkēṟṟic cīrār ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē ērār iṉpa aṉupavaṅkaḷ ellām porunti irukkiṉṟēṉ tīrā ulakil aṭicciṟiyēṉ ceyyum paṇiyait terittaruḷē.
translation: Graciously giving me insatiable nectar and, through love, raising me to a state of bliss, O glorious Lord of the Small Hall, You have made me Your treasured child. I am now filled with all beautiful, blissful experiences. In this unending world, please reveal the service this lowly servant is to perform.
commentary: The experience of divine grace is portrayed as receiving an "insatiable nectar" (amutham), a spiritual nourishment that leads to a permanent state of bliss. Having been filled with this joy, the devotee’s focus shifts from personal salvation to active purpose. The question is no longer just about expressing joy, but about understanding the specific service or work that God wants them to perform.

tamil: மெய்வைப் பழியா நிலைக்கேற்றி விளங்கும் அமுதம் மிகஅளித்தே
தெய்வப் பதியே சிவமேநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
ஐவைப் பறிந்தேன் துரிசெல்லாம் அறுத்தேன் நின்பால் வளர்கின்றேன்
பொய்வைப் படையேன் இவ்வுலகில் புரியும் பணியைப் புகன்றருளே.
translit: meyvaip paḻiyā nilaikkēṟṟi viḷaṅkum amutam mikaaḷittē teyvap patiyē civamēniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē aivaip paṟintēṉ turicellām aṟuttēṉ niṉpāl vaḷarkiṉṟēṉ poyvaip paṭaiyēṉ ivvulakil puriyum paṇiyaip pukaṉṟaruḷē.
translation: Raising me to the undying state of a true treasure and giving me abundant, radiant nectar, O Divine Master, O Sivam, You have made me Your treasured child. I have uprooted the five, I have severed all afflictions, and I am growing up with You. As one who will not possess false treasures, graciously declare the service I am to perform in this world.
commentary: Achieving the "undying state" involves a radical inner purification. "Uprooting the five" refers to freeing oneself from the powerful grip of the five senses, which normally bind a person to the world and its afflictions. By renouncing the "false treasures" of worldly attachment, the devotee is ready for a life of true purpose and asks God to reveal the service they are meant to perform.

tamil: நாரா யணனு நான்முகனு நயந்து வியக்க நிற்கின்றேன்
ஏரார் உலகில் இனிஅடியேன் செய்யும் பணியை இயம்புகவே.
translit: nārā yaṇaṉu nāṉmukaṉu nayantu viyakka niṟkiṉṟēṉ ērār ulakil iṉiaṭiyēṉ ceyyum paṇiyai iyampukavē.
translation: [The first half of this verse is lost in Vallalar's manuscript.] … I stand while Narayanan and Nanmugan look on in wonder. In this beautiful world, tell me now the service your servant is to do.
commentary: The devotee's transformation is so great that even the great gods of the Hindu tradition, Vishnu (Narayanan) and the creator-god Brahma (Nanmugan), look upon this state with awe. This highlights the supreme nature of the grace Vallalar describes, which elevates a human soul to a position admired by the celestials themselves. Despite this exalted status, the focus remains humbly fixed on discovering the right service to perform. Verses 11 and 12 survive in Vallalar's own hand; of verse 11 only its second half remains.

tamil: பிறந்தேற் கென்றும் இறவாது பிறவா தோங்கும் பெருமைதந்து
சிறந்தே சிற்றம் பலவாநின் செல்வப் பிள்ளை ஆக்கினையே
திறந்தேர் முனிவர் தேவரெலாந் தேர்ந்து நயப்ப நிற்கின்றேன்
அறந்தேர் உலகில் இனிஅடியேன் செய்யும் பணியை அருளகவே.2
translit: piṟantēṟ keṉṟum iṟavātu piṟavā tōṅkum perumaitantu ciṟantē ciṟṟam palavāniṉ celvap piḷḷai ākkiṉaiyē tiṟantēr muṉivar tēvarelān tērntu nayappa niṟkiṉṟēṉ aṟantēr ulakil iṉiaṭiyēṉ ceyyum paṇiyai aruḷakavē.2
translation: You granted me, who was born, the soaring greatness of never dying and never being born again, and made me your own treasured child, O Lord of Chitrambalam. I stand while discerning sages and all the celestials look on and admire me. In this world that seeks righteousness, please graciously state the service your servant should now perform.
commentary: The final goal is achieved: complete freedom from the cycle of birth and death. This grace comes from the Lord of Chitrambalam, the "small hall of consciousness," locating the divine presence within the self. Even as sages and gods look on in admiration, the final thought is of duty to the world. The devotee's repeated question, "what is my service?", frames the entire purpose of this divine transformation as a preparation for helping a world that seeks righteousness.
NOTES
Note 278

tamil: 4067, 4068. இவ்வொன்றரைப் பாட்டும் பெருமான் கையெழுத்தில் இருப்பதாகக்கூறி ஆ. பா. இவற்றைத் தனிப்பாசுரப் பகுதியில் சேர்த்துள்ளார். பொருளமைதிகருதி இவை ஈண்டு இப்பதிகத்துடன் சேர்க்கப்பெற்றன.
translit: 4067, 4068. ivvoṉṟaraip pāṭṭum perumāṉ kaiyeḻuttil iruppatākakkūṟi ā. pā. ivaṟṟait taṉippācurap pakutiyil cērttuḷḷār. poruḷamaitikaruti ivai īṇṭu ippatikattuṭaṉ cērkkappeṟṟaṉa.
translation: 4067, 4068. Stating that these one and a half verses are found in the Swami's own hand, Ā. Pā. placed them in the section of separate verses (Taṉippācuram). On grounds of coherence of sense, they are here included with this patikam.

tamil: இப்பார் முதல்எண் மூர்த்தமதாய் இலங்கும் கருணை எங்கோவே
தப்பா யினதீர்த் தென்னையும்முன் தடுத்தாட் கொண்ட தயாநிதியே
எப்பா லவரும் புகழ்ந்தேத்தும் இறைவா எல்லாம் வல்லோனே
அப்பா அரசே இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: ippār mutaleṇ mūrttamatāy ilaṅkum karuṇai eṅkōvē tappā yiṉatīrt teṉṉaiyummuṉ taṭuttāṭ koṇṭa tayānitiyē eppā lavarum pukaḻntēttum iṟaivā ellām vallōṉē appā aracē iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: O my gracious King, shining as the eight forms beginning with this earth! O treasure of compassion, who corrected my errors and formerly intervened to take me into your service! O Lord praised by people from all directions, O all-powerful one, O Father, O King! See, I can no longer endure this at all.
commentary: This is a cry of raw desperation. The speaker acknowledges God's vastness, seeing the divine presence in the very elements of creation, and recalls God's past mercy. Yet, this awareness only sharpens the pain of current separation, leading to the simple, heartbreaking plea: "I can't bear this any longer."

tamil: புரைசேர் துயரப் புணரிமுற்றும் கடத்தி ஞான பூரணமாம்
கரைசேர்த் தருளி இன்னமுதக் கடலைக் குடிப்பித் திடல்வேண்டும்
உரைசேர் மறையின் முடிவிளங்கும் ஒளிமா மணியே உடையானே
அரைசே அப்பா இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: puraicēr tuyarap puṇarimuṟṟum kaṭatti ñāṉa pūraṇamām karaicērt taruḷi iṉṉamutak kaṭalaik kuṭippit tiṭalvēṇṭum uraicēr maṟaiyiṉ muṭiviḷaṅkum oḷimā maṇiyē uṭaiyāṉē araicē appā iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: You must make me cross entirely the flawed ocean of sorrow, bring me graciously to the shore of perfect wisdom, and have me drink the ocean of sweet ambrosia. O great radiant gem shining at the apex of the celebrated Vedas! O my Master! O King, O Father! See, I can no longer endure this at all.
commentary: Life is described as a "flawed ocean of sorrow," a powerful image of being lost in endless suffering. The speaker asks for rescue and to be brought to the shore of perfect wisdom (jnana) and to drink the "ocean of sweet ambrosia" (amutam), the divine nectar of immortality and bliss. It is a plea to replace suffering entirely with enlightenment and union.

tamil: கண்ணார் அமுதக் கடலேஎன் கண்ணே கண்ணுட் கருமணியே
தண்ணார் மதியே கதிர்பரப்பித் தழைத்த சுடரே தனிக்கனலே
எண்ணா டரிய பெரியஅண்டம் எல்லாம் நிறைந்த அருட்சோதி
அண்ணா அரசே இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: kaṇṇār amutak kaṭalēeṉ kaṇṇē kaṇṇuṭ karumaṇiyē taṇṇār matiyē katirparappit taḻaitta cuṭarē taṉikkaṉalē eṇṇā ṭariya periyaaṇṭam ellām niṟainta aruṭcōti aṇṇā aracē iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: O ocean of ambrosia that fills my eyes! O my very eye, O pupil within my eye! O cool, full moon! O flourishing radiance spreading its rays! O unique fire! O Grace-Light that fills all the great, countless universes! O great one, O King! See, I can no longer endure this at all.
commentary: The relationship with God here is both intensely personal and infinitely vast. God is as close as the pupil in one's own eye and as immense as the Grace-Light (ArutJothi) that fills all of creation. This simultaneous experience of intimacy and immensity makes the feeling of separation all the more painful, driving the repeated cry of desperation.

tamil: பொய்யா தென்றும் எனதுளத்தே பொருந்தும் மருந்தே புண்ணியனே
கையார்ந் திலங்கு மணியேசெங் கரும்பே கனியே கடையேற்குச்
செய்யா உதவி செய்தபெருந் தேவே மூவாத் தெள்ளமுதே
ஐயா அரசே இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: poyyā teṉṟum eṉatuḷattē poruntum maruntē puṇṇiyaṉē kaiyārn tilaṅku maṇiyēceṅ karumpē kaṉiyē kaṭaiyēṟkuc ceyyā utavi ceytaperun tēvē mūvāt teḷḷamutē aiyā aracē iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: O medicine that unfailingly abides in my heart forever! O virtuous one! O gem shining in my hand, O red sugarcane, O ripe fruit! O great God who did for me, the lowliest one, an unprecedented kindness! O ageless, clear ambrosia! O master, O King! See, I can no longer endure this at all.
commentary: God is felt as an intensely personal and tangible gift: a medicine that heals the heart, a gem held in the hand, the sweetness of sugarcane. It is an act of pure grace. Vallalar expresses deep humility, seeing himself as "the lowliest one" who has received an incredible, unearned kindness from the divine.

tamil: இத்தா ரணியில் என்பிழைகள் எல்லாம் பொறுத்த என்குருவே
நித்தா சிற்றம் பலத்தாடும் நிருத்தா எல்லாஞ் செயவல்ல
சித்தா சித்தி புரத்தமர்ந்த தேவே சித்த சிகாமணியே
அத்தா அரசே இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: ittā raṇiyil eṉpiḻaikaḷ ellām poṟutta eṉkuruvē nittā ciṟṟam palattāṭum niruttā ellāñ ceyavalla cittā citti purattamarnta tēvē citta cikāmaṇiyē attā aracē iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: O my guru who forgave all my faults on this earth! O eternal one! O dancer in the Little Hall! O Siddha who can do all things! O God seated in Siddhipuram (city of perfection)! O crest-jewel of Siddhas! O Father, O King! See, I can no longer endure this at all.
commentary: Here, God is the supreme teacher or guru who has forgiven all the speaker's faults. The verse invokes the image of the cosmic dancer in the "Little Hall" (Chitrambalam), whose movement animates the universe. By calling God the ultimate Siddha (a perfected being with limitless power), Vallalar affirms his faith that God has the absolute ability to bring about the spiritual liberation he so desperately seeks.

tamil: எம்மே தகவும் உடையவர்தம் இதயத் தமர்ந்த இறையவனே
இம்மே தினியில் எனைவருவித் திட்ட கருணை எம்மானே
நம்மே லவர்க்கும் அறிவரிய நாதா என்னை நயந்தீன்ற
அம்மே அப்பா இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: emmē takavum uṭaiyavartam itayat tamarnta iṟaiyavaṉē immē tiṉiyil eṉaivaruvit tiṭṭa karuṇai emmāṉē nammē lavarkkum aṟivariya nātā eṉṉai nayantīṉṟa ammē appā iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: O God who abides in the hearts of those who possess every virtue! O my compassionate Master who caused me to come into this world! O Lord, difficult to know even for those superior to us! O Mother, O Father, who lovingly gave birth to me! See this: I cannot endure it any longer.
commentary: Vallalar addresses God as the ultimate parent, both Mother and Father, the compassionate source of his very existence. This creates a powerful emotional tension. If God lovingly brought him into this world, why is the world so full of pain? The desperate cry, "I cannot endure it any longer," is therefore a plea for escape and a child's appeal to the parent who is responsible for their entire situation.

tamil: செப்பார் கலைகள் மொழிந்தபொருள் திறங்கள் அனைத்துந் தெரிந்துதெளிந்
திப்பா ரிடைநின் புகழ்பாடு கின்ற பெரிய ரின்மொழிப்பாட்
டொப்பாச் சிறியேன் புன்மொழிப்பாட் டெல்லாம் உவந்த உடையானே
அப்பா அரசே இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: ceppār kalaikaḷ moḻintaporuḷ tiṟaṅkaḷ aṉaittun terintuteḷin tippā riṭainiṉ pukaḻpāṭu kiṉṟa periya riṉmoḻippāṭ ṭoppāc ciṟiyēṉ puṉmoḻippāṭ ṭellām uvanta uṭaiyāṉē appā aracē iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: O Master, you delight in all the wretched songs of this small one, which are nothing compared to the sweet songs of the great ones who sing your praise on this earth, having fully known and understood all the meanings conveyed by the glorious scriptures! O Father, O King! See this: I cannot endure it any longer.
commentary: This is a moving expression of humility. Vallalar considers his own devotional poems to be "wretched songs," especially when compared to the great hymns of great saints who have mastered scripture. Yet, he holds a deep faith that God, his Master, lovingly accepts and even delights in his imperfect, heartfelt offerings. It affirms that sincerity of devotion is more valuable than intellectual or artistic perfection.

tamil: துப்பார் கனகப் பொதுவில்நடத் தொழிலால் உலகத் துயர்ஒழிக்கும்
வைப்பாம் இறைவா சிவகாம வல்லிக் கிசைந்த மணவாளா
ஒப்பார் உயர்ந்தார் இல்லாத ஒருவா எல்லாம் உடையானே
அப்பா அரசே இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: tuppār kaṉakap potuvilnaṭat toḻilāl ulakat tuyaroḻikkum vaippām iṟaivā civakāma vallik kicainta maṇavāḷā oppār uyarntār illāta oruvā ellām uṭaiyāṉē appā aracē iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: O God, our treasure, who ends the world’s suffering through the act of dancing in the glorious golden hall! O Bridegroom perfectly suited for Sivakama Valli! O Unique One with no equal and no superior, who possesses everything! O Father, O King! See this: I cannot endure it any longer.
commentary: Vallalar uses familiar images from temple worship, like God's cosmic dance that sustains the world and his marriage to the goddess Sivakama Valli. By invoking these traditional symbols of divine power and order, he appeals to God as the ultimate treasure who has the ability to end all suffering.

tamil: ஒப்பா ருரைப்பார் நின்பெருமைக் கெனமா மறைகள் ஓலமிடும்
துப்பார் வண்ணச் சுடரேமெய்ச் சோதிப் படிக வண்ணத்தாய்
வெப்பா னவைதீர்த் தெனக்கமுத விருந்து புரிதல் வேண்டும்என்றன்
அப்பா அரசே இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: oppā ruraippār niṉperumaik keṉamā maṟaikaḷ ōlamiṭum tuppār vaṇṇac cuṭarēmeyc cōtip paṭika vaṇṇattāy veppā ṉavaitīrt teṉakkamuta viruntu purital vēṇṭumeṉṟaṉ appā aracē iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: The great Vedas wail, asking who can be your equal, who can describe your greatness. O Flame of glorious color! O One with a form like true Jothi and crystal! You must end my burning afflictions and give me a feast of amrita. My Father, my King! See this: I cannot endure it any longer.
commentary: The greatest scriptures, the Vedas, cry out in helpless wonder that no one can equal or describe God's greatness, which Vallalar experiences as pure, crystal-clear Jothi. His plea is direct: that God end his burning afflictions and give him a feast of amrita, the divine nectar of deathless bliss.

tamil: வெப்பார் உள்ளக் கலக்கமெலாம் இற்றைப் பொழுதே விலக்கிஒழித்
திப்பா ரிடைஎன் கருத்தின்வண்ணம் எல்லாம் விரைவின் ஈந்தருள்க
ஒப்பால் உரைத்த தன்றுண்மை உரைத்தேன் கருணை உடையானே
அப்பா அரசே இனிச்சிறிதும் ஆற்ற மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: veppār uḷḷak kalakkamelām iṟṟaip poḻutē vilakkioḻit tippā riṭaieṉ karuttiṉvaṇṇam ellām viraiviṉ īntaruḷka oppāl uraitta taṉṟuṇmai uraittēṉ karuṇai uṭaiyāṉē appā aracē iṉicciṟitum āṟṟa māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: This very day, banish all the feverish turmoil in my heart and, on this earth, swiftly grant me everything my mind desires. I am not speaking in analogies; I have spoken the truth, O compassionate Master! O Father, O King! See this: I cannot endure it any longer.
commentary: This is an urgent demand born of deep pain. By insisting he speaks the plain truth without analogy, Vallalar conveys the raw reality of his suffering and his absolute faith that the compassionate God he addresses has the power to end it immediately.

translit: poḻutu viṭintateṉ uḷḷameṉ kamalam pūttatu poṉṉoḷi poṅkiya teṅkum toḻutuniṟ kiṉṟaṉaṉ ceypaṇi ellām collutal vēṇṭumeṉ vallacaṟ kuruvē muḻutumā ṉāṉeṉa ākama vēta muṟaikaḷe lāmmoḻi kiṉṟamuṉ ṉavaṉē eḻututal ariyacīr aruṭperuñ cōti eṉtantai yēpaḷḷi eḻuntaruḷ vāyē.
translation: Dawn has broken. The lotus of my heart has bloomed. A golden light has surged everywhere. I stand in worship; You must tell me every task I am to perform, O my potent Satguru. O Primordial One, whom all the ways of the Agamas and Vedas proclaim as the Absolute Whole, O ArutPerunJothi of glory beyond description! My Father, please arise from your sacred couch.
commentary: The breaking of dawn is a metaphor for an inner spiritual awakening. The "blooming lotus of the heart" signifies a consciousness now open and ready to receive grace. He asks God, his Satguru (true teacher), to give him his life's work, identifying this teacher with the ultimate reality that the ancient Agamas and Vedas (sacred scriptures) speak of. He names this reality ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light), addressing it with the intimacy of a son to his father.

translit: tuṟkuṇa māyaipōyt tolaintatu ñāṉam tōṉṟiṭap poṉṉoḷi tōṟṟiya katirtāṉ ciṟkuṇa varaimicai utayañcey tatumā cittikaḷ aṭippaṇi ceytiṭac cūḻnta naṟkuṇac caṉmārkka caṅkattār ellām naṇṇiṉar tōttiram paṇṇiniṟ kiṉṟār eṟkuṇa vaḷittaeṉ aruṭperuñ cōti eṉṉammai yēpaḷḷi eḻuntaruḷ vāyē.
translation: The maya of evil qualities has gone; it is destroyed. As wisdom dawns, the sun that brings forth the golden light has risen over the mountain of consciousness. All the members of the virtuous Sanmarkkam Sangam, at whose feet the great siddhis wait to serve, have drawn near and stand singing your praises. My ArutPerunJothi, who fed me, my Mother, please arise from your sacred couch.
commentary: The arrival of spiritual light actively destroys illusion. Here, the night that is ending is maya (the illusion that veils reality), and the rising sun is gnosis (direct spiritual wisdom). The members of the Sanmarkkam Sangam (association for the true path) have gathered to witness this awakening, and the great siddhis (powers of attainment) wait to serve at their feet. The Light that rises is the Mother who feeds the soul.

translit: nilanteḷin tatukaṇa maḻuṅkiṉa cuvaṇa nīṭoḷi tōṉṟiṟṟuk kōṭolik kiṉṟa alarntatu tāmarai āṇava iruḷpōy aḻintatu kaḻintatu māyaimāl iravu pularntatu toṇṭarō ṭaṇṭarum kūṭip pōṟṟiyō civaciva pōṟṟieṉ kiṉṟār ilaṅkuru vaḷittaeṉ aruṭperuñ cōti eṉkuru vēpaḷḷi eḻuntaru ḷāyē.
translation: The land has become clear, the stars have grown dim. The long golden light has appeared; the horns are sounding. The lotuses have bloomed. The darkness of anavam is gone, destroyed. The vast night of maya has passed. It has dawned. Devotees and celestials have gathered, exclaiming, "Praise! Siva, Siva, praise!" My ArutPerunJothi, who granted me this radiant form, my Guru, please arise from your sacred couch.
commentary: The dawning of grace purifies consciousness at its root. As the outer world becomes clear, the inner darkness of anavam (the innate sense of a separate "I") is destroyed, and the long night of maya finally ends. The entire cosmos, from human devotees to celestial beings, joins in celebrating this new day. The divine is now addressed as "my Guru," the one who has bestowed a radiant, transformed body upon the devotee.

translit: kallāya maṉaṅkaḷum karaiyappoṉ ṉoḷitāṉ kaṇṭatu kaṅkulum viṇṭatu toṇṭar pallārum eytiṉar pāṭiniṉ ṟāṭip paravukiṉ ṟāraṉpu viravukiṉ ṟārāy nallārmeyñ ñāṉikaḷ yōkikaḷ piṟarum naṇṇiṉar cūḻntaṉar puṇṇiya nitiyē ellāñcey vallaeṉ aruṭperuñ cōti eṉteyva mēpaḷḷi eḻuntaruḷ vāyē.
translation: The golden light has appeared, causing even stone-like minds to melt. The darkness of night has dispersed. Many devotees have come; they stand singing and dancing, offering praise, their beings suffused with love. The virtuous, the true Gnostics, the Yogis, and others have drawn near and now surround you, O Treasure of holy merit! My ArutPerunJothi, who is all-powerful, my God, please arise from your sacred couch.
commentary: Divine grace is powerful enough to transform even the most hardened hearts, making them melt like wax. The poet describes a scene of ecstatic celebration, where devotees, true Gnostics (meyññāṉikaḷ), and Yogis have all gathered, drawn by the light. This grace is for all who are open to it. He addresses God as the "all-powerful" and "my God," the source of all goodness and power.

translit: puṉmālai iravelām pularntatu ñāṉap poruppiṉmēl poṟkatir polintatu pulavōr coṉmālai toṭuttaṉar tutittuniṟ kiṉṟār cuttacaṉ mārkkacaṅ kattavar ellām maṉmālai mālaiyā vantucūḻ kiṉṟār vāṉavar neruṅkiṉar vāḻieṉ kiṉṟār eṉmālai aṇintaeṉ aruṭperuñ cōti eṉpati yēpaḷḷi eḻuntaruḷ vāyē.
translation: The dim evening and the whole of night have passed. Upon the mountain of gnosis, a golden ray now gleams. The poets have woven garlands of words and stand offering praise. The members of the Suddha Sanmarkkam Sangam all come in vast throngs, surrounding you. The celestials press close, crying "Hail!" My ArutPerunJothi, who wears my garland, my Lord, please arise from your sacred couch.
commentary: The "mountain of gnosis" represents the highest peak of spiritual wisdom, and the "golden ray" is the first glimpse of enlightenment. The gathering of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (Pure True Path) community shows that this awakening is the foundation for a new spiritual society. When Vallalar says the Lord "wears my garland," he is using a traditional, intimate expression to show that his personal devotion has been received and accepted by the divine.

translit: orumaiyiṉ ulakelām ōṅkuka eṉavē ūtiṉa ciṉṉaṅkaḷ ūtiṉa caṅkam perumaikoḷ camaraca cuttacaṉ mārkkap perumpukaḻ pēciṉar periyavar cūḻntār arumaiyum eḷimaiyum ākiaṉ ṟāki ampalat tēcitti āṭalcey patiyē irumaiyum aḷittaeṉ aruṭperuñ cōti eṉara cēpaḷḷi eḻuntaruḷ vāyē.
translation: So that all worlds may flourish in unity, horns are blown and conches are sounded. The great ones have gathered, speaking the great fame of the glorious Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam. O Lord who performs the play of siddhi in the Ambalam, becoming both rare and easy, both what is and what is not! My ArutPerunJothi who granted me both worlds, my King, please awaken and arise.
commentary: This awakening is more than for one person's benefit; its ultimate purpose is universal harmony, or what Vallalar calls Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure True Path of Harmony). He describes God with paradoxes, rare yet easy, being and non-being, to point to a reality beyond simple logic. The divine "play of siddhi (supernatural power)" takes place in the Ambalam, the sacred inner space of consciousness, and grants the seeker mastery over both the material and spiritual worlds.

translit: ciṉaippaḷḷit tāmaṅkaḷ koṇarntaṉar aṭiyār civaciva pōṟṟieṉ ṟuvakaikoḷ kiṉṟār niṉaippaḷḷi uṇṇatteḷ ḷāramu taḷikkum nēramin nērameṉ ṟāriyar pukaṉṟār muṉaippaḷḷi payiṟṟāteṉ taṉaikkalvi payiṟṟi muḻutuṇar vittuṭal paḻutelām tavirttē eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppiya aruṭperuñ cōti eṉṉappa ṉēpaḷḷi eḻuntaruḷ vāyē.
translation: Devotees bring garlands with fresh buds, rejoicing and chanting, "Siva, Siva, praise be!" The noble ones have announced that this is the time to offer the clear, rare ambrosia. Without making me learn in a rudimentary school, you taught me the true knowledge, made me realize the whole, and removed all my body's flaws. O ArutPerunJothi who awakened me from my sleep, my Father, please awaken and arise.
commentary: True knowledge, Vallalar insists, is a direct gift from God, an inner transmission that bypasses conventional schooling. This divine teaching is whole, perfecting the mind with wisdom and healing the physical body of all its flaws. The line "who awakened me from my sleep" makes the poem's theme explicit: the entire song is about being awakened from the slumber of ordinary consciousness into a state of divine awareness.

translit: matampiṭit tavarellām vāyppiṭip puṇṭu vantuniṟ kiṉṟaṉar vāytiṟap pippāṉ katampiṭit tavarellām kaṭumpiṇi yālē kalaṅkiṉar cūḻntaṉar ulampuṟu kiṉṟār patampiṭit tavarellām ampalap pāṭṭē pāṭiṉar āṭiṉar paraviniṟ kiṉṟār itampiṭit teṉaiyāṇṭa aruṭperuñ cōti eṉayya ṉēpaḷḷi eḻuntaruḷ vāyē.
translation: All who were seized by religious dogma stand silenced, waiting for you to open their mouths. All who were seized by anger, now afflicted by severe diseases, have gathered around in distress, lamenting. All who hold fast to your feet sing only the songs of the Ambalam; they are singing, dancing, and standing in praise. O ArutPerunJothi who took up my well-being and ruled me, my Master, please awaken and arise.
commentary: The arrival of divine light serves as a moment of truth. Those clinging to rigid religious dogma or consumed by anger find their foundations collapsing. In contrast, those who simply hold to God in pure devotion are filled with joyful song and dance. The path to God is not through intellectual certainty or emotional force, but through loving surrender, which leads to singing the "songs of the Ambalam" (the inner sacred space).

translit: maruḷoṭu māyaipōyt tolaintatu mataṅkaḷ vāymūṭik koṇṭaṉa malarntatu kamalam aruḷoḷi viḷaṅkiya torutiruc capaiyum alaṅkarik kiṉṟaṉar tulaṅkivīṟ ṟirukkat teruḷoṭu poruḷummēṉ mēleṉak kaḷittuc cittelāñ ceytiṭat tiruvaruḷ purintē iruḷaṟut teṉaiyāṇṭa aruṭperuñ cōti eṉvaḷḷa lēpaḷḷi eḻuntaruḷ vāyē.
translation: Delusion and māyā have perished; the religions have fallen silent. The lotus has bloomed. A sacred hall, radiant with the light of grace, is being decorated for you to sit enthroned in splendor. My great Benefactor, ArutPerunJothi, who cut away the darkness and ruled me, bestowing ever-increasing clarity and substance and granting the sacred grace to perform all siddhis, please awaken and arise.
commentary: When grace dawns, delusion and māyā perish and the religions themselves fall silent. The lotus blooms, and a sacred hall radiant with the light of grace is made ready for the Lord to sit enthroned. The ArutPerunJothi who cut away the darkness grants ever-increasing clarity and substance, and the grace to perform all siddhis.

translit: alaṅkarik kiṉṟōmōr tiruccapai atilē amarntaruṭ cōtikoṇ ṭaṭicciṟi yōmai valampeṟum iṟavāta vāḻvilvait tiṭavē vāḻttukiṉ ṟōmmuṉṉar vaṇaṅkiniṟ kiṉṟōm vilaṅkiya tiruḷelām viṭintatu poḻutu viraintemak karuḷutal vēṇṭumit taruṇam ilaṅkunal taruṇamem aruṭperuñ cōti emtantai yēpaḷḷi eḻuntaruḷ vāyē.
translation: We are decorating a sacred hall. We stand before you, bowing and praising you to be seated there and, with your grace-light, to place us, your humble servants, in a victorious, deathless life. All obstructing darkness has vanished; the day has dawned. You must grace us quickly. This is the shining, opportune moment, our ArutPerunJothi, our Father! Please awaken and arise.
commentary: The time for transformation is now. The devotee's role is to prepare the inner self, the "sacred hall," for the divine presence. The goal is a deathless life here and now. The poem ends with a sense of urgency, declaring that the perfect moment for grace has arrived.

translit: iravu viṭintatu iṇaiyaṭi vāytta paravi makiḻntēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa pālamutu uṇṭēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: The night has dawned, I have attained the matching feet. Leap for joy, singing, "I have praised and rejoiced!" Leap for joy, singing, "I have drunk the ambrosia of milk!"
commentary: Spiritual awakening is a joyous dawn after the long night of ignorance. To attain God's "matching feet" is to find perfect refuge and union. This realization is a deeply nourishing experience, like drinking the "ambrosia of milk" that is divine grace.

translit: poḻutu viṭintatu poṟpatam vāytta toḻutu makiḻntēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa tūyavaṉ āṉēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: The day has dawned, I have attained the golden feet. Leap for joy, singing, "I have worshipped and rejoiced!" Leap for joy, singing, "I have become pure!"
commentary: The attainment of God's presence, symbolized by the "golden feet," is what makes a person truly pure. Worship is the very process that purifies the soul and brings overwhelming joy.

translit: tūkkam tolaintatu cūriyaṉ tōṉṟiṉaṉ ēkkam tavirntēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa iṉṉamutu uṇṭēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: Sleep has vanished, the sun has appeared. Leap for joy, singing, "I have shed my yearning!" Leap for joy, singing, "I have drunk the sweet ambrosia!"
commentary: The "sleep" that has vanished is the soul's state of spiritual unconsciousness. With the appearance of the divine "sun," the deep-seated "yearning" for God, which is a source of great pain for the seeker, is finally satisfied. This fulfillment is a taste of sweet, divine bliss.

translit: tuṉpam tavirntatu tūkkam tolaintatu iṉpam kiṭaittateṉṟu untīpaṟa eṇṇam palittateṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: Suffering has ended, sleep has vanished. Leap for joy, singing, "Bliss has been found!" Leap for joy, singing, "My intention has been fulfilled!"
commentary: The end of spiritual ignorance ("sleep") brings a definitive end to all suffering. The soul's ultimate intention, to find and unite with God, has now been achieved, resulting in pure bliss.

translit: ñāṉam utittatu nātam olittatu tīṉan tavirntateṉṟu untīpaṟa ciṟcapai kaṇṭēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: Gnosis has arisen, the Natham has resounded. Leap for joy, singing, "Misery has been cast off!" Leap for joy, singing, "I have seen the Chit Sabhai!"
commentary: Spiritual awakening is an experience of direct knowledge, or gnosis (ñāṉam), more than belief. This knowing is accompanied by hearing the Natham, the primordial divine sound that underlies creation. The ultimate vision is of the Chit Sabhai ("hall of consciousness"), the sacred space within oneself where God's presence is directly perceived.

translit: tiraiyaṟṟu viṭṭatu ceñcuṭar tōṉṟiṟṟu paraioḷi ōṅkiṟṟeṉṟu untīpaṟa palittatu pūcaiyeṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: The veil has vanished, the red flame has appeared, and the light of Parai has risen high: sing Untīpaṟa (a call in a celebratory folk game). The pūcai has succeeded: sing Untīpaṟa.
commentary: The "veil" of illusion that separates the soul from God has been removed. In its place, the divine appears as a brilliant "red flame" and as the light of Parai, the Supreme Power. This inner realization is the true fruit of all worship; the external pūcai (ritual worship) is only successful when it leads to this direct, internal experience of God.

translit: uḷḷiruḷ nīṅkiṟṟueṉ uḷḷoḷi ōṅkiṟṟut teḷḷamutu uṇṭēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa tittikka uṇṭēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: The inner darkness is gone, my inner light has risen high, and I have drunk the clear amutam: sing Untīpaṟa. I drank it, and it was sweet: sing Untīpaṟa.
commentary: Realization is described here in tangible, sensory terms. The inner darkness of ignorance is replaced by a rising inner light, and this experience brings with it a taste of amutam, the sweet nectar of immortality.

translit: entaiyaik kaṇṭēṉ iṭarelām nīṅkiṉēṉ cintai makiḻntēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa cittikaḷ peṟṟēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: I have seen my Father, all my troubles are gone, and my mind rejoices: sing Untīpaṟa. I have received the siddhis: sing Untīpaṟa.
commentary: The direct, intimate vision of God, addressed here as "Father," immediately puts an end to all worldly and spiritual troubles. This state of union also naturally bestows siddhis, or perfected spiritual powers.

translit: tantaiyaik kaṇṭēṉnāṉ cākā varampeṟṟēṉ cintai kaḷittēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa cittelām vallēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: I have seen the Father, I have received the boon of deathlessness, and my mind exults: sing Untīpaṟa. I am master of all spiritual powers: sing Untīpaṟa.
commentary: Seeing God confers the ultimate attainment: the "boon of deathlessness," a state beyond physical decay. This mastery over death is the greatest of all spiritual powers and the culmination of the divine vision.

translit: muttiyaip peṟṟēṉam muttiyiṉāl ñāṉa cittiyai uṟṟēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa cittaṉum āṉēṉeṉṟu untīpaṟa.
translation: I have obtained mutti, and through that liberation I have attained ñāṇa siddhi: sing Untīpaṟa. I have become a Cittan: sing Untīpaṟa.
commentary: Spiritual liberation (mutti) is the foundation for a higher state. Through liberation, one achieves ñāṇa siddhi (the perfection of wisdom) and becomes a Cittan, a perfected master who has realized their full divine potential.

tamil: எண்ணா நின்றேன் எண்ணமெலாம் எய்த அருள்செய் கின்றதனித்
தண்ணா ரமுதே சிற்சபையில் தனித்த தலைமைப் பெருவாழ்வே
கண்ணா ரொளியே ஒளிஎல்லாம் கலந்த வெளியே கருதுறும்என்
அண்ணா ஐயா அம்மாஎன் அப்பா யான்உன் அடைக்கலமே.
translit: eṇṇā niṉṟēṉ eṇṇamelām eyta aruḷcey kiṉṟataṉit taṇṇā ramutē ciṟcapaiyil taṉitta talaimaip peruvāḻvē kaṇṇā roḷiyē oḷiellām kalanta veḷiyē karutuṟumeṉ aṇṇā aiyā ammāeṉ appā yāṉuṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: I was thinking, and you grant the grace for all my thoughts to be realized. O unique, cool ambrosia! O singular, supreme, great life in the Chit Sabhai! O light of my eyes! O space where all light has merged! You who are the object of my thoughts, my elder brother, my master, my mother, my father, I take refuge in you.
commentary: Surrender begins with recognizing God's presence everywhere, from the most personal to the most universal. God is addressed as the supreme life in the Chit Sabhai (the hall of consciousness) and also as the intimate relations of family: mother, father, brother. This is a statement that the divine is the source of our thoughts, the light in our eyes, and the ultimate safe harbor for the soul.

tamil: திரைசேர் மறைப்பைத் தீர்த்தெனக்கே தெரியா வெல்லாந் தெரிவித்துப்
பரைசேர் ஞானப் பெருவெளியில் பழுத்த கொழுத்த பழந்தந்தே
கரைசேர் இன்பக் காட்சிஎலாம் காட்டிக் கொடுத்தே எனையாண்ட
அரைசே ஐயா அம்மாஎன் அப்பா யான்உன் அடைக்கலமே.
translit: tiraicēr maṟaippait tīrtteṉakkē teriyā vellān terivittup paraicēr ñāṉap peruveḷiyil paḻutta koḻutta paḻantantē karaicēr iṉpak kāṭcielām kāṭṭik koṭuttē eṉaiyāṇṭa araicē aiyā ammāeṉ appā yāṉuṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: You removed the concealing veil and revealed to me everything I did not know. In the great space of wisdom where Parai resides, you gave me the ripened, succulent fruit. You showed me all the blissful visions that bring one to the shore and made me your own. O King, my master, my mother, my father, I take refuge in you.
commentary: The spiritual path leads from ignorance to knowledge, and this knowledge is revealed. Vallalar describes God as the one who peels back the veil of illusion, showing the soul what it could not see on its own. This revelation is an experience, a "succulent fruit" of wisdom given in the space of Parai, the supreme divine power.

tamil: தேனே அமுதே சிற்சபையில் சிவமே தவமே செய்கின்றோர்
ஊனே புகுந்த ஒளியேமெய் உணர்வே என்றன் உயிர்க்குயிராம்
வானே என்னைத் தானாக்கு வானே கோனே எல்லாம்வல்
லானே ஐயா அம்மாஎன் அப்பா யான்உன் அடைக்கலமே.
translit: tēṉē amutē ciṟcapaiyil civamē tavamē ceykiṉṟōr ūṉē pukunta oḷiyēmey uṇarvē eṉṟaṉ uyirkkuyirām vāṉē eṉṉait tāṉākku vāṉē kōṉē ellāmval lāṉē aiyā ammāeṉ appā yāṉuṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: O honey, O ambrosia! O Sivam in the hall of consciousness! O the very penance of those who perform it! O light that entered my flesh! O true awareness! O life of my life! O Heaven! O heavenly one who makes me become you! O King! O all-powerful one! My master, my mother, my father, I take refuge in you.
commentary: This verse dissolves the distance between the worshipper and the worshipped. God is not somewhere else; God is the "light that entered my flesh," the "true awareness" within, the "life of my life." Even the spiritual effort of penance is described as God's own action. The ultimate goal is to be with God and for God to "make me become you," a complete merging of the individual self into the divine.

tamil: கடையேன் உள்ளக் கவலைஎலாம் கழற்றிக் கருணை அமுதளித்தென்
புடையே அகத்தும் புறத்தும்அகப் புறத்தும் விளங்கும் புண்ணியனே
தடையே தவிர்க்கும் கனகசபைத் தலைவா ஞான சபாபதியே
translit: kaṭaiyēṉ uḷḷak kavalaielām kaḻaṟṟik karuṇai amutaḷitteṉ puṭaiyē akattum puṟattumakap puṟattum viḷaṅkum puṇṇiyaṉē taṭaiyē tavirkkum kaṉakacapait talaivā ñāṉa capāpatiyē aṭaiyēṉ ulakaiuṉai aṭaintēṉ aṭiyēṉuṉṟaṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: You removed all the worries from the heart of this lowly one and gave me the ambrosia of compassion. O virtuous one who shines beside me, within, without, and both within and without! O leader of the Kanaka Sabai who removes all obstacles! O lord of the Gnana Sabai! I will not seek the world; I have sought you. I, your servant, take refuge in you.
commentary: Divine grace brings inner peace by dissolving worldly anxieties, replacing them with the "ambrosia of compassion." God is then experienced as a constant presence shining everywhere: inside us, outside us, and in the space between. Vallalar invokes the sacred Kanaka Sabai (golden hall) and Gnana Sabai (hall of wisdom), re-imagining them as inner states of consciousness. Having found this all-pervading reality, the path becomes clear: to seek nothing from the world, but to take refuge in the Divine alone.

tamil: இகத்தும் பரத்தும் பெறும்பலன்கள் எல்லாம் பெறுவித் திம்மையிலே
முகத்தும் உளத்தும் களிதுளும்ப மூவா இன்ப நிலைஅமர்த்திச்
சகத்துள் ளவர்கள் மிகத்துதிப்பத் தக்கோன் எனவைத் தென்னுடைய
அகத்தும் புறத்தும் விளங்குகின்றோய் அடியேன் உன்றன் அடைக்கலமே.
translit: ikattum parattum peṟumpalaṉkaḷ ellām peṟuvit timmaiyilē mukattum uḷattum kaḷituḷumpa mūvā iṉpa nilaiamarttic cakattuḷ ḷavarkaḷ mikattutippat takkōṉ eṉavait teṉṉuṭaiya akattum puṟattum viḷaṅkukiṉṟōy aṭiyēṉ uṉṟaṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: You enable me to receive all the benefits to be gained in this world and the next. In this very life, you establish me in a state of ageless bliss, making joy overflow in my face and heart. You have made me a worthy one, to be greatly praised by the people of the world. O you who shine within and without me, I, your servant, take refuge in you.
commentary: Contrary to purely ascetic views, the path of grace brings fulfillment both in this world and the next. The result is an "ageless bliss" so powerful that joy overflows visibly from the heart and face. The devotee is made a respected, "worthy one" among people, showing that spiritual attainment and a blessed earthly life go together.

tamil: நீண்ட மறைகள் ஆகமங்கள் நெடுநாள் முயன்று வருந்திநின்று
வேண்ட அவைகட் கொருசிறிதும் விளங்கக் காட்டா தென்மொழியைப்
பூண்ட அடியை என்தலைமேல் பொருந்தப் பொருத்தி என்தன்னை
ஆண்ட கருணைப் பெருங்கடலே அடியேன் உன்றன் அடைக்கலமே.
translit: nīṇṭa maṟaikaḷ ākamaṅkaḷ neṭunāḷ muyaṉṟu varuntiniṉṟu vēṇṭa avaikaṭ koruciṟitum viḷaṅkak kāṭṭā teṉmoḻiyaip pūṇṭa aṭiyai eṉtalaimēl poruntap porutti eṉtaṉṉai āṇṭa karuṇaip peruṅkaṭalē aṭiyēṉ uṉṟaṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: O great ocean of compassion, you did not reveal yourself even slightly to the long Vedas and Agamas that strove, suffered, and pleaded for ages. Yet you accepted my words, perfectly placed your adorned feet upon my head, and made me your own. I, your servant, have taken refuge in you.
commentary: Direct experience of grace can surpass even the most revered scriptures. Vallalar states that God remained hidden from the ancient Vedas and Agamas (sacred texts) despite their long and difficult striving. In contrast, God responded to his simple, heartfelt words, granting him the highest blessing of placing the divine "feet upon my head," a symbol of initiation and acceptance. This highlights a path of personal devotion and pure compassion over one of institutional religion or scholarly learning.

tamil: பாடுஞ் சிறியேன் பாட்டனைத்தும் பலிக்கக் கருணை பாலித்துக்
கோடு மனப்பேய்க் குரங்காட்டம் குலைத்தே சீற்றக் கூற்றொழித்து
நீடும் உலகில் அழியாத நிலைமேல் எனைவைத் தென்னுளத்தே
ஆடும் கருணைப் பெருவாழ்வே அடியேன் உன்றன் அடைக்கலமே.
translit: pāṭuñ ciṟiyēṉ pāṭṭaṉaittum palikkak karuṇai pālittuk kōṭu maṉappēyk kuraṅkāṭṭam kulaittē cīṟṟak kūṟṟoḻittu nīṭum ulakil aḻiyāta nilaimēl eṉaivait teṉṉuḷattē āṭum karuṇaip peruvāḻvē aṭiyēṉ uṉṟaṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: O great life of compassion, you bestowed grace to make all the songs of this lowly singer bear fruit, destroyed the dance of my crooked monkey-mind-demon, eliminated the furious god of death, placed me in an imperishable state in this vast world, and now dance within my being. I, your servant, have taken refuge in you.
commentary: Grace brings about a complete inner and outer transformation with tangible results. It gives power to his poetry, calms the restless "monkey-mind," and most radically, overcomes mortality by "eliminating the furious god of death." Having granted this imperishable state, the Divine is a joyful, living presence that now "dances" within his own being.

tamil: கட்டுக் கடங்கா மனப்பரியைக் கட்டும் இடத்தே கட்டுவித்தென்
மட்டுக் கடங்கா ஆங்கார மதமா அடங்க அடக்குவித்தே
எட்டுக் கிசைந்த இரண்டும்எனக் கிசைவித் தெல்லா இன்னமுதும்
அட்டுக் கொடுத்தே அருத்துகின்றோய் அடியேன் உன்றன் அடைக்கலமே.
translit: kaṭṭuk kaṭaṅkā maṉappariyaik kaṭṭum iṭattē kaṭṭuvitteṉ maṭṭuk kaṭaṅkā āṅkāra matamā aṭaṅka aṭakkuvittē eṭṭuk kicainta iraṇṭumeṉak kicaivit tellā iṉṉamutum aṭṭuk koṭuttē aruttukiṉṟōy aṭiyēṉ uṉṟaṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: O you who cook and serve me all sweet ambrosia! You had the untamable horse of my mind tied in its proper place and had the rutting elephant of my boundless arrogance completely subdued. You made suitable for me the two that accord with the eight. I, your servant, have taken refuge in you.
commentary: True self-mastery is a gift from God, more than an achievement of willpower. Here, the wild mind is a horse and the ego is a rutting elephant, both of which God helps to tame. The cryptic reference to "the two that accord with the eight" points to a specific spiritual alignment that God makes possible for the devotee.

tamil: புல்லுங் களபப் புணர்முலையார் புணர்ப்பும் பொருளும் பூமியும்என்
தொல்லும் உலகப் பேராசை உவரி கடத்தி எனதுமனக்
கல்லுங் கனியக் கரைவித்துக் கருணை அமுதங் களித்தளித்தே
அல்லும் பகலும் எனதுளத்தே அமர்ந்தோய் யான்உன் அடைக்கலமே.
translit: pulluṅ kaḷapap puṇarmulaiyār puṇarppum poruḷum pūmiyumeṉ tollum ulakap pērācai uvari kaṭatti eṉatumaṉak kalluṅ kaṉiyak karaivittuk karuṇai amutaṅ kaḷittaḷittē allum pakalum eṉatuḷattē amarntōy yāṉuṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: O you who are seated in my being day and night! You made me cross the ocean of my ancient, worldly, great desire for the embrace of women with sandalwood paste-smeared breasts, for wealth, and for land. You caused my stone-like mind to soften and melt, joyfully granting me the ambrosia of compassion. I have taken refuge in you.
commentary: Grace liberates a person from the endless cycle of worldly cravings for pleasure, wealth, and status. The deepest change is internal: God's compassion melts a heart that was hard as stone, filling it with a sweetness that replaces all other desires.

tamil: பிச்சங் கவரி நிழற்றியசைத் திடமால் யானைப் பிடரியின்மேல்
நிச்சம் பவனி வருகின்ற நிபுணர் எல்லாம் தொழுதேத்த
எச்சம் புரிவோர் போற்றஎனை ஏற்றா நிலைமேல் ஏற்றுவித்தென்
அச்சந் தவிர்த்தே ஆண்டுகொண்டோய் அடியேன் உன்றன் அடைக்கலமே.
translit: piccaṅ kavari niḻaṟṟiyacait tiṭamāl yāṉaip piṭariyiṉmēl niccam pavaṉi varukiṉṟa nipuṇar ellām toḻutētta eccam purivōr pōṟṟaeṉai ēṟṟā nilaimēl ēṟṟuvitteṉ accan tavirttē āṇṭukoṇṭōy aṭiyēṉ uṉṟaṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: O you who removed my fear and made me your own! While all the masters, who perpetually ride in procession on the necks of great elephants, shaded by waving peacock-feather and yak-tail whisks, bow and praise, and while those who perform sacrifices extol, you raised me to an unparalleled state. I, your servant, have taken refuge in you.
commentary: The state granted by divine grace surpasses all worldly power and religious prestige. Vallalar describes a complete reversal of status, where the most powerful kings and respected priests now look up to the humble devotee who has been touched by God. True authority belongs to the one who has received grace, not the one with earthly rank.

tamil: இருளைக் கெடுத்தென் எண்ணமெலாம் இனிது முடிய நிரம்புவித்து
மருளைத் தொலைத்து மெய்ஞ்ஞான வாழ்வை அடையும் வகைபுரிந்து
தெருளைத் தெளிவித் தெல்லாஞ்செய் சித்தி நிலையைச் சேர்வித்தே
translit: iruḷaik keṭutteṉ eṇṇamelām iṉitu muṭiya nirampuvittu maruḷait tolaittu meyññāṉa vāḻvai aṭaiyum vakaipurintu teruḷait teḷivit tellāñcey citti nilaiyaic cērvittē aruḷaikkoṭutteṉ taṉaiāṇṭōy aṭiyēṉ uṉṟaṉ aṭaikkalamē.
translation: O You who destroyed the darkness, brought all my intentions to sweet fulfillment, dispelled delusion, created a way for me to attain the life of true wisdom, clarified my understanding, made me reach the state of all-accomplishing siddhi, gave me grace, and made me Your own: I, your servant, am under your protection.
commentary: God's grace is a complete program of transformation that removes every obstacle to spiritual freedom. It dispels ignorance, clears away delusion, and grants meyjñānam (true wisdom) and siddhi, the spiritual capacity to accomplish all things. This is a change of heart and the attainment of a whole new level of being.

translit: cattiyam cattiyam aruṭperuñ cōtit tantaiya rēeṉait tāṅkukiṉ ṟīrē uttamam ākumnun tiruccamu katteṉ uṭalporuḷ āviyai uvappuṭaṉ aḷittēṉ ittakai ulakiṭai avaikkumeṉ taṉakkum ētuñ cutantaram illaiiṅ kiṉinīr ettakai āyiṉum ceytukoḷ kiṟpīr eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: It is the truth, it is the truth! O Father of the Vast Grace-Light, you are the one sustaining me. Before your supreme, sacred presence, I have joyfully given my body, possessions, and soul. In this world, I no longer have any independent claim over them. From this moment on, you may do with them as you please. You awakened me from my slumber and gave me true bliss.
commentary: The true spiritual life begins with the total and joyful surrender of oneself to God. Vallalar formally gives his body, possessions, and soul to the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light), declaring that he no longer has any independent rights over them. It is a happy offering, made in response to the grace that first awakened him from spiritual slumber.

translit: āṇainum āṇaieṉ aruṭperuñ cōti āṇṭava rētiru ampalat tavarē nāṇaiviṭ ṭuraikkiṉṟa vāṟitu kaṇṭīr nāyaka rēumai nāṉviṭa māṭṭēṉ kōṇaieṉ uṭalporuḷ āviyum numakkē koṭuttaṉaṉ iṉieṉmēl kuṟaicolla vēṇṭām ēṇainiṉ ṟeṭuttakaip piḷḷaināṉ aṉṟō eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: I swear by you, I swear by you, my Lord of the Vast Grace-Light, O one of the sacred Hall! See, this is how I speak, having cast off all shame. O Master, I will not let you go. I have given my flawed body, possessions, and soul to you. From now on, do not find fault with me. Am I not the child you lifted from the cradle? You awakened me from my slumber and gave me true bliss.
commentary: After complete surrender, the relationship with God becomes one of fearless intimacy. Having given everything, Vallalar now speaks with a child's boldness, swearing an oath not to let God go and even telling God not to find fault with the "flawed" self he has offered. The image of being a baby lifted from a cradle expresses a deep sense of dependence and trust.

translit: akattoṉṟu puṟattoṉṟu niṉaittatiṅ killai aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ āṇṭava rēnīr cakatteṉṟum eṅkaṇum cāṭciyāy niṉṟīr taṉipperun tēvarīr tiruccamu kattē ukatteṉatuṭalporuḷ āviyai numakkē orumaiyiṉ aḷittaṉaṉ irumaiyum peṟṟēṉ ikattaṉṟip parattiṉum eṉakkōrpaṟ ṟilaikāṇ eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: Here, I have not thought one thing inwardly and another outwardly. O Vast Grace-Light, my Lord, you stand as the eternal witness everywhere in the world. Before your sacred presence, O unique, great God, I have joyfully offered my body, possessions, and soul to you with single-minded devotion. I have received the rewards of both worlds. See, I have no attachment, not in this world nor in the world beyond. You awakened me from my slumber and gave me true bliss.
commentary: Sincere, wholehearted surrender is the path to ultimate freedom. Vallalar asserts his complete honesty, stating that by giving his body, possessions, and soul with single-minded focus, he has gained "the rewards of both worlds." The result of this total offering is liberation from all bonds and a state of non-attachment to anything in this life or the next.

translit: tappaṭi eṭuttukkoṇ ṭulakavar pōlē cāṟṟiṭa māṭṭēṉnāṉ cattiyam coṉṉēṉ ceppaṭi vittaicey cittareṉ ṟōtum tēvarīr vallapat tiruccamu kattē ippaṭi vāṉmutal eṅkaṇum aṟiya eṉṉuṭal ātiyai īntaṉaṉ umakkē eppaṭi āyiṉum ceytukoḷ kiṟpīr eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: Unlike the people of the world who take false steps, I will not speak in such a way; I have spoken the truth. Before the mighty, sacred presence of you, the God acclaimed as the Siddha who performs wonders like a magician, I have given my body and all else to you, so that the heavens and all creation may know. You may do with them as you please. You awakened me from my slumber and gave me true bliss.
commentary: This act of surrender is a formal, public testimony, not a private or hollow promise. Vallalar contrasts his truthful declaration with the deceptive ways of the world, making his vow before God and all of creation. In acknowledging God as a Siddha (a master of miraculous powers), he affirms the absolute authority God now holds over the self that has been so completely offered.

translit: taruṇattuk kēṟṟavā collippiṉ māṟṟum tappurai ītaṉṟu cattiyam coṉṉēṉ karuṇaip perukkiṉil kalanteṉa tuḷḷē kaṉaviṉum naṉaviṉum kaḷipparuḷ kiṉṟīr varuṇap potuvilum mācamu katteṉ vaṇporu ḷātiyai naṇpoṭu koṭuttēṉ iruḷnac caṟuttamu tantara vallīr eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: This is not a false promise, spoken to suit the moment and later taken back; I have spoken the truth. Mingling with the flood of your compassion, you bestow bliss upon me in dream and in waking from within my heart. In your great presence, the universal space common to all social classes, I have lovingly given my valuable possessions and all else. You have the power to destroy the poison of darkness and grant me nectar. You awakened me from my slumber and gave me true bliss.
commentary: He stresses that his offering is an eternal truth, spoken from a place of deep, lived experience of God's compassion. This act of giving takes place in God's presence, which he describes as a universal space beyond all social distinctions like caste. It is an act of love, trusting that God will remove all darkness and grant immortal life.

translit: vāymaṭṭil colkiṉṟa vārttaiaṉ ṟitueṉ maṉamottuc colliya vāymaimuk kālum tāymaṭṭil aṉṟieṉ tantaiyum kuruvum cāmiyum ākiya taṉipperun takaiyīr āymaṭṭil eṉṉuṭal ātiyai numakkē aṉpuṭaṉ koṭuttaṉaṉ āṇṭava rēnīr ēymaṭṭil eppaṭi yēṉuñcey kiṟpīr eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: This is not a word spoken merely with the mouth; it is the truth, spoken utterly with my mind's full accord. O matchless great Being, you are my mother, my father, my Guru, and my God. With love, I have given my body and its core essence to you. O Lord, you may do with it whatever is fitting, in any way you will. You awakened me from sleep and granted me the bliss of truth.
commentary: This declaration of surrender comes from the deepest alignment of his mind and heart, more than his lips. He addresses God as the one who fulfills every primary relationship: mother, father, Guru (spiritual teacher), and Lord. In giving his very self to this all-encompassing reality, he expresses complete trust in whatever God chooses to do with his life.

translit: tittikkap pēcik kacappuḷḷē kāṭṭum tiruṭṭuppēc caṉṟunum tiruvuḷam aṟiyum ettikkum aṟiyaeṉ uṭalporuḷ āvi eṉpavai mūṉṟumuḷ aṉpoṭu koṭuttēṉ cittikku mūlattait teḷivitteṉ uḷḷē tirunaṭam ceykiṉṟa tēvarīr tāmē ittikkil eppaṭi yēṉuñcey kiṟpīr eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: This is not deceitful talk, sweet on the outside while hiding bitterness within; your sacred will knows this. For all directions to know, I have given my body, possessions, and soul, all three, with inner love. You are the great God who clarified the root of all siddhi and performs the sacred dance within me. In this world, you may do with me whatever you will. You awakened me from sleep and granted me the bliss of truth.
commentary: Again, he insists on his sincerity, contrasting it with sweet words that hide a bitter heart. His offering is made with "inner love" to the God who is the very power performing the sacred dance inside his own being. This God is the source of all siddhi (supernatural or spiritual powers), and having surrendered to this source, Vallalar is open to whatever God wills for him.

translit: puṉmārkkat tuḷḷum puṟattum vēṟākip pukaṉṟacol aṉṟunum poṉṉaṭi kaṇṭa caṉmārkka caṅkattuc cātukkaḷ kāṇac cattiyam cattiyam cattiyam coṉṉēṉ taṉmārkkat teṉṉuṭal ātiyai numakkē tantaṉaṉ tiruvaruṭ canniti muṉṉē eṉmārkkat teppaṭi yēṉuñcey kiṟpīr eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: This is not a word spoken while following a vile path, being different inside and out. In the sight of the holy ones of the Sanmarkkam assembly who have seen your golden feet, I have spoken the truth, the truth, the truth. Of my own accord I have given my body and all that is mine to you, before your holy presence of grace. On my path, do with me whatever you will. You awakened me from sleep and granted me the bliss of truth. In my own path, do with me whatever you will. You awakened me from sleep and granted me the bliss of truth.
commentary: This final affirmation is a public oath. He declares his truthfulness to God and before the community of the Sanmarkkam (the True Path), his spiritual fellowship. By repeating "truth" three times, he makes a solemn vow. His personal surrender is the path itself, and he trusts God to guide his life completely from this point onward.

translit: iccaivē ṟillaiiṅ keṉkarut tellām eṉṉuḷ amarntaṟin tēiruk kiṉṟīr viccai elāmvalla nuntiruc camuka viṇṇappam eṉṉuṭal ātiyai numakkē niccalum tantaṉaṉ eṉvacam iṉṟi niṉṟaṉaṉ eṉṟaṉai nīrceyva tellām ecceyal āyiṉum ceytukoḷ kiṟpīr eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: I have no other desire here; you reside within me and already know all my thoughts. This is my plea before your holy presence, you who are master of all arts: I have given my body and its core essence to you for all time. I stand without being in my own control. Therefore, whatever you do to me, whatever the act, you may do it. You awakened me from sleep and granted me the bliss of truth.
commentary: True surrender is the complete emptying of personal will. Vallalar expresses a state of perfect trust where he no longer needs to ask for anything, because God is already within him and knows his every thought. By giving up control over himself, he invites God to act through him in any way God chooses.

translit: maṉceytu koṇṭacaṉ mārkkattil iṅkē vāṉceytu koṇṭatu nāṉceytu koṇṭēṉ muṉceytu koṇṭatum iṅṅaṉaṅ kaṇṭīr mūvakai yāmuṭal ātiyai numatu poṉceytu koṇṭa potuviṉil āṭum poṉṉaṭi kāṇap poruntik koṭuttēṉ eṉceytu koṇṭālum ceytukoḷ kiṟpīr eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: Here in the Sanmarkkam that the world has made enduring, what heaven has done, I too have done. You have seen that what I did before was also just like this. I have fittingly given the three, my body and all that is mine, to behold your golden feet that dance in the golden Common Space. Whatever you make of me, you may do it. You awakened me from sleep and granted me the bliss of truth.
commentary: This act of self-surrender is understood as an alignment with the universal divine order. He offers the three things he has offered throughout this decade, his body, his possessions and his soul, for the sole purpose of beholding God's dance in the potu, the universal common space open to all.

translit: teyvaṅkaḷ palapala cintaicey vārum cērkati palapala ceppukiṉ ṟārum poyvanta kalaipala pukaṉṟiṭu vārum poyccama yātiyai meccukiṉ ṟārum meyvanta tiruvaruḷ viḷakkamoṉ ṟillār mēlviḷai vaṟikilar vīṇkaḻik kiṉṟār eyvanta tuṉpoḻit tavarkkaṟi varuḷvīr eṉaippaḷḷi eḻuppimey iṉpantan tīrē.
translation: There are those who contemplate many different gods, and those who speak of many different paths to salvation, and those who teach many arts that come from falsehood, and those who praise false religions and the like. They are without the one illumination of sacred grace that comes from truth. Not knowing the future consequences, they waste their time. You must end the suffering that has befallen them and graciously grant them wisdom. You have awakened me from my slumber and given me the bliss of truth.
commentary: Vallalar names plainly those who worship many gods, who preach many different goals, who teach arts born of falsehood, and who praise the false religions. Lacking the one light of grace that comes from truth, they do not see what follows and waste their lives. Having named this truth, he turns to God in compassion and asks Him to end their suffering and grant them true knowledge.
NOTES
Note 325

tamil: உகத்து - உகந்து என்பதன் வலித்தல் விகாரம் - முதற்பதிப்பு.
translit: ukattu - ukantu eṉpataṉ valittal vikāram - mutaṟpatippu.
translation: ukattu — the hardened form (valittal vikāram) of ukantu; first edition.
Note 326

translit: camukam - ca. mu. ka. patippu.
translation: camukam — reading of the S. Mu. Ka. Edition.

sections.title: Hymn to the Power of Consciousness

tamil: சோதிக் கொடியே ஆனந்த சொருபக் கொடியே சோதிஉருப்
ஆதிக் கொடியே உலகுகட்டி ஆளுங் கொடியே சன்மார்க்க
நீதிக் கொடியே சிவகாம நிமலக் கொடியே அருளுகவே.
translit: cōtik koṭiyē āṉanta corupak koṭiyē cōtiurup pātik koṭiyē cōtivalap pākak koṭiyēeṉaiīṉṟa ātik koṭiyē ulakukaṭṭi āḷuṅ koṭiyē caṉmārkka nītik koṭiyē civakāma nimalak koṭiyē aruḷukavē.
translation: O vine of light, vine whose very form is bliss, vine who is half of the luminous form, vine on the right side of the Light! O primordial vine who gave birth to me, vine who establishes and rules the worlds! O vine of the Sanmarkkam's law, pure vine of Sivakāma, grant your grace.
commentary: The divine feminine power is addressed as a "vine" (koṭi), an image suggesting grace, life, and interconnectedness. She is at once the light of consciousness, the bliss of existence, and the creative partner who forms half of the divine. As Sivakāma ("Beloved of Siva"), she is in perfect union with the transcendent, and as the "vine of the Sanmarkkam's law," she is the guiding principle of the True Path itself.

tamil: பொருணற் கொடியே மாற்றுயர்ந்த பொன்னங் கொடியே போதாந்த
வருணக் கொடியே எல்லாஞ்செய் வல்லார் இடஞ்சேர் மணிக்கொடியே
தருணக் கொடியே என்தன்னைக் தாங்கி ஓங்குந் தனிக்கொடியே
கருணைக் கொடியே ஞானசிவ காமக் கொடியே அருளுகவே.
translit: poruṇaṟ koṭiyē māṟṟuyarnta poṉṉaṅ koṭiyē pōtānta varuṇak koṭiyē ellāñcey vallār iṭañcēr maṇikkoṭiyē taruṇak koṭiyē eṉtaṉṉaik tāṅki ōṅkun taṉikkoṭiyē karuṇaik koṭiyē ñāṉaciva kāmak koṭiyē aruḷukavē.
translation: O vine of true substance, golden vine of the highest purity! O vine of the hue of Bōdhānta, jeweled vine who has joined the All-Powerful One! O youthful vine, unique vine who supports and uplifts me! O vine of compassion, vine of wisdom-filled divine love, grant your grace.
commentary: The divine feminine is both the absolute reality and a personal protector. She is described as being the color of Bōdhānta (a state of awareness beyond ordinary consciousness), yet is also the compassionate vine that personally supports and uplifts the devotee.

tamil: நீட்டுக் கொடியே சன்மார்க்க நீதிக் கொடியே சிவகீதப்
நாட்டுக் கொடியே எனைஈன்ற ஞானக் கொடியே என்னுறவாம்
கூட்டுக் கொடியே சிவகாமக் கொடியே அடியேற் கருளுகவே .
translit: nīṭṭuk koṭiyē caṉmārkka nītik koṭiyē civakītap pāṭṭuk koṭiyē iṟaivarvalap pākak koṭiyēparanāta nāṭṭuk koṭiyē eṉaiīṉṟa ñāṉak koṭiyē eṉṉuṟavām kūṭṭuk koṭiyē civakāmak koṭiyē aṭiyēṟ karuḷukavē .
translation: O unfurled banner, vine of the Sanmarkkam's law! O vine who is the song of the Siva Gīta, vine on the right side of the Lord! O vine from the land of Paranāda, vine of wisdom who gave birth to me! O vine who is my intimate companion, vine of divine love, grant grace to me, your devotee.
commentary: Here, the divine feminine is the source of all sacred expression: she is the law of Sanmarkkam, the very song of scripture (Siva Gīta), and she originates from the land of Paranāda (the transcendent sound). Yet for all this cosmic status, her most important role is as an intimate companion to the soul.

tamil: மாலக் கொடியேன் குற்றமெலாம் மன்னித் தருளி மரணமெனும்
சாலக் கொடியை ஒடித்தெனக்குட் சார்ந்து விளங்கும் தவக்கொடியே
காலக் கருவைக் கடந்தொளிர்வான் கருவும் கடந்து வயங்குகின்ற
கோலக் கொடியே சிவஞானக் கொடியே அடியேற் கருளுகவே.
translit: mālak koṭiyēṉ kuṟṟamelām maṉṉit taruḷi maraṇameṉum cālak koṭiyai oṭitteṉakkuṭ cārntu viḷaṅkum tavakkoṭiyē kālak karuvaik kaṭantoḷirvāṉ karuvum kaṭantu vayaṅkukiṉṟa kōlak koṭiyē civañāṉak koṭiyē aṭiyēṟ karuḷukavē.
translation: O vine of spiritual discipline, you forgave the faults of this vine of delusion that I am, shattered the terrible vine of death, and now reside shining within me! O beautiful vine, you flourish, having transcended the seed of time and even the seed of the heavens! O vine of the wisdom of Siva, grant grace to me, your devotee.
commentary: The relationship with the divine feminine power changes everything. She is an active force that forgives, breaks death itself, and takes up residence within the devotee. By her grace the soul passes beyond time and attains the wisdom of the deathless life.

tamil: நாடாக் கொடிய மனம்அடக்கி நல்ல மனத்தைக் கனிவித்துப்
பாடாப் பிழையைப் பொறுத்தெனக்கும் பதம்ஈந் தாண்ட பதிக்கொடியே
தேடாக் கரும சித்திஎலாம் திகழத் தயவால் தெரிவித்த
கோடாக் கொடியே சிவதருமக் கொடியே அடியேற் கருளுகவே.
translit: nāṭāk koṭiya maṉamaṭakki nalla maṉattaik kaṉivittup pāṭāp piḻaiyaip poṟutteṉakkum patamīn tāṇṭa patikkoṭiyē tēṭāk karuma cittielām tikaḻat tayavāl terivitta kōṭāk koṭiyē civatarumak koṭiyē aṭiyēṟ karuḷukavē.
translation: O vine of the Lord, you subdued my wicked mind that does not seek you, made my good mind ripen, forgave the fault of my unsung praise, and gave me a spiritual state, ruling over me. O unbending vine, you graciously revealed all the unsought siddhis in their full splendor. O vine of the righteous path of Siva, grant your grace to me, your devotee.
commentary: Grace accomplishes what our own effort cannot: it tames the wandering mind and ripens our good intentions. It then bestows spiritual gifts, or siddhis (spiritual accomplishments), out of its own spontaneous generosity.

tamil: மணங்கொள் கொடிப்பூ முதல்நான்கு வகைப்பூ வடிவுள் வயங்குகின்ற
வணங்கொள் கொடியே ஐம்பூவும் மலிய மலர்ந்த வான்கொடியே
கணங்கொள் யோக சித்திஎலாம் காட்டுங் கொடியே கலங்காத
குணங்கொள் கொடியே சிவபோகக் கொடியே அடியேற் கருளுகவே.
translit: maṇaṅkoḷ koṭippū mutalnāṉku vakaippū vaṭivuḷ vayaṅkukiṉṟa vaṇaṅkoḷ koṭiyē aimpūvum maliya malarnta vāṉkoṭiyē kaṇaṅkoḷ yōka cittielām kāṭṭuṅ koṭiyē kalaṅkāta kuṇaṅkoḷ koṭiyē civapōkak koṭiyē aṭiyēṟ karuḷukavē.
translation: O revered flag, shining within the forms of the four types of flowers, beginning with fragrant flowers on vines! O celestial flag that has blossomed abundantly as the five great elements! O flag that reveals all the yogic powers of the celestial hosts! O flag of unwavering character! O flag of the blissful experience of Siva! Please grant your grace to me, your humble servant.
commentary: The divine is present in all of creation, from the flowers on a vine to the five great elements that make up the cosmos. By recognizing this presence in the world around us, we can access higher states of awareness and blissful union with God.

tamil: புலங்கொள் கொடிய மனம்போன போக்கில் போகா தெனைமீட்டு
நலங்கொள் கருணைச் சன்மார்க்க நாட்டில் விடுத்த நற்கொடியே
வலங்கொள் ஞான சித்திஎலாம் வயங்க விளங்கு மணிமன்றில்
குலங்கொள் கொடியே மெய்ஞ்ஞானக் கொடியே அடியேற் கருளுகவே.
translit: pulaṅkoḷ koṭiya maṉampōṉa pōkkil pōkā teṉaimīṭṭu nalaṅkoḷ karuṇaic caṉmārkka nāṭṭil viṭutta naṟkoṭiyē valaṅkoḷ ñāṉa cittielām vayaṅka viḷaṅku maṇimaṉṟil kulaṅkoḷ koṭiyē meyññāṉak koṭiyē aṭiyēṟ karuḷukavē.
translation: O good flag that rescued me from following the path of my cruel, sense-driven mind and dispatched me to the nation of benevolent, grace-filled Sanmarkkam! O noble flag in the Hall of Gems where all the victorious powers of wisdom shine radiantly! O flag of true wisdom! Please grant your grace to me, your humble servant.
commentary: The divine actively rescues us from being lost in the endless chase of sensory desires. It gently but firmly places us back on the benevolent path of Sanmarkkam, the way of true wisdom and universal compassion.

tamil: வெறிக்கும் சமயக் குழியில்விழ விரைந்தேன் தன்னை விழாதவகை
மறிக்கும் ஒருபே ரறிவளித்த வள்ளற் கொடியே மனக்கொடியைச்
செறிக்கும் பெரியர் உளத்தோங்கும் தெய்வக் கொடியே சிவஞானம்
குறிக்கும் கொடியே ஆனந்தக் கொடியே அடியேற் கருளுகவே.
translit: veṟikkum camayak kuḻiyilviḻa viraintēṉ taṉṉai viḻātavakai maṟikkum orupē raṟivaḷitta vaḷḷaṟ koṭiyē maṉakkoṭiyaic ceṟikkum periyar uḷattōṅkum teyvak koṭiyē civañāṉam kuṟikkum koṭiyē āṉantak koṭiyē aṭiyēṟ karuḷukavē.
translation: O generous flag that gave me the great intelligence to prevent myself from falling when I was rushing to fall into the pit of maddening religions! O divine flag that soars in the hearts of the great ones who restrain the vine of the mind! O flag that signifies the wisdom of Siva! O flag of bliss! Please grant your grace to me, your humble servant.
commentary: Vallalar thanks the Mother for holding him back from the pit of the religions, which madden the mind, just as he was rushing to fall into it. He gives the credit to the great intelligence she gave him. The same Power soars in the hearts of the great who have restrained the mind, and points the way to the wisdom of Siva.

tamil: கடுத்த விடர்வன் பயம்கவலை எல்லாம் தவிர்த்துக் கருத்துள்ளே
அடுத்த கொடியே அருளமுதம் அளித்தென் தனைமெய் அருட்கரத்தால்
எடுத்த கொடியே சித்திஎலாம் இந்தா மகனே என்றெனக்கே
கொடுத்த கொடியே ஆனந்தக் கொடியே அடியேற் கருளுகவே.
translit: kaṭutta viṭarvaṉ payamkavalai ellām tavirttuk karuttuḷḷē aṭutta koṭiyē aruḷamutam aḷitteṉ taṉaimey aruṭkarattāl eṭutta koṭiyē cittielām intā makaṉē eṉṟeṉakkē koṭutta koṭiyē āṉantak koṭiyē aṭiyēṟ karuḷukavē.
translation: O flag that removed all harsh suffering, great fear, and anxiety, and drew near within my consciousness! O flag that gave me the nectar of graceand lifted me up with your true hand of grace! O flag that gave all the powers to me, saying, "Here, my son, take them!" O flag of bliss! Please grant your grace to me, your humble servant.
commentary: Divine grace is an intimate, parental love that actively cares for the soul. Grace removes all fear and suffering, offers spiritual nourishment (arul amudam, the nectar of grace), and lifts the devotee like a child. In a moment of deep tenderness, God bestows all spiritual powers (siddhis) with the words, "Here, my son, take them."

tamil: ஏட்டைத் தவிர்த்தென் எண்ணமெலாம் எய்த ஒளிதந் தியான்வனைந்த
பாட்டைப் புனைந்து பரிசளித்த பரம ஞானப் பதிக்கொடியே
கோட்டைக் கொடியே ஆனந்தக் கொடியே அடியேற் கருளுகவே.
translit: ēṭṭait tavirtteṉ eṇṇamelām eyta oḷitan tiyāṉvaṉainta pāṭṭaip puṉaintu paricaḷitta parama ñāṉap patikkoṭiyē tēṭṭait taṉippēr aruṭceṅkōl celuttumcutta caṉmārkkak kōṭṭaik koṭiyē āṉantak koṭiyē aṭiyēṟ karuḷukavē.
translation: O vine of the supreme abode of wisdom, you removed my want, gave me the light to achieve everything I conceived, adorned the songs I composed, and gave me a reward! O flag on the fortress of Suddha Sanmarkkam, which wields the unique, great scepter of grace, the ultimate attainment! O flag of bliss! Please grant your grace to me, your humble servant.
commentary: Grace removes the devotee's want and weariness and gives him an inner light by which every aim he conceived is fulfilled. It even adorns his songs and rewards him for them. This is Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure True Path), a fortress where the only law is the 'scepter of grace', the one attainment worth seeking.
NOTES

translit: iṭappākak koṭiyē - pi. irā. patippu.
translation: iṭappākak koṭiyē — reading of the P. Irā. edition. (Covers the reference marks 352 and 353.)

translit: tēṭiya tuṇṭu niṉaturu vuṇmai teḷintiṭac ciṟituniṉ ṉuṭaṉē ūṭiya tuṇṭu piṟartamai aṭuttē uraittatum uvantatum uṇṭō āṭiya pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ ampalat tarumperuñ cōti kūṭiya niṉṉaip pirikilēṉ pirivaik kūṟavuṅ kūcumeṉ nāvē.
translation: I have sought the truth of your form. To gain clarity, I have even feigned a quarrel with you. But have I ever approached others, spoken with them, or delighted in them? Your dancing foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. O Great, Rare Jothi of the Ambalam! Having united with you, I cannot be separated. My tongue recoils even from speaking of separation.
commentary: The devotee's love for God is so all-consuming that the very idea of separation is unspeakable. Vallalar uses the language of human love, admitting to feigning small quarrels to draw closer, but insists he has never once looked to another for comfort. He feels united with the divine light, the "Great, Rare Jothi of the Ambalam" (the sacred expanse of consciousness), and this union is so fundamental to his being that his tongue cannot even form the word "separation."

translit: maṭampuri maṉattāṟ kalaṅkiya tuṇṭu vaḷḷalē niṉtiru varavuk kiṭampuri ciṟiyēṉ kalaṅkiṉēṉ eṉiṉum iṟaiyumvē ṟeṇṇiya tuṇṭō naṭampuri pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ nāṉceyum vakaiyiṉi naṉṟē tiṭampurin taruḷik kāttiṭal vēṇṭum ciṟitum nāṉ poṟukkalēṉ civaṉē.
translation: My foolish mind has caused me agitation, it is true. O Patron, though I, this lowly one, make a place for your sacred arrival, I have been agitated. Even so, have I ever, even for an instant, thought of another? Your dancing foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. From now on, the way I act will indeed be good. You must grant me firmness and protect me with grace. I cannot bear this any longer, not even for a moment, O Sivam!
commentary: Despite the mind's foolishness and agitation, the soul's devotion to God has remained absolute. This is a deeply human prayer that acknowledges personal weakness but offers it as the very reason for complete surrender. The devotee begs Sivam (God, the Auspicious One) for the "firmness" and protection to keep that steady focus, because the internal struggle has become too much to bear alone.

translit: nīkkiya maṉampiṉ aṭutteṉaik kalakki niṉṟatē aṉṟiniṉ aḷavil nōkkiya nōkkam piṟaviṭa yattē nōkkiya tiṟaiyum iṅkuṇṭō tūkkiya pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ tuyariṉip poṟukkalēṉ ciṟitum tēkkiya kaḷippil ciṟappavan teṉṉait teḷivittal niṉkaṭaṉ civaṉē.
translation: The mind I had pushed away returned to agitate me. Other than that, has the gaze I fixed upon you ever, even for an instant, turned toward other worldly matters? Your raised foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. I can no longer bear this sorrow, not even for a moment. It is your duty, O Sivam, to come in glorious, overflowing bliss and grant me clarity.
commentary: The source of his suffering is the restless mind, which pulls him away from a state of peace. Yet, he affirms that his inner focus, his spiritual gaze, has remained fixed on God without being distracted by worldly desires. The pain of this internal conflict has become unbearable, leading him to make a bold and intimate demand: it is now God's duty to intervene with bliss and grant him the clarity he desperately needs.

translit: īṉṟanaṟ ṟāyun tantaiyum kuruvum eṉṉuyirk kiṉpamum potuvil āṉṟameyp poruḷē eṉṟiruk kiṉṟēṉ aṉṟivē ṟeṇṇiya tuṇṭō ūṉṟiya pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ uṟukaṇiṅ kāṟṟalēṉ ciṟitum tōṉṟieṉ uḷattē mayakkelān tavirttut naṉṟaruḷ purivatuṉ kaṭaṉē.
translation: I hold you to be the good mother who bore me, my father, my guru, the bliss of my own life, and the perfected True Substance in the Common Expanse. Have I ever thought otherwise? Your firmly planted foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. I cannot bear this suffering here, not even for a moment. It is your duty to appear within my heart, dispel all my confusion, and bestow your good grace.
commentary: God is the sum of all essential relationships: mother, father, guru (spiritual teacher), and the very joy of his life. Vallalar sees God as the single True Substance present in the Common Expanse, accessible to all. Having placed his entire existence in God, the current feeling of confusion and distance is unendurable. He again insists that it is God’s personal duty to appear in his heart and save him.

translit: māyaiyāṟ kalaṅki varuntiya pōtum vaḷḷaluṉ taṉṉaiyē matittuṉ cāyaiyāppiṟaraip pārttatē allāl talaivavēṟeṇṇiya tuṇṭō tūyapoṟ pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ tuyariṉic ciṟitumiṅ kāṟṟēṉ nāyakā eṉatu mayakkelām tavirttē naṉṟaruḷ purivatuṉ kaṭaṉē.
translation: Even when I was agitated and suffered because of maya, O Patron, I esteemed only you and saw others merely as your shadow. Beyond that, O Master, have I ever thought differently? Your pure golden foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. I can no longer bear this sorrow here, not even for a moment. O Lord, it is your duty to dispel all my confusion and grant your good grace.
commentary: Even when lost in suffering caused by maya (the cosmic power of illusion), his devotion remained unshaken. In a striking statement of his perception, he says that he saw all other beings and things as mere shadows of the one Divine reality. Having held this singular focus, he feels he can no longer bear his sorrow and calls upon God to fulfill his duty by dispelling the illusion and bestowing grace.

translit: vaṇṇam vēṟeṉiṉum vaṭivuvē ṟeṉiṉum maṉṉiya uṇmai oṉṟeṉṟē eṇṇiya tallāl caccitā ṉantat tiṟaiyumvē ṟeṇṇiya tuṇṭō aṇṇalniṉ pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ añariṉic ciṟitumiṅ kāṟṟēṉ tiṇṇamē niṉmēl āṇaieṉ taṉṉait teḷivittuk kāppatuṉ kaṭaṉē.
translation: Though colors differ and forms differ, I have only ever thought that the enduring Reality is one. Have I ever thought, even slightly, of anything other than Being-Consciousness-Bliss? Noble Lord, Your foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. I can no longer bear even a little of this anguish here. Truly, I swear upon You: it is Your duty to enlighten me and protect me.
commentary: The poet declares his core insight: behind all the apparent differences in color and form, the underlying Reality is one. He has always understood God to be Sacchidananda (Being-Consciousness-Bliss). The anguish he feels comes from the gap between this knowledge and his direct experience. In a final, desperate appeal, he makes an oath upon God, framing it as God's undeniable duty to provide the enlightenment that will save him.

translit: ūṭalcey matamum camayamum ivaṟṟil uṟṟakaṟ paṉaikaḷum tavirntēṉ vāṭalcey maṉattāl kalaṅkiṉēṉ eṉiṉum maṉṟiṉai maṟantatiṅ kuṇṭō āṭalcey pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ aiyavō ciṟitumiṅ kāṟṟēṉ pāṭalcey kiṉṟēṉ paṭikkiṉṟēṉ eṉakkup parintaruḷ purivatuṉ kaṭaṉē.
translation: I have renounced the quarreling religions and creeds, and the fabrications associated with them. Though I was agitated by a withered mind, have I ever forgotten the Hall here? Your dancing foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. Alas, I can no longer bear even a little of this. I am composing songs, I am reading them; it is Your duty to take pity on me and grant me grace.
commentary: Vallalar declares that he has left behind the quarrelling religions and creeds, and all the fabrications that belong to them. For him the true site of worship is the Maṉṟam, the hall where God's dance unfolds. Even as his mind suffers, he insists he has never forgotten it. His songs themselves become part of his plea for God's mercy.

translit: uḷḷatē uḷḷa tiraṇṭilai ellām oruciva mayameṉa uṇarntēṉ kaḷḷanēr maṉattāl kalaṅkiṉēṉ eṉiṉum karuttayal karutiya tuṇṭō vaḷḷaluṉ pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ mayakkiṉic ciṟitumiṅ kāṟṟēṉ teḷḷamu taruḷi mayakkelām tavirttē teḷivittal niṉkaṭaṉ civaṉē.
translation: I have realized that what exists is all that exists, that there are not two, and that everything is pervaded by the one Sivam. Though I was agitated by a deceitful mind, have I ever entertained a different thought? Bountiful Lord, Your foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. I can no longer bear even a little of this confusion. O Sivan, it is Your duty to grant me the clear nectar, remove all my confusion, and enlighten me.
commentary: This is a powerful declaration of non-duality: nothing exists except the one divine being, Sivam. Vallalar acknowledges that his mind can still be treacherous and cause him to forget this, but his underlying conviction is absolute. He frames his request as a plea and as a logical necessity: it is God's duty to grant the clarity that will end the confusion caused by the mind.

translit: emmata nilaiyum niṉṉaruḷ nilaiyil ilaṅkutal aṟintaṉaṉ ellām cammatam ākkik koḷkiṉṟēṉ allāl taṉittuvē ṟeṇṇiya tuṇṭō cemmaluṉ pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ ciṟitumiṅ kiṉittuyar āṟṟēṉ immatik kaṭiyēṉ kuṟittavā ṟuḷḷa tiyaṟṟuva tuṉkaṭaṉ entāy.
translation: I have come to know that the state of every religion shines within the state of Your grace. I accept them all; have I ever thought of them as separate and different? Perfect Lord, Your foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. I can no longer bear even a little sorrow here. My Father, it is Your duty to accomplish what I, this devotee, have intended with this mind.
commentary: This verse expresses a radical and harmonious universalism. All religions, in their own way, are seen as reflecting the singular light of God's grace. Rather than rejecting other paths, Vallalar accepts them all as part of a greater truth. His personal devotion is so firm that he feels he has the right to ask God to fulfill his spiritual intentions.

translit: akampuṟam maṟṟai akappuṟam puṟattē aṭuttiṭum puṟappuṟam nāṉkil ikantatum ilaiōr ēkatē cattāl iṟaiyumiṅ keṇṇiya tuṇṭō ukantaniṉ pātam aṟiyanāṉ aṟiyēṉ uṟukaṇiṅ kiṉicciṟi tuntāṉ ikampeṟal āṟṟēṉ mayakkelām tavirttiṅ keṉṉaiāṇ ṭaruḷva tuṉkaṭaṉē.
translation: In the four realms of the inner, the outer, the inner-outer, and the adjoining outer-outer, I have not transgressed, nor have I ever thought, even in part, of anything else. Your beloved foot is my witness: I have known no such thing. I can no longer bear to remain in this world with even a little of this intense suffering. It is Your duty to remove all confusion and take me as Your own in grace.
commentary: Using terms for every level of experience (inner, outer, and the blends between them), Vallalar states that his devotion has been total and all-encompassing. Having dedicated his entire being to God, he finds his current state of suffering in the world unbearable. The prayer culminates in the ultimate request: for God to end his confusion and fully claim him, bringing an end to the feeling of separation.
NOTES
Note 244

translit: cāyaiyāṟ 245. talaivareṉ - paṭivēṟupāṭukaḷ. ā. pā.
translation: cāyaiyāṟ; 245. talaivareṉ — variant readings. Ā. Pā. edition.
