translit: kaḷḷattai ellām kaṭakkaviṭṭēṉ niṉaruḷām veḷḷattai ellām mika:uṇṭēṉ - uḷḷattē kāṇāta kāṭcielām kāṇkiṉṟēṉ ōṅkumaṉṟa vāṇā niṉakkaṭimai vāyttu.
translation: I have let all falsehood pass me by; I have drunk deeply from the flood of Your grace. In my heart I see all sights previously unseen, O Life of the high Hall, now that I am blessed to be Your servant.
commentary: By letting go of all illusion and immersing himself in divine grace, the devotee gains a new kind of sight. He now perceives spiritual realities within his own heart that were previously hidden from view. This inner vision is a direct result of becoming a servant to God, who is the life-force of the supreme space of consciousness.

translit: kālaiyilē niṉṟaṉṉaik kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ caṉmārkkac cālaiyilē iṉpam taḻaikkiṉṟēṉ - ñālamicaic cākā varampeṟṟēṉ tattuvattiṉ mēlnaṭikkum ēkā niṉakkaṭimai ēṟṟu.
translation: In the morning, I saw You. On the path of Sanmarkkam, I flourish in bliss. On this earth, I have received the boon of deathlessness, O Singular One who dances above the principles, having accepted servitude to You.
commentary: The "morning" signifies a spiritual awakening, a moment of direct realization of God. This awakening places him on the Sanmarkkam (the True Path), where the way itself is one of flourishing joy. The final fruit of this path is the boon of deathlessness, achieved by serving the one supreme reality that exists beyond all cosmic principles.

translit: mūvarkaḷum ceyya muṭiyā muṭipellām yāvarkaḷuṅ kāṇa eṉakkaḷittāy - mēvukaṭai nāykkut tavicaḷittu naṉmuṭiyum cūṭṭutalen tāykkut taṉiiyaṟkai tāṉ.
translation: You have granted to me, for all to see, every attainment that even the Three could not achieve. Granting a throne to a lowly dog that approaches and placing a fine crown on it is the unique nature of my Mother.
commentary: God's grace can bestow spiritual states that are beyond the reach of even the highest deities, traditionally known as the Three (Brahma, Vishnu, and Siva). Vallalar uses the humble image of a lowly dog being given a crown and a throne to show that divine grace is not earned by status or power. The divine Mother's nature is to elevate anyone who comes to Her, no matter how insignificant they may seem.

translit: koḷḷaieṉa iṉpam koṭuttāy niṉatucelvap piḷḷaieṉa eṟkup peyariṭṭāy - teḷḷamutam tantāy camaracacaṉ mārkkacaṅkat tēvaittāy entāy karuṇai itu.
translation: You gave bliss in abundance. You named me Your cherished child. You gave me clear ambrosia. You placed me in the Samarasa Sanmarkka Sangam. My Father, such is Your compassion.
commentary: The gifts of God's compassion are both personal and communal. Vallalar receives inner bliss, spiritual sustenance ('clear ambrosia'), and a new identity as God's child. Grace also gives him his place in the Samarasa Sanmarkka Sangam, the fellowship where all can follow the True Path of universal harmony.

translit: kaṇṭēṉ kaḷittēṉ karuṇait tiruamutam uṇṭēṉ uyarnilaimēl ōṅkukiṉṟēṉ - koṇṭēṉ aḻiyāt tiruuruvam accōeñ ñāṉṟum aḻiyācciṟ ṟampalattē yāṉ.
translation: I saw. I rejoiced. I drank the sacred ambrosia of grace. I am rising to the highest state. I have received a deathless, sacred form. Ah! I am in the eternally imperishable Chitrambalam.
commentary: The spiritual path culminates in a complete transformation, leading to a "deathless, sacred form" and a permanent state within divine consciousness. The short, direct statements, "I saw. I rejoiced.", express the certainty of this experience. He is now situated in Chitrambalam, the "hall of consciousness," the eternal, imperishable space of God's own being.

translit: pārttēṉ paṇintēṉ paḻicciṉēṉ meyppuḷakam pōrttēṉeṉ uḷḷamelām pūrittēṉ - ārttēniṉ ṟāṭukiṉṟēṉ pāṭukiṉṟēṉ aṉpuruvā ṉēṉaruḷai nāṭukiṉṟēṉ ciṟcapaiyai nāṉ.
translation: I saw, I bowed, I praised. My body was cloaked in blissful tremors; my whole being swelled with joy. Roaring, I stand and dance; I sing. I have become the very form of love. I seek Grace; I seek the Chit Sabhai.
commentary: The encounter with God is an overwhelming, ecstatic experience that consumes the whole person. It bursts forth in physical expression: blissful tremors, dancing, and singing. The transformation is so complete that he has "become the very form of love" itself, and his seeking continues to be for that final reality, the Chit Sabhai or Hall of Consciousness.

translit: eṇṇukiṉṟēṉ eṇṇaṅkaḷ ellām tarukiṉṟāṉ uṇṇukiṉṟēṉ uṇṇa:uṇṇa ūṭṭukiṉṟāṉ - naṇṇutiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭañcey kiṉṟāṉeṉ kuṟṟam palapoṟuttuk koṇṭu.
translation: I contemplate, and He gives me all thoughts. I partake, and as I continue to partake, He keeps feeding me. He performs His sacred dance in the holy Chitrambalam that I approach, having forgiven my many faults.
commentary: After union, the sense of being a separate self who thinks and acts disappears. God becomes the source of all thought and all nourishment. This state is granted by a grace that forgives all faults, allowing one to approach the divine dance within the holy Chitrambalam.

translit: koṇṭāṉ aṭimai kuṟiyāṉ piḻaioṉṟum kaṇṭāṉkaḷittāṉ kalantiruntāṉ - paṇṭāya nāṉmaṟaiyum ākamamum nāṭun tiruppotuvil vāṉmayattāṉ eṉṉai makiḻntu.
translation: He who is the very form of space, in the sacred common hall sought by the ancient Vedas and Agamas, delightedly took me as His servant. He marks no fault. He saw me, rejoiced, and remained mingled with me.
commentary: The ultimate reality, sought even by the ancient Vedas and Agamas, is not a judgmental being. It is an infinite, open space that accepts the soul completely, without finding any fault. The union is joyful for God as well, who embraces and merges with the individual, making them one.

translit: kaṇṭēṉ kaḷittēṉ karuṇait tiruamutam uṇṭēṉ aḻiyā urampeṟṟēṉ - paṇṭē eṉaiuvantu koṇṭāṉ eḻilñāṉa maṉṟam taṉaiuvantu koṇṭāṉ taṉai.
translation: I saw and I rejoiced; I partook of the sacred nectar of compassion and gained undying strength. I saw Him: the one who lovingly made the beautiful Hall of Wisdom His own, the one who lovingly made me His own long ago.
commentary: The experience of seeing God is like drinking a nectar of compassion that grants immortal strength. It leads to a realization: God resides in the Jñāna Maṉṟam (the Hall of Wisdom within) and has also lovingly considered the soul His own from the very beginning. The search becomes the discovery of a love that was always there.

translit: tātaiyām eṉṉuṭaiya tāyāmeṉ caṟkuruvām mētaiyām iṉpa viḷaivumām - ōtu kuṇavāḷaṉ tillaiaruṭ kūttaṉ umaiyāḷ maṇavāḷaṉ pāta malar.
translation: The lotus feet of the celebrated virtuous one, the dancer of grace in Tillai, the husband of Uma, are my father, my mother, my true guru, my wisdom, and the very fruition of bliss.
commentary: The divine presence, symbolized by the "lotus feet" of God, is the complete and sole source of existence. It is one's true father and mother, the ultimate teacher (guru), the source of all wisdom, and the final experience of bliss. All relationships and goals find their fulfillment in God, here described with the traditional names of the dancer in Tillai and husband of Uma.

translit: tiruvāmeṉ teyvamām teḷḷamuta ñāṉak kuruvām eṉaikkākkum kōvām - paruvaraiyiṉ tēppiḷḷai yāmem civakāma vallimakiḻ māppiḷḷai pāta malar.
translation: They are wealth, my God, my clear, nectar-like Guru of wisdom, the King who protects me, the flower-like feet of the Bridegroom who delights our Sivakama Valli, the divine child of the great mountain.
commentary: God's feet are the source of all value and safety. They represent spiritual wealth, a personal deity, a guru who provides the nectar of wisdom (gnana), and a king who offers protection. This divine protector is Siva, the bridegroom who brings joy to his consort, Sivakama Valli, who is herself the daughter of the great mountain, Himalaya.

translit: eṉaṟivām eṉaṟiviṉ iṉpamām eṉṉaṟiviṉ taṉaṟivām uṇmait taṉinilaiyām - maṉṉukoṭic cēlaiiṭṭāṉ vāḻac civakāma cuntariyai mālaiiṭṭāṉ pātamalar.
translation: They are my awareness, the bliss of my awareness, the self-awareness within my awareness, the true and solitary state: the flower-like feet of the one who garlanded Sivakama Sundari so that Kama, who bears the enduring fish banner, might live again.
commentary: The divine feet are external supports and the very essence of our inner world. They are the awareness we possess, the joy found within that awareness, and the self-aware principle that observes it all. This is the final, true state of being, embodied by the God who unites with his beloved consort, Sivakama Sundari.

translation: ōṅkumaṟai — variant reading; Ā. Pā. edition.

Note 266

translit: varam - paṭivēṟupāṭu. ā. pā.
translation: varam — variant reading; Ā. Pā. edition.

translit: mālilē mayaṅki maṇṇilē anitta vāḻvilē varavilē malañcār tōlilē ācai vaittuvīṇ poḻutu tolaikkiṉṟār tolaikkanāṉ uṉatu kālilē ācai vaittaṉaṉ nīyum kaṉaviṉum naṉaviṉum eṉainiṉ pālilē vaittāy eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: Deluded by desire, they waste their time on this earth, on this impermanent life, on their possessions, placing their hopes on this skin full of impurities. While they waste away, I have placed my desire on Your feet. And You, in both dream and waking, have kept me by Your side. This is enough for me. The penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: This verse draws a sharp contrast between two ways of life. Most people waste their energy on fleeting things: status, possessions, and the physical body. The speaker has made a different choice, placing all hope and desire on God's feet alone. In return, God has kept the devotee close, a reward so great that it feels like the successful culmination of a lifetime of spiritual effort.

translit: matattilē camaya vaḻakkilē māyai maruṭṭilē iruṭṭilē maṟavāk katattilē maṉattai vaittuvīṇ poḻutu kaḻikkiṉṟār kaḻikkanāṉ uṉpūm patattilē maṉattai vaittaṉaṉ nīyum parinteṉai aḻivilā nalla patattilē vaittāy eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: They waste their time, placing their minds in religious dogma, in sectarian customs, in the confusion of māyā, in darkness, and in unforgetting anger. While they waste away, I have placed my mind on Your flower-like feet. And You, out of compassion, have placed me in a good, indestructible state. This is enough for me. The penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: The distractions of the world are more than material; they are also intellectual and emotional. People get lost in rigid dogmas, sectarian fights, anger, and the general confusion of māyā (the illusion of the world). By consciously rejecting these and focusing only on God's feet, the devotee has been granted a state of being that is permanent and peaceful, a gift born of divine compassion.

translit: kulattilē camayak kuḻiyilē narakak kuḻiyilē kumaintuvīṇ poḻutu nilattilē pōkki mayaṅkiē māntu niṟkiṉṟār niṟkanāṉ uvantu valattilē niṉatu vacattilē niṉṟēṉ makiḻntunī eṉuḷam eṉumam palattilē niṉṟāy eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: Suffering in the pit of caste, the pit of religion, the pit of hell, they waste their time on this earth, standing deluded and deceived. While they stand there, I have joyfully stood within Your power, under Your control. You, in turn, have joyfully stood in the sacred hall that is my heart. This is enough for me. The penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: Caste, religion and hell are named here together as pits in which people suffer and waste their lives on this earth. Vallalar steps out of all of them by standing joyfully in God's power alone. The result is a beautiful reversal: God now stands within Vallalar's own heart, making it the sacred hall (ambalam).

translit: kūṭavum piṉṉē piriyavum cārnta koḻunarum makaḷirum nāṇa nīṭaeṉ uḷattē kalantukoṇ ṭeṉṟum nīṅkiṭā tiruntunī eṉṉō ṭāṭavum ellām vallacit tiyaippeṟ ṟaṟivuru vākināṉ uṉaiyē pāṭavum peṟṟēṉ eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: To the shame of husbands and wives who unite only to later part, You have mingled deep within my heart and remain there, never leaving. I have received the all-powerful siddhi, become the very form of consciousness, and gained the blessing of dancing with You and singing of You alone. This is enough for me. The penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: The union between the soul and God is more intimate and lasting than any human relationship. Unlike human partners who eventually part, God has merged with his very being, never to leave. This divine intimacy transforms him, granting siddhi (extraordinary spiritual abilities) and making him a being of pure consciousness. The relationship is so complete that he feels he can now dance with God, sharing in the divine play.

translit: uyattiṭam aṟiyā tiṟantavar tamaiiv vulakilē uyirpeṟṟu mīṭṭum nayattoṭu varuvit tiṭumoru ñāṉa nāṭṭamum kaṟpakō ṭiyiṉum vayattoṭu cākā varamumeṉ taṉakkē vaḻaṅkiṭap peṟṟaṉaṉ maraṇa payattaiviṭ ṭoḻittēṉ eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: I have been granted for myself the gaze of gnosis that can graciously bring back to life in this world those who have died without knowing the path of salvation, and I have received the boon of not dying for countless eons, remaining in full command. I have abandoned and cast off the fear of death. This is enough for me. The penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: Here, the fruits of devotion become truly extraordinary. Vallalar declares that he has received the power to conquer death itself. This includes the "gaze of gnosis" (divine, life-giving knowledge), which can bring the dead back to life, and for himself, the boon of a deathless physical existence. Because of these gifts of grace, the fundamental human fear of death has been completely erased from his life.

translit: nāṭalcey kiṉṟēṉ aruṭperuñ cōti nātaṉai eṉuḷē kaṇṭu kūṭalcey kiṉṟēṉ eṇṇiya ellām kūṭiṭak kulaviiṉ puruvāy āṭalcey kiṉṟēṉ cittelām vallāṉ ampalam taṉṉaiyē kuṟittup pāṭalcey kiṉṟēṉ eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: I seek and find the Lord of the Vast Grace-Light within me, and I unite with him. As all my aspirations come to fruition, I dance, flourishing as a form of bliss. I sing songs dedicated to the Ambalam of the one who has all conscious powers. This is enough for me; the penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: This verse describes the joyful culmination of his spiritual path. He seeks and finds the Lord of the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi) within himself. This inner union turns his life into a blissful dance, fulfilling all his heart's desires. His purpose is now simple and ecstatic: to sing in praise of the inner sacred hall (Ambalam) where the all-powerful God resides.

translit: tutipeṟum ayaṉō ṭariaraṉ mutalōr cūḻntucūḻn tiḷaittoru taṅkaḷ vitiyainon tiṉṉum viḻittiruk kiṉṟār viḻittirun tiṭavumnō vāmē matiyilēṉ aruḷāl cuttacaṉ mārkka maṉṟilē vayaṅkiya talaimaip patipatam peṟṟēṉ eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: The praised Brahma, Vishnu, Siva, and others surround him again and again, growing weary. Lamenting their fate, they remain ever-watchful. Yet I, the unwise one, have, by Grace and without any struggle, received the state of the supreme Lord who shines in the hall of the Suddha Sanmarkkam. This is enough for me; the penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: Here, Vallalar makes a bold claim about the power of Grace. Even the great gods of the Hindu pantheon, Brahma, Vishnu, and Siva, are depicted as still striving and unfulfilled. In contrast, Vallalar, who calls himself 'unwise', has attained the supreme state effortlessly, simply by accepting divine Grace. This shows that the path of Suddha Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Purity and Goodness) offers a direct route to God that can surpass even the status of celestial beings.

translit: puricaivāṉ ulakil pūvula kellām puṇṇiya ulakamāyp polintē karicelām tavirntu kaḷippelām aṭaintu karuttoṭu vāḻavum karuttil turicelām tavirkkum cuttacaṉ mārkkam tulaṅkavum tiruvaruṭ cōtip paricelām peṟṟēṉ eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: I have received all the gifts of the holy Grace-Light so that the fortified celestial worlds and all earthly worlds may shine as worlds of merit, so that people may live with purpose, abandoning all flaws and attaining all joy, and so that the Suddha Sanmarkkam, which removes all defects from the mind, may flourish. This is enough for me; the penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: Spiritual gifts are for the benefit of all. Vallalar sees his own transformation as part of a universal plan to make heaven and earth into 'worlds of merit'. His personal attainment is inseparable from his mission to help the Suddha Sanmarkkam flourish, so that it can remove suffering and elevate all of humanity.

translit: vētamē viḷaṅka meymmaiyē vayaṅka vemmaiyē nīṅkiṭa vimala vātamē vaḻaṅka vāṉamē muḻaṅka vaiyamē uyyaōr parama nātamē toṉikka ñāṉamē vaṭivāy naṉmaṇi maṉṟilē naṭikkum pātamē piṭittēṉ eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: So that the Vedas may be clarified, the ultimate Truth may shine, harshness may depart, the stainless Vadam may be bestowed, the heavens may thunder, the world may be saved, and a supreme Nadam may resonate, I have grasped the feet that dance in the hall of precious gems as the very form of Gnanam. This is enough for me; the penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: A direct experience of God is the surest source of truth, clarifying and completing all other forms of knowledge. Vallalar states that by connecting with the divine, which he sees as the very form of Gnanam (wisdom), the true meaning of the Vedas (sacred scriptures) is revealed and the world can be saved. This personal encounter with God is the final authority, bringing clarity to doctrine (Vadam) and sounding with the primal sound of creation (Nadam).

translit: kaṭṭamum kaḻaṉṟēṉ kavalaiviṭ ṭoḻittēṉ kalakkamum tīrntaṉaṉ piṟavic caṭṭamum kiḻittēṉ tūkkamum tuṟantēṉ cāvaiyum nōvaiyum tavirntēṉ ciṭṭamum aṭaintēṉ ciṟcapai uṭaiyāṉ celvameyp piḷḷaieṉ ṟorupērp paṭṭamum tarittēṉ eṉakkitu pōtum paṇṇiya tavampalit tatuvē.
translation: I have shed my constraints, abandoned worry, and ended my agitation. I have torn up the decree of birth, renounced sleep, and avoided death and disease. I have attained perfection and have worn the title, "Precious True Son of the Lord of the Chit Sabhai". This is enough for me; the penance I performed has borne fruit.
commentary: Spiritual realization brings complete freedom from every human limitation. Vallalar catalogues his liberation: he is free from constraint, anxiety and agitation; he has torn up the decree of birth like a legal document; he has given up sleep; and he has escaped both death and disease. This perfect state culminates in a new identity, the title 'Precious True Son' of the Lord of the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness).

tamil: நானந்த மடையாதெந் நாளினும்உள் ளவனாகி நடிக்கும் வண்ணம்
ஆனந்த நடம்புரிவான் ஆனந்த அமுதளித்தான் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: nāṉanta maṭaiyāten nāḷiṉumuḷ ḷavaṉāki naṭikkum vaṇṇam āṉanta naṭampurivāṉ āṉanta amutaḷittāṉ antō antō.
translation: So that I might exist forever, never reaching an end, He who performs the dance of bliss gave me the nectar of bliss. Oh, wonder! Oh, wonder!
commentary: God's grace has granted the speaker an unending, blissful existence. The "nectar of bliss" is the drink of immortality, a gift that ensures the soul will never again face an end. This eternal life is a direct participation in God's own joyful nature.

tamil: சாதிமதம் சமயமுதற் சங்கற்ப விகற்பம்எலாம் தவிர்ந்து போக
ஆதிநடம் புரிகின்றான் அருட்சோதி எனக்களித்தான் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: cātimatam camayamutaṟ caṅkaṟpa vikaṟpamelām tavirntu pōka ātinaṭam purikiṉṟāṉ aruṭcōti eṉakkaḷittāṉ antō antō.
translation: So that all conceptual fabrications and distinctions, such as caste, creed, and religion, would vanish, He who performs the primordial dance gave me the Grace-Light. Oh, wonder! Oh, wonder!
commentary: The experience of the Grace-Light dissolves all artificial human divisions, including caste, religion, and creed. These categories are seen as mental constructions that vanish in the face of direct divine realization. The primordial dance of God reveals a truth that unifies all, erasing the conflicts born from these limited identities.

tamil: துரியபதம் அடைந்தபெருஞ் சுத்தர்களும் முத்தர்களும் துணிந்து சொல்லற்
கரியபதம் எனக்களித்தான் அம்பலத்தில் ஆடுகின்றான் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: turiyapatam aṭaintaperuñ cuttarkaḷum muttarkaḷum tuṇintu collaṟ kariyapatam eṉakkaḷittāṉ ampalattil āṭukiṉṟāṉ antō antō.
translation: He who dances in the Ambalam gave me a state that even the great pure ones and liberated beings who have reached the plane of Turiya find difficult to dare describe. Oh, wonder! Oh, wonder!
commentary: The spiritual state granted to the speaker is beyond description, even for highly realized sages. Beings who have attained Turiya, the transcendent fourth state of consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, still cannot put into words the experience God has given him. This gift comes directly from the divine dancing in the Ambalam, the sacred expanse of consciousness.

tamil: மருட்பெருஞ்சோ தனைஎனது மட்டுமிலா வணங்கருணை வைத்தே மன்றில்
அருட்பெருஞ்சோ திப்பெருமான் அருளமுதம் எனக்களித்தான் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: maruṭperuñcō taṉaieṉatu maṭṭumilā vaṇaṅkaruṇai vaittē maṉṟil aruṭperuñcō tipperumāṉ aruḷamutam eṉakkaḷittāṉ antō antō.
translation: Placing limitless, venerable grace upon my great trial of delusion, the Great Lord, the Vast Grace-Light in the sacred hall, gave me the nectar of grace. Oh, wonder! Oh, wonder!
commentary: Divine grace intervened directly in a time of deep confusion and spiritual trial. Instead of being consumed by delusion, the speaker was met with boundless compassion from the Vast Grace-Light. This grace transformed his suffering into an experience of receiving the "nectar of grace," a life-giving essence that heals and saves.

tamil: துன்பமெலாம் ஒருகணத்தில் தொலைத்தருளி எந்நாளும் சுகத்தில் ஓங்க
அன்புடையான் அம்பலத்தான் அருட்சோதி எனக்களித்தான் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: tuṉpamelām orukaṇattil tolaittaruḷi ennāḷum cukattil ōṅka aṉpuṭaiyāṉ ampalattāṉ aruṭcōti eṉakkaḷittāṉ antō antō.
translation: Graciously dispelling all my sorrows in a single moment so that I may forever flourish in bliss, the Loving One, He of the Ambalam, gave me the Grace-Light. Oh, wonder! Oh, wonder!
commentary: The transformation brought by the Grace-Light is instantaneous and absolute. It removes sorrow completely in a single moment, establishing a new, permanent state of bliss. This emphasizes the immense and immediate power of divine grace.

tamil: பந்தமெலாம் தவிர்த்தருளிப் பதந்தருயோ காந்தமுதல் பகரா நின்ற
அந்தமெலாம் கடந்திடச்செய் தருளமுதம் எனக்களித்தான் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: pantamelām tavirttaruḷip patantaruyō kāntamutal pakarā niṉṟa antamelām kaṭantiṭaccey taruḷamutam eṉakkaḷittāṉ antō antō.
translation: He graciously removed all my bonds, granted me the ultimate state, made me transcend all the proclaimed systems starting with Yogānta, and gave me the nectar of grace. Oh, amazing, amazing!
commentary: Vallalar claims that the state he has been granted surpasses the final goals of all established spiritual systems. He mentions Yogānta (a school of thought focused on the ultimate aim of Yoga) as an example of a system he has now transcended, suggesting his path reveals a destination beyond what was previously known.

tamil: பேராலும் அறிவாலும் பெரியரெனச் சிறப்பாகப் பேச நின்றோர்
ஆராலும் பெறலரிய தியாததனைப் பெறுவித்தான் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: pērālum aṟivālum periyareṉac ciṟappākap pēca niṉṟōr ārālum peṟalariya tiyātataṉaip peṟuvittāṉ antō antō.
translation: He made me obtain that which is impossible for anyone to get, even for those celebrated as great by name and by knowledge. Oh, amazing, amazing!
commentary: This experience cannot be achieved through personal intellect, knowledge, or worldly greatness. Even those celebrated as the wisest and most accomplished cannot attain it on their own. It is a pure gift of grace, separate from any conventional measure of human merit.

tamil: தினைத்தனையும் அறிவறியாச் சிறியனென நினையாமல் சித்தி யான
அனைத்துமென்றன் வசமாக்கி அருளமுதம் எனக்களித்தான் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: tiṉaittaṉaiyum aṟivaṟiyāc ciṟiyaṉeṉa niṉaiyāmal citti yāṉa aṉaittumeṉṟaṉ vacamākki aruḷamutam eṉakkaḷittāṉ antō antō.
translation: Without seeing me as a lowly one who lacks even a millet seed's worth of knowledge, He brought all that is siddhi under my control and gave me the nectar of grace. Oh, amazing, amazing!
commentary: Divine grace is given unconditionally, without regard for one's own sense of unworthiness. Vallalar feels he lacks even the smallest amount of knowledge, yet God has granted him all siddhis, which are extraordinary spiritual powers and attainments. Grace is a free gift, not something earned through merit.

tamil: பொதுவாகிப் பொதுவில்நடம் புரிகின்ற பேரின்பப் பொருள்தான் யாதோ
அதுநானாய் நான்அதுவாய் அத்துவிதம் ஆகின்றேன் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: potuvākip potuvilnaṭam purikiṉṟa pēriṉpap poruḷtāṉ yātō atunāṉāy nāṉatuvāy attuvitam ākiṉṟēṉ antō antō.
translation: Whatever that substance of great bliss is, the one that is universal and dances in the common expanse, I am becoming That, That is becoming me, and I am becoming non-dual. Oh, amazing, amazing!
commentary: This verse describes the pinnacle of spiritual experience: the complete dissolution of the individual self into God. The "common expanse" is the universal space of pure consciousness where God "dances," and the "substance of great bliss" is God's own nature. This is a state of non-duality (attuvitam), where the distinction between "I" and "That" disappears in a perfect union.

tamil: மருள்வடிவே எஞ்ஞான்றும் எவ்விடத்தும் எதனாலு மாய்வி லாத
அருள்வடிவாய் இம்மையிலே அடைந்திடப்பெற் றாடுகின்றேன் அந்தோ அந்தோ.
translit: maruḷvaṭivē eññāṉṟum evviṭattum etaṉālu māyvi lāta aruḷvaṭivāy immaiyilē aṭaintiṭappeṟ ṟāṭukiṉṟēṉ antō antō.
translation: I, who was the very form of delusion, have been blessed to attain in this very life the form of grace that is imperishable at all times, in all places, and by any means, and I dance in celebration. Oh, amazing, amazing!
commentary: The transformation from a state of delusion to a state of grace is absolute, permanent, and occurs within this very lifetime. It is attained here and now. He describes his former self as the "very form of delusion" to emphasize the totality of the change into an eternal "form of grace," an experience so strong it moves him to dance.

tamil: எக்கரையும் காணாதே இருட்கடலில் கிடந்தேனை எடுத்தாட் கொண்டு
அக்கரைசேர்த் தருளெனுமோர் சர்க்கரையும் எனக்களித்தான் அந்தோ அந்தோ315.
translit: ekkaraiyum kāṇātē iruṭkaṭalil kiṭantēṉai eṭuttāṭ koṇṭu akkaraicērt taruḷeṉumōr carkkaraiyum eṉakkaḷittāṉ antō antō.
translation: I was lying in an ocean of darkness, unable to see any shore. He lifted me up and took me as His own, brought me to the other shore, and gave me a sugar called grace. Oh! Oh!
commentary: Being lost in the world without God is like drowning in a dark, shoreless ocean. God's grace is the force that rescues the soul, lifting it from despair and carrying it to a place of safety and sweetness. The simple, direct metaphor of grace as "sugar" makes this spiritual reality feel immediate and delightful.
NOTES
Note 315

tamil: இப்பதினோராம் செய்யுள் ஒரு தனிப்பாடல். பொருள் ஒற்றுமை கருதி இப்பதிகத்தில் சேர்க்கப்பெற்றது.
translit: ippatiṉōrām ceyyuḷ oru taṉippāṭal. poruḷ oṟṟumai karuti ippatikattil cērkkappeṟṟatu.
translation: This eleventh stanza is an independent song; it has been included in this decad on account of unity of meaning.

translit: cittipurattē tiṉantōṟum cīrkoḷaruḷ cattiviḻā nīṭit taḻaittōṅka - etticaiyil uḷḷavarum vantē uvakai uṟukamatat tuḷḷal oḻika tolaintu.
translation: May the festival of glorious Grace-Power last long and flourish daily in Cittipuram. May people from all directions come and be joyful. May the arrogant frenzy of religious sectarianism cease and be destroyed.
commentary: Vallalar envisions a spiritual center, the Cittipuram (City of Perfection), where the celebration of divine grace is constant. This celebration is open to all, but it requires the end of all religious pride and conflict. True universal joy depends on universal acceptance.

translit: oṉṟē civameṉ ṟuṇarntiv vulakamelām naṉṟē orumaiyuṟṟu naṇṇiyē - maṉṟē naṭampuriyum pāta naḷiṉamalark kuḷḷam iṭampurika vāḻka icaintu.
translation: Realizing that Sivam is One, may this entire world attain a good unity. May the heart make a place for the lotus-flower feet of the one who dances in the Hall, and may all live in accord.
commentary: The foundation for global unity is the shared understanding that the Divine, here called Sivam, is a single reality for everyone. When people open their hearts to this one dancing presence, symbolized by the divine feet, social harmony will naturally follow.

translit: ciṟcapaiyum poṟcapaiyum citti viḷakkattāl naṟcakamēl nīṭūḻi naṇṇiṭuka - caṟcapaiyōr pōṟṟivaram peṟṟuvakai pūrikka vāḻntiṭuka nāṟṟicaiyum vāḻka nayantu.
translation: Through the illumination of Siddhi, may the Cirsabai and the Porsabai endure for long ages on this good earth. May the members of the Sat Sabai live, swelling with joy as they offer praise and receive boons. May all four directions flourish with delight.
commentary: He blesses the Cirsabai (Hall of Consciousness) and the Porsabai (Golden Hall), the halls of the Lord's dance, praying that through the light of Siddhi they endure on this good earth for long ages. The members of the Sat Sabai, the assembly of the true, are to live swelling with joy, and the blessing reaches out to all four directions.

translit: accan tavirttē aruḷiṟ celuttukiṉṟa viccai aracē viḷaṅkiṭuka - naccaravam ātik koṭiya:uyir attaṉaiyum pōyoḻika nītik koṭiviḷaṅka nīṇṭu.
translation: O King of Knowledge, who removes fear and guides us into Grace, may you shine forth! May all cruel life, such as poisonous snakes, cease to exist. May the banner of justice fly high and shine brightly.
commentary: The ultimate ruler of this ideal world is a principle of Divine Knowledge that dispels fear and leads all beings to grace. Vallalar's vision of justice is all-encompassing, including the end of human conflict and the transformation of cruelty in nature itself.

translit: karuṇaiilā āṭci kaṭuki oḻika aruḷnayanta naṉmārkkar āḷka - teruḷnayanta nallōr niṉaitta nalampeṟuka naṉṟuniṉait tellōrum vāḻka icaintu.
translation: May rule devoid of compassion quickly cease. May those of the good path, who desire Grace, rule. May the good people who desire clarity obtain the blessings they envision. Thinking good thoughts, may everyone live in harmony.
commentary: True political power, Vallalar states, must be founded on compassion. He calls for an end to any form of governance that lacks this quality and prays that those who follow the Sanmarkkam (the good and true path) will lead instead. The vision is for a world where good intentions are fulfilled and everyone can live together in peace, governed by grace and kindness.

translit: pulloḻukkam ellām puṇariyiṭaip pōyoḻika nalloḻukkam oṉṟē nalampeṟuka - illoḻukkil cettārkaḷ ellām tirumpa eḻuntumaṉam ottārāy vāḻka uvantu.
translation: Let all base conduct go and perish in the sea. Let good conduct alone flourish. May all the dead rise again and live joyfully in the worldly path, united in mind.
commentary: Alongside a prayer for moral purification, where all base conduct is washed away, Vallalar introduces one of his boldest claims: the resurrection of the dead. This is not a metaphor for spiritual rebirth. He literally envisions a time when those who have died will physically return, restored to life to live in perfect harmony with one another.

translit: cettār eḻuka civamē poruḷeṉṟē ittā raṇiyil iruntoḷirka - cuttaciva caṉmārkkam oṉṟē taḻaikka tayavaṟiyāt tuṉmārkkam pōka tolaintu.
translation: Let the dead arise. Declaring that Sivam alone is the Reality, may they live and shine forth on this earth. May Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam alone flourish. May the evil path that knows no compassion be destroyed and disappear.
commentary: The resurrection of the dead is directly linked to a new state of consciousness. Those who return will live with the clear understanding that Sivam, the formless and benevolent Divine, is the sole reality. The world they inhabit will be one where the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (the Pure Path of Goodness) is the only way of life, and all paths lacking compassion have vanished entirely.

translit: cettavarkaḷ ellām tirumpa eḻuntuvarac cittamvaittuc ceykiṉṟa cittiyaṉē - cuttaciva caṉmārkka caṅkat talaivaṉē niṟpōṟṟum eṉmārkkam niṉmārkka mē.
translation: O Master of powers, who sets your will to make all the dead rise again! O Leader of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam Fellowship! The path I take in praising you is your path alone.
commentary: Here, Vallalar addresses the divine power directly, acknowledging it as the "Master of powers" capable of resurrecting the dead. He sees this divine being as the leader of the spiritual community he founded, the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam Fellowship. The verse ends with a statement of total surrender: his own path of devotion is nothing other than the path shown to him by the Divine itself.

translit: nallārum eṉṉai nayantārum naṉmaicola vallārum eṉṉai vaḷarttārum - ellārum nīeṉ ṟirukkiṉṟēṉ niṉmalaṉē nīpeṟṟa cēyeṉ ṟirukkiṉṟēṉ cērntu.
translation: O Immaculate One! The good people, those who cherished me, those able to speak well of me, and those who raised me: I hold that all of them are you. I hold myself to be the child you bore, united with you.
commentary: God is the living presence found within every person who has shown love and support. Vallalar sees the divine in his benefactors and family, and sees himself as a child born of this same divine source, intimately connected to it.

translit: āṭaeṭut tāṉeṉ ṟaṟaikiṉṟīr eṉtalaimēl cūṭaeṭut tāṉeṉṟu colkiṉṟēṉ - nāṭaṟiya ivvaḻakkai yārpāl icaittaṟuttuk koḷkiṟpām kavvaiaṟṟa ampalattāṉ kāl.
translation: You all declare, "He lifted it to dance." I say, "He lifted it to place upon my head." To whom can we take this dispute, so that the world may know, and have it settled? It is the foot of the blameless One in the Ambalam.
commentary: This verse challenges a traditional understanding of Siva's cosmic dance. While others see Siva's lifted foot as a universal symbol, Vallalar reinterprets it as an intimate gesture of grace meant specifically for him, a blessing placed upon his head. The final judge of this dispute is a direct appeal to God in the Ambalam (the Hall of Consciousness).

translit: nōvātu nōṉpeṉaippōl nōṟṟavarum eññāṉṟum cāvā varameṉaippōl cārntavarum - tēvāniṉ pēraruḷai eṉpōlap peṟṟavarum evvulakil yāruḷarnī caṟṟē aṟai.
translation: Those who have performed spiritual disciplines without suffering like me, attained the boon of never dying like me, and, O God, received Your great grace like me: who is there like that in any world? You tell me.
commentary: Spiritual life is often seen as a path of physical austerity, but Vallalar declares his own journey was free from such sufferings. He makes the bold claim that no one else has ever achieved the deathless state and received God's grace in this effortless way, challenging God to name another. This highlights his teaching that the path of compassion is one of joy, not painful austerity.

translit: vētamum vētattiṉ antamum pōṟṟa viḷaṅkiyaniṉ pātamum māmuṭi yumkaṇṭu koḷḷum paṭieṉakkē pōtamum pōtat taruḷamu tumtanta puṇṇiyaṉē nātamum nāta muṭiyum kaṭanta naṭattavaṉē.
translation: O Virtuous One who gave me knowledge and the grace-nectar of that knowledge so that I could behold Your feet and great crown, which are praised by the Vedas and their culmination! O Dancer who transcends both primal soundand its very end!
commentary: God's grace provides spiritual knowledge and the very capacity to understand it. This divine gift allows a direct vision of God, an experience that surpasses what is merely described in scriptures like the Vedas. The verse praises God as a reality beyond even the most fundamental cosmic principle, the primal sound (nādam).

translit: vaṇṇappoṉ ṉampala vāḻvēeṉ kaṇṇiṉuḷ māmaṇiyē cuṇṇappoṉ nīṟṟoḷi ōṅkiya cōtic cukapporuḷē eṇṇappa yiṉṟaeṉ eṇṇam elāmmuṉṉar īka:iteṉ viṇṇappam ēṟṟu varuvāyeṉ pālvirain tēviraintē.
translation: O Life of the beautiful Golden Hall, O great Gem within my eye! O blissful Substance, O Jothi that shines brighter than fragrant golden sacred ash! Grant all that I have long cultivated in my thoughts. This is my plea: accept it and come to me, quickly, very quickly!
commentary: Addressing God with intimate names, Vallalar expresses his intense longing for complete union. He calls God the life of the "Golden Hall" (the heart of consciousness), the gem within his eye, and the radiant Jothi (divine light). His plea is for God to manifest the spiritual reality he has yearned for, showing the powerful and personal nature of his devotion.

translit: ciṟcapai appaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉaruḷ teḷḷamutam caṟcapai uḷḷam taḻaikka:uṇ ṭēṉuṇmai tāṉaṟinta naṟcapaic cittikaḷ ellāmeṉ kaivacam naṇṇappeṟṟēṉ poṟcapai ōṅkap purintāṭu taṟkup pukuntaṉaṉē.
translation: I have beheld the Father in the Hall of Consciousness. I have drunk the clear nectar of grace, causing the hearts of the Assembly of the True to flourish. I have gained possession of all the supernatural powers of the good assembly that knows the truth. I have entered the Golden Hallto perform the dance that will make it thrive.
commentary: Vallalar describes a sequence of spiritual realization. First, he perceives God in the citsabai (the inner hall of consciousness). This vision allows him to drink the nectar of grace, which in turn nurtures the satsabai (the assembly of true beings). Finally, having gained all siddhis (supernatural powers), he enters the porsabai (the golden hall), ready to participate in the divine dance.

translit: varaiyaṟṟa cīrpperu vāḻvutan teṉmaṉam maṉṉieṉṟum puraiyaṟṟa meynnilai ēṟṟimeyñ ñāṉap potuviṉiṭait tiraiyaṟṟa kāṭci aḷittiṉ ṉamutat teḷivaruḷi naraiyaṟṟu mūppaṟ ṟiṟappaṟ ṟirukkavum nalkiyatē.
translation: It gave me a great life of boundless glory, abided in my mind, and elevated me to a flawless, true state forever. It granted me an unveiled vision in the universal expanse of true wisdom, bestowed the clarity of sweet nectar, and enabled me to live without gray hair, without aging, and without death.
commentary: Here, Vallalar catalogs the ultimate gifts of grace. He has been given a glorious life, a mind established in unchanging truth, and a direct, "unveiled vision" in the universal space of pure jñāna (divine wisdom). The culmination of these gifts is the perfected, immortal body: a physical state free from gray hair, aging, and death.

translit: tāyāki eṉuyirt tantaiyum ākieṉ caṟkuruvāyt tēyāp perumpatam ākieṉ cattiyat teyvamumāy vāyārap pāṭumnal vākkaḷit teṉuḷam maṉṉukiṉṟa tūyā tirunaṭa rāyāciṟ ṟampalac cōtiyaṉē.
translation: O Pure One, O King of the sacred dance, O Jothi of the little hall! You abide in my mind, having become my mother, the father of my life, my true guru, the great, undiminishing state, and my own true God. You gave me the fine gift of speech to sing Your praises wholeheartedly.
commentary: The relationship with the Divine is deeply personal and all-encompassing. God, experienced as Jothi (Divine Light) in the Chitrambalam (the inner space of consciousness), becomes one's mother, father, teacher (guru), and ultimate reality. This intimate connection is what inspires the very ability to sing and express this truth.

translit: ātiyum antamum illāt taṉiccuṭa rākiiṉpa nītiyum nīrmaiyum ōṅkap potuvil niruttamiṭum cōtiyum vētiyum nāṉaṟin tēṉic cekatalattil cātiyum pētac camayamum nīṅkit taṉittaṉaṉē.
translation: I came to know the Jothi and the Primal Cause, the one who dances in the common space as a unique flame with no beginning or end, so that the justice and nature of bliss may flourish. In this world, I stand utterly alone, having abandoned caste and divisive religions.
commentary: Realizing God as the universal Jothi (Light) and primal source of all existence makes worldly divisions like caste and religion meaningless. This direct perception of the Divine, which dances for the well-being of all, leads to a state of standing alone, free from the constraints of social identity and sectarian beliefs.

translit: taṉṉē rilāta talaivāciṟ ṟampalam taṉṉileṉṉai iṉṉē aṭaikuvit tiṉparuḷ vāyitu vētaruṇam aṉṉē eṉaippeṟṟa appāeṉ ṟuṉṉai aṭikkaṭikkē coṉṉēṉmuṉ collukiṉ ṟēṉpiṟa ētun tuṇintilaṉē.
translation: O peerless Leader! Make me attain you in Chitrambalam right now and grant me bliss. This is the moment. I have repeatedly called you "O Mother, O Father who gave birth to me!". I have said it before, and I say it again now; I have resolved on nothing else.
commentary: This is a prayer of intense urgency, a demand for immediate union with God in the Chitrambalam (the inner hall of consciousness). The repetition of "Mother" and "Father" emphasizes a simple, intimate, and total reliance on the Divine. This single-minded focus is the only thing the speaker has resolved upon, showing absolute commitment.

translit: tēkāti mūṉṟumuṉ pāṟkoṭut tēṉniṉ tiruvaṭikkē mōkā tipaṉeṉ ṟulakavar tūṟṟa muyalukiṉṟēṉ nākā tiparum viyantiṭa eṉetir naṇṇieṉṟum cākā varantantu caṉmārkka nītiyum cāṟṟukavē.
translation: I have given the three, my body and all that is mine, to you, to your sacred feet. I strive for the people of the world to slander me as "the lord of infatuation". Now, appear before me, to the amazement of even the lords of the Nagas (serpent deities), grant the boon of never dying, and declare the principles of Sanmarkkam.
commentary: The speaker declares a complete surrender of his body, his possessions and his soul to God's sacred feet. He welcomes the world's ridicule, content to be called infatuated with the Divine. Having given everything, he asks God to appear, grant the boon of never dying, and declare the principles of Sanmarkkam, the True Path for all.

translit: kaṟṟēṉciṟ ṟampalak kalviyaik kaṟṟuk karuṇaineṟi uṟṟēṉek kālamum cākāmal ōṅkum oḷivaṭivam peṟṟēṉ uyarnilai peṟṟēṉ ulakil piṟanilaiyaip paṟṟēṉ civāṉantap paṟṟēeṉ paṟṟeṉap paṟṟiṉaṉē.
translation: I have learned the education of Chitrambalam. Having learned it, I have attained the path of compassion. I have received a form of light that flourishes and never dies. I have attained the high state. In this world, I will not grasp any other state. I have grasped attachment to the bliss of Siva as my only attachment.
commentary: The striving is over; here, Vallalar declares his victory. The "education of Chitrambalam" has led him to the path of compassion, which in turn has granted him the ultimate prize: an immortal, radiant body of light. He has found his final refuge, an unshakable attachment to the bliss of Siva, and will seek no other state in this world.

translit: tīmaikaḷ yāvum tolaittuviṭ ṭēṉit tiṉantoṭaṅkic cēmanal iṉpac ceyalē viḷaṅkameyc cittielām kāmamuṟ ṟeṉṉaik kalantukoṇ ṭāṭak karuṇainaṭat tāmaṉeṉ uḷḷamum cāravum peṟṟaṉaṉ cattiyamē.
translation: Starting from this day, I have destroyed all evils, so that only the action of secure, good bliss shines forth. I have received the blessing of the Lord of the compassionate dance entering my heart, and of all the true siddhis, filled with desire, merging with me to celebrate. This is the truth.
commentary: This verse marks a turning point. Vallalar announces that from this day forward, all evil is gone, replaced by a life of pure, blissful action. He feels the divine presence, the "Lord of the compassionate dance," filling his heart, and all the true siddhis (spiritual powers) are now his to command, joining him in a joyful celebration of this union.

sections.title: The Lady Speaks to Her Friend

translit: vētānta nilaiyoṭu cittānta nilaiyum mēvum potunaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum nātāntat tiruvīti naṭappāyō tōḻi naṭavāmal eṉmoḻi kaṭappāyō tōḻi.
translation: I must see the universal dance that unites the state of Vedanta with the state of Siddhanta. O friend, will you walk the sacred street of Nadantam? Or will you, by not walking, transgress my word?
commentary: The soul expresses a deep longing to experience the divine dance that resolves all philosophical differences. She wishes to see the unity between Vedanta (the path of final knowledge) and Siddhanta (the path of perfected truth), which are often seen as distinct. She urges her friend, the mind, to join her on the way to Nadantam, a sublime state of consciousness beyond even the primordial divine sound.

translit: tompata uruvoṭu tatpata veḷiyil tōṉṟaci patanaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum empatamāki icaivāyō tōḻi icaiyāmal vīṇilē acaivāyō tōḻi.
translation: I must see the dance of 'Asi' that appears in the space of 'Tat' with the form of 'Tvam'. O friend, will you merge with my state and agree? Or will you, without agreeing, simply waver in vain?
commentary: Here, the soul speaks of one of the deepest statements of Indian philosophy: "That Thou Art" (Tat Tvam Asi). She yearns to witness the living reality of this union, the "dance" where 'Thou' (Tvam, the individual self) is seen within the vast space of 'That' (Tat, the supreme reality). She asks her friend, representing her own mind, to stop wavering and fully consent to this divine experience.

translit: ciṉmaya veḷiyiṭait taṉmaya mākit tikaḻum potunaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum eṉmaya māki iruppāyō tōḻi iccai mayamāy iruppāyōtōḻi.
translation: In the space of pure consciousness, I must see the glorious universal dance that, becoming one with its essence, shines forth. O friend, will you become one with me? Will you be utterly filled with longing?
commentary: The divine dance unfolds within a space of pure consciousness (cinmaya). To see this dance is to merge with it, becoming one with its very essence. Vallalar expresses this as a deep, all-consuming longing. He asks his friend, his own soul, to share in this singular, overwhelming desire for union, leaving all other attachments behind.

translit: navanilai mēṟpara nātat talattē ñāṉat tirunaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum mavuṉat tiruvīti varuvāyō tōḻi vārāmal vīṇpaḻi taruvāyō tōḻi.
translation: In the realm of Nāda, the supreme space above the nine states, I must see the sacred dance of wisdom. O friend, will you come along the sacred street of silence? Or by staying away, will you cause pointless blame?
commentary: The highest wisdom is found in deep inner silence. Vallalar longs to see the dance of wisdom that unfolds in the state of Nāda (the primal, cosmic sound), a state beyond all ordinary stages of consciousness. The path to this final experience, however, is mauna (deep silence). He invites his soul to walk this silent path, warning that to refuse is to miss the entire point of the spiritual quest.

translit: āṟāṟuk kappuṟa mākum potuvil atuvatu vānaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum ēṟāmal iḻiyāmal iruppāyō tōḻi ēṟi iḻintiṅ kiṟappāyōtōḻi.
translation: In the universal expanse beyond the thirty-six tattvas, I must see the dance in which That becomes That. O friend, will you remain steady, neither ascending nor descending? Or will you keep ascending and descending, only to die here?
commentary: True liberation means going beyond all the building blocks of reality and finding a state of perfect stillness. Vallalar describes a universal space beyond the thirty-six tattvas (the constituent principles of the cosmos, from earth to consciousness). In this final state, the dance is one of pure, non-dual identity: "That becomes That." He urges his soul to find this steady state and to stop the endless cycle of spiritual ascent and descent, which is as futile as the cycle of birth and death.

translit: vakāra veḷiyil cikāra uruvāy makārat tirunaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum vikāra ulakai veṟuppāyō tōḻi vēṟāki eṉcol maṟuppāyō tōḻi.
translation: I must see the sacred 'ma' dance, in the form of 'ci', within the space of 'va'. O friend, will you despise this perverted world? O friend, will you become estranged and reject my words?
commentary: The secret of the divine is encoded in sacred sounds. This verse refers to syllables from the great Saiva mantra, Na-maḥ-śi-vā-ya. 'Va' represents divine energy or grace, and 'ci' (for Siva) represents God. Vallalar sees the dance as the soul ('ma', another syllable) taking on the very form of God ('ci') within the vast space of divine energy ('va'). He presents a choice: embrace this inner reality, or remain attached to the distorted outer world and reject the call to transformation.

translit: nātānta nilaiyoṭu pōtānta nilaikku naṭuvām potunaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum cūtāntaṟ pōtattaic cuṭuvāyō tōḻi tuṭṭaneṟiyil keṭuvāyō tōḻi.
translation: I must see the universal dance that takes place between the state of Nādānta and the state of Bōdhānta. O friend, will you burn away the consciousness steeped in deceit? O friend, will you perish on a wicked path?
commentary: The divine dance is revealed in a reality that transcends even the highest mystical states. It exists in a space between Nādānta (the end of all mystical sound) and Bōdhānta (the end of all conceptual thought). To see this, one must burn away the deceptive ego-consciousness that traps the soul in a limited, false view of the world.

translit: aṟivil aṟivai aṟiyum potuvil āṉantat tirunaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum ceṟivil aṟivākic celvāyō tōḻi cellāmal meynneṟi velvāyō tōḻi.
translation: I must see the sacred dance of bliss in the universal space where one knows the Intelligence within intelligence. O friend, will you become wisdom steeped in attachments and leave? O friend, will you go on, becoming knowledge in that fullness? O friend, without going, do you think you will win the true path?
commentary: The true vision of bliss comes when one's own awareness recognizes the divine Intelligence that is its source. Vallalar warns against seeking a "wisdom" that remains tangled in worldly attachments, as this is a false victory. Real success on the spiritual path is achieving a pure wisdom that is completely unattached.

translit: eṉṉait taṉṉōṭē iruttum potuvil iṉpat tirunaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum niṉṉaiviṭ ṭeṉṉōṭē nilaippāyō tōḻi nilaiyāmal eṉṉaiyum alaippāyō tōḻi.
translation: I must see the sacred dance of delight in the universal space where He seats me with Himself. O friend, will you abandon your ego-self and become steadfast with me? O friend, by being unsteady, will you torment me as well?
commentary: The highest delight is experiencing union with God, where the Divine seats the soul with Himself. This is possible only if one surrenders the separate ego-self. Vallalar pleads with his own mind to abandon its ego, warning that an unsteady mind torments the entire person and prevents this sacred union.

translit: turiyattiṟ kappālun tōṉṟum potuvil jōtit tirunaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum kariyaikkaṇ ṭāṅkatu kāṇpāyō tōḻi kāṇātu pōyppaḻipūṇpāyō tōḻi.
translation: I must see the sacred dance of Jothi in the universal space that appears even beyond Turīyam. O friend, having seen the Witness, will you then see That? O friend, will you fail to see it and end up bearing the blame?
commentary: The final vision is of the dance of Jothi (the Supreme Light of Grace) in a state beyond even Turīyam, the fourth state of pure consciousness. The path requires first realizing one's self as the silent Witness of all experience. Only from that stable vantage point can one perceive the final Light, and the responsibility to do so rests with the seeker.

translit: tattuvat tuṭpuṟan tāṉām potuvil cattān tirunaṭam nāṉkāṇal vēṇṭum kottaṟu vittaik kuṟippāyō tōḻi kuṟiyā tulakil veṟippāyō tōḻi.
translation: I must see the sacred dance of Being in the universal space, where He Himself is inside and outside the tattvas. O friend, will you indicate the flawless art to achieve this? Or will you just stare blankly in the world without giving a sign, O friend?
commentary: The divine dance reveals God as pure Being, the reality that is simultaneously inside and outside all the tattvas (the fundamental principles that make up the cosmos). The speaker asks her companion for the "flawless art," the spiritual technique, to realize this truth. The alternative is to remain lost in the world, staring blankly without understanding the nature of reality.

translit: kātalkaim mikunta teṉceyvēṉ eṉainī kaṇṭukoḷ kaṇavaṉē eṉṟāḷ ōtaluṉ pukaḻē aṉṟināṉ oṉṟum uvantilēṉ uṇmaiyī teṉṟāḷ pētaināṉ piṟitōr pukalilēṉ ceyta piḻaiyelām poṟuttaruḷ eṉṟāḷ mātaya vuṭaiya vaḷḷalē eṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: "My love has overflowed, what can I do? You must see me and accept me, my Husband!" she said. "Other than reciting your praise, I delight in nothing else, this is the truth," she said. "I, a naive girl, have no other refuge; please forgive all the mistakes I have made," she said. "O Patron of great compassion!" she said, my daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: Overwhelmed by love, the soul declares her complete surrender to God. She confesses that her only joy is praising Him, admits her naivety and past mistakes, and throws herself upon His mercy. Her own mother, who bore her through a boon, overhears this and is struck by her daughter's absolute devotion.

translit: mayaṅkiṉēṉ eṉiṉum vaḷḷalē uṉaināṉ maṟappaṉō kaṉaviṉum eṉṟāḷ uyaṅkiṉēṉ uṉṉai maṟantiṭil aiyō uyirtari yāteṉak keṉṟāḷ kayaṅkiṉēṉ kayaṅkā vaṇṇaniṉ karuṇaik kaṭalamu taḷittaruḷ eṉṟāḷ vayaṅkuciṟ capaiyil varataṉē eṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: "Though I am bewildered, O Patron, would I ever forget you, even in a dream?" she said. "I suffer; if I were to forget you, alas, I could not bear to live," she said. "I am wasting away. To stop my wasting away, grant me the nectar of your sea of grace," she said. "O Bestower of boons in the shining Hall of Consciousness!" she said, my daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: The soul's devotion is so total that her very life depends on remembering God. She declares that forgetting him, even in a dream, would be unbearable, and the pain of separation is causing her to waste away. She pleads for the life-giving nectar of grace from the God who dwells in the ciṟcapai (the shining Hall of Consciousness).

translit: añcaleṉ ṟeṉaiit taruṇanī vantē aṉpiṉāl aṇaittaruḷ eṉṟāḷ pañcupōl paṟantēṉ ayyavō tuṉpam paṭamuṭi yāteṉak keṉṟāḷ ceñcevē eṉatu karuttelām uṉatu tiruvuḷam aṟiyumē eṉṟāḷ vañcakam aṟiyā vaḷḷalē eṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: "Saying, 'Do not fear,' come to me at this very moment and embrace me with love," she said. "I am adrift like cotton, alas! I cannot bear this suffering," she said. "Your sacred heart knows all my thoughts perfectly," she said. "O Patron who knows no deceit!" she said, my daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: The soul begs for an immediate experience of God's loving embrace to end her suffering. Feeling lost and adrift, she expresses a deep trust that God, who is without deceit, already knows the complete sincerity of her heart's longing. It is a desperate plea for present union.

translit: pūmiyō poruḷō virumpilēṉ uṉṉaip puṇarntiṭa virumpiṉēṉ eṉṟāḷ kāmieṉ ṟeṉainī kaiviṭēl kāmak karutteṉak killaikāṇ eṉṟāḷ cāminī varavu tāḻttiṭil aiyō caṟṟunāṉ tarittiṭēṉ eṉṟāḷ māmiku karuṇai vaḷḷalē eṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: "I desire neither the earth nor wealth; I desire to unite with you," she said. "Do not abandon me, calling me lustful; see, I have no carnal intent," she said. "My Lord, if you delay your coming, alas, I cannot endure even for a moment," she said. "O Patron of exceedingly abundant grace!" she said, my daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: In this devotional poetry, the soul often speaks as a female lover pining for God. Here, the soul makes it clear that its intense desire is for a purely spiritual union with the divine. Having rejected all other attachments, it tells God that any further delay in his arrival is simply unbearable.

translit: aṭuttunāṉ uṉṉaik kalantaṉu pavikka ācaimēṟ poṅkiya teṉṟāḷ taṭuttiṭa muṭiyā tiṉicciṟu poḻutum talaivaṉē tāḻttiṭēl eṉṟāḷ toṭuttula kuḷḷār tūṟṟutal vāyāl colamuṭi yāteṉak keṉṟāḷ maṭuttaven tuyartīrt teṭuttaruḷ eṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: "My desire to draw near, unite with you, and experience you has surged," she said. "It cannot be restrained. From now on, O Master, do not delay even for a moment," she said. "I cannot express with my mouth the gossip the people of this world unceasingly level at me," she said. "End the burning sorrow that has engulfed me, lift me up, and grant your grace," she said, my daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: The soul's spiritual longing has become an overwhelming flood. This all-consuming devotion makes it a stranger in the ordinary world, a target of gossip and ridicule. The suffering is therefore twofold: the internal pain of separation from God, and the external pain of social rejection. The soul begs God to end this dual torment and lift it up.

translit: taṭuttiṭal vallār illainiṉ aruḷait tarukanaṟ ṟaruṇamī teṉṟāḷ koṭuttiṭil aiyō niṉṉaruṭ perumai kuṟaiyumō kuṟaintiṭā teṉṟāḷ naṭuttaya vilarpōṉ ṟiruttaluṉ ṟaṉakku ñāyamō naṇpaṉē eṉṟāḷ vaṭuttiṉum vāyēṉ allaṉnāṉ eṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: She said, "No one can block Your grace, so give it to me, this is the perfect moment. If You give it, will the greatness of Your grace diminish? It will not. Is it right for You to be like one without compassion, O Friend? I am not one who speaks falsely in the least." My daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: The soul's pleading turns into a bold, loving challenge. It argues that since God's grace is infinite and all-powerful, there is no reason to withhold it, especially since giving it costs nothing. It questions God directly, asking how a being of pure compassion can act in a way that seems uncompassionate. This is the intimate argument of a soul that sees God as a dear friend.

translit: poṉcey niṉvaṭivaip puṇarntiṭa niṉaittēṉ poṅkiya tācaimēl eṉṟāḷ eṉceyvēṉ eṉaiyum viḻuṅkiya taiyō eṉṉaḷa vaṉṟukāṇ eṉṟāḷ koṉceyum ulakar eṉṉaiyum uṉatu kuṟippaiyum kuṟittilār eṉṟāḷ vaṉceyum avarvāy ōyvateṉ ṟeṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: She said, "I longed to unite with Your golden form, and desire surged within me. What can I do? Alas, it has swallowed me whole! It is beyond my control, you see. The people of this vain world have understood neither me nor Your intention. When will their cruel mouths ever fall silent?" My daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: Spiritual desire is portrayed as an uncontrollable force that has completely consumed the soul. This intense inner state is contrasted with the misunderstanding of the outside world, whose cruel gossip adds to the devotee's suffering. The soul feels caught between her overwhelming love for God and the incomprehension of society.

translit: melintaeṉ uḷattai aṟintaṉai tayavu mēvilai eṉṉaiyō eṉṟāḷ nalintapō tiṉṉum pārttumeṉ ṟiruttal nallavark kaṭuppatō eṉṟāḷ malinta ivvulakar vāyppatar tūṟṟa vaittaluṉ marapala eṉṟāḷ valinteṉaik kalanta vaḷḷalē eṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: She said, "You know my heart has grown weak, yet You show no compassion, why? When I am suffering, is it right for a good person to just keep watching? It is not Your nature to let these worldly people slander me with their worthless talk, O generous one who willfully united with me!" My daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: The soul appeals to God's compassionate nature, reminding him that he has already "willfully united" with her in the past. This makes his current silence even more painful. It is a desperate plea for the return of an intimacy that has already been tasted and is now deeply missed.

translit: oṉṟilēṉ piṟitoṉ ṟuṉṉaruṭ cōti oṉṟuṟa oṉṟiṉēṉ eṉṟāḷ naṉṟilēṉ eṉiṉum niṉtiru vaṭiyai nampiṉēṉ nayantaruḷ eṉṟāḷ kuṉṟilē iruttaṟ kuriyanāṉ tuyarak kuḻiyilē iruntiṭēṉ eṉṟāḷ maṉṟilē naṭañcey vaḷḷalē eṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: She said, "I have nothing else; I have become one with the oneness of Your Grace-Jothi. Though I have no merit, I have trusted in Your sacred feet, so look upon me with favor and grant your grace. I, who deserve to be on a mountain, will not remain in this pit of sorrow, O generous one who dances in the Hall!" My daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: The soul declares her complete reliance on God, having cast aside everything else for the sake of his ArutJothi (grace-light). Despite feeling unworthy, her faith in God's "sacred feet" is absolute. The imagery of being in a "pit of sorrow" when she belongs on a mountain powerfully expresses her sense that this state of separation is unnatural and must end.

translit: āṭiya pātat taḻakaṉeṉ ṟaṉaittāṉ aṉpiṉāl kūṭiṉaṉ eṉṟāḷ kōṭimā tavaṅkaḷ puriyiṉum piṟarkkuk kūṭutal kūṭumō eṉṟāḷ pāṭiya paṭieṉ karuttelām nirappip paricelām purintaṉaṉ eṉṟāḷ vāṭiya uḷamum taḷirttaṉaṉ eṉṟāḷ varattiṉāl nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: She said, "The beautiful one with the dancing feet has united with me out of love. Could others attain this union, even if they performed tens of millions of great austerities? Just as I sang, He fulfilled my every thought and bestowed every gift. He made my withered heart sprout anew." My daughter, whom I received through a boon.
commentary: After verses of painful longing, the poem resolves in joyous union. The soul announces that her prayers have been answered: God has united with her purely out of love. This union fulfills her deepest desires and brings her withered spirit back to life, demonstrating that sincere, loving surrender is the true path to grace.

sections.title: The Friend Describes the Heroine's State

translit: ammatavēḷ kaṇaioṉṟō aiṅkaṇaiyum viṭuttāṉ aruḷaṭaiyum ācaiyiṉāl āruyirtāṉ poṟuttāḷ immatamō ciṟitumilāḷ kalaviyilē eḻunta ēkaciva pōkaveḷḷat tiraṇṭupaṭāḷ eṉiṉum emmatamō ekkulamō eṉṟuniṉaip puḷatēl ivaḷmatamum ivaḷkulamum ellāmum civamē cammatamō tēvartiru vāymalara vēṇṭum capaiyilnaṭam purikiṉṟa taṉipperiya turaiyē.
translation: That god of love has shot not one arrow, but all five. She holds onto her precious life only from a desire to attain grace. She has not the slightest trace of worldly passion; even so, she is not separate from the flood of singular Siva-bliss that arises in union. If you have any thought as to what her creed or clan might be, know that her creed, her clan, and her everything is Siva. Do you consent? Your sacred lips must blossom and speak, O singular, great Lord who dances in the Sabai!
commentary: The soul's longing for God is portrayed as an unbearable assault, like being shot by all five arrows of the god of love. The friend makes clear that this is a pure, all-consuming desire for the experience of Siva-bliss, the joy of oneness with the divine. By declaring that the soul's creed and clan are now "Siva," she argues that the soul has lost its old identity and can only be defined by its relationship with God.

translit: aṅkaliṭṭakaḷattaḻakar ampalavar tiruttōḷ ācaiyeṉum pēyakaṟṟal āvatilai eṉavē poṅkaliṭṭa tāyarmukam toṅkaliṭṭup pōṉār pūvaimukam pūmukampōl pūrittu makiḻntāḷ eṅkaḷiṭṭam tiruvaruḷmaṅ kalañcūṭṭal aṉṟi iraṇṭupaṭā toṉṟākki iṉpaṭaivit tiṭavē taṅkaḷiṭṭam yātutiru vāymalara vēṇṭum capaiyilnaṭam purikiṉṟa taṉipperiya turaiyē.
translation: Realizing it is impossible to cast out the demon of desire for the sacred shoulders of the Lord of the Ambalam, the beautiful one with the poison-stained throat, the faces of her scolding mothers fell in dismay. This maiden's face, however, blossomed like a flower, swelling with joy. Our desire is for you to bestow the auspicious garland of your divine grace, making her one with you without division, and granting her bliss. What is your desire? Your sacred lips must blossom and speak, O singular, great Lord who dances in the Hall!
commentary: The soul's spiritual longing is so powerful that her worldly family despairs, seeing it as a "demon of desire" they cannot control. While they grieve, the soul herself is radiant with joy. The friend pleads with God, the beautiful one of the Ambalam (hall of consciousness), to complete the union by bestowing his grace, which is poetically imagined as an auspicious wedding garland.

translit: paṉampaḻamē eṉiṉumintap pacitavirttāl pōtum pārumeṉap pakarkiṉṟa pāvaiyarpōl pakarāḷ iṉampaḻamō kaṅkalantāḷ civāṉupavat tallāl entaaṉu pavaṅkaḷilum iccaiillāḷ avartam maṉampaḻamō kāyōeṉ ṟaṟintuvara viṭuttāḷ maṟṟavarpōl kācupaṇat tācaivaittu varuntāḷ taṉampaḻamō tēvartiru vāymalara vēṇṭum capaiyilnaṭam purikiṉṟa taṉipperiya turaiyē.
translation: She does not speak like those women who say, "I'll take even a palmyra fruit, as long as it satisfies this hunger." She is immersed in the flood of that peerless, ripe fruit; she has no desire for any experience other than the experience of Siva. She sent me to find out if your heart is ripe or unripe. Unlike others, she does not grieve with desire for coins and cash. Are her breasts the ripe fruit you seek? Your sacred lips must blossom and speak, O singular, great Lord who dances in the Hall!
commentary: The soul's desire is absolute and uncompromising. Unlike those who would settle for any small spiritual comfort to ease their "hunger," she desires only the full, ripe fruit of the direct experience of Siva. She has sent her friend to determine if God's heart is "ripe," meaning ready and willing to reciprocate this love. The verse dismisses worldly wealth and continues the intimate lover-beloved metaphor.

translit: pullavarē poyulaka pōkamuṟa viḻaivār puṇṇiyarē civapōkam poruntutaṟku viḻaivār kallavarē maṇiivarē eṉṟaṟintāḷ ataṉāl kaṉaviṭaiyum poyyuṟavu karutukilāḷ ciṟitum nallavarē eṉiṉumumai nāṭārēl avarai naṉkumati yāḷivaḷai naṇṇaeṇṇam uḷatō vallavarē numatutiru vāymalara vēṇṭum vayaṅkutiru maṇimaṉṟil vāḻperiya turaiyē.
translation: Only the base desire the pleasures of this false world; the virtuous desire to attain the bliss of Siva. She knows who is a stone and who is a gem. Therefore, she does not consider any false relationship in the slightest, even in her dreams. Even if people are good, she does not value them if they do not seek you. Do you intend to draw near to her? O all-powerful one, your sacred lips must blossom and speak, O great Lord who dwells in the radiant Hall of Gems!
commentary: A clear distinction is made between those who chase fleeting worldly pleasures and the virtuous who seek only the bliss of Siva. The soul is presented as having sharp spiritual discernment, able to tell a "stone" from a "gem." Her loyalty is absolute: she has no time for anyone, however good they may seem, if they do not seek God. The poem ends with a direct question: given her purity and devotion, will you finally draw near to her?

translit: tattuvarum tattuvañcey talaivarkaḷum piṟarum taṉittaṉiyē valintuvantu taṉetirniṟ kiṉṟār ettuṇaiyum maṟṟavarai ēṟeṭuttup pārāṉ iruviḻikaḷ nīrcorivāḷ eṉṉuyirnā yakaṉē ottuyiril kalantukoṇṭa uṭaiyāyeṉ ṟumaiyē ōtukiṉṟāḷ ivaḷaḷavil uttamarē umatu cittametu tēvartiru vāymalara vēṇṭum ciṟcapaiyil poṟcapaiyil tikaḻperiya turaiyē.
translation: The Tattvas, the masters who command the Tattvas, and others all forcefully come and stand before her, one by one. She does not even glance up at them. Her two eyes pour tears as she chants only of you, saying, "O Lord of my life! Master who has mingled as one with my soul!" Regarding her, O supreme one, what is your will? Your sacred lips must blossom and speak, O great Lord who shines in the Chit Sabhai and the Pon Sabai.
commentary: The soul's devotion to the supreme God makes her turn away from all lower spiritual powers. Even the Tattvas (the fundamental principles of reality) and the cosmic beings who control them fail to capture her attention. Her entire being is focused on the one Lord who has merged with her own soul, and she weeps constantly for him. The messenger asks God directly what his intention is toward this soul who worships him in the Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness) and Pon Sabai (Golden Hall), sacred centers of divine manifestation.

translit: aṉṉaiyaikkaṇ ṭammānī ampalatteṉ kaṇavar aṭiyavaḷēl mikavaruka allaḷeṉil iṅkē eṉṉaiuṉak kirukkiṉṟa tēkukaeṉ ṟuraippāḷ iccaielām ummiṭattē icaintaṉaḷiṅ kivaḷai muṉṉaiyaḷeṉ ṟeṇṇātīr tāḻttiruppīr āṉāl muṭukiuyir viṭuttiṭuvāḷ kaṭukivaral uḷatēl maṉṉavarē umatutiru vāymalara vēṇṭum vayaṅkutiru maṇimaṉṟil vāḻperiya turaiyē.
translation: When she sees her mother, she says, “Ma’am, if you are a devotee of my husband in the Ambalam, you are most welcome. If not, what business do you have here? Go away.” All her desires are set on you; do not think of her as the person she was before. If you delay, she will quickly give up her life. If you intend to come swiftly, O King, your sacred mouth must blossom with the word, O great Lord who lives in the shining, jeweled hall.
commentary: A soul's devotion to God becomes the sole standard for all its relationships. Here, the pining soul, personified as a woman, tells her own mother she is welcome only if she is also a devotee of the Lord of the Ambalam (the sacred hall). The messenger warns God that the soul's transformation is complete and she cannot bear any more delay; her life now depends on his swift arrival.

translit: karavaṟiyā ampalatteṉ kaṇavaraikkaṇ ṭalatu kaṇtuyilēṉ uṇṭikoḷēṉ kaḷittamarēṉ eṉpāḷ iravaṟiyāḷ pakalaṟiyāḷ etirvarukiṉ ṟavarai iṉṉavareṉ ṟaṟiyāḷiṅ kiṉṉaluḻak kiṉṟāḷ varavetirpārt tuḻalkiṉṟāḷ ivaḷaḷavil umatu maṉakkaruttiṉ vaṇṇametu vāymalara vēṇṭum viravumoru kaṇamumiṉit tāḻkkiluyir tariyāḷ meyppotuvil naṭampuriyum mikapperiya turaiyē.
translation: She declares, “Until I see my husband in the guileless Ambalam, I will not close my eyes to sleep, I will not take food, I will not sit in happiness.” She does not know night from day. She does not recognize those who approach her. She is suffering here. She wanders about, expecting your arrival. Regarding her, whatever your heart's intention is, your sacred mouth must blossom with the word. If you delay even one more moment, she will not hold on to her life, O greatest Lord who dances in the true common space.
commentary: The pain of separation from God consumes the soul's entire existence. Unable to eat, sleep, or feel joy, the soul loses all awareness of night and day, recognizing no one. Her life has become a constant, suffering-filled wait for God's arrival. The messenger conveys the urgency, warning the Lord who dances in the Meyppodhu (the true common space) that if he waits even a moment longer, her life will be lost.

translit: ūrācai uṭalācai uyirporuḷiṉ ācai uṟṟavarpeṟ ṟavarācai oṉṟumilāḷ umatu pērācaip pēypiṭittāḷ kaḷḷuṇṭu pitaṟṟum piccieṉap pitaṟṟukiṉṟāḷ piṟarpeyarkēṭ ṭiṭilō nārācañ cevipukuntāl eṉṉanali kiṉṟāḷ nāṭaṟinta tituellām naṅkaiivaḷ aḷavil nīrācaip paṭṭatuṇṭēl vāymalara vēṇṭum nittiyamā maṇimaṉṟil nikaḻperiya turaiyē.
translation: She has no desire for town, body, life, or wealth; no desire for relatives or parents. She is possessed by the demon of immense desire for you. She babbles like a madwoman who has drunk toddy. If she hears the names of others, she suffers as if a molten iron rod has entered her ear. The whole country knows all this. If you have any desire for this young woman, your sacred mouth must blossom with the word, O great Lord who manifests in the eternal, great, jeweled hall.
commentary: Intense love for God can look like madness to the world. The soul has abandoned every worldly attachment and is now "possessed" by her desire for God alone, babbling his name like a drunkard. The sound of any other name is physically painful to her. The messenger presents this state of total, obsessive devotion to God and asks if he returns the feeling and will come to her.

translit: eṉṉuyiril kalantukoṇṭār varilavartām irukka iṭampuṉaika eṉkiṉṟāḷ iccaimaya mākit taṉṉuyirtaṉ uṭalmaṟantāḷ iruntaṟiyāḷ paṭuttum tarittaṟiyāḷ eḻunteḻuntu taṉittorucār tirivāḷ aṉṉamuṇa aḻaittālum kēṭpatilāḷ ulakil aṇaṅkaṉaiyār aticayikkum kuṇaṅkaḷpala peṟṟāḷ miṉṉivaḷai viḻaivatuṇṭēl vāymalara vēṇṭum meyppotuvil naṭampuriyum mikapperiya turaiyē.
translation: She says, “If the one who has mingled with my soul comes, prepare a place for him to stay.” Wholly overcome by longing, she has forgotten her own soul and her own body. She cannot stay seated, nor can she bear to lie down; she gets up repeatedly and wanders off alone. Even when called to eat, she does not listen. She has acquired many qualities that make even celestial women in the world marvel. If you desire this lightning-like woman, your sacred mouth must blossom with the word, O greatest Lord who dances in the true common space.
commentary: The soul, having already tasted a moment of divine union, lives in a state of constant, restless anticipation. She has forgotten her own body and the world around her, driven only by the expectation of God's return. Her friend tells God that this intense devotion has given her a beauty and spiritual quality that even celestial beings admire, making the delay in union all the more poignant.

translit: ampalattē naṭampuriyum eṉatutaṉit talaivar aṉpuṭaṉeṉ uḷaṅkalantē aruṭperuñcō tiyiṉāl tampalattē perumpōkan tantiṭuvār itutāṉ cattiyañcat tiyamataṉāl cārntavartām irukka empalattē malaraṇaiyaip puṉaikaeṉap palakāl iyampukiṉṟāḷ ivaḷaḷavil icaintunuma taruḷām cempalattē uṟutaruṇam vāymalara vēṇṭum ciṟcapaipoṟ capaiōṅkit tikaḻperiya turaiyē.
translation: She says repeatedly, “My peerless leader who dances in the Ambalam will lovingly merge with my heart and, through ArutPerunJothi, grant me the great bliss of union in his own realm. This is the truth, the truth! Therefore, prepare a bed of flowers in my space for the one I depend on.” Regarding her, you must consent, and your sacred mouth must blossom, declaring the opportune moment for union in the perfect realm of your grace, O great Lord who shines, exalted in the Chit Sabhai and Ponsabai.
commentary: The soul expresses absolute faith that God will grant the ultimate bliss of union through the power of ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light). So certain is she of this promise that she commands her friends to prepare for his arrival. The companion relays this desperate, faithful plea to God, asking Him to finally speak the word that will make the promised union in the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness) and Ponsabai (golden hall) a reality.

tamil: அங்கு அல் எனப்பிரித்து அவ்விடத்துஇருள் எனப் பொருள்கொள்க - முதற்பதிப்பு.இருள் - நஞ்சு.

translation: Resolve as aṅku + al and take the sense 'darkness in that place'. First edition. iruḷ — 'poison'.

sections.title: The Heroine Tells Her Mother About the Hero's Actions

translit: aṉṉappārp pālaḻa kāmnilai yūṭē ampalam ceytuniṉ ṟāṭum aḻakar tuṉṉappārt teṉṉuyirt tōḻiyum nāṉum cūtāṭu kiṉṟaac cūḻalil vantē uṉṉaippārt tuṉṉuḷḷē eṉṉaippā rātē ūraippārt tōṭi uḻalkiṉṟa peṇṇē eṉṉaippār eṉkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā eṉkai piṭikkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā.
translation: He is the Beautiful One who dances, having made the Ambalam his own, in a state of beauty like a flock of swans. While my dear friend and I were playing a board game, he came near to where we were gathered. He said, "O woman, who looks at yourself but not at me within you, and just runs around looking at the town! Look at me!" What is this, mother! He is grabbing my hand! What is this, mother!
commentary: The soul, speaking as a young woman to her mother, describes how God suddenly interrupted her worldly life. While she was distracted playing a game, He appeared and chided her for looking outward at the world instead of inward at Him, who resides within her. His action is startling and decisive; He grabs her hand, signifying grace pulling the soul away from its distractions and toward a direct relationship with the divine.

translit: atupā vakamukat tāṉanta nāṭṭil ampalam ceytuniṉ ṟāṭum aḻakar vitupā vakamukat tōḻiyum nāṉum meyppā vaṉaiceyyum vēḷaiyil vantu potupā vaṉaiceyyap pōkātō peṇṇē poyppā vaṉaiceytu kaippāṉēṉ aiyō itupāvam eṉkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭiammā eṉkai piṭikkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā.
translation: He is the Beautiful One who dances, having made the Ambalam his own, in the land of bliss that has the nature of the Absolute. While my friend with the moon-like face and I were engaged in true contemplation, he came and said, "O woman, why don't you do the universal contemplation? Why perform this false contemplation and make it bitter? This is a sin!" What is this, mother! He is grabbing my hand! What is this, mother!
commentary: Here, God intervenes in the soul's own spiritual practice. He dismisses her focused meditation as a "false contemplation," urging her toward a "universal contemplation" instead. This is a striking statement: even sincere religious effort can be a distraction if it is not aligned with a universal, all-encompassing awareness of God. Grace acts forcefully to pull the soul from limited, personal spiritual exercises into a boundless communion.

translit: aṟaṅkātal ceytēṉai āṇṭukoṇ ṭiṅkē aruṭperuñ cōtiyāy āṭum aḻakar uṟaṅkāta vaṇṇañciṟ ṟampalama pāṭi utikkiṉṟa oṇmaiyil tutikkiṉṟa pōtu puṟaṅkātal ceyvārpōl ceyyātē peṇṇē poṟkampam ēṟiṉai corkkamaṅ kappāl iṟaṅkātē eṉkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā eṉkai piṭikkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā.
translation: He is the Beautiful One who dances here as the Vast Grace-Light, having accepted me, who loved righteousness. While I was sleeplessly singing of the Cirrambalam and praising the rising light, he said, "O woman, do not act like those who pursue external love! You have climbed the golden pillar; heaven is beyond that. Do not descend!" What is this, mother! He is grabbing my hand! What is this, mother!
commentary: On the spiritual path, it is easy to become satisfied with early progress or to be tempted to turn back. Here, the devotee's praise of the Cirrambalam (the small, inner sacred space) is like climbing a golden pillar. God warns her not to treat this devotion like an ordinary "external love" and not to descend from this height. The goal is complete union with the ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light, which lies beyond.

translit: annāḷvan teṉṟaṉai āṇṭaruḷ ceyta ayyar amutareṉ aṉpar aḻakar naṉṉāḷ kaḻikkiṉṟa naṅkaiya rōṭu nāṉam palampāṭi naṇṇuṟum pōtu piṉṉāḷeṉ ṟeṇṇip pitaṟṟātē peṇṇē pēraruṭ cōtip perumaṇam ceynāḷ innāḷē eṉkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā eṉkai piṭikkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā.
translation: He is my Master, my Nectar, my Beloved, the Beautiful One, who came that day and graciously made me his own. While I was with other women who were spending their good days, singing of the Ambalam and drawing near, he said, "O woman, do not babble, thinking it will be some future day! The day of the great wedding of the Vast Grace-Light is this very day!" What is this, mother! He is grabbing my hand! What is this, mother!
commentary: A common human tendency is to postpone our deepest spiritual aspirations, believing the time is not yet right. God directly refutes this spiritual procrastination. He declares that the "great wedding," the soul's union with the divine ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light), is not a reward to be earned in a distant future. It is a possibility available this very day, right now.

translit: tappōtu vāruḷam cārntiṭa uṉṉār cattiyar uttamar nittama ṇāḷar oppōta oṇṇāta meyppōta maṉṟiṉ uṇmaiyaip pāṭināṉ aṇmaiyil niṉṟēṉ appōteṉ ṟeṇṇi ayarntiṭēl peṇṇē aṉpuṭai niṉṉaiyām iṉpuṟak kūṭal ippōtē eṉkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā eṉkai piṭikkiṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā.
translation: He is the Truthful One, the Supreme One, the Eternal Bridegroom, who does not think to approach the hearts of those who go astray. I stood nearby, singing of the truth of the peerless Hall of True Knowledge. He said, "O woman, do not despair, thinking it will be 'then'!
