If that great prakṛti itself, and Kuṭilai its source, and the union of all powers from Parai onward that the mind conceives, if all of them emerge from just a slight stirring that appears from the luminous, flower-like foot that performs the Turīya dance in the universal expanse, then what can be said of the measure of the greatness of grace of our Leader, who performs as the rare, great substance? You do not realize it, my friend.
commentary: The entire cosmos, from the physical elements to the subtlest principles like prakṛti (primordial nature) and the highest divine powers (śaktis) like Parai (the supreme power), are all born from a single, tiny movement of God. His dance takes place in Turīya, the state of pure consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and sleep. This means that all of manifest reality is just a minor effect of a transcendental creative act, making God's own substance and grace immeasurably great.

translit: poṉvaṇṇap pūtamutal taṉmaiuṇmai akattē poṟpuṟamāk karuviḷakkam poruntaveṇmai cemmai taṉvaṇṇap pacumaiyoṭu karumaikalap pākum taṉmaiyiṉil taṉmaiyatāyt taṉittataṟkōr mutalāy maṉavaṇṇat toḷiuruvam uyirppiṉoṭu tōṉṟa vālaṇukkūṭ ṭaṅkaḷaiav vakainiṟuvi naṭattum miṉvaṇṇat tiruccapaiyil āṭukiṉṟa patattiṉ meyvaṇṇam pukaluvatār viḷampāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: The true nature of the elements, beginning with the golden one, is internal. It is a nature formed from the blend of white, red, its own green, and black, giving a glorious external manifestation to the germinal cause. Being that very nature, and being a unique source for it, it makes a luminous form of the mind's color appear along with life breath, establishing and conducting the assemblies of pure atoms in just that way. Who can declare the true nature of the foot that dances in the Sacred Hall, which is the color of lightning? Tell me, my friend.
commentary: The physical world is built from subtle, inner qualities, which Vallalar describes as a blend of primal colors. God, as the ultimate source, combines these energies to create the atomic structures of matter and breathes life into them. This act of creation is His dance, performed in the Sacred Hall of consciousness. Its nature is like a flash of lightning: brilliant, instantaneous, and powerful, a reality whose essence is beyond description.

translit: poṟpuṭaiya aiṅkaruvuk kātāra karaṇam pukaṉṟaaṟu kōṭiavaik kāṟilakkam avaṟṟuk kaṟpuṟumōr aṟupatiṉā yiramavaṟṟuk kaṭaiyā ṟāyiramāṅ kavaṟṟukkōr aṟunūṟiṅ kivaikkē viṟpoliyum aṟupatumaṟ ṟivaikkāṟiṅ kinta viyaṉkaraṇa cattikaḷai virittuviḷak kuvatāyc ciṟparamāy maṇimaṉṟil tirunaṭaṉam puriyum tiruvaṭiyiṉ perumaievar ceppuvarkāṇ tōḻi.
translation: For the five glorious generative causes, the foundational instruments are said to be six crore. For these, there are six lakh. For them, a specified sixty thousand. For them, six thousand. For these, six hundred. For these, a shining sixty, and for them, six here. As that which expands and illuminates all these vast instrumental powers, who can speak of the greatness of the sacred foot that performs the holy dance in the Jeweled Hall as transcendent consciousness? Look, my friend.
commentary: Reality is built upon a staggering number of causal forces, which Vallalar calls foundational instruments (ādhāra karaṇam). By listing a cascade of huge numbers, from crores down to six, he gives a sense of the mind-boggling complexity of the universe's structure. Yet, all these countless instrumental powers (karaṇa śaktis) are not independent; they are all brought to life and governed by the single divine dance of transcendent consciousness (cit-param).

translit: ēṟṟamuṟum aiṅkaruvuk kātāra karaṇam eḻukōṭi īṅkivaṟṟuk kēḻilakkam ivaikkē tōṟṟamuṟum eḻupatiṉā yiramivaṟṟuk keḻumai tuṉṉiyanū ṟivaṟṟiṉukkuc collum eḻupatutāṉ āṟṟaluṟum ivaitamakkōr ēḻāmik karaṇam aṉaittiṉaiyum taṉittaṉiyē tōṟṟinilai poruttic cāṟṟariya vaṭivuvaṇṇam cuvaippayaṉuṇ ṭākkum cāmitiru vaṭipperumai cāṟṟuvatār tōḻi.
translation: For the five eminent generative causes, the foundational instruments are seven crore. For these, seven lakh. For them, seventy thousand appear. For these, seven thousand; for them, a dense seven hundred; for these, a stated seventy; and for these potent ones, there is a seven. As that which makes all these instruments appear individually, establishes them, and creates their indescribable forms, colors, tastes, and benefits, who can declare the greatness of the Master's sacred foot, my friend?
commentary: Like the previous verse, this passage uses another series of enormous numbers to emphasize the infinite layers of causality that create our world. Everything we experience, from the shape and color of an object to its taste and purpose, is the result of these countless instrumental powers. And all of them, in their individuality, are created and sustained by the one "Master's sacred foot," showing that a single divine source is behind all of creation's endless variety.

translit: viḷaṅkiyaaiṅ karuccatti ōraṉantaṅ karuvil viḷaikiṉṟa cattikaḷōr aṉantamviḷai vellām vaḷampeṟavē tarukiṉṟa cattikaḷōr aṉantam māṇpaṭaiyat taruvikkum cattikaḷōr aṉantam uḷaṅkoḷaniṉ ṟatiṭṭikkum cattikaḷōr aṉantam ōṅkiya:ic cattikaḷait taṉittaṉiyē iyakkit taḷaṅkoḷaīṇ ṭavvavaṟṟiṟ kuṭpuṟamniṉ ṟoḷirum cāmitiru vaṭipperumai cāṟṟuvatār tōḻi.
translation: The manifest five generative powers are an infinity. The powers that arise from the generative cause are an infinity. The powers that bestow richness on all that arises are an infinity. The powers that cause things to attain greatness are an infinity. The powers that stand and preside so the mind may grasp them are an infinity. Activating each of these exalted powers individually, and shining here from within and without them so they are held firm, who can declare the greatness of the Master's sacred foot, my friend?
commentary: The universe is filled with infinite types of creative energy, or śaktis. There are infinite generative powers (karu-śakti), infinite powers of manifestation, and infinite powers that sustain and enrich creation. Vallalar's point is that while these divine energies are countless, they are not chaotic. Each one is individually activated and guided by the one "Master's sacred foot," which works both inside and outside of them to hold the cosmos in perfect order.

translit: kāṇikiṉṟa aiṅkaruviṉ vittiṉiyal palavum karutuṟumaṅ kurattiṉiyal paṟpalavum aṭiyiṉ māṇukiṉṟa iyalkaḷpala palappalavum naṭuvil maṉṉumiyal palapalavum palappalavum muṭiyiṉ pūṇumiyal aṉantavakai purintapala palavum poruntuvatāy avvavaṟṟiṉ puṇarkkaiyuntāṉ āki ēṇukiṉṟa avaikaḷukkuṭ paṟṟāmal naṭikkum eḻiṟkaruṇaip patapperumai iyampuvatār tōḻi.
translation: The many natures of the seed of the five visible sources, the myriad natures of the conceivable sprout, the many, many excellent natures of the base, the many, many, many established natures of the middle, and the infinite kinds of many, many natures assumed by the crown, being all that is fitting, becoming the very union of all these things, yet acting within them all without attachment, who can speak of the greatness of those beautiful, compassionate Feet, O friend?
commentary: Using the image of a growing plant, this verse shows the divine presence at every stage of creation, from the seed of potential to the final flourishing. The Master's Feet are the creator and the very substance of each part, their combination, and the unattached actor playing within it all. This expresses the paradox of God being both the creation itself and completely free from it.

translit: viṇṇiṭattē mutaṉmuppū viriyaatil orupū vāyaṅkucattik kūṭṭattāl vantaṉaōr aṉantam paṇṇuṟumat taṉmaiyuḷē tiṇmaiorukōṭi palittacattik kūṭṭattāl paṇittaṉaōr aṉantam eṇṇuṟumit tiṇmaikaḷum ivaṟṟiṉatu vikaṟpam ellāmum taṉittaṉiniṉ ṟilaṅkanilai purintē viṇṇeṉṉum paṭiavaṟṟil kalantukala vātu viḷaiyāṭum aṭipperumai viḷampuvatār tōḻi.
translation: In the expanse, the first three flowers blossom. From one of those flowers, through a union of Saktis, an infinity of things came forth. Within that nature, a crore of densities arose, and through the union of potent Saktis, an infinity of things were ordained. Making all these countless densities and their variations stand and shine separately, the Feet play, mingling and not mingling with them in what is called the expanse. Who can declare the greatness of these Feet, O friend?
commentary: Creation begins as a subtle blossoming in the vastness of space. From these primary "flowers," or principles, unfolds the infinite variety and density of the material world. The divine Feet are described as a playful presence, participating in this cosmic game by being both mixed into creation and separate from it.

translit: viṇṇiṭattē mutaṉmuppū viriyaatil orupū viriyaatiṉ maṟṟorupū virintiṭa:iv vaimpūk kaṇṇiṭattē piṟitorupū kaṇmalara atilē kaṭṭaviḻa vēṟorupū viṭṭaeḻu pūvum peṇṇiṭattē nāṉkāki āṇiṭattē mūṉṟāyp pirivilavāyp pirivuḷavāyp piṟaṅkiyuṭal karaṇam naṇṇiṭattērn tiyaṟṟiatiṉ naṭuniṉṟu viḷaṅkum nallatiru vaṭipperumai colluvatār tōḻi.
translation: In the expanse, the first three flowers blossom. From them, one flower blossoms; from that, another flower blossoms. As another flower opens within these five, and from that, yet another unfurls, making seven flowers in total, these become four in the female and three in the male. Being both inseparable and separable, they shine, carefully creating the body and the inner faculties. Who can tell the greatness of the good, sacred Feet that stand in their midst and illumine them, O friend?
commentary: The cosmic principles of creation, symbolized by blossoming flowers, are the same principles that form the human body. Vallalar makes a direct, intimate link between the universal and the individual, showing how cosmic forces are present and divided within male and female forms. The same divine grace that orchestrates the universe also meticulously builds our bodies and minds.

translit: vaṇpūvil vaṭivupala vaṇṇaṅkaḷ palamēl matikkumiyal palaoḷiyiṉ vāymaipala oḷikkuḷ naṇpūṟum cattipala cattikaḷuḷ vayaṅkum nātaṅkaḷ palanāta naṭuvaṇaiōr kalaiyil paṇpāya naṭaṅkaḷpala palapeyarppum kāṭṭum patikaḷpala ivaikkellām patiyākip potuvil kaṇpāya ivaṟṟiṉoṭu kalantukala vāmal kāṇukiṉṟa tiruvaṭiccīr kaḻaṟuvatār tōḻi.
translation: In the bountiful flower are many forms and many colors. Above them, many esteemed natures; many truths of light; within the light, many intimate Saktis spring forth; within the Saktis shine many Nādams; at the center of Nādam, in a single Kalai (a part of consciousness), are many graceful dances; and there are many lords who display many names. Being the supreme Lord of them all in the common space, the sacred Feet are seen mingling and not mingling with these perceptible things. Who can proclaim the glory of those Feet, O friend?
commentary: The entire universe, with all its forms, colors, lights, powers (śakti), primal sounds (nādam), and even its many gods, is seen as one magnificent, multi-layered reality. The Master’s Feet are the ultimate reality behind it all, the one Lord presiding over this diversity from a common, universal space (potu), witnessing and participating in all things while remaining untouched.

translit: ōṅkiyaaim pūivaikkuḷ oṉṟiṉoṉṟu tiṇmai uṟṟaṉamaṟ ṟatuatuvum paṟṟuvaṉa paṟṟat tāṅkiyamā cattikaḷiṉ peruṅkūṭṭam kalaiyāt taṉmaipurin tāṅkāṅkut taṉittaṉiniṉ ṟilaṅkit tēṅkiyapō tavaikalaiyac ceykaipala purintu tikaḻoḷiyāy aruḷveḷiyāyt tiṟaviloḷiveḷiyil pāṅkuṟanēr viḷaṅkukiṉṟa tiruvaṭiyiṉ perumai pakutturaittu vallavarār pakarāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: Among these lofty five flowers, each is denser than the next. The great assembly of Mahā-Saktis holds them, enabling each to grasp what it grasps, ensuring the assembly does not disperse. They stand and shine separately here and there. When they stagnate, the divine performs many acts to disperse them, shining as radiant light, as the expanse of grace, and shining forth fittingly and directly in the unfailing expanse of light. Tell me, O friend, who is capable of analyzing and describing the greatness of those sacred Feet?
commentary: The "flowers" of creation have different densities, from subtle to gross. They are held in their distinct states by immense powers called mahā-śakti (great powers). Sometimes, however, this cosmic energy can become stagnant. When this happens, the divine intervenes with a burst of light and grace to stir things up and restore the flow of existence. The greatness of this dynamic, ever-present power is impossible to fully analyze or describe.

translit: virintiṭumaiṅ karuviṉilē viṭayacatti aṉanta vitamukaṅkoṇ ṭilakaavai vikitavikaṟ pākip pirintiṭumāṉ ilakkaṇaṅkaḷ palakōṭi piriyāp peruñcatti ilakkaṇaṅkaḷ paṟpalakō ṭikaḷāyt terintiṭunā ṉilakkuḷḷē iruntuveḷip paṭavum ceykaipala purikiṉṟa tiṟaluṭaittā rakamēl erintiṭutī naṭuveḷikkaṇ iruntatiru vaṭiyiṉ ellaiyaiyār collavallār iyampāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: In the expanding five karu, the viṣaya śakti shines with infinite forms. They become varied modifications, splitting into many crores of masculine characteristics and many, many crores of characteristics of the inseparable great śakti. From within the four manifest goals, they emerge and perform many acts. Above this tāraka, who can speak the limit of the sacred feet that exist in the space amidst the burning fire? Tell me, my friend.
commentary: The five primordial wombs, or karu, are the sources of creation. From them arises the viṣaya śakti, the power of sense experience, which then unfolds into the countless masculine and feminine characteristics that make up our world. Above all this creative activity is a guiding light or star (tāraka), and even beyond that, in a transcendent space described as a "burning fire," resides the ultimate divine presence, whose true nature no one can know.

translit: tōṉṟiyaaiṅ karuviṉilē collarumōr iyaṟkait tulaṅkumatil palakōṭik kulaṅkoḷkurut tuvikaḷ āṉṟuviḷaṅ kiṭumavaṟṟiṉ acalaipala kōṭi amaintiṭummaṟ ṟavaikaḷuḷē amalaikaḷ ōraṉantam ēṉṟuniṟain tiṭumavaṟṟiṟ kaṇippataṉuk karitāy ilaṅkupira kācikaḷtām iruntaṉamaṟ ṟivaṟṟil ūṉṟiyatā rakacatti ōṅkumatiṉ naṭuvē uṟṟatiru vaṭipperumai uraippavarār tōḻi.
translation: In the manifested five karu, an indescribable nature shines. Within it, many crores of lineages of kuruttuvi-s mature and glow. Among them are many crores of acalai-s. Within those, an infinity of amalai-s are accepted and fill them. Among them are pirakācikai-s, shining and difficult to count. The tāraka śakti is firmly established in these and rises high. Who can speak of the greatness of the sacred feet at its center, friend?
commentary: Vallalar offers a glimpse into the staggering complexity of the spiritual cosmos by naming successive orders of subtle beings or powers: kuruttuvi, acalai ('the unmoving ones'), amalai ('the pure ones'), and pirakācikai ('the luminous ones'). This list is meant to overwhelm the intellect, showing how vast and layered creation truly is. At the heart of this entire cosmic hierarchy is a central guiding power, the tāraka śakti, and at the center of that power are the divine Feet.

translit: uṟaintiṭumaiṅ karuviṉilē uruvacatti vikaṟpam uṉṉutaṟkum uṇarvataṟkum oṇṇāeṇ ṇilavē niṟaintaavai taṉittaṉiyē nikaḻntilaṅka avaikkuḷ nērmaioṇmai uṟuvittan nērmaioṇmai akattē kuṟaintilavām palavēṟu kuṇaṅkaḷuṟap purintu kuṇaṅkaḷuḷē kuṟikaḷpala kūṭṭuvittāṅ kamarntē maṟaintamaṇam veḷippaṭuttum malaraṭiyiṉ perumai vakutturaikka vallavarār vaḻuttāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: In the abiding five karu, the modifications of rūpa śakti are countless, impossible to think of or perceive. These abundant powers manifest and shine individually. Within them, He bestows rightness and radiance. Within that rightness and radiance, He creates many different, undiminished qualities. Within those qualities, He joins many signs and presides. Who is able to classify and speak of the greatness of the flower-like feet that reveal the hidden fragrance? Praise it, my friend.
commentary: The power that creates form, the rūpa śakti, is so vast and varied that it is impossible for the mind to grasp. Into this infinite potential, the divine brings order ("rightness") and light ("radiance"), creating all the qualities and symbols we see in the world. The final line is beautiful: the divine presence, the "flower-like feet," releases a hidden fragrance, revealing the secret, sweet essence of all existence.

translit: cūḻntiṭumaiṅ karuviṉilē corupacatti pētam colliṉoṭu maṉaṅkaṭanta ellaiyilā taṉavē tāḻntilavāy avaiavaiyum taṉittaṉiniṉ ṟilaṅkat takumavaikkuḷ navaviḷakkam tarittanta viḷakkam vāḻntiṭaōr cattinilai vayaṅkiyuṟap purintu matikkumantac cattitaṉil maṉṉucattar āki āḻntiṭumōr paramparattai acaittuniṉṟu naṭikkum aṭipperumai uraippavarār aṟiyāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: In the encompassing five karu, the distinctions of svarūpa śakti are limitless, beyond speech and mind. Without being diminished, each one is fit to stand and shine individually. Within them, He bestows the nine illuminations. To make that illumination thrive, He makes a state of śakti shine brightly. In that esteemed śakti He becomes the abiding Śaktar, and stands moving the deep Paramparam, the Supreme beyond the supreme, and dances. Who can speak of the greatness of those feet? You do not know it, my friend. Who can speak of the greatness of those feet? You know, my friend.
commentary: After describing the power of form, Vallalar turns to svarūpa śakti, the power of essential nature, which is also limitless and beyond speech and mind. God gives it the nine illuminations, establishes a state of śakti to sustain them, becomes the Śaktar, the possessor of that power, and stands moving even the deep Paramparam, the Supreme beyond the supreme, as He dances.

translit: pacuniṟatta aiṅkaruvil pakarntacuvait taṉmai paṟpalakō ṭikaḷāmav vuṟpavacat tikaḷil vacuniṟatta vivitanava cattipala kōṭi vayaṅkumavaik kuḷāti vayaṅkuvaḷav vāti tacaniṟatta vākaatil taṉittaṉiōṅ kāri cārntiṭuvaḷ avaḷakattē taṉipparaicārn tiṭuvaḷ ticainiṟattap parainaṭuvil tirunaṭaṉam puriyum tiruvaṭiyiṉ peruvaṭiyaic ceppuvatār tōḻi.
translation: In the green-colored five karu, the spoken qualities of taste are many, many crores. In those generative śakti-s, many crores of the nine various śakti-s of brilliant color shine. Within them, Ādi shines. That Ādi has ten colors. In each, Ōṅkāri individually takes her place. Within her, the unique Parai takes her place. Who can speak of the grandeur of the sacred feet that perform the sacred dance in the center of Parai, who has the colors of the directions? Tell me, friend.
commentary: Here, creation is described as an unfolding of the divine feminine power, śakti. Starting from the five primal sources (karu), this power generates qualities like taste and cascades into various energies. Vallalar depicts this as a series of nested principles: first Ādi (the Primal One), within her is Ōṅkāri (the power of the sacred sound Om), and at the very core is Parai (the Supreme Power). The sacred dance of God occurs at the center of Parai, showing that the ultimate reality is found in the innermost heart of the divine feminine.

translit: pūttacuṭarp pūakattē puṟattēcūḻ iṭattē pūttumikak kāyttumati amutoḻukap paḻuttu māttakaiya peruñjōti maṇimaṉṟuḷ viḷaṅkum vaṇṇamoru ciṟitaṟiya māṭṭāmal maṟaikaḷ ēttuvatum ēṟuvatum iṟaṅkuvatum āki irukkiṉṟa eṉṟuṇarntōr iyampiṭilic ciṟiyēṉ tōttirañcey tammaikaṇṭu makiḻntiṭaam maṉṟil tulaṅkumaṭip perumaiyaieṉ colluvatu tōḻi.
translation: It blossoms in the flower of light, within, without, and in the surrounding space. It flowers profusely, forms fruit, and ripens until the moon’s nectar flows. The Vedas, unable to know even a little of the way the great Jothi of magnificent nature shines in the Maṇimaṉṟam, can only praise, ascend, and descend. Even if those who have realized this speak of it, what can I, this little one, say about the greatness of the feet that shine in that hall, for me to praise and rejoice in seeing? What can I say, O friend?
commentary: The supreme divine reality is a Great Light, or Jothi, that shines in a "hall of gems" (Maṇimaṉṟam), a symbol for a perfected state of consciousness. This reality is so vast that even the Vedas, the most sacred Hindu scriptures, cannot fully comprehend it; they are depicted as struggling to ascend and descend, never quite reaching the truth. Faced with this immensity, the speaker expresses deep humility, acknowledging that if even the wisest texts fall short, words are inadequate to describe the direct experience of God.

translit: vaḷampeṟuviṉ aṇukkuḷḷēoru matiiravi aḻalāy vayaṅkiyatā rakaiyāyiv vakaiaṉaittum tōṟṟum taḷampeṟuciṟ colitaparā cattimayam ākit taṉittacatti māṉākit tattuvamel lāmpōy uḷampukuta maṇimaṉṟil tirunaṭamcey taruḷum orutalaivaṉ cēvaṭiccir uraippavarev vulakil aḷantaṟiyum eṉamaṟaikaḷ araṟṟumeṉil ciṟiya aṭicciyurait tiṭappaṭumō aṟiyāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: Within a single fertile atom, it manifests as a moon, a sun, a fire, and a shining star. Becoming the very form of the supreme Sakti, the source-ground from which all these things appear, and becoming the singular Saktimān who transcends all tattvas, the one Lord graciously performs the holy dance in the Hall of Gems, entering the heart. If the Vedas themselves cry out, "Who in any world can measure and know this enough to describe it?", how could it possibly be described by this lowly handmaiden? Do you not know this, my friend?
commentary: The entire cosmos, with its sun, moon, and stars, is present in potential within a single tiny atom. This is because all of creation emerges from the supreme divine power, parā śakti. God is the sole possessor of this power (śaktimān), existing beyond all the cosmic principles (tattvas) that structure reality. This same immeasurable being dances in the "hall of gems" that is the enlightened heart. The verse emphasizes that this truth is beyond all intellectual measure, accessible only through direct inner realization.

translit: paraviyaaiṅ karuviṉilē paruvacatti vayattē paraiatiṭṭit tiṭanāta vintumayak kattē viraviyatat tuvaaṇukkaḷ oṉṟōṭoṉ ṟāyoṉṟi viḷaṅkaavaṟ ṟaṭinaṭuvī ṟivaṟṟiṉilmū vitamāy uraviyaluṟ ṟuyiriyakki aṟivaiaṟi vittē ōṅkutiru ampalattil oḷinaṭaṉam puriyum taraviyaliṟ ṟitueṉayār terinturaippār ciṟiya tamiyaḷurait tiṭuntaramō cāṟṟāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: In the pervasive five causes, under the sway of the manifest Sakti, as the supreme one presides in the fusion of Nāda and Vindu, the atoms of the tattvas mingle and merge one with another to shine. Exerting force in their beginning, middle, and end in three different ways, it impels life and makes consciousness know. Who can truly know and declare, "This is the nature of the radiant dance performed in the exalted Tiru Ampalam"? Is it of a quality that I, a small, solitary woman, can describe? Tell me, my friend.
commentary: The entire universe comes into being through a divine dance. Vallalar offers a poetic vision of creation where primal sound, Nāda, and a primal point of light, Vindu, merge to form the building blocks of reality. This divine energy is what animates every living thing and awakens consciousness. The deepest mystery is a living, creative dance that we are all part of.

translit: cōtimalai orutalaiyil cōtivaṭi vākic cūḻntamaṟṟōr talaiñāṉa corūpamaya māki ōtiyavē ṟorutalaiyil upayavaṇṇam āki uraittiṭumaiṅ karuvakaikkōr mupporuḷum utavi ātinaṭu antamilā āṉanta uruvāy ampalattē āṭukiṉṟa aṭiiṇaiyiṉ perumai vētiyaṉum tirumālum uruttiraḷum aṟiyār viḷaivaṟiyēṉ aṟivēṉō viḷampāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: On one side of the mountain of light, it becomes the form of light. On the other surrounding side, it becomes the very form of wisdom. On yet another side, it becomes a form of both. It provides the one threefold substance for the five kinds of causes. The greatness of that pair of feet, dancing in the hall as the form of bliss without beginning, middle, or end, is not known by the Vedic one, Tirumāl, or Rudra. I do not know what will come of this. Will I ever know? Speak, my friend.
commentary: The divine is a unity that expresses itself in many ways: as pure light, as deep wisdom, and as a blend of both. Vallalar states that this supreme reality is the source of everything and is itself a form of endless bliss. Its true nature is so deep that even the great celestial beings of the Hindu tradition, such as Brahma, Vishnu (Tirumāl), and Rudra, cannot fully grasp it.

translit: pūoṉṟē muppūaim pūeḻupū navamām pūirupat taiaimpūvāyp pūttumalarn tiṭavum nāṉoṉṟu maṇamvēṟu vaṇamvēṟu vēṟā naṇṇiviḷaṅ kuṟavumatiṉ naṟpayaṉmāt tiraiyil mēvoṉṟā iruppaatiṉ naṭuniṉṟu ñāṉa viyaṉnaṭaṉam purikiṉṟa viraimalarccē vaṭiyiṉ pāoṉṟu peruntakaimai uraippavarār ciṟiyēṉ pakarntiṭaval lunaḷ allēṉ pārāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: The one flower blossoms and unfolds as three flowers, five flowers, seven flowers, nine flowers, twenty-five flowers, and fifty-one flowers. And though I am one, the fragrances are different and the colors appear distinct. Its good fruit, in an instant, becomes one. Standing in its center, He performs the vast dance of wisdom. Who can describe the unique greatness of those fragrant, flower-like sacred feet? I, this little one, am not able to declare it. Look, my friend.
commentary: The One God blossoms into the beautiful diversity of the many. Vallalar uses the metaphor of a single flower becoming many flowers of different colors and scents. The numbers mentioned (3, 5, 7, etc.) refer to the complex categories of reality (tattvas) described in Indian philosophy. He is saying that all these different systems and realities spring from one source, and the goal of the spiritual path is to experience the single, unified essence that lies behind them all.

sections.title: Asserting Her Exclusive Bond to Her Friend

translit: nayantanaṭa nāyakaruṉ nāyakarē eṉiṉum nāṭiyaman tiraṅkaḷcila kūṭiurai yiṭavē viyantumaṟṟait tēvarelām varavumavar nēyam virumpātē iruppateṉnī eṉkiṉṟāy tōḻi vayantarumin tirarpiramar nāraṇarkā raṇarkaḷ maṟṟaiyarkaḷ maṟṟaiyarkaḷ maṟṟaiyarkaḷ evarkkum payantakuṭi allaṭināṉ tirucciṟṟam palattē patinaṭañcey aṭippaṇikkē patittakuṭi aṟiyē.
translation: O friend, you ask, “Even if the beloved Lord of the Dance is your husband, when other gods come in wonder, seeking to speak sacred words with you, why do you show no desire for their affection? What is this?” My dear, I am not from a lineage that fears the mighty Indras, Brahmas, Narayanas, the causal lords, or any others, and others, and others. Know this: my lineage is one established solely for service to the feet that perform the sovereign dance in Thiru Chitrambalam.
commentary: The friend asks why the soul ignores the other gods who come to her. Her answer is a declaration of belonging: she is not of a family that bows in fear to Indras, Brahmas, Narayanas or any others. Her lineage exists for one purpose only, service to the dancing feet in Thiru Chitrambalam. Devotion to the One leaves no room for fear of the many.

translit: nayantanaṭa nāyakaruṉ nāyakarē eṉiṉum naṅkainiṉaik kaṇṭiṭavē nāṭimaṟṟait talaivar viyantuvaru kiṉṟatukaṇ ṭupacariyā tiṅkē mēlnōkki iruppateṉnī eṉkiṉṟāy tōḻi vayantarupār mutalnāta varaiyuḷanāṭ ṭavarkkum maṟṟavarai naṭattukiṉṟa mānāṭṭār tamakkum payantakuṭi allaṭināṉ tirucciṟṟam palattē patinaṭañcey aṭippaṇikkē patittakuṭi aṟiyē.
translation: O friend, you ask, “Even if the beloved Lord of the Dance is your husband, O lady, when other lords come seeking to see you, why do you watch them come in wonder and yet not greet them, instead looking upward and remaining aloof? What is this?” My dear, I am not from a lineage that fears the inhabitants of the realms from the mighty earth up to Nada, nor the great beings who rule over them. Know this: I am from a lineage established solely for service to the feet that perform the sovereign dance in Thiru Chitrambalam.
commentary: Complete devotion to the one supreme God renders all other deities and celestial powers insignificant. The soul explains that her lineage is defined by service to the Lord of the Dance in Thiru Chitrambalam, the sacred hall of consciousness. Because of this exclusive allegiance, she has no reason to fear or feel obligated to any other being in the cosmic hierarchy, from those on earth up to the level of Nada (primordial sound). This is a declaration of spiritual freedom.

translit: nayantanaṭa nāyakaruṉ nāyakarē eṉiṉum nāṭummaṟṟait talaivartamaik kaṇṭapoḻu teṉiṉum viyantavarkkōr nalluraiyum collātē tarukki vītiyilē naṭappateṉnī eṉkiṉṟāy tōḻi vayantarumiv vaṇṭapaki raṇṭamaṭṭō nāta varaiyōap pālumuḷa mānāṭṭār tamakkum payantakuṭi allaṭināṉ tirucciṟṟam palattē patinaṭañcey aṭippaṇikkē patittakuṭi aṟiyē.
translation: O friend, you ask, “Even if the beloved Lord of the Dance is your husband, when you see other lords who seek you out, you do not speak a single kind word of admiration to them, but instead walk arrogantly in the street. What is this?” My dear, whether it be the beings of this universe and the outer universes, or those up to the realm of Nada, or even the great beings who exist beyond that, I am not of a lineage that fears any of them. Know this: I am from a lineage established solely for service to the feet that perform the sovereign dance in Thiru Chitrambalam.
commentary: What appears as arrogance to the world is, for the devoted soul, simply a steady focus on the highest. The soul is so absorbed in the highest reality that she cannot be distracted by lesser powers, even those governing entire universes. Her whole existence is dedicated to service of the supreme Lord, and engaging with anything else would be a betrayal of that singular purpose.

translit: kaṭuṅkuṇattōr peṟaṟkariya naṭattaracē niṉakkuk kaṇavareṉi ṉumpiṟaraik kaṇṭapoḻu teṉiṉum naṭuṅkuṇattāl niṉṟucila nalvārttai pakarāy naṅkāyī teṉeṉanī navilkiṉṟāy tōḻi oṭuṅkupala tattuvarkkum tattuvarai naṭattum upayanilait talaivarukkum avartalaivar kaḷukkum naṭuṅkuṭi allaṭināṉ tirucciṟṟam palattē naṭañceyaṭip paṇikkeṉṟē nāṭṭiyanaṟ kuṭiyē.
translation: O friend, you say, “The King of Dance, unattainable by those of harsh nature, may be your husband, O lady. But even when you see others, you do not stand with a humble disposition and speak a few kind words. What is this?” My dear, I am not of a lineage that trembles before the many subservient tattvas, or the lords of the dual state who direct them, or even their lords. I am of a good lineage, established solely for service to the dancing feet in Thiru Chitrambalam.
commentary: The soul's allegiance to God places her beyond the influence of the universe's fundamental operating system. She does not bow to the tattvas (the elemental principles of reality that make up the mind and cosmos) or to the divine lords who direct them. Her devotion is more than a preference for one god over others; it is a state of being that transcends the entire cosmic machinery.

translit: maṭaṅkalantār peṟaṟkariya naṭattaracē niṉakku maṇavāḷar eṉiṉumuṉpāl vārttaimakiḻn turaikka iṭaṅkalanta mūrttikaḷtām vantālaṅ kavarpāl eṇṇamilā tirukkiṉṟāy eṉkoleṉṟāy tōḻi maṭaṅkucama yattalaivar matattalaivar ivarkkum vayaṅkumivark kupakarikkum māttalaivar kaḷukkum aṭaṅkukuṭi allaṭināṉ tirucciṟṟam palattē āṭalaṭip paṇikkeṉṟē amaittakuṭi aṟiyē.
translation: O friend, you asked, "The King of Dance, unattainable by the ignorant, may be your husband. But when the deities who hold their various stations come to speak joyfully with you, you pay them no regard. Why is that?" My dear, I am not of a lineage that submits to the leaders of the passing religions, the heads of the doctrines, or even the great leaders who support them. Know this: I am of a lineage formed solely for service to the dancing feet in Thiru Chitrambalam.
commentary: The path to God requires moving beyond all organized religions and established doctrines. The friend is perplexed that the soul ignores even the deities who hold their stations in the cosmos when they come to speak with her. The soul replies that she does not submit to the leaders of any religion or doctrine, however prominent. Her loyalty is to the dancing feet alone, not to any institution or belief system created in God's name.

translit: aṟaṅkulavu tōḻiiṅkē nīuraitta vārttai aṟivaṟiyār vārttaieta ṉāleṉilim moḻikēḷ uṟaṅkuvatum viḻippatumpiṉ uṇṇuvatum iṟattal uṟuvatuṭaṉ piṟattalpala peṟuvatumāy uḻalum maṟaṅkulavum aṇukkaḷpalar ceytavira tattāl matattalaimai patattalaimai vāyttaṉaraṅ kavarpāl iṟaṅkalilēṉ pēcutalāl eṉpayaṉō naṭañcey iṟaivaraṭip pukaḻpēci irukkiṉṟēṉ yāṉē.
translation: O virtuous friend, the words you just spoke are the words of someone who lacks true knowledge. If you ask why, listen. Many souls steeped in vice struggle, cycling through sleeping and waking, eating, dying, being born, and acquiring many things. Through the vows they performed, they attained leadership over religions and worldly positions. I do not stoop to their level; what is the use of even talking about them? I am here simply speaking the praise of the feet of the dancing Lord.
commentary: All other leaders, whether religious or worldly, are simply souls still trapped in the cycle of birth, death, and suffering. The soul explains that while they may have attained high positions through past discipline, they are not themselves free. Therefore, engaging with them is pointless. The only worthwhile activity is to focus on the one Lord who is beyond this cycle and who alone can grant true liberation.

translit: civamayamē vēṟilaiel lāmeṉanī tāṉē tēmoḻiyāy paṟpalakāl ceppiyiṭak kēṭṭēṉ tavamayattār palacamayat talaivarmatat talaivar tattuvartat tuvattalaivar avartalaivar talaivar ivaravareṉ ṟayalvēṟu pirittavarpāl vārttai iyampuvateṉ eṉṟāyī teṉkoleṉṟāy tōḻi navamayamnī uṇarntaṟiyāy ātaliliv vaṇṇam naviṉṟaṉainiṉ aiyamaṟa nāṉpukalvēṉ kēḷē.
translation: O sweet-spoken friend, I have heard you yourself say many times, "Everything is pervaded by Civa; nothing else exists." You then asked, "So why do you speak of the masters of penance, the heads of various religions, the chiefs of doctrines, the philosophers, the leaders of philosophies, and the leaders of their leaders, separating them as 'these people' and 'those people' as if they are different? What is this?" O friend, you spoke this way because you do not yet truly understand the new state of being. I will now speak to clear your doubt. Listen.
commentary: The friend raises a sharp philosophical point: if everything is pervaded by Civa (the Auspicious One, the Supreme Being), as the speaker herself has said, then why treat anyone as separate or inferior? The speaker acknowledges the seeming contradiction and prepares to reveal a more subtle truth, setting up a key distinction between an intellectual idea and a lived, experiential reality.

translit: oḷioṉṟē aṇṭapaki raṇṭamelām viḷaṅki ōṅkukiṉṟa taṉiaṇṭa pakiraṇṭaṅ kaḷilum veḷiniṉṟa carācarattum akattiṉoṭu puṟattum viḷampumakap puṟattiṉoṭu puṟappuṟattum niṟaintē uḷiniṉṟa iruḷnīkki ilaṅkukiṉṟa taṉmai ulakaṟiyum nīaṟiyā taṉṟukaṇṭāy tōḻi taḷiniṉṟa oḷimayamē vēṟilaiel lāmum tāṉeṉavē tākamaṅkaḷ cāṟṟutalcat tiyamē.
translation: One Light alone illumines all universes and the spaces beyond them, standing supreme and unique. It fills the universes and the spaces beyond, pervading the space where all moving and unmoving things exist, inside and out, in the inner-outer and the outer-outer planes. The way it dispels the inner darkness and shines forth is known to the world; it is not something you are unaware of, my friend. It is indeed true that the sacred Vedas and Agamas declare that everything is this state of pure light, standing firm as a sanctuary, and that nothing else exists; that all is Itself.
commentary: It is a fundamental truth, confirmed by the ancient scriptures (Vedas and Agamas), that a single, all-pervading Light is the ultimate reality of all existence. This Light is more than in things; it is things, filling every corner of the cosmos and every level of being. This principle is the basis for the statement that "all is God."

translit: ēṟṟiṭuvē tākamaṅkaḷ oḷimayamē ellām eṉṟamoḻi taṉainiṉaittē iraviliruṭ ṭaṟaiyil cāṟṟiṭumaṇ pāttirattai maravaṭṭil kaḷaikkal caṭṭikaḷai vēṟupala cārntakaru vikaḷait tēṟṟamiku taṇraic cīvarkaḷpaṟ palaraic ceppiyaav viruṭṭaṟaiyil taṉittaṉicērt tālum ūṟṟamuṟum iruḷnīṅki oḷikāṇpa tuḷatō uḷatēlnī uraittamoḻi uḷatākum tōḻi.
translation: Thinking of that statement from the revered Vedas and Agamas that "everything is pervaded by light," consider this. In a dark room at night, place clay pots, wooden bowls, stones, cooking pans, and various other implements. Even add many clear-minded, cool-natured living beings to that dark room. Is the dense darkness thereby removed, allowing light to be seen? If it is, O friend, then what you said would be true.
commentary: This verse offers a powerful analogy to show the limits of intellectual knowledge. Knowing that everything is theoretically "made of light" does not help you see in a dark room; the light must actually be manifest. In the same way, simply accepting the idea that all beings are divine in essence does not mean they are free from the darkness of ignorance. The divine nature must be actively realized and expressed to become a reality.

translit: paramataṉō ṭulakuyirkaḷ kaṟpaṉaiyē ellām pakarcivamē eṉa:uṇarntōm ātaliṉāl nāmē piramameṉap piṟarkkuraittup poṅkivaḻin tāṅkē pēcukiṉṟa periyavartam periyamatam piṭiyēl uramikupēr ulakuyirkaḷ paramivaikā riyattāl uḷḷaṉavē kāraṇattāl uḷḷaṉa:il laṉavē taramikupēr aruḷoḷiyāl civamayamē ellām tāmeṉavē uṇarvatucaṉ mārkkaneṟi piṭiyē.
translation: Do not cling to the great religion of those "great ones" who, overflowing with pride, declare to others, "We ourselves are Brahmam," based on the intellectual realization that the Supreme, the world, and its souls are all concepts and only Civa is real. The vast and powerful world, its souls, and the Supreme exist as effects; as cause, they do not exist in that form. To realize, through the sublime, great light of grace, that everything is indeed pervaded by Civa and is Itself, this is the way of Sanmarkkam. Hold fast to that.
commentary: Vallalar warns plainly: do not hold to the great religion of those who, overflowing with pride, declare "We ourselves are Brahmam" because they hold the world, souls and the Supreme to be mere imagination. The world, souls and the Supreme are real as effects. The way of Sanmarkkam is to know, through the great light of grace, that everything is pervaded by Civa. This knowing is given by grace; it is not a philosophical claim.

translit: piramameṉṟum civameṉṟum pēcukiṉṟa nilaitāṉ perunilaiyē innilaiyil pētamuṇṭō eṉavē taramaṟiya viṉavukiṉṟāy tōḻiitu kēḷnī camaracacaṉ mārkkanilai cārtieṉil aṟivāy tiramuṟavā yiṉumellām ākiallā tākum tiruvaruḷām veḷiviḷaṅka viḷaṅkutaṉip poruḷām ciramuṟumōr potuuṇmaic civampirama muṭiyē tikaḻmaṟaiā kamampukalum tiṟaṉitukaṇ ṭaṟiyē.
translation: My friend, you ask to know its nature, inquiring if the state spoken of as Brahman and as Sivam is the great state, and if there is any distinction within it. Listen to this. If you attain the state of Samarasa Sanmarkkam, you will know. Though firm, it becomes all things while also being none of them. It is the unique substance that shines when the space of divine grace shines. It is the supreme, universal truth of Sivam, the very crown of Brahman. This is the reality the glorious Vedas and Agamas proclaim. See it and know.
commentary: The ultimate reality, whether called Brahman or Sivam, cannot be understood through intellectual debate. To know it, Vallalar says you must attain the state of Samarasa Sanmarkkam, the path of total spiritual harmony and truth. In that state, you will directly experience the paradoxical nature of God: a singular reality that becomes all things while remaining distinct from them. This direct seeing is the true purpose of the scriptures.

translit: ilaṅkukiṉṟa potuuṇmai iruntanilai pukaleṉ ṟiyampukiṉṟāy maṭavāykēḷ yāṉaṟiyun taramō tulaṅkumatai uraittiṭavum kēṭṭiṭavum paṭumō colaḷavō poruḷaḷavō tuṉṉumaṟi vaḷavō vilaṅkukiṉṟa tattuvaṅkaḷ attaṉaiyum kaṭanta mēṉilaieṉ ṟantamelām viḷampukiṉṟa taṉṟi valaṅkoḷumam mēṉilaiyiṉ uṇmaietu eṉṟāl mavuṉañcā tippataṉṟi vāytiṟappa tilaiyē.
translation: You ask me to describe the state where the radiant universal truth resides. O naive friend, listen. Am I capable of knowing it? Can that shining reality be spoken of or heard? Is it within the measure of words, of substance, or of the intellect that grasps them? All the ultimate texts proclaim only that it is the high state transcending all the obstructing tattvas. Beyond that, if one asks what the truth of that supreme state is, they observe silence; they do not open their mouths.
commentary: The ultimate state of truth cannot be described in words. Vallalar explains that it is beyond language, beyond physical substance, and beyond the grasp of the mind. It is a state that transcends all the tattvas, the fundamental cosmic principles that construct reality as we experience it. Faced with this supreme reality, the only appropriate response is silence.

translit: vāytiṟavā mavuṉamatē ākumeṉil tōḻi mavuṉacatti veḷiēḻum parattaparat toḻiyum tūyaparā paramatuvē eṉṟālaṅ katutāṉ tulaṅkunaṭu veḷitaṉilē kalantukarai vatukāṇ mēyanaṭu veḷieṉṟāl taṟparamām veḷiyil viraviyiṭum taṟparamām veḷieṉṟāl atuvum āyaperu veḷitaṉilē aṭaṅkumitu maṭṭē aḷappatoru vāṟataṉmēl aḷappatari taritē.
translation: My friend, if you say it is the silence in which the mouth does not open, the seven voids of Mavuna Sakthi themselves will dissolve in Parathparam. If you say it is that pure Parathparam, see that it mixes and dissolves into the radiant nadu veli. If you say it is that pervading nadu veli, it will merge into the space of Tatparam. If you say it is the space of Tatparam, that too will be contained within the peru veli. This is the limit of one way of measuring; to measure beyond this is difficult, most difficult.
commentary: Even the concept of "silence" is not the final answer. Vallalar describes a series of cosmic voids or spaces, each dissolving into a vaster, more subtle one. The power of silence (Mavuna Sakthi) dissolves into Parathparam (the reality beyond the beyond), which in turn merges into the nadu veli (middle space), then the Tatparam (space of the absolute), and finally the peru veli (the great primal space). This maps a way into ever-deeper levels of reality, suggesting that any state the mind can name is still contained within something immeasurably larger.

translit: kiḷakkiṉṟa maṟaiaḷavai ākamappē raḷavai kiḷantiṭumeyc cātaṉamām aḷavaiaṟi vaḷavai viḷakkuminta aḷavaikaḷaik koṇṭuneṭuṅ kālam mēlavarkaḷ aḷantaḷantu melikiṉṟār āṅkē aḷakkiṉṟa karuvielām tēyntiṭak kaṇṭārē aṉṟioru vāṟēṉum aḷavukaṇṭār ilaiyē tuḷakkamuṟu ciṟṟaṟivāl oruvāṟeṉ ṟuraittēṉ coṉṉaveḷi varaiyēṉum tuṇintaḷakkap paṭumō.
translation: Taking the proclaimed measure of the Vedas, the great measure of the Agamas, the measure of the true sadhanas that are spoken of, and the measure of intellect, with these measures, the great ones have for ages measured and measured, only to grow weary. They saw all their instruments of measurement wear away, but they did not find its measure in any way at all. With my own wavering, limited intellect, I have described it in one manner. Yet can even the spaces I have spoken of be definitively measured?
commentary: No human tool, not scripture, not spiritual practice (sadhana), and not even the sharpest intellect, can ever measure or contain the infinite reality of God. For ages, the great ones have tried and only found that their tools, including the Vedas and Agamas, were finite and wore away. This is a statement of humility: the divine is a boundless reality to be experienced, and that experience will always be greater than our capacity to explain it.

translit: aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ āruyi rilkalan tāṭukiṉṟa aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ aṉpiṟ kalantaṟi vāyviḷaṅkum aruṭperuñ cōtitteḷ ḷāramu tākiuḷ aṇṇikkiṉṟa aruṭperuñ cōtiniṉ ācaioṉ ṟēeṉṉuḷ ārkiṉṟatē.
translation: Vast Grace-Light, which mingles and dances in my precious life; Vast Grace-Light, which mingles in my love and shines as consciousness; Vast Grace-Light, which becomes the clear, fulfilling nectar that sweetens within me; O Vast Grace-Light, desire for you alone fills my being.
commentary: The experience of God is a complete and intimate merging with one's own being. The Vast Grace-Light is a living reality that dances within one's life-force, illuminates one's consciousness, and fills the heart with a sweet nectar. This direct, personal connection eclipses all other wants, leaving only the desire for God.

translit: ārkiṉṟa teḷḷamu tiṉcuvai eṉeṉ ṟaṟaivaṉantō cārkiṉṟa ciṟṟam palapperuñ cīriṉaic cāṟṟutoṟum cērkiṉṟa nāvuṭaṉ uḷḷamum āviyum tittittalē nērkiṉṟa tāleṉ aruṭperuñ cōti niṟaintuḷattē.
translation: Alas, how can I describe the taste of this fulfilling, clear nectar? Each time I speak of the great glory of Chitrambalam that I am approaching, my tongue, heart, and life-force all turn sweet, because my Vast Grace-Light fills my being.
commentary: The bliss of divine union is so deep that it cannot be described in words. The very act of speaking about the sacred inner space (Chitrambalam) makes the entire being, from tongue to life-force, turn sweet. This shows that the experience is a tangible reality that floods the senses, a direct taste of God's presence.

translit: uḷattē peruṅkaḷip puṟṟaṭi yēṉmika uṇṇukiṉṟēṉ vaḷattē aruṭperuñ cōtiyi ṉāloḷi vāynteṉatu kuḷattē niṟaintaṇai yuṅkaṭan tōṅkik kulavupari maḷattē mikuntu vayaṅkum amutam maṉamakiḻntē.
translation: With a joyful mind and great bliss, I, your servant, drink deeply the nectar that, made luminous by the bounteous Vast Grace-Light, fills my inner pool, overflows its banks, rises high, and shines with an abounding, exquisite fragrance.
commentary: Grace is experienced as a luminous nectar that fills and overflows the soul. This imagery portrays a state of being completely saturated with the divine presence, a bliss so abundant it cannot be contained. The experience delights all the inner senses, manifesting as light, a sweet taste, and a beautiful fragrance.

translit: maṉamakiḻn tēṉmaṉa māyaiyai nīkkiṉaṉ mānilattē ciṉamoṭum kāmamum tīrntēṉ elāmvalla cittumpeṟṟēṉ iṉamikum cuttacaṉ mārkkap peruneṟi eytiniṉṟēṉ kaṉamikum maṉṟil aruṭperuñ cōtiyaik kaṇṭukoṇṭē.
translation: My mind is joyful, I have dispelled the mind's illusion, I am free from anger and lust on this great earth, I have obtained the all-powerful siddhi, and I have attained and now stand in the great, supreme path of Suddha Sanmarkkam, all because I saw the Vast Grace-Light in the glorious hall.
commentary: Direct perception of the Vast Grace-Light is the key to complete inner transformation. Seeing God is what makes true liberation possible: it brings joy, ends illusion, purifies the heart of anger and lust, and grants spiritual powers (siddhi). This vision is the very foundation of the path of Suddha Sanmarkkam (the true path of universal harmony).

translit: kaṇṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyaik kaṇkaḷil kaṇṭukaḷi koṇṭēṉ civāṉantak kūttāṭik koṇṭik kuvalayattē toṇṭē tiruam palantaṉak kākkic cukaamutam uṇṭēṉ uyirtaḻait tōṅkukiṉ ṟēṉuḷ uvappuṟavē.
translation: I saw the Vast Grace-Light with my own eyes and became blissful. Dancing the dance of Siva-bliss, I have dedicated my service in this world solely to the sacred hall. I have drunk the nectar of bliss, and now, with inner delight, my life flourishes and soars.
commentary: The personal experience of divine light naturally overflows into joyful, selfless action. The "dance of Siva-bliss" is an expression of ecstatic union with the divine, which then motivates a life of service. This vision is the very thing that makes life flourish in the world.

translit: uṟavē eṉatiṉ ṉuyirēeṉ uḷḷattil uṟṟiṉikkum naṟavē aruṭperuñ cōtimaṉ ṟōṅku naṭattaracē iṟavēṉ eṉattuṇi veytiṭac ceytaṉai eṉṉaiiṉi maṟavēl aṭicciṟi yēṉoru pōtu maṟakkiṉumē.
translation: O my relation, my very life, nectar that entered my heart and is sweet within it! O King of Dance who flourishes in the hall of ArutPerunJothi! You made me resolve that I will not die. Do not forget me now, even if I, your lowly servant, should ever forget you.
commentary: The divine is addressed here with startling intimacy, as "my relation" and "my very life." This close bond has given Vallalar a radical conviction: that he will overcome death itself. His final plea is touchingly human, asking the divine to remember him even if his own limited mind were to forget, showing an absolute trust in God's faithfulness over his own.

translit: maṟappēṉ alēṉuṉṉai ōrkaṇa mēṉum maṟakkilaṉṟē iṟappēṉ itucat tiyamcat tiyamcat tiyamicaittēṉ piṟappē tavirtteṉai āṭkoṇ ṭamutam peritaḷitta ciṟappē aruṭperuñ cōtimaṉ ṟōṅku ceḻuñcuṭarē.
translation: I will not forget you, not for a single moment. If I forget, I will die that very day. This is the truth, the truth, the truth I declare! O Greatness who ended my birth cycle and took me as your own, granting me abundant nectar! O rich Flame flourishing in the hall of the Vast Grace-Light!
commentary: This verse is a solemn vow, the flip side of the previous plea. Forgetting the divine is a lapse in memory and a form of death itself. By repeating "this is the truth" three times, Vallalar frames this constant remembrance as the absolute condition for his existence. This state of connection is what has freed him from the endless cycle of birth and death.

translit: cuṭarē aruṭperuñ cōtiya ṉēpeṇ cukattaimikka viṭarē eṉiṉum viṭuvaren tāyniṉai viṭṭayaloṉ ṟaṭarēṉ araikkaṇa mumpirin tāṟṟalaṉ āṇaikaṇṭāy iṭarē tavirtteṉak kellā nalamumiṅ kīntavaṉē.
translation: O Flame! Lord of the Vast Grace-Light! Even men steeped in lust may one day give up the pleasure of women, but I, O my Father, will not leave You to go after anything else. I cannot bear to be parted from You even for half a moment; this is my solemn oath, know it. O You who ended my distress and gave me every good thing here!
commentary: Vallalar measures his bond with God against the strongest worldly attachment. Even a man enslaved by lust may one day let it go, but he cannot leave God for anything else, nor bear separation for even half a moment. He seals this with an oath and calls God 'my Father,' the One who removed every distress and gave him every good.

translit: tavanēya mumcutta caṉmārkka nēyamum cattiyamām civanēya mumtanteṉ uḷḷam teḷiyat teḷittaṉaiyē navanēya maṉṟil aruṭperuñ cōtiyai nāṭiniṉṟa ivaṉē avaṉeṉak koḷvāruṉ aṉpar irunilattē.
translation: You gave me love for spiritual austerity, love for the Suddha Sanmarkkam, and love for Sivam which is truth, clarifying my mind until it became clear. On this vast earth, Your devotees will hold, "This one, who stood in the hall of new love seeking the Vast Grace-Light, is He Himself."
commentary: God has purified his heart by giving him three loves: love of tavam, love of the Suddha Sanmarkkam, and love of Sivam, which is truth. Grace has so transformed him that devotees on this earth will look at him and say, "This one is He": the seeker has become one with the Light he sought.

translit: nilattē puḻutta puḻuvum alēṉpuṉ nilattiḻinta malattē puḻutta puḻuaṉai yēṉaiav vāṉtutikkum kulattē talaimai koṭutteṉ uḷattil kulavukiṉṟāy talattē aruṭperuñ cōtiap pāeṉ tayānitiyē.
translation: I am not even a worm born of the earth; I am like a worm born from filth, lower than the base earth itself. To me, such a one, you gave leadership in the lineage praised by the celestials, and now you flourish within my heart. O Father, Vast Grace-Light of this sacred place! O my treasure of compassion!
commentary: Vallalar expresses deep humility, seeing his unenlightened self as lower than a worm born in filth. From this state of utter worthlessness, God has lifted him to the highest spiritual status and now lives within his heart. This extreme contrast highlights the boundless, changing power of the Vast Grace-Light, which he calls his Father and his treasure of compassion.

translit: nitiyē eṉṉuḷḷa niṟaivē potuvil niṟaintaciva patiyē aruṭperuñ cōtiya ṉēam palamviḷaṅkum katiyē eṉkaṇṇum karuttum kaḷikkak kalantukoṇṭa matiyē amuta maḻaiyēniṉ pēraruḷ vāḻiyavē.
translation: O Treasure, the fullness within my heart! O Lord Siva, filling the universal expanse! O ArutPerunJothi! O Refuge shining in the sacred space! O Wisdom that has merged with me, making my eyes and mind rejoice! O Rain of ambrosia! May Your great grace flourish!
commentary: God is experienced in many ways at once: as personal inner wealth, as the universal Lord (Siva), as the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), and as the refuge shining in the sacred space of consciousness. This divine presence has merged with him completely, flooding his mind and senses with the joy of ambrosia. The final line is a simple, heartfelt blessing for the grace that makes all this possible.

translit: vāḻieṉ ṟēeṉai mālayaṉ ātiyar vantaruṭpēr āḻieṉ ṟētutit tēttap purintaṉai aṟputamnī ṭūḻiaṉ ṟēeṉṟum cākā varamum uvantaḷittāy vāḻimaṉ ṟōṅkum aruṭperuñ cōtiniṉ maṉṉaruḷē.
translation: You worked a miracle, making Vishnu, Brahma, and others come and praise me, hailing me as a great ocean of grace. You joyfully granted me the boon of never dying, for long eons and forever. O ArutPerunJothi who flourishes in the sacred hall, may Your sovereign grace flourish!
commentary: Divine grace has performed a stunning miracle, raising him to a state where even the great gods like Vishnu and Brahma praise him. Beyond this honor, God has granted him the ultimate boon: a deathless existence, forever. This points to one of Vallalar's most distinctive teachings, that the grace of ArutPerunJothi can bestow spiritual liberation and physical immortality.

translit: maṉṉiya niṉaru ḷāramu tamtantu vāḻvittunāṉ uṉṉiya uṉṉiya ellām utavieṉ uḷḷattilē taṉṉiyal ākik kalantit taruṇam tayavuceytāy tuṉṉiya niṉṉaruḷ vāḻka aruṭperuñ cōtiyaṉē.
translation: Giving me the sweet ambrosia of Your eternal grace, You brought me to life. You granted all that I ever conceived. At this very moment, You have bestowed the favor of merging into my heart and becoming its very nature. May Your intimate grace flourish, O ArutPerunJothi!
commentary: The union with God is a lived, present reality. God's grace (arul) is a life-giving ambrosia that fulfills all aspirations. The greatest gift is God's own presence, which merges so completely with the devotee's heart that it becomes their true, inherent nature.

translit: aruḷaḷittāṉ aṉpaḷittāṉ ampalattāṉ uṇmaip poruḷaḷittāṉ eṉṉuṭ puṇarntāṉ - teruḷaḷittāṉ eccō taṉaiyum iyaṟṟāmal āṇṭukoṇṭāṉ accō eṉakkavaṉpōl ār.
translation: He gave grace. He gave love. The Lord of the Ambalam gave the true substance and united with me within. He gave clarity. Without making me perform any kind of trial, He took me into His service. Oh, who is there for me like Him?
commentary: God's grace is given freely, without demanding difficult spiritual tests or trials. The Lord of the Ambalam (sacred hall) simply gives love, truth, and clarity, taking the soul into His service out of pure, unconditional compassion. The feeling is one of deep gratitude for a love that asks for nothing in return.

translit: āraṇamum ākamamum āṅkāṅ kuṇarttukiṉṟa kāraṇamum kāriyamum kāṭṭuvittāṉ - pūraṇaṉciṟ ṟampalattāṉ eṉṉācai appaṉ elāvalla cempalattai eṉuḷattē cērttu.
translation: The perfect one, the Lord of the Chitrambalam, my beloved Father, placed the all-powerful, perfect state within my mind and revealed to me the cause and effect that the Vedas and Agamas explain in various places.
commentary: Direct experience of God reveals the ultimate truths that scriptures can only point towards. Instead of just learning from the Vedas and Agamas (sacred texts), the devotee receives the living reality of that knowledge directly from God. The Lord of the Chitrambalam (the inner space of consciousness) places the state of perfection itself within the heart.

translit: cērttāṉ patameṉ cirattē tiruvaruṭkaṇ pārttāṉeṉ eṇṇamelām pālittāṉ - tīrttāṉeṉ tuṉpamelām tūkkamelām cūḻātu nīkkiviṭṭāṉ iṉpamelām tantāṉ icaintu.
translation: He placed His feet upon my head. He looked upon me with His eyes of grace. He fulfilled my every wish. He ended all my suffering. He ended all my suffering. He removed all sleep so that it can no longer surround me, and He willingly gave me every bliss.
commentary: The touch of the divine brings about a complete and immediate transformation. Placing the feet on the head is a traditional symbol of the highest blessing, and here it signifies the end of all suffering, the clearing of all delusion, and the arrival of perfect, unending bliss.

translit: icaintāṉeṉ uḷḷat tiruntāṉ eṉaiyum nacaintāṉeṉ pāṭṭai nayantāṉ - acaintāṭu māyai maṉamaṭakki vaittāṉ aruḷeṉumeṉ tāyaimakiḻ ampalavaṉ tāṉ.
translation: He willingly abides in my heart. He desired me too, and He delighted in my song. He subdued and held in check Māyai and the swaying mind: He, the Lord of the Ambalam, who rejoices with my Mother, Grace.
commentary: The relationship with God is mutual and intimate: God desires the soul just as the soul desires God. His presence in the heart subdues both Māyai and the restless mind. Grace, whom Vallalar calls his Mother, is His consort, and the Lord of the Ambalam rejoices with her.

translit: tāṉē aruḷāṉāṉ tāṉē poruḷāṉāṉ tāṉēel lāmvalla tāṉāṉāṉ - tāṉētāṉ nāṉāṉāṉ eṉṉuṭaiya nāyakaṉā ṉāṉñāṉa vāṉāṉāṉ ampalattem māṉ.
translation: He Himself became grace. He Himself became the reality. He Himself became the all-powerful Self. He Himself became I. He became my Master. Our Great One of the Ambalam became the vast expanse of wisdom.
commentary: In the final state of union, all distinctions between the self and God dissolve. Vallalar describes a merging where God becomes the very substance of reality, grace, and even his own identity: "He Himself became I." This union transforms the soul into a vast expanse of pure wisdom (jnana).

translit: māṉmutalā uḷḷa vaḻakkellām tīrttaruḷit tāṉmutalāy eṉṉuḷamē cārntamarntāṉ - tēṉmutalāt tittikkum paṇṭamelām cērttāṅkeṉ cintaitaṉil tittikkum ampalattāṉ tērntu.
translation: He resolved all worldly conventions and, as the Primal One, entered and settled within my heart. The Lord of the Ambalam, having chosen me, sweetens my mind like a collection of all sweet things, beginning with honey.
commentary: The divine presence liberates a person from the constraints of worldly rules and expectations. Once God, the Primal One, enters the heart, the mind is filled with a sweetness that surpasses any earthly pleasure. It is a direct, felt experience of overwhelming joy.

translit: tērntēṉ teḷintēṉ civamē poruḷeṉa:uḷ ōrntēṉ aruḷamutam uṇkiṉṟēṉ - cārntēṉciṟ ṟampalattil ellāmval lāṉai avaṉaruḷāl empalattel lāmvalaṉā ṉēṉ.
translation: I have discerned, I have gained clarity, and I have realized within that Sivam is the true substance. I am consuming the nectar of grace. I have taken refuge in the all-powerful One of the Sitrambalam, and by His grace, I too have become capable in all things.
commentary: True understanding comes from realizing that God, or Sivam (the Auspicious One), is the only substance of existence. This realization is a state of being sustained by divine grace, which confers the all-capable power of the divine onto the soul.

translit: āṉēṉ avaṉā avaṉaruḷāl āṅkāṅku nāṉē kaḷittu naṭikkiṉṟēṉ - tāṉēeṉ tantaieṉpāl vaitta tayavainiṉaik kuntōṟum cintaiviyak kiṉṟēṉ terintu.
translation: By His grace, I have become Him. Here and there, it is I who dance in bliss. Each time I think of the compassion my Father has shown toward me, my mind marvels with understanding.
commentary: The separation between the soul and God dissolves completely. The individual's life is no longer their own; they become an instrument for God's blissful play in the world. Reflecting on this transformation fills the heart with wonder at the depth of God's compassion.

translit: terintēṉ aruḷāl civamoṉṟē eṉṟu purintēṉ civampalikkum pūcai - virintamaṉac cēṭṭaielām tīrttuviṭṭēṉ cittellām vallaaruḷ nāṭṭaielām kaikkoṇṭēṉ nāṉ.
translation: By grace, I have realized that Sivam alone exists. I have performed the worship that makes Sivam manifest. I have put a stop to all the agitations of my wandering mind. I have taken possession of the entire realm of grace, which holds all power over consciousness.
commentary: The highest form of worship is the direct realization that God alone is real. This clarity stills the mind's constant activity and gives the soul full command over the inner world of consciousness and grace.

translit: nāṉceyta naṟṟavantāṉ yātō naviṟṟaritu vāṉceyta tēvarelām vantēval - tāṉceytu tampalameṉ ṟēmatikkat tāṉvanteṉ ṉuṭkalantāṉ ampalavaṉ taṉaruḷi ṉāl.
translation: What good tavam did I perform? It is impossible to say. All the celestial beings of heaven came to serve me, regarding me as their refuge. By His grace, the Lord of the Ambalam Himself came and merged within me.
commentary: The experience of divine union feels entirely unearned, a pure gift of grace. The devotee's status is so elevated that even celestial beings serve him, yet he knows this honor comes from God's spontaneous act of merging with his soul.

sections.title: Garland for the Northern Chidambaram of Gnosis

translit: aruḷōṅku kiṉṟa taruṭperuñ cōti yaṭaintateṉṟaṉ maruḷōṅku ṟāmal tavirttatu nalla varamaḷittē poruḷōṅki nāṉaruṭ pūmiyil vāḻap purintateṉṟum teruḷōṅka ōṅkuva tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: The burgeoning Vast Grace-Light approached me, prevented my delusion from growing by granting a good boon, and made me live, exalted in substance, on the earth of grace. What always rises for clarity to flourish is Uttara Jnana Chidambaram.
commentary: Uttara Jñāna Chidambaram, 'the northern Chidambaram of wisdom,' is the name Vallalar gave to Vadalur, north of Thillai, where the Sathya Gnana Sabhai stands. Here he praises it as the seat of the Vast Grace-Light that came to him, ended his delusion with a good boon, and established him in the land of grace. It rises forever so that clarity may rise.

translit: iṇaieṉṟu tāṉtaṉak kēṟṟatu pōṟṟum eṉakkunalla tuṇaieṉṟu vantatu cuttacaṉ mārkkattil tōyntateṉṉai aṇaieṉ ṟaṇaittukkoṇ ṭaintoḻil īnta taruḷulakil tiṇaiaintu mākiya tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: Hailing itself as its own fitting equal, it came as a good companion to me. It immersed me in the Suddha Sanmarkkam, said "Embrace me," embraced me, and granted me the five functions in the world of grace. What has become all five landscapes is Uttara Jnana Chidambaram.
commentary: This divine presence is simultaneously supreme beyond compare and an intimate friend who embraces the soul. It personally draws Vallalar into the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure Path of Truth and Universal Oneness) and entrusts him with the five functions: the divine powers of creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, and grace. This reality becomes the very fabric of existence, symbolized by the five landscapes of classical Tamil poetry.

translit: ulakame lāntoḻa uṟṟa teṉakkuṇmai oṇmaitantē ilakae lāmpaṭait tāruyir kāttaruḷ eṉṟateṉṟum kalakami lāccutta caṉmārkka caṅkam kalantatupārt tilakame ṉāniṉṟa tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: It presented itself for all worlds to worship, giving me true radiance. It commanded, "Shine, create all, protect precious lives, and bestow grace." It joined the ever-peaceful Suddha Sanmarkka Sangam. What stands as the tilakam of the world is Uttara Jnana Chidambaram.
commentary: Receiving divine radiance is not for one's own sake; it comes with a mission to serve the world. Vallalar is commanded to shine, create, protect all living beings, and bestow grace. This divine principle also joins his Suddha Sanmarkka Sangam (the community of the Pure Path), showing that the fellowship itself is a manifestation of God on earth. It is the world's tilakam, the auspicious mark on the forehead that signifies its most vital and sacred point.

translit: pavamē tavirppatu cākā varamum payappatunal tavamē purintavark kiṉpan taruvatu tāṉtaṉakkē uvamē yamāṉa toḷiōṅku kiṉṟa toḷiruñcutta civamē niṟaikiṉṟa tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: It is what removes birth itself and grants the boon of deathlessness. It gives bliss to those who have performed good austerities. It is its own standard of comparison, the burgeoning light. What is filled with shining, pure Sivam is Uttara Jnana Chidambaram.
commentary: The ultimate promise of this path is the complete conquest of mortality. This divine reality frees one from the cycle of birth and death, granting physical deathlessness. It is the source of bliss for those who engage in true spiritual discipline (tavam) and is filled with pure Sivam (the ultimate auspicious reality), a light so complete it is its own only measure.

translit: ottā raiyumiḻin tāraiyum nērkaṇ ṭuvakkaoru mittārai vāḻvippa tēṟṟārk kamutam viḷampiiṭu vittāraik kāppatu cittāṭu kiṉṟatu mētiṉimēl cettārai mīṭkiṉṟa tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: Rejoicing to see equals and the lowly alike, it makes those who live in unity flourish. It protects those who call out and have food served to those who come in need. It performs its Siddha-play on this earth. What raises the dead is Uttara Jnana Chidambaram.
commentary: This verse shows Jeevakarunyam at work. The grace of this place rejoices to see equals and the lowly alike, makes those who live in unity flourish, and protects those who call out and serve food to the hungry who come to them. It plays as a Siddha on this earth and performs the greatest miracle: it raises the dead.

tamil: சித்தாடல் செய்கின்ற தெல்லா உலகும் செழிக்க வைத்த
translit: ettālum mikka teṉakkaruḷ īntatel lāmumvalla cittāṭal ceykiṉṟa tellā ulakum ceḻikka vaitta tittā raṇikkaṇi āyatu vāṉtoḻaṟ kēṟṟateṅkum cettāl eḻuppuva tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: It gave me grace superior to all else. It performs the all-powerful, miraculous play. It made all worlds flourish. It has become an ornament for this earth, is worthy of worship by the heavens, and everywhere raises the dead. This is the Uttara Gnana Chidambaram (the Northern Chidambaram of Gnosis).
commentary: The grace Vallalar received from this divine center is, for him, the highest possible gift. He sees its power as the force that makes all worlds thrive. The verse repeats the astonishing claim that this power can raise the dead, establishing Uttara Gnana Chidambaram as a place of universal significance, honored by both earthly and celestial beings.

translit: kuruneṟik kēeṉṉaik kūṭṭik koṭuttatu kūṟaritām peruneṟik kēceṉṟa pērkkuk kiṭaippatu pēyulakak karuneṟik kēṟṟavar kāṇaṟ kariyatu kāṭṭukiṉṟa tiruneṟik kēṟkiṉṟa tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: It joined me to the path of the Guru. It is attained by those who walk the great, indescribable path. It is difficult to see for those who follow the dark path of this demonic world. It is in keeping with the sacred path it itself reveals. This is the Uttara Gnana Chidambaram.
commentary: This divine center acts as the ultimate spiritual guide, the Guru, placing the seeker on the true path. While it is the destination for all sincere seekers, it remains hidden from those who live by a negative, "demonic" consciousness. The path and the goal are one and the same.

translit: kollā neṟiyatu kōṭā nilaiyatu kōpamilār collāl uvantatu cuttacaṉ mārkkan tuṇintatula kellām aḷippa tiṟantāl eḻuppuva tētamoṉṟum cellā vaḷattiṉa tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: It is the path of non-killing, the unswerving state. It delights in the words of those without anger. It is what the Suddha Sanmarkkam has affirmed. It grants all worlds and raises the dead. It is a wealth that no flaw can enter. This is the Uttara Gnana Chidambaram.
commentary: The character of this divine reality is inseparable from the ethics it represents: absolute non-violence and freedom from anger. This path is the essence of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure Path of Truth). Vallalar concludes by describing its power as a perfect, untainted treasure that creates, sustains, and even resurrects life.

translit: kāṇāta kāṭcikaḷ kāṭṭuvik kiṉṟatu kālamellām vīṇāḷ kaḻippavark keytari tāṉatu veñciṉattāl kōṇāta neñcil kulāviniṟ kiṉṟatu kūṭiniṉṟu cēṇāṭar vāḻttuva tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: It reveals visions never seen before. It is difficult to attain for those who waste their lives. It resides joyfully in hearts not warped by fierce anger. The celestials gather together to praise it. This is the Uttara Gnana Chidambaram.
commentary: Spiritual progress is a matter of purifying the heart. This divine reality reveals itself to those who have freed themselves from anger, while remaining inaccessible to those who drift through life without purpose. Attaining this state brings visions and experiences beyond the ordinary world.

translit: colvanta vēta muṭimuṭi mītil tulaṅkuvatu kalvanta neñciṉar kāṇaṟ kariyatu kāmamilār nalvan taṉaiceya naṇṇiya pēṟatu naṉṟeṉakkē celvantan tāṭkoṇṭa tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: It shines on the very summit of the spoken Vedas. It is difficult to perceive for those with hearts of stone. It is the blessing attained by the lustless who offer good worship. It has graciously given me wealth and taken me as its own. This is the Uttara Gnana Chidambaram.
commentary: The final truth, which the scriptures (Vedas) point toward, is a lived reality experienced by those whose hearts are soft and free from worldly desires like lust. Vallalar identifies true wealth as the grace of being accepted and owned by God.

translit: ēkānta māki veḷiyāy iruntatiṅ keṉṉaimuṉṉē mōkānta kārattiṉ mīṭṭateṉ neñca muyaṅkirumpiṉ mākānta māṉatu valviṉai tīrtteṉai vāḻvitteṉṟaṉ tēkānta nīkkiya tuttara ñāṉa citamparamē.
translation: It existed as a solitary expanse here before me, rescued me from the dense darkness of delusion, became the great magnet for the iron of my heart, resolved my harsh karma, made me live, and removed my body's end: it is Uttara Jnana Chidambaram.
commentary: Here, the divine is an active force in the devotee's life. It dispels the confusion of worldly delusion, draws the soul toward it like a magnet attracts iron, and erases the effects of past actions (karma). Last, it bestows a new kind of life by overcoming the finality of bodily death.

translit: cīrviḷaṅku cuttat tirumēṉi tāṉtarittup pārviḷaṅka nāṉpaṭutta pāyalilē - tārviḷaṅka vantāy eṉaittūkki maṟṟorucār vaittaṉaiyē entāyniṉ uḷḷamaṟi yēṉ.
translation: You came to the mat on which I lay, bearing a pure, sacred form of radiant glory and a shining garland, so that the world was lit. You lifted me and laid me down on the other side. My Father, I cannot know Your heart.
commentary: The experience of grace is presented as a physical event. As the poet lies on his mat, God appears in a tangible, radiant form, lifts his body, and moves him to another place or state of being. The poet is left in awe, unable to comprehend the nature of this divine act.

translit: payattō ṭorupāl paṭuttiruntēṉ eṉpāl nayattō ṭaṇaintē nakaittu - vayattālē tūkki eṭutteṉaimēl cūḻalilē vaittaṉaināṉ pākkiyavāṉ āṉēṉ patintu.
translation: I was lying on one side in fear. You approached me with kindness and a smile. By your power, you lifted me up and placed me in a higher state. Firmly established, I have become a blessed one.
commentary: He was not seeking enlightenment or praying for help; he was simply lying down in fear. Grace came to him anyway, as an unasked act of kindness that lifted him into a blessed state.

translit: eṉṉēniṉ taṇṇaruḷai eṉṉeṉpēṉ ivvulakil muṉṉē tavantāṉ muyaṉṟēṉō - koṉṉē paṭuttayarntēṉ nāṉpaṭutta pāyarukuṟ ṟeṉṉai eṭuttorumēl ēṟṟivaittā yē.
translation: Oh, what can I say of your cool grace? What can I possibly say? Did I undertake austerities in this world before? I just lay exhausted for no reason, and you came near the mat where I lay, lifted me, and placed me on high.
commentary: The poet questions whether some forgotten good deed or past austerity earned him this grace. He concludes it was not earned at all; he was simply lying down, exhausted and helpless, when God came and elevated him. This reinforces the idea that grace is a pure gift, independent of merit.

translit: cintā kulattoṭunāṉ teyvamē eṉṟuniṉain tantō paṭuttuḷ ayarvuṟṟēṉ - entāy eṭuttāḷ eṉaniṉaiyā tēkiṭantēṉ eṉṉai eṭuttāy tayavaiviya vēṉ.
translation: My mind troubled, I thought, "Oh God!", and lay down, utterly weary within. I lay there, my father, not even thinking that you would lift and claim me as your own. But you did lift me. I am amazed at your compassion.
commentary: His despair was so complete that he had given up all hope of being saved. He lay in mental anguish, not even capable of thinking that God might intervene. The shock and wonder come from being lifted up from this state of utter helplessness, revealing a compassion that operates beyond human expectation or even prayer.

translit: uṉṉukiṉṟa tōṟumeṉa tuḷḷam urukukiṉṟa teṉṉuraippēṉ eṉṉuraippēṉ entāyē - tuṉṉiniṉṟu tūkkam tavirtteṉṉait tūkkieṭut taṉpoṭumēl ākkamuṟa vaittāy atu.
translation: Every time I think of it, my heart melts. What can I say? What can I say, my father? You came close, drove away my stupor, lifted me with love, and placed me on high to flourish. This is what you have done.
commentary: The memory of this unearned intervention is a source of continuous wonder and devotion. God's action is a rescue and a transformation, lifting him out of a stupor and setting him on a path to flourish. This memory becomes a perpetual source of overwhelming gratitude.

translit: nāṉpaṭutta pāyarukil naṇṇi eṉaittūkki ūṉpaṭutta tēkam oḷiviḷaṅkat - tāṉpatitta mēliṭattē vaittaṉaināṉ vemmaielām tīrntēṉniṉ kāliṭattē vāḻkiṉṟēṉ kāṇ.
translation: You came near the mat where I lay, lifted me up, and made my flesh-bound body shine with light. You placed me in the high place You established. I was relieved of all my burning affliction. See, I now live at Your feet.
commentary: The experience of grace has a physical dimension. Being "lifted" by God results in the body itself shining with light, a sign of spiritual purification and a release from affliction. His life is now reframed as one lived in constant closeness to God, "at Your feet."

translit: puṇṇiyantāṉ yātu purintēṉō nāṉaṟiyēṉ paṇṇiyatuṉ pōṭē paṭuttiruntēṉ - naṇṇieṉait tūkki eṭutteṉatu tuṉpamelān tīrttaruḷi ākkiyiṭeṉ ṟēyaruḷtan tāy.
translation: I do not know what merit I performed. I lay there with the suffering of my own making. You came near, lifted me up, graciously ended all my suffering, and gave me grace, saying, "Create!"
commentary: He had done nothing to earn it; he lay with the suffering of his own making. God came, lifted him, ended all his suffering, and gave him grace with a command: "Create!" Grace does not only rescue, it entrusts. The same commission appears in the poems that follow, where God gives Vallalar the five functions, beginning with creation (088/12, 089).

translit: añciañci ūṇum aruntāmal āṅkorucār pañciṉ uḻantē paṭuttayarntēṉ - viñciaṅku vantāy eṉaittūkki maṟṟorucār vaittamutu tantāyeṉ nāṉcey tavam.
translation: Trembling with fear, I did not even eat. I lay exhausted on one side, suffering like carded cotton. You came there, lifted me up, placed me on the other side, and gave me nectar. What penance did I perform to deserve this?
commentary: The state of suffering is depicted with vivid physical details: fear, inability to eat, a feeling of being torn apart. God’s response is equally tangible, providing safety and amutu (nectar), the divine food that grants spiritual nourishment and eternal life. The verse ends by again marveling that such a gift could be given without any penance to earn it.

translit: nāṉē tavampurintēṉ nāṉē kaḷippaṭaintēṉ tēṉē eṉumamutam tēkka:uṇṭēṉ - ūṉē oḷiviḷaṅkap peṟṟēṉ uṭaiyāṉ eṉaittāṉ aḷiviḷaṅkat tūkkiaṇait tāṉ.
translation: It was I who performed the penance. It was I who attained bliss. I drank my fill of nectar that is like honey. I received the gift of my very flesh shining with light. The Master lifted and embraced me, making grace manifest.
commentary: After receiving grace, the speaker’s perspective shifts. He now sees that his entire life, including the suffering, was the very "penance" that God guided him through. The sign of this successful union is a physical transformation: his flesh begins to shine with light, showing that the divine has become manifest in his very body.

translit: vāḻi eṉaittūkki vaitta karatalaṅkaḷ vāḻi elāmvalla maṇimaṉṟam - vāḻinaṭam vāḻi aruṭcōti vāḻinaṭa rāyaṉ vāḻi civañāṉa vaḻi.
translation: Long live the hands that lifted and placed me. Long live the all-powerful jeweled court. Long live the dance. Long live the grace-light. Long live the King of Dance. Long live the path of supreme divine knowledge.
commentary: An overwhelming experience of grace naturally bursts forth into praise. Vallalar celebrates every aspect of his salvation: the hands that rescued him, the sacred space of the jeweled court (maṇimaṉṟam), the cosmic dance of God, the transforming grace-light, the divine Lord himself, and the path of supreme divine knowledge (Siva-Gnanam) that has now opened to him.

sections.title: Confronting the Heart (At Tillai and Parvatipuram)

translit: aṉṉaiyappaṉ māviṉattār āykuḻalār ācaiyiṉāl teṉṉaioppa nīṇṭa ciṟuneñcē - eṉṉaieṉṉai yāvakaicēr vāyil eyiṟṟillai eṉkilaiyō āvakaiain tāyppatamā ṟārntu.
translation: O small heart, grown as tall as a coconut palm with longing for mother, father, great kin and fair-haired women! Alas, alas, why do you not say 'Thillai,' the city whose walls hold gateways of every kind? (The closing clue, ஆவகை ஐந்தாய்ப் பதம் ஆறு ஆர்ந்து, should be rendered from the Urainadai.)
commentary: This pathigam is built of riddles that hide the names Thillai and Pārvatipuram. Vallalar scolds his small heart, grown tall as a coconut palm with longing for family and women, and asks why it will not simply say 'Thillai,' the walled city of the dancing Lord, and turn there.

translit: nīrkkicainta nāma nilaimūṉṟu koṇṭapeyar pōrkkicainta teṉṟaṟiyāp puṉṉeñcē - nīrkkicaintē oṉṟuoṉṟuoṉṟu oṉṟuoṉṟuoṉṟu oṉṟuoṉṟu tillaimaṇi maṉṟoṉṟu vāṉai makiḻntu.
translation: O wretched heart, you who do not know that the name which is suited to water and has three states is also suited for battle! Yielding to grace, joyfully praise the One in the jeweled hall of Thillai, the heavenly One, who is One, One, One, One, One, One, One, One.
commentary: The name of God contains a secret power, acting as both a source of peace and a weapon for the inner battle against desire. Vallalar tells his heart to stop its foolish wandering and focus entirely on the supreme Being in the jeweled hall (maṇimaṉṟam) of Thillai. By repeating "One" eight times, he stresses the need to fix the mind on the single, absolute reality of God, abandoning all other thoughts.

translit: īṟṟiloṉṟāy maṟṟai iyalvarukka mākiyapēr ēṟṟa paṟavai irumaikkum - cāṟṟuvamai aṉṟē talaimakaṭkā ampalavar tampālē(ku) eṉṟē eṉakkuniṉak kum.
translation: The name of that particular bird, which is singular at its end and whose other letters form a natural class, is a fitting simile for a pair. Is it not? For the sake of our supreme Lady, did I not tell both you and me to go to the Lord of the Hall?
commentary: This verse contains another riddle, this time about a mythical bird called the anril, which is a symbol of inseparable love. He uses it as a metaphor for the divine couple, the Lord and the Lady (Siva and Shakti), who are always together. It is a poetic way of reminding himself, and his heart, that the goal is to seek refuge with the Divine in this state of perfect, loving union.

translit: kaittalaimē liṭṭalaiyiṟ kaṇṇuṭaiyāḷ kālmalarkkuk kaittalaimē liṭṭalaiyiṟ kaṇrkoṇ - ṭuyttalaimēl kāṇāyēl uṇmaik katinilaiyaik kaikkaṇiyāk kāṇāyē neñcē kaḷittu.
