translation: O heart, if you do not worship at the flower-like feet of the Goddess who keeps her eye on the skull held in the Lord's hand, if you fail, with tear-filled eyes and hands placed upon your head, to truly see her and bear her grace upon your crown, you will never joyfully see the state of true liberation as a jewel in your own hand.
commentary: The only path to true liberation is heartfelt, emotional devotion to the Goddess. Vallalar uses potent imagery to make this point: the Lord holds a skull, symbolizing his power over death, while the Goddess's gaze upon it shows that she is the one who grants freedom from it. This freedom is won by a surrender so complete that it brings tears to the eyes and makes you raise your hands in reverence. For such a devotee, liberation becomes a tangible reality, as certain as a jewel held in the palm of your hand.

translit: kallō maṇalō kaṉiyō karumpōeṉ(ṟu) ellōmum iṅkē irukkiṉṟōm - collōm atuvāy ataṉporuḷāy appālāy yārkkum potuvāy naṭikkiṉṟa pōtu.
translation: "Is he stone? Or sand? Is he a ripe fruit? Or sugarcane?" All of us are here, unable to say, while he performs his dance: being That, being its meaning, being beyond it, and being common to all.
commentary: God's true nature is beyond all human categories. People wonder if the divine is remote and unfeeling like a stone, or sweet and accessible like sugarcane, but Vallalar says we are all left speechless. As God dances, sustaining all of existence, He is at once the thing itself, the meaning behind it, the mystery beyond it, and a presence equally available to everyone.

translit: atupār atilē aṭaintuvati maṟṟāṅ(ku) atilēḻai yaippuramey yaṉpāl - atilē nalamē vatilēniṉ ṉāvūr tiruvam palamēvak kāṭṭum paricu.
translation: Look there. Reach it and reside. There, with true love, protect this poor one. Residing there in goodness is the way it will reveal the sacred Ambalam of your Avur.
commentary: This is a direct instruction for spiritual practice: fix your attention on the divine and make that awareness the place where you live. From this inner stability, act with love and compassion for your own soul. This verse is a riddle. Pār ('look'), vati ('dwell') and pura ('protect') spell out Pārvatipuram, the name Vallalar gave to Vadalur. Dwell there in goodness, the heart is told, and it will show you the sacred Ambalam.

translit: nampār vatipāka ṉampurattil niṉṟuvantōṉ ampārat teṉkiḻakkē ampalattāṉ - vempātu pārttāl aḷippāṉ teriyuñ citamparamnī pārttāyip pāṭṭiṉ paricu.
translation: Our Lord who shares His form with Pārvati, who came from that town, is the Lord of the Ambalam that lies to its southeast. If you look without wavering, He will give His grace and Chidambaram will be seen. You have now seen the meaning of this song.
commentary: The riddle continues. 'Pārvati' and 'puram' together name Pārvatipuram, Vallalar's Vadalur; the Ambalam of Chidambaram lies to its southeast. The Lord who dances at Chidambaram is the Lord who came from Pārvatipuram. Look without agitation, and His grace will show you Chidambaram.

translit: naṭippār vatitillai naṟkō purattiṉ aṭippāvai yumvaṭakkē ārntu - koṭippāya niṉṟu vaḷarmalaipōl neñcēpārt tālteriyum iṉṟevviṭat teṉṉilippāṭ ṭil.
translation: The base of the fine gopuram of Thillai, where the Dancer dwells, is to the north. It stands growing like a mountain with streaming flags. O heart, if you look, it will be revealed. If you ask where it is today, the answer is in this song.
commentary: The riddles of Thillai and Pārvatipuram continue. Hidden in 'naṭippār vati Tillai' is the name Pārvati, and the verse points north from Thillai's fine gopuram, to the place that rises like a mountain hung with banners: Pārvatipuram, Vadalur. 'Look, heart, and you will see it; if you ask where it is today, it is in this song.'

translit: pūmi poruntu purattēnamatuciva kāmitaṉai vēṭṭuk kalantamarntāṉ - nēmi aḷittāṉmāl kaṇmalaruk kāṉantak kūttil kaḷittāṉ avaṉṟāṉ kaḷittu.
translation: In the city that joins the earth, he desired our Sivakami, united with her, and settled there. He is the one who granted the discus to Vishnu for his eye-flower. He himself reveled, rejoicing in the dance of bliss.
commentary: The divine is portrayed here as deeply involved with creation. God unites with Sivakami (the divine feminine, representing consciousness and power), settles in the world, and bestows grace. The "dance of bliss" is a joyful expression of this cosmic engagement.
NOTES
Note 286

tamil: அடிப்பார்வையும் - முதற்பதிப்பு, சிவாசாரியர் அகவற் பதிப்பு., பொ. சு., பி. இரா.,ச. மு. க.
translit: aṭippārvaiyum - mutaṟpatippu, civācāriyar akavaṟ patippu., po. cu., pi. irā.,ca. mu. ka.
translation: aṭippārvaiyum — reading of the first edition, the Civācāriyar Akaval edition, Po. Su., P. Irā., S. Mu. Ka.
Note 287

translit: pūmiporuntupuram - pārvatipuram(pūmi - pār, poruntu - vati).
translation: pūmiporuntupuram: Pārvatipuram (pūmi = pār, "earth"; poruntu = vati, "to dwell").

sections.title: Having Nothing to Give in Return

tamil: கடையேன் புரிந்த குற்றமெலாம் கருதா தென்னுட் கலந்துகொண்டு
தடையே முழுதும் தவிர்த்தருளித் தனித்த ஞான அமுதளித்துப்
புடையே இருத்தி அருட்சித்திப் பூவை தனையும் புணர்த்திஅருட்
கொடையே கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: kaṭaiyēṉ purinta kuṟṟamelām karutā teṉṉuṭ kalantukoṇṭu taṭaiyē muḻutum tavirttaruḷit taṉitta ñāṉa amutaḷittup puṭaiyē irutti aruṭcittip pūvai taṉaiyum puṇarttiaruṭ koṭaiyē koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: Ignoring all the faults committed by me, the lowliest one, You mingled within me, completely removed every obstacle, and gave me the unique ambrosiaof wisdom. You seated me by Your side, united me with the maiden called Gracious Power, and bestowed the very gift of Grace. What recompense can I possibly give You?
commentary: Grace is a gift given freely, not something earned by being good. Vallalar expresses astonishment that God would ignore all his faults, remove his inner obstacles, grant him the ambrosia (amutam) of pure wisdom, and even unite him with divine power itself. The overwhelming feeling is one of wonder at receiving a love that asks for nothing back.

tamil: கடுத்த மனத்தை அடக்கிஒரு கணமும் இருக்க மாட்டாதே
படுத்த சிறியேன் குற்றமெலாம் பொறுத்தென் அறிவைப் பலநாளும்
தடுத்த தடையைத் தவிர்த்தென்றும் சாகா நலஞ்செய் தனிஅமுதம்
கொடுத்த குருவே நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: kaṭutta maṉattai aṭakkioru kaṇamum irukka māṭṭātē paṭutta ciṟiyēṉ kuṟṟamelām poṟutteṉ aṟivaip palanāḷum taṭutta taṭaiyait tavirtteṉṟum cākā nalañcey taṉiamutam koṭutta kuruvē niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: I am a wretched, lowly one, unable to control my raging mind even for a moment. You forgave all my faults, removed the obstacle that had long blocked my intellect, and gave me the unique ambrosia that grants the eternal good of deathlessness. O Guru who gave this, what recompense can I possibly give You?
commentary: The experience of grace is heightened by a keen awareness of one's own imperfection. Vallalar sees himself as someone unable to quiet his own mind for even a moment, yet God forgave his failings and bestowed the ultimate gift: deathlessness. The Guru who gives this is God himself, acting as the ultimate teacher.

tamil: மருவும் உலகம் மதித்திடவே மரண பயந்தீர்த் தெழில்உறுநல்
உருவும் பொருள்ஒன் றெனத்தெளிந்த உணர்வும் என்றும் உலவாத
திருவும் பரம சித்திஎனும் சிறப்பும் இயற்கைச் சிவம்எனும்ஓர்
குருவும் கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: maruvum ulakam matittiṭavē maraṇa payantīrt teḻiluṟunal uruvum poruḷoṉ ṟeṉatteḷinta uṇarvum eṉṟum ulavāta tiruvum parama cittieṉum ciṟappum iyaṟkaic civameṉumōr kuruvum koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: So that the world around me would honour it, You removed the fear of death and gave me a beautiful, good form; the clear realization that the Reality is One; ever-undiminishing wealth; the eminence called Supreme Siddhi; and a Guru who is the natural Sivam. What recompense can I possibly give You?
commentary: God’s grace transforms every part of life, from the physical to the spiritual. Vallalar lists the gifts he has received: a renewed body free from the fear of death; clear insight into reality; inexhaustible spiritual wealth (tiru); supreme spiritual power (Parama-Siddhi); and the ultimate teacher, God understood as Natural Siva (Iyarkai Civam), the very fabric of existence. Faced with such complete transformation, the only possible response is stunned gratitude.

tamil: சேட்டித் துலகச் சிறுநடையில் பல்கால் புகுந்து திரிந்துமயல்
நீட்டித் தலைந்த மனத்தைஒரு நிமிடத் தடக்கிச் சன்மார்க்கக்
கோட்டிக் கியன்ற குணங்களெலாம் கூடப் புரிந்து மெய்ந்நிலையைக்
காட்டிக் கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: cēṭṭit tulakac ciṟunaṭaiyil palkāl pukuntu tirintumayal nīṭṭit talainta maṉattaioru nimiṭat taṭakkic caṉmārkkak kōṭṭik kiyaṉṟa kuṇaṅkaḷelām kūṭap purintu meynnilaiyaik kāṭṭik koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: My mind behaved wantonly, repeatedly entering the petty ways of the world and wandering in prolonged delusion. In a single minute, You subdued that mind, made it embody all the qualities fit for the Sanmarkkam assembly, and revealed the state of Truth. What recompense can I possibly give You?
commentary: The power of grace can accomplish in an instant what a lifetime of personal effort cannot. The mind, lost for years in worldly delusion, is subdued "in a single minute." It is a sudden, radical transformation initiated by the Guru. This purified mind is then made fit to join the Sanmarkkam (the True Path) and perceive reality directly.

tamil: தோலைக் கருதித் தினந்தோறும் சுழன்று சுழன்று மயங்கும்அந்த
வேலைக் கிசைந்த மனத்தைமுற்றும் அடக்கி ஞான மெய்ந்நெறியில்
கோலைத் தொலைத்துக் கண்விளக்கம் கொடுத்து மேலும் வேகாத
காலைக் கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: tōlaik karutit tiṉantōṟum cuḻaṉṟu cuḻaṉṟu mayaṅkumanta vēlaik kicainta maṉattaimuṟṟum aṭakki ñāṉa meynneṟiyil kōlait tolaittuk kaṇviḷakkam koṭuttu mēlum vēkāta kālaik koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: Fixated on skin, my mind spun daily in delusion, well-suited for that task. You subdued that mind completely. You took away the staff I leaned on, gave clarity to my eyes, and moreover gave me the vēkāk kāl, the breath that fire cannot burn. What recompense can I possibly give You?
commentary: Grace frees the mind from its obsession with the perishable body. The staff the blind man leaned on is taken away and true sight is given. The crowning gift is the vēkāk kāl, the breath that fire cannot burn, one of the attainments Vallalar names when he speaks of the deathless life.

tamil: பட்டிப் பகட்டின் ஊர்திரிந்து பணமே நிலமே பாவையரே
தெட்டிற் கடுத்த பொய்ஒழுக்கச் செயலே என்று திரிந்துலகில்
ஒட்டிக் குதித்துச் சிறுவிளையாட் டுஞற்றி யோடும் மனக்குரங்கைக்
காட்டிக் கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: paṭṭip pakaṭṭiṉ ūrtirintu paṇamē nilamē pāvaiyarē teṭṭiṟ kaṭutta poyoḻukkac ceyalē eṉṟu tirintulakil oṭṭik kutittuc ciṟuviḷaiyāṭ ṭuñaṟṟi yōṭum maṉakkuraṅkaik kāṭṭik koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: You exposed and handed over to me the monkey-mind that roams through towns with rustic pomp, pursuing only money, land, and women, acts of deceitful, false conduct. It wanders the world clinging, leaping, performing childish games, and running about. What return can I possibly give to you?
commentary: The first gift of grace is often self-awareness. The Guru does not simply tame the restless "monkey-mind"; he exposes it and "hands it over" to the seeker. This act of grace allows the individual to see their own mind's chaotic nature with objective clarity. Recognizing the mind's childish pursuit of money, land, and pleasure is the essential first step toward transcending it.

tamil: மதியைக் கெடுத்து மரணம்எனும் வழக்கைப் பெருக்கி இடர்ப்படும்ஓர்
விதியைக் குறித்த சமயநெறி மேவா தென்னைத் தடுத்தருளாம்
பதியைக் கருதிச் சன்மார்க்கப் பயன்பெற் றிடஎன் உட்கலந்தோர்
கதியைக் கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: matiyaik keṭuttu maraṇameṉum vaḻakkaip perukki iṭarppaṭumōr vitiyaik kuṟitta camayaneṟi mēvā teṉṉait taṭuttaruḷām patiyaik karutic caṉmārkkap payaṉpeṟ ṟiṭaeṉ uṭkalantōr katiyaik koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: You graciously stopped me from following the religious paths that corrupt the intellect, perpetuate the practice of death, and prescribe a fate of suffering. To ensure I received the benefit of Sanmarkkam, you made me contemplate the Master, mingled within my being, and gave me the ultimate state of refuge. What return can I possibly give to you?
commentary: Vallalar names plainly what the religious paths do: they corrupt the intellect, multiply the custom of death, and bind people to a fate of suffering. God stopped him from entering them, turned his mind to the Lord of grace, and mingled within him so that he would reap the fruit of Sanmarkkam. This path is not another religion but the living presence of the Master within, the only true refuge.

tamil: தருண நிதியே என்னொருமைத் தாயே என்னைத் தடுத்தாண்டு
வருண நிறைவில் சன்மார்க்கம் மருவப் புரிந்த வாழ்வேநல்
அருண ஒளியே எனச்சிறிதே அழைத்தேன் அழைக்கும் முன்வந்தே
கருணை கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: taruṇa nitiyē eṉṉorumait tāyē eṉṉait taṭuttāṇṭu varuṇa niṟaivil caṉmārkkam maruvap purinta vāḻvēnal aruṇa oḷiyē eṉacciṟitē aḻaittēṉ aḻaikkum muṉvantē karuṇai koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: “O opportune treasure! O my one, true mother! O life that stopped me and now rules me, making me attain Sanmarkkam in its full perfection! O beautiful light of dawn!” I had barely begun to call out like this when you came, even before my call was finished, and gave me your compassion. What return can I possibly give to you?
commentary: God's grace does not have to be waited for or earned through long effort. Vallalar expresses a feeling of deep intimacy and connection: the moment he even begins to call out, God is already there with an answer. This shows a relationship built on immediate, loving response.

tamil: பொற்பங் கயத்தின் புதுநறவும் சுத்த சலமும் புகல்கின்ற
நற்பஞ் சகமும் ஒன்றாகக் கலந்து மரண நவைதீர்க்கும்
கற்பங் கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: poṟpaṅ kayattiṉ putunaṟavum cutta calamum pukalkiṉṟa veṟpan taramā matimatuvum viḷaṅkupacuviṉ tīmpālum naṟpañ cakamum oṉṟākak kalantu maraṇa navaitīrkkum kaṟpaṅ koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: Mixing together as one the fresh nectar of the golden lotus, pure water, the praised ambrosia of the moon from the mountain expanse, the sweet milk of the radiant cow, and the fine five-fold blend, you gave me the kaṟpam that ends the disease of death. What return can I possibly give to you?
commentary: The goal of spiritual life for Vallalar is the conquest of death itself. He names the gift plainly: a kaṟpam, the Siddha elixir, made of the fresh nectar of the golden lotus, pure water, the moon's ambrosia from the mountain, the sweet milk of the cow and the fine five-fold blend, given to end the disease of death. He states it as fact: God has given him what removes death.

tamil: புலையைத் தவிர்த்தென் குற்றமெலாம் பொறுத்து ஞான பூரணமா
நிலையைத் தெரித்துச் சன்மார்க்க நீதிப் பொதுவில் நிருத்தமிடும்
மலையைக் காட்டி அதனடியில் வயங்க இருத்திச் சாகாத
கலையைக் கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: pulaiyait tavirtteṉ kuṟṟamelām poṟuttu ñāṉa pūraṇamā nilaiyait terittuc caṉmārkka nītip potuvil niruttamiṭum malaiyaik kāṭṭi ataṉaṭiyil vayaṅka iruttic cākāta kalaiyaik koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: You made me abandon killing and flesh-eating, forgave all my faults, and made clear to me the state of perfect wisdom. You showed me the Mountain that dances in the common space of Sanmarkkam’s justice, seated me radiantly at its feet, and gave me the art of deathlessness. What return can I possibly give to you?
commentary: This verse lays out a clear spiritual path: it begins with an ethical commitment to non-killing and compassion. This purity allows for God's forgiveness and opens the way to wisdom. The ultimate vision is of God, the "Mountain," dancing in a universal space of justice, and at its feet, one learns the secret of deathlessness. Ethics, wisdom, and immortality are linked.

tamil: அருணா டறியா மனக்குரங்கை அடக்கத் தெரியா ததனொடுசேர்ந்
திருணா டனைத்தும் சுழன்றுசுழன் றிளைத்துக் களைத்தேன் எனக்கந்தோ
தெருணா டுலகில் மரணம்உறாத் திறந்தந் தழியாத் திருஅளித்த
கருணா நிதியே நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: aruṇā ṭaṟiyā maṉakkuraṅkai aṭakkat teriyā tataṉoṭucērn tiruṇā ṭaṉaittum cuḻaṉṟucuḻaṉ ṟiḷaittuk kaḷaittēṉ eṉakkantō teruṇā ṭulakil maraṇamuṟāt tiṟantan taḻiyāt tiruaḷitta karuṇā nitiyē niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: I did not know how to control this monkey-mind that knows no dawn. Joining with it, I wandered and spun through all the lands of darkness, growing weary and exhausted. To me, alas, in this world of clarity, you granted the power not to die and gave me imperishable grace, O Treasure of Compassion. What repayment can I possibly give you?
commentary: After struggling helplessly with his own chaotic mind and wandering in spiritual darkness, Vallalar feels rescued. He expresses his exhaustion and despair, which makes the gift of grace feel even greater. God grants him the one thing he could not achieve on his own: the power to overcome death and find an unshakable, imperishable peace.

tamil: மண்ணுள் மயங்கிச் சுழன்றோடு மனத்தை அடக்கத் தெரியாதே
பெண்ணுள் மயலைப் பெருங்கடல்போல் பெருக்கித் திரிந்தேன் பேயேனை
விண்ணுள் மணிபோன் றருட்சோதி விளைவித் தாண்ட என்னுடைய
கண்ணுள் மணியே நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: maṇṇuḷ mayaṅkic cuḻaṉṟōṭu maṉattai aṭakkat teriyātē peṇṇuḷ mayalaip peruṅkaṭalpōl perukkit tirintēṉ pēyēṉai viṇṇuḷ maṇipōṉ ṟaruṭcōti viḷaivit tāṇṭa eṉṉuṭaiya kaṇṇuḷ maṇiyē niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: Not knowing how to control the mind that spins and runs, deluded by the world, I wandered about, letting my obsession with women swell like a great ocean. For me, a ghoul, you produced a Grace-Jothi like a gem in the heavens and took me as your own. O Gem within my eye, what repayment can I possibly give you?
commentary: In a moment of raw honesty, Vallalar confesses his past struggles with lust and worldly delusion. He calls himself a "ghoul" to stress how unworthy and lost he felt. The turning point was a direct experience of God as an aruṭcōti, a Jothi or Light of pure Grace. By calling God the "gem within my eye," he shows that the divine is the very source of his own sight and awareness.

tamil: புலந்த மனத்தை அடக்கிஒரு போது நினைக்க மாட்டாதே
அலந்த சிறியேன் பிழைபொறுத்தே அருளா ரமுதம் அளித்திங்கே
உலந்த உடம்பை அழியாத உடம்பாப் புரிந்தென் உயிரினுளே
கலந்த பதியே நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: pulanta maṉattai aṭakkioru pōtu niṉaikka māṭṭātē alanta ciṟiyēṉ piḻaipoṟuttē aruḷā ramutam aḷittiṅkē ulanta uṭampai aḻiyāta uṭampāp purinteṉ uyiriṉuḷē kalanta patiyē niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: I was unable to control my sulking mind and think of you even for a moment. Forgiving the faults of this suffering, insignificant one, you gave me the nectar of grace. Here, you transformed my perishing body into an imperishable body, O Master who has mingled with my very soul! What repayment can I possibly give you?
commentary: Here, he speaks of a physical transformation that is a core part of his teaching. While most traditions seek to liberate the soul from the body, Vallalar states that God's grace made his mortal, perishing body into an immortal, imperishable one. This miracle is presented as the ultimate act of grace, where the divine Master forgives his faults and completely remakes his physical form and merges with his soul.

tamil: தனியே கிடந்து மனங்கலங்கித் தளர்ந்து தளர்ந்து சகத்தினிடை
இனியே துறுமோ என்செய்வேன் எந்தாய் எனது பிழைகுறித்து
முனியேல் எனநான் மொழிவதற்கு முன்னே கருணை அமுதளித்த
கனியே கரும்பே நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: taṉiyē kiṭantu maṉaṅkalaṅkit taḷarntu taḷarntu cakattiṉiṭai iṉiyē tuṟumō eṉceyvēṉ entāy eṉatu piḻaikuṟittu muṉiyēl eṉanāṉ moḻivataṟku muṉṉē karuṇai amutaḷitta kaṉiyē karumpē niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: Lying alone in this world, my mind agitated, growing weaker and weaker, I wondered, "What will happen now? What can I do?" My Father, even before I could plead, "Do not be angry over my faults," you gave me the nectar of compassion. O sweet Fruit, O Sugarcane! What repayment can I possibly give you?
commentary: This verse captures a moment of utter despair, where he felt alone and helpless. The central point is that God's compassion acted before he could even properly ask for it. Grace was not a reward for prayer; it was an unconditional gift that anticipated his suffering. The loving names he uses for God, "sweet Fruit" and "Sugarcane," convey the deep sweetness and relief he felt in that moment.

tamil: பெண்ணே பொருளே எனச்சுழன்ற பேதை மனத்தால் பெரிதுழன்ற
புண்ணே எனும்இப் புலைஉடம்பில் புகுந்து திரிந்த புலையேற்குத்
தண்ணேர் மதியின் அமுதளித்துச் சாகா வரந்தந் தாட்கொண்ட
கண்ணே மணியே நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: peṇṇē poruḷē eṉaccuḻaṉṟa pētai maṉattāl perituḻaṉṟa puṇṇē eṉumip pulaiuṭampil pukuntu tirinta pulaiyēṟkut taṇṇēr matiyiṉ amutaḷittuc cākā varantan tāṭkoṇṭa kaṇṇē maṇiyē niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: I suffered greatly due to a foolish mind that spun, chasing after women and wealth. For me, a base person who entered and wandered in this vile body which is but a wound, you gave me nectar like the cool moon, granted the boon of immortality, and took me as your own. O my very Eye, O Gem, what repayment can I possibly give you?
commentary: Vallalar describes his past life, driven by desire for "women and wealth," as a sickness. He views the ordinary human body as a "wound," a source of suffering. God's grace is a cooling nectar that soothes the fever of these desires. The result is the final healing: the "boon of immortality," which transforms this wounded, vile body into a perfected, deathless one.

tamil: பொருத்திக் கொடுத்த புலைஉடம்பில் புகுந்தேன் புணைத்தற் கிணங்காத
எருத்தில் திரிந்தேன் செய்பிழையை எண்ணா தந்தோ எனைமுற்றும்
திருத்திப் புனித அமுதளித்துச் சித்தி நிலைமேல் சேர்வித்தென்
கருத்தில் கலந்தோய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: poruttik koṭutta pulaiuṭampil pukuntēṉ puṇaittaṟ kiṇaṅkāta eruttil tirintēṉ ceypiḻaiyai eṇṇā tantō eṉaimuṟṟum tiruttip puṉita amutaḷittuc citti nilaimēl cērvitteṉ karuttil kalantōy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: I entered this vile, fleshy body that was fitted to me and wandered like a bull that resists the yoke. Alas, you did not count my mistakes; instead, you completely corrected me, gave me pure ambrosia, and raised me to the state of siddhi. O you who then merged with my consciousness, what recompense can I possibly give to you?
commentary: Our resistance to a spiritual life is like a stubborn bull fighting the yoke, wandering uselessly. Yet divine grace does not punish this willfulness; it actively corrects and transforms the soul. This transformation is forgiveness and a complete elevation to a state of siddhi (spiritual perfection) and, most intimately, a merging of the divine with one's own consciousness.

tamil: பெண்ணுக் கிசைந்தே பலமுகத்தில் பேய்போல் சுழன்ற பேதைமனத்
தெண்ணுக் கிசைந்து துயர்க்கடலாழ்ந் திருந்தேன் தன்னை எடுத்தருளி
விண்ணுக் கிசைந்த கதிர்போல்என் விவேகத் திசைந்து மேலும்என்தன்
கண்ணுக் கிசைந்தோய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: peṇṇuk kicaintē palamukattil pēypōl cuḻaṉṟa pētaimaṉat teṇṇuk kicaintu tuyarkkaṭalāḻn tiruntēṉ taṉṉai eṭuttaruḷi viṇṇuk kicainta katirpōleṉ vivēkat ticaintu mēlumeṉtaṉ kaṇṇuk kicaintōy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: I yielded to women and spun like a demon in many ways; giving in to the thoughts of my foolish mind, I was submerged in an ocean of sorrow. You graciously lifted me out, entered my discerning intellect like a sun that belongs in the sky, and then became a perfect sight for my eyes. O you who did this, what recompense can I possibly give to you?
commentary: A life lost to sensual desires and confusion is like drowning in an ocean of sorrow. Grace acts as a rescue, lifting the soul out of that despair. The divine then enters the mind as a clarifying light, like the sun, sharpening one's discernment and making God's presence a clear and perceptible reality.

tamil: மாட்சி அளிக்கும் சன்மார்க்க மரபில் மனத்தைச் செலுத்துதற்கோர்
சூழ்ச்சி அறியா துழன்றேனைச் சூழ்ச்சி அறிவித் தருளரசின்
ஆட்சி அடைவித் தருட்சோதி அமுதம் அளித்தே ஆனந்தக்
காட்சி கொடுத்தாய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே
translit: māṭci aḷikkum caṉmārkka marapil maṉattaic celuttutaṟkōr cūḻcci aṟiyā tuḻaṉṟēṉaic cūḻcci aṟivit taruḷaraciṉ āṭci aṭaivit taruṭcōti amutam aḷittē āṉantak kāṭci koṭuttāy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē
translation: I struggled, knowing no strategy to direct my mind onto the path of Sanmarkkam, which bestows greatness. You taught me the strategy, made me attain the reign of your grace-kingdom, gave me the ambrosia of the Grace-Light, and granted me the vision of bliss. What recompense can I possibly give to you?
commentary: The spiritual path, Sanmarkkam (the True Path), requires a specific method for directing the mind, which is not obvious or easy to find. Grace does more than point the way; it teaches this "strategy," leading the soul into a state of blissful union, nourished by a divine Grace-Light.

tamil: பொய்யிற் கிடைத்த மனம்போன போக்கில் சுழன்றே பொய்உலகில்
வெய்யிற் கிடைத்த புழுப்போல வெதும்பிக் கிடந்த வெறியேற்கு
மெய்யிற் கிடைத்தே சித்திஎலாம் விளைவித் திடுமா மணியாய்என்
கையிற் கிடைத்தோய் நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: poyyiṟ kiṭaitta maṉampōṉa pōkkil cuḻaṉṟē poyulakil veyyiṟ kiṭaitta puḻuppōla vetumpik kiṭanta veṟiyēṟku meyyiṟ kiṭaittē cittielām viḷaivit tiṭumā maṇiyāyeṉ kaiyiṟ kiṭaittōy niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: I spun about, following the whims of a mind born of falsehood. In this false world, I lay suffering like a worm scorched by the fierce sun. To me, a madman, you appeared in truth, and as the great gem that produces all siddhis, you came right into my hands. What recompense can I possibly give to you?
commentary: The ordinary world, driven by a mind rooted in illusion, is a place of intense, helpless suffering. To the soul lost in this "madness," grace appears as the one solid reality. It is a tangible power, a gem that grants all siddhis (spiritual perfections) and places this potential for transformation directly into one's hands.

tamil: போதல் ஒழியா மனக்குரங்கின் போக்கை அடக்கத் தெரியாது
நோதல் புரிந்த சிறியேனுக் கிரங்கிக் கருணை நோக்களித்துச்
சாதல் எனும்ஓர் சங்கடத்தைத் தவிர்த்தென் உயிரில் தான்கலந்த
காதல் அரசே நின்தனக்குக் கைம்மா றேது கொடுப்பேனே.
translit: pōtal oḻiyā maṉakkuraṅkiṉ pōkkai aṭakkat teriyātu nōtal purinta ciṟiyēṉuk kiraṅkik karuṇai nōkkaḷittuc cātal eṉumōr caṅkaṭattait tavirtteṉ uyiril tāṉkalanta kātal aracē niṉtaṉakkuk kaimmā ṟētu koṭuppēṉē.
translation: Not knowing how to control the ways of my ever-wandering monkey-mind, I, a lowly one, was in distress. Taking pity on me, you cast a merciful gaze, removed the affliction called death, and merged with my very soul. O King of Love, what recompense can I possibly give to you?
commentary: The mind is famously compared to a restless monkey, and Vallalar admits he had no idea how to control it. God's response was an act of pure compassion: a merciful gaze that broke through his distress. The ultimate gift was the removal of the fear and reality of death, achieved through God intimately merging with his own soul. This is why God is addressed as the "King of Love," whose grace is a personal, loving embrace.
NOTES
Note 329

tamil: விளங்கும் - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ, சு., பி. இரா., ச. மு. க.
translit: viḷaṅkum - mutaṟpatippu., po, cu., pi. irā., ca. mu. ka.
translation: viḷaṅkum — reading of the first edition, Po. Su., P. Irā., S. Mu. Ka.

translit: nāṉpuṉainta coṉmālai naṉmālai eṉṟaruḷit tāṉpuṉaintāṉ ñāṉa capaittalaivaṉ - tēṉpuṉainta collāḷ civakāma cuntariyait tōḷpuṇarnta nallāṉtaṉ tāṭkē nayantu.
translation: The Lord of the Hall of Wisdom, the good one who embraces the shoulders of Sivakama Sundari whose speech is like honey, graciously deemed the garland of words I composed a 'good garland' and wore it himself, desiring it for his own feet.
commentary: The central image is one of gracious acceptance. Vallalar feels his poems, his "garland of words," are graciously accepted by God. God does more than approve of them; he wears them as a personal adornment, a sign of their value to him. This act of divine love is shown by the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom, who is depicted with his consort, Sivakama Sundari.

translit: collukiṉṟa eṉciṟuvāyc coṉmālai attaṉaiyum vellukiṉṟa tumpaieṉṟē mēlaṇintāṉ - valliciva kāma cavuntarikkuk kaṇṇaṉaiyāṉ ñāṉacapaic cēmanaṭa rājaṉ terintu.
translation: The protector of the Hall of Wisdom, Nata Rajan, who is like an eye to the creeper-like Sivakama Saundari, discerningly wore all the word-garlands from my humble mouth upon himself, treating them as victorious tumbai garlands.
commentary: Vallalar's humility is contrasted with God's immense grace. He sees his own words as coming from a "small, humble mouth." Yet God, the divine king Nata Rajan, receives them as if they were tumbai garlands, the white blossoms worn by ancient kings to symbolize victory in battle. God sees the devotee's sincere offering as a triumphant achievement.

translit: ētāku mōeṉanāṉ eṇṇi icaittaelām vētāka mameṉṟē mēlaṇintāṉ - pātāra vintam eṉatucira mēlamartti meyaḷitta entainaṭa rājaṉ icaintu.
translation: Agreeably, my father Nata Rajan, who placed his lotus feet on my head and granted me Truth, wore upon himself all that I sang while wondering what would come of it, taking them to be the Vedas and Agamas.
commentary: Vallalar reveals he composed his songs with doubt, unsure of their worth. In a breathtaking gesture of grace, God accepts these very songs and treats them as equal to the Vedas and Agamas, the foundational scriptures of the tradition. This is the ultimate validation. The act is sealed by the intimate blessing of God placing his feet on the devotee's head, confirming him in the path of Truth.

translit: iṉṉuraiaṉ ṟeṉṟulakam ellām aṟintiṭuka eṉṉuraiyum poṉṉuraieṉ ṟēaṇintāṉ - taṉṉuraikku nēreṉṟāṉ nīṭulakil niṉpōl uraikkavallār āreṉṟāṉ ampalavaṉ āyntu.
translation: Let the entire world know this: my words are not sweet poetry. And yet, the Lord of the Hall, after examining them, wore them as if they were words of gold. He declared them equal to His own words. He asked, "In this vast world, who else can speak like you?"
commentary: The value of one's words comes from God's acceptance. Vallalar insists his poems are nothing special, yet the Lord of the Hall (Ambalavan, another name for Siva) declares them "words of gold" and equal to His own speech. This shows his astonishment at a grace so great it finds supreme value in a humble offering.

translit: eṉpāṭṭuk keṇṇāta teṇṇi icaittēṉeṉ taṉpāṭṭaic cattiyamāt tāṉpuṉaintāṉ - muṉpāṭṭuk kālaiyilē vantu karuṇaiaḷit tētarumac cālaiyilē vāeṉṟāṉ tāṉ.
translation: I sang, thinking whatever came to my mind; He wore my willful song as Truth itself. He came before me early in the morning, granted grace, and told me, "Come to the Dharma Salai."
commentary: The experience of divine grace leads directly to a life of compassionate service. After accepting Vallalar's simple songs as truth, God gives him a clear instruction: "Come to the Dharma Salai." The Dharma Salai was the hall of charity Vallalar founded to feed the hungry. The message is that an intimate connection with God is not for personal enjoyment alone; it must be expressed through action that relieves the suffering of others.

translit: eṉṉē aticayamī tivvulakīr eṉṉuraiyaip poṉṉē eṉamēṟ puṉaintukoṇṭāṉ - taṉṉēril nalā raṇaṅkaḷelām nāṇiyavē ellāñcey vallāṉ tirukkaruṇai vāyppu.
translation: Oh people of this world, what a wonder this is! He accepted my words and adorned Himself with them as if they were gold. The good, incomparable Vedas themselves were put to shame. Such is the bestowal of the holy grace of the All-powerful One who does everything.
commentary: The direct, personal experience of grace can feel more vital and immediate than even the most sacred traditions. Vallalar expresses wonder that God cherished his words so much that the ancient Vedas (holy scriptures) themselves seemed to pale in comparison. This is an expression of awe at the overwhelming power of God's unconditional love for the individual soul.

translit: muṉpiṉaṟi yātu moḻintamoḻi mālaielām aṉpiṉ icain tantō aṇintukoṇṭāṉ - eṉparuvam pārātu vanteṉ paruvaralel lāmtavirttut tārā varaṅkaḷelām tantu.
translation: Alas, He lovingly accepted and wore all the garlands of words I uttered without forethought. Disregarding my immaturity, He came, removed all my suffering, and granted me every unobtainable boon.
commentary: God's acceptance is unconditional, embracing even words spoken from a place of immaturity and confusion. This divine parent overlooks our flaws, coming to us exactly as we are to relieve our pain and give us gifts we could never earn on our own.

translit: poṉṉoppa tāmorunī pōṟṟiyacoṉ mālaieṉṟē eṉṉappaṉ eṉcol icaintaṇintāṉ - taṉoppil vallāṉ icaintatuvē māmālai aṟputamī tellām tiruvaruṭcī rē.
translation: My Father accepted and wore my words, saying, "This garland of words you offered in praise is like gold." That the incomparable, All-powerful One accepted it is the greatest garland of all. This wonder is entirely the glory of holy grace.
commentary: The real offering is God's act of accepting the poem. Vallalar sees that the true wonder lies in divine grace, which finds value in our simple human efforts and transforms them into something precious. The glory belongs entirely to grace.

translit: piṉmuṉaṟi yēṉnāṉ pitaṟṟiyacoṉ mālaielām taṉmuṉaraṅ kēṟṟeṉavē tāṉuraittāṉ - eṉmuṉ iruntāṉeṉ ṉuḷḷē irukkiṉṟāṉ ñāṉa maruntāṉciṟ ṟampalattāṉ vāyntu.
translation: All the garlands of words I babbled, knowing neither before nor after, He Himself commanded to be formally presented before Him. He stood before me; He resides within my heart. The Lord of Chitrambalam, the medicine of wisdom, has fittingly done so.
commentary: God dignifies even our most incoherent and babbled expressions, treating them as a formal offering. This divine presence is experienced both as a being standing before him and as the indwelling reality within his own heart. The Lord of Chitrambalam (the inner space of consciousness) is the source of this deep, healing wisdom.

translit: nīyēeṉ piḷḷaiiṅku niṉpāṭṭil kuṟṟamoṉṟum āyēmeṉ ṟantō aṇintukoṇṭāṉ - nāyēṉcey puṇṇiyamiv vāṉiṟ puviyiṉ mikapperitāl eṇṇiyael lāmpurikiṉ ṟēṉ.
translation: Alas, He adorned Himself with my songs, saying, "You are my child. Here, in your song, We will find no fault." The merit that I, a mere dog, have acquired is vaster than this sky and earth; I am accomplishing everything I have envisioned.
commentary: The divine accepts the devotee's offering with the love of a parent, refusing to find any fault in it. This unconditional acceptance transforms Vallalar's self-perception from that of a worthless being to someone possessing spiritual merit vaster than the universe. This inner wealth of grace is what empowers him to accomplish all his visionary goals.

translit: eṇṇukiṉṟēṉ eṇṇutoṟeṉ eṇṇamelām tittikka naṇṇukiṉṟa teṉpukalvēṉ nāṉilattīr - uṇṇukiṉṟa uḷḷamutō nāṉtāṉ uñaṟṟutavat tāṟkiṭaitta teḷḷamutō ampalavaṉ cīr.
translation: I contemplate, and whenever I do, all my thoughts become sweet. O people of the world, what can I say of what has come to me? The glory of the Lord of the Ambalam, is it the ambrosia consumed within, or the clear ambrosia obtained through the penance I performed?
commentary: The experience of divine grace transforms the very nature of thought, making it sweet and blissful. Vallalar is overwhelmed by this state, unable to fully explain its source. He poses a question to which the answer is both: this divine ambrosia is a gift from the Lord of the Ambalam (sacred space) who dwells within, and it is also the fruit of his spiritual discipline.

translit: ākki aḷittalmuta lāntoḻilōr aintiṉaiyum tēkki amutorunī ceyeṉṟāṉ - tūkki eṭuttāṉ aṇaittāṉ iṟavāta tēkam koṭuttāṉciṟ ṟampalatteṉ kō.
translation: He said, “You alone, mastering them, perform the five functions beginning with creation and sustenance.” He lifted me up, embraced me, and gave me a deathless body, my King of Chitrambalam.
commentary: This verse makes a staggering claim: God has entrusted Vallalar with the five cosmic functions, which are creation, preservation, destruction, veiling, and grace. This signifies a state of oneness with the divine so complete that the individual soul acts with the capacity of God. This union is sealed with the granting of a deathless physical body, the ultimate sign of spiritual perfection.

translit: ciruṭṭimutal aintoḻilnāṉ ceyyaeṉak karuḷpurintāy poruṭṭikaḻniṉ peruṅkaruṇaip puṉitaamu tuvantaḷittāy teruṭṭikaḻniṉ aṭiyavartam tiruccapaiyiṉ naṭuiruttit teruṭṭieṉai vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: You graced me to perform the five functions, beginning with creation. You gladly gave the sacred ambrosia of Your great, meaning-filled compassion. Seating me in the middle of the sacred assembly of Your devotees who shine with clarity, you nurture me with wisdom. You dance in the Hall of Consciousness.
commentary: God’s grace is a continuous nurturing. Vallalar has been granted the highest spiritual authority, the "five functions" of cosmic activity, and is given a place of honor in the assembly of perfected souls. This divine care unfolds within the Chit Sabhai, the inner space of pure consciousness where God's blissful dance is eternally present.

translit: paṭaittalmutal aintoḻilcey paṇieṉakkē paṇittiṭṭāy uṭaittaṉippē raruṭcōti ōṅkiyateḷ ḷamutaḷittāy koṭaittaṉippō kaṅkoṭuttāy niṉaṭiyar kuḻunaṭuvē tiṭattamartti vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: You commanded me to perform the task of the five functions, beginning with creation. You gave the sublime, clear ambrosia of Your unique, great Grace-Light. You granted a singular, generous bliss. Firmly seating me amidst the assembly of Your devotees, you nurture me. You dance in the Hall of Consciousness.
commentary: Vallalar again describes the divine commission to perform the five cosmic functions, this time framing it as a sacred duty. The grace he receives is the "clear ambrosia" of the unique, great Grace-Light, the source of all light and consciousness. The result is a deep bliss, experienced while being nurtured among the community of saints.

translit: ayaṉmutalōr aivarceyum toḻileṉakkē aḷittiṭṭāy uyarvuṟupē raruṭcōtit tiruvamutam uvantaḷittāy mayarvaṟuniṉ aṭiyavartam capainaṭuvē vaittaruḷic ceyamuṟavē vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: You granted to me alone the functions performed by the five, beginning with Brahma. You gladly gave the sacred ambrosia of the sublime, vast Grace-Light. Graciously placing me in the middle of the assembly of Your delusion-free devotees, you nurture me toward success. You dance in the Hall of Consciousness.
commentary: The claim becomes even more explicit: Vallalar has been granted the very functions performed by the great gods, starting with Ayan (the creator god, Brahma). This suggests a state of consciousness that has absorbed the powers normally associated with even the highest deities. This empowerment is paired with being nurtured among "delusion-free devotees," showing that the highest spiritual states are realized in connection with others on the path.

translit: aivarceyum toḻileṉakkē aḷittāyniṉ aruḷamuteṉ kaivaraccey tuṇṇuvittāy kaṅkaṇameṉ karattaṇintāy caivareṉum niṉṉaṭiyār capainaṭuvē vaittaruḷit teyvameṉṟu vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: You granted to me the functions performed by the five. You placed Your grace-ambrosia in my hand and made me consume it. You adorned my wrist with the sacred bracelet. Graciously placing me in the middle of the assembly of Your devotees, the Shaivites, you nurture me as a divine being. You dance in the Hall of Consciousness.
commentary: The kanganam, a sacred bracelet tied to mark the start of a solemn undertaking, symbolizes his formal commissioning by God. He is given power and formally appointed to wield it. Being placed among Shaivites (devotees of Siva) and nurtured "as a divine being" shows his transformation is recognized within his spiritual family, elevating him from a seeker to an embodiment of the divine.

translit: muttoḻilō aintoḻilum muṉṉimakiḻn teṉakkaḷittāy puttamutam uṇṇuvittōr poṉṉaṇieṉ karattaṇintāy cittareṉum niṉṉaṭiyār tiruccapaiyil naṭuiruttic citturuviṉ vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: Whether the three functions or the five, you joyfully granted them to me. You made me consume fresh ambrosia and adorned my hand with a golden ornament. Seating me in the middle of the sacred assembly of Your devotees known as Siddhas, you nurture me into the very form of consciousness. You dance in the Hall of Consciousness.
commentary: Whether it is the three core cosmic functions (creation, preservation, destruction) or the full five, Vallalar has been granted authority over them all. He is now placed among the Siddhas, a revered lineage of perfected masters who have attained supernatural abilities and overcome death. This indicates his initiation into their ranks, as he is nurtured into becoming the "form of consciousness" itself: a conscious being and the very substance of awareness.

translit: aintoḻilnāṉ ceyappaṇittāy aruḷamutam uṇavaḷittāy ventoḻiltīrn tōṅkiyaniṉ meyyaṭiyār capainaṭuvē entaiuṉaip pāṭimakiḻn tiṉpuṟavē vaittaruḷic centamiḻiṉ vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: You tasked me with performing the five functions and gave me the food of grace-nectar. You graciously placed me in the midst of the assembly of Your true devotees, who have risen beyond harsh deeds, to sing Your praises, my Father, and rejoice in bliss. You nurture me through refined Tamil; You dance in the hall of consciousness.
commentary: After being entrusted with cosmic power, the ultimate purpose is revealed to be an act of devotion: to sing God's praises and experience bliss among true devotees. In a striking final line, Vallalar says he is nurtured by "refined Tamil" (sentamiḻ), identifying the language itself as a divine vehicle for his spiritual growth. For him, poetry is more than a description of grace; it is an instrument of grace.

translit: nāṉmukaṉnā raṇaṉmutalām aivartoḻil nayantaḷittāy mēṉmaipeṟum aruṭcōtit tiruvamutum viyantaḷittāy pāṉmaiyuṟu niṉṉaṭiyār capainaṭuvē patittaruḷit tēṉmaiyoṭu vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: You lovingly bestowed the functions of the five, including Brahma and Vishnu. You wondrously bestowed the sacred nectar of the glorious Grace-Light. You graciously established me in the midst of the assembly of Your devotees of noble character, and You nurture me with sweetness. You dance in the hall of consciousness.
commentary: Vallalar makes the astonishing claim that he has been given the specific cosmic duties of the great gods Brahma (the creator) and Vishnu (the preserver). This is more than a general blessing; it is a direct bestowal of the highest divine functions known within the tradition. The experience is accompanied by consuming the "sacred nectar of the glorious Grace-Light" (aruṭcōti), a liquid form of God's grace that transforms the recipient.

translit: nāyeṉavē tirintēṉai valintaḻaittu nāṉmukaṉmāl tūyaperun tēvarceyum toḻilpuriyeṉ ṟamutaḷittāy nāyakaniṉ ṉaṭiyarcapai naṭuvirukka vaittaruḷic cēyeṉavē vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: Me, who wandered like a dog, You forcefully called. You told me to perform the functions carried out by Brahma, Vishnu, and other pure, great gods, and You gave me nectar. O Lord, You graciously had me sit in the midst of the assembly of Your devotees and are raising me as Your child. You dance in the hall of consciousness.
commentary: The feeling of personal unworthiness makes the gift of grace feel even more miraculous. To see oneself as a wandering dog, only to be personally called by God and raised like a son, captures the essence of grace as an unearned, unconditional love. God does more than accept him; God actively seeks him out, elevates him to the highest status, and nurtures him with parental affection.

translit: pulvaḻaṅku puḻuataṉil ciṟiyēṉaip puṇarntaruḷic colvaḻaṅku toḻilaintum tuṇintukoṭut tamutaḷittāy kalvipeṟu niṉṉaṭiyar kaḻakanaṭu vaitteṉṉaic celvamoṭu vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: Me, who am more lowly than a worm on a blade of grass, You graciously embraced. You boldly granted me the five functions spoken of in the scriptures and gave me nectar. You placed me in the center of the gathering of Your learned devotees and are nurturing me with abundance. You dance in the hall of consciousness.
commentary: The speaker's sense of humility deepens, seeing himself as lower than a worm, yet God still embraces him. This extreme contrast highlights a central teaching: divine grace is not dependent on one's merit or status. God's power can transform even the most seemingly insignificant being, giving them cosmic responsibilities and placing them among the most learned and wise souls.

translit: terumaṉaitō ṟalaintēṉai alaiyāmē cērttaruḷi aruḷoḷiyāl aintoḻilum ceyappaṇittē amutaḷittu maruviyaniṉ meyyaṭiyār capainaṭuvē vaittaḻiyāt tiruvaḷittu vaḷarkkiṉṟāy ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟāy.
translation: Me, who wandered from street to street and house to house, You graciously took in so I would wander no more. With Your light of grace, You tasked me to perform the five functions and gave me nectar. You placed me in the midst of the assembly of Your true, intimate devotees, bestowing imperishable fortune and nurturing me. You dance in the hall of consciousness.
commentary: God's grace brings an end to the soul's aimless and painful wandering through life. By taking him in, God provides a permanent, secure place within the community of true devotees. The "imperishable fortune" he receives is the eternal treasure of a life centered in divine service and illumined by the light of grace (aruḷoḷi).

tamil: துனிநாள் அனைத்தும் தொலைத்துவிட்டேன் தூக்கம் தவிர்த்தேன் சுகம்பலிக்கும்
கனிநாள் இதுவே என்றறிந்தேன் கருத்து மலர்ந்தேன் களிப்புற்றேன்
தனிநா யகனே கனகசபைத் தலைவா ஞான சபாபதியே
இனிநான் இறையும் கலக்கமுறேன் இளைக்க மாட்டேன் எனக்கருளே.
translit: tuṉināḷ aṉaittum tolaittuviṭṭēṉ tūkkam tavirttēṉ cukampalikkum kaṉināḷ ituvē eṉṟaṟintēṉ karuttu malarntēṉ kaḷippuṟṟēṉ taṉinā yakaṉē kaṉakacapait talaivā ñāṉa capāpatiyē iṉināṉ iṟaiyum kalakkamuṟēṉ iḷaikka māṭṭēṉ eṉakkaruḷē.
translation: I have destroyed all days of sorrow and given up sleep. I understood that this is the ripe day for bliss to bear fruit. My thought has blossomed; I am filled with joy. O sole Lord, Chief of the Golden Hall, Master of the Hall of Wisdom! From now on, I will not be agitated in the least. I will not grow weary. Grant me Your grace.
commentary: This verse is a declaration of victory over suffering. 'I have given up sleep' is meant as said: Vallalar taught that sleep is to be reduced and overcome. The Kanaka Sabai (Golden Hall) is at Chidambaram; the Jñāna Sabai (Hall of Wisdom) belongs to Vallalar's own vision, embodied in the Sathya Gnana Sabhai at Vadalur. He announces that the ripe day has come and his old life is over.

tamil: அருளும் பொருளும் யான்பெறவே அடுத்த தருணம் இதுஎன்றே
தெருளும் படிநின் அருள்உணர்த்தத் தெரிந்தேன் துன்பத் திகைப்பொழிந்தேன்
மருளும் மனந்தான் என்னுடைய வசத்தே நின்று வயங்கியதால்
இருளும் தொலைந்த தினிச்சிறிதும் இளைக்க மாட்டேன் எனக்கருளே.
translit: aruḷum poruḷum yāṉpeṟavē aṭutta taruṇam itueṉṟē teruḷum paṭiniṉ aruḷuṇarttat terintēṉ tuṉpat tikaippoḻintēṉ maruḷum maṉantāṉ eṉṉuṭaiya vacattē niṉṟu vayaṅkiyatāl iruḷum tolainta tiṉicciṟitum iḷaikka māṭṭēṉ eṉakkaruḷē.
translation: Your grace made me clearly understand that this is the right moment for me to receive both grace and the ultimate substance. Knowing this, I cast off the bewilderment of suffering. Because my deluded mind came under my control and shone brightly, the darkness is gone. From now on, I will not grow weary in the least. Grant me Your grace.
commentary: Liberation is revealed by grace (Arul) at the "right moment." The key transformation is the mastering of the mind. Once the mind, which creates delusion and suffering, is brought under control, it ceases to be an obstacle and instead becomes a source of light, dispelling all inner darkness.

tamil: அருளே உணர்த்த அறிந்துகொண்டேன் அடுத்த தருணம் இதுஎன்றே
இருளே தொலைந்த திடர்அனைத்தும் எனைவிட் டகன்றே ஒழிந்தனவால்
தெருளே சிற்றம் பலத்தாடும் சிவமே எல்லாம் செய்யவல்ல
பொருளே இனிநான் வீண்போது போக்க மாட்டேன் கண்டாயே.
translit: aruḷē uṇartta aṟintukoṇṭēṉ aṭutta taruṇam itueṉṟē iruḷē tolainta tiṭaraṉaittum eṉaiviṭ ṭakaṉṟē oḻintaṉavāl teruḷē ciṟṟam palattāṭum civamē ellām ceyyavalla poruḷē iṉināṉ vīṇpōtu pōkka māṭṭēṉ kaṇṭāyē.
translation: As grace itself made it known, I have understood that this is the opportune moment. The darkness is gone; all troubles have left me and vanished completely. O perfect Clarity! O Sivam who dances in the Chitrambalam! O Substance with the power to do all things! Know this: from now on, I will not waste my time.
commentary: Here, the overwhelming feeling is one of clarity and purpose. The dance of Sivam (the Supreme Being) in the Chitrambalam (the inner space of the heart) has dispelled all darkness. This new clarity creates a deep sense of responsibility. Having been given this supreme gift, Vallalar vows that not another moment of his life will be wasted on anything less than the divine.

tamil: கண்டே களிக்கும் பின்பாட்டுக் காலை இதுஎன் றருள்உணர்த்தக்
கொண்டே அறிந்து கொண்டேன்நல் குறிகள் பலவுங் கூடுகின்ற
தொண்டே புரிவார்க் கருளும்அருட் சோதிக் கருணைப் பெருமனே
உண்டேன் அமுதம் உண்கின்றேன் உண்பேன் துன்பை ஒழித்தேனே.
translit: kaṇṭē kaḷikkum piṉpāṭṭuk kālai itueṉ ṟaruḷuṇarttak koṇṭē aṟintu koṇṭēṉnal kuṟikaḷ palavuṅ kūṭukiṉṟa toṇṭē purivārk karuḷumaruṭ cōtik karuṇaip perumaṉē uṇṭēṉ amutam uṇkiṉṟēṉ uṇpēṉ tuṉpai oḻittēṉē.
translation: As grace revealed that this is the time of the "latter song" in which one rejoices upon seeing, I have received and understood. Many good omens are converging. O great Lord of compassion, O Grace-Light who bestows grace on those who perform pure service! I have consumed the ambrosia; I am consuming it; I will consume it. I have eliminated suffering.
commentary: Grace reveals this time as the "latter song," the part of life where one enjoys the fruit of direct vision, more than sings in longing. This experience of ArutJothi (the Grace-Light) is confirmed by auspicious signs. The feeling of bliss is all-encompassing, described as consuming amutham (divine nectar) in the past, present, and future. It is an eternal state, where suffering has been completely and permanently eradicated.

tamil: ஒழித்தேன் அவலம் அச்சம்எலாம் ஓடத் துறந்தேன் உறுகண்எலாம்
கழித்தேன் மரணக் களைப்பற்றேன் களித்தேன் பிறவிக் கடல்கடந்தேன்
பழித்தேன் சிற்றம் பலம்என்னாப் பாட்டை மறந்தேன் பரம்பரத்தே
விழித்தேன் கருத்தின் படிஎல்லாம் விளையா டுதற்கு விரைந்தேனே.
translit: oḻittēṉ avalam accamelām ōṭat tuṟantēṉ uṟukaṇelām kaḻittēṉ maraṇak kaḷaippaṟṟēṉ kaḷittēṉ piṟavik kaṭalkaṭantēṉ paḻittēṉ ciṟṟam palameṉṉāp pāṭṭai maṟantēṉ paramparattē viḻittēṉ karuttiṉ paṭiellām viḷaiyā ṭutaṟku viraintēṉē.
translation: I have eliminated all misery and fear; I have cast out all afflictions, making them flee. I have removed the weariness of death and am free of it. I have become joyful. I have crossed the ocean of birth. I have condemned and forgotten the song that does not say "Chitrambalam." I have awakened in the Supreme Expanse and have hurried to play out everything according to my mind's will.
commentary: The experience of liberation is total: fear, affliction, the weariness of death, and the cycle of birth are all gone. Any spiritual path that does not focus on God's presence in the Chitrambalam is now seen as meaningless and is cast aside. This awakening into the "Supreme Expanse" grants a divine freedom, the ability to act with a will that is now enlightened.

tamil: விரைந்து விரைந்து படிகடந்தேன் மேற்பால் அமுதம் வியந்துண்டேன்
கரைந்து கரைந்து மனம்உருகக் கண்ர் பெருகக் கருத்தலர்ந்தே
வரைந்து ஞான மணம்பொங்க மணிமன் றரசைக் கண்டுகொண்டேன்
திரைந்து நெகிழ்ந்த தோலுடம்பும் செழும்பொன் உடம்பாய்த் திகழ்ந்தேனே.
translit: viraintu viraintu paṭikaṭantēṉ mēṟpāl amutam viyantuṇṭēṉ karaintu karaintu maṉamurukak kaṇr perukak karuttalarntē varaintu ñāṉa maṇampoṅka maṇimaṉ ṟaracaik kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ tiraintu nekiḻnta tōluṭampum ceḻumpoṉ uṭampāyt tikaḻntēṉē.
translation: Quickly, quickly, I crossed the stages and drank the supreme ambrosia in wonder. My heart dissolved and melted, tears flowed, and my consciousness blossomed. As the fragrance of wisdom arose, I saw and took for myself the King of the bejeweled hall. My wrinkled, sagging, skin-covered body shone, transformed into a body of radiant gold.
commentary: The spiritual ascent is described as a rapid climb through different stages, culminating in a direct vision of God. This is more than a mental or emotional event. Vallalar states that the experience has a tangible, physical consequence: his aging, mortal body becomes a shining, immortal body of gold. For him, the highest spiritual attainment is the body transformed.

tamil: தேனே கன்னல் செழும்பாகே என்ன மிகவும் தித்தித்தென்
ஊனே புகுந்தென் உளத்தில்அமர்ந் துயிரில் கலந்த ஒருபொருளை
வானே நிறைந்த பெருங்கருணை வாழ்வை மணிமன் றுடையானை
நானே பாடிக் களிக்கின்றேன் நாட்டார் வாழ்த்த நானிலத்தே.
translit: tēṉē kaṉṉal ceḻumpākē eṉṉa mikavum tittitteṉ ūṉē pukunteṉ uḷattilamarn tuyiril kalanta oruporuḷai vāṉē niṟainta peruṅkaruṇai vāḻvai maṇimaṉ ṟuṭaiyāṉai nāṉē pāṭik kaḷikkiṉṟēṉ nāṭṭār vāḻtta nāṉilattē.
translation: The one substance, sweet beyond measure like honey, sugarcane, and rich syrup, entered my very flesh, settled in my mind, and mingled with my life. He is the life of great grace that fills the sky, the master of the bejeweled hall. On this wide earth, I sing and rejoice in him, praised by all its people.
commentary: God is no longer a distant being, but a "one substance" experienced with intense sweetness. This divine presence has fully merged with every part of the speaker: his body ("flesh"), his mind, and his very life. His existence is now a song of joy, celebrating this intimate union for all the world to hear.

tamil: நிலத்தே அடைந்த இடர்அனைத்தும் நிமிடத் தொழித்தே நிலைபெற்றேன்
வலத்தே அழியா வரம்பெற்றேன் மணிமன் றேத்தும் வாழ்வடைந்தேன்
குலத்தே சமயக் குழியிடத்தே விழுந்திவ் வுலகம் குமையாதே
நலத்தே சுத்த சன்மார்க்கம் நாட்டா நின்றேன் நாட்டகத்தே.
translit: nilattē aṭainta iṭaraṉaittum nimiṭat toḻittē nilaipeṟṟēṉ valattē aḻiyā varampeṟṟēṉ maṇimaṉ ṟēttum vāḻvaṭaintēṉ kulattē camayak kuḻiyiṭattē viḻuntiv vulakam kumaiyātē nalattē cutta caṉmārkkam nāṭṭā niṉṟēṉ nāṭṭakattē.
translation: In a single minute, I eliminated all the suffering I had on earth and became firmly established. I received the powerful, indestructible boon and attained a life that praises the bejeweled hall. So that this world does not fall into the pits of caste and religion and suffer, I am establishing the good Suddha Sanmarkkam in this land.
commentary: Personal liberation is the beginning of a mission to help the world. Having freed himself from suffering, Vallalar's immediate response is to establish the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the pure true path). His aim is to save humanity from the divisions of caste and formal religion, which he sees as sources of deep suffering.

tamil: அகத்தே கறுத்துப் புறத்துவெளுத் திருந்த உலகர் அனைவரையும்
சகத்தே திருத்திச் சன்மார்க்க சங்கத் தடைவித் திடஅவரும்
இகத்தே பரத்தைப் பெற்றுமகிழ்ந் திடுதற் கென்றே எனைஇந்த
உகத்தே இறைவன் வருவிக்க உற்றேன் அருளைப் பெற்றேனே.
translit: akattē kaṟuttup puṟattuveḷut tirunta ulakar aṉaivaraiyum cakattē tiruttic caṉmārkka caṅkat taṭaivit tiṭaavarum ikattē parattaip peṟṟumakiḻn tiṭutaṟ keṉṟē eṉaiinta ukattē iṟaivaṉ varuvikka uṟṟēṉ aruḷaip peṟṟēṉē.
translation: The Lord caused me to come into this age for the very purpose of correcting all the people of the world who are dark inside and white outside, and making them join the Sanmarkkam Sangam so that they too may attain the supreme state in this very world and rejoice. I have arrived and received his grace.
commentary: Vallalar sees his work as a divinely ordained mission to heal human hypocrisy. He describes people as being "dark inside and white outside," and states that God sent him specifically to guide them. The goal is to bring everyone into the Sanmarkkam Sangam (the community of the true path), so that all people might attain the highest spiritual state in this life, not in some future world.

tamil: பெற்றேன் என்றும் இறவாமை பேதம் தவிர்ந்தே இறைவன்எனை
உற்றே கலந்தான் நானவனை உற்றே கலந்தேன் ஒன்றானேம்
எற்றே அடியேன் செய்ததவம் யாரே புரிந்தார் இன்னமுதம்
துற்றே உலகீர் நீவிர்எலாம் வாழ்க வாழ்க துனிஅற்றே.
translit: peṟṟēṉ eṉṟum iṟavāmai pētam tavirntē iṟaivaṉeṉai uṟṟē kalantāṉ nāṉavaṉai uṟṟē kalantēṉ oṉṟāṉēm eṟṟē aṭiyēṉ ceytatavam yārē purintār iṉṉamutam tuṟṟē ulakīr nīvirelām vāḻka vāḻka tuṉiaṟṟē.
translation: I have received eternal deathlessness. Shedding all differences, the Lord reached and mingled with me; I reached and mingled with him. We became one. What is this penance that I, his servitor, performed? Who else has ever performed it? O people of the world, having consumed this sweet ambrosia, may you all live long, live long, free from sorrow.
commentary: This is a declaration of final victory: he has attained a deathless state through perfect union with God. The distinction between himself and the divine has been erased; they have become one. He presents this achievement as an open invitation to all of humanity to share in this "sweet ambrosia" and live forever, free from all sorrow.

translit: appā eṉakkeyppil vaippāy irukkiṉṟa āramutē ippāril eṉtaṉṉai nīyē varuvit ticaivuṭaṉē tappāta tantiram mantiram yāvaiyum tantulakil veppā ṉatutavirt taintoḻil ceyya vitittaṉaiyē.
translation: Father! My rare ambrosia, a treasure for me in times of weakness! On this earth, You Yourself brought me into being. With your full consent, You gave me all the unfailing tantras and mantras and ordained me to remove the world's feverish suffering and perform the five great functions.
commentary: Vallalar's life and work are a direct command from God, whom he addresses as Father. He states that God brought him into the world and equipped him with all the necessary spiritual tools, the tantras (sacred methods) and mantras (sacred sounds). His ordained mission is to perform the five great cosmic functions (creation, preservation, destruction, concealment, and grace) to end the world's suffering.

translit: vitittaṉai eṉṉainiṉ taṉmaka ṉāka vitittuḷattē patittaṉai eṉṉuṭ patintaṉai ciṟṟam palanaṭamum utittoḷir poṉṉam palanaṭa mumoruṅ kēeṉakkē katittaḻi yāmaiyum iṉpamum kaivarak kāṭṭiṉaiyē.
translation: You ordained me as Your very own son. You established Yourself in my heart; You became imprinted within me. You revealed to me, all at once, the dance in the Hall of Consciousness and the dance in the emergent, radiant Golden Hall, bringing surging immortality and bliss into my grasp.
commentary: God's grace has established an unbreakable bond, like a father adopting a son and imprinting his own nature within the son's heart. This inner union grants Vallalar a simultaneous vision of two divine dances: one in the inner space of his own consciousness (Chitrambalam) and another in the radiant, cosmic Golden Hall, securing for him a state of eternal bliss.

translit: kāṭṭiṉai ñāṉa amutaḷit tāynaṟ kaṉakacapai āṭṭiṉai eṉpakkam ākkiṉai meypporuḷ aṉṟuvantu nīṭṭiṉai eṉṟum aḻiyā varantantu niṉcapaiyil kūṭṭiṉai nāṉmuṉam ceytavam yātatu kūṟukavē.
translation: You showed me the dance in the good Golden Hall and made it my own; You gave me the ambrosia of wisdom. That day, You came and offered me the True Substance. Giving me the boon of eternal deathlessness, You welcomed me into Your hall. What penance did I perform before? Please tell me.
commentary: The experience of grace is so overwhelming that Vallalar questions what he could possibly have done to deserve it. God has revealed everything: the dance of reality, the ambrosia of wisdom, the True Substance of existence, and the ultimate boon of a deathless life in the divine presence.

translit: kūṟukan tāyciva kāmak koṭiyaik koṭiyilveḷḷai ēṟukan tāyeṉṉai īṉṟukan tāymey ilaṅkutiru nīṟukan tāyula kellām taḻaikka nimircaṭaimēl āṟukan tāymaṉṟil āṭṭukan tāyeṉṉai āṇṭavaṉē.
translation: You delight in having Sivakami, the creeper, as Your half. You delight in the white bull on Your flag. You delight in having brought me forth. You delight in the sacred ash shining on Your body. You delight in the river on Your towering locks, so that all worlds may flourish. You delight in the dance in the hall, my Master!
commentary: This verse is a song of praise listing the things that bring delight to God. It moves from cosmic symbols, like God's consort (Sivakami) and the celestial river, to the most personal: God's delight in having brought Vallalar himself into being. The final line reveals the ultimate source of divine joy: the eternal dance of creation in the hall of consciousness.

translit: āṇṭava ṉētiru ampalat tēaru ḷāliyaṟṟum tāṇṭava ṉēeṉait tantava ṉēmuṟṟun tantavaṉē nīṇṭava ṉēuyirk kellām potuviṉil niṉṟavaṉē vēṇṭa aṉēka varaṅkoṭut tāṭkoṇṭa mēlavaṉē.
translation: My Master! Dancer who performs the Tandava in the sacred hall by grace! You who gave me, You who gave everything! You who are vast! You who stand impartially for all souls! Supreme one, who gives countless boons when asked and has taken me into Your service!
commentary: God is praised here as the Master who is both personal and universal. He is the cosmic dancer, the one who gave Vallalar life, and the vast, impartial presence that stands for all souls equally. This supreme being generously gives boons to all who ask and has personally taken Vallalar into his care.

translit: mēlava ṉētiru ampalat tāṭal viḷakkummalark kālava ṉēkaṉal kaiyava ṉēnutaṟ kaṇṇavaṉē mālavaṉ ēttum civakāma cuntara valliyaiōr pālava ṉēeṉaip pālakaṉ ākkiya paṇpiṉaṉē.
translation: He is the Supreme One, the one whose flower-like feet reveal the dance in the sacred Ambalam, the one with fire in his hand, the one with an eye on his forehead. He holds on one side Sivakama Sundara Valli, whom Vishnu praises. He is the gracious one who has made me his child.
commentary: The same immense and powerful God of the cosmos is also a loving, parental figure. Vallalar again recites Siva's iconic attributes: the dance in the sacred hall (Ambalam), the cosmic fire, the third eye of wisdom, and a divine consort praised even by the great god Vishnu. After building this image of awesome power, the verse ends with a turn to deep intimacy: this same God has made him "his child."

translit: vāṭṭamel lāntavirn tēṉaruṭ pēroḷi vāykkappeṟṟēṉ kūṭṭamel lāmpukaḻ ampala vāṇaraik kūṭappeṟṟēṉ tēṭṭamel lāmvalla cittipeṟ ṟēṉic cekatalattē āṭṭamel lāmviḷai yāṭukiṉ ṟēṉeṉak kārcariyē.
translation: I have shed all my afflictions. I have received the great light of grace. I have united with the Lord of Ambalam, whom all assemblies praise. I have attained the siddhi that accomplishes all quests. Here on this earth, I play all the games. Who is my equal?
commentary: The result of spiritual attainment is a new kind of playful and fearless existence within it. Having received grace, Vallalar is free from suffering and has gained siddhi (supernatural attainment). He describes this new state as "playing all the games" on earth, suggesting a life lived with mastery, lightness, and supreme confidence born from divine union.

translit: nāṉceyta puṇṇiyam yārcey taṉarinta nāṉilattē vāṉceyta tēvarum kāṇāta kāṭci makiḻntukaṇṭēṉ ūṉceyta meyyum uyirum uṇarvum oḷimayamāk kōṉceya vēpeṟṟuk koṇṭēṉuṇ ṭēṉaruṭ kōṉamutē.
translation: Who on this vast earth has performed the meritorious deeds that I have? I have rejoiced to see a vision unseen even by the devas of heaven. I have received the blessing of the King transforming my fleshly body, my life, and my consciousness into pure light. I have consumed the ambrosia of the gracious King.
commentary: The ultimate spiritual achievement is the transformation of one's entire being, including the physical body, into a substance of light. Vallalar expresses wonder at his state, which he says surpasses that of the devas (celestial beings in heaven). This experience is a mental realization or a vision and a complete change of his very substance: his body, life-force, and consciousness have all become light.

translit: eṉaiyāṉ matittup pukalkiṉṟa taṉṟiḵ tentaipirāṉ taṉaiyāṉ matittiṅkup peṟṟanal vāḻvatu cāṟṟukiṉṟēṉ viṉaiyāṉ melinta melivaiel lāmvirain tētavirttut taṉaiyāṉ puṇarntiṭac cākā varattaiyum tantaṉaṉē.
translation: I am not speaking this out of self-esteem; I am declaring the good life I have received here by revering my Father, the Lord. He swiftly removed all the enfeeblement caused by my karma and gave me the boon of deathlessness, so that I could unite with Him.
commentary: This extraordinary state of being is a gift of grace from God. Vallalar makes clear that his declarations are expressions of gratitude for what his "Father" has given him. This grace has wiped away the weakening effects of karma (the results of past actions) and granted him deathlessness, the final condition required for an unbroken union with God.

translit: ciṟṟam palattait terintukoṇ ṭēṉem civaṉaruḷāl kuṟṟam palavum tavirntuniṉ ṟēṉeṇ kuṇakkuṉṟilē veṟṟampal ceytavar ellām viraintu viraintuvantē naṟṟam palamtaru vāyeṉkiṉ ṟārinta nāṉilattē.
translation: By the grace of our Sivan, I have come to know the Chitrambalam. Having shed my many faults, I stand firm on the Mountain of Eight Qualities. On this vast earth, all those who engaged in empty talk now rush to me, saying, "Grant us the true benefit!"
commentary: True spiritual authority comes from inner experience, not outward status. By realizing God within the Chitrambalam, the inner hall of consciousness, Vallalar has shed his imperfections. This transformation is so complete that those who once mocked him now rush to him for guidance, recognizing the authentic spiritual wealth he possesses.

translit: oṉṟukaṇ ṭēṉtiru ampalat tēoḷi ōṅkukiṉṟa naṉṟukaṇ ṭēṉula kellām taḻaikka naṭampurital iṉṟukaṇ ṭēṉeṉṟum cākā varattai eṉakkaruḷa maṉṟukaṇ ṭārkkinta vāḻvuḷa teṉṟu makiḻntaṉaṉē.
translation: I saw a singular wonder in the sacred hall where light excels. I saw the excellence of the dance performed so all worlds may flourish. Today, I saw Him grant me the boon of never dying, and I rejoiced, realizing that this life is truly for those who have seen the Hall.
commentary: The key to immortal life lies in a specific inner vision: seeing God's cosmic dance. This dance, which gives life to all worlds, is witnessed inside the sacred hall of one's own being. Realizing this truth is more than a philosophical insight; for Vallalar, it is the very event that unlocks a deathless physical existence.

translit: ulakupukaḻ tiruvamutam tirucciṟṟam palattē uṭaiyavariṉ ṟutaviṉarnāṉ uṇṭukuṟai tīrntēṉ ilakuciva pōkavaṭi vākimakiḻ kiṉṟēṉ iḷaippaṟiyēṉ tavippaṟiyēṉ iṭarceypaci aṟiyēṉ vilakalilāt tiruvaṉaiyīr nīvirelām pocittē viraintuvammiṉ ampalattē viḷaṅkutiruk kūttiṉ alakaṟiyāt tiṟampāṭi āṭutumnām ituvē aruḷaṭaiyum neṟieṉavē tākamamārp paṉavē.
translation: Today in Thiru Chitrambalam, the Master gave me the world-renowned sacred ambrosia. I consumed it, and all my deficiencies are cured. I have become a form of radiant Sivan's bliss and I rejoice. I know no weariness, no agitation, no tormenting hunger. O you who are like the steadfast Goddess of Fortune, all of you, consume it and come quickly! We shall sing of the immeasurable power of the sacred dance shining in the Hall and dance together. The Vedas and Agamas roar that this is the very path to attaining Grace.
commentary: The experience of divine grace is like a nourishing ambrosia that ends all suffering, including physical hunger and exhaustion. Having been perfected by this grace, Vallalar’s immediate impulse is to share it. He calls everyone to come, consume this bliss, and join in celebrating the cosmic dance, affirming that even the ancient scriptures, the Vedas and Agamas, declare this shared joy to be the true path to God.

translit: mātavattāl nāṉpeṟṟa vāṉamutē eṉatu vāḻvēeṉ kaṇṇamarnta maṇiyēeṉ makiḻvē pōtavattāl kaḻittēṉai valintukalan tāṇṭa poṉṉēpoṉ ṉampalattē puṉitanaṭat taracē tītavattaip piṟappituvē civamākum piṟappāc ceyvitteṉ avattaiyelām tīrttaperum poruḷē pūtalattē aṭicciṟiyēṉ niṉatutiru vaṭikkē pukaḻmālai cūṭṭukiṉṟēṉ puṉaintukalan taruḷē.
translation: O celestial ambrosia I received through great austerity! O my life, O gem resting in my eye, O my joy! O Gold who forcibly mingled with me and ruled me, who had wasted my days in vain! O King of the sacred dance in the Golden Hall! O great reality who transformed this wretched, sinful birth into a birth that is Sivan itself, curing all my afflictions! Here on earth, I, your humble slave, am placing this garland of praise upon Your sacred feet. Adorn Yourself with it, merge with me, and bestow Your grace.
commentary: God’s grace is an active, powerful force that can completely transform a person’s life. Vallalar contrasts his own past, wasted in what he now sees as misguided spiritual practices, with the overwhelming grace that seized him and remade him. The ultimate miracle is that this intervention turned his flawed human birth into an existence that is itself divine, a "birth that is Sivan," the very embodiment of God.

translit: aḷantiṭuvē tākamattiṉ aṭiyumnaṭu muṭiyum appuṟamum appālum ataṉmēlum viḷaṅki vaḷarntiṭuciṟ ṟampalattē vayaṅkiyapē roḷiyē māṟṟaṟiyāp poṉṉēeṉ maṉṉēkaṇ maṇiyē taḷarntaeṉai akkaṇattē taḷarvoḻittā ṉantam tantaperun takaiyēeṉ taṉittataṉit tuṇaivā uḷantarucam matamāṉa paṇiiṭṭāy eṉakkē uṉpaṇiyē paṇiyallāl eṉpaṇivē ṟilaiyē.
translation: O great light shining in Chitrambalam, a light that grows and illumines beyond the beginning, middle, and end of the measurable Vedas and Agamas, beyond that, and even further beyond that! O gold of flawless purity! O my king! O gem of my eye! O great benefactor who, in that very instant, removed my weariness and gave me bliss! O my sole, unique companion! You have given me a service that my heart fully accepts. Your service is my only service; I have no other work.
commentary: The divine is a vast, living light that cannot be contained by even the most sacred scriptures like the Vedas and Agamas. After experiencing this boundless reality in Chitrambalam, all personal ambitions fall away. Vallalar finds that his life's sole purpose has become clear: to serve God, a task he embraces with his whole heart.

translit: nāṭukalan tāḷkiṉṟōr ellārum viyappa naṇṇieṉai mālaiiṭṭa nāyakaṉē nāṭṭil īṭukarain tiṭaṟkaritām tirucciṟṟam palattē iṉpanaṭam purikiṉṟa iṟaiyavaṉē eṉainī pāṭukaeṉ ṉōṭukalan tāṭukaeṉ ṟeṉakkē paṇiiṭṭāy nāṉceyperum pākkiyameṉ ṟuvantēṉ kōṭutava ṟātuṉaināṉ pāṭutaṟkiṅ kēṟṟa kuṇapporuḷum ilakkiyamum koṭuttumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: O my Lord, who approached and placed a garland on me, to the astonishment of all the rulers of the world! O God who performs the blissful dance in Thiru Chitrambalam, whose greatness is impossible to describe in this world! You commanded me: “Sing of Me! Mingle with Me and dance!” I rejoiced, seeing this as my great good fortune. So that I may sing of You without fault, please graciously give me the virtuous substance and literary skill suited for it, and be pleased.
commentary: The divine union is described as a public marriage, where God places a garland on him in a gesture of choosing him. This union comes with a divine command: to sing and dance in praise. This is the greatest possible good fortune. His prayer is for the skill and inner substance to fulfill this sacred work perfectly.

translit: naṇpuṭaiyāy eṉṉuṭaiya nāyakaṉē eṉatu naluṟavē ciṟcapaiyil naṭampuriyum talaivā eṇpuṭaiyā maṟaimuṭikkum eṭṭāniṉ pukaḻai yātaṟivēṉ pāṭukaeṉ ṟeṉakkēval iṭṭāy paṇpuṭainiṉ meyyaṉpar pāṭiyapē raṉpil paḻuttapaḻam pāṭṭiloru pāṭṭumaṟi yēṉē taṇpuṭainaṉ moḻittiraḷumcuvaipporuḷum avaikkē takka:iyal ilakkiyamum tantaruḷvāy eṉakkē.
translation: O You who are my friend! My Lord! My good kinsman! O Chief who performs the dance in the Hall of Consciousness! What do I know of Your fame, which is beyond the reach of the very crests of the revered Vedas? Yet, you commanded me, “Sing!” I do not know even a single one of the songs, ripened in great love, that Your virtuous true devotees have sung. Please grant to me a collection of cool, good words, their delicious meaning, and the literary form and skill appropriate for them.
commentary: God is addressed in the most intimate terms: friend, lord, and kinsman. Despite this closeness, Vallalar feels utterly unqualified for the task of singing God's praise, a reality he says exceeds the highest wisdom of the scriptures. He admits he does not know the classic songs of past saints and so asks God to supply everything needed for the task, from the words themselves to their poetic form.

translit: paṇintaṭaṅkum maṉattavarpāl parintamarum patiyē pāṭukiṉṟōr uḷḷakattē kūṭukiṉṟa kuruvē kaṇintamaṟai palakōṭi ākamampal kōṭi kaṭavuḷniṉa taruṭpukaḻaik kaṇippataṟkup palakāl tuṇintutuṇin teḻunteḻuntu toṭarntutoṭarn taṭikaḷ cumantucuman tiḷaittiḷaittuc colliyaval laṉaveṉ ṟaṇintamoḻi māṟṟivali taṇintaeṉṟāl antō aṭiyēṉniṉ pukaḻuraikkal āvatuvō aṟintē.
translation: O Lord who lovingly abides with those of humble and subdued minds! O Guru who unites with the inner being of those who sing your praise! If countless ripened Vedas and countless Agamas, in their effort to measure the fame of your grace, dared and rose up again and again, pursued it relentlessly, bore the burden until they were utterly weary, and then, their strength diminished, changed their ornate words and admitted, "What we said is not adequate", alas! Is it possible for me, your servant, knowing all this, to speak of your fame?
commentary: The poem ends with a powerful expression of awe. If the entire body of sacred scriptures ultimately failed to capture the full extent of divine grace, what chance does a single person have? This is both a statement of despair and recognition that God's reality is infinitely greater than any human attempt to describe it, which is why God alone must be the one to inspire the song.

translit: vitippavarkaḷ palakōṭi titippavarpal kōṭi mēlavarkaḷ orukōṭi viraintuvirain tuṉaiyē matippavarkaḷ ākiavar matiyālē palakāl matittumatit tavarmatipeṇ matiyāki alantē tutippatuvē nalameṉakkoṇ ṭiṟṟaivarai ēṟṟa coṟporuḷkaḷ kāṇātē cuḻalkiṉṟār eṉṟāl kutippoḻiyā maṉacciṟiya kuraṅkoṭuḻal kiṉṟēṉ kuṟitturaippēṉ eṉṉa:uḷam kūcukiṉṟa taracē.
translation: If countless creators, countless preservers, and a crore of celestial beings swiftly became your admirers, contemplated you with their intellects again and again until their minds grew bewildered and they suffered, and, concluding that merely praising you is best, are still spinning to this day, unable to find fitting words and meanings, O King, my heart shrinks at the thought that I, who wander with the small monkey of a mind that never stops leaping, could presume to speak definitively of you.
commentary: Even the greatest divine beings, the creators and preservers of worlds, have tried to comprehend God with their intellects and failed, left dizzy and bewildered. If they are confounded, Vallalar feels his own mind, which he compares to a restless, leaping monkey, is utterly unqualified for the task. The passage captures the futility of trying to grasp the infinite with the finite mind.

translit: oḷiyāki uḷoḷiyāy uḷoḷikkuḷ oḷiyāy oḷioḷiyiṉ oḷiyāyav oḷikkuḷumōr oḷiyāy veḷiyāki veḷiveḷiyāy veḷiyiṭaimēl veḷiyāy mēlveḷimēl peruveḷiyāyp peruveḷikkōr veḷiyāy aḷiyāki atuāki atuvumallā tāki appālāy appālum allatuvāy niṟaivām taḷiyāki ellāmāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa ñāṉa capaittalaivā niṉiyalaic cāṟṟuvatev vaṇamē.
translation: Becoming light, the light within, the light within the inner light, the light of the light of light, and a light even within that light; becoming space, the space of space, the space above space, the great space above that higher space, and a space even for that great space; becoming compassion, becoming That, and yet not being That; becoming that which is beyond, and not even that which is beyond; becoming fullness, becoming a temple, becoming everything, O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom who shines forth as all this, in what way can I possibly describe your nature?
commentary: This verse attempts to describe the indescribable nature of God through a cascade of overwhelming images. God is portrayed as an infinite layering of light and space, present at every level of reality, from the innermost core to the outermost expanse. God is everything we can conceive of ("everything," "a temple"), the ultimate principle ("That"), and also what lies beyond all concepts ("not being That," "beyond"). Addressing the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom (Gnana Sabai), Vallalar concludes that such a paradoxical, all-encompassing reality defies any possible description.

translit: vākkoḻintu maṉamoḻintu matioḻintu matiyiṉ vātaṉaiyum oḻintaṟivāy vayaṅkiniṉṟa iṭattum pōkkoḻintum varavoḻintum pūraṇamāy atuvum pōṉapoḻu tuḷḷapaṭi pukaluvatep paṭiyō nīkkoḻinta niṟaivēmeyn nilaiyēeṉ ṉuṭaiya nēyamē āṉanta niruttamiṭum patiyē ēkkoḻintār uḷattirukkum iṟaiyēeṉ kuruvē ellāmāy allatumāy ilaṅkiyameyp poruḷē.
translation: Even in the state where speech, mind, intellect, and the intellect’s impressions have all ceased, and you shine forth as pure consciousness; where coming and going have ceased and you are fullness, and even when that state itself passes away, how is it possible to speak of what is, as it is? O undiminishing fullness! O true state! O my beloved! O Lord who performs the dance of bliss! O God who dwells in the hearts of those free from desire! O my Guru! O True Substance, shining as everything and as that which is not everything!
commentary: True spiritual experience happens when the mind and its chatter completely cease. In that silence, God is revealed as pure consciousness, a state of absolute fullness beyond all coming and going. Vallalar asks a critical question: how can one possibly use words to describe a reality that is only accessible when words, thoughts, and even the self have dissolved? The attempt to speak about it is impossible, so he shifts from description to direct, loving address, calling God his beloved, his Guru, and the true substance of all that is.

translit: eṉiyalē yāṉaṟiyēṉ ivvulakiṉ iyalōr eḷaḷavum tāṉaṟiyēṉ ellāmum uṭaiyōy niṉiyalai aṟivēṉō aṟintavaṉē pōla nikaḻttukiṉṟēṉ piḷḷaieṉa nilaippeyarpeṟ ṟiruntēṉ taṉiyalām taṉiñāṉa capaittalaimaip patiyē cattiyaṉē nittiyaṉē tayānitiyē ulakam piṉiyalmā ṉiṭappiḷḷai pēcciṉumōr paṟavaip piṟappiṉuṟum kiḷippiḷḷaip pēccuvakkiṉ ṟatuvē.
translation: I do not know my own nature. I do not know the nature of this world, not even by the measure of a sesame seed. O You who possess everything, how then could I know Your nature? I speak as if I am one who knows, for I have been given the enduring name of 'child'. O Lord of the unique Hall of Wisdom, which is your very nature! O Truth! O Eternal One! O Treasure of Compassion! The world delights more in the prattle of a fledgling parrot than in the later, well-formed speech of a human child.
commentary: True spiritual seeking is rooted in humility, not in intellectual certainty.
