Vallalar knows nothing of himself or of the world, so he cannot claim to know God, yet he speaks as one who knows, because he has been given the name of 'child'. Just as the world delights more in the prattle of a young parrot than in a human child's speech, his words, spoken without true knowledge, are still received with delight.
NOTES
Note 354

tamil: மொழித்திறனும் - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு., ச. மு. க.
translit: moḻittiṟaṉum - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu., ca. mu. ka.
translation: moḻittiṟaṉum — reading of the first edition, Po. Su., S. Mu. Ka.

translit: matimaṇṭa lattamutam vāyāra uṇṭē patimaṇṭa lattaracu paṇṇa - nitiya navanēya mākkum naṭarāja ṉēyeñ civaṉē katavait tiṟa.
translation: O Nataraja, a treasure who establishes the nine kinds of devotion! Our Siva, open the door, so I may drink my fill of the nectar from the moon's sphere and rule the kingdom of the Lord's domain.
commentary: The devotee begs for entry into a higher state of consciousness, which is experienced as a blissful nectar. In yogic traditions, the "nectar from the moon's sphere" is an image for the ambrosia of immortality that flows from the crown of the head in deep meditation. "Opening the door" is a powerful metaphor for God granting access to this deep inner experience.

translit: intār aruḷamutam yāṉaruntal vēṇṭumiṅkē nantā maṇiviḷakkē ñāṉacapai - entāyē kōvē eṉatu kuruvē eṉaiyāṇṭa tēvē katavait tiṟa.
translation: O unceasing gem-lamp! My Father in the Hall of Wisdom! My King, my Guru, O God who has taken me as your own! Open the door, for I must drink this flower-sweet nectar of grace right here.
commentary: The desire for grace is urgent and personal, addressed to God in many intimate roles: Father, Teacher, and King. By addressing the "unceasing gem-lamp" in the Gnana Sabai (Hall of Wisdom), Vallalar shows his deep and loving connection to the divine. His plea to drink the nectar "right here" emphasizes the possibility of realization in this very life, more than in a future one.

translit: cākā aruḷamutam tāṉarunti nāṉkaḷikka nākā tiparcūḻ naṭarājā - ēkā pavaṉē paraṉē parāparaṉē eṅkaḷ civaṉē katavait tiṟa.
translation: O Nataraja, surrounded by serpent kings! O unique one, O source of being, O supreme one, O transcendent one! Our Siva, open the door, so I may drink the deathless nectar of grace and rejoice.
commentary: The ultimate spiritual goal is to attain a deathless state through God's grace. This verse explicitly names what the devotee seeks: the "deathless nectar." For Vallalar, this is not a metaphor for joy; it refers to a literal, physical transformation into an immortal being. The poem frames this supreme attainment as a gift received by pleading at God's door.

translit: aruḷōṅku taṇṇamutam aṉpāl arunti maruḷnīṅki nāṉkaḷittu vāḻap - poruḷān tavanēyar pōṟṟum tayānitiyē eṅkaḷ civaṉē katavait tiṟa.
translation: O treasure of compassion, you who are the true substance, praised by loving ascetics! Our Siva, open the door, so I may drink the cool nectar of abundant grace with love, be free from delusion, and live in joy.
commentary: The focus shifts to God's nature as compassion itself. The nectar of grace is described as cool and refreshing, something to be drunk with love. It changes a person: it removes delusion, the fundamental confusion about reality that causes suffering, and allows one to live in a state of sustained happiness.

translit: vāṉōrk kariteṉavē māmaṟaikaḷ cāṟṟukiṉṟa ñāṉō tayaamutam nāṉarunta - āṉāt tiṟappā valarpōṟṟum ciṟṟam palavā ciṟappā katavait tiṟa.
translation: O one of Chitrambalam, praised by poets of tireless skill! Graciously open the door, so that I may drink the nectar of wisdom's dawn, which the great Vedas proclaim is rare even for the gods.
commentary: This verse emphasizes how precious and rare the experience of grace is, calling it the "nectar of wisdom's dawn." This divine connection is not easily won; even the gods in heaven struggle to attain it, as the ancient scriptures (Vedas) testify. God is located in Chitrambalam, the "Little Hall," a name for the sacred center of consciousness.

translit: ellāmum vallacitteṉ ṟellā maṟaikaḷuñcol nallār amutamatu nāṉarunta - nallārkku nalvāḻ vaḷikkum naṭarāyā maṉṟōṅku celvā katavait tiṟa.
translation: Open the door, O King of Dance who gives a good life to the virtuous, O Treasure flourishing in the Hall, so I may drink the good nectar that all scriptures declare is the all-powerful Siddhi.
commentary: The divine nectar is now revealed to be the ultimate goal of all spiritual paths: Siddhi, or perfected power and attainment. This is not merely a feeling of bliss: it is the all-powerful Siddhi itself, the grace that can do all things, and the realization of the soul's highest potential. The direct experience of grace is the source of all spiritual accomplishments mentioned in the scriptures.

translit: ēḻnilaikkum mēṟpāl irukkiṉṟa taṇṇamutam vāḻnilaikka nāṉuṇṭu māṇpuṟavē - kēḻnilaikka āvāeṉ ṟeṉṉaiuvan tāṇṭatiru ampalamā tēvā katavait tiṟa.
translation: O great Deva of the sacred Hall, you joyfully accepted and ruled me, expressing delight to establish my unique status. Open the door, so I may drink the cool nectar from beyond the seven realms, that I may live forever and be glorified.
commentary: The plea becomes deeply personal, recalling a moment when God joyfully claimed the speaker as his own. The nectar he seeks is a transcendent substance from a reality "beyond the seven realms," meaning it is beyond all ordinary cosmic planes of existence. The goal is now explicitly stated as eternal life, a state of immortal glory made possible only by this divine grace.

translit: īṉa ulakat tiṭarnīṅki iṉpuṟavē ñāṉa amutamatu nāṉarunta - ñāṉa uruvē uṇarvē oḷiyē veḷiyē tiruvē katavait tiṟa.
translation: O Form of Gnosis, O Consciousness, O Light, O Space, O Sacredness! Open the door, so that I may drink the nectar of Gnosis, be freed from the afflictions of this lowly world, and experience bliss.
commentary: The nectar that ends suffering is identified here as Gnosis, or true spiritual knowledge. Vallalar addresses God as the fundamental principles of reality: Consciousness, Light, and even the pure Space in which everything exists. To drink this nectar is to merge with this ultimate reality and find bliss.

translit: tiraiyō tacattē tikaḻkiṉṟa eṉṟē varaiyōtu taṇṇamutam vāyppa - uraiōtu vāṉēem māṉēpem māṉē maṇimaṉṟil tēṉē katavait tiṟa.
translation: O great One extolled in scripture! My Master! My Lord! O Honey in the Gem-Hall! Open the door, so I may obtain the cool nectar which, as the sacred texts define, shines on Trayodashi.
commentary: Trayodasam here is the thirteenth station of the inner ascent, beyond the twelfth (dvādaśāntam) above the crown of the head. The cool nectar that shines there, as the sacred texts declare, is what Vallalar asks to drink when the Lord opens the door.

translit: cōtimalai mēlvīṭṭil tūya tiruvamutam mētiṉimēl nāṉuṇṇa vēṇṭiṉēṉ - ōtariya ēkā aṉēkā eḻiṟpotuvil vāḻñāṉa tēkā katavait tiṟa.
translation: O indescribable One and Many! O Embodiment of Gnosis who lives in the beautiful Common Space! I have prayed to consume, while still on this earth, the pure sacred nectar from the house atop the Mountain of Jothi. Open the door.
commentary: The prayer here is for the highest spiritual realization, symbolized by the nectar from the "Mountain of Jothi" (divine light), to be experienced fully while living on earth. This is a central theme for Vallalar: spiritual liberation is a transformation within the world.

sections.title: The Blessing of the Imperishable Form of Grace

tamil: சிவங்க னிந்தசிற் றம்பலத் தருள்நடம் செய்கின்ற பெருவாழ்வே
நவங்க னிந்தமேல் நிலைநடு விளங்கிய நண்பனே அடியேன்றன்
தவங்க னிந்ததோர் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி தரித்தருள் புரிந்தாயே
பவங்க னிந்தஇவ் வடிவமே அழிவுறாப் பதிவடி வாமாறே.
translit: civaṅka ṉintaciṟ ṟampalat taruḷnaṭam ceykiṉṟa peruvāḻvē navaṅka ṉintamēl nilainaṭu viḷaṅkiya naṇpaṉē aṭiyēṉṟaṉ tavaṅka ṉintatōr viṇṇappam tiruccevi tarittaruḷ purintāyē pavaṅka ṉinta:iv vaṭivamē aḻivuṟāp pativaṭi vāmāṟē.
translation: O Great Life performing the dance of grace in the Cirrambalam where Sivam has ripened! O Friend shining in the center of the supreme, ripened state! You have taken into Your sacred ear the prayer of this servant, ripened by penance, and granted it, so that this very body, ripened through worldly birth, becomes the imperishable divine form.
commentary: The decad opens with a declaration: God has already heard Vallalar's prayer and granted that this very body, ripened through worldly birth, becomes the imperishable divine form. He sees worldly life as a ripening that prepared the body for this transfiguration, given from the dancing presence of God in the Cirrambalam.

tamil: விளங்கு கின்றசிற் றம்பலத் தருள்நடம் விளைக்கின்ற பெருவாழ்வே
களங்க மில்லதோர் உளநடு விளங்கிய கருத்தனே அடியேன்நான்
விளம்பி நின்றதோர் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி வியந்தருள் புரிந்தாயே
உளங்கொள் இவ்வடி விம்மையே மந்திர ஒளிவடி வாமாறே.
translit: viḷaṅku kiṉṟaciṟ ṟampalat taruḷnaṭam viḷaikkiṉṟa peruvāḻvē kaḷaṅka millatōr uḷanaṭu viḷaṅkiya karuttaṉē aṭiyēṉnāṉ viḷampi niṉṟatōr viṇṇappam tiruccevi viyantaruḷ purintāyē uḷaṅkoḷ ivvaṭi vimmaiyē mantira oḷivaṭi vāmāṟē.
translation: O Great Life creating the dance of grace in the radiant Cirrambalam! O Master shining in the center of a flawless mind! You have marveled at the prayer I, Your humble servant, declared, and granted it, so that this cherished body, in this very birth, becomes a form of mantra-light.
commentary: The goal of bodily transformation is defined here as becoming a "form of mantra-light." This suggests a body that is no longer made of gross matter but of pure, conscious vibration, like the sacred sound of a mantra. This transformation is to happen "in this very birth," reinforcing the urgency of his plea.

tamil: விஞ்சு கின்றசிற் றம்பலத் தருள்நடம் விளைக்கின்ற பெருவாழ்வே
எஞ்சல் அற்றமா மறைமுடி விளங்கிய என்னுயிர்த் துணையேநான்
அஞ்சல் இன்றியே செய்தவிண் ணப்பம்ஏற் றகங்களித் தளித்தாயே
துஞ்சும் இவ்வுடல் அழிவுறா தோங்குமெய்ச் சுகவடி வாமாறே.
translit: viñcu kiṉṟaciṟ ṟampalat taruḷnaṭam viḷaikkiṉṟa peruvāḻvē eñcal aṟṟamā maṟaimuṭi viḷaṅkiya eṉṉuyirt tuṇaiyēnāṉ añcal iṉṟiyē ceytaviṇ ṇappamēṟ ṟakaṅkaḷit taḷittāyē tuñcum ivvuṭal aḻivuṟā tōṅkumeyc cukavaṭi vāmāṟē.
translation: O Great Life creating the dance of grace in the transcendent Cirrambalam! O my life's Companion shining at the crown of the great, flawless Vedas! You have accepted the prayer I made without fear, rejoiced in Your heart, and granted it, so that this body that would die becomes an exalted, true form of bliss that never perishes.
commentary: Here, the immortal body is described as a "true form of bliss." This builds on the previous verses: the transformed state is eternal or luminous and is an existence of pure, unceasing joy. Vallalar addresses God as his "life's Companion," showing the intimate, personal nature of his relationship with the divine.

tamil: ஓங்கு கின்றசிற் றம்பலத் தருள்நடம் ஒளிர்கின்ற பெருவாழ்வே
தேங்கு லாவிய தெள்ளமு தேபெருஞ் செல்வமே சிவமேநின்
பாங்க னேன்மொழி விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி பதித்தருள் புரிந்தாயே
ஈங்கு வீழுடல் என்றும்வீ ழாதொளிர் இயல்வடி வாமாறே.
translit: ōṅku kiṉṟaciṟ ṟampalat taruḷnaṭam oḷirkiṉṟa peruvāḻvē tēṅku lāviya teḷḷamu tēperuñ celvamē civamēniṉ pāṅka ṉēṉmoḻi viṇṇappam tiruccevi patittaruḷ purintāyē īṅku vīḻuṭal eṉṟumvī ḻātoḷir iyalvaṭi vāmāṟē.
translation: O Great Life, radiant with the dance of grace in the exalted Cirrambalam! O clear ambrosia brimming with sweetness! O great wealth! O Sivam! You have set in Your sacred ear the prayer spoken by me, Your companion, and granted it, so that this body, destined to fall here, becomes a radiant, essential form that never falls.
commentary: This verse starkly contrasts the body's natural fate, to "fall here" in death, with its divine potential to become a form "that never falls." By calling God "Sivam" (the auspicious reality), "clear ambrosia," and "great wealth," Vallalar expresses the divine fullness that can accomplish this ultimate change.

tamil: இலங்கு கின்றசிற் றம்பலத் தருள்நடம் இடுகின்ற பெருவாழ்வே
துலங்கு பேரருட் சோதியே சோதியுள் துலங்கிய பொருளேஎன்
புலங்கொள் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவிக் கேற்றருள் புரிந்தனை இஞ்ஞான்றே
அலங்கும் இவ்வுடல் எற்றையும் அழிவுறா அருள்வடி வாமாறே.
translit: ilaṅku kiṉṟaciṟ ṟampalat taruḷnaṭam iṭukiṉṟa peruvāḻvē tulaṅku pēraruṭ cōtiyē cōtiyuḷ tulaṅkiya poruḷēeṉ pulaṅkoḷ viṇṇappam tiruccevik kēṟṟaruḷ purintaṉai iññāṉṟē alaṅkum ivvuṭal eṟṟaiyum aḻivuṟā aruḷvaṭi vāmāṟē.
translation: O Great Life performing the dance of grace in the luminous Cirrambalam! O Jothi of brilliant, great grace! O Reality shining within that Jothi! You have graciously accepted my prayer, born of my senses, into your sacred ear this very day, so that this trembling body becomes a form of grace that is never, ever destroyed.
commentary: As in every verse of this decad, Vallalar declares with confidence that God, the 'Jothi' (light) of grace, has accepted his prayer 'this very day.' His 'trembling body,' frail and mortal, is now assured to become a 'form of grace' (aruḷvaṭivam), a body made of the divine substance that can never be destroyed.

tamil: சிறந்த பேரொளித் திருச்சிற்றம் பலத்திலே திகழ்கின்ற பெருவாழ்வே
துறந்த பேருளத் தருட்பெருஞ் சோதியே சுகப்பெரு நிலையேநான்
மறந்தி டாதுசெய் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி மடுத்தருள் புரிந்தாயே
பிறந்த இவ்வுடல் என்றும்இங் கழிவுறாப் பெருமைபெற் றிடுமாறே.
translit: ciṟanta pēroḷit tirucciṟṟam palattilē tikaḻkiṉṟa peruvāḻvē tuṟanta pēruḷat taruṭperuñ cōtiyē cukapperu nilaiyēnāṉ maṟanti ṭātucey viṇṇappam tiruccevi maṭuttaruḷ purintāyē piṟanta ivvuṭal eṉṟumiṅ kaḻivuṟāp perumaipeṟ ṟiṭumāṟē.
translation: O Great Life, shining in the Thiru Chitrambalam of excellent, great light! O ArutPerunJothi in the great hearts of the renunciate! O State of great bliss! You have listened with Your sacred ear to the plea I made without forgetting, and granted it, so that this body I was born with attains the greatness of never perishing here.
commentary: The divine, called ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light), shines in the Thiru Chitrambalam and in the great hearts of those who have renounced. Vallalar declares that this Grace-Light has heard the plea he never ceased to make, and has granted that the body he was born with receives the greatness of never perishing here.

tamil: வயங்கு கின்றசிற் றம்பலந் தன்னிலே வளர்கின்ற பெருவாழ்வே
மயங்கு றாதமெய் அறிவிலே விளங்கிய மாமணி விளக்கேஇங்
கியங்கு சிற்றடி யேன்மொழி விண்ணப்பம் ஏற்றருள் புரிந்தாயே
தயங்கும் இவ்வுடல் எற்றையும் அழிவுறாத் தனிவடி வாமாறே.
translit: vayaṅku kiṉṟaciṟ ṟampalan taṉṉilē vaḷarkiṉṟa peruvāḻvē mayaṅku ṟātamey aṟivilē viḷaṅkiya māmaṇi viḷakkēiṅ kiyaṅku ciṟṟaṭi yēṉmoḻi viṇṇappam ēṟṟaruḷ purintāyē tayaṅkum ivvuṭal eṟṟaiyum aḻivuṟāt taṉivaṭi vāmāṟē.
translation: O Great Life, growing in the resplendent Chitrambalam! O great jeweled lamp shining in true, unconfused knowledge! You have accepted the spoken plea of this humble servant who moves about here, and granted it, so that this faltering body becomes a unique form that never perishes.
commentary: A clear and steady mind is the vessel for this divine transformation. God is seen as a lamp of "true, unconfused knowledge," a powerful contrast to the "faltering body" and the ordinary human state of confusion. By connecting to this divine clarity, the unstable physical form can be remade into something unique and eternal.

tamil: தீட்டு கின்றசிற் றம்பலந் தன்னிலே திகழ்கின்ற பெருவாழ்வே
காட்டு கின்றதோர் கதிர்நடு விளங்கிய கடவுளே அடியேன்நான்
நீட்டி நின்றதோர் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி நிறைத்தருள் புரிந்தாயே
பூட்டும் இவ்வுடல் எற்றையும் அழிவுறாப் பொன்வடி வாமாறே.
translit: tīṭṭu kiṉṟaciṟ ṟampalan taṉṉilē tikaḻkiṉṟa peruvāḻvē kāṭṭu kiṉṟatōr katirnaṭu viḷaṅkiya kaṭavuḷē aṭiyēṉnāṉ nīṭṭi niṉṟatōr viṇṇappam tiruccevi niṟaittaruḷ purintāyē pūṭṭum ivvuṭal eṟṟaiyum aḻivuṟāp poṉvaṭi vāmāṟē.
translation: O Great Life, shining in the radiant Chitrambalam! O God who shines in the center of a revealing ray of light! You have filled Your sacred ear with the long plea I, Your servant, made, and granted it, so that this bound-together body becomes a golden form that never perishes.
commentary: The body is described as "assembled," suggesting it is a temporary construction of parts. The prayer is to remake this form into a permanent "golden form," a classic symbol of incorruptible purity and value. This great change is a gift of grace from the divine light that shines within the Chitrambalam, the sacred inner space.

tamil: தடையி லாதசிற் றம்பலந் தன்னிலே தழைக்கின்ற பெருவாழ்வே
கடையி லாப்பெருங் கதிர்நடு விளங்கும்ஓர் கடவுளே அடியேன்நான்
இடைவு றாதுசெய் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவிக் கேற்றருள் புரிந்தாயே
புடையின் இவ்வுடல் எற்றையும் அழிவுறாப் பொன்வடி வாமாறே.
translit: taṭaiyi lātaciṟ ṟampalan taṉṉilē taḻaikkiṉṟa peruvāḻvē kaṭaiyi lāpperuṅ katirnaṭu viḷaṅkumōr kaṭavuḷē aṭiyēṉnāṉ iṭaivu ṟātucey viṇṇappam tiruccevik kēṟṟaruḷ purintāyē puṭaiyiṉ ivvuṭal eṟṟaiyum aḻivuṟāp poṉvaṭi vāmāṟē.
translation: O Great Life, flourishing in the unobstructed Chitrambalam! O God who shines in the center of a boundless, great ray of light! You have received into Your sacred ear the plea I, Your servant, made without pause, and granted it, so that this enclosing body becomes a golden form that never perishes.
commentary: Repetition here conveys a steady, single-pointed focus. The devotee makes his plea "without pause," seeking only one thing: the transfiguration of his body into a deathless golden form. The description of Chitrambalam as "unobstructed" points to a state of pure, open consciousness where such a miracle becomes possible.

tamil: கையின் நெல்லிபோல் விளங்குசிற் றம்பலங் கலந்தருள் பெருவாழ்வே
மெய்யி லேவிளைந் தோங்கிய போகமே மெய்ப்பெரும் பொருளேநான்
ஐய மற்றுரைத் திட்டவிண் ணப்பம்ஏற் றளித்தனை இஞ்ஞான்றே
செய்யும் இவ்வுடல் என்றுமிங் கழிவுறாச் சிவவடி வாமாறே.
translit: kaiyiṉ nellipōl viḷaṅkuciṟ ṟampalaṅ kalantaruḷ peruvāḻvē meyyi lēviḷain tōṅkiya pōkamē meypperum poruḷēnāṉ aiya maṟṟurait tiṭṭaviṇ ṇappamēṟ ṟaḷittaṉai iññāṉṟē ceyyum ivvuṭal eṉṟumiṅ kaḻivuṟāc civavaṭi vāmāṟē.
translation: O Great Life, graciously mingled with the Chitrambalam, which is as clear as a gooseberry on the palm! O Bliss that has manifested and grown in truth! O Great True Substance! This very day, you have accepted and granted the plea I stated without a doubt, so that this active body may become a Siva-form that never perishes here.
commentary: The decad closes as it began, in certainty. The experience of God is now 'as clear as a gooseberry on the palm,' a traditional image for something perfectly and directly known. Vallalar declares that this very day his prayer has been accepted and granted, and that his physical body is remade into an immortal Siva-form, a body infused with divine nature itself.

sections.title: Marveling at the Truth of Great Grace

translit: naṉṟē taruntiru nāṭakam nāṭoṟum ñāṉamaṇi maṉṟē viḷaṅkap purikiṉṟa āṉanta vārkaḻalōy iṉṟē aruṭperuñ cōtitan tāṇṭaruḷ eytukaṇam oṉṟē eṉiṉum poṟēṉaru ḷāṇai uraittaṉaṉē.
translation: O You with long anklets of bliss, who performs the sacred drama that grants only good, making the jeweled hall of wisdom shine daily! Today, grant the Vast Grace-Light and rule me; let grace arrive. I cannot endure even a single moment of delay. I have declared this by the command of grace.
commentary: Spiritual longing here reaches a pitch of absolute urgency. The devotee feels he cannot wait even a single moment longer for the experience of the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light). It is a declaration of readiness, spoken with the authority of grace itself. He sees the world as God's "sacred drama" and feels it is time for the final act of union to begin.

translit: taṟcōti eṉṉuyirc cattiya cōti taṉittalaimaic ciṟcōti maṉṟoḷir tīpaka cōtieṉ cittattuḷḷē naṟcōti ñāṉanal nāṭaka cōti nalampurinta poṟcōti āṉanta pūraṇa cōtiem puṇṇiyaṉē.
translation: The light of the Self, the light of truth that is my very soul, the supreme, solitary light of consciousness, the lamp-light that illuminates the sacred hall, the good light within my consciousness, the light of the good drama of wisdom, the golden light that has bestowed goodness, the perfect, complete light of bliss, You are our holy virtue.
commentary: God is praised as a magnificent cascade of light. This light, or jōti, is experienced as the light of the Self, the truth of the soul, and the very fabric of consciousness. The verse identifies the divine with every form of benevolent and illuminating energy, from the light that fills the cosmos to the light that shines within the devotee's own heart.

translit: tiraikaṇṭa māyaik kaṭalkaṭan tēṉaruṭ cīrviḷaṅkum karaikaṇ ṭaṭaintaṉaṉ akkarai mēlcark karaikalanta uraikaṇṭa teḷḷamu tuṇṭēṉ aruḷoḷi ōṅkukiṉṟa varaikaṇṭa taṉmicai uṟṟēṉ ulakam matittiṭavē.
translation: I have crossed the ocean of illusion, which is full of waves. I have seen and reached the shore where the glory of grace shines. On that shore, I drank the clear ambrosia mixed with fine sugar. I have ascended the mountain where the light of grace rises high, for the world to witness and esteem.
commentary: Spiritual liberation is depicted here as a crossing from a turbulent ocean to a peaceful shore. The "ocean of illusion" represents the confusing world of ordinary life, while the "shore of grace" is the state of spiritual clarity and safety. Having arrived, the speaker partakes of "ambrosia," the sweetness of divine experience, and ascends a "mountain of light," signifying a stable, elevated state of consciousness that serves as a beacon for others.

translit: maṉakkēta māṟṟivem māyaiyai nīkki malintaviṉai taṉakkē viṭaikoṭut tāṇavam tīrttaruḷ taṇṇamutam eṉakkē mikavum aḷittaruṭ cōtiyum īntaḻiyā iṉakkēṇmai yuntanteṉ uṭkalan tāṉmaṉṟil eṉṉappaṉē.
translation: My Father in the sacred hall removed my mental anguish, dispelled cruel illusion, dismissed my abundant karma, and destroyed the ego. He generously granted me the cool ambrosia of grace, bestowed the grace-light, and gave me undying, kindred fellowship, mingling deep within me.
commentary: This verse describes spiritual transformation as a direct act of God's grace. The divine is shown actively clearing away the primary obstacles to enlightenment: mental suffering, worldly illusion (māyā), the weight of past actions (karma), and the prideful ego (āṇavam). In their place, God grants illumination and an intimate, unbreakable relationship, mingling directly with the soul.

translit: vātitta māyai viṉaiyā ṇavameṉum vaṉmalattaic cētitteṉ uḷḷam tirukkōyi lākkoṇṭu cittielām pōtit tuṭampaiyum poṉṉuṭam pākkinaṟ puttamutum cātit taruḷiya niṉṉaruṭ kiyāṉceyat takkateṉṉē.
translation: You cut away the powerful impurities known as tormenting illusion, karma, and ego. You took my heart as a holy temple, taught me all siddhis, transformed my body into a golden one, and graciously manifested the good, new ambrosia. For this grace of Yours, what can I do in return?
commentary: Overwhelmed by the scale of divine grace, the speaker asks what could possibly be offered in return. The transformation is absolute: God has removed the core impurities of illusion, karma, and ego, and has made the speaker's own heart a temple. Grace has also granted spiritual powers (siddhis) and transformed the physical body into a perfect, incorruptible "golden" form, signifying a state of complete spiritual and physical perfection.

translit: cettār eḻukeṉac cintaicey muṉṉañ ciritteḻavē ittā raṇiyil aruṭperuñ cōti eṉakkaḷittāy ettālum eṉṟum aḻiyā vaṭivutan teṉṉuḷniṉṉai vaittāy maṇimaṉṟa vāṇaniṉ pēraruḷ vāymaiyeṉṉē.
translation: Even before I could think, "Let the dead arise," you made them rise up smiling. So that the dead rise up smiling even before I can think, 'Let the dead arise,' You gave me the ArutPerunJothi on this earth. You gave me a form that never perishes by any means and placed Yourself within me. O Life of the Jeweled Hall! What truth your great grace is!
commentary: Grace is presented here as a power that transcends all limitations, including death. The ability to raise the dead happens with effortless spontaneity, a sign of the absolute nature of divine power. This supreme grace, the ArutPerunJothi, has bestowed an immortal body and placed God permanently within the speaker's own being, revealing the ultimate truth and power of divine compassion.

translit: ākkaloṉ ṟōtoḻil aintaiyum tantinta aṇṭapiṇṭa vīkkamel lāmceṉṟuṉ iccaiyiṉ vaṇṇam viḷaṅkukanī ēkkamu ṟēleṉ ṟuraittaruṭ cōtiyum īnteṉakkē ūkkame lāmuṟa uṭkalan tāṉeṉ uṭaiyavaṉē.
translation: "I give you creation and all five cosmic functions. Manifest according to your will, going beyond all the expansions of the cosmos and the body. Do not yearn," you said, and gave me the Grace Jothi. My Master has mingled deep within me, filling me with all strength.
commentary: The highest state of union with God involves being granted a share in God’s own cosmic powers. The 'five functions' of creating, sustaining, destroying, concealing, and revealing are traditionally God's alone. Here, God bestows them upon Vallalar, empowering him to act with a divine will. The words 'Do not yearn' are a reassurance: he need no longer pine or be anxious, for he is told to shine according to his own will, a will now one with God's through the inner mingling with the Grace Jothi.

translit: eṉṉēeṉ mītem perumāṉ karuṇai iruntavaṇṇam taṉṉē rilāta aruṭperuñ cōtiyait tantulakuk kaṉṉē eṉaviḷai yāṭuka eṉṟaḻi yātaceḻum poṉṉēr vaṭivum aḷitteṉ ṉuyiril puṇarntaṉaṉē.
translation: What can I say of the way my Lord's compassion was upon me! He gave me the incomparable ArutPerunJothi, told me, "Play in this world like a mother," granted me a splendid, imperishable golden form, and united with my very soul.
commentary: The purpose of receiving an imperishable golden body and the power of ArutPerunJothi is compassionate service. God’s instruction is simple and deep: "Play in this world like a mother." This reframes the goal of spiritual attainment, directing it outward as a mission of nurturing, unconditional love for all beings.

translit: accō eṉeṉṟu pukalvēṉeṉ āṇṭavaṉ ampalattāṉ eccō taṉaiyum iyaṟṟāteṉ ṉuṭkalan tiṉṉaruḷām meyccōti īnteṉai mēṉilaik kēṟṟi viraintuṭampai iccōti ākkiaḻiyā nalantanta viccaiyaiyē.
translation: Oh! What can I say of the marvel performed by my Ruler, the Lord of the Sacred Hall! Without subjecting me to any test, he mingled within me, gave me the True Jothi of his sweet grace, elevated me to the highest state, and swiftly transformed my body into this very Jothi, granting me imperishable well-being.
commentary: The gift of grace is entirely unconditional and does not depend on passing spiritual tests. Many traditions describe a path of difficult trials, but Vallalar emphasizes that God simply entered him freely, without any prior test of his worthiness. This pure act of grace elevated him, transforming his very body into the True Jothi, or light of God, and granting him a state of eternal well-being.

translit: vāḻieṉ āṇṭavaṉ vāḻieṅ kōṉaruḷ vāymaieṉṟum vāḻiem māṉpukaḻ vāḻieṉ nātaṉ malarppataṅkaḷ vāḻimeyc cuttacaṉ mārkkap peruneṟi māṇpukoṇṭu vāḻiiv vaiyamum vāṉamum maṟṟavum vāḻiyavē.
translation: Long live my Ruler! Long live the eternal truth of my King’s grace! Long live the glory of our great one! Long live my Lord’s flower-like feet! Long live the great path of the true Suddha Sanmarkkam, with all its majesty! Long live this world, the heavens, and all else! May they flourish!
commentary: This final verse of the poem is a great blessing that flows out from personal gratitude to encompass all of existence. Having received the ultimate grace, Vallalar’s response is to wish for the eternal flourishing of God, of grace itself, and of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Universal True Path he taught). His blessing then extends to this world, the heavens, and everything else, showing how true realization results in a universal, all-embracing love.

sections.title: The Blessing of the Golden Form

translit: aruṭperuñ cōti apayam apayam poruṭperuñ cōtip puṇaitan - tiruṭperuṅkār aḷḷaṟ kaṭalkaṭatti akkaraimēl āṉantam koḷḷaṟ kapayaṅ koṭu.
translation: O Vast Grace-Light, refuge, refuge! Give me the raft of the Vast Light of Reality to cross the great, dark sea of mire and grant me refuge to attain bliss on the other shore.
commentary: This verse is a cry for help, asking God to provide a way across the "sea of mire" that is worldly life. The Vast Grace-Light is the destination and the raft needed for the crossing. The plea for refuge, repeated twice, shows a deep sense of urgency and total reliance on God to escape suffering and reach the shore of bliss.

translit: āramutam tanteṉṉuḷ accamelām tīrttaruḷic cīramuta vaṇṇat tiruvaṭikaṇ - ṭārvamikap pāṭi uṭampuyirum pattivaṭi vākikkūt tāṭik kaḷikka aruḷ.
translation: Grant me the grace to receive rare ambrosia, dispelling all my fears; to see Your sacred feet, the color of sublime ambrosia, with great longing; and to sing, dance, and rejoice, my body and life becoming a form of devotion.
commentary: True devotion is an experience that consumes one's entire being. Vallalar asks for the grace to feel devotion in his heart and to have his very body and life become an expression of it. This state is reached by receiving divine ambrosia, which removes fear and allows him to see God's form, inspiring him to sing and dance in ecstatic joy.

translit: iṭartolainta ñāṉṟē iṉaivum tolainta cuṭarkalanta ñāṉṟē cukamum - muṭukiuṟṟa tiṉṉē kaḷittiṭutum eṉneñcē ampalavaṉ poṉṉēr patattaip pukaḻ.
translation: The moment affliction vanishes, sorrow vanishes too. The moment I merge with the Light, bliss swiftly comes. O my heart, today let us rejoice! Praise the golden feet of the Lord of the Ambalam.
commentary: The end of suffering and the beginning of joy happen in the very same moment. As soon as one merges with the divine Light, sorrow vanishes and bliss rushes in. The verse is an instruction to the heart to stop hesitating and praise the Lord of the Ambalam (sacred hall), because that praise is the key to this immediate and joyful transformation.

translit: īṉamelām tīrntaṉavē iṉpamelām eytiṉavē ūṉamelām kaiviṭ ṭoḻintaṉavē - ñāṉamuḷōr pōṟṟumciṟ ṟampalattum poṉṉampa lattunaṭam pōṟṟum paṭippeṟṟa pōtu.
translation: All baseness has vanished, all bliss has been attained, and all flaws have been abandoned and are gone, now that I have gained the ability to praise the dance in the Chitrambalam and the Ponnambalam, which the wise themselves praise.
commentary: The ability to perceive and praise God's divine dance is what purifies the soul. Vallalar describes this dance taking place in the Chitrambalam (hall of consciousness) and the Ponnambalam (golden hall), which are sacred spaces of perception both within and beyond the self. Once this vision is gained, all flaws and negativity are instantly removed, and only bliss remains.

translit: uḷḷak kavalaiyelām ōṭi oḻintaṉavē vaḷḷaṟ peruñcōti vāyttaṉavē - kaḷḷak karuttoḻiya ñāṉak karuttiyaintu nātaṉ poruttamuṟṟeṉ uḷḷamarnta pōtu.
translation: All worries of the heart have run away and vanished, and the generous Vast Light has been attained, now that deceitful thoughts have ceased, I have aligned with thoughts of wisdom, and the Lord has fittingly settled in my heart.
commentary: Peace of mind and the attainment of divine Light are the direct results of mental discipline. When the mind is purified of deceit and aligns with spiritual wisdom (jnanam), the heart becomes a fitting home for the Lord, and worry naturally disappears.

translit: ūṉa uṭampē oḷiuṭampāy ōṅkiniṟka ñāṉa amuteṉakku nalkiyatē - vāṉap poruṭperuñ cōtip potuvil viḷaṅkum aruṭperuñ cōti atu.
translation: The Supreme Grace-Light, the great flame of substance that shines in the universal celestial space, bestowed upon me the nectar of wisdom so that my physical body would become a body of light and stand exalted.
commentary: This verse expresses a core teaching: divine grace can physically transform the mortal body into a body of light. The "Supreme Grace-Light" bestows a "nectar of wisdom" that doesn't just enlighten the soul but literally transmutes the flawed, physical body into a perfected, luminous, and immortal form.

translit: ellām ceyavallāṉ entaiyaruḷ ampalavaṉ nallāṉ eṉakkumika naṉkaḷittāṉ - ellārum kaṇṭuviyak kiṉṟār karuṇait tiruvamutam uṇṭuviyak kiṉṟēṉ uvantu.
translation: My Father, the Lord of Ambalam who can do all things, the Good One, has given to me most generously. Everyone sees this and is amazed. I, joyfully consuming the sacred nectar of compassion, am amazed as well.
commentary: The experience of grace is so overwhelming that it astonishes both onlookers and the person receiving it. Grace is a tangible "sacred nectar of compassion" that can be joyfully consumed. The transformation it brings is so evident that it becomes a source of wonder for everyone.

translit: ēcā ulakavarkaḷ ellārum kaṇṭuniṟkat tēcār oḷiyāl ciṟiyēṉai - vācāma kōcarattiṉ ēṟṟik koṭuttāṉ aruḷamutam īcaṉattaṉ ampalava ṉē.
translation: While all the irreproachable people of the world watched, the Lord, my Father, the one of the Ambalam, elevated me, this lowly one, with a radiant light to the state beyond speech and mind and gave me the nectar of grace.
commentary: Divine grace elevates the humble to a state beyond human comprehension. Vallalar emphasizes his own lowliness to show that God's power is absolute and does not depend on worldly merit. He is lifted to a state known as vāsāma gōcaram, which is beyond the reach of both speech and the ordinary mind, a state of pure, direct experience.

translit: aiyaṉeṉak kīnta aticayattai eṉpukalvēṉ poyyaṭiyēṉ kuṟṟam poṟuttaruḷi - vaiyat taḻiyāmal ōṅkum aruḷvaṭivam nāṉōr moḻiāṭu taṟku muṉam.
translation: What can I say of the wonder my Lord gave me? Before I could even utter a word, he forgave the faults of this false devotee and granted me a form of grace that stands exalted in this world, never perishing.
commentary: Divine grace and forgiveness can be so immediate that they arrive even before one can ask for them. Vallalar feels his devotion is "false" and full of faults, yet this is no barrier. The gift he receives is a feeling and a tangible, imperishable "form of grace," a divinized body that exists in this world without being subject to decay.

translit: oppuyarvoṉ ṟillā oruvaṉ aruṭcōti appaṉelām vallatiru ampalattāṉ - ippuviyil vantāṉ iravi varutaṟku muṉkaruṇai tantāṉeṉ ṉuṭkalantāṉ tāṉ.
translation: The one peerless Light of Grace, who has no equal or superior, my Father, the all-powerful one of the sacred Ambalam, came to this earth. Before the sun arrived, he gave his compassion and he himself mingled within me.
commentary: God is a personal presence who comes to this world to be with the devotee. The description of this happening "before the sun arrived" suggests an inner dawning of light that precedes the physical day. The greatest act of grace is God's own self, which "mingled within" and became one with the soul.

translit: ōta ulavā orutōḻaṉ toṇṭaruḷaṉ cātal oḻitteṉṉait tāṉākkip - pūtalattil aintoḻilcey eṉṟē aruṭcōtik kōlaḷittāṉ ventoḻilpōy nīṅka viraintu.
translation: The one companion, inexhaustible through praise, who dwells within his devotees, abolished death for me and made me Himself. Saying, “Perform the five divine functions on this earth,” Saying, 'Perform the five divine functions on this earth,' He swiftly gave me the sceptre of the Grace-Light, causing my harsh deeds to depart.
commentary: Union with the divine prepares the devotee for a new mission in the world. Having been made one with God and freed from death, the devotee is now commissioned to carry out the "five divine functions," the cosmic work of creation, preservation, and dissolution. He becomes a direct agent for God's power on earth, enabled by a body of "Grace-Light" and freed from all past karma.

translit: auviyantīr uḷḷat taṟiñarelām kaṇṭuvakkac cevviyacaṉ mārkkam ciṟantōṅka - ovvi viraintuvanteṉ uṭkalantu meyyēmey yāka nirantoṉṟāyniṉṟāṉ nilattu.
translation: So that all the wise ones with envy-free hearts may see and rejoice, and for the perfect Sanmarkkam to flourish, He consented, came swiftly, and merged within me. With truth itself as the ultimate reality, He stood on this earth, pervading all as one.
commentary: This divine union is not a private experience for one person's benefit. Its purpose is to establish the Sanmarkkam, the true path of universal compassion and oneness, so that all pure-hearted people can witness it and find their own way to God.

translit: cōtip piḻampē cukavaṭivē meyññāṉa nītip potuvē niṟainitiyē - cōtik kaṭavuḷē māyaiiru kaṉmamiruḷ ellām viṭavuḷē niṉṟu viḷaṅku.
translation: O flame of Jothi! O form of bliss! O universal principle of true wisdom! O perfect treasure! O God of Jothi! Stand within me and shine, dispelling māyā, the two karmas, and all darkness.
commentary: This is a direct appeal for the divine Jothi (light) to purify the soul from within. The prayer is for this inner light to completely burn away the core obstacles to freedom: māyā (the illusion of separateness), and the two karmas (the binding results of past good and bad actions).

translit: tuṉpamelām tīrnta cukamellām kaitanta aṉparelām pōṟṟa aruḷnaṭañcey - iṉpaṉ aruṭperuñciṟ cōtitiru ampalattāṉ vētap poruṭperuñcit teṉṉuṭ pukuntu.
translation: The blissful one, the vast grace-light of consciousness of the sacred hall, who performs the dance of grace praised by all devotees, the great consciousness that is the meaning of the Vedas, entered within me. All my suffering has ended; all bliss is delivered into my hands.
commentary: The divine is portrayed as a blissful, dancing consciousness that fills the sacred hall of one's own awareness. Vallalar states that when this ultimate reality, the source of all sacred texts, enters a person, the result is immediate and total: suffering ends, and perfect bliss begins.

translit: tūkkam keṭuttuc cukaṅkoṭuttāṉ eṉtaṉakkē ākkameṉa ōṅkumpoṉ ampalattāṉ - ēkkamelām nīṅkiṉēṉ eṇṇam nirampiṉēṉ poṉvaṭivam tāṅkiṉēṉ cattiyamāt tāṉ.
translation: He of the golden hall, who flourishes as my very own prosperity, destroyed my sleep and gave me bliss. I am freed from all longing. My intent is fulfilled. I have taken on a golden form. This is the truth.
commentary: Union with the divine brings a final, total transformation. "Destroying sleep" means awakening from the dream of ordinary, ignorant consciousness into a state of permanent bliss. With all longing gone and his purpose fulfilled, he has achieved a perfected, immortal "golden form," a state he insists is a literal truth.

translit: tuṉpam keṭuttuc cukaṅkoṭuttāṉ eṉtaṉakkē aṉpakattil vāḻumciṟ ṟampalattāṉ - iṉpuruvam tāṅkiṉēṉ cākāt taṉivaṭivam peṟṟoḷiyāl ōṅkiṉēṉ uṇmai urai.
translation: The one of Chitrambalam who lives in the loving heart destroyed my suffering and gave me bliss. I have taken on a form of bliss, received a unique and deathless body, and risen high through light. I speak the truth.
commentary: The key to receiving this bliss is a loving heart, which becomes the Chitrambalam (the inner hall of consciousness) where God resides. This loving connection with the divine leads to the ultimate attainment: a blissful, immortal body that transcends death and shines with pure light.
NOTES
Note 330

tamil: நிறைந்தொன்றாய் - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு., ச. மு. க.நிரைந்தொன்றாய் - பி. இரா. ' நிரந்தொன்றாய் ' என்பது அடிகள் எழுத்து.
translit: niṟaintoṉṟāy - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu., ca. mu. ka. niraintoṉṟāy - pi. irā. ' nirantoṉṟāy ' eṉpatu aṭikaḷ eḻuttu.
translation: niṟaintoṉṟāy — reading of the first edition, Po. Su., S. Mu. Ka. niraintoṉṟāy — P. Irā. 'nirantoṉṟāy' is the form written in the Swami's own hand.

translit: aruḷnilai viḷaṅkuciṟ ṟampalame ṉuñciva cukātīta veḷinaṭuvilē aṇṭapaki raṇṭakō ṭikaḷum carācaram aṉaittumavai ākkalmutalām poruḷnilaic cattaroṭu cattikaḷ aṉantamum poṟpoṭuvi ḷaṅkiōṅkap puṟappuṟam akappuṟam puṟamakam ivaṟṟiṉmēl pūraṇā kāramākit teruḷnilaic caccitā ṉantakira ṇātikaḷ ciṟappamutal antamiṉṟit tikaḻkiṉṟa meyññāṉa cittiaṉu pavanilai teḷintiṭa vayaṅkucuṭarē curuḷnilaik kuḻalammai āṉanta valliciva cuntarik kiṉiyatuṇaiyē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: O Flame that shines to clarify the experiential state of attaining true wisdom! In the middle of the space of Siva's transcendent bliss, which is the Chitrambalam where the state of grace shines, you become the form of fullness over the outer-outer, inner-outer, outer, and inner realms. You cause billions of universes and their exteriors, all moving and unmoving things, and the infinite Saktars and Saktis in their essential state, who perform creation and other functions, to flourish in splendor, making the rays of Saccidānanda excel in a state of clarity, shining without beginning or end. O beloved companion to the Mother with spiraling locks of hair, Ānandavalli, the beautiful one of Siva! O Treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, O Vast Grace-Light, Lord Nataraja!
commentary: This verse presents a vast, cosmic vision of God as the ultimate source of everything. From the center of Chitrambalam (the Hall of Consciousness), God presides over billions of universes and all the powers, both male (Saktars) and female (Saktis), that run creation. God is the all-pervading light of Saccidānanda (being-consciousness-bliss), the singular treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Pure Siva), and the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light) that illuminates all existence.

translit: eṉiyal uṭampilē eṉpilē aṉpilē itayatti lētayavilē eṉuyiri lēeṉṟaṉ uyiriṉuk kuyirilē eṉiyaṟ kuṇamataṉilē iṉiyaleṉ vākkilē eṉṉuṭaiya nākkilē eṉcevip pulaṉicaiyilē eṉirukaṇ maṇiyilē eṉkaṇmaṇi oḷiyilē eṉaṉu pavantaṉṉilē taṉiyaleṉ aṟivilē aṟiviṉuk kaṟivilē tāṉē kalantumuḻutum taṉmayama tākkiyē tittittu mēṉmēl tatumpiniṟai kiṉṟaamutē tuṉṉiya peruṅkaruṇai veḷḷamē aḻiyāta cukamē cukātītamē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: O Nectar that mixes yourself completely with my natural body, my bones, my love, my heart, my compassion, my life, the life of my life, my inherent nature, my sweet speech, my tongue, the music in my sense of hearing, the pupils of my two eyes, the light in my pupils, my experience, my natural knowing, and the knowing within knowing, making everything one with yourself, sweetening it and, ever-increasingly, brimming over to fill me! O dense flood of great compassion, O imperishable bliss, O transcendent bliss! O Treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, O Vast Grace-Light, Lord Nataraja!
commentary: The vast, cosmic God of the previous verse is here experienced as an intensely intimate presence. Vallalar describes the divine flooding every part of his being: his body, his heart, his life, his senses, and his very consciousness. This presence is an overflowing nectar, a sweetness that makes everything divine from within.

translit: uṭalelām uyirelām uḷamelām uṇarvelām uḷḷaṉae lāṅkalantē oḷimayama tākkiiruḷ nīkkiek kālattum utayātta māṉamiṉṟi iṭalelām vallaciva cattikira ṇāṅkiyāy ēkamāy ēkapōka iṉpanilai eṉṉumoru ciṟcapaiyiṉ naṭuvē ilaṅniṟai kiṉṟacuṭarē kaṭalelām puvielām kaṉalelām vaḷielām kakaṉelām kaṇṭaparamē kāṇāta poruḷeṉak kalaielām pukalaeṉ kaṇkāṇa vantaporuḷē toṭalelām peṟaeṉak kuḷḷum puṟattummeyt tuṇaiyāy viḷaṅkumaṟivē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: O Flame, shining and filling the middle of the Ciṟcapai, which is the state of singular blissful experience! You mix with all of the body, all of life, all of the heart, all of feeling, and all that exists, making them into a form of light and removing the darkness. You shine at all times without rising or setting, as the One whose form is the rays of all-powerful Siva-Sakti. O Supreme Being, seen as all oceans, all earth, all fire, all wind, and all sky! O Being who came to be seen by my eyes, though all the scriptural arts declare you the unseen Reality! O Knowing that shines as my true companion within and without, enabling my attainment of all things! O Treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, O Vast Grace-Light, Lord Nataraja!
commentary: The ultimate spiritual truth, which scriptures (kalai) often describe as an unseen and abstract reality, can be directly perceived. Vallalar declares that this supreme Being, the source of the entire cosmos, has come to be seen by his own eyes. This direct experience of God, who is both within and without, removes all darkness and turns all of existence into pure light.

translit: meytaḻaiya uḷḷaṅ kuḷirntuvakai māṟātu mēṉmēṟ kalantupoṅka viccaiaṟi vōṅkaeṉ iccaiaṟi vaṉupavam viḷaṅkaaṟi vaṟivatāki uytaḻai vaḷittelām vallacit tatutan tuvaṭṭātuḷ ūṟiūṟi ūṟṟeḻun teṉṉaiyum tāṉākki eṉṉuḷē uḷḷapaṭi uḷḷaamutē kaitaḻaiya vantavāṉ kaṉiyē elāṅkaṇṭa kaṇṇē kalāntanaṭuvē kaṟpaṉaii lātōṅku ciṟcapā maṇiyē kaṇipparuṅ karuṇainiṟaivē tuytaḻai parappit taḻaintataru vēaruṭ cukapōka yōka:uruvē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: O Nectar that exists within me just as you are! O heavenly Fruit that came to fill my hands! O Eye that has seen all! O Gem of the Ciṟcapai that rises without fabrication in the midst of Kalānta! O Fullness of immeasurable compassion! O Tree that spreads tender leaves and flourishes! O Form of the yoga of graceful, blissful enjoyment! You cause my body to flourish, my heart to cool, and joy to well up and mix ever higher without ceasing. You make the knowledge of will grow, clarify the experience of the knowledge of desire, and become the knowing of knowing. Granting the all-powerful Siddhi that bestows the flourishing of salvation, you seep and seep within me without drying up, spring forth, and make even me into yourself. O Treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, O Vast Grace-Light, Lord Nataraja!
commentary: The union with God is a deeply personal process that brings tangible results: a flourishing body, a peaceful heart, and overflowing joy. This divine presence seeps into the soul, granting Siddhi (spiritual attainment) and finally transforming the individual into the divine itself. This Gem of the Hall of Consciousness rises, free of all fabrication, in the very midst of Kalāntam, one of the six summits (antams) of spiritual knowledge.

translit: eṇṇilā aṇṭapaki raṇṭattiṉ mutalilē iṭaiyilē kaṭaiyilēmēl ēṟṟatti lēavaiyuḷ ūṟṟatti lētiraṇ ṭeytuvaṭi vantaṉṉilē kaṇṇuṟā aruvilē uruvilē kuruvilē karuvilē taṉmaitaṉilē kalaiyāti nilaiyilē catticat tākik kalantōṅku kiṉṟaporuḷē teṇṇilāk kāntamaṇi mēṭaivāyk kōṭaivāyc cērntaṉu pavittacukamē cittelāñ ceyavalla teyvamē eṉmaṉat tirumāḷi kaittīpamē tuṇṇuṟāc cāntaciva ñāṉikaḷ uḷattē cutantarit toḷiceyoḷiyē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: O Being that, as Sakti and Sat, mixes and rises in the beginning, middle, and end of innumerable universes and outer-universes, in their heights, in the source within them, in the forms they assume, in the unseen formlessness, in form, in the Guru, in the seed, in their inherent nature, and in the state of the scriptural arts and other principles! O Bliss experienced, like uniting with one on a moonstone terrace in the summer! O Deity who can perform all siddhis! O Lamp in the sacred palace of my mind! O Light that shines with sovereign authority in the hearts of peaceful Siva-Jñānis who know no fear! O Treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, O Vast Grace-Light, Lord Nataraja!
commentary: God is present everywhere, from the vastness of innumerable universes to the most intimate spaces of the human heart. The divine is the underlying reality (Sat) and creative energy (Sakti) of all that exists, appearing in form, formlessness, and as the Guru (spiritual teacher). Vallalar contrasts this cosmic scale with deeply personal experiences: a blissful feeling, a lamp lighting his mind, and the sovereign light shining in the hearts of Siva-Jñānis (sages who know God).

translit: ampuviyi lēpuviyiṉ aṭiyilē muṭiyilē ammaṇṭa lantaṉṉilē akalatti lēpuviyiṉ akilatti lēavaik kāṉavaṭi vātitaṉilē vimpamuṟa vēniṟain tāṅkavai nikaḻntiṭa viḷakkumavai avaiyākiyē mēlumavai avaiyāki avaiavaia lātatoru meynnilaiyum āṉaporuḷē tampamicai eṉaiēṟṟi amutūṟṟi aḻiyāt talattiluṟa vaittaaracē cākāta vittaik kilakkaṇa ilakkiyam tāṉāyi runtaparamē tompatamum uṭaṉuṟṟa taṟpatamum acipatac cukamumoṉ ṟāṉacivamē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: On this beautiful earth, at the earth's base and its summit, within that sphere; in its breadth, in its entirety, and in the primordial form that is their cause, you are perfectly immanent. You illumine them so they manifest, becoming those very things. And while being those things, you are also the True Substance in a state that is none of them. O King who lifted me onto a pillar, fed me ambrosia, and established me in the immortal realm! O Supreme One who is yourself the grammar and literature for the art of deathlessness! O Sivam where 'Thou,' 'That,' and the bliss of 'Art' all become one! O Treasure of the Pure Siva Sanmarkkam, Lord of the Dance, the Vast Grace-Light!
commentary: God is both the substance of the entire world and the transcendent reality beyond it. God lifted Vallalar onto the pillar, poured ambrosia into him, and set him in the imperishable place; God is himself the grammar and the living text of the art of not dying (sākāta vittai). The goal is the state of Sivam, where the individual soul ('Thou,' tompadam) and the absolute Godhead ('That,' tatpadam) merge into a single blissful union ('Art,' asipadam).

translit: nīrilē nīruṟṟa niṟaiyilē niṟaiuṟṟa nilaiyilē nuṇmaitaṉilē nikaḻvilē nikaḻvuṟṟa tikaḻvilē niḻalilē nekiḻilē taṇmaitaṉilē ūrilē annīriṉ uppilē uppiluṟum oṇcuvaiyi lētiraiyilē uṟṟanīrk kīḻilē mēlilē naṭuvilē uṟṟiyal uṟuttumoḷiyē kārilē orukōṭi poḻiyiṉum tuṇaipeṟāk karuṇaimaḻai poḻimēkamē kaṉakacapai naṭuniṉṟa kaṭavuḷē ciṟcapaik kaṇṇōṅkum oruteyvamē tūrilē palamaḷit tūrilē vaḷarkiṉṟa cukacorupa māṉataruvē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: In water, in its inherent fullness, in that state of fullness, and in its subtlety; in its manifestation, in its radiant gleam, in its reflection, in its fluidity, and in its coolness; in its flow, in the water’s salt, in the bright taste of the salt, and in the waves, O Light that pervades and defines the nature of what is below, above, and in the middle of the water! O Cloud that showers a rain of compassion that a crore of storm clouds pouring down could never match! O God who stands in the center of the Golden Hall, the one Deity rising high in the Hall of Consciousness! O Tree of blissful form that gives fruit from afar and grows right here in town! O Treasure of the Pure Siva Sanmarkkam, Lord of the Dance, the Vast Grace-Light!
commentary: The divine is found in the cosmos and is intimately present in the very essence of ordinary things, like water. Vallalar shows how God is the defining light within water's coolness, saltiness, and flow. This accessible God is like a tree that offers its fruit to everyone right where they live, and a cloud that showers a compassion far greater than any rainstorm.

translit: oḷḷiya neruppilē uppilē oppilā oḷiyilē cuṭarilēmēl ōṭṭilē cūṭṭilē uḷḷāṭum āṭṭilē uṟumāti antattilē teḷḷiya niṟattilē aruvatti lēelām ceyavalla ceykaitaṉilē cittāy viḷaṅkiupa cittāya cattikaḷ ciṟakkavaḷar kiṉṟaoḷiyē vaḷḷiya civāṉanta malaiyē cukātīta vāṉamē ñāṉamayamē maṇiyēeṉ irukaṇṇuḷ maṇiyēeṉ uyirēeṉ vāḻvēeṉ vāḻkkaivaippē tuḷḷiya maṉappēyai uḷḷuṟa aṭakkimeyc cukameṉak kīntatuṇaiyē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: In the bright fire, in its heat, in its peerless light, and in its upward flame; in its spread, in its heat, in the dance within it, and in its beginning and end; in its clear color, in its formlessness, and in the action that can do all things, O Light who shines as consciousness, making the derivative powers flourish and grow! O generous Mountain of Siva's bliss! O Sky beyond all pleasure! O Embodiment of wisdom! O Gem, Pupil of my two eyes, my very life, my living, and my life’s treasure! O Companion who subdued the leaping demon-mind from within and gave me true bliss! O Treasure of the Pure Siva Sanmarkkam, Lord of the Dance, the Vast Grace-Light!
commentary: Just as with water, God is present in every quality of fire, from its light and heat to the dance within its flame. Vallalar identifies this universal presence as the same power that works within him personally, subduing the restless "demon-mind" to grant a state of true, unshakable bliss. This connects the cosmic force that animates the universe to the inner spiritual work of calming one's own thoughts.

translit: aṟaikiṉṟa kāṟṟilē kāṟṟuppi lēkāṟṟiṉ ātinaṭu antattilē āṉapala palakōṭi cattikaḷiṉ uruvāki āṭumataṉ āṭṭattilē uṟaikiṉṟa niṟaivilē ūkkatti lēkāṟṟiṉ uṟṟapala peṟṟitaṉilē ōṅkiavai tāṅkimiku pāṅkiṉuṟu cattarkaṭ kupakarit taruḷumoḷiyē kuṟaikiṉṟa matiniṉṟu kūcaōr āyiram kōṭikira ṇaṅkaḷvīcik kulaamuta mayamāki evvuyi riṭattum kulāvumoru taṇmatiyamē tuṟainiṉṟu poṟaioṉṟu tūyaraṟi vāṟkaṇṭa corupamē turiyapatamē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: In the roaring wind, in the nature of wind, in the wind's beginning, middle, and end; in its dance, where it takes the form of many crores of energies and performs; in its immanent fullness, in its force, and in the many qualities of the wind, O Light who rises high, sustains them all, and with great grace assists the masters of power! You are the one cool moon who, casting a thousand crore rays that make the waning moon shrink in shame, becomes a noble ambrosia and plays within every living being. O Form seen by the pure who stand firm in their path with singular patience! O state of Turīyam! O Treasure of the Pure Siva Sanmarkkam, Lord of the Dance, the Vast Grace-Light!
commentary: The divine presence fills the wind, animating it as the source of all energies and powers. This same powerful force is also described as a soothing, cool light, like a spiritual moon that brings ambrosial bliss to all living things. Vallalar calls this state Turīyam (the fourth state), a condition of pure consciousness beyond the ordinary states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, which is perceived by those who are patient and pure.

translit: vāṉilē vāṉuṟṟa vāyppilē vāṉiṉaru vattilē vāṉiyalilē vāṉaṭiyi lēvāṉiṉ naṭuvilē muṭiyilē vaṇṇatti lēkalaiyilē māṉilē nittiya valattilē pūraṇa varattilē maṟṟaiyatilē vaḷaraṉan tāṉanta cattarcat tikaḷtammai vaittaaruḷ uṟṟaoḷiyē tēṉilē pālilē carkkaraiyi lēkaṉit tiraḷilē tittikkumōr tittippe lāṅkūṭṭi uṇṭālum oppeṉac ceppiṭāt teḷḷamutamē tūnilā vaṇṇattil uḷḷōṅkum āṉanta corupamē corupacukamē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: In the sky, in the potential inherent in the sky, in its formlessness, and in its nature; at the sky’s base, in its middle, at its summit, in its color, and in its aspects; in its greatness, in its eternal power, in its perfect boon, and in all else, you are the Light of Grace who established the infinite, blissful masters of power and their energies. You are a clear ambrosia whose taste cannot be compared even to eating a mixture of all sweetness found in honey, milk, sugar, and clusters of ripe fruit. O Form of bliss that rises high within, having the color of pure moonlight! O bliss of that very Form! O Treasure of the Pure Siva Sanmarkkam, Lord of the Dance, the Vast Grace-Light!
commentary: Having described God's presence in earth, water, fire, and air, Vallalar now turns to the sky or space, the subtlest element. The divine pervades every aspect of it, from its vastness to its formlessness. He then tries to describe the experience of God, concluding that it is a unique sweetness far greater than any taste the world can offer. It is a bliss that has a quality like pure moonlight, shining within.

translit: eṉṟiravi taṉṉilē iravicoru pattilē iyaluruvi lēaruvilē ēṟiṭṭa cuṭarilē cuṭariṉuṭ cuṭarilē eṟiāta pattiraḷilē oṉṟiravi oḷiyilē ōṅkoḷiyiṉ oḷiyilē oḷioḷiyiṉ oḷinaṭuvilē oṉṟāki naṉṟāki niṉṟāṭu kiṉṟaaruḷ oḷiyēeṉ uṟṟatuṇaiyē aṉṟiravil vanteṉak karuḷoḷi aḷittaeṉ ayyaṉē aracaṉēeṉ aṟivaṉē amutaṉē aṉpaṉē iṉpaṉē appaṉē aruḷāḷaṉē tuṉṟiyaeṉ uyiriṉuk kiṉiyaṉē taṉiyaṉē tūyaṉē eṉnēyaṉē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: In the sun, in the very nature of the sun, in its manifest form, in its formlessness, in the magnificent flame, in the flame within the flame, in the canopy of its radiating rays, in the singular light of the sun, in the light of the soaring light, in the center of the light of light of light, you are the Grace-Light that stands and dances as one, as goodness. O my true companion, my Master who came that night and gave me the light of grace, my King, my Knower, my Nectar, my Beloved, my Bliss, my Father, O gracious One, O Sweetness to my dense life, O singular One, O pure One, my beloved Friend, O Treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, O Vast Grace-Light, O Lord Nataraja!
commentary: The series culminates with light itself, locating God within the sun, in its flame, and at the very core of light itself as the "light of light of light." This ultimate, dazzling cosmic principle is not remote. In the second half of the verse, Vallalar pours out a stream of intimate names, calling this Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi) his father, friend, beloved, and companion. The poem beautifully resolves the cosmic and the personal: the God who is the heart of the sun is the same God who comes as a friend in the night.

translit: aṇimatiyi lēmatiyiṉ aruvilē uruvilē avvuruviṉ uruvattilē amutakira ṇattilē akkiraṇa oḷiyilē avvoḷiyiṉ oḷitaṉṉilē paṇimatiyiṉ amutilē avvamu tiṉippilē pakkanaṭu aṭimuṭiyilē pāṅkupeṟa ōṅkumoru cittēeṉ uḷḷē palittapara māṉantamē maṇioḷiyil āṭumaruḷ oḷiyē nilaittaperu vāḻvē niṟaintamakiḻvē maṉṉēeṉ aṉpāṉa poṉṉēeṉ aṉṉēeṉ varamē vayaṅkuparamē tuṇimatiyil iṉpaaṉu pavamāy iruntakuru turiyamē periyaporuḷē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: In the beautiful moon, in the moon's formlessness, in its form, in the form of that form, in its nectar-like rays, in the light of those rays, in the light of that light, in the nectar of the cool moon, in the sweetness of that nectar, in its sides, center, base, and crown, you are the singular Consciousness that soars elegantly, the supreme bliss that has manifested within me. O Grace-Light that dances in the light of the gem, O permanent, great life, O full delight, O King, my beloved Gold, my Mother, my Boon, O radiant Supreme One, O Guru who was the blissful experience in my clear mind, O Turiya, O great Reality, O Treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, O Vast Grace-Light, O Lord Nataraja!
commentary: Vallalar finds God in every layer of the moon: its form and formlessness, its rays and the light of those rays, the sweetness of its nectar. In each of these the One Consciousness rises and becomes supreme bliss within him. The long cascade of names that follows, Mother, Gold, Guru, Turiya, ends where it always ends: ArutPerunJothi, Lord Nataraja.

translit: aṇṭaoru maippakuti irumaiyām pakutimēl āṅkāri yappakutiyē ātipala pakutikaḷ aṉantakō ṭikaḷiṉnaṭu aṭiyiṉoṭu muṭiyumavaiyil kaṇṭapala vaṇṇamuta lāṉaaka nilaiyum kaṇittapuṟa nilaiyummēṉmēl kaṇṭatika rikkiṉṟa kūṭṭamum viḷaṅkak kalantuniṟai kiṉṟaoḷiyē koṇṭapala kōlamē kuṇamē kuṇaṅkoṇṭa kuṟiyē kuṟikkaoṇṇāk kuruturiya mēcutta civaturiya mēelām koṇṭataṉi ñāṉaveḷiyē toṇṭarita yattilē kaṇṭeṉa iṉikkiṉṟa cukayōka aṉupōkamē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: You are the Light that pervades and illuminates the unitary region of the cosmos, the dual region, the region of ego above that, the many primordial regions in the middle of their infinite multitudes with their bases and crowns, the various internal states like color that are seen, the external states that are discerned, and the ever-increasing gatherings seen beyond them. O You who are the many forms taken, the qualities, the mark that has qualities, and that which cannot be marked, O Guru-Turiya, O Suddha Siva-Turiya, O singular expanse of wisdom that contains all, O blissful yoga-experience that sweetens the hearts of your servants like sugarcane, O Treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, O Vast Grace-Light, O Lord Nataraja!
commentary: From the single region of the cosmos to the dual, from the many primordial regions to the countless worlds and the inner and outer states seen in them, one Light pervades all. That Light takes every form and quality, yet no mark can define it. The same vast Light is tasted in the hearts of devotees like the sweetness of sugarcane, the bliss of union.

translit: karaiyilāk kaṭalilē kaṭaluppi lēkaṭaṟ kaṭaiyilē kaṭaliṭaiyilē kaṭalmutali lēkaṭal tiraiyilē nuraiyilē kaṭalōcai ataṉnaṭuvilē varaiyilā veḷḷap perukkatti lēvaṭṭa vaṭivilē vaṇṇamatilē maṟṟataṉ vaḷattilē uṟṟapala cattiyuḷ vayaṅkiavai kākkum oḷiyē puraiyilā oruteyva maṇiyēeṉ uḷḷē pukuntaṟi vaḷittaporuḷē poyyāta celvamē naiyāta kalviyē puṭamvait tiṭātapoṉṉē maraiyilā vāḻvē maṟaippilā vaippē maṟuppilā taruḷvaḷḷalē maṇimaṉṟil naṭuniṉṟa oruteyva mēelām vallanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: In the shoreless sea, in the sea's salt, at the sea's bottom, in the sea's middle, at the sea's beginning, in the sea's waves, in its foam, in the middle of the sea's sound, in the boundless flood, in its circular form, in its color, in its other riches, you are the Light that shines within the many powers it holds and protects them. O flawless, singular divine Gem, O Reality that entered within me and gave me awareness, O wealth that does not fail, O learning that does not diminish, O gold that has not been refined in a crucible, O life without end, O treasure without concealment, O benefactor who gives grace without refusal, O singular Divinity standing in the center of the Gem Hall, O Lord Nataraja, capable of all things!
commentary: God's presence fills every physical detail of the world, from the salt in the sea to the sound of its waves. This same divine reality is also the source of our own awareness, knowledge, and life. Vallalar sees this all-pervading reality as Lord Nataraja, the dancing God, who is active within the Manimandram (the Gem Hall of consciousness).

translit: uṟṟiyalum aṇuvāti malaianta māṉa:uṭal uṟṟakaru vākimutalāy uyirāy uyirkkuḷuṟum uyirāki uṇarvāki uṇarvuḷuṇar vākiuṇarvuḷ paṟṟiyalum oḷiyāki oḷiyiṉoḷi yākiam paramāyc citamparamumāyp paṇpuṟuci tamparap poṟcapaiyu māyataṉ pāṅkōṅku ciṟcapaiyumāyt teṟṟiyalum accapaiyiṉ naṭuvilnaṭam iṭukiṉṟa civamāy viḷaṅkuporuḷē cittelām ceyeṉat tiruvāk kaḷitteṉait tēṟṟiaruḷ ceytakuruvē maṟṟiyalum ākieṉai vāḻvitta meyññāṉa vāḻvēeṉ vāḻviṉvaramē maṇimaṉṟil naṭuniṉṟa oruteyva mēelām vallanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: Becoming the seed and origin of bodies ranging from the fitting atom to the final mountain, becoming life, the life within life, becoming consciousness, the consciousness within consciousness, becoming the light that fills it, the light of light, becoming the sky and Chidambaram, becoming the golden hall in refined Chidambaram and the Hall of Consciousness that soars elegantly there, you are the Reality that shines as Siva, dancing in the middle of that clear hall. O Guru who granted the divine word, "Perform all siddhis," and consoled and graced me, O life of true wisdom that became all else and made me live, O boon of my life, O singular Divinity standing in the center of the Gem Hall, O Lord Nataraja, capable of all things!
commentary: The divine is present at every level of existence, from the smallest physical particle to the deepest core of our own consciousness. Vallalar describes a movement inward, finding God as the life within our life, the awareness within our awareness, and finally as pure light. This inner reality is personified as the dancing Siva, the supreme Guru who grants spiritual powers (siddhis) and the wisdom to truly live.

translit: evvulakum evvuyirum epporuḷum uṭaiyatāy ellāñcey vallatāki iyaṟkaiyē uṇmaiyāy iyaṟkaiyē aṟivāy iyaṟkaiyē iṉpamāki avvaiyiṉ aṉātiyē pācamila tāyccutta aruḷāki aruḷveḷiyilē aruḷneṟi viḷaṅkavē aruḷnaṭam ceytaruḷ aruṭperuñ cōtiyākik kavvaiaṟu taṉimutaṟ kaṭavuḷāy ōṅkumeyk kāṭciyē karuṇainiṟaivē kaṇṇēeṉ aṉpiṟ kalanteṉai vaḷarkkiṉṟa katiyē kaṉintakaṉiyē vevviṉai tavirttoru viḷakkēṟṟi eṉṉuḷē vīṟṟirun taruḷumaracē meyññāṉa nilainiṉṟa viññāṉa kalaruḷē mēvunaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: You possess all worlds, all beings, and all things; You have the power to do everything; You are nature as truth, nature as intelligence, and nature as bliss. Being beginningless, without bondage, and made of pure grace, You became the Vast Grace-Light, performing the grace-dance in the expanse of grace so the path of grace may brightly shine. O True Vision that has risen as the singular First God who removes all sorrow! O fullness of compassion! O my very eye! O refuge who mingles with my love and nurtures me! O ripened fruit! O King who averts my harsh karma, lights a lamp within me, and graciously presides there! O Lord of the Dance who dwells within the Vignana Kalar established in the state of true wisdom!
commentary: God's very substance is self-existent truth, intelligence and bliss (iyaṟkai uṇmai, iyaṟkai aṟivu, iyaṟkai iṉpam): not acquired, not caused, but God's own nature. This divine reality is defined by pure grace, free from the spiritual bonds (pācam) that bind souls. Vallalar names this reality ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light, which is both the supreme principle and a personal guide who removes karma and nurtures the soul. This grace-light is especially present to the Vignana Kalar, highly advanced souls who have purified themselves of spiritual impurities.

translit: nātānta pōtānta yōkānta vētānta naṇṇuṟu kalāntamuṭaṉē navilkiṉṟa cittāntam eṉṉumā ṟantattiṉ ñāṉameyk koṭināṭṭiyē mūtāṇṭa kōṭika ḷoṭuñcarā caramelām muṉṉip paṭaittalmutalām muttoḻilum irutoḻilum muṉṉiṉ ṟiyaṟṟiaim mūrttikaḷum ēvalkēṭpa vātāntam uṟṟapala cattika ḷoṭuñcattar vāyntupaṇi ceyya:iṉpa mārācci yattilē tiruvaruṭ ceṅkōl vaḷattoṭu celuttumaracē cūtāṇṭa neñciṉil tōyāta nēyamē turiyanaṭu niṉṟacivamē cuttaciva caṉmārkka nitiyē aruṭperuñ cōtinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: You planted the flag of true wisdom at the culmination of the six final doctrines: Nadantam, Bodhantam, Yogantam, Vedantam, the associated Kalantam, and the one called Siddhantam. You stand forth to perform the three primary and two secondary cosmic functions, intending into existence the ancient, countless universes with all their moving and unmoving beings, while the five great deities await Your command and many Shaktis and Shaktars, having reached their own conclusions, are fit to serve You. O King who wields the scepter of holy grace with abundance in Your blissful kingdom! O Love that does not touch a deceitful heart! O Sivam who stands in the center of the transcendent state! O treasure of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam! O ArutPerunJothi, Lord of the Dance!
commentary: God's truth is the ultimate goal that all major spiritual and philosophical paths, including Siddhantam, are striving to reach. This supreme reality is the sole power behind the universe's creation and function; even the greatest gods are simply its agents. Vallalar calls the way to this reality the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Pure Goodness and Oneness with God). This supreme Lord of the Dance, ArutPerunJothi, does not engage with a deceitful heart, emphasizing the need for inner purity.

translit: orupiramaṉ aṇṭaṅkaḷ aṭimuṭip perumaiyē uṉṉamuṭi yāavaṟṟiṉ ōrāyi raṅkōṭi mālaṇṭam araṉaṇṭam uṟṟakō ṭākōṭiyē tirukalaṟu palakōṭi īcaṉaṇ ṭamcatā civaaṇṭam eṇṇiṟanta tikaḻkiṉṟa maṟṟaip peruñcatti cattartam cīraṇṭam eṉpukaluvēṉ uṟuvumiv vaṇṭaṅkaḷ attaṉaiyum aruḷveḷiyil uṟuciṟu aṇukkaḷāka ūṭacaiya avveḷiyiṉ naṭuniṉṟu naṭaṉamiṭum oruperuṅ karuṇaiaracē maruvieṉai āṭkoṇṭu makaṉākki aḻiyā varantanta meyttantaiyē maṇimaṉṟiṉ naṭuniṉṟa oruteyva mēelām vallanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: The full measure of the universes of a single Brahma cannot even be conceived; compared to them, the universes of Vishnu are a thousand crore, and the universes of Aran are countless crores more. The universes of the flawless Ishvara are many crores, and the universes of Sadasiva are innumerable. What can I even say of the glorious, excellent universes of the other great Shaktis and Shaktars? While all these universes drift and move like tiny atoms in the expanse of grace, You, O King of great compassion, are the one who stands in the middle of that expanse and dances! O true father, who drew near, accepted me as Your own, made me Your son, and gave me the boon of immortality! O the one God standing in the center of the Gem Hall! O all-powerful Lord of the Dance!
commentary: The physical cosmos, with its countless universes, is unimaginably vast, yet it is all just a collection of tiny specks within the infinite expanse of grace. God is not contained within this cosmos; the cosmos is contained within God's grace. At the center of this infinity, a compassionate God dances, and from this place of supreme power, He reaches out to embrace the individual soul, making him a son and granting immortality.

translit: varavucela vaṟṟapari pūraṇā kāracuka vāḻkkaimuta lāeṉakku vāyttaporu ḷēeṉkaṇ maṇiyēeṉ uḷḷē vayaṅkioḷir kiṉṟaoḷiyē iravupakal aṟṟaoru taruṇattil uṟṟapē riṉpamē aṉpiṉviḷaivē eṉtantai yēeṉatu kuruvēeṉ nēyamē eṉṉācai yēeṉ aṟivē karavuneṟi cellāk karuttiṉil iṉikkiṉṟa karuṇaiamu tēkarumpē kaṉiyē aruṭperuṅ kaṭalēe lāmvalla kaṭavuḷē kalaikaḷellām viraviuṇar variyaciva turiyaaṉu pavamāṉa meymmaiyē caṉmārkkamā meyññāṉa nilainiṉṟa viññāṉa kalaruḷē mēvunaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: O Substance that has granted me, as my ultimate possession, a life of blissful perfection, free from coming and going! O pupil of my eye! O Light that brightly shines within my soul! O great bliss experienced at a moment beyond night and day! O fruit of love! My father! My guru! My love! My desire! My knowledge! O nectar of compassion that is sweet in the mind that does not walk the path of deceit! O sugarcane! O fruit! O great ocean of grace! O all-powerful God! O Truth that is the experience of Siva Turiyam, which is beyond the grasp of all the arts combined! O Lord of the Dance who dwells within the Vignana Kalar established in the state of true wisdom that is the Sanmarkkam!
commentary: The supreme God of the cosmos is also the most intimate and personal reality one can know. This verse is a torrent of devotional names for God: the pupil of the eye, the light in the soul, a great bliss beyond time, the fruit of love, father, and teacher. This experience of God, called Siva Turiyam (a high state of consciousness centered on the divine), is a truth beyond all learning or art. It is the core of the Sanmarkkam (the True Path), and it is realized by the Vignana Kalar, souls who have attained the highest wisdom and in whom God dwells.

translit: pārāti pūtamoṭu poṟipulaṉ karaṇamum pakutiyum kālammutalāp pakarkiṉṟa karuviyum avaikkumēl uṟucutta paramāti nātamvaraiyum cīrāya paravintu paranāta muntaṉatu tikaḻaṅkam eṉṟuraippat tiruvaruṭ peruveḷiyil āṉanta naṭaṉamiṭu teyvamē eṉṟumaḻiyā ūrāti tanteṉai vaḷarkkiṉṟa aṉṉaiyē uyartantai yēeṉuḷḷē uṟṟatuṇai yēeṉṟaṉ uṟavēeṉ aṉpē uvappēeṉ ṉuṭaiya:uyirē ārālum aṟiyāta uyarnilaiyil eṉaivaitta aracē aruṭcōtiyē akaranilai muḻutumāy appālu mākiniṟai amutanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: It is said that the elements beginning with earth, the sense organs, the senses, the inner faculties, primal matter, time and all such instruments, and even the pure realities above them, up to Paramanadam, along with the glorious Paravindu and Paranadam, are Your shining limbs. O Divine One who performs the dance of bliss in the great expanse of holy grace! O mother and noble father who gave me an immortal home and nurtured me! O companion within me! My kin! My love! My joy! My very life! O King who placed me in a high state unknown to anyone! O Grace-Light! O Lord of the Dance of Nectar, who fills the entire state of A and also exists beyond it!
commentary: Every part of existence, from the densest matter to the most subtle spiritual principles, makes up the body of God. The physical world, our senses, our minds, time itself, and even the highest cosmic realities like Paramanadam, Paravindu, and Paranadam (realms of primal sound and light) are described as God's limbs. This all-encompassing God, who dances in the expanse of grace, is also the most personal of beings: a mother, a father, a companion, and the very life of the soul. God is the reality behind the primal state represented by the letter 'A' but also extends infinitely beyond it.

translit: uraivicuvam uṇṭaveḷi upacānta veḷimēlai uṟumavuṉa veḷiveḷiyiṉmēl ōṅkumā mavuṉaveḷi yātiyuṟum aṉupavam oruṅkaniṟai uṇmaiveḷiyē tiraiyaṟu peruṅkaruṇai vāriyē ellāñcey cittē eṉakkuvāytta celvamē oṉṟāṉa teyvamē uyvakai teritteṉai vaḷarttacivamē parainaṭu viḷaṅkumoru cōtiyē ellām paṭaittiṭuka eṉṟeṉakkē paṇpuṟa uraittaruṭ pēramuta ḷittameyp paramamē paramañāṉa varainaṭu viḷaṅkuciṟ capainaṭuvil āṉanta vaṇṇanaṭa miṭuvaḷḷalē māṟāta caṉmārkka nilainīti yēelām vallanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: Oh space of Truth, where the experience of all states, beginning with the space that consumed the spoken cosmos, the space of deep peace, the space of silence above it, and the great space of silence, culminates in one unified fullness! Oh waveless, great ocean of compassion! Oh Cittē that accomplishes everything! Oh wealth that has come to me! Oh the one God! Oh Sivam who showed me the way to be saved and nurtured me! Oh singular Jothi shining in the midst of Parai! Oh true Supreme Being who gave me the great ambrosia of grace, kindly telling me, "Create everything"! Oh benevolent one who performs the dance of blissful form in the center of the Chit Sabhai, which shines in the middle of the mountain of supreme wisdom! Oh unchanging justice of the state of Sanmarkkam, all-powerful Natarajapati!
commentary: God is the ultimate Truth that contains all levels of spiritual experience, and this divine power is now shared with the devotee. Vallalar describes a series of 'spaces' or states of consciousness that the soul passes through, culminating in a final, unified "space of Truth." God is the Cittē, the infinite consciousness-power that can do anything, and the Jothi (Light) shining within Parai (the supreme divine energy). In an astonishing expression of union, God gives Vallalar the great nectar of grace and tells him, "Create everything," inviting him to share in the divine creative act.

translit: ūḻitō ṟūḻipala aṇṭapakir aṇṭat tuyirkkelām tariṉumantō oruciṟitum ulavāta niṟaivāki aṭiyēṟ kuvappoṭu kiṭaittanitiyē vāḻinī ṭūḻiyeṉa vāymalarn taḻiyā varantanta vaḷḷalēeṉ matiyiṉiṟai matiyē vayaṅkumati amutamē matiamutiṉ uṟṟacukamē ēḻiṉō ṭēḻulakil uḷḷavarkaḷ ellāmi teṉṉaieṉ ṟaticayippa iravupakal illāta perunilaiyil ēṟṟieṉai iṉpuṟac ceytakuruvē āḻiyō ṭaṇiaḷit tuyirelām kāttuviḷai yāṭeṉ ṟuraittaaracē akaranilai muḻutumāy appālu mākioḷir apayanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: Oh treasure that came to me with delight, a fullness that does not diminish in the slightest even if given to all the souls in many universes and the cosmos beyond for eon after eon! Oh benevolent one who, with smiling lips, blessed me, "May you live for long eons," and granted me the boon of immortality! Oh moon that fills my intellect, oh ambrosia of that shining moon, oh bliss that comes from the ambrosia of that moon! Oh Guru who made me blissful, elevating me to the great state without night and day, causing everyone in the fourteen worlds to wonder in amazement, "What is this?"! Oh King who gave me the royal discus and ornaments and said, "Protect all lives and play"! Oh Natarajapati of refuge who shines as the entirety of the primal 'A' state and also beyond it!
commentary: God's grace is an infinite, inexhaustible treasure that elevates the soul to a divine status. This grace is so abundant it could be given to every being in every universe for all time and never be diminished. By receiving it, Vallalar is granted immortality and raised to a state beyond night and day, making all beings in the fourteen worlds wonder. The king of the cosmos gives him a divine command of blissful freedom: "Protect all lives and play." This reveals that the goal is salvation and becoming a joyful, compassionate guardian of life itself.

translit: pūtamuta lāyapala karuvikaḷ aṉaittumeṉ pukalvaḻip paṇikaḷkēṭpap poypaṭāc cattikaḷ aṉantakō ṭikaḷummeyp poruḷkaṇṭa cattarpalarum ētamaṟa eṉṉuḷam niṉaittavai niṉaittāṅ kicainteṭut tutavaeṉṟum iṟavāta perunilaiyil iṇaicolā iṉpuṟ ṟirukkaeṉai vaittakuruvē nātamutal irumūṉṟu varaiyanta nilaikaḷum nalampeṟac caṉmārkkamām ñāṉaneṟi ōṅkaōr tiruvaruṭ ceṅkōl naṭattivaru nallaaracē vātamiṭu camayamata vātikaḷ peṟaṟkariya māmatiyiṉ amutaniṟaivē maṇimaṉṟiṉ naṭuniṉṟa oruteyva mēelām vallanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: Oh Guru who placed me in the great state of deathlessness to enjoy incomparable bliss forever, making all the instruments, starting with the elements, obey my commands, and making countless flawless Saktis and many realized Satthars perceive my thoughts and harmoniously deliver what I have thought! Oh good King who wields a scepter of holy grace so that the path of wisdom, which is Sanmarkkam, may flourish, benefiting all the states from Natham to the six Antams! Oh fullness of the ambrosia of great wisdom, unattainable by the polemicists of argumentative religions and creeds! Oh singular God standing in the middle of the Maṇimaṉṟam, all-powerful Natarajapati!
commentary: Divine grace has given Vallalar mastery over reality itself: the elements obey his word, and divine powers (Saktis) and realized ones (Satthars) fulfil what he thinks. The Guru who placed him in this deathless state is the good King who wields the 'scepter of holy grace,' so that the path of wisdom, Sanmarkkam, may flourish and the six summits (antams), beginning with Nādāntam, may be fulfilled in it. This fullness of wisdom is beyond the reach of those who argue for religions and creeds.

translit: vāṭṭamoṭu ciṟiyaṉēṉ ceyvakaiyai aṟiyātu maṉamika mayaṅkiorunāḷ maṇṇiṟ kiṭantaruḷai uṉṉiula kiyaliṉai maṟantutuyil kiṉṟapōtu nāṭṭamuṟu vaikaṟaiyil eṉaru kaṇainteṉṉai naṉṟuṟa eḻuppimakaṉē nalyōka ñāṉameṉi ṉumpurital iṉṟinī nalitalaḻa kōeḻuntē īṭṭukaniṉ eṇṇam palikkaaruḷ amutamuṇ ṭiṉpuṟuka eṉṟakuruvē eṉācai yēeṉṟaṉ aṉpē niṟaintapē riṉpamē eṉcelvamē vēṭṭavai aḷikkiṉṟa nitiyamē cākāta vittaiyil viḷaintacukamē meyññāṉa nilainiṉṟa viññāṉa kalaruḷē mēvunaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: One day, as I, a small and distressed man, lay on the ground, not knowing what to do, my mind greatly confused, thinking of grace and forgetting worldly ways, I fell asleep. Oh Guru who, at the beautiful dawn, came near me, woke me properly, and said, "My son, is it beautiful for you to suffer without even practicing good yoga or wisdom? Arise! So your intentions may be fulfilled, receive the ambrosia of grace and be blissful"! Oh my desire, my love, my overflowing great bliss, my wealth! Oh treasure that gives whatever is desired! Oh bliss that results from the art of not dying! Oh Natarajapati who abides within the Vijñānakalar (a class of highly evolved souls) who stand firm in the state of true wisdom!
commentary: This verse recalls a moment of deep human despair that was met with an intimate divine response. Feeling small, lost, and confused, Vallalar fell into a desperate sleep. At dawn, God came to him as a personal Guru (spiritual teacher), speaking with the tenderness of a parent to awaken him from his suffering. This direct intervention, the gift of the "ambrosia of grace," is the source of his bliss, his power, and his attainment of the "art of not dying."
