translit: eṉceyvēṉ ciṟiyaṉēṉ eṉceyvēṉ eṉeṇṇam ētāka muṭiyumōeṉ ṟeṇṇiiru kaṇṇiṉīr kāṭṭik kalaṅkiniṉ ṟēṅkiya irāvilorunāḷ miṉceymeyñ ñāṉa:uru vākināṉ kāṇavē veḷiniṉ ṟaṇaitteṉuḷḷē mēvieṉ tuṉpan tavirttaruḷi aṅṅaṉē vīṟṟiruk kiṉṟakuruvē naṉceyvāy iṭṭaviḷai vatuviḷain tatukaṇṭa nalkuravi ṉōṉaṭainta naṉmakiḻviṉ orukōṭi paṅkatikam ākavē nāṉkaṇṭu koṇṭamakiḻvē vaṉceyvāy vātaruk kariyaporu ḷēeṉṉai valiyavan tāṇṭaparamē maṇimaṉṟiṉ naṭuniṉṟa oruteyva mēelām vallanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: One night, as I stood weeping, agitated and languishing, thinking, "What can I, a small man, do? What will I do? How will my intentions ever come to fruition?", you appeared before my very eyes as a form of true wisdom made of lightning, stood manifest, embraced me, and entered me. Oh Guru who thus dispelled my suffering and remains majestically seated there! Oh my joy, which is ten million times greater than the good joy of a poor man who sees the harvest ripening in his fertile field! Oh substance inaccessible to harsh-mouthed debaters! Oh Supreme Being who forcefully came and ruled me! Oh singular God standing in the middle of the Manimantram, all-powerful Natarajapati!
commentary: Here Vallalar describes another moment of crisis transformed by a direct, physical, and overwhelming experience of God. As he stood weeping in helpless anguish, God appeared before him as a tangible form "made of lightning," embraced him, and merged with his being. This union instantly dispelled his suffering and filled him with a joy he describes as ten million times greater than that of a starving man seeing his fields ready for harvest. The experience was an act of irresistible grace that "forcefully came and ruled" him.

translit: tuṉpelān tīrntaṉa cukampalit tatuniṉaic cūḻntataruḷ oḷiniṟaintē cuttacaṉ mārkkanilai aṉupavam niṉakkē cutantarama tāṉatulakil vaṉpelām nīkkinal vaḻiyelām ākkimey vāḻvelām peṟṟumikavum maṉṉuyir elāmkaḷit tiṭaniṉait taṉaiuṉṟaṉ maṉaniṉaip piṉpaṭikkē aṉpanī peṟuka:ula vātunī ṭūḻiviḷai yāṭuka aruṭcōtiyām āṭcitan tōmuṉaik kaiviṭōm kaiviṭōm āṇainam āṇaieṉṟē iṉpuṟat tiruvāk kaḷitteṉuḷ ḷēkalan ticaivuṭaṉ iruntakuruvē ellāñcey vallacit tākimaṇi maṉṟiṉil ilaṅkunaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: “All your suffering has ended; happiness has manifested. The light of grace surrounds and fills you. The experience of the state of Suddha Sanmarkkam is now your rightful possession in this world. Because you have intended to remove all cruelty, create all good paths, attain the true life, and make all enduring souls rejoice, in accordance with your heart’s thoughts, receive this, O beloved one. Play through the long ages without perishing. We have given you the dominion of the Jothi of Grace. We will not forsake you, we will not forsake you! This is our vow, our vow!” O Guru who gave me these pleasing sacred words, mingled within me, and remained in harmony! O all-powerful Siddha who is everything, O Lord of the Dance who shines in the jeweled hall!
commentary: This verse is a direct proclamation from God, commissioning Vallalar and confirming his new state. God declares that this ultimate transformation is granted because Vallalar’s own heart already desired to end cruelty and bring joy to all souls. His compassionate intention aligned perfectly with the divine will, unlocking this immense grace. He is given dominion of the Jothi (Divine Light), possession of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure True Path), and an immortal life to "play" and carry out his mission, all backed by God's unbreakable vow: "We will not forsake you."

translit: pēruṟṟa ulakiluṟu camayamata neṟielām pēyppiṭip puṟṟapiccup piḷḷaiviḷai yāṭṭeṉa uṇarntiṭā tuyirkaḷpala pētamuṟ ṟaṅkumiṅkum pōruṟ ṟiṟantuvīṇ pōyiṉār iṉṉumvīṇ pōkāta paṭiviraintē puṉitamuṟu cuttacaṉ mārkkaneṟi kāṭṭimeyp poruḷiṉai uṇarttiellām ēruṟṟa cukanilai aṭaintiṭap puritinī eṉpiḷḷai ātalālē ivvēlai purikaeṉ ṟiṭṭaṉam maṉattilvē ṟeṇṇaṟka eṉṟakuruvē nīruṟṟa oḷḷiya neruppē neruppiṉuḷ niṟaintiruḷ akaṟṟumoḷiyē nirkkuṇā ṉantapara nātānta varaiōṅku nītinaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: “In this renowned world, many souls, not realizing that all the paths of religion and creed are but the crazed games of children possessed by demons, have fallen into division, fought here and there, died, and gone to waste. So that they do not go to waste any longer, you must act swiftly. Show them the sacred path of Suddha Sanmarkkam, make them realize the true substance, and have them all attain a state of glorious happiness. Do this work, for you are my child. We have commanded it. Do not think otherwise in your heart.” O Guru who said this! O brilliant fire contained in water! O light within the fire that dispels the darkness! O Lord of the Dance of justice, who soars to the very limit of Nadantha (a transcendent state of consciousness beyond manifest sound), the transcendent bliss beyond attributes!
commentary: God commands Vallalar to lead humanity away from the conflict and division caused by competing religions, which he dismisses as childish games. The mission is to guide people to the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Purity), a universal spirituality that transcends religious dogma and leads directly to happiness and truth.

translit: cākāta kalviyē kalvioṉ ṟēcivam tāṉeṉa aṟintaaṟivē takumaṟivu malamaintum veṉṟaval lapamē taṉittapū raṇavallapam vēkāta kālāti kaṇṭukoṇ ṭepporuḷum viḷaiyaviḷai vittatoḻilē meyttoḻila tākumin nāṉkaiyum oruṅkē viyantaṭain tulakamellām mākāta luṟaelām vallacit tākiniṟai vāṉavara mēiṉpamām maṉṉumitu nīpeṟṟa cuttacaṉ mārkkattiṉ marapeṉ ṟuraittakuruvē tēkāti mūṉṟumnāṉ tarumuṉaruḷ ceyteṉait tēṟṟiaruḷ ceytacivamē ciṟcapaiyiṉ naṭuniṉṟa oṉṟāṉa kaṭavuḷē teyvanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: “The art of not dying is the only true learning. The awareness that knows ‘Sivam is the One’ is the only proper knowledge. The power that has conquered the five impurities is the only unique, complete power. The work that makes all things manifest, having found the unburning air (vēkāk kāl) and the principles that go with it, is the only true work. You have wonderfully attained all four of these at once, so the whole world loves you, and you have become an all-powerful Siddha. This enduring, blissful, supreme boon is the tradition of the Suddha Sanmarkkam you have received,” declared the Guru. O Sivam who graced me and uplifted me with your grace even before I offered the three bodies! O the one God standing in the center of the Chit Sabhai! O divine Lord of the Dance!
commentary: The true spiritual path redefines the meaning of human achievement. True learning is achieving immortality, true knowledge is realizing the oneness of God, true power is inner purity, and true work is divine creation. God declares that Vallalar has attained all four, becoming an all-powerful Siddha (one with perfected spiritual powers) and a master of the deathless body.

translit: nīṭulakil uṟṟavarkaḷ naṉkuṟa uraikkiṉṟa niṉvārttai yāvumnamatu nīḷvārttai yākumitu uṇmaimaka ṉēcaṟṟum neñcamañ cēl uṉakkē āṭuṟum aruṭperuñ cōtiīn taṉameṉṟum aḻiyāta nilaiyiṉniṉṟē aṉpiṉāl eṅkeṅkum eṇṇiya paṭikkunī āṭivāḻ keṉṟakuruvē nāṭunaṭu nāṭṭattil uṟṟaaṉu pavañāṉam nāṉiḷaṅ kālaiaṭaiya nalkiya peruṅkaruṇai appaṉē ammaiyē naṇpaṉē tuṇaivaṉēeṉ ūṭupiri yātuṟṟa iṉpaṉē aṉpaṉē oruvaṉē aruvaṉēuḷ ūṟumamu tākiōr āṟiṉmuṭi mītilē ōṅkunaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: “All the words you speak for the good of the people in this enduring world are our own great words. This is the truth, my son. Do not fear in your heart at all. We have given you the dancing Great Jothi of Grace. Standing in an ever-undecaying state, live and dance with love, everywhere, just as you have thought,” said the Guru. O my great grace, who enabled me in my youth to attain the experiential wisdom found in the central dance! My father! My mother! My friend! My companion! My inseparable inner bliss! My beloved! O the One! The formless one! O you who became the nectar welling up inside and who soars above the crown of the six centers! O Lord of the Dance!
commentary: God grants Vallalar a final assurance: his words will now carry divine authority. He is empowered by the Great Jothi of Grace to act freely with love, his will now one with the divine will. Vallalar’s reply shows the intimacy of this union, addressing God as his own mother, father, friend, and inseparable bliss.

translit: annāḷil ampalat tiruvāyi liṭaiuṉak kaṉpuṭaṉ uraittapaṭiyē aṟputame lāmvalla namaruṭ pēroḷi aḷittaṉam makiḻntuṉuḷḷē innāḷ toṭuttunī eṇṇiya paṭikkē iyaṟṟiviḷai yāṭimakiḻka eṉṟumiṟa vānilaiyil iṉpaaṉu pavaṉāki iyalcutta mātimūṉṟum ennāḷum uṉiccai vaḻipeṟṟu vāḻkayām eytiniṉ ṉuṭkalantēm iṉienta āṟṟiṉum pirivuṟēm uṇmaiī temmāṇai eṉṟakuruvē maṉṉāki eṉperiya vāḻvāki aḻiyāta varamāki niṉṟacivamē maṇimaṉṟiṉ naṭuniṉṟa oruteyva mēelām vallanaṭa rājapatiyē.
translation: “Just as we lovingly told you that day at the sacred gate of the Ambalam, we have now joyfully given you our great light of grace, which is capable of all wonders, within you. From this day forth, act, play, and rejoice just as you have thought. In a state of deathlessness, become one who experiences bliss. May the three natural states, Suddha and the rest, always be attained according to your will. We have reached and mingled within you. We will never be separate from you in any way. This is the truth. This is our vow,” said the Guru. O Sivam who became my king, my great life, and my undying boon! O the one God standing in the middle of the jeweled hall! O all-powerful Lord of the Dance!
commentary: This verse describes the culmination of the spiritual path: a permanent and inseparable union with God. The instruction to "play" suggests a life of spontaneous, joyful, creative action, free from fear and limitation. Vallalar is granted total freedom to act in the world from a deathless state of bliss, becoming an eternal co-creator with the Divine.

translit: kāyelām kaṉieṉak kaṉivikkum oruperuṅ karuṇaiamu tēeṉakkuk kaṇkaṇṭa teyvamē kalikaṇṭa aṟputak kāṭciyē kaṉakamalaiyē tāyelām aṉaiyaeṉ tantaiyē orutaṉit talaivaṉē niṉperumaiyaic cāṟṟiṭa niṉaittiṭa matittiṭa aṟintiṭac cārkiṉṟa tōṟumantō vāyelān tittikkum maṉamelān tittikkum matielān tittikkumeṉ maṉṉiyamey aṟivelān tittikkum eṉṉilatil varumiṉpam eṉpukaluvēṉ tūyelām peṟṟanilai mēlaruṭ cukamelām tōṉṟiṭa viḷaṅkucuṭarē turiyaveḷi naṭuniṉṟa periyaporu ḷēaruṭ cōtinaṭa rājakuruvē.
translation: O great nectar of grace that ripens all unripe fruit, O God I have seen with my own eyes, O wondrous vision seen in this age of Kali, O golden mountain, my father who is like all mothers, and my singular Lord! Alas, whenever I approach to speak of, think of, value, or know Your greatness, my whole mouth sweetens, my whole mind sweetens, my whole intellect sweetens, and my whole stable, true knowledge sweetens. If so, what can I say of the bliss that arises from it? O Effulgence that shines, making the entire bliss of grace appear in the state where all purity has been attained! O great Being who stands in the center of the transcendent expanse! O Guru Nataraja of Grace-Jothi!
commentary: The very thought of God is so overwhelmingly blissful that it fills every part of Vallalar's being with a physical sweetness. This verse emphasizes that the divine is a directly felt, sensory experience that defies words. God is the "great Being" found in the turīya veḷi, the transcendent expanse of pure consciousness beyond the ordinary states of waking, dreaming, and sleep.

translit: eyppaṟa eṉakkuk kiṭaittaperu nitiyamē ellāñcey vallacittāy eṉkaiyil akappaṭṭa ñāṉamaṇi yēeṉṉai eḻumaiyum viṭātanaṭpē kaippaṟaeṉ uḷḷē iṉikkiṉṟa carkkaraik kaṭṭiyē karuṇaiamutē kaṟpaka vaṉattē kaṉintakaṉi yēeṉatu kaṇkāṇa vantakatiyē meyppayaṉ aḷikkiṉṟa tantaiyē tāyēeṉ viṉaielān tīrttapatiyē meyyāṉa teyvamē meyyāṉa civapōka viḷaivēeṉ meymmaiuṟavē tuyppuṟumeṉ aṉpāṉa tuṇaiyēeṉ iṉpamē cuttacaṉ mārkkanilaiyē turiyaveḷi naṭuniṉṟa periyaporu ḷēaruṭ cōtinaṭa rājakuruvē.
translation: O great treasure I received that ends my weariness, O gem of wisdom that fell into my hands as the all-powerful Siddha, O friendship that will not leave me for all seven births! O lump of rock candy that sweetens within me, dispelling all bitterness, O nectar of grace, O fruit ripened in the grove of wish-fulfilling trees, O refuge who came before my very eyes! O father and mother who grant the true benefit, O master who resolved all my karma, O true God, O true harvest of Siva’s bliss, O my true kinship, my loving companion in all enjoyment, my bliss, the very state of Suddha Sanmarkkam! O great Being who stands in the center of the transcendent expanse! O Guru Nataraja of Grace-Jothi!
commentary: God is portrayed as the most intimate and precious reality in one's life: a treasure, a constant friend, and the final refuge who dissolves the consequences of past actions (karma or vinai). The verse culminates by identifying God with the path itself, the state of Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Path of Pure Truth and Harmony). God is both the goal and the way.

translit: tuṉpuṟu maṉattaṉāy eṇṇāta eṇṇināṉ cōrntoru puṟampaṭuttut tūṅkutaru ṇatteṉṟaṉ arukiluṟ ṟaṉpiṉāl tūyatiru vāymalarntē iṉpuṟu mukattilē puṉṉakai tatumpavē irukaimalar koṇṭutūkki eṉṟaṉai eṭuttaṇait tāṅkumaṟ ṟōriṭat tiyaluṟa iruttimakiḻvāy vaṉpaṟu peruṅkaruṇai amutaḷit tiṭarnīkki vaittaniṉ tayavaiantō vaḷḷalē uḷḷutoṟum uḷḷaka melāmiṉpa vāriamu tūṟiūṟit tuṉpamaṟa mēṟkoṇṭu poṅkit tatumpumic cukavaṇṇam eṉpukaluvēṉ turiyaveḷi naṭuniṉṟa periyaporu ḷēaruṭ cōtinaṭa rājakuruvē.
translation: When, with a troubled mind, I had thought unthinkable thoughts, grown weary, and was lying on my side falling asleep, You came near me. With love, Your pure, sacred mouth spoke, a gentle smile brimming on Your blissful face. You lifted me with Your two flower-like hands, took me up and embraced me, and then joyfully seated me properly in another place. You gave me the great nectar of grace that ends all harshness and thus removed my suffering. Alas, O generous one! Whenever I think of this kindness of Yours, a flood of blissful nectar seeps and wells up within my entire inner self, rising to dispel all sorrow and overflowing. What can I say of this state of bliss? O great Being who stands in the center of the transcendent expanse! O Guru Nataraja of Grace-Jothi!
commentary: This verse recounts a moment of personal grace. During a time of weariness and despair, God provides tangible comfort, like a parent lifting and embracing a child. The memory of this simple, loving act becomes an endless source of inner bliss that washes away all sorrow, showing that divine intervention is often a quiet, tender, and personal experience.

translit: ōṅkiya peruṅkaruṇai poḻikiṉṟa vāṉamē orumainilai uṟuñāṉamē upayapata catataḷamum eṉatitaya catataḷat tōṅkanaṭu vōṅkucivamē pāṅkiyal aḷitteṉṉai aṟiyāta oruciṟiya paruvattil āṇṭapatiyē pācaneṟi cellāta nēcartamai īcarām paṭivaikka vallaparamē āṅkiyalva teṉṟumaṟ ṟīṅkiyalva teṉṟumvā yāṭuvōrk kariyacukamē āṉanta mayamāki atuvuṅ kaṭantaveḷi yākiniṟai kiṉṟaniṟaivē tūṅkiviḻu ciṟiyaṉait tāṅkieḻu keṉṟeṉatu tūkkan tolaittatuṇaiyē turiyaveḷi naṭuniṉṟa periyaporu ḷēaruṭ cōtinaṭa rājakuruvē.
translation: O sky that showers down abundant, great grace! O wisdom established in the state of oneness! O Siva, who rises in the center as the hundred-petaled lotuses of Your two feet rise within the hundred-petaled lotus of my heart! O master who, granting me the role of a female companion, took me in Your charge in my small, unknowing youth! O supreme one, able to make lovers who do not follow the path of bondage into Lords themselves! O bliss, rare for those who argue, 'It is there,' and 'It is here'! O bliss, rare for those who prattle on about “what is good” and “what is bad”! O fullness that fills everything, having become the form of bliss and then the expanse that transcends even that! O companion who supported this little one as I was falling from drowsiness, who told me to rise, and who dispelled my sleep! O great Being who stands in the center of the transcendent expanse! O Guru Nataraja of Grace-Jothi!
commentary: True spiritual life is found in the direct experience of divine love and oneness, not in arguments about good and bad. Vallalar uses the classic devotional image of the soul as a female companion (pāṅki) to describe his relationship with God, who guided him from his "unknowing youth." The divine presence awakens the soul from spiritual sleep and establishes it in a state of bliss that is beyond all dualistic thinking.

sections.title: The Garland of the Guru Gem

translit: māṟṟaṟi yātace ḻumpacum poṉṉē māṇikka mēcuṭar vaṇṇak koḻuntē kūṟṟaṟi yātape runtavar uḷḷak kōyil irunta kuṇapperuṅ kuṉṟē vēṟṟaṟi yātaciṟ ṟampalak kaṉiyē viccaiyil vallavar meccuvi runtē cāṟṟaṟi yātaeṉ cāṟṟuṅ kaḷittāy taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O rich, pure gold of untestable quality! O ruby! O tender flame of radiant color! O great mountain of virtue, seated in the heart-temples of great ascetics unknown to Death! O fruit of the Chitrambalam that knows no other! O feast praised by those skilled in esoteric arts! You delighted in my speech, which is itself unworthy of being spoken. O peerless King of Dance, my gem of a true guru!
commentary: The divine teacher is a reality of supreme, untestable value, accessible only through devotion. Vallalar praises his guru with images of ultimate worth: pure gold, a ruby, a radiant flame. This treasure is found in the hearts of great ascetics who have overcome death, yet it also delights in the humble, unworthy praise of the poet, showing that divine greatness is matched by its loving acceptance.

translit: kaṟkarai yumpaṭi karaivikkuṅ karuttē kaṇmaṇi yēmaṇi kalantakaṇ oḷiyē coṟkarai yiṉṟiya oḷiyiṉuḷ oḷiyē turiyamuṅ kaṭantiṭṭa periyacem poruḷē ciṟkarai tiraiyaṟu tiruvaruṭ kaṭalē teḷḷamu tēkaṉi yēceḻum pākē carkkarai yēatu cārntacen tēṉē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O thought that causes even stone to melt! O apple of my eye! O light of the eye, mingled with its gem! O light within the light that is beyond the shore of words! O great, perfect reality that has surpassed even the Turiya state! O ocean of sacred grace, whose shore is consciousness, free of waves! O clear ambrosia! O fruit! O rich syrup! O sugar! O pure honey that goes with it! O peerless King of Dance, my gem of a true guru!
commentary: The guru's presence is a power that can dissolve the hardest heart and flood the soul with sweetness. It is a "thought that causes even stone to melt," breaking down all resistance. This divine reality is a light beyond what words can capture, transcending even the Turiya state (the fourth state of pure consciousness). The experience is one of being immersed in an ocean of grace and tasting every form of sweetness at once.

translit: eṉṉuyi rēeṉa tiṉṉuyirk kuyirē eṉaṟi vēeṉa taṟiviṉuk kaṟivē aṉṉaiyil iṉiyaeṉ ampalat tamutē aṟputa mēpata mēeṉa taṉpē poṉṉiṇai aṭimalar muṭimicai poruntap poruttiya tayavuṭaip puṇṇiyap poruḷē taṉṉiyal aṟivaruñ cattiya nilaiyē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O my life! O life of my sweet life! O my knowing! O knowing of my knowing! O ambrosia of my Ambalam, sweeter than a mother! O wonder! O sacred feet! O my love! O blessed substance of grace, who placed your paired golden flower-feet to rest upon my head! O state of truth, whose nature is difficult to grasp! O peerless King of Dance, my gem of a true guru!
commentary: The divine guru is the very essence of one's own self. Vallalar addresses the guru as the "life of my life" and the "knowing of my knowing," indicating a state where the separation between devotee and divine has dissolved. This intimacy, sweeter than a mother's love, is crowned by the highest symbol of blessing and surrender: the guru placing his feet upon the devotee's head.

translit: kāymaṉak kaṭaiyaṉaik kāttameyp poruḷē kalaikaḷuṅ karutarum oruperum patiyē tēymatic camayaruk kariyaoṇ cuṭarē cittelām vallatōr cattiya mutalē āymatip periyaruḷ amarntaciṟ paramē ampalat tāṭalcey cempatat taracē tāymatip pariyatōr tayavuṭaic civamē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O true substance who protected this base one with a hateful mind! O one great master, inconceivable even to the sacred arts! O brilliant flame, inaccessible to followers of the waning-moon religions! O first cause of truth, all-powerful in consciousness! O transcendent consciousness, abiding in the grace of the great ones of discerning intellect! O king with perfect feet, who performs the dance in the Ambalam! O Sivam of great compassion, dearer than a mother’s esteem! O peerless King of Dance, my gem of a true guru!
commentary: The divine teacher’s grace is given freely to the humble, while remaining hidden from those who rely on limited knowledge. Vallalar presents himself as a flawed person who was saved, showing that grace is for those who struggle. This same compassionate being is inaccessible to formal disciplines or narrow religious views, which he calls "waning-moon religions." The true divine reality, Sivam, reveals itself through a compassion greater than a mother’s.

translit: uruvamum aruvamum upayamum uḷatāy uḷatila tāyoḷir orutaṉi mutalē karuviṉil eṉakkaruḷ kaṉintaḷit tavaṉē kaṇṇuṭai yāyperuṅ kaṭavuḷar patiyē tirunilai peṟaeṉai vaḷarkkiṉṟa paramē civakuru turiyattil teḷiaṉu pavamē taruvaḷar poḻivaṭal capainiṟai oḷiyē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O one, peerless first cause, who shines as form, formlessness, and both; as being and non-being! O one who, in the womb, ripened with grace for me and bestowed it! O you who possess eyes! O master of the great gods! O supreme one who is raising me to attain the sacred state! O Siva-Guru! O clear experience in the Turiya state! O light that fills the Hall at Vadalur, a grove of flourishing bounty! O peerless King of Dance, my gem of a true guru!
commentary: The divine is the source of all existence, present as form, as formlessness, and beyond both. Vallalar describes a deeply personal connection to this reality, a grace that nurtured him even in the womb. God acts as the ultimate teacher, or Siva-Guru, guiding the soul to a clear experience in Turiya, a state of pure consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. This divine light is centered in the sacred hall at Vadalur, the physical heart of his mission.

translit: āṟanta nilaikaḷiṉ aṉupava niṟaivē atuatu vāyoḷir potuvuṟu nitiyē kūṟenta nilaikaḷum orunilai eṉavē kūṟieṉ uḷḷattil kulaviya kaḷippē pēṟinta neṟieṉak kāṭṭieṉ taṉaiyē peruneṟik kēṟṟiya oruperum poruḷē cāṟenta nāḷkaḷum viḷaṅkumōr vaṭalvāyt taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: You are the fulfillment of the experience of the six high states, the universal treasure shining as each and every thing. You are the joy that bloomed in my heart after you declared that all proclaimed states are but one state. You are the one great substance who showed me the path of the great end and elevated me to that great path. O peerless Nataraja, my Satguru-jewel, who shines in Vadalur where the sacred essence is ever-present.
commentary: All the various stages of spiritual ascent described in different traditions are fulfilled in one single reality. The greatest joy comes from realizing that these seemingly separate states are all expressions of one divine truth. Vallalar celebrates God as the true spiritual master (Satguru) who revealed this unified "great path" to him, the peerless Nataraja (King of Dance) whose presence makes Vadalur a place of constant spiritual nourishment.

translit: cākāta talaiitu vēkāta kālām taramitu kāṇeṉat tayavucey turaittē pōkāta puṉalaiyum terivitteṉ uḷattē poṟpuṟa amarntatōr aṟputac cuṭarē ākāta pērkaḷuk kākāta niṉaivē ākiya eṉakkeṉṟum ākiya cukamē tākātal eṉattarum tarumacat tiramē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: You graciously declared, "Behold, this is the standard: the deathless head, the un-burning air." You graciously declared, 'Behold, this is the deathless head; this is the unburning air; this is the standard.' You revealed the unwasting water and sat beautifully in my mind, O wondrous flame. You are a thought inaccessible to the unfit, the bliss that has become mine forever, the hall of dharma that gives out of a loving thirst. O peerless Nataraja, my Satguru-jewel.
commentary: The highest spiritual achievement is the physical transformation of the body into an immortal vessel of grace. The "deathless head" and "un-burning air" refer to this state, a body that cannot be harmed by death or decay, which God reveals as the ultimate standard. This truth, a wondrous flame in the mind, is a bliss available only to those who are receptive. God is also like a hall of charity (dharma), giving grace out of boundless, loving compassion.

translit: tattuva macinilai ituitu tāṉē cattiyam kāṇeṉat taṉitturait teṉakkē ettuvan taṉaikaḷum nīkkimeyn nilaikkē ēṟṟināṉ iṟavāta iyalaḷit taruḷāl cittuvan tulakaṅkaḷ evaṟṟiṉum āṭac ceyvitta pēraruṭ civaparañ cuṭarē cattuva neṟitaru vaṭalaruṭ kaṭalē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: Declaring to me alone, "This, this itself is the state of Tat Tvam Asi; behold this truth," you removed all my deceptive attachments, elevated me to the state of truth, and by your grace, granted me the nature of immortality. O supreme flame of Siva, whose great grace made siddhis manifest and perform in all worlds! O ocean of grace in Vadalur that bestows the path of sattva! O peerless Nataraja, my Satguru-jewel.
commentary: Tat Tvam Asi ("That you are") is a famous declaration from Indian philosophy about the identity between the individual and the supreme reality. Here, it is a truth to be directly experienced. This personal realization, given by grace, is what removes illusion, grants immortality, and unlocks siddhis (supernatural powers). It is the fruit of following the path of sattva (purity).

translit: itupati ituporuḷ itucukam aṭaivāy ituvaḻi eṉaeṉak kiyalpuṟa uraittē vituamu toṭuciva amutamum aḷittē mēṉilaik kēṟṟiya meynilaic cuṭarē potunaṭam iṭukiṉṟa puṇṇiyap poruḷē puraiyaṟum uḷattiṭaip poruntiya maruntē catumaṟai muṭikaḷiṉ muṭiyuṟu civamē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: You naturally declared to me, "This is the Lord, this is the substance, this is the bliss, attain it. This is the path." Giving me the moon's ambrosia along with the ambrosia of Siva, you elevated me to the highest state, O flame of the true state. O virtuous being who performs the universal dance! O medicine that settled in my flawless heart! O Siva who is the crown atop the crowns of the four Vedas! O peerless Nataraja, my Satguru-jewel.
commentary: The teacher points directly to the goal and the way, making it breathtakingly simple: "This is it. Attain it." The "ambrosia of the moon" and "ambrosia of Siva" are metaphors for divine grace that elevates the soul. God is described as a healing medicine within the heart and the final truth that even the sacred scriptures, the Vedas, are striving to comprehend.

translit: eṉṉilai ituvuṟu niṉṉilai ituvām irunilai kaḷumoru nilaieṉa aṟivāy muṉṉilai ciṟituṟalitumayal uṟalām muṉṉilai piṉṉilai muḻunilai uḷavām innilai aṟintavaṇ eḻunilai kaṭantē iyaṉilai aṭaikaeṉ ṟiyampiya paramē taṉṉilai ākiya naṉṉilai aracē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O Supreme One, who proclaimed: "This is your state, and this is My state. Know that both states are one. Know that both states are one. Even a little of the state of standing before Me as another is delusion. There is a fore-state, an after-state, and a complete state. Knowing these, transcend the seven states and reach the natural state." O King of the good state which is your very own state! O peerless Nataraja, my Satguru-jewel.
commentary: The teacher declares that the soul's state and God's state are one, and warns that to keep even a little of the sense of God as another, standing before oneself, is delusion. Knowing the before-state, the after-state and the complete state, one is to pass beyond the seven states and arrive at the 'natural state,' a condition of effortless, total union.

translit: kāraṇam itupuri kāriyam itumēl kāraṇa kāriyak karuvitu palavāy āraṇam ākamam ivaivirit turaittē aḷantiṭum nīavai aḷantiṭaṉ makaṉē pūraṇa nilaiaṉu pavamuṟil kaṇamām poḻutiṉil aṟitiep poruḷnilai kaḷumē tāraṇi taṉileṉṟa tayavuṭai aracē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O gracious King, unique King of Dance, my gem of a true guru, you said: “This is the cause, understand. This is the effect. Beyond that, this is the instrument of cause and effect in its many forms. The Āraṇam and Āgamam expand and explain these things, but you who measure them, do not get lost in that measuring, my son. If you experience the state of fullness, you will know the nature of all things in an instant on this earth.”
commentary: The sacred scriptures, the Āraṇam (Vedas) and Āgamam (sacred texts), offer complex maps of reality, detailing cause and effect. The divine teacher gives a clear warning: do not get lost in the map. True understanding comes from a direct experience of pūraṇam (fullness). In that single moment of complete experience, all knowledge dawns at once, making intellectual study unnecessary.

translit: paṉṉeṟic camayaṅkaḷ mataṅkaḷeṉ ṟiṭumōr pavaneṟi ituvarai paraviya titaṉāl cenneṟiaṟintilar iṟantiṟan tulakōr ceṟiiruḷ aṭaintaṉar ātaliṉ iṉinī puṉṉeṟi tavirttoru potuneṟi eṉumvāṉ puttamu taruḷkiṉṟa cuttacaṉ mārkkat taṉṉeṟi celuttuka eṉṟaeṉ aracē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O my King, unique King of Dance, my gem of a true guru, you said: “Until now, the path of worldly existence has spread, known as the many paths of sects and religions. Because of this, the people of the world did not know the true path; they died again and again, reaching dense darkness. Therefore, you must now abandon those wretched paths and guide people onto the singular path of the pure Sanmarkkam, which bestows the celestial new nectar known as the common path.”
commentary: The many conflicting sects and religions have led humanity astray, trapping people in ignorance and the cycle of death and rebirth. God instructs Vallalar to turn from these failed paths. He is to establish the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the pure true path) as a single, common way for everyone, offering a new, life-giving truth that transcends religious division.

translit: aṭiitu muṭiitu naṭunilai itumēl aṭinaṭu muṭiyilā tatuitu makaṉē paṭimicai aṭinaṭu muṭiaṟin taṉaiyē patiaṭi muṭiyilāp paricaiyum aṟivāy ceṭiyaṟa ulakiṉil aruḷneṟi ituvē ceyaluṟa muyaluka eṉṟaciṟ paramē taṭimukil eṉaaruḷ poḻivaṭal aracē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O supreme being of consciousness, O mighty King who showers grace like a thick cloud, unique King of Dance, my gem of a true guru, you said: “This is the base, this is the crown, this is the middle state. Beyond that, this is what has no base, middle, or crown, my son. On this earth, you have known the base, middle, and crown; you will also come to know the nature of the Lord, who is without base, middle, or crown. This is the path of grace that will utterly remove impurities from the world. Strive to make it happen!”
commentary: One must first understand the structured nature of existence, but then move beyond it to know God, who is limitless and without structure. This verse describes a progression: first, you learn about the "base, middle, and crown" of reality, but the ultimate goal is to realize the Lord (Pati), who has no such divisions. This realization is the "path of grace," and Vallalar is commanded to strive to establish it on earth to purify the world.

translit: naṇṇiya mataveṟi palapala avaiyē naṉṟaṟa niṉṟaṉa ceṉṟaṉa cilavē aṇṇiya ulakiṉar aṟikilar neṭunāḷ alaitaru kiṉṟaṉar alaivaṟa makaṉē puṇṇiyam uṟutiru varuḷneṟi ituvē potuneṟi eṉaaṟi vuṟamuya lutinī taṇṇiya amutuṇat tantaṉam eṉṟāy taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O unique King of Dance, my gem of a true guru, you said: “The various religious fanaticisms that took hold have stood devoid of goodness; some have already passed away. People, drawing near to them, have not known the truth and have wandered for a very long time. To end this wandering, my son, you must strive to make them understand that this sacred path of grace, which confers merit, is the common path. We have given you the cool nectar to consume.”
commentary: Divisive religious fanaticism is spiritually bankrupt and has left humanity lost and confused. This verse pronounces such paths as devoid of goodness and already fading. The solution, given by God to Vallalar, is to promote a "common path" of grace. This path is open to all, ends the aimless wandering, and confers true spiritual merit (puṇṇiyam).

translit: añcalai nīoru ciṟitumeṉ makaṉē aruṭperuñ cōtiyai aḷittaṉam uṉakkē tuñciya māntarai eḻuppuka nalamē cūḻntacaṉ mārkkattil celuttuka cukamē viñcuṟa meypporuḷ mēṉilai taṉilē viñcaikaḷ palavuḷa viḷakkuka eṉṟāy tañcameṉ ṟavarkkaruḷ cattiya mutalē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O Primal Truth who bestows grace on those who seek refuge, unique King of Dance, my gem of a true guru, you said: “Do not fear in the slightest, my son. We have given the Great Vast Grace-Light to you alone. Awaken those who have died. Guide them onto the Sanmarkkam, which is filled with goodness, and lead them to bliss. Excel in the high state of the true substance; there are many supernatural powers there. Reveal them.”
commentary: God directly commissions Vallalar for his world-transforming mission, removing all fear. He is given the ArutPerunJothi (the Great Vast Grace-Light) and commanded to perform seemingly impossible feats: to awaken those who have died and to guide all people to the goodness and bliss of the Sanmarkkam. He is also told to demonstrate the viñcaikaḷ (supernatural powers) that arise from realizing the "true substance" (Meypporuḷ), making the divine potential manifest on Earth.

translit: vētattiṉ muṭimicai viḷaṅkumōr viḷakkē meypporuḷ ākama viyaṉmuṭic cuṭarē nātattiṉ muṭinaṭu naṭamiṭum oḷiyē navaiaṟum uḷattiṭai naṇṇiya nalamē ētattiṉ niṉṟeṉai eṭuttaruḷ nilaikkē ēṟṟiya karuṇaieṉ iṉṉuyirt tuṇaiyē tātuṟṟa uṭampaḻi yāvakai purintāy taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O singular lamp shining atop the crown of the Vedas! O flame on the vast crown of the Agamas of true substance! O light that dances at the center of the crown of Nada! O goodness that has reached my flawless heart! O compassionate one, companion to my sweet life, who lifted me from ruin and elevated me to a state of grace! You made it so this body, composed of elements, will not perish. O unique Nataraja, my true guru-gem!
commentary: Vallalar praises God as the single light of truth that shines at the heart of all scriptures, like the Vedas and Agamas, and as the inner vibration of Nada (primordial sound). He then makes a personal and striking statement: this same divine compassion has transformed his physical body, making it immortal.

translit: cantira cūriyar oḷipeṟa viḷaṅkum taṉiaruṭ peruveḷit talatteḻuñ cuṭarē vantira viṭaieṉak karuḷamu taḷittē vāḻkaeṉ ṟaruḷiya vāḻmutaṟ poruḷē mantira mēeṉai vaḷarkkiṉṟa maruntē mānilat tiṭaieṉai varuvitta patiyē tantiram yāvaiyum uṭaiyameyp poruḷē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O flame that rises from the expanse of the unique, great space of grace, shining so the sun and moon receive their light! O primal substance of life who came in the night, gave me the ambrosia of grace, and blessed me, saying 'Live long'! O mantra, O medicine that nurtures me! O Master who brought me into this great world! O true substance that possesses all sacred techniques! O unique King of Dance, my true guru-gem!
commentary: God is a personal, nurturing force. Vallalar calls God the source of light for the cosmos, the ambrosia that grants him life, and even the sacred formula (mantra) and medicine that sustain him.

translit: amararum muṉivarum aticayit tiṭavē aruṭperuñ cōtiyai aṉpuṭaṉ aḷittē kamamuṟu civaneṟik kēṟṟieṉ ṟaṉaiyē kātteṉa tuḷattiṉil kalantameyp patiyē emaṉeṉum avaṉiṉi ilaiilai makaṉē eyppaṟa vāḻkaeṉ ṟiyampiya aracē camaraca caṉmārkka caṅkattiṉ mutalē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: So that even celestials and sages were wonderstruck, you lovingly bestowed the Vast Grace-Light. You elevated me onto the fragrant path of Siva, O true Master who protected me and mingled in my heart! O King who declared, "The one called Yama is no more, no more, my son! Live without weariness!" O head of the Samarasa Sanmarkka Sangam! O unique King of Dance, my true guru-gem!
commentary: This verse makes a startling declaration: death has been conquered. God has given Vallalar the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi) and assured him that Yama, the god of death, no longer has power. This victory over death is the central promise of the Samarasa Sanmarkka Sangam (Association for the True Path of Universal Harmony).

translit: naṉmārkkat tavaruḷam naṇṇiya varamē naṭuveḷi naṭuniṉṟu naṭañceyum paramē tuṉmārkka vātikaḷ peṟaṟkaru nilaiyē cuttaci vāṉantap puttamu tuvappē eṉmārkkam eṉakkaḷit teṉaiyumēl ēṟṟi iṟavāta perunalam īntameyp poruḷē caṉmārkka caṅkattār taḻuviya patiyē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O boon that reaches the hearts of those on the good path! O supreme one who stands and dances in the center of the central space! O state unattainable by those who argue for the evil path! O bliss of pure Sivananda, O fresh ambrosia! O true substance who gave me my own path, elevated me, and granted the great goodness of immortality! O Master embraced by the people of the Sanmarkka Sangam! O unique King of Dance, my true guru-gem!
commentary: The divine state is accessible to those on the good path but impossible for those who cling to negativity and argument. Vallalar affirms that God gave him a unique path, the Sanmarkkam, which leads to the "great goodness of immortality" and is now embraced by his followers.

translit: ātiyum antamum iṉṟioṉ ṟāki akampuṟam akappuṟam puṟappuṟam niṟaintē ōtiyum uṇarntumiṅ kaṟivarum poruḷē uḷaṅkoḷciṟ capainaṭu viḷaṅkumeyp patiyē cōtiyum cōtiyiṉ mutaluntāṉ ākic cūḻnteṉai vaḷarkkiṉṟa cutantara amutē cātiyum camayamum tavirttavar uṟavē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O substance without beginning or end, filling the inside, outside, the inner-outside, and the outer-outside, difficult to know here by study or by feeling! O true Master shining in the center of the Chit Sabhai that captivates the heart! O independent ambrosia that, being both the light and the origin of the light, surrounds and nurtures me! O kinsman to those who have shed caste and religion! O unique King of Dance, my true guru-gem!
commentary: True spirituality transcends conventional religious identity and intellectual knowledge. God is both the vast, unknowable substance filling all existence and an immediate, nurturing light experienced in the inner Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness). God is the very kinsman of those who have cast off caste and religion: whoever lets these divisions go finds God as their own family.

translit: kaṟpaṉai muḻuvatum kaṭantavar uḷattē kalantukoṇ ṭiṉikkiṉṟa kaṟpakak kaṉiyē aṟpaṉai yāṇṭukoṇ ṭaṟivaḷit taḻiyā aruḷnilai taṉiluṟa aruḷiya amutē paṟpala ulakamum viyappaeṉ taṉakkē patamalar muṭimicaip patittameyp patiyē taṟpara parampara citampara nitiyē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O Kalpaga fruit, sweetening and mingling in the hearts of those who have completely transcended imagination! O Amudam who ruled over this wretched one, gave me knowledge, and graciously allowed me to attain the imperishable state of grace! O true Lord who, to the astonishment of many worlds, placed your flower-like feet upon my head, for me alone! O treasure of Chidambaram, the Supreme Beyond, the Beyond of the Beyond! O singular Nataraja, my jewel of a Satguru!
commentary: The experience of grace is deeply personal and changes everything. The poet sees himself as wretched and unworthy, yet God, like a celestial Kalpaga (wish-fulfilling tree), bestows upon him the Amudam (nectar of immortality) and an unshakable state of grace. This intimate blessing, symbolized by the Master placing his feet on the devotee's head, makes the true master (Satguru) the devotee's most precious treasure.

translit: pavaneṟi celumavar kaṉavilum aṟiyāp paramporu ḷākieṉ uḷampeṟum oḷiyē navaneṟi kaṭantatōr ñāṉameyc cukamē nāṉaruḷ nilaipeṟa nalkiya nalamē civaneṟi yēciva neṟitaru nilaiyē civanilai taṉiluṟum aṉupava niṟaivē tavaneṟi celumavark kiṉiyanal tuṇaiyē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O Light that fills my heart, the Supreme Being unknown even in the dreams of those on the path of worldly existence! O true bliss of wisdom that has transcended the nine paths! O goodness that granted me the attainment of the state of grace! O path of Siva itself! O state that grants the path of Siva! O fullness of experience found in the state of Siva! O sweet, good companion to those who walk the path of tapas! O singular Nataraja, my jewel of a Satguru!
commentary: The experience of God is both the way and the destination. The path of Siva, the state of Siva, and the realization of Siva are all one. This state of blissful wisdom transcends all conventional religious systems and is the reward for sincere spiritual discipline (tapas), while remaining completely unimaginable to those absorbed in worldly pursuits.

translit: aṟiyāmal aṟikiṉṟa aṟiviṉuḷ aṟivē aṭaiyāmal aṭaikiṉṟa aṭaiviṉuḷ aṭaivē ceṟiyāmal ceṟikiṉṟa ceṟiviṉuṭ ceṟivē tiḷaiyāmal tiḷaikkiṉṟa tiḷaippuṟu tiḷaippē piriyāmal eṉṉuḷam kalantameyk kalappē piṟavāmal iṟavāmal eṉaivaitta perukkē taṟiyāki uṇarvārum uṇarvarum poruḷē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O awareness within the awareness that knows without the process of knowing! O attainment within the attainment that is reached without the process of reaching! O intimacy within the intimacy that is present without constriction! O bliss within the bliss that is experienced without effort! O true union that merged inseparably with my heart! O vastness that has kept me from birth and death! O substance, difficult to grasp even for those who perceive you with fixed concentration! O singular Nataraja, my jewel of a Satguru!
commentary: The ultimate state of awareness is one of effortless being, beyond the mind's usual processes. Vallalar describes it through a series of paradoxes: knowing without trying to know, arriving without striving to reach, and experiencing bliss without effort. This is the true union with God, a state of inseparable oneness that frees one from the cycle of birth and death.

translit: karutāmal karutumōr karuttiṉuṭ karuttē kāṇāmal kāṇumōr kāṭciyiṉ viḷaivē erutākat tirintēṉuk kikaparam aḷittē iṟavāta varamuntan taruḷiya oḷiyē varutākan tavirttiṭa vantateḷ ḷamutē māṇikka malainaṭu maruviya paramē tarutāṉa muṇaveṉac cāṟṟiya patiyē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O idea within the idea that is conceived without thinking! O fruit of the vision that is seen without seeing! O Light who, for me who wandered like an ox, gave this world and the next and granted the boon of deathlessness! O clear Amudam who came to quench my burning thirst! O Supreme One dwelling amidst the ruby mountain! O Lord who proclaimed that the gift to give is food! O singular Nataraja, my jewel of a Satguru!
commentary: Divine grace can transform a life of aimless wandering into one of true purpose and eternal life. Vallalar praises the Light that quenched his spiritual thirst with Amudam (the nectar of immortality) and granted him the boon of deathlessness. In the midst of this praise he states the heart of Jeevakarunyam: God taught him that the gift to give is food, given to the hungry.

translit: ēkāa ṉēkāeṉ ṟēttiṭu maṟaikkē eṭṭāta nilaiyēnāṉ eṭṭiya malaiyē ōkāḷa mataṅkaḷai muḻuvatum māṟṟi orunilai ākkaeṉ ṟuraittameyp paramē īkātal uṭaiyavark kiruniti aḷittē iṉpuṟap purikiṉṟa iyalpuṭai iṟaiyē cākāta varantantiṅ keṉaikkātta aracē taṉinaṭa rājaeṉ caṟkuru maṇiyē.
translation: O state unattainable to the Vedas that praise you as “One and Many,” yet you are the mountain I have scaled! O true Supreme Being who instructed, 'Completely transform all the nauseating religions and make them into one state'! O Lord whose nature it is to grant the two great treasures to those who love to give, making them rejoice! O King who protected me here by giving me the boon of deathlessness! O singular Nataraja, my jewel of a Satguru!
commentary: The ultimate reality is a direct experience that goes beyond even the most sacred scriptures like the Vedas. Vallalar describes receiving a divine instruction to transform the world's competing religions into a single, unified state of being. This path is rooted in the joy of giving, and it leads to the ultimate boon: a deathless life protected by grace.
NOTES
Note 246

tamil: சிறிதுற - பி. இரா.பதிப்பு. சிறிதுறில் - படிவேறுபாடு. ஆ. பா.

translation: ciṟituṟa — reading of the P. Irā. edition. ciṟituṟil — variant reading. Ā. Pā. edition.
Note 247

tamil: சென்னெறி - முதற்பதிப்பு, பொ.,சு., பி. இரா., ச. மு. க.
translit: ceṉṉeṟi - mutaṟpatippu, po.,cu., pi. irā., ca. mu. ka.
translation: ceṉṉeṟi — reading of the first edition, and of the Po. Su., P. Irā., and S. Mu. Ka. Editions.

translit: tiruvaḷarpē raruḷuṭaiyāṉ ciṟcapaiyāṉ ellām ceyyavalla taṉittalaimaic cittaṉellām uṭaiyāṉ uruvamumāy aruvamumāy upayamumāy alavāy ōṅkum aruṭperuñjōti oruvaṉuṇṭē avaṉṟāṉ perumaiyiṉāl eṉaiyīṉṟāṉ nāṉoruvaṉ tāṉē piḷḷaiavaṉ piḷḷaieṉap periyarelām aṟivār irumaiyuṟu tattuvarkāḷ eṉṉaiaṟi yīrō īṅkumatu tuḷḷalelām ētumnaṭa vātē.
translation: The one who possesses great, flourishing grace, he of the hall of consciousness, the Siddhan with sole authority to do everything, who possesses all, that unique One exists. He is form, formless, both, and beyond them: the exalted ArutPerunJothi. Out of his greatness, he fathered me. I am his only child; all the great ones know I am his son. O you tattvas of duality, do you not know me? All your frantic leaping will accomplish nothing here.
commentary: A person who has realized their true self is no longer a subject of the universe but its master. The tattvas are the basic building blocks of reality, the very principles of mind and matter that create our experience of a world of difference and separation. Vallalar declares that his identity as the "son" of God, the singular Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), places him above their influence. He addresses them directly, announcing that their power over him is finished.

translit: maṉameṉumōr pēykkuraṅku maṭaippayalē nītāṉ maṟṟavarpōl eṉainiṉaittu maruṭṭātē kaṇṭāy iṉamuṟaeṉ colvaḻiyē iruttiyeṉil cukamāy iruntiṭunī eṉcolvaḻi ēṟṟilaiā ṉālō tiṉaiyaḷavuṉ atikāram cellavoṭṭēṉ ulakam cirikka:uṉai aṭakkiṭuvēṉ tiruvaruḷāl kaṇattē naṉavileṉai aṟiyāyō yāreṉa:iṅ kiruntāy ñāṉacapait talaivaṉukku nallapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O idiotic boy, you demonic monkey called mind! Do not think of me as you do others and try to delude me, you hear me. If you agreeably follow my words, you will live in peace. But if you do not accept my words, I will not let you wield even a millet-seed’s worth of authority. By divine grace, I will subdue you in an instant, making the world laugh. In your waking state, do you not know me? Who did you think you were dealing with? I am the favored son of the Lord of the hall of wisdom.
commentary: The mind, often seen as the source of our identity, is here demoted to a "demonic monkey" or a disobedient child. This striking reversal shows a complete shift in inner authority. The speaker is no longer a victim of his own thoughts, but their master. He can command the mind to be still, and this command is backed by divine grace, the power of the Lord of the hall of wisdom (Jnana Sabai).

translit: paṉmukañcēr maṉameṉumōr pariyācap payalē pataiyātē citaiyātē pārkkumiṭam ellām koṉmukaṅkoṇ ṭaṭikkaṭipōyk kutiyātē eṉatu kuṟippiṉvaḻi niṉṟiṭuniṉ kutippunaṭa vātu eṉmuṉamōr puṉmuṉaimēl iruntapaṉit tuḷinī immeṉummuṉ aṭakkiṭuvēṉ eṉṉaiaṟi yāyō piṉmuṉeṉa niṉaiyēlkāṇ ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkum periyataṉit talaivaṉukkup periyapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O mocking boy, you many-faced mind! Do not be agitated, do not fall apart. Do not go leaping about everywhere, again and again, with a vacant expression. Abide by my intention; your leaping will not work. Before me, you are a dewdrop on the tip of a blade of grass. I will subdue you in a flash. Do you not know me? Do not think in terms of ‘before’ and ‘after’, you see. I am the great son of the great, unique Lord who dances in the hall of consciousness.
commentary: From the viewpoint of the realized self, the endlessly restless mind is revealed to be fragile and powerless. Though it seems to leap about creating constant distraction, its substance is as fleeting as a dewdrop on a blade of grass. The authority to command the mind comes from a direct connection to the divine, here called the unique Lord who dances in the hall of consciousness (Chit Sabhai), the living, intelligent center of all existence.

translit: virintamaṉam eṉumciṟiya viḷaiyāṭṭup payalē virintuvirin talaiyātē meliyātē viṭayam purintaneṟi purintavamē pōkātē poṟivāyp puraiyātē viraiyātē pukuntumayaṅ kātē terintuteḷin torunilaiyil cittirampōl irunī ciṟitacaintāl akkaṇamē citaittiṭuvēṉ kaṇṭāy parinteṉainī yāreṉṟu pārttāyciṟ capaivāḻ patitaṉakkē aruṭpaṭṭam palittapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O little playful boy called the ‘expansive mind’! Do not wander about, expanding endlessly. Do not grow weak. Do not go to waste on the path of sense objects. Do not enter the gateways of the senses, do not rush, do not get caught up and become deluded. Know, become clear, and remain in one state like a painting. If you stir in the slightest, I will destroy you that very instant, you see. Have you looked closely to see who I am? I am the son for whom the coronation of grace from the very Lord who dwells in the hall of consciousness has come to fruition.
commentary: The final command to the mind is to become perfectly still. All its tendencies to wander outward toward sense experiences must cease. The ideal state is to be fixed and unmoving, "like a painting." This state is imposed by the authority of the soul. This authority is absolute because it is a divine right, granted through a "coronation of grace" from God himself.

translit: pāymaṉameṉ ṟuraittiṭumōr parāymuruṭṭup payalē palpoṟiyām paṭukkāḷip payalkaḷoṭum kūṭic cēymaiyiṉum aṇmaiyiṉum tirintōṭi āṭit tiyaṅkātē oruvārttai tiruvārttai eṉṟē āyvuṟakkoṇ ṭaṭaṅkukanī aṭaṅkilaiyēl uṉaittāṉ aṭiyoṭuvēr aṟuttiṭuvēṉ āṇaiaruḷ āṇai pēymatiyā nīeṉaittāṉ aṟiyāyō ellām peṟṟavaṉtaṉ celvākkup peṟṟapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O coarse, stubborn boy called the ‘leaping mind’! Do not join with those lazy bums, the various senses, to wander, run, and play both far and near, becoming bewildered. Take the one word as the sacred word, analyze it, and be still. If you are not still, I will cut you out root and stem. I swear by grace, this is my oath! O you of demonic intellect! Do you not know me? I am the son who has received the influence of the One who possesses all.
commentary: Here, the mind and the senses are portrayed as a gang of unruly troublemakers. To quiet them, Vallalar gives a specific instruction: focus on "the one word," likely a sacred name or concept, and become still. The tone is severe; if the mind refuses, he vows to rip it out "root and stem." This forceful language shows that mastering the mind is not really a passive wish but an active, and sometimes ruthless, internal battle.

translit: mayaṅkuputti eṉumulaka vaḻakkāḷip payalē vaḻituṟaiyī teṉṟaṟiyāy vakaiciṟitum aṟiyāy uyaṅkivicā rittiṭavē ōṭukiṉṟāy uṇarum uḷavaṟiyāy vīṇuḻaippiṅ kuḻaippatileṉ payaṉō vayaṅkumaṉam aṭaṅkiyavā ṟaṭaṅkukanī ilaiyēl maṭittiṭuvēṉ kaṇattiluṉai vāymaiitu kaṇṭāy iyaṅkaeṉṉai aṟiyāyō yāreṉaeṇ ṇiṉaiyō ellāñcey vallavaṉuk kiṉiyapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O confused intellect, you worldly litigant, you rascal! You do not know the path or the way; you know none of the means. You wear yourself out, running around and inquiring. You do not know the secret of realization. What is the use of this worthless toil you perform? Subside, just as the radiant mind has subsided. If you do not, I will destroy you in an instant. This is the truth, understand. Do you not know me, who moves? Who did you think I was? I am the dear child of the One who is all-powerful.
commentary: Now Vallalar addresses the intellect, commonly known as buddhi, the part of the mind that reasons, argues, and gets lost in endless analysis. He calls it a "worldly litigant," a perfect description for the mental chatter that endlessly debates worldly matters without ever finding the true path. This faculty, too, must fall silent. His authority comes from being the "dear child" of the all-powerful creator, a relationship that makes him master of his own inner faculties.

translit: kalaiyaṟiyāc cittameṉum kaṉamōcap payalē kālaṟiyāy talaiaṟiyāy kāṇpaṉakaṇ ṭaṟiyāy nilaiyaṟiyāy oṉṟaioṉṟā niccayittiv vulakai neṟimayaṅka mayakkukiṉṟāy nīyōiṅ kuṟuvāy alaiyaṟiyāk kaṭalpōlē acaivaṟaniṉ ṟiṭunī acaivāyēl akkaṇattē aṭakkiṭuvēṉ uṉaittāṉ alaivaṟivāy eṉṟaṉainī aṟiyāyō nāṉtāṉ āṇṭavaṉtaṉ tāṇṭavaṅkaṇ ṭamarntapiḷḷai kāṇē.
translation: O mind that knows no art, you great deceiving rascal! You know neither the beginning nor the end; you see things but do not truly perceive them. You do not know the stable state. You declare one thing to be another, confusing this world and confounding the path. Will you remain here? Stand motionless, like a wave-free sea. If you move, I will subdue you in that very second. You who know only agitation, do you not know me? See, I am the child who has witnessed the Lord's cosmic dance and am seated in peace.
commentary: Vallalar goes deeper, addressing the faculty of consciousness (cittam) that perceives and interprets the world. He calls it a "deceiver" because it constantly misreads reality, "declaring one thing to be another." The goal is for this consciousness to become as still as a "wave-free sea." His authority to command this stillness comes from direct spiritual experience: he has witnessed God's cosmic dance and is now established in that unshakable peace.

translit: akaṅkāram eṉumpollā aṭavātip payalē aṭukkaṭukkāy eṭukkiṉṟāy aṭuttumuṭuk kiṉṟāy cekaṅkāṇat talaikālum teriyāmal alaintu tirikiṉṟāy niṉcepantāṉ ciṟitumnaṭa vātu ikaṅkāṇa aṭaṅkukanī aṭaṅkāyēl kaṇattē irunta:iṭam teriyātē erintiṭaccey tiṭuvēṉ cukaṅkāṇa niṉṟaṉainī aṟiyāyō nāṉtāṉ cuttaciva caṉmārkkam peṟṟapiḷḷai kāṇē.
translation: O ego, you wicked, stubborn rascal! You rise up again and again; you press on and urge forward. You wander and roam, for all the world to see, completely lost and confused. Your schemes will not succeed in the least. Subside, for this world to witness. If you do not subside, I will, in an instant, make you burn up so that no trace of where you stood remains. You who seek only pleasure, do you not know me? See, I am the child who has received the Pure Siva Sanmarkkam.
commentary: The final confrontation is with the ego (ahaṅkāram), the deep-seated sense of "I." Vallalar calls it a "wicked, stubborn rascal" whose schemes of self-importance will fail. The ultimatum is absolute: subside, or be burned away so completely that not even a memory of it remains. This total effacement of the ego is the goal, and his power to achieve it comes from having received the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, the pure spiritual path to God which he embodies.

translit: māṉeṉumōr cakaccālac ciṟukkiitu kēḷuṉ vañcakakkūt tellāmōr mūṭṭaieṉak kaṭṭi īṉamuṟa niṉtalaimēl ēṟṟeṭuttuk koṇṭuṉ ēvalpuri peṇkaḷoṭē ivviṭamviṭ ṭēkik kāṉaṭaintu karuttaṭaṅkip piḻaittiṭunī ilaiyēl kaṇattiluṉai māyppēṉuṉ kaṇattiṉoṭuṅ kaṇṭāy ēṉeṉainī aṟiyāyō ciṟcapaiyil naṭañcey iṟaivaṉaruṭ peruñjōtik kiṉiyapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O Māṉ (Mahat, the great principle of primal nature), you conniving little wench, listen to this! Bundle up all your treacherous dramas into a single pack, lift it shamefully onto your own head, and along with your serving maids, leave this place. Go to the forest, subdue your intentions, and save yourself. If you do not, I will destroy you and your whole retinue in an instant, you see. Why, do you not know me? I am the dear child of the Grace-Light of the Lord who dances in the hall of consciousness.
commentary: Māṉ, the great principle of primal nature (Mahat), with all her dramas and deceptions, has no place in a life touched by grace. The speaker claims his identity as a child of ArutPerunJothi (the Vast Grace-Light), the ultimate reality dancing in the Chit Sabhai, and this relationship gives him the power to banish her with all her retinue.

translit: māyaieṉum paṭutiruṭṭuc ciṟukkiitu kēḷuṉ māyaielām cumaicumaiyā varintu kaṭṭik koṇṭuṉ cāyaieṉum peṇiṉattār talaimēlum uṉatu talaimēlum cumantukoṇṭōr cantuvaḻi pārttē pēyeṉakkāṭ ṭiṭaiōṭip piḻaittiṭunī ilaiyēl pēcumuṉṉē māyttiṭuvēṉ piṉṉummuṉṉum pārēṉ āyeṉainī aṟiyāyō ellāñcey vallār aruḷamutuṇ ṭaruḷnilaimēl amarntapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O Māyai, you vile, thieving wench, listen to this! Gather and bind all your illusions into bundle after bundle. Load them onto your head and the heads of your shadowy female kin, find a back alley, and run like a demon into the forest to save yourself. If you do not, I will destroy you before you can speak; I will not hesitate for a moment. Inquiring one, do you not know me? I am the child who has drunk the grace-nectar of the all-powerful Lord and is seated in the state of grace.
commentary: The power of illusion (Māyai) dissolves when one is filled with divine grace. The speaker has drunk the nectar of grace (aruḷ amutu) and is now established in a state where illusion has no power. From this unshakable position, the speaker can command Māyai and its shadowy deceptions to vanish without a moment's hesitation.

translit: māmāyai eṉumperiya vañcakinī itukēḷ varainta:uṉtaṉ paricaṉappeṇ vakaitokaikaḷ uṭaṉē pōmāṟuṉ ceyalaṉaittum pūraṇamāk koṇṭu pōṉavaḻi teriyātē pōypiḻainī ilaiyēl cāmāṟuṉ taṉaiiṉṟē cāyttiṭuvēṉ itutāṉ cattiyameṉ ṟeṇṇutieṉ taṉṉaiaṟi yāyō āmāṟu ciṟcapaiyil aruḷnaṭaṉam purivār aruḷamutuṇ ṭaruḷnilaimēl amarntapiḷḷai kāṇē.
translation: You great cheat called Maamaayai, listen to this. At once, take your designated retinue of women, your varieties and numbers, and go away completely. Go somewhere untraceable and save yourself. If not, I will strike you down to your death this very day. Consider this the truth. Do you not know me? Behold, I am the child seated upon the state of grace, having drunk the nectar of grace from the one who performs the dance of grace in the Chit Sabhai.
commentary: Even the most profound forms of cosmic illusion (Maamaayai) and her assistants are powerless against a soul established in grace. This verse emphasizes the finality of the speaker's spiritual victory. By partaking of God's own grace in the Chit Sabhai, the speaker has attained a permanent state of being that is beyond the reach of any illusion.

translit: kaṉmameṉum peruñcilukuk kaṭuṅkalakap payalē kaṅkukarai kāṇāta kaṭalpōlē viṉaikaḷ naṉmaiyoṭu tīmaieṉap palavikaṟpaṅ kāṭṭi naṭattiṉainiṉ naṭattaielām ciṟitumnaṭa vātu eṉmuṉirun taṉaieṉilnī aḻintiṭuvāy ataṉāl ikkaṇattē niṉiṉattō ṭēkukanī ilaiyēl iṉmaiyuṟa māyttiṭuvēṉ eṉṉaiyaṟi yāyō ellāñcey vallavaṉuk kiṉiyapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: You harsh, rebellious rogue from the great, troublesome family called Kanmam! Like a shoreless sea, you presented deeds with many distinctions, such as good and evil, and carried on. None of your conduct will now succeed in the slightest. If you remain before me, you will be destroyed. Therefore, leave this very instant with your kin. If not, I will destroy you into non-existence. Do you not know me? I am the dear child of the all-powerful one who accomplishes everything.
commentary: The law of karma (Kanmam), with its endless cycle of good and bad deeds, loses its hold on a soul devoted to God. Karma is the force that traps beings in action and consequence, like a vast ocean. By becoming a "dear child" of the all-powerful Lord, the speaker has moved beyond karma's domain and can command it to cease.

translit: ettuṇaiyum kāṭṭāta āṇavameṉ ṟiṭumōr iruṭṭaṟaikkōr atikārak kuruṭṭumuṭap payalē ittaṉaināḷ piṭittatuṉaik kaṇṭuturat tiṭavē iṉṉumaraik kaṇantariyēṉ ikkaṇattē niṉatu pottiyacuṟ ṟattuṭaṉē pōyviṭuti ilaiyēl pūraṇamey aruḷoḷiyāl poṉṟuvippēṉ niṉaiyē cattiyañcoṉ ṉēṉeṉainī aṟiyāyō ñāṉa capaittalaivaṉ tarutalaimait taṉippiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: You blind, crippled rogue, master of a dark room called Aanavam that shows nothing at all! I have finally caught you today to chase you away. I will not tolerate you for even half a moment more. At this instant, depart with your hidden kin. If not, I will make you perish by the perfect, true light of grace. I have spoken the truth. Do you not know me? I am the sole child granted supremacy by the Lord of the Gnana Sabai.
commentary: The final battle is with Aanavam (ego), the core impurity that creates the sense of a separate self. The ego is described as the blind, crippled master of a dark room because it cuts the soul off from the light of God. Empowered by the Lord of the Gnana Sabai (hall of wisdom), the speaker asserts his total authority over the ego, ordering it to vanish or be destroyed by the light of grace.

translit: perumāyai eṉṉumoru peṇpiḷḷai nītāṉ peṟṟavuṭam pitucākāc cuttavuṭam pākki oruñāṉat tiruvamutuṇ ṭōṅkukiṉṟēṉ iṉiniṉ upakarippōr aṇuttuṇaiyum uḷattiṭaināṉ virumpēṉ aruḷāya jōtieṉak kupakarikkiṉ ṟatunī aṟiyāyō eṉṉaḷavil amaikaayal amarka teruḷāya ulakiṭaieṉ caritamuṇarn tilaiyō ciṟcapaieṉ appaṉukkuc ciṟantapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: You are a girl called great illusion. The body you gave, I am making into a deathless, pure body and thriving by drinking the sacred nectar of wisdom. Henceforth, I desire in my heart not even an atom of help from your supporters. The Jothi of grace assists me. Do you not know? With me, stay within your bounds. Stay elsewhere. In this world of clarity, have you not heard my story? I am the cherished child of my father of the Chit Sabhai.
commentary: The body itself is seen as a product of 'great illusion.' But instead of simply being a limitation, the speaker is actively transforming it into a deathless, pure form. He no longer needs any support from the material world, because the Jothi (divine light) of grace is now his sole sustainer. His identity is rooted in his connection to God in the Chit Sabhai, not in the physical world created by illusion.

translit: pēcutirō tāyieṉum peṇmaṭavāy itukēḷ piṉmuṉaṟi yāteṉainī eṉmuṉmaṟaik kātē vēcaṟamā mala:iravu muḻutumviṭin tatukāṇ vīcumaruṭ peruñjōti viḷaṅkukiṉṟa taṟinī ēcuṟuniṉ ceyalaṉaittum eṉṉaḷavil naṭavā titaiaṟintu virainteṉaiviṭ ṭēkuka:ik kaṇattē mācaṟumeṉ caritamoṉṟum terintilaiyō ellām vallaoru cittarukkē nallapiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: You foolish woman called Tirodhayi, listen to this. You who know neither before nor after, do not obscure me from myself. Behold, the great, wearying night of the primal malam has completely dawned. Know that the spreading, great Jothi of grace is now shining. None of your despicable actions will succeed with me. Understand this and leave me quickly, this very instant. Have you not learned anything of my flawless story? I am the good child of the one Siddhar who is capable of all things.
commentary: The speaker now addresses Tirodhayi, a specific divine power that veils or conceals truth from the soul. He commands this cosmic force to stop its work. The long night of malam (primal impurity) is over, and the divine Jothi (light) has dawned. He asserts his new status as the child of the supreme Siddhar (a perfected being), a state in which spiritual concealment has no more power.

translit: tūkkameṉum kaṭaippayalē cōmpēṟi itukēḷ tuṇintuṉatu cuṟṟamoṭu collumaraik kaṇattē tākkuperuṅ kāṭṭakattē ēkukanī iruntāl tappātuṉ talaipōkum cattiyamī taṟivāy ēkkamelām tavirttuviṭṭēṉ ākkamelām peṟṟēṉ iṉpamuṟu kiṉṟēṉnī eṉṉaiaṭai yātē pōkkilvirain tōṭukanī poṟcapaiciṟ capaivāḻ pūraṇarkkiṅ kaṉpāṉa poruḷaṉeṉa aṟintē.
translation: O sleep, you lowly scoundrel! O lazy one, listen to this! In the half-moment I say this, you must decisively take your kin and go into a vast, dense forest. If you stay, your head will surely be lost. Know that this is the truth. I have cast off all yearning and received all that is good. I am blissful, so do not approach me. Flee quickly on your way, knowing that I am the one cherished by the Absolute Lord who dwells in the Golden Halland the Hall of Consciousness.
commentary: Having commanded the great cosmic forces of illusion and karma to depart, he now turns to the ordinary experiences of sleep and laziness. These too are seen as forms of darkness and inertia that have no place in a life of supreme, conscious bliss. His new identity is tied to the Lord of the Poṟsabai (Golden Hall) and Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness), divine spaces of pure awareness where unconsciousness cannot enter.

translit: payameṉumōr koṭumpāvip payalēnī itukēḷ paṟṟaṟaeṉ taṉaiviṭuttup paṉikkaṭalvīḻn toḷippāy tayaviṉurait tēṉiṉṉum iruttieṉil uṉatu taṉṟalaikkut tīmpuvarum talaimaṭṭō niṉatu ceyaluṟumuḷ uṭampaḻiyum cuṟṟamelām iṟakkum tīrntatiṉi illaieṉṟē tiruvārttai piṟakkum ayaliṭainērn tōṭukanī eṉṉaiaṟi yāyō ampalatteṉ appaṉaruḷ nampupiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O fear, you terrible, sinful scoundrel, listen to this! Leave me completely and hide yourself by falling into the icy sea. I have told you this out of kindness. If you still remain, harm will come to your head. And more than your head: your inner, active body will be destroyed, and all your kin will die. The sacred word will be uttered that you are finished, with nothing left. Flee to some other place. Do you not know me? I am the child who trusts in the grace of my Father of the sacred expanse.
commentary: Here, Vallalar commands fear to leave him completely. His warning is a statement of power: he is so full of divine grace that negative forces like fear cannot survive in his presence and will be utterly destroyed. His confidence is rooted in his relationship with God, whom he calls his Father dwelling in the sacred inner expanse, the Ambalam.

translit: kōpameṉum pulaippayalē kāmavalaip payalē koṭumōkak kaṭaippayalē kuṟumpumatap payalē tāpa:ulō pappayalē māṟcariyap payalē tayavuṭaṉiṅ kicaikkiṉṟēṉ tāḻntirukkā tīrkāṇ tīpamelām kaṭantiruḷcēr nilañcārap pōvīr ciṟitupoḻu tiruntālum tiṇṇamiṅkē aḻivīr cāpamuṟā muṉṉamaṟin tōṭumiṉō eṉṉait tāṉaṟiyīr taṉittalaivaṉ talaippiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O anger, you vile, base thing! O lust, you ensnaring scoundrel! O cruel delusion, you lowly scoundrel! O mischievous arrogance, you scoundrel! O greed that brings suffering, you scoundrel! O jealousy, you scoundrel! I am telling you this with kindness, so do not linger here. Go to the land of darkness that lies beyond all light. If you stay even for a moment, you will surely be destroyed here. Understand this and flee before you are cursed! You do not know me. I am the firstborn child of the one, peerless Lord.
commentary: Vallalar bundles together the classic vices of anger, lust, delusion, arrogance, greed, and jealousy. He addresses them directly, personifying them as a gang of villains. With a tone of both kind warning and absolute authority, he orders them to flee to the deepest darkness, because they cannot survive in the light of his new reality as the “firstborn” of God.

translit: pacieṉumōr perumpāvip payalētuṉ peṉumōr paṭupāvip payalēā patteṉumpoyp payalē vaciyavattaik kaṭaippayalē taṭaippayalē iṭarām vaṉpayalē nīvīrelām eṉpuṭainil lātīr naciya:umak kuḷamuḷatō ikkaṇattē nīvīr naṭantuvirain tōṭumiṉō nāṭaṟiyā vaṉattē kaciyumaṉat teṉaiaṟiyīr ciṟcapaiyil viḷaṅkum kaṭavuḷmakiḻn taḷittataṉik katirppiḷḷai nāṉē.
translation: O hunger, you great sinful scoundrel! O suffering, you utterly sinful scoundrel! O calamity, you false scoundrel! O state of delusion, you lowly scoundrel! O obstruction, you scoundrel! O cruel hardship, you scoundrel! None of you are to stand beside me. Do you wish to be destroyed? At this very moment, get up and flee into a forest unknown to any nation. You do not know me, one with a melting heart. I am the unique, radiant child, joyfully bestowed by the God who shines in the Hall of Consciousness.
commentary: This verse extends the banishment to the very experiences of suffering: hunger, pain, calamity, and obstruction. These are emotions and the fundamental hardships of mortal life. Vallalar commands them to leave, asserting a state that transcends these basic realities. He attributes this power to his identity as a radiant, beloved child of the God who shines in the Chit Sabhai, the inner Hall of Consciousness.

translit: maraṇameṉum peruntiruṭṭu māpāvip payalē vaiyakamum vāṉakamum maṟṟakamum kaṭantē paraṇamuṟu pēriruṭṭup perunilamum tāṇṭip pacaiaṟanī oḻintiṭuka iṅkiruntāy eṉilō iraṇamuṟa uṉaimuḻutum maṭittiṭuvēṉ itutāṉ eṉṉuṭaiyāṉ aruḷāṇai eṉkurumēl āṇai araṇuṟumeṉ taṉaiviṭuttē ōṭukanī nāṉtāṉ aruṭperuñjō tippatiyai aṭaintapiḷḷai kāṇē.
translation: O death, you great thieving, monstrously sinful scoundrel! Go beyond the earthly world, the celestial world, and all other worlds. Cross even the great land of vast darkness beyond the cosmic vault, and vanish without a trace. If, however, you stay here, I will utterly destroy you, leaving you mangled. This is the command of my Master's grace; it is an oath upon my Guru. Leave me, who am a fortress, and flee. For you see, I am the child who has attained the Lord of the Vast Grace-Light.
commentary: Having banished illusion, negative emotions, and physical suffering, Vallalar now confronts the last fear: death. He personifies it as a master criminal and commands it to vanish forever, threatening its utter destruction if it remains. It is a declaration of his new reality, a state of immortality granted by his attainment of the Lord of ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light.
NOTES
Note 331

tamil: எனவே - சாலையிலுள்ள மூலம். முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு. பி. இரா.
translit: eṉavē - cālaiyiluḷḷa mūlam. mutaṟpatippu., po. cu. pi. irā.
translation: eṉavē — reading of the original manuscript held at the Cālai; also the first edition, Po. Su., P. Irā.
Note 332

tamil: 'தாக்கு' என்றே எல்லாப் படிகளிலும் முதல் அச்சிலும் காண்கிறது. மூலத்தில் இது'தணிந்த' என்பதுபோலும் தெளிவற்றுத் தோன்றுகின்றது. - ஆ. பா.ஆ. பா. மூலத்தில் என்று சொல்வது அடிகள் கையெழுத்து மூலத்தையே. முதற்பதிப்பு.பொ. சு., பி. இரா. ச. மு. க. பதிப்புகளில் தாக்கு என்ற பாடமே காணப்படுகிறது.சாலையில் உள்ள அடிகள் கையெழுத்துப் படியில் 'தணிந்த' என்றே உள்ளது.மிகத் தெளிவாகவும் காணப்படுகிறது.
translit: 'tākku' eṉṟē ellāp paṭikaḷilum mutal accilum kāṇkiṟatu. mūlattil itu 'taṇinta' eṉpatupōlum teḷivaṟṟut tōṉṟukiṉṟatu. - ā. pā. ā. pā. mūlattil eṉṟu colvatu aṭikaḷ kaiyeḻuttu mūlattaiyē. mutaṟpatippu. po. cu., pi. irā. ca. mu. ka. patippukaḷil tākku eṉṟa pāṭamē kāṇappaṭukiṟatu. cālaiyil uḷḷa aṭikaḷ kaiyeḻuttup paṭiyil 'taṇinta' eṉṟē uḷḷatu. mikat teḷivākavum kāṇappaṭukiṟatu.
translation: 'tākku' is what appears in all copies and in the first printing. In the original it appears indistinct, as though 'taṇinta'. — Ā. Pā. What Ā. Pā. calls the original is the manuscript in the Swami's own hand. The first edition and the Po. Su., P. Irā. and S. Mu. Ka. editions all carry the reading tākku. In the Swami's autograph copy held at the Cālai it reads 'taṇinta', and it is perfectly legible there.

translit: maṇampuri kaṭikai iraṇṭarai eṉumōr varaiyuḷa tātalāl makaṉē eṇampurin tuḻalēl cavuḷamā tiyacey teḻiluṟu maṅkalam puṉaintē kuṇampurin tematu makaṉeṉum kuṟippaik kōlattāl kāṭṭuka eṉavē vaṇampuri maṇimā maṉṟileṉ tantai vāymalarn taruḷiṉar makiḻntē.
translation: "My son, because there is a set time of two and a half kadigai for the wedding, do not wander about, lost in thought. Perform the caulam and other preparatory rites, and adorn yourself in beautiful, auspicious attire. Thus, through your appearance, show the sign that you are 'our son'." So my Father spoke graciously and joyfully in the beautiful, gem-adorned great Hall.
commentary: God, speaking as a father to his son, announces that the spiritual "wedding" is imminent, set to occur in just two and a half kadigai (about one hour). The preparations are described using the language of a human wedding, including the caulam (a traditional head-shaving ceremony), which grounds the mystical event in a relatable reality. The command to adorn himself shows that this inner union is also an outward transformation, marking him as belonging to God.

translit: emporuḷ eṉumeṉ aṉpuṭai makaṉē iraṇṭaraik kaṭikaiyil uṉakkē ampuvi vāṉam aṟiyamey aruḷām aṉaṅkaṉaitaṉaimaṇam purivit tumparum viyappa uyarnilai tarutum uṇmaiī tātalāl ulakil vempuṟu tuyartīrn taṇintukoḷ eṉṟār meyppotu naṭattiṟai yavarē.
translation: "My beloved son, who is our very substance, within two and a half kadigai, we will have you marry the formless one who is true grace, for all the beautiful earth and sky to witness. We will grant you the highest state, to the astonishment of the celestials. This is the truth. Therefore, leave behind the world's scorching sorrow and adorn yourself," said the Lord of the Dance in the true, common space.
commentary: The nature of this mystical marriage is revealed: the bride is Anangan, "the formless one," who is the embodiment of true grace. This is union with the formless essence of divinity itself. The result of this union is a state so exalted it will astonish even the celestials. The promise comes from the Lord of the Dance, assuring the devotee that this is the final truth and the end of all sorrow.

translit: aṉpuṭai makaṉē meyyaruḷ tiruvai aṇṭarkaḷ viyappuṟa niṉakkē iṉpuṭai urimai maṇampuri vippām iraṇṭaraik kaṭikaiyil viraintē tuṉpuṭai yavaikaḷ muḻuvatum tavirntē tūymaicēr naṉmaṇak kōlam poṉpuṭai viḷaṅkap puṉaintukoḷ eṉṟār potunaṭam purikiṉṟār tāmē.
translation: "Beloved son, to the astonishment of the denizens of the cosmos, we will quickly perform for you the blissful marriage of rightful union with the Divine Fortune who is true grace, within two and a half kadigai. Having completely abandoned all that brings sorrow, adorn yourself in the pure and fine wedding attire, gleaming with gold," said He who performs the common Dance.
commentary: God again urges his "beloved son" to prepare for the union, this time describing the bride as "the Divine Fortune (Tiru) who is true grace." This emphasizes that the union brings enlightenment and supreme well-being. The preparation requires a complete turning away from sorrow and an embrace of purity, symbolized by the pure and fine wedding attire.

translit: ītukēḷ makaṉē meyyaruḷ tiruvai iraṇṭaraik kaṭikaiyil niṉakkē ūtiyam peṟavē maṇampuri vippām uṇmaiī tātalāl iṉivīṇ pōtupōk kāmal maṅkalak kōlam puṉaintuḷam makiḻkanī eṉṟār tītutīrt teṉṉai iḷantaiyil tāṉē teruṭṭiya ciṟcapai yavarē.
translation: "Hear this, my son. So that you may receive the reward, we will have you marry the Divine Fortune who is true grace within two and a half kadigai. This is the truth. Therefore, from now on, without wasting time, adorn yourself in auspicious attire and rejoice in your heart," said the One from the Chit Sabhai, who dispelled my faults and instructed me even in my youth.
commentary: The "marriage" to grace is now presented as a just "reward" for Vallalar's devotion. He is told to stop wasting time and to feel the joy of this union in his heart immediately. The promise comes from the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness), the divine presence Vallalar recognizes as the source of guidance throughout his life.

translit: viraintukēḷ makaṉē ulakelām kaḷikka meyyaruḷ tiruviṉai niṉakkē varaintunaṉ maṇañcey toruperu nilaiyil vaittuvāḻ vikkiṉṟōm ataṉāl iraintuḷam kavalēl iraṇṭaraik kaṭikai ellaiyuḷ eḻilmaṇak kōlam niraintuṟap puṉaiti eṉṟuvāy malarntār niruttañcey oruttaruḷ uvantē.
translation: "Listen quickly, my son. So that all the worlds may rejoice, we will formally perform your good marriage to the Divine Fortune who is true grace, placing you in a great state and making you flourish. Therefore, do not let your heart clamor with worry. Within the time limit of two and a half kadigai, adorn yourself fully in beautiful wedding attire," so spoke graciously the One who performs the dance, rejoicing within.
commentary: This union is an event that will make "all the worlds rejoice." God reassures him directly, telling him not to worry or be anxious, reinforcing the absolute certainty of the promise. The command is to prepare for a beautiful ceremony that has cosmic significance.

translit: kaḷippoṭu makaṉē aruḷoḷit tiruvaik kaṭikaiōr iraṇṭarai ataṉil oḷippilā tulakam muḻuvatum aṟiya uṉakkunaṉ maṇampuri vippām aḷippuṟu makiḻvāl maṅkalak kōlam aṇipeṟap puṉaikanī viraintē veḷippaṭa uraittām eṉṟaṉar maṉṟil viḷaṅkumeyp poruḷiṟai yavarē.
translation: "My son, with joy, within two and a half kadigais, we will have you properly married to the divine lady of Grace-Light for the whole world to know, without concealment. With abundant joy, quickly adorn yourself beautifully in auspicious wedding attire. We have spoken this openly," said the Lord of True Substance who shines in the cosmic hall.
commentary: God emphasizes that this divine marriage will happen openly, "without concealment," for the whole world to witness. The voice states this plainly to remove any doubt. Vallalar is asked to prepare with abundant joy for a public, undeniable experience of grace.

translit: kalaṅkiṭēl makaṉē aruḷoḷit tiruvaik kaḷippoṭu maṇampuri vippām vilaṅkiṭēl vīṇil pōtupōk kāmal viraintunaṉ maṅkalak kōlam nalaṅkoḷap puṉaintu makiḻka:iv vulakar navilumav vulakavar piṟarum ilaṅkaniṉ maṇamē ēttuvar eṉṟār iyaluṟu ciṟcapai yavarē.
translation: "Do not be distressed, my son. With joy, we will have you married to the divine lady of Grace-Light. Do not obstruct it. Without wasting time in vain, quickly adorn yourself well in auspicious wedding attire and rejoice. The people of this world, the renowned people of that world, and others will all gloriously praise your wedding," said the one of the Circhabai.
commentary: Reassuring Vallalar not to be distressed, the divine voice frames the union as an event that will be celebrated by all beings. People on earth, souls in other realms, and celestial beings will all praise his "wedding" to Grace-Light. The promise comes from the being in the Circhabai (hall of consciousness), confirming that this personal transformation has universal importance.

translit: aiyuṟēl itunam āṇainam makaṉē aruḷoḷit tiruvainiṉ taṉakkē meyyuṟu makiḻvāl maṇampuri vippām viraintiraṇ ṭaraikkaṭi kaiyilē kaiyaṟa vaṉaittum tavirntunī mikavum kaḷippoṭu maṅkalak kōlam vaiyamum vāṉum pukaḻntiṭap puṉaika eṉṟaṉar maṉṟiṟai yavarē.
translation: "Do not doubt, our son, this is our command. We will have you married with true joy to the divine lady of Grace-Light, for you alone. Quickly, within two and a half kadigais, cast off all helplessness and, with great joy, adorn yourself in auspicious wedding attire for the earth and heavens to praise," said the Lord of the cosmic hall.
commentary: God's command is absolute and meant to dispel all doubt. The wedding is for Vallalar, yet it is performed for the earth and heavens to praise, showing that his personal realization has universal significance. This union is a transformation that lights up the world.

translit: tūṅkalai makaṉē eḻukanī viraintē tūyanīr āṭuka tuṇintē pāṅkuṟa ōṅku maṅkalak kōlam paṇpoṭu puṉaintukoḷ kaṭikai īṅkiraṇ ṭaraiyil aruḷoḷit tiruvai eḻiluṟa maṇampuri vippām ēṅkalai itunam āṇaikāṇ eṉṟār iyaṉmaṇi maṉṟiṟai yavarē.
translation: "Do not slumber, my son, rise quickly. Resolutely bathe in pure water. Properly adorn yourself in the fine, auspicious wedding attire.
