Here, within two and a half kadigais, we will have you beautifully married to the divine lady of Grace-Light. Do not languish; see, this is our command," said the Lord of the Manimanram.
commentary: The preparations for the wedding, bathing and dressing in auspicious attire, are symbolic of purification and readiness for the ultimate spiritual state. God's command to "rise" and "not slumber" is a call to awaken fully to the reality of grace. The Manimanram (hall of gems) signifies the luminous, precious nature of the inner space where this divine event occurs.

translit: mayaṅkiṭēl makaṉē aruḷoḷit tiruvai maṇampuri vikkiṉṟām ituvē vayaṅkunal taruṇak kālaikāṇ nīnaṉ maṅkalak kōlamē viḷaṅka iyaṅkoḷap puṉaiti iraṇṭaraik kaṭikai ellaiyuḷ eṉṟuvāy malarntār cayaṅkoḷa eṉakkē taṇṇamu taḷitta tantaiyār ciṟcapai yavarē.
translation: "Do not be bewildered, my son. We are having you married to the divine lady of Grace-Light. See, this is the brilliant, opportune morning. Adorn yourself to shine radiantly in your good wedding attire within the limit of two and a half kadigais." So spoke my Father, the one of the Circhabai, who gave me cool ambrosia that I might attain victory.
commentary: The "opportune morning" signifies that the perfect moment for union has arrived, orchestrated by divine will. Vallalar refers to God as the Father who gave him "cool ambrosia," a metaphor for the grace that grants immortal life and victory over all limitations. This series of verses portrays the final step of spiritual attainment as a lovingly arranged celebration.
NOTES
Note 333

tamil: அங்கனை - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு. பி. இரா., ச. மு. க.
translit: aṅkaṉai - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu. pi. irā., ca. mu. ka.
translation: aṅkaṉai — reading of the first edition, Po. Su., P. Irā., S. Mu. Ka.

translit: aruṭpe runtaṉic cōtiam palattilē naṭikkum poruṭpe runtiru naṭamatu pōṟṟuvīr pulavīr maruṭpe rumpakai nīkkimey vāḻvupeṟ ṟiṭalām teruṭpe rumpatat tāṇaiī taṟimiṉō teḷintē.
translation: O wise ones, praise the great, sacred dance of the Ultimate Substance performed in the Ambalam by the great, unique Jothi of Grace. You can remove the great enemy of delusion and attain the true life. This is the command of the great state of clarity; know this with certainty.
commentary: Vallalar states the path to liberation with utmost simplicity. True life, free from delusion, is attained by praising the "sacred dance" of God. This dance is the ceaseless, living activity of the Divine, experienced as a great, unique Light of Grace (ArutPerunJothi). The Ambalam, or sacred hall, is the inner space of one's own consciousness where this divine reality can be witnessed and praised.

translit: vāram ceytapoṉ maṉṟilē naṭikkumpoṉ aṭikkē āram ceytaṇin tavarkkumuṉ ariayaṉ mutalōr vīram celkilā taṟimiṉō vētamēl āṇai ōram colkilēṉ naṭuniṉṟu colkiṉṟēṉ ulakīr.
translation: Know that before those who have garlanded and adorned themselves with the golden feet that dance with love in the golden hall, the power of Hari, Ayan, and the others does not prevail. This is a command upon the Vedas. O people of the world, I do not speak with bias; I stand in the center and declare this.
commentary: Complete, loving devotion to the dancing feet of God places a person beyond the influence of all other cosmic powers. This is a bold claim, placing the devotee's experience above the authority of even the highest gods of the Hindu pantheon, like Hari (Vishnu) and Ayan (Brahma). Vallalar seals this with an oath upon the Vedas and insists he is not being partisan: he stands in the center and speaks to the whole world.

translit: āti antamum illatōr ampalat tāṭum cōti taṉṉaiyē niṉaimiṉkaḷ cukampeṟa viḻaivīr nīti koṇṭurait tēṉitu nīvīrmēl ēṟum vīti maṟṟaiya vītikaḷ kīḻccelum vīti.
translation: O you who desire to attain bliss, meditate only on the Jothi that dances in the Ambalam which has no beginning or end. I have spoken this with justice. This is the path for you to ascend; all other paths lead downwards.
commentary: There is only one path that leads upward to bliss: meditating on the eternal, dancing Jothi. Vallalar states this without compromise, declaring that all other spiritual or worldly paths ultimately lead downward. He frames this as a matter of cosmic justice (nīti), an inviolable principle, to convey the gravity of the seeker's choice.

translit: nātam colkiṉṟa tirucciṟṟam palattilē naṭikkum pātam colkiṉṟa pattarē nittareṉ ṟaṟimiṉ vētam colkiṉṟa paricitu meymmaiyāṉ pakka vātañ colkilēṉ naṭuniṉṟu colkiṉṟēṉ matittē.
translation: Know that only the devotees who speak of the feet that dance in the sacred Chitrambalam, which is proclaimed by the cosmic sound, are the eternal ones. This is the nature spoken of by the Vedas. Truly, I do not speak from a partial argument; I stand in the center and declare this with discernment.
commentary: True immortality is defined not by birth or creed, but by devotion to the divine reality dancing within the Chitrambalam (the hall of consciousness). This inner space is the source of the Nātham, the primal cosmic sound that underlies all of creation. Again, Vallalar stresses that he is speaking from a central, unbiased position, revealing a universal truth.

translit: turiya mēlpara veḷiyilē cukanaṭam puriyum periya tōraruṭ cōtiyaip peṟutalē evaikkum ariya pēṟumaṟ ṟavaielām eḷiyavē aṟimiṉ uriya immoḻi maṟaimoḻi cattiyam ulakīr.
translation: Attaining the great Jothi of Grace, which performs the dance of bliss in the supreme space above Turiya, is the rarest of all attainments. Know that all other achievements are easy by comparison. O people of the world, this fitting word is the word of the scriptures; it is the truth.
commentary: The single most valuable and difficult of all possible achievements is to realize the great Jothi of Grace. All worldly successes and other spiritual powers are easy to gain by comparison. This ultimate experience occurs in a "supreme space" beyond Turiya, the fourth state of consciousness that already transcends waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, indicating a state of absolute transcendence.

translit: āka māntamum vētattiṉ antamum aṟaiyum pāka māmpara veḷinaṭam paravuvīr ulakīr mōka māntaruk kuraittilēṉ itucukam uṉṉum yōka māntarkkuk kālamuṇ ṭākavē uraittēṉ.
translation: O people of the world, praise the dance in the great supreme space, which is proclaimed by the Āgamas and the essence of the Vedas. I have not spoken of this for people mired in delusion; I have spoken so that the yogic people who contemplate this bliss may have the opportunity.
commentary: Vallalar says his teaching on the divine dance in supreme space is the ultimate essence of all scriptures, including both the Vedas and the Āgamas (texts on ritual and worship). He isn't addressing this to those caught up in worldly attachments, but specifically to sincere seekers who contemplate this bliss, giving them a clear path forward.

translit: vāṉa nāṭarum nāṭarum maṉṟilē vayaṅkum ñāṉa nāṭakak kāṭciyē nāmpeṟal vēṇṭum ūṉa nāṭakak kāṭciyāl kālattai oḻikkum īṉa nāṭakap periyarkāḷ vammiṉō īṇṭē.
translation: We must attain the vision of the drama of wisdom that shines in the Hall, a vision sought even by rulers of heaven and earth. O you great ones who waste your time on the spectacle of flawed physical dramas, come here now.
commentary: The most valuable pursuit is to witness the "drama of wisdom," God's dance in the sacred Hall of consciousness, a sight desired even by celestial beings. Vallalar calls out to those who are wasting their lives on the passing, imperfect spectacles of the physical world to turn their attention here instead.

translit: camayam ōrpala kōṭiyum camayaṅkaḷ tōṟum amaiyum teyvaṅkaḷ aṉantamum ñāṉacaṉ mārkkat temaiyum ummaiyum uṭaiyatōr ampalat tiṟaiyum amaiya āṅkatil naṭampuri patamumeṉ ṟaṟimiṉ.
translation: Know this: the crores of religions, the infinite deities established in each of those religions, are indeed the one Lord of the Hall, who possesses both you and me in the Jñāna Sanmarkkam, and the very foot that fittingly performs the dance there.
commentary: All the countless religions and their many gods are, in truth, just different faces of the one Lord who dances in the sacred Hall. This single God, who is the heart of the Jñāna Sanmarkkam (path of wisdom and goodness), contains everyone, including you and me.

translit: āṟu kōṭiyām camayaṅkaḷ akattiṉum avaimēl vīṟu cērntacit tāntavē tāntanā tāntam tēṟum maṟṟaiya antattum civamoṉṟē aṉṟi vēṟu kaṇṭilēṉ kaṇṭirēl periyarkāḷ viḷampīr.
translation: Within the sixty million religions, and above them in the glorious Siddhānta, Vedānta, Nādānta, and other clear philosophical systems, I have seen nothing other than the one Sivam. O great ones, if you have seen anything different, please declare it.
commentary: After surveying millions of religions and the highest philosophical systems like Siddhānta, Vedānta, and Nādānta, the only ultimate reality is Sivam (the supreme Divine). Vallalar states this as a conclusion based on direct experience, challenging anyone to show him a different truth.

translit: kalaii runtatōr tirucciṟṟam palattilē karuṇai nilaii runtatu niṉaittavai yāvaiyum peṟalām malaii runteṉa iruppirēl vammiṉō aṉṟik kolaivi rumpuvīr eṉiṟpuṟat tēkumiṉ kulaintē.
translation: In the Thiru Chitrambalam (sacred subtle hall) where all arts and sciences reside, grace is firmly established; you can obtain everything you imagine. If you sit immobile like a mountain, come here now. But if you are one who delights in killing, get out, utterly shattered.
commentary: In the Thiru Chitrambalam grace is established, and everything one longs for can be received. The invitation is open to all who will sit firm as a mountain. But the verse draws one line without apology: whoever delights in killing must leave, shattered. Grace and killing cannot stand in the same place.

translit: katii rukkiṉṟa tirucciṟṟam palattilē karuṇai nītii rukkiṉṟa tātalāl nīvīrkaḷ ellām patiya iṅṅaṉē vammiṉō kolaipayil vīrēl vitiyai nōmiṉō pōmiṉō camayavep pakattē.
translation: In Thiru Chitrambalam, where salvation resides, compassionate justice exists. Therefore, all of you, come here firmly. If you practice killing, then blame fate and go away into the feverish exterior of religions.
commentary: Compassionate justice lives in the Thiru Chitrambalam, so Vallalar calls everyone to come and settle there. Again he names the one condition. Those who practice killing can only blame their own fate and go back to the heated outer courts of religion. The door of grace is open to all, but killing closes it from within.

translit: aruḷvi ḷaṅkiya tirucciṟṟam palattilē aḻiyāp poruḷvi ḷaṅkutal kāṇmiṉō kāṇmiṉō puviyīr maruḷu ḷaṅkoḷum vātaṉai tavirntaruḷ valattāl teruḷvi ḷaṅkuvīr ñāṉacaṉ mārkkamē teḷimiṉ.
translation: In Thiru Chitrambalam where grace shines, behold, O people of the earth, behold the imperishable Substance shining! Abandon the affliction of a deluded mind, and by the power of grace, you will shine with clarity. Realize clearly the Gnana Sanmarkkam.
commentary: After the warnings comes the call. Vallalar asks the people of the earth to look and see the imperishable Reality shining in the Thiru Chitrambalam. Let the delusion of the mind fall away, and by the power of grace clarity will shine in you. What he asks them to know clearly has a name: the Sanmarkkam of wisdom (Gnana Sanmarkkam).
NOTES
Note 355

tamil: அமைய அம்பலத்தாடும் பொற்பதமும் என்றறிமின் - முதற்பதிப்பு, பொ. சு., பி. இரா.
translit: amaiya ampalattāṭum poṟpatamum eṉṟaṟimiṉ - mutaṟpatippu, po. cu., pi. irā.
translation: amaiya ampalattāṭum poṟpatamum eṉṟaṟimiṉ — reading of the first edition, Po. Su., P. Irā.

translit: appaṉvaru taruṇamitē aiyamilai kaṇṭāy añcātē añcātē akilamicai uḷḷārk keyppaṟavē cattiyameṉ ṟuraittiṭuniṉ uraikkōr eḷḷaḷavum paḻutuvarā teṉṉiṟaivaṉ āṇai ippuviyō vāṉakamum vāṉakattiṉ puṟattum evvuyirum evvaurum ēttimakiḻn tiṭavē ceppamuṟu tiruvaruṭpē roḷivaṭivāyk kaḷittē cettārai eḻupputalnām tiṇṇamuṇar maṉaṉē.
translation: The time for the Father's arrival is now, see! There is no doubt. Do not fear, do not fear. Declare to everyone in the whole world that this is the truth, so their suffering ends. By my Lord's command, not even the slightest fault will come to your words. Joyfully taking the form of the great light of perfect, sacred grace, so that every life and every being on this earth, in the heavens, and beyond the heavens may praise and rejoice, we will raise the dead. O mind, know this for certain.
commentary: Vallalar tells his own mind not to fear: the time of the Father's coming is now, beyond doubt. He is to declare it to the whole world as truth, so that its suffering may end, and by God's command not a word of it will fail. The promise is stated plainly: taking the form of the great light of grace, we will raise the dead.

translit: iṟaivaṉvaru taruṇamitē iraṇṭilaiañ calai nī eḷḷaḷavum aiyamuṟēl evvulakum kaḷippa niṟaimoḻikoṇ ṭaṟaika:itu paḻutuvarā tiṟaiyum nīvēṟu niṉaittayarēl neñcēnāṉ pukaṉṟa muṟaimoḻieṉ ṉuṭaiyavaṉtāṉ moḻintamoḻi eṉakkōr moḻiilaieṉ uṭalāvi mutalaṉaittum tāṉē poṟaiyuṟakkoṇ ṭaruṭjōti taṉvaṭivum uyirum poruḷumaḷit teṉaittāṉāp puṇarttiyatu kāṇē.
translation: The time of the Lord's arrival is now. There is no doubt; do not fear. Do not have the slightest suspicion. So that all worlds may rejoice, proclaim this with a word of truth. It will not fail in the least. O heart, do not think otherwise and grow weary. The word I have spoken is the very word spoken by my Lord. I have no word of my own. See, He patiently took my body, life, and all I am, and gave me the form, life, and substance of His ArutJothi, uniting with me to make me Himself.
commentary: The word Vallalar speaks is not his own. He says so directly: what he proclaims is the word his Lord has spoken, and he has no word of his own. The reason follows. God took his body, life and all that he is, and gave him in return the form, life and substance of the ArutJothi, uniting with him until he became God's own.

translit: eṉiṟaivaṉ varutaruṇam itukaṇṭāy itaṟkōr eṭṭuṇaiyum aiyamilai eṉṉuḷirun teṉakkē taṉṉaruḷteḷ ḷamutaḷikkum talaivaṉmoḻi itutāṉ cattiyamcat tiyamneñcē caṟṟummayak kaṭaiyēl maṉṉulakat tuyirkaḷelām kaḷittuviyan tiṭavē vakutturaittut terittiṭuka varunāḷuṉ vacattāl uṉṉiurait tiṭamuṭiyā tātaliṉāl iṉṟē uraittiṭutal upakāram uṇarntiṭuka viraintē.
translation: The time of my Lord's arrival is now, see! There is not even an atom's worth of doubt about this. This is the word of the Master who, dwelling within me, gives me the clear ambrosia of His own grace. It is truth, truth, O heart! Do not be confused in the least. So that all lives in this enduring world may rejoice and be amazed, explain it clearly and make it known. Because on the day it comes, you will not be able to think and speak of your own accord, declaring it today itself is a service. Understand this quickly.
commentary: Vallalar speaks to his own heart, urging it to understand that God's arrival is an event happening now. This is a direct message from the divine within. The urgency is practical: he must announce it immediately, because when the divine grace fully descends, the mind will be too overwhelmed with bliss to form words. Declaring it beforehand is a service to others.

translit: ellāñcey vallataṉip peruntalaimaic cittaṉ eṉamaṟaiā kamampukalum eṉiṟaivaṉ makiḻntē nallārkaḷ viyakkaeṉak kicaittapaṭi iṅkē nāṉuṉakku moḻikiṉṟēṉ naṉṟaṟivāy maṉaṉē pallārum kaḷippaṭaiyap pakaliravum tōṟṟāp paṇpiṉaruṭ peruñjōti naṇpiṉoṭu namakkē ellānaṉ maikaḷumuṟa varutaruṇam ituvē ivvulakam uṇarntiṭanī icaittiṭuka viraintē.
translation: O mind, know this well. I am telling you now what my Lord, whom the Vedas and Agamas praise as the unique, great, sovereign Siddhan with the power to do everything, joyfully told me, to the astonishment of the virtuous. The time is now for the ArutPerunJothi, whose nature transcends day and night, to come to us in friendship, so that we may receive all good things. Announce this quickly so that this world may know.
commentary: The coming divine presence is the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light) itself. Vallalar describes this supreme power, praised in the ancient scriptures (Vedas and Agamas), as a Siddhan (a perfected, all-powerful being) who is arriving in a spirit of friendship. The arrival is one of benevolence, bringing "all good things" to humanity.

translit: karunāḷkaḷ attaṉaiyum kaḻintaṉanī ciṟitum kalakkamuṟēl itutoṭaṅkik karuṇainaṭap perumāṉ tarunāḷiv vulakamelām kaḷippaṭaiya namatu cārpiṉaruṭ peruñjōti taḻaittumika viḷaṅkum tirunāḷkaḷ āmitaṟkōr aiyamilai itutāṉ tiṇṇamitai ulakaṟiyat terittiṭuka maṉaṉē varunāḷil uraittiṭalām eṉaniṉaittu mayaṅkēl varunāḷil iṉpamayam ākiniṟai vāyē.
translation: All the dark days are gone; do not be troubled in the least. Beginning from now, these are the days given by the great Lord of the Compassionate Dance. These will be sacred days when, for this whole world to rejoice, the ArutPerunJothi that is with us will flourish and shine brightly. There is no doubt about this; it is certain. O mind, make this known so the world may understand. Do not be deluded by the thought, “I can announce it on a future day.” In the days to come, you will become complete, filled with bliss.
commentary: A great turning point has been reached: the "dark days" of suffering are over. Vallalar declares the start of a new era, a sacred time when the ArutPerunJothi will shine openly for the entire world to see. He again warns his own mind not to delay spreading this news, because the transformation into a state of complete bliss is happening now, not in some distant future.

translit: uḷḷapaṭi uraikkiṉṟēṉ cattiyamām uraiyī tuṇarntiṭuka maṉaṉēnī ulakamelām aṟiya vaḷḷalvaru taruṇamitu taruṇamitē eṉṟu vakutturaittut terittiṭuka mayakkamaṇut tuṇaiyum koḷḷalaieṉ kurunātaṉ aruṭjōtip perumāṉ kuṟippitueṉ kuṟippeṉavum kuṟiyātē kaṇṭāy naḷḷulakil iṉināḷaik kuraittumeṉat tāḻkkēl nāḷaitoṭṭu namakkoḻiyā ñāṉanaṭak kaḷippē.
translation: I am speaking the truth just as it is; this is a true statement. Understand this, O mind! For all the world to know, declare plainly that this is the moment the great Benefactor will come, this very moment. Have not even an atom of confusion. This is the intention of my master-guru, the great Lord of Grace-Jothi; do not think of it as my own intention, you see. In this good world, do not delay, thinking, "I will say it tomorrow." Starting tomorrow, the bliss of the Dance of Wisdom will be unending for us.
commentary: Vallalar stresses that this message is a direct transmission from his divine master, the Lord of ArutJothi (Grace-Light). He commands his heart to announce the Benefactor's arrival without delay, setting an astonishingly specific timeline: "Starting tomorrow." The promised result is an unending state of bliss known as the Gnana Nadam, the divine Dance of Wisdom.

translit: māyaiviṉai āṇavamā malaṅkaḷelām tavirttu vāḻvaḷikkum peruṅkaruṇai vaḷḷalvaru taruṇam mēyatitu vāmitaṟkōr aiyamilai iṅkē viraintulakam aṟintiṭavē viḷampukanī maṉaṉē nāyakaṉṟaṉ kuṟippitueṉ kuṟippeṉanī niṉaiyēl nāḷaikkē viritturaippēm eṉamatittut tāḻkkēl tūyatiru aruṭjōtit tirunaṭaṅkāṇ kiṉṟa tūyatiru nāḷvarunāḷ toṭāṅkioḻi yāvē.
translation: This is the moment the great, compassionate Benefactor comes, who grants life by removing all the great impurities of illusion, karma, and ego. This is it; there is no doubt about it. Here and now, O mind, announce it quickly so the world may know. This is the Lord's intention; do not think it is my own. Do not delay, thinking, "I will explain it in detail tomorrow." The sacred days of witnessing the holy Dance of the pure, divine Grace-Jothi, once they begin, will be unending.
commentary: The arrival of the divine Benefactor has a specific purpose: to grant true life by removing the three fundamental impurities, or malams, that bind the soul. These are māyai (the illusion that veils reality), vinai (the accumulated results of past actions), and āṇavam (the core sense of ego). The coming of grace is an act of purification that makes an unending experience of the divine dance possible.

translit: māṟṟuraikka muṭiyāta tirumēṉip perumāṉ varutaruṇam itukaṇṭāy maṉaṉēnī mayaṅkēl nēṟṟuraittēṉ ilaiuṉakkiṅ kivvāṟeṉ iṟaivaṉ nikaḻttuka:iṉ ṟeṉṟapaṭi nikaḻttukiṉṟēṉ itutāṉ kūṟṟutaitta tiruvaṭimēl āṇaiitu kaṭavuḷ kuṟippeṉakkoṇ ṭulakamelām kutukalikka viraintē cāṟṟiṭuti varunāḷil uraittumeṉat tāḻkkēl taṉittalaivaṉ aruḷnaṭañcey cāṟoḻiyā iṉiyē.
translation: This is the moment the great Lord with a sacred form beyond compare will come; see this, O mind, and do not be confused. I did not say this to you yesterday; I speak today just as my Lord commanded me, "Speak now." This is an oath upon the sacred feet that kicked Death. Taking this as God's intention, quickly proclaim it so all the world may rejoice. Do not delay, thinking, "I will speak of it in the coming days." From now on, the festival of the peerless Lord performing the Dance of Grace will be ceaseless.
commentary: To convey the absolute certainty of his message, Vallalar declares he is speaking under direct command from God. He seals his words with a powerful oath on "the sacred feet that kicked Death," a reference to God's ultimate power over mortality itself. Taking this as a divine decree, he insists the news must be spread so the world can rejoice in a new, ceaseless festival of grace.

translit: ētumaṟi yācciṟiya payalkaḷiṉum ciṟiyēṉ ipperiya vārttaitaṉak kiyāṉāreṉ iṟaivaṉ ōtukanī eṉṟapaṭi ōtukiṉṟēṉ maṉaṉē uḷḷapaṭi cattiyamī tuṇarntiṭuka namatu tītumuḻu tumtavirttē cittielām aḷikkat tiruvaruḷām peruñjōti appaṉvaru taruṇam ītituvē eṉṟulakam aṟiyavirain turaippāy ellārum kaḷippaṭaintuḷ icaintētti yiṭavē.
translation: I am smaller than even small boys who know nothing. Who am I to speak these great words? I speak as my Lord commanded me, "You must speak." O mind, understand that this is the truth as it is. So that he may remove all our evils and grant all powers, quickly declare for the world to know that this, this is the very moment the Father, the great Jothi who is divine Grace, will come, so that everyone may be filled with bliss and praise him in unison from their hearts.
commentary: Vallalar expresses deep humility, seeing himself as an unworthy messenger for such a great truth. By stressing his own smallness, he highlights that the message is purely a divine transmission. The purpose of this divine arrival is to erase all human failings and grant perfected abilities or spiritual powers (siddhis), bringing universal bliss.

translit: taṉittalaivaṉ ellāñcey vallacittaṉ ñāṉa capaittalaivaṉ eṉuḷattē taṉittiruntuḷ uṇarttak kaṉitta:uḷat toṭumuṇarntē uṇarttukiṉṟēṉ itaiōr kataieṉanī niṉaiyēlmeyk karutturaieṉ ṟaṟika iṉittaaruṭ peruñcōti āṇaiellām uṭaiya iṟaivaṉvaru taruṇamitu cattiyamām itaṉaip paṉittavula kavaraṟintē uyyumvakai iṉṉē pakarntiṭuka nāḷaiaruṭ paramacukac cāṟē.
translation: As the peerless Lord, the all-powerful Siddhar, the head of the Hall of Wisdom, resides alone in my heart and inwardly inspires me, I, having understood with a ripened heart, am making it known. Do not think of this as just a story; know it as a statement of true meaning. Upon the oath of the sweet, great Grace-Jothi, this is the moment the Lord who possesses everything comes. This is the truth. So that the people of this suffering world may know this and be saved, declare it this very day. Tomorrow is the festival of the supreme bliss of Grace.
commentary: This message comes directly from the Lord who presides over the Gnana Sabai, the inner space of pure wisdom. Vallalar insists this is a factual statement meant to save a world lost in suffering. The announcement must be made today, because the celebration of divine bliss begins tomorrow.

translit: tantēkam eṉakkaḷittār tamaruḷum poruḷum tammaiyumiṅ keṉakkaḷittār emmaiyiṉum piriyār entēkam atiṟpukuntār eṉuḷattē iruntār eṉuyiril kalantanaṭat tiṟaiyavarkā laiyilē vantēiṅ kamarntaruḷvar ātaliṉāl viraintē māḷikaiyai alaṅkarittu vaittiṭuti itaṟkuc cantēkam illaieṉṟaṉ taṉittalaivar vārttai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: He gave His body to me. He gave me His grace, His substance, and Himself, right here. He will never be separate from me, in any lifetime. He entered this body of mine; He resided in my heart. The Lord of Dance who merged with my very life will come in the morning and take His seat here to bestow His grace. Therefore, hurry and decorate the mansion. Have no doubt about this. The word of my one and only Lord is the truth, the truth, O lady, the truth, the truth!
commentary: The poem shifts into the intimate voice of a soul in love with God. This union is described as total and physical: God has entered the devotee's very body, heart, and life. The instruction is to prepare the "mansion," which represents one's own being, for the imminent arrival of the divine Beloved. The repeated insistence on "truth" conveys an unshakable, ecstatic conviction.

translit: naṉpāṭṭu maṟaikaḷukkum mālayarkkum kiṭaiyār namaḷavil kiṭaippārō eṉṟuniṉait tēṅki eṉpāṭṭuk kiruntēṉai valintukalan taṇaintē iṉpamuṟat taṉimālai iṭṭanaṭat tiṟaivar muṉpāṭṭuk kālaiyilē varukuvarmā ḷikaiyai muḻutumalaṅ karittiṭuka aiyuṟavō ṭorunī taṉpāṭṭuk kiruntuḷaṟēl aiyartiru vārttai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: He is unattainable even to the fine-versed Vedas, to Vishnu, and to Brahma. I was languishing, thinking, "How could He be attainable to one such as me?" While I was left to my own devices, the Lord of Dance forcefully came, merged with and embraced me, and to my delight, placed a special garland upon me. He will come in the early morning. Decorate the entire mansion. Do not sit there by yourself, filled with doubt and babbling nonsense. The sacred word of the Lord is the truth, the truth, O lady, the truth, the truth!
commentary: Addressing the doubt that such a great God could be accessible to an ordinary person, Vallalar explains that God himself closed the distance. The union was a forceful act of grace from the divine Beloved. The "garland" is a traditional symbol of being chosen and accepted, like in a marriage. The poem dismisses doubt as useless chatter in the face of God's own promise.

translit: muṉpāṭṭuk kālaiyilē varukuvareṉ kaṇavar mōcamilai mōcameṉa moḻikiṉṟār moḻika piṉpāṭṭuk kālaiyilē niṉaittaelām muṭiyum picakilaiim moḻiciṟitum picakilaiiv vulakil tuṉpāṭṭuc ciṟṟiṉattār ciṟumoḻikēṭ ṭuḷḷam tuḷaṅkēlnam māḷikaiyaic cūḻaalaṅ karippāy taṉpāṭṭut tiruppotuvil naṭattiṟaivar āṇai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: My husband will come in the early morning. Some people are saying, "It's a deception, a deception!" Let them say it. Later this morning, everything we have hoped for will come to pass. This promise is not flawed, not in the slightest. In this world, do not let your heart waver by listening to the petty words of that wretched, small-minded crowd. Go and decorate our mansion all around. By the command of the Lord of Dance, who performs as He wills in the sacred common space, it is the truth, the truth, O lady, the truth, the truth!
commentary: The soul acknowledges the cynicism of the outside world, where people dismiss her spiritual certainty as a "deception." The instruction is to ignore the chatter of this "small-minded crowd" and remain steadfast in faith. The promise of divine union is guaranteed by the command of God himself.

translit: uḷḷuṇṭa uṇmaielām nāṉaṟivēṉ eṉṉai uṭaiyaperun takaiaṟivār ulakiṭattē māyaik kaḷḷuṇṭa ciṟṟiṉattār yātaṟivār eṉatu kaṇavartiru varavintak kālaiyilām kaṇṭāy naḷḷuṇṭa māḷikaiyai maṅkalaṅkaḷ nirampa naṉkupuṉain talaṅkarippāy nāṉmoḻinta moḻiyait taḷḷuṇṭiṅ kaiyamuṟēl naṭattiṟaivar āṇai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: I know all the truth that lies within. The great noble one who owns me knows it. What can the small-minded people of this world, who are drunk on the liquor of illusion, possibly know? You will see, my husband's sacred arrival is this very morning. Adorn and decorate the inner chambers of the mansion well, filling them with auspicious things. Do not reject what I have said and give in to doubt. By the command of the Lord of Dance, it is the truth, the truth, O lady, the truth, the truth!
commentary: The basis for the soul's confidence is an inner, experienced truth, a knowledge shared only between herself and God. Those who are "drunk on the liquor of illusion," meaning they are lost in worldly concerns, simply cannot perceive this reality. The call is to prepare the "inner chambers" of the self, turning away from external validation and trusting this internal certainty.

translit: eṉṉuṭaiya taṉikkaṇavar aruṭjōti uṇmai yāṉaṟivēṉ ulakavarkaḷ eṅṅaṉamkaṇ ṭaṟivār uṉṉalaṟa uṇṇutaṟkum uṟaṅkutaṟkum aṟivār ulamputalkēṭ ṭaiyamuṟēl ōṅkiyamā ḷikaiyait tuṉṉuṟummaṅ kalamviḷaṅka alaṅkarippāy iṅkē tūṅkutalāl eṉṉapalaṉ cōrvaṭaiyēl potuvil taṉṉuṭaiya naṭampuriyum talaivartiru āṇai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: The truth is that my one and only husband is ArutJothi; I know this. How could the people of the world possibly see and know it? They only know how to eat and sleep, without a single thought. Do not listen to their chatter and start doubting. Decorate the high mansion so it gleams with abundant signs of auspiciousness. What is the use of sleeping now? Do not grow weary. By the sacred command of the Lord who performs His dance in the common space, it is the truth, the truth, O lady, the truth, the truth.
commentary: Here the divine beloved is named: ArutJothi, the Grace-Light. This knowledge is a personal revelation, inaccessible to those absorbed in the mundane cycle of eating and sleeping. The verse urges the spiritual seeker to awaken from this slumber of ordinary consciousness, because with God's arrival imminent, there is no time to waste.

translit: eṉṉaimaṇa mālaiiṭṭār eṉṉuyiril kalantār ellāmcey vallacittar eṉakkaṟivit tataṉai iṉṉa:ula kiṉaraṟiyār ātaliṉāl palavē iyampukiṉṟār iyampukanam talaivarvaru taruṇam maṉṉiyakā laiyilākum māḷikaiyai viraintu maṅkalaṅkaḷ puṉaintiṭuka mayaṅkiaiyam aṭaiyēl taṉnikartā ṉāmpotuvil naṭampurivār āṇai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: He placed the wedding garland on me and merged with my very soul. The all-powerful Siddhar revealed this to me. The people of this world do not know it, so they say many things. Let them speak. The moment of our Lord's arrival is set for the morning. Quickly, adorn the mansion with auspicious decorations. Do not become confused or harbor any doubt. By the command of the one who dances in the common space, who is his own equal: this is the truth, the truth, O woman, the truth, the truth.
commentary: The union is described as a marriage, sealed by a garland from the Lord himself, who is identified here as a Siddhar (a perfected being with mastery over all powers). It signifies a concrete, life-changing event revealed to the soul. The world's ignorance is irrelevant in the face of this direct, divine confirmation.

translit: kiḷaiaṉanta maṟaiyālum niccayikkak kūṭāk kiḷaroḷiyār eṉaḷavil kiṭaittataṉit talaivar aḷaiyaeṉak kuṇarttiyatai yāṉaṟivēṉ ulakar aṟivārō avaruraikoṇ ṭaiyamuṟēl iṅkē iḷaivaṭaiyēṉ māḷikaiyai maṅkalaṅkaḷ nirampa iṉitupuṉain talaṅkarippāy kālaiitu kaṇṭāy taḷarvaṟacciṟ ṟampalattē naṭampurivār āṇai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: The brilliant Light that even the countless branches of the Vedas cannot ascertain is the unique Lord I have gained. I know what he intimately revealed to me; how would the people of the world know? Do not doubt on account of their words. Do not grow weary here. Decorate the mansion beautifully, filling it with auspicious things. See, it is morning now. By the command of the one who dances tirelessly in the Chitrambalam: this is the truth, the truth, O woman, the truth, the truth.
commentary: Direct experience of God surpasses even the highest scriptural authority. The brilliant Light the soul has encountered is a reality so vast that the Vedas (ancient sacred texts) cannot fully define it. The divine dance happens in the Chitrambalam (the hall of consciousness), locating this highest experience within the devotee's own being.

translit: āraṟivār ellāmcey vallavareṉ uḷḷē aṟivitta uṇmaiyaimāl ayaṉmutalōr aṟiyār pāraṟiyā tayalvēṟu pakarvatukēṭ ṭorunī paiyuḷoṭum aiyamuṟēl kālaiitu kaṇṭāy nēruṟanī viraintuvirain taṇipeṟamā ḷikaiyai nīṭaalaṅ karippāyuḷ nēyamoṭu kaḷittē tārakamiṅ keṉakkāṉa naṭattiṟaivar āṇai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: Who can know the truth the all-powerful one revealed within me? Even Vishnu, Brahma, and the others do not know it. The world, not knowing, says different things. Hearing them, do not be filled with sorrow and doubt. See, it is morning. With inner love and joy, you must quickly, quickly, and fittingly decorate the mansion grandly. By the command of the Lord of the Dance, who is my savior here: this is the truth, the truth, O woman, the truth, the truth.
commentary: The truth revealed within is a secret known only to the soul and God. It is so personal that even major deities like Vishnu and Brahma are unaware of it. This highlights the supremacy of direct, inner revelation over traditional religious hierarchies. The preparation for God's arrival is an act of pure love and joy.

translit: aiyareṉak kuḷḷiruntiṅ kaṟivitta varattai yāraṟivār nāṉaṟivēṉ avaraṟivār allāl poyulakar aṟivārō pullaṟivāl palavē pukalkiṉṟār atukēṭṭup puntimayak kaṭaiyēl meyyareṉai āḷuṭaiyār varukiṉṟa taruṇam mēviyatu māḷikaiyai alaṅkarippāy viraintē taiyaloru pāluṭaiya naṭattiṟaivar āṇai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: Who knows the boon the Lord revealed from within me? I know it, and He knows it, but how would the people of this false world know? With their paltry knowledge, they say many things. Hearing them, do not let your mind become confused. The moment for the arrival of the True One who rules me has come. Decorate the mansion quickly. By the command of the Lord of the Dance, who has the Woman as one half of his form: this is the truth, the truth, O woman, the truth, the truth.
commentary: The Lord's presence is a special grace, a boon granted from within. The opinions of the "false world," guided by limited understanding, are insignificant. By invoking the image of the Lord who has "the Woman as one half of his form" (a reference to the divine union of Siva and Shakti), the verse connects this personal experience to a powerful symbol of divine completeness.

translit: uṭaiyavareṉ uḷattiruntē uṇarvitta varattai ulakavarkaḷ aṟiyārkaḷ ātaliṉāl palavē iṭaipukalkiṉ ṟāratukēṭ ṭaiyamuṟēl iṅkē iravuviṭin tatukālai eytiyatāl iṉiyē aṭaivuṟanam taṉittalaivar taṭaiyaṟavan taruḷvar aṇipeṟamā ḷikaiyaivirain talaṅkarittu makiḻka caṭaiyacaiyap potunaṭañcey iṟaivartiru vārttai cattiyamcat tiyammātē cattiyamcat tiyamē.
translation: The people of the world do not know the boon the Master revealed from within my heart, so they say many interfering things. Hearing them, do not doubt. Here, the night has broken and morning has arrived. From now on, our unique Lord will come appropriately and without obstacle to bestow his grace. Quickly decorate the mansion beautifully and rejoice. This sacred word of the Lord who performs the common dance, his matted locks swaying, is the truth, the truth, O woman, the truth, the truth.
commentary: The waiting is over; the darkness of spiritual ignorance has passed, and the morning of grace has dawned. The Lord's arrival is now certain and imminent. The command to decorate the mansion and rejoice reflects the soul's confident joy. The final image of the dancing Lord with swaying locks grounds the experience in the beloved, traditional form of Siva Nataraja.

sections.title: Telling the People of the World the Way to Salvation

translit: kaṭṭōṭē kaṉattōṭē vāḻkiṉṟōm eṉpīr kaṇṇōṭē karuttōṭē karuttaṉaik karutīr paṭṭōṭē paṇiyōṭē tirikiṉṟīr teruvil paciyōṭē vantāraip pārkkavum nērīr koṭṭōṭē muḻakkōṭē kōlaṅkāṇ kiṉṟīr kuṇattōṭē kuṟippōṭē kuṟippataik kuṟiyīr eṭṭōṭē iraṇṭucērt teṇṇavum aṟiyīr ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: You say, “We live with structure and status,” but you do not contemplate the Lord with your eyes and mind. You wander the streets in silk and jewels, but you will not even look at those who come in hunger. You watch performances with drumming and clamor, but you do not aim for the true goal with good character and intention. You do not even know how to add two to eight and count. How much madness you embrace, O people of this crazed world!
commentary: Vallalar criticizes a life focused on status and wealth that ignores both God and the hungry. People chase empty spectacles but miss the true goal of life. The line about not knowing how to add "two to eight" refers to the letters that form the sacred syllable Om (A+U), signifying a complete ignorance of even the most basic spiritual truths.

translit: āṟāmal aviyāmal aṭaintakō pattīr aṭarvuṟa ulakiṭai añcātu tirivīr māṟāmal maṉañceṉṟa vaḻiceṉṟu tikaippīr vaḻituṟai kāṇkilīr paḻipaṭum paṭikkē nāṟāta malarpōlum vāḻkiṉṟīr mūppu naraitirai maraṇattuk keṉceyak kaṭavīr ēṟāmal vīṇilē iṟaṅkukiṉ ṟīrē ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: Your anger never cools or subsides. You roam the world aggressively and without fear. Unchanging, you follow wherever your mind leads and end up bewildered, not seeing the path, and thus heading for disgrace. You live like a flower without fragrance. What will you do about old age, grey hair, wrinkles, and death? Instead of ascending, you descend in vain. How much madness you embrace, O people of this crazed world!
commentary: A life consumed by anger and aimless desire is like a flower with no scent; it has the form of life but lacks its true essence. Vallalar warns that such an existence is a wasted life, leaving a person completely unprepared for the inevitable realities of old age and death.

translit: āyāmai yālēnīr ātia ṉāti ākiya cōtiyai aṟintukoḷ killīr māyāmai piṟavāmai vaḻiyoṉṟum uṇarīr maṟavāmai niṉaiyāmai vakaiciṟi taṟiyīr kāyāmai paḻukkiṉṟa karuttaiyum karutīr kaṇmūṭit tirikiṉṟīr kaṉivoṭum irappōrk kīyāmai oṉṟaiyē iṉtuṇai eṉpīr ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: Because you do not investigate, you fail to know the Jothi that is the beginning and without beginning. You do not grasp the one path to immortality and freedom from rebirth. You know nothing of the state beyond forgetting and thinking. You do not contemplate the idea of the unripe fruit ripening. You wander with your eyes closed and, to those who beg with tenderness, you hold not-giving as your one sweet companion. How much madness you embrace, O people of this crazed world!
commentary: Spiritual truth is not found because people fail to investigate it. They remain ignorant of the eternal Jothi (divine light) and the path to immortality because they never truly look. He ends with a stark accusation: they treat the act of withholding from the needy as a cherished companion.

translit: cāmāntar ākāt tarañciṟi tuṇarīr tattuva ñāṉattai iṟṟeṉat teriyīr māmānta nōyuṟṟa kuḻaviyil kuḻaintīr vāḻkkaiyi lēaṟpa makiḻcciyum peṟṟīr kāmānta kārattil kaṇmūṭit tirivīr kaṟpaṉa kaṟkilīr karuttaṉaik karutā tēmāntu tūṅkukiṉ ṟīrviḻik kiṉṟīr ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: You do not have the slightest understanding of the quality that keeps one from being an ordinary mortal. You do not clearly know what the knowledge of ultimate reality is. You are as helpless as a child with a wasting disease, finding only trivial pleasures in life. You wander with your eyes closed in the deep darkness of lust. You do not learn what must be learned; without contemplating the Lord, you are deceived, sleeping and waking. How much madness you embrace, O people of this crazed world!
commentary: Entangled in sensual desire and trivial pleasures, people lack any understanding of how to transcend ordinary mortality. Vallalar compares this state to being as helpless as a sick child, trapped in a "deep darkness." By failing to learn what is essential, their life becomes a meaningless cycle of sleeping and waking, without ever truly awakening to God.

translit: accaiyum uṭampaiyum aṟivakai aṟiyīr ammaiyum appaṉum āreṉat teriyīr paccaiyum cemmaiyum karumaiyum kūṭip palittanum vāḻkkaiyil paṇpoṉṟum illīr piccaiyiṭ ṭuṇṇavum piṉpaṭu kiṉṟīr piṉpaṭu tīmaiyiṉ muṉpaṭu kiṉṟīr iccaiyil kaṇmūṭi eccakam kaṇṭīr ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: You do not know how to know the soul and the body. You do not know who the Mother and Father are. In the life that has resulted from the coming together of green, red, and black, you have no good qualities. You are reluctant even to give alms before you eat. You are at the forefront of the evils that follow. Closing your eyes in desire, what have you found but filth? How much madness you embrace, O people of this crazed world.
commentary: True knowledge begins with knowing oneself, but people here understand neither their own soul nor their divine origins as children of the cosmic Mother and Father. Their lives are an undisciplined mix of the raw energies of nature (represented as black, red, and green) without any guiding virtue. This deep ignorance leads to a life of selfishness, where one chases desire only to find it is empty and corrupting.

translit: vaṭṭimēl vaṭṭikoḷ mārkkattil niṉṟīr vaṭṭiyai vaḷarkkiṉṟa mārkkattai aṟiyīr peṭṭimēl peṭṭivait tāḷkiṉṟīr vayiṟṟup peṭṭiyai nirappikkoṇ ṭoṭṭiyuḷ iruntīr paṭṭiṉi kiṭappāraip pārkkavum nērīr paḻaṅkañci āyiṉum vaḻaṅkavum niṉaiyīr eṭṭipōl vāḻkiṉṟīr koṭṭipōl kiḷaittīr ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: You follow the way of charging interest upon interest, but you do not know the way of real growth. You rule by stacking chest upon chest. You fill the box of your stomach and remain mired in your attachments. You refuse to even look at those who are starving; you never think to offer them even old gruel. You live like a poison tree and branch out like a thorny bush. How much more will you acquire, you people of this mad world?
commentary: The obsessive pursuit of material wealth is a counterfeit of true spiritual growth. Vallalar contrasts the worldly way of accumulating money, like charging interest on interest, with the real inner development that is life's purpose. The final image is devastating: a person focused only on hoarding becomes like a poison tree, offering no nourishment or shelter to anyone.

translit: vaṉcolliṉ allatu vāytiṟap paṟiyīr vāymaiyum tūymaiyum kāymaiyil vaḷarntīr muṉcollum āṟoṉṟu piṉcolva toṉṟāy mūṭṭukiṉ ṟīrviṉai mūṭṭaiyaik kaṭṭi maṉcollum mārkkattai maṟantutuṉ mārkka vaḻinaṭak kiṉṟīram maraṇattīrp pukkē eṉcolla irukkiṉṟīr piṉcolva taṟiyīr ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: You do not know how to open your mouths for anything but harsh words. The truth and purity you have cultivated are rooted in malice. What you say first is one thing, and what you say later is another. You tie up a bundle of karma, constantly stirring up trouble. Forgetting the path praised by the wise, you walk the way of wickedness. At that final judgment of death, what will you have to say? You do not know what you will say then. How much more will you acquire, you people of this mad world?
commentary: Dishonesty in word and deed creates a heavy spiritual burden. Vallalar points to the hypocrisy of people who say one thing and do another, all while tying a bundle of negative karma (the consequences of one's actions) to themselves. He ends with a chilling question: when facing the final judgment of death, what defense can such a life offer?

translit: tuṉmārkka naṭaiyiṭait tūṅkukiṉ ṟīrē tūkkattai viṭukiṉṟa tuṇaioṉṟum karutīr caṉmārkka caṅkattaic cārntiṭa viḻaiyīr cāvaiyum piṟappaiyum tavirntiṭa virumpīr paṉmārkkam celkiṉṟa paṭiṟṟuḷam aṭakkīr pacittavar tammukam pārttuṇa vaḷiyīr eṉmārkkam eccukam yātunum vāḻkkai ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: You are sleeping in the midst of your wicked ways. You give no thought to any help that would awaken you from this slumber. You have no desire to join the fellowship of the righteous path; you do not wish to escape death and rebirth. You do not restrain your deceitful heart, which wanders down many paths. You do not look upon the faces of the hungry and offer them food. What is your path? What is your happiness? What is this life you lead? How much more will you acquire, you people of this mad world?
commentary: Most people are living as if they are asleep, unaware of their spiritual purpose or the path to freedom. Vallalar describes this state as a "wicked way" because it is a life that ignores both God and the suffering of others. He offers Sanmarkkam, the True Path, as the community and teaching that can awaken a person from this slumber. The first sign of waking up is the simple, direct act of feeding the hungry.

translit: poykaṭṭik koṇṭunīr vāḻkiṉṟīr iṅkē pulaikaṭṭik koṇṭa:ip poyyuṭal vīḻntāl ceykaṭṭi vāḻkiṉṟa cerukkaṟṟu narakil ciṟupuḻu ākit tikaittiṭal aṟiyīr kaikaṭṭi vāypotti niṟpāraik kaṇṭē kaikoṭṭic cirikkiṉṟīr karuṇaioṉ ṟillīr eykaṭṭi iṭaimoykkum īyiṉum ciṟiyīr ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: You live here, having built your life on lies. You do not realize that when this false body, built on defilement, collapses, your pride in a self-made life will be shattered, and you will become a tiny, bewildered worm in hell. Seeing those who stand with folded hands and covered mouths in deference, you clap your hands and laugh. You have no compassion whatsoever. You are more base than the flies that swarm a discarded arrow. How much more will you acquire, you people of this mad world?
commentary: Pride in one's own achievements and contempt for others is a fragile and false foundation for life. Vallalar delivers a warning that when this "false body" dies, the proud and cruel will face a state of absolute powerlessness and humiliation. The inability to show compassion to others is, for him, a sign of being less than human.

translit: paṇṇāta tīmaikaḷ paṇṇukiṉ ṟīrē pakarāta vaṉmoḻi pakarukiṉ ṟīrē naṇṇāta tīyiṉam naṇṇukiṉ ṟīrē naṭavāta naṭattaikaḷ naṭakkavan tīrē kaṇṇākak kākkiṉṟa karuttaṉai niṉaintē kaṇṇāra nīrviṭṭuk karutaṟi yīrē eṇṇāta teṇṇavum nērumōr kālam ettuṇai koḷkiṉṟīr pittula kīrē.
translation: You commit evils that should not be committed. You speak harsh words that should not be spoken. You associate with wicked people who should be avoided. You conduct yourselves in ways that should not be followed. You do not know how to think of the Master who protects you like the apple of His eye, letting tears fill your eyes as you contemplate Him. A time will come when you must face the unthinkable. How much more will you acquire, you people of this mad world?
commentary: After listing the characteristics of a life gone astray, Vallalar reminds the listener that even in this state, God is present, protecting them intimately "like the apple of His eye." The path back begins with remembering this divine presence with heartfelt emotion, even tears. To continue ignoring this connection, however, invites a time of reckoning when one must face the "unthinkable" consequences of one's actions.

sections.title: Declaring the Way to Attain the Sacred Community

translit: cātiyilē mataṅkaḷilē camayaneṟi kaḷilē cāttiraccan taṭikaḷilē kōttiraccaṇ ṭaiyilē ātiyilē apimāṉit talaikiṉṟa ulakīr alaintalaintu vīṇēnīr aḻitalaḻa kalavē nītiyilē caṉmārkka nilaitaṉilē niṟutta niruttamiṭum taṉittalaivar oruttaravar tāmē vītiyilē aruṭcōti viḷaiyāṭal puriya mēvukiṉṟa taruṇamitu kūvukiṉṟēṉ umaiyē.
translation: O people of the world, who wander about, obsessed with castes, religions, religious paths, the clamor of scriptures, and the quarrels of lineage! It is not right for you to wander and wander, only to be destroyed in vain. To establish you in justice, in the state of Sanmarkkam, the one unique Leader who performs the cosmic dance is Himself coming. This is the moment for Him to perform the play of the Grace-Jothi in the streets. I am calling out to you.
commentary: Vallalar directly addresses a world torn apart by religious and social conflict. He sees attachments to caste, creed, and scripture as pointless quarrels that only lead to destruction. He proclaims that this era of division is ending, because a divine power, the "Grace-Jothi" (ArutJothi, Grace-Light), is coming to establish a single, universal True Path (Sanmarkkam) for all. This is an urgent, present reality.

translit: kāṭuveṭṭi nilantiruttik kāṭṭeruvum pōṭṭuk karumpaiviṭṭuk kaṭuviraittuk kaḷikkiṉṟa ulakīr kūṭuviṭṭup pōyiṉapiṉ etupurivīr eṅkē kuṭiyiruppīr aiyōnīr kuṟittaṟiyīr iṅkē pāṭupaṭṭīrpayaṉaṟiyīr pāḻkkiṟaittuk kaḻittīr paṭṭatelām pōtumitu paramarvaru taruṇam īṭukaṭṭi varuvīrēl iṉpammikap peṟuvīr eṇmaiurait tēṉalaṉnāṉ uṇmaiyurait tēṉē.
translation: O people of the world, who clear the forest, prepare the land, and apply wild manure, only to ignore sugarcane and sow bitter mustard seeds, rejoicing in it! After your soul leaves its body-cage, what will you do? Where will you dwell? Alas, you do not realize this here. You have toiled without knowing the true benefit; you have wasted your efforts on futile things. Enough of all this suffering. This is the moment the Supreme One arrives. If you come prepared, you will receive immense bliss. I have not spoken trivialities; I have spoken the truth.
commentary: People are like farmers who do all the hard work of preparing a field but then plant a useless, bitter crop instead of sweet sugarcane. With this powerful metaphor, Vallalar shows how people spend their entire lives on pursuits that bring no lasting spiritual value. This futile labor is contrasted with the "immense bliss" available to those who properly prepare for the arrival of the Supreme One.

translit: āṟṟuveḷḷam varuvataṉmuṉ aṇaipōṭa aṟiyīr akaṅkārap pēypiṭittīr āṭutaṟkē aṟivīr kūṟṟuvaruṅ kālataṉuk ketupurivīr aiyō kūṟṟutaitta cēvaṭiyaip pōṟṟavirum pīrē vēṟṟuraittu viṉaiperukki melikiṉṟa ulakīr vīṇulakak koṭuvaḻakkai viṭṭuviṭṭu vammiṉ cāṟṟuvakka eṉatutaṉit tantaivaru kiṉṟa taruṇamitu cattiyañciṟ cattiyaiccār vataṟkē.
translation: You do not know to build a dam before the river floods. Possessed by the demon of ego, you only know how to dance to its tune. Alas, when Kootru comes, what will you do? You have no desire to praise the sacred feet that kicked Kootru away. O people of the world, who grow weak by speaking divisive words and multiplying your karma, abandon the cruel ways of this futile world and come! This is the moment my unique Father is arriving. I swear it is true, it is the time to attain the Power of Consciousness-Truth.
commentary: Spiritual unpreparedness is like failing to build a dam before a flood or being possessed by the "demon of ego." People live recklessly, ignoring the inevitable arrival of Kootru, the god of death. Vallalar points to the only true refuge: the divine power that has already conquered death. He announces that this very power is now arriving and accessible to all who abandon their self-destructive ways.

translit: poyviḷakkap pukukiṉṟīr pōtukaḻik kiṉṟīr pulaikolaikaḷ purikiṉṟīr kalakalaeṉ kiṉṟīr kaiviḷakkup piṭittorupāḻṅ kiṇaṟṟilviḻu kiṉṟa kaḷiyareṉak kaḷikkiṉṟīr karuttiruntum karutīr aiviḷakku mūppumara ṇātikaḷai niṉaittāl aṭivayiṟṟai muṟukkātō koṭiyamuyaṟ ṟulakīr meyviḷakka eṉatutantai varukiṉṟa taruṇam mēviyatīṇ ṭaṭaivīrēl āvipeṟu vīrē.
translation: You engage in explaining falsehoods and waste your time. You eat flesh and commit murder, and you laugh merrily. You rejoice like drunkards who fall into a desolate well while holding a lamp; you have minds, yet you do not think. O people of the world engaged in cruel pursuits, if you think about affliction, old age, and death, will it not twist your guts? This is the moment my Father arrives to reveal the Truth. If you draw near and are touched, you will attain true life.
commentary: People knowingly walk toward their own ruin, like a drunkard holding a lamp who still falls into a well. The lamp is the mind or consciousness, which people possess but are too intoxicated with worldly life to use for their own safety. Vallalar tries to shock them from this state by reminding them of the gut-twisting fear of aging and death, offering the "Father's" arrival as the only path to a "true life" beyond that fear.

translit: eyvakaicārmataṅkaḷilē poyvakaiccāt tiraṅkaḷ eṭutturaittē ematuteyvam ematuteyvam eṉṟu kaivakaiyē kataṟukiṉṟīr teyvamoṉṟeṉ ṟaṟiyīr karipiṭittuk kalakamiṭṭa periyariṉum periyīr aivakaiya pūtavuṭam paḻintiṭileṉ purivīr aḻiyuṭampai aḻiyāmai ākkumvakai aṟiyīr uyvakaieṉ taṉittantai varukiṉṟa taruṇam uṟṟativaṇ uṟṟiṭuvīr peṟṟiṭuvīr uvappē.
translation: Taking up the various false scriptures of your divisive religions, you cry out, “Our god! Our god!” You wail in your own ways, not knowing that God is One. You are even greater fools than the great men who fought after grasping parts of an elephant. When this body, made of the five elements, perishes, what will you do? You do not know the way to make this perishable body imperishable. The moment for your salvation has arrived; my unique Father is coming. It is here now. Approach, and you will attain joy.
commentary: Vallalar calls these scriptures false and the shouting over 'our god, our god' blind folly: those who quarrel this way are greater fools than the men who fought after each grasped only a part of the elephant, for they do not know that God is One. This quarrel distracts from the real human problem: our physical bodies, made of the five elements (bhūtas), perish. The salvation offered now is the way to make this perishable body imperishable.

translit: uṭampuvaru vakaiaṟiyīr uyirvakaiyai aṟiyīr uṭalparukka uṇṭunitam uṟaṅkutaṟkē aṟivīr maṭampukupēy maṉattālē mayaṅkukiṉṟīr maṉattai vacappaṭuttīr vacappaṭuttum vaḻituṟaikaṟ ṟaṟiyīr iṭampeṟupoy vāḻkkaiyilē iṉpatuṉpam aṭuttē eṇṇieṇṇi iḷaikkiṉṟīr ēḻaiula kīrē naṭampurieṉ taṉittantai varukiṉṟa taruṇam naṇṇiyatu naṇṇumiṉō puṇṇiyañcār vīrē.
translation: You do not know how the body comes to be, nor do you know the nature of life. You only know how to eat daily to fatten the body and how to sleep. You are bewildered by a demonic mind filled with ignorance. You have not mastered your mind, nor have you learned the methods to do so. In this false life you have obtained, you grow weary, constantly dwelling on alternating pleasure and pain. O poor people of the world! The moment of my solitary Father's arrival, He who performs the dance, is near. Come close, you who will gain merit.
commentary: We focus on eating, sleeping, and the superficial needs of the body, but we fail to understand life's deeper reality or how our own minds work. Vallalar says we are bewildered by an undisciplined mind that keeps us trapped in a cycle of pleasure and pain. The true spiritual task is to master this mind, and he announces that the divine grace of the "dancing Father" is now accessible, offering a path to gain this control.

translit: naraimaraṇa mūppaṟiyā nalla:uṭam piṉarē naṟkulattār eṉaaṟiyīr nāṉilattīr nīvir varaiyiluyar kulameṉṟum tāḻntakulam eṉṟum vakukkiṉṟīr irukulamum māṇṭiṭakkāṇ kiṉṟīr puraiyuṟunum kulaṅkaḷelām puḻukkulameṉ ṟaṟintē puttamutam uṇṭōṅkum puṉitakulam peṟavē uraipeṟumeṉ taṉittantai varukiṉṟa taruṇam uṟṟativaṇ uṟṟiṭuvīr uṇmaiurait tēṉē.
translation: O people of this vast earth, you do not recognize that only those with good bodies, which know no gray hair, death, or old age, belong to the true, good lineage. You draw endless distinctions, creating 'high lineage' and 'low lineage', yet you witness both these lineages perish. Understand that all your flawed lineages are but lineages of worms. The moment of my renowned, solitary Father's arrival is here now, for you to receive the sacred lineage that flourishes by consuming the new ambrosia. Come close; I have told you the truth.
commentary: Worldly status, whether high or low birth, is meaningless because death comes for everyone. Vallalar declares that all these social hierarchies are nothing more than "lineages of worms." The only true and good family, he says, consists of people who have attained a body that does not age or die. He announces that the way to join this sacred lineage is by receiving a "new ambrosia," a divine grace that is now being offered to all.

translit: kaṉamuṭaiyēm kaṭṭuṭaiyēm eṉṟuniṉait tiṅkē kaḷittiṟumān tirukkiṉṟīr oḷippiṭamum aṟiyīr ciṉamuṭaiya kūṟṟuvarum ceytiaṟi yīrō cettanuma tiṉattāraic ciṟitumniṉai yīrō tiṉakaraṉpōl cākāta tēkamuṭai yavarē tiruvuṭaiyār eṉaaṟintē cērntiṭumiṉ īṇṭē maṉamakiḻntu kēṭkiṉṟa varamellām eṉakkē vaḻaṅkutaṟkeṉ taṉittantai varutaruṇam ituvē.
translation: Believing 'We have wealth, we have influence,' you live here, rejoicing with arrogance. You do not even know a place to hide. Are you not aware of the coming of the wrathful Kootruvan? Do you give even a small thought to your own people who have died? Understand that only those who possess a deathless body, like the sun, are the truly prosperous. Gather here now. This very moment is the time my solitary Father arrives to joyfully grant me every boon I ask for.
commentary: Wealth and social influence create a false sense of security, but they offer no protection from death. Vallalar asks us to face the coming of Kootruvan (the God of Death) and remember all those we know who have already died. He redefines prosperity: true wealth is a body that is immortal and radiant like the sun. This is the moment, he declares, when divine grace is available to achieve this state.

translit: vaiyakattīr vāṉakattīr maṟṟakattīr numatu vāḻkkaielām vāḻkkaieṉa matittumayaṅ kātīr maiyakattē uṟumaraṇa vātaṉaiyait tavirtta vāḻkkaiyatē vāḻkkaieṉa matittataṉaip peṟavē meyakattē virumpiiṅkē vantiṭumiṉ eṉatu meypporuḷām taṉittantai ittaruṇan taṉilē ceyakattē vaḷarñāṉa cittipuran taṉilē cittāṭal purikiṉṟār tiṇṇamitu tāṉē.
translation: O people of the earthly world, the celestial world, and all other worlds! Do not be deluded by considering your lives to be true life. To obtain what is esteemed as true life, a life that has averted the agony of death which afflicts this central world, desire it in your inmost self and come here. At this very moment, my solitary Father, who is the True Substance, is performing his divine play of powers in Gnana Siddhipuram, which flourishes amid the fields. This is certain. This is certain.
commentary: Even the lives of gods in heavenly realms are not true life, because they too are subject to ending. Vallalar says true life is one that has conquered death completely. That transformation is made possible by the divine play of powers (Siddhi) that God is performing right now in Gnana Siddhipuram, Vallalar's name for Vadalur, the town of wisdom rising among the fields, and it is open to anyone who sincerely desires it and comes.

translit: karaṇammikak kaḷippuṟavē kaṭalulakum vāṉum katipatieṉ ṟāḷukiṉṟīr atipatiyīr nīvir maraṇapayam tavirātē vāḻvatileṉ payaṉō mayaṅkātīr uyaṅkātīr vantiṭumiṉ īṇṭē tiraṇamumōr aintoḻilaic ceyyaoḷi vaḻaṅkum cittipuram eṉaōṅkum uttiraciṟ capaiyil caraṇameṉak kaḷitteṉaiyum tāṉākka eṉatu taṉittantai varukiṉṟa taruṇamitu tāṉē.
translation: You rule the world and the heavens as lords of destiny, your inner faculties filled with delight. But O you rulers, what is the use of living a life that has not banished the fear of death? Do not be bewildered, do not languish. Come here now. This very moment is the time my solitary Father is arriving. This very moment is the time my solitary Father is arriving. He comes to the Uttara Chit Sabhai, hailed as Siddhipuram, where light is granted for even a blade of grass to perform the five cosmic functions, to joyfully take me in when I take refuge and make me one with Himself.
commentary: What is the point of being a ruler if you still fear death? Vallalar dismisses worldly authority as useless against this fundamental fear. He points to a different kind of power, found in the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness), a place so potent that divine light enables even a blade of grass to perform cosmic functions. This is where one can take refuge (saranam) and merge with God, attaining true fearlessness.
NOTES
Note 356

translit: pāṭupaṭṭup - ca. mu. ka. patippu.
translation: pāṭupaṭṭup — reading of the S. Mu. Ka. edition.
Note 357

translit: evvakaicār - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu. patippu.
translation: evvakaicār — reading of the first edition and the Po. Su. edition.
Note 358

tamil: முதற்பதிப்பிலும், பொ. சு. பதிப்பிலும் 'கனமுடையேம்' என்பது ஒன்பதாம்பாடலாகவும் 'வையகத்தீர்' என்பது எட்டாம் பாடலாகவும் உள்ளன.
translit: mutaṟpatippilum, po. cu. patippilum 'kaṉamuṭaiyēm' eṉpatu oṉpatāmpāṭalākavum 'vaiyakattīr' eṉpatu eṭṭām pāṭalākavum uḷḷaṉa.
translation: In the first edition and in the Po. Su. edition, 'kaṉamuṭaiyēm' stands as the ninth verse and 'vaiyakattīr' as the eighth.

translit: kaṇṇiṟ kalantāṉ karuttiṟ kalantāṉeṉ eṇṇiṟ kalantē irukkiṉṟāṉ - paṇṇiṟ kalantāṉeṉ pāṭṭiṟ kalantāṉ uyiril kalantāṉ karuṇai kalantu.
translation: He has mingled in my eye, mingled in my thought; he remains mingled in my every thought. He has mingled in the melody, mingled in my song; he has mingled in my life, suffused with compassion.
commentary: The divine is not somewhere "out there." It is experienced as a presence that has completely merged with one's own faculties: sight, thought, creativity, and life itself. This union is a gentle mingling born of pure compassion.

translit: ellā nalamum eṉakkē koṭukkiṉṟāṉ ellām ceyavallāṉ eṉperumāṉ - ellāmāy niṉṟāṉ potuvil niruttam purikiṉṟāṉ oṉṟāki niṉṟāṉ uvantu.
translation: He gives all good things to me. My great Lord can do all things. He stands as everything; he performs the dance in the common space. He stands as one, delightedly.
commentary: In this state of union, the devotee recognizes God as the singular source of all blessings and the ultimate power that can do anything. The Lord is a part of reality and is reality itself, standing as everything, yet dancing as a distinct presence in the universal "common space" (podu) where he is accessible to all.

translit: eṇṇukiṉṟēṉ eṇṇaṅkaḷ ellām tarukiṉṟāṉ paṇṇukiṉṟēṉ paṇṇuvittup pāṭukiṉṟāṉ - uṇṇukiṉṟēṉ teḷḷamutam uḷḷan teḷiyat tarukiṉṟāṉ vaḷḷalnaṭa rāyaṉ makiḻntu.
translation: I think, and he gives me all thoughts. I compose melodies, and he makes me compose and sing. I partake of the clear nectar he gives for my mind to attain clarity. The generous King of Dance gives this, delighted.
commentary: Personal agency is redefined. The speaker's ability to think, compose, and sing is understood as a gift from the divine. God is the source of these actions and the giver of the clarity, the "clear nectar," that nourishes the mind.

translit: cittiyelān tantē tiruvam palattāṭum nittiyaṉeṉ uḷḷē niṟaikiṉṟāṉ - cattiyamī tantō ulakīr aṟiyīrō nīvirelām cantōṭa māyirumiṉ cārntu.
translation: Having given all siddhis, the eternal one who dances in the sacred hall fills my inner self. This is the truth. Alas, O people of the world, do you not know? All of you, draw near him and be joyful.
commentary: While God may grant siddhis (spiritual powers), the greatest attainment is simply God's own presence filling your heart. Vallalar presents this inner union as an absolute truth and a source of deep joy. He makes an urgent, compassionate plea to everyone: this experience is available to all who draw near to the divine.

translit: ayyāeṉ ṟōrkāl aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ appoḻutē eyyēṉ makaṉēeṉ ṟeytukiṉṟāṉ - aiyōeṉ appaṉ peruṅkaruṇai yārkkuṇ ṭulakattīr ceppamuṭaṉ pōṟṟumiṉō cērntu.
translation: I call out "Ayya!" just once, and at that very moment, he arrives, saying, "I am here, my son!" Aiyō! Who in this world has my Father's great compassion? O people of the world, join together and praise him fittingly.
commentary: The connection to God can be incredibly intimate and immediate, like that of a child to a loving parent. A single, heartfelt call of "Father!" (Ayya!) brings an instant, loving response. Overwhelmed by this tenderness, Vallalar invites everyone to experience this same personal, compassionate relationship.

translit: appāeṉ ṟōrkāl aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ appoḻutē appā makaṉēeṉ ṟārkiṉṟāṉ - tuppār caṭaiyāṉciṟ ṟampalattāṉ tāṉētāṉ āṉāṉ uṭaiyāṉ uḷattē uvantu.
translation: The moment I call out "Father!", he roars back, "Father! Son!". The one with gleaming matted locks, the one of Chitrambalam, the Master, has joyfully become his very self within my heart.
commentary: The divine response to his call reveals a union where identities merge. When Vallalar calls out "Father!", God's reply, "Father! Son!", collapses the distinction between them. This shows that the Master of Chitrambalam (the inner sacred space) has joyfully become one with Vallalar's own consciousness.

translit: tāṉēvan teṉuḷattē cārntu kalantukoṇṭāṉ tāṉē eṉakkut tarukiṉṟāṉ - tāṉēnāṉ ākap purintāṉeṉ appaṉ peruṅkaruṇai mēkattiṟ kuṇṭō viḷampu.
translation: He came of his own accord, entered my heart, and merged with me. He gives to me of his own accord. He himself made me become him. Tell me, can even a rain cloud compare to my Father's great compassion?
commentary: Divine grace is God entering and merging so completely with the soul that the soul itself becomes divine. Vallalar expresses that this act of changing love, of God making the devotee into His own likeness, is a form of generosity far beyond even the life-giving rain clouds.

translit: pālum koṭuttāṉ patitiṟakkum ōrtiṟavuk kōlum koṭuttāṉ kuṇaṅkoṭuttāṉ - kālum talaiyum aṟiyum taramum koṭuttāṉ nilaiyum koṭuttāṉ niṟaintu.
translation: He gave me milk. He gave a key to unlock the Lord's domain. He gave me good qualities. He gave the capacity to know the breath (kāl) and the head (talai). He gave me a stable state, filling me completely.
commentary: God's grace provides everything needed for realization: nourishment ('milk'), the key that opens the Lord's domain, good qualities, and the capacity to know the breath (kāl) and the head (talai), the unburning air and the deathless head of Vallalar's teaching. The final gift is a stable state, filling him completely.

translit: vevviṉaiyum māyai viḷaivum tavirntaṉavē cevvaiaṟi viṉpam ciṟantaṉavē - evvayiṉum āṉāṉciṟ ṟampalattē āṭukiṉṟāṉ taṇaruḷām tēṉnāṉ uṇ ṭōṅkiyatu tērntu.
translation: Fierce karma and the effects of maya have been averted; perfect knowledge and bliss have flourished. Realizing this, I drank the cool honey of grace from him who became all things and dances in Chitrambalam, and I have soared high.
commentary: Union with the Divine resolves the fundamental problems of existence. The consequences of past actions (vinai, or karma) and the deluding power of cosmic illusion (maya) are removed. In their place, true knowledge and bliss emerge. This transformation comes from drinking the "honey of grace" offered by the God who is both present in all things and dancing in the sacred space of the heart.

translit: vañcaviṉai ellām maṭintaṉavaṉ māyaiiruḷ añcieṉai viṭṭē akaṉṟaṉavāl - eñcalilā iṉpamelām eṉṟaṉaiyē eyti niṟaintaṉavāl tuṉpamelām pōṉa tolaintu.
translation: All deceitful karma has perished. The darkness of harsh maya, in fear, has fled from me. All inexhaustible bliss has reached and filled me. All suffering has vanished, utterly destroyed.
commentary: This is a declaration of complete spiritual freedom. Negative karma (vinai) and the darkness of illusion (maya) are suppressed and permanently destroyed. All suffering is gone, replaced by a constant, overflowing bliss that fills one's entire being.

translit: ammai tirōtai akaṉṟāḷ eṉaivirumpi ammaiyaruṭ catti aṭaintaṉaḷē - immaiyilē māmāyai nīṅkiṉaḷpoṉ vaṇṇavaṭi vuṟṟateṉṟum cāmā ṟilaieṉakkut tāṉ.
translation: Mother Tirodhayi has departed. Loving me, the mother, Arut-Sakti, has arrived. In this very life, Mahamaya has left. My form has become golden, and for me, there is no way to die, ever.
commentary: Vallalar personifies the cosmic forces at play. Tirodhayi, the divine power that veils reality to keep souls in ignorance, has departed. She is replaced by Arut-Sakti, the personified power of Grace, who has lovingly embraced him. As a result of this grace, the grand illusion of the material world (Mahamaya) has left, and his very body has become golden and immortal.

translit: nāṉē tavampurintēṉ nāṉilattīr ampalavaṉ tāṉēvan teṉṉait taṭuttāṇṭāṉ - ūṉē pukuntāṉeṉ uḷḷam pukuntāṉ uyiril pukuntāṉ karuṇai purintu.
translation: O people of the world, I myself performed great penance. The Dancer of the Hall himself came, intervened, and made me his own. Out of compassion, he entered my very flesh, he entered my mind, and he entered my soul.
commentary: He tells the world that his state is the result of his own intense spiritual effort, which drew God to him. The union is absolute. God, the Dancer of the Hall, did more than appear before him but, out of compassion, entered and filled every part of his existence: his physical body, his mind, and his innermost soul. This is a complete and intimate merging.

translit: oṉṟē civameṉ ṟuṇarntēṉ uṇarntāṅku niṉṟēmeyñ ñāṉa nilaipeṟṟēṉ - naṉṟēmeyc cittiyelām peṟṟēṉ tiruampa lattāṭi pattielām peṟṟa palaṉ.
translation: I realized that Sivam is the One. Abiding in that realization, I attained the state of true wisdom. Indeed, I have obtained all the true siddhis; this is the fruit gained from all my devotion to the sacred Dancer of the Ambalam.
commentary: The core realization is that Sivam, the Divine, is the one and only reality. Living from this truth leads directly to the highest wisdom and the attainment of all true siddhis, or spiritual perfections. For Vallalar, these powers are the natural outcome of a life of complete devotion to God, the Dancer of the sacred Hall (Ambalam).

translit: tūkkaṅ keṭuttāṉ cukaṅkoṭuttāṉ eṉṉuḷattē ēkkan tavirttāṉ iruḷaṟuttāṉ - ākkamikat tantāṉ eṉaiīṉṟa tantaiyē eṉṟaḻaikka vantāṉeṉ appaṉ makiḻntu.
translation: He took away my sleep and gave me bliss. He ended the longing in my heart and severed the darkness. He bestowed great flourishing. My Father came with joy, for me to call him, 'The very Father who gave me birth.'
commentary: The relationship with God is depicted as deeply personal and tender. God removes the soul's "sleep" of ignorance, ends its restless searching, and fills it with bliss. This divine being is a nurturing parent, the "very Father who gave me birth," who comes joyfully to be recognized as such. This shifts the focus from awe to deep, intimate love.

translit: vāṭṭamelām tīrttāṉ makiḻvaḷittāṉ meyññāṉa nāṭṭamelām tantāṉ nalaṅkoṭuttāṉ - āṭṭamelām āṭukanī eṉṟāṉtaṉ āṉanta vārkaḻalaip pāṭukanī eṉṟāṉ paraṉ.
translation: He cured all my weariness and granted me joy. He gave me a complete focus on true wisdom and bestowed every good thing. The Supreme One commanded, 'You, perform all the dances,' and, 'You, sing of my long anklet of bliss.'
commentary: Once the devotee is filled with divine joy and wisdom, his life is given a new purpose. The Supreme One (Paran) commands him to "dance" and "sing," meaning his actions and words are no longer his own but become a direct expression of God's blissful play in the world.

translit: tāṉnāṉ eṉumpētan taṉṉait tavirttāṉnāṉ āṉāṉciṟ ṟampalavaṉ antōnāṉ - vāṉāṭar ceytaṟ kariyatavam ceytēṉ makiḻkiṉṟēṉ eytaṟ kariyacukam ēyntu.
translation: He removed the distinction between 'Himself' and 'me'. The Lord of the small hall became me! Oh, I have performed austerities difficult even for the celestials and, having attained a bliss that is hard to reach, I rejoice.
commentary: This is a statement of ultimate union with the divine. Vallalar describes the moment the feeling of a separate self ("me") disappears, and God becomes his entire identity. He experiences a complete merging, a state of bliss so rare that he considers it the fruit of austerities beyond what even heavenly beings can perform.

translit: cutta vaṭivum cukavaṭivām ōṅkāra nitta vaṭivum niṟaintōṅku - citteṉumōr ñāṉa vaṭivumiṅkē nāṉpeṟṟēṉ eṅkeṅkum tāṉaviḷai yāṭṭiyaṟṟat tāṉ.
translation: Here I have received a pure form, the eternal form of Omkara which is bliss itself, and a form of wisdom called consciousness, full and transcendent, so that He may perform His divine play everywhere.
commentary: The spiritual union results in a physical transformation. Vallalar declares that he has received here the three bodies of his path: the pure form (suddha deham), the eternal form of Ōṅkāra (pranava deham), which is bliss itself, and the form of wisdom that is pure consciousness (jñāna deham). These bodies become the perfect instrument for God's divine play to unfold everywhere.

translit: nāṉuraikkum vārttaielām nāyakaṉcol vārttaiaṉṟi nāṉuraikkum vārttaiaṉṟu nāṭṭīrnāṉ - ēṉuraippēṉ nāṉār eṉakkeṉaōr ñāṉa:uṇar vētucivam ūṉnāṭi nillā uḻi.
translation: O people of the world, all the words I speak are the Lord's words; they are not words that I speak. Why would I speak? Who am I? What feeling of wisdom could I possess, if Siva did not stand, inhabiting this physical body?
commentary: This verse is a powerful declaration of being a divine instrument. Vallalar explains that his teachings are not his own opinions or wisdom; they are the direct words of the Lord (Siva) speaking through him. Without the divine presence inhabiting his physical body, he says, there would be no 'I' to speak at all.

translit: āraṇamum ākamamum āṅkāṅ kuraikkiṉṟa kāraṇamum kāriyamum kāṭṭuvittāṉ - tāraṇiyil kaṇṭēṉ kaḷikkiṉṟēṉ kaṅkulpakal aṟṟaviṭat tuṇṭēṉ amutam uvantu.
translation: He revealed to me the cause and effect spoken of in the Vedas and Agamas. Here on earth, I have seen it and I rejoice. In that place beyond night and day, I have joyfully consumed the ambrosia.
commentary: The truths described in the ancient scriptures, the Vedas and Agamas, are more than theories for Vallalar; he has experienced them directly. This experience is a state of timeless joy, like drinking the nectar of immortality, which validates the scriptural teachings for him on a personal level.

translit: tuṉmārkkam ellām tolaittuviṭṭēṉ cuttaciva caṉmārkka caṅkam talaippaṭṭēṉ - eṉmārkkam naṉmārkkam eṉṟēvāṉ nāṭṭār pukaḻkiṉṟār maṉmārkkat tālē makiḻntu.
translation: I have destroyed all wicked paths. I have joined the assembly of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam. The celestials, delighting in this enduring path, praise my way as the good path.
commentary: Here Vallalar declares his allegiance to a single, specific path he calls the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Pure Siva). He presents this as a decisive choice, turning away from all other paths which he now sees as flawed or inadequate.

translit: paṉmārkkam ellām pacaiyaṟ ṟoḻintaṉavē caṉmārkkam oṉṟē taḻaittatuvē - coṉmārkkat tellā ulakum icaintaṉavē emperumāṉ kollā neṟiaruḷaik koṇṭu.
translation: All the many paths have lost their substance and vanished. Only Sanmarkkam has flourished. Because our great Lord has granted the grace of the path of non-killing, all the worlds have come into accord with the path of my word.
commentary: In Vallalar's vision, all other spiritual paths are losing their relevance and fading away. His Sanmarkkam (True Path) alone thrives because it is based on the supreme principle of non-killing. This principle is so powerful and universally true that he sees all worlds consenting to its grace.

translit: cātikulam eṉṟum camayamatam eṉṟumupa nītiiyal āccirama nīṭṭeṉṟum - ōtukiṉṟa pēyāṭṭa mellām pitirntoḻinta vēpiṟartam vāyāṭṭam tīrntaṉavē maṟṟu.
translation: The demonic dances proclaimed as caste and clan, religion and creed, and the drawn-out rules of social conduct and life-stages, all have shattered and ceased. The verbal posturing of others has also ended.
commentary: The arrival of the true spiritual path shatters all the artificial divisions that separate humanity. Vallalar dismisses caste, religious creeds, and rigid social rules as "demonic dances," empty and divisive performances that have now lost their power. What remains is a unified humanity, free from the arguments these structures create.

translit: cintā kulantavirttuc ciṟṟam palapperumāṉ vantāṉ eṉaittāṉ valintaḻaittē - aintoḻilum nīyēcey eṉṟeṉakkē nērntaḷittāṉ eṉṉuṭaiya tāyē aṉaiyāṉ taṉittu.
translation: Dispelling my mind's turmoil, the great Lord of Chitrambalam came. He insistently called me and, by his own will, decreed and granted this to me: "You yourself perform the five cosmic functions." He who is like my own mother did this, alone.
commentary: The Lord of Chitrambalam (the sacred inner space) has given Vallalar a divine commission. He has been tasked with performing the "five cosmic functions": creation, preservation, destruction, concealment, and grace. This is a role traditionally reserved for God alone, indicating a complete fusion of the human and divine will.

translit: kūkā eṉaaṭuttōr kūṭi aḻātavaṇṇam cākā varameṉakkē tantiṭṭāṉ - ēkāaṉ ēkā eṉamaṟaikaḷ ēttuñciṟ ṟampalattāṉ mākā talaṉā makiḻntu.
translation: So that those around me would not gather and wail in mourning, he gave me the boon of never dying. The Lord of Chitrambalam, whom the sacred texts praise as "The One, The Not-One," did this joyfully, as my great lover.
commentary: God has granted Vallalar the boon of physical immortality, so that his loved ones will never have to mourn his death. This ultimate spiritual gift is framed as an act of compassion for others. The giver of this boon, described as both "The One and The Not-One," bestows it with the intimacy of a great lover.

translit: nāṭukiṉṟa temperumāṉ nāṭṭamatē nāṉulakil āṭukiṉṟa tentaiaruḷ āṭṭamatē - pāṭukiṉṟa pāṭṭellām ampalavaṉ pāta malarppāṭṭē nīṭṭellām āṅkavaṉṟaṉ nīṭṭu.
translation: What I seek is the seeking of my great Lord. The dance I dance in the world is the dance of my Father's grace. All the songs I sing are songs of the lotus feet of the Lord of the Ambalam. My every extension is his extension.
commentary: In this state of complete union, there is no longer a distinction between Vallalar's will and God's will. His every seeking, action, and song originates from the Divine. He experiences his entire existence as a dance of God's grace, an extension of the divine presence in the world.

translit: cattiyañcey kiṉṟēṉ cakattīr aṟimiṉkaḷ cittielām valla civamoṉṟē - nittiyameṉ ṟeṇṇumeṇṇat tālēnam eṇṇamelām kaikūṭum naṇṇumiṉpat tēṉeṉṟu nāṉ.
translation: I swear this is true, people of the world, know this! Sivam alone is capable of all siddhis. By the thought that holds It as eternal, all our intentions will be fulfilled and the honey of bliss will come to us. This I swear.
commentary: Vallalar makes a solemn promise: Sivam (the supreme Divine) is the source of all siddhis (supernatural powers). He offers a direct path to fulfillment, by holding the thought of the Divine's eternal nature in the mind. By this simple act, he says, all intentions can be realized.

translit: nāṉē tavampurintēṉ namperumāṉ nallaruḷāl nāṉē aruṭcitti nāṭaṭaintēṉ - nāṉē aḻiyā vaṭivam avaimūṉṟum peṟṟēṉ iḻiyāmal āṭukiṉṟēṉ iṅku.
translation: By our great Lord's good grace, I myself performed tapas. I myself reached the land of grace-siddhi. I myself obtained the three immortal bodies. Without any decline, I dance here.
commentary: Grace is the key that unlocks spiritual attainment. Through God's grace, Vallalar performed the necessary spiritual practices (tapas) and achieved a state of perfected power (siddhi). He then announces a specific, extraordinary result: obtaining the three immortal bodies, a central attainment in his path that promises a deathless physical existence. His "dance" is a life of joyful, perfected being.

translit: evvulakum aṇṭaṅkaḷ ettaṉaiyum nāṉkāṇa ivvulakil entai eṉakkaḷittāṉ - evvuyirum caṉmārkka caṅkam taṉaiaṭaiyac ceyvittē eṉmārkkam kāṇpēṉ iṉi.
