translation: My Father granted me in this world the ability to see all worlds and countless universes. After making every living being reach the Sanmarkka Sangam, I will then realize my own path.
commentary: Having received the vision of all worlds and countless universes, Vallalar declares what he will do with it: bring every living being into the Sanmarkka Sangam (the fellowship of the true path). Only when all lives have reached it will he regard his path as fulfilled. His attainment is bound to the good of every being.

translit: cāttiraṅkaḷ ellām taṭumāṟṟam colvataṉṟi nēttiraṅkaḷ pōṟkāṭṭa nērāvē - nēttiraṅkaḷ ciṟṟam palavaṉ tiruvaruṭcīr vaṇṇameṉṟē uṟṟiṅ kaṟintēṉ uvantu.
translation: All the sastras only speak of confusion; they cannot show things clearly like eyes can. I have joyfully realized here that true eyes are the very nature of the glorious grace of the Lord of Chitrambalam.
commentary: All the sastras (scriptures), Vallalar declares, speak nothing but confusion; they cannot show reality as eyes do. True 'eyes', the power to see reality clearly, are not necessarily the physical organs but the glorious nature of divine grace itself. This grace, associated with the Chitrambalam (the inner space of consciousness), is the only reliable guide. He places grace-given seeing above the authority of any text.

translit: vētāka maṅkaḷeṉṟu vīṇvātam āṭukiṉṟīr vētāka mattiṉ viḷaivaṟiyīr - cūtākac coṉṉavalāl uṇmaiveḷi tōṉṟa uraikkavilai eṉṉa payaṉō ivai.
translation: You engage in pointless arguments, citing the Vedas and Agamas. You do not know the true outcome of the Vedas and Agamas. They were spoken deceptively, not uttered to make the expanse of truth appear openly. Of what use are they?
commentary: Arguing over sacred texts like the Vedas and Agamas is a waste of time. Vallalar makes the sharp claim that these ancient scriptures were written in a way that veils truth, leading to endless debate instead of direct realization. He questions their ultimate value, urging people to seek the open expanse of truth itself rather than getting lost in doctrinal disputes.

translit: cākāta kalvit taramaṟital vēṇṭumeṉṟum vēkāta kāluṇartal vēṇṭumuṭaṉ - cākāt talaiaṟital vēṇṭum taṉiaruḷāl uṇmai nilaiaṭaital vēṇṭum nilattu.
translation: One must know the standard of deathless learning, perceive the unconsumed vital principle, and know the deathless head-principle; by singular Grace, one must attain the true state right here on earth.
commentary: The true spiritual goal is to achieve a deathless physical body, right here on earth. This transformation requires mastering three key areas: the knowledge that confers immortality, the body's vital principle so it is never depleted, and the highest center of consciousness in the head (Sahakalai). This state is not attained through human effort alone, but is granted by a singular, focused Grace.

translit: poyuraieṉ ṟeṇṇutirēl pōmiṉ puṟakkaṭaiyil meyyuraieṉ ṟeṇṇutirēl mēvumiṉō - aiyaṉaruḷ cittielām valla tirukkūt tulavāmal ittiṉantoṭ ṭāṭukiṟpāṉ iṅku.
translation: If you think these are false words, go to the outer gate. If you think they are true words, draw near. The Lord, whose sacred dance, empowered by Grace, is capable of all siddhis, will perform it here unceasingly, starting from this very day.
commentary: A direct invitation is given to either accept this truth or step aside. Vallalar announces that the Lord's divine activity, a sacred dance of grace capable of all siddhis (supernatural powers), is starting now and will continue without end. It is a present reality for those who have the faith to draw near and witness it.

translit: vāṉvanta tēvarkaḷum mālayaṉum maṟṟavarum tāṉvantu cūḻntār talaikkaṭaiyil - tēṉvanta maṅkai civakāma valliyoṭum emperumāṉ iṅkunaṭañ ceyvāṉ iṉi.
translation: The celestials from the heavens, Vishnu, Brahma, and the others have all come and gathered at the main gate. Our great Lord, with the honey-sweet maiden Sivakama Valli, will now perform His dance here.
commentary: The divine event Vallalar announces is of cosmic significance. He paints a scene where even the great gods of the heavens, including Vishnu and Brahma, have gathered as spectators. The main event is the dance of the Supreme Lord with His consort Sivakama Valli, who personifies divine grace, signifying a new and powerful manifestation of compassion on Earth for all to see.

translit: cattielām koṇṭataṉit tantai naṭarāyaṉ cittielām vallāṉ tiruvāḷaṉ - nittiyaṉtāṉ ūḻipala ceṉṟālum ōvāmal ivviṭattē vāḻinaṭañ ceyvāṉ makiḻntu.
translation: Natarajan, the singular Father who holds all powers, the Lord of Grace capable of all siddhis, He, the eternal one, will joyfully live and perform His dance in this very place without ceasing, even if many eons should pass.
commentary: The divine dance is an eternal and joyful presence. Vallalar declares that God, as Natarajan (the Lord of the Dance), will perform here forever, making this place a permanent center of divine power that will outlast even cosmic ages.

translit: iṉṟu toṭaṅkiyiṅkē emperumāṉ ennāḷum naṉṟu tulaṅka naṭampurivāṉ - eṉṟumeṉcol cattiyameṉ ṟeṇṇic cakattīr aṭaimiṉkaḷ nittiyampeṟ ṟuyyalām nīr.
translation: Starting today, our great Lord will perform His dance here for all time so that goodness may shine brightly. O people of the world, considering my words to be eternally true, take refuge. You can attain the eternal state and be saved.
commentary: The vision of the eternal dance becomes a direct path to salvation for everyone. Vallalar urges all people to believe his words and come to this place, promising that by doing so, they can attain an eternal, liberated state of being.

translit: eṉuṭalum eṉporuḷum eṉuyirum tāṉkoṇṭāṉ taṉuṭalum taṉporuḷum taṉuyirum - eṉṉiṭattē tantāṉ aruṭciṟ capaiyappā eṉṟaḻaittēṉ vantāṉvan tāṉuḷ makiḻntu.
translation: He took my body, my possessions, and my life. He gave his body, his possessions, and his life to me. I called out, "Father of the gracious Hall of Consciousness!" and he came, he came, with inner joy.
commentary: This verse reveals the core of Vallalar's union with God: a complete and mutual exchange. The soul gives its entire self, body and life included, and in return, God gives His own divine self. This total surrender is what allows him to call upon God as a responsive "Father" in the "Hall of Consciousness".

translit: cettārai ellām tirumpa eḻupputaliṅ kettāl muṭiyumeṉil emmavarē - cittām aruṭperuñ cōti ataṉāl muṭiyum teruṭperuñ cattiyamī tē.
translation: O my people, if you ask how it is possible to raise all the dead back to life here, it is accomplished by ArutPerunJothi, which is the power of consciousness. This is the great, clear truth.
commentary: Vallalar makes one of his boldest claims: the power of divine grace can even reverse death. When asked how raising the dead is possible, he answers that it is accomplished through the power of ArutPerunJothi, the Grace-Great Light. He states it literally, as a clear, absolute truth.

translit: ivvulakil cettārai ellām eḻukaeṉil evvulakum pōṟṟa eḻuntiruppār - cevvulakil ciṟṟam palattāṉ tiruvaruḷpeṟ ṟārnōkkam uṟṟavarai uṟṟavarkaḷ uṟṟu.
translation: TRANSLATION: If those who are joined to the ones who have received the gaze of those graced by the Lord of Chitrambalam in the perfect world should say to all the dead of this world, 'Arise!', they will rise, praised by every world. COMMENTARY: The power to revive the dead flows outward from grace. Not only those who have received the Lord's grace, but those who have received their gaze, and even those who have come close to these, can say 'Arise!' and the dead will rise. Grace is a living force that is passed on from one to another.
commentary: The power to revive the dead can flow through a person who has achieved divine grace. The simple gaze of such a person is enough to raise the deceased, and this power even extends to those who were close to the person being revived. This shows grace as a tangible force that can be transmitted.

translit: yāṉpurital vēṇṭuṅkol ivvulakil cettārai ūṉpurintu mīḷa uyirppittal - vāṉ purinta ampalattāṉ nallaruḷāl antōnāṉ mēṟpōrtta kampalattāl ākum kaḷittu.
translation: Do I even need to perform this act myself, remaking the flesh to revive the dead in this world? Ah, by the good grace of the Lord of Ambalam, who is desired by the heavens, it can be accomplished joyfully by the very blanket I have wrapped around myself.
commentary: The divine power to give life is so completely integrated into a transformed person that they do not even need to consciously perform the act. Vallalar says the very blanket he wears, infused with the grace of the Lord of Ambalam (the celestial Hall of consciousness), can accomplish this miracle. The power becomes a natural attribute, not a willed effort.

translit: eṉṉē ulakil iṟantār eḻutalmika aṉṉē aticayameṉ ṟāṭukiṉṟār - iṉṉē tiruvam palattāṉ tirunōkkam peṟṟārk kuruvam palattēeṉ ṟuṉ.
translation: What wonder! They dance and exclaim, "Oh, what a miracle that the dead in the world are rising!" Know this: for those who have this day received the sacred gaze of the Lord of the Holy Hall, their form exists in many places at once.
commentary: While the world marvels at the miracle of the dead rising, Vallalar explains its cause. Those who have received God's grace are no longer bound to a single physical body and can exist in many places simultaneously. This ability is a natural result of their union with the divine.

translit: āṭātīr caṟṟum acaiyātīr vēṟoṉṟai nāṭātīr poyulakai nampātīr - vāṭātīr caṉmārkka caṅkattaic cārvīr viraintiṉiiṅ keṉmārkka mumoṉṟā mē.
translation: Do not waver, do not be agitated in the slightest. Do not seek anything else. Do not trust the false world. Do not languish. Quickly join the Sanmarkka Sangam. Hereafter, here, every path shall become one.
commentary: After describing these possibilities, Vallalar gives direct advice for how to attain them. He urges people to turn away from worldly distractions and attachments and instead join the Sanmarkka Sangam, the community he established. He presents this path of truth, compassion, and worship of light as the definitive way forward.

translit: mārkkamelām oṉṟākum mānilattīr vāymaiitu tūkkamelām nīkkit tuṇintuḷattē - ēkkamviṭṭuc caṉmārkka caṅkattaic cārntiṭumiṉ cattiyamnīr naṉmārkkam cērvīrin nāḷ.
translation: O people of this great world, all paths will become one. This is the truth. Shaking off all slumber and with determination in your hearts, abandon your sorrow. Join the Sanmarkka Sangam. Truly, you will attain the good path this very day.
commentary: All spiritual and religious paths are ultimately destined to merge into a single, universal truth. Vallalar presents his Sanmarkkam as the most direct expression of this unified way. He urges people to stop hesitating and join, promising that they can find the right path immediately.

translit: innāḷē kaṇṭīr iṟantār eḻukiṉṟa naṉṉāḷeṉ vārttaikaḷai nampumiṉō - innāḷ aruṭperuñ cōti aṭaikiṉṟa nāḷmey aruṭperuñ cattiyamī tām.
translation: See for yourselves: this very day is the auspicious day when the dead rise. Believe my words! This day is the day of attaining ArutPerunJothi. This itself is the true, great grace-truth.
commentary: The time for spiritual fulfillment is right now. Vallalar declares that this very day holds the potential for the promised miracles, including the rising of the dead and the attainment of ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light. It is a statement of immediate possibility.

translit: ēmān tirukkum emaraṅkāḷ ivvulakil cāmāntar ākāt tarampeṟavē - kāmānta kārattai viṭṭuk karutumiṉō ittaruṇam nīrattaic cērvīr nijam.
translation: O my people living in delusion! To attain a state in this world where you will not die, abandon the utter darkness of desire and contemplate this. At this very moment, you will attain the true state. This is certain.
commentary: The path to a deathless life in this world requires a fundamental shift in consciousness. The main obstacle is what Vallalar calls the "utter darkness of desire." By turning away from craving and toward contemplation of God, one can achieve the immortal state this very moment.

translit: vīṇē parākkil viṭātīr umatuḷattai nāṇē uṭaiya namaraṅkāḷ - ūṇākat teḷḷamutam iṉṟeṉakkuc cērttaḷittāṉ cittāṭa uḷḷiyanāḷ ītaṟimiṉ uṟṟu.
translation: O my people, you who possess modesty, do not let your minds wander in vain! He has gathered and given me clear ambrosia as food today. Understand deeply that this is the day He intended for the play of divine powers.
commentary: Vallalar shares a personal experience of receiving divine ambrosia, the food of the gods, as a sign of his union with the divine. He announces that this event marks the beginning of a new era, a time when extraordinary spiritual powers, known as Siddhis, will become manifest. The age of miracles has arrived.

translit: pōṟṟi uraikkiṉṟēṉ poyeṉ ṟikaḻātīr nāṟṟicaikkaṇ vāḻum namaraṅkāḷ - āṟṟalaruḷ appaṉvaru kiṉṟāṉ aruḷviḷaiyāṭ ṭāṭutaṟkeṉ ṟippuviyil ittaruṇam iṅku.
translation: O our people living in the four directions, I declare this in praise, do not scorn it as a lie: the Father of powerful grace is coming to this earth, here, at this very moment, to perform his play of grace.
commentary: The sense of urgency intensifies as Vallalar insists he is speaking the literal truth. He proclaims that God, the "Father of powerful grace," is arriving here and now. It is a present reality unfolding, a divine "play" about to begin on earth.

translit: āḷuṭaiyāṉ nammuṭaiya appaṉ varukiṉṟa nāḷetuvō eṉṟu naliyātīr - nīḷa niṉaiyātīr cattiyamnāṉ nērnturaittēṉ innāḷ aṉaiyāṉ varukiṉṟāṉ āyntu.
translation: Do not torment yourselves wondering which day our ruling Master, our Father, will come. Do not ponder it at length. I solemnly declare this as the truth: He is coming this very day. Know this for certain.
commentary: Vallalar comforts those who are anxious about when God's grace will manifest. He makes a solemn promise, declaring it as the truth, that the day has arrived. The message is to let go of anxious waiting and to recognize that the divine presence is here and now.

sections.title: The Practice of Wisdom (Beating the Mouth-drum)

translit: niṉaintuniṉain tuṇarntuṇarntu nekiḻntunekiḻn taṉpē niṟaintuniṟain tūṟṟeḻuṅkaṇṇīrataṉāl uṭampu naṉaintunaṉain taruḷamutē naṉṉitiyē ñāṉa naṭattaracē eṉṉurimai nāyakaṉē eṉṟu vaṉaintuvaṉain tēttutumnām vammiṉula kiyalīr maraṇamilāp peruvāḻvil vāḻntiṭalām kaṇṭīr puṉainturaiyēṉ poypukalēṉ cattiyañcol kiṉṟēṉ poṟcapaiyil ciṟcapaiyil pukuntaruṇam ituvē.
translation: Thinking and thinking, realizing and realizing, melting and melting, becoming utterly filled with love, our bodies drenched in the tears that spring forth, let us praise him, crafting our words again and again, saying: "O ambrosia of grace! O true treasure! O King of the wisdom-dance! O Lord who is rightfully mine!" Come, people of the world! You see, we can live the great life without death. I do not speak with embellishment; I do not tell lies. I am speaking the truth. This is the opportune moment to enter the Golden Hall and the Hall of Consciousness.
commentary: This verse describes the inner process of devotion, a cascade of feeling that moves from contemplation to realization, to the heart "melting" in love. This intense emotional state, where the body is drenched in tears of bliss, is the true way to praise God. Vallalar presents this devotional ecstasy as the direct path to a deathless life and the key to entering the sacred spaces of the Poṟsabai (Golden Hall) and Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness).

translit: pukuntaruṇam itukaṇṭīr nammavarē nāṉtāṉ pukalkiṉṟēṉ eṉmoḻiōr poymoḻieṉ ṉātīr ukuntaruṇam uṟṟavarum peṟṟavarum piṟarum uṭaimaikaḷum ulakiyalum uṟṟatuṇai aṉṟē mikuntacuvaik karumpēceṅ kaṉiyēkōṟ ṟēṉē meyppayaṉē kaipporuḷē vilaiyaṟiyā maṇiyē takuntataṉip perumpatiyē tayānitiyē katiyē cattiyamē eṉṟuraimiṉ pattiyoṭu paṇintē.
translation: See, this is the opportune moment to enter! O our people, it is I who am telling you; do not say my words are false. At the moment your body falls, relatives, parents, others, possessions, and worldly affairs are not true support. Bow with devotion and declare: "O sugarcane of immense sweetness! O ripe red fruit! O pure honey! O true fruition! O wealth in hand! O priceless gem! O worthy, peerless, great Lord! O treasure of compassion! O refuge! O Truth!"
commentary: Vallalar repeats his urgent call, emphasizing that worldly relationships and possessions offer no real help when the body dies. The only true refuge is God. He provides a list of devotional names, describing God as the ultimate sweetness, the most valuable treasure, and the source of all compassion. To call upon God with these names, with sincere devotion, is the only meaningful act in the face of mortality.

translit: paṇintupaṇin taṇintaṇintu pāṭumiṉō ulakīr paramparamē citamparamē parāparamē varamē tuṇintuvanta vētānta cuttaaṉu pavamē turiyamuṭi aṉupavamē cuttacittān tamatāyt taṇintanilaip peruñcukamē camaracacaṉ mārkka cattiyamē iyaṟkaiyuṇmait taṉippatiyē eṉṟu kaṇintuḷattē kaṉintuniṉain turaittiṭilap poḻutē kāṇāta kāṭcielām kaṇṭukoḷa lāmē.
translation: Bow down again and again, draw near again and again, and sing, O people of the world! Declare: "O Supreme One! O Chidambaram! O Transcendent-Immanent One! O greatest Boon! O pure experience of Vedanta, boldly realized! O experience at the summit of Turiya! O great bliss of the tranquil state which is pure Siddhanta! O Truth of Samarasa Sanmarkkam! O unique Lord of natural Truth!" If you think this and speak with a heart that cherishes and melts, at that very moment, you can see all the sights that have never been seen.
commentary: True praise comes from a heart that melts in devotion. Vallalar lists names for God that embrace different spiritual traditions, calling God the essence of Vedanta and Siddhanta (major schools of Indian philosophy), the experience beyond ordinary consciousness (Turiya), and the truth of his own Samarasa Sanmarkkam (Path of Harmonious Truth). He says that if we can feel this in our hearts, more than say the words, we will be granted visions of things beyond ordinary sight.

translit: kaṇṭatelām anittiyamē kēṭṭatelām paḻutē kaṟṟatelām poyyēnīr kaḷittatelām vīṇē uṇṭatelām malamēuṭ koṇṭatelām kuṟaiyē ulakiyalīr ituvaraiyum uṇmaiyaṟin tilirē viṇṭataṉāl eṉiṉinīr camaracacaṉ mārkka meynneṟiyaik kaṭaippiṭittu meypporuḷnaṉ kuṇarntē eṇṭakuciṟ ṟampalattē entaiaruḷ aṭaimiṉ iṟavāta varampeṟalām iṉpamuṟa lāmē.
translation: All that has been seen is transient; all that has been heard is worthless; all that has been learned is false; all that you have rejoiced in is pointless. All that has been eaten is filth; all that has been imbibed is deficient. O people of the world! Until now, have you not known the truth? Now that I have revealed this, you must follow the true path of Samarasa Sanmarkkam, realize the true substance well, and attain the grace of my Father in the revered Hall of Consciousness. You can receive the boon of deathlessness and attain bliss.
commentary: All our ordinary worldly pursuits, including what we see, learn, and enjoy, are empty and fleeting. Vallalar's words are a wake-up call, asking why we remain ignorant of this fundamental truth. He points to his path, the Samarasa Sanmarkkam, as the one way to realize what is truly real and permanent. By following it, one can receive divine grace and the greatest gift: a life without death.

translit: iṉpuṟalām evvulakum ēttiṭavāḻn tiṭalām ellāmcey vallacitti iṟaimaiyumpeṟ ṟiṭalām aṉpuṭaiyīr vammiṉiṅkē camaracacaṉ mārkkam aṭaintiṭumiṉ akavaṭiviṅ kaṉakavaṭi vākip poṉpuṭainaṉ koḷiroḷiyē puttamutē ñāṉa pūraṇamē āraṇattiṉ poruḷmuṭimēl poruḷē vaṉpuṭaiyār peṟaṟkaritām maṇiyēciṟ capaiyiṉ māmaruntē eṉṟuraimiṉ tīmaiyelām tavirntē.
translation: You can attain bliss. You can live praised by all worlds. You can obtain the siddhi of all-accomplishing might and sovereignty. O loving ones, come here! Enter Samarasa Sanmarkkam. Your inner form becomes a golden form here. Forsaking all evil, declare: "O light shining brightly, surrounded by gold! O new ambrosia! O perfection of wisdom! O Substance upon the crown of the meaning of the Vedas! O gem unattainable by the hard-hearted! O great medicine of the Hall of Consciousness!"
commentary: The rewards of this path are total: bliss and praise from all worlds and even siddhi (supernatural power). Vallalar invites all loving people to join the Samarasa Sanmarkkam, where a great transformation occurs: the physical body itself becomes a radiant golden form. The path requires abandoning all that is harmful and turning to God, who is praised as the "great medicine" that heals all ills and grants eternal life.

translit: tīmaielām naṉmaieṉṟē tiruuḷaṅkoṇ ṭaruḷic ciṟiyēṉuk karuḷamutat teḷivaḷitta tiṟattai āmayantīrt tiyaṟkaiiṉpa aṉupavamē mayamāy ampalattē viḷaṅkukiṉṟa aruṭperuñcō tiyaiōr ōmayavāṉ vaṭivuṭaiyār uḷḷakattē niṟainta oruporuḷaip peruṅkaruṇai uṭaiyaperum patiyai nāmaruvi iṟavāta nalampeṟalām ulakīr nallaoru taruṇamitu vallaivammiṉ nīrē.
translation: He graciously took all evils as good and gave me, a lowly one, the clarity of gracious nectar. He is the one who cured my affliction and is the very embodiment of natural, blissful experience. He is the ArutPerunJothi shining in the Ambalam. He is the One Substance who fills the hearts of those whose very form is the great Om. He is the Great Lord of immense compassion. O people of the world, we can approach him and receive the blessing of deathlessness. This is a good opportunity. Come quickly, all of you.
commentary: God's compassion is so immense that it sees even our failings as good, transforming them into a gift of grace. This God is the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light) shining in the Ambalam (sacred space), a being of pure compassion. Vallalar insists that this is the perfect moment for everyone to approach this compassionate Lord and gain the gift of a deathless life.

translit: nīrpiṟarō yāṉumakku nēya:uṟa valaṉō neṭumoḻiyē uraippaṉaṉṟik koṭumoḻicol vēṉō cārpuṟavē aruḷamutam tanteṉaiyēmēl ēṟṟit taṉittaperum cukamaḷitta taṉittaperum patitāṉ cīrpeṟavē tiruppotuvil tirumēṉi tarittuc cittāṭal purikiṉṟa tirunāḷkaḷ aṭutta ōrpuṟavē itunalla taruṇamiṅkē vammiṉ ulakiyalīr uṉṉiyavā ṟuṟṟiṭuvīr viraintē.
translation: Are you strangers? Am I not a loving relative to you? I speak only profound truths; would I ever speak harsh words? The unique Great Lord gave me gracious nectar for support, elevated me, and granted me unique, great bliss. The sacred days when he, having taken a sacred form in the glorious sacred hall, performs his Siddha-play are near. This is a good opportunity. Come here, O people of the world! You will quickly attain all that you desire.
commentary: Vallalar speaks here with the intimacy of a loving family member pleading with his listeners to trust him. He assures them that the time is near for God to perform His Siddha-play, a display of divine, miraculous power in the world. His message is one of urgent invitation, emphasizing that this rare opportunity is at hand.

translit: viraintuvirain taṭaintiṭumiṉ mētiṉiyīr iṅkē meymaiuraik kiṉṟēṉnīr vēṟuniṉai yātīr tiraintutirain tuḷuttavarum iḷamaiaṭain tiṭavum cettavarkaḷ eḻuntiṭavum cittāṭal puriya varaintuvarain tellāñcey vallacittaṉ tāṉē varukiṉṟa taruṇamitu varampeṟalām nīvīr karaintukarain tuḷamurukik kaṇkaḷiṉnīr perukik karuṇainaṭak kaṭavuḷaiuṭ karutumiṉō kaḷittē.
translation: Hurry, hurry and come here, people of the earth! I am telling you the truth; do not think otherwise. This is the moment the All-Powerful Siddhan himself is coming, to perform the Siddha-play where even the wrinkled and wasted will regain their youth and the dead will rise. You can all receive boons. With hearts melting completely and tears streaming from your eyes, joyfully contemplate within you the God of the compassionate dance.
commentary: The urgency intensifies with a promise of physical miracles. Vallalar announces the coming of the all-powerful Siddhan (one with perfected miraculous powers), whose divine play will make the old young again and even raise the dead. The way to prepare for this event is through deep, heartfelt emotion: to contemplate God with a melting heart and tears of joy.

translit: kaḷittulakil aḷavikanta kālamula kellām kaḷippaṭaiya aruṭcōtik kaṭavuḷvaru taruṇam teḷittiṭumet taruṇamatō eṉṉātīr ituvē cettavarai eḻuppukiṉṟa tikaḻtaruṇam ulakīr oḷitturaikkiṉ ṟēṉalaṉnāṉ vāyppaṟaiārk kiṉṟēṉ oruciṟitum accamuṟēṉ uḷḷapaṭi uṇarntēṉ aḷittiṭuciṟ ṟampalatteṉ appaṉaruḷ peṟavē ācaiuṇṭēl vammiṉiṅkē nēcamuṭai yīrē.
translation: Do not ask, "When is that moment of clarity?" This is the very moment the God of Grace-Light is coming so that the whole world can rejoice for immeasurable time. This is the glorious moment when the dead are raised, O people of the world! I am not speaking in secret; I am beating the drum with my mouth and shouting it. I feel not the slightest fear, for I have realized the truth as it is. If you desire to receive the grace of my Father in the bountiful Chitrambalam, come here, you who are filled with love.
commentary: The promised age of miracles is happening right now. Vallalar declares this truth openly and fearlessly, like a town crier shouting the news, because he has experienced it himself. He makes a final, urgent call: anyone who truly desires God's grace from the Chitrambalam (the little hall of consciousness) should come immediately.

translit: ācaiuṇṭēl vammiṉ iṅkē aruṭcōtip perumāṉ ammaiyumāy appaṉumāy aruḷumaru ḷāḷaṉ ēcaṟanīt teṉaiāṭkoṇ ṭeṇṇiyavā ṟaḷittāṉ ellāñcey vallacittaṉ eṉṉuyiril kalantāṉ tēcuṭaiya potuvilaruḷ cittinaṭam puriyat tiruvuḷaṅkoṇ ṭeḻuntaruḷum tirunāḷiṅ kituvē mōca:urai eṉaniṉaittu mayaṅkātīr ulakīr mukkālat tiṉumaḻiyā mūrttamaṭain tiṭavē.
translation: If you have the desire, come here. The great Lord ArutPerunJothi is the Gracious One who bestows grace as both Mother and Father. He removed all my faults, made me his own, and granted my every wish. The All-Powerful Siddhan has mingled with my very life. This right here is the sacred day he has graciously willed to arrive, to perform the dance of grace and siddhi in the radiant common space. Do not be confused, thinking these are deceitful words, O people of the world. Come, so that you may attain a form that is indestructible through all three divisions of time.
commentary: Vallalar grounds his public announcement in his own intimate experience: the divine, who is both Mother and Father, has removed his faults and merged with his very being. The promise he extends to others is the same one he has received, the attainment of a deathless physical form. This transformation from a mortal to an indestructible state is the siddhi (perfected attainment) now available to everyone.

translit: aṭaintiṭumiṉ ulakīriṅ kitutaruṇam kaṇṭīr aruṭcōtip perumpatieṉ appaṉvaru taruṇam kaṭaintataṉit tiruvamutam kaḷittarutti eṉakkē kāṇāta kāṭcielām kāṭṭukiṉṟa taruṇam iṭaintorucār alaiyātīr cukameṉaippōl peṟuvīr yāṉvēṟu nīrvēṟeṉ ṟeṇṇukilēṉ uraittēṉ uṭaintacama yakkuḻiniṉ ṟeḻuntuṇarmiṉ aḻiyā oruneṟiyām caṉmārkkat tiruneṟipeṟ ṟuvantē.
translation: O people of the world, come and join! See, this is the opportune moment. It is the moment my Father, the great Lord of Grace-Light, is coming. It is the moment He, having churned the unique, sacred ambrosia and joyfully fed it to me, shows me all the sights never seen before. Do not wander about, distressed. You will attain bliss just as I have. I do not consider myself to be separate and you to be separate; I have spoken. Rise up and become aware, leaving the pit of broken religions, having received and rejoiced in the sacred path of Sanmarkkam, the one imperishable way.
commentary: Here, Vallalar expresses a profound sense of unity with all people, declaring, "I do not consider myself to be separate and you to be separate." He invites everyone to share in the bliss he has found by leaving behind what he calls the "pit of broken religions." In their place, he offers Sanmarkkam (the true path), presented not as another religion, but as the one, universal way to an imperishable life.

translit: tiruneṟioṉ ṟēatutāṉ camaracacaṉ mārkkac civaneṟieṉ ṟuṇarntulakīr cērntiṭumiṉ īṇṭu varuneṟiyil eṉaiyāṭkoṇ ṭaruḷamutam aḷittu vallapacat tikaḷellām vaḻaṅkiyaōr vaḷḷal peruneṟiyil cittāṭat tiruvuḷaṅkoṇ ṭaruḷip peruṅkaruṇai vaṭiviṉoṭu varutaruṇam ituvē karuneṟivīḻn tuḻalātīr kalakkamaṭai yātīr kaṇmaiyiṉāl karuttorumit tuṇmaiurait tēṉē.
translation: There is only one sacred path. O people of the world, realize it is the Siva-path of Samarasa Sanmarkkam and join it here. A Benefactor took me as his slave on the path I came, gave me the ambrosia of grace, and bestowed all the Vallabha Saktis. He has graciously willed to perform his Siddhi-play on the great path, and this is the very moment He is coming in a form of great compassion. Do not fall into the dark path and struggle; do not be agitated. Out of compassion, with a unified mind, I have spoken the truth.
commentary: The one true path is given a specific name: Samarasa Sanmarkkam, the way of harmony and unity. Vallalar clarifies that his own extraordinary abilities, the Vallabha Saktis (powers of omnipotence), were gifts freely given by a compassionate divine benefactor. It is this same generous God, he announces, who is now arriving to share this grace with the world.

translit: uṇmaiyuraik kiṉṟēṉiṅ kuvantaṭaimiṉ ulakīr uraiitaṉil cantēkit tuḷaṟivaḻi yātīr eṇmaiyiṉāṉ eṉaniṉaiyīr ellāñcey vallāṉ eṉṉuḷamarn ticaikkiṉṟāṉ itukēṇmiṉ nīvir taṇmaiyoṭu cuttaciva caṉmārkka neṟiyil cārntuvirain tēṟumiṉō cattiyavāḻ vaḷikkak kaṇmaitarum oruperuñcīrk kaṭavuḷeṉap pukalum karuṇainiti varukiṉṟa taruṇamitu tāṉē.
translation: I am speaking the truth; O people of the world, joyfully come and join here. Do not doubt these words and get lost, babbling incoherently. Do not think of me as a simple man. The One who can do everything is seated within me and is speaking. You must listen to this! Join and quickly ascend the path of Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam with tranquility. This is indeed the moment that the Treasury of Compassion, praised as the God of great glory who bestows compassion to grant the life of truth, is coming.
commentary: Vallalar makes his most direct claim: he speaks as a vessel for God. "The One who can do everything is seated within me and is speaking," he declares, urging people to listen to the divine message itself. The path he points to, Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (the pure and true path), leads to a life of truth granted by the arriving "Treasury of Compassion."

translit: tāṉētāṉ ākielām tāṉāki alaṉāyt taṉippatiyāy viḷaṅkiṭumeṉ tantaiyaieṉ tāyai vāṉēav vāṉkaruvē vāṉkaruviṉ mutalē vaḷḷāleṉ ṟaṉparelām uḷḷāniṉ ṟavaṉait tēṉēcem pākēeṉ ṟiṉittiṭunteḷ ḷamutaic ciṟcapaiyil peruvāḻvaic cintaiceymiṉ ulakīr ūṉēyum uṭalaḻiyā tūḻitoṟum ōṅkum uttamacit tiyaippeṟuvīr cattiyamcoṉ ṉēṉē.
translation: O people of the world, contemplate him: my Father, my Mother, who shines as the sole Lord, being Himself, becoming all things, and yet being none of them. Contemplate him whom all devotees meditate on, calling him "O Sky! O Embryo of that sky! O Origin of that embryo! O Benefactor!". Contemplate the clear ambrosia that is sweet like honey and fine syrup, the great life in the Chit Sabhai. You will attain the supreme Siddhi, where the fleshly body does not perish but flourishes through eons. I have spoken the truth.
commentary: The path to attaining a perfected, immortal body is to contemplate God's paradoxical nature. This God is everything yet beyond everything, both a personal father and mother and the formless origin of the cosmos. By focusing on this divine presence, which he experiences as a sweet ambrosia in the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness), one can achieve the supreme Siddhi (spiritual perfection): a physical body that does not decay but flourishes for ages.

translit: cattiyavē tāntamelām cittānta mellām taṉittaṉimēl uṇarntuṇarntum taṉaiyuṇartaṟ karitāy nittiyaciṟ capainaṭuvē niṟaintunaṭam puriyum nittapari pūraṇaṉaic cittacikā maṇiyai attakaiyōr perumpatiyai arumaruntai aṭiyēṉ āviyaieṉ āviyilē amarntatayā nitiyaic cittiyelām eṉakkaḷitta civakatiyai ulakīr cintaiceytu vāḻttumiṉō nintaielām tavirntē.
translation: He is difficult to realize in himself, even after one has progressively realized all of true Vedanta and all of Siddhanta. He is the eternally perfect one, the crest-jewel of Siddhas, who pervades and dances in the center of the eternal Chit Sabhai. He is such a great Lord, the rare medicine, my very soul, the treasury of compassion seated within my soul, the Sivagati that granted me all Siddhis. O people of the world, having abandoned all blame, contemplate and praise him.
commentary: Even mastering the highest paths, Vedanta and Siddhanta, is not enough to truly know God. Realization comes from knowing God as a living presence, the 'treasury of compassion seated within my soul'. This indwelling God is the Sivagati, the final refuge, who has granted Vallalar all Siddhis (spiritual perfections).

translit: nintaiyilār neñcakattē niṟaintaperun takaiyai nilaiyaṉaittum kāṭṭiyaruḷ nilaiaḷitta kuruvai entaiyaieṉ taṉittāyai eṉṉirukaṇ maṇiyai eṉuyirai eṉuṇarvai eṉaṟivuḷ aṟivai cintaiyilē taṉittiṉikkum teḷḷamutai aṉaittum ceyyavalla taṉittalaimaic civapatiyai ulakīr muntaimala iruṭṭoḻiya muṉṉumiṉō karaṇa muṭukkoḻittuk kaṭaimaraṇa naṭukkoḻittu muyaṉṟē.
translation: O people of the world, strive! Eradicate the agitation of your inner faculties and the trembling fear of the final death. To dispel the primordial darkness of impurity, contemplate the great One who fills the hearts of the blameless; the Guru who revealed all states and granted the ultimate state; my father, my unique mother, the apple of my eye; my life, my feeling, the awareness within my awareness; the clear ambrosia uniquely sweet in the mind; the singular, sovereign Lord Sivan who can do all things.
commentary: To overcome the fear of death and the mind's inner turmoil, one must focus on God. This focus is on the divine experienced intimately as a parent, a Guru (spiritual teacher), one's own life, and the awareness within one's awareness. By meditating on this inner, compassionate Lord, the primordial darkness of impurity is dispelled, quieting the restless inner faculties (karaṇam) and freeing one from the terror of mortality.

translit: muyaṉṟulakil payaṉaṭaiyā mūṭamatam aṉaittum muṭukiaḻin tiṭavumoru mōcamumil lātē iyaṉṟaoru caṉmārkkam eṅkunilai peṟavum emmiṟaivaṉ eḻuntaruḷal itutaruṇam kaṇṭīr tuyiṉṟuṇarntē eḻuntavarpōl iṟantavarkaḷ ellām tōṉṟaeḻu kiṉṟatitu toṭaṅkinikaḻn tiṭumnīr payiṉṟaṟiya viraintuvammiṉ paṭiyāta paṭippaip paṭittiṭalām uṇarntiṭalām paṟṟiṭalām cukamē.
translation: This is the moment, you see, for our Lord to arrive, so that all the foolish religions in the world that strive without benefit may be swiftly destroyed, and the one consummate Sanmarkkam, without any deceit, may be established everywhere. Like those who wake from sleep, all who have died are now appearing and rising up; this has begun and will continue to happen. Come quickly to learn and know this. You can learn the unlearnable lesson, realize it, and grasp it in bliss.
commentary: Vallalar announces that a new spiritual age has begun, one that will make all previous religions obsolete. The Lord is arriving now to establish the one true Sanmarkkam (path of truth) everywhere. As a sign of this new era, the dead are beginning to rise as if waking from sleep, an event that he says is already underway. He urges everyone to come quickly, not to miss this unprecedented opportunity to learn the "unlearnable lesson" directly and attain a state of bliss.

translit: cukamaṟiyīr tuṉpamoṉṟē tuṇintaṟintīr ulakīr cūtaṟintīr vātaṟintīr tūymaiyaṟin tilirē ikamaṟiyīr paramaṟiyīr eṉṉēnuṅ karuttī teṉpurivīr maraṇamvaril eṅkuṟuvīr antō akamaṟintīraṉakamaṟin taḻiyāta ñāṉa amutavaṭi vampeṟalām aṭaintiṭumiṉ īṇṭē mukamaṟiyār pōliruntīr eṉṉaiaṟi yīrō muttarelām pōṟṟumaruṭ cittarmakaṉ nāṉē.
translation: O people of the world, you do not know bliss; you have only resolutely known suffering. You know deception and argument, but you do not know purity. You understand neither this world nor the next. What is this intention of yours? What will you do? Where will you go when death comes? Alas! You can know your inner self, know the Flawless One, and attain the undying form of wisdom-ambrosia. Attain it right here! You act as if you do not recognize me. Do you not know who I am? I am the son of the grace-Siddhar praised by all the liberated ones.
commentary: Vallalar issues a sharp challenge: people are experts in suffering and argument but know nothing of purity or true bliss, leaving them helpless before death. The way out, he says, is to turn inward, know the Flawless One, and attain an undying body of pure wisdom. He then makes a personal claim to authority, identifying himself as the spiritual son of the grace-Siddhar (a perfected master) who is revered by all muktar (liberated souls).

translit: nāṉuraikkum vārttaielām nāyakaṉṟaṉ vārttai nampumiṉō namaraṅkāḷ naṟṟaruṇam ituvē vāṉuraitta maṇimaṉṟil naṭampuriem perumāṉ varavetirkoṇ ṭavaṉaruḷāl varaṅkaḷelām peṟavē tēṉuraikkum uḷamiṉikka eḻukiṉṟēṉ nīvīr terintaṭainteṉ uṭaṉeḻumiṉ cittipeṟal ākum ēṉuraittēṉ irakkattāl eṭutturaittēṉ kaṇṭīr yāṉaṭaiyum cukattiṉainīr tāṉaṭaital kuṟittē.
translation: All the words I speak are the words of the Lord. Believe me, our people, this is the opportune moment. I am now rising up, my heart sweetening like honey, to welcome our great Lord who dances in the jeweled hall acclaimed by the heavens and to receive all boons by his grace. You too, understand this and rise up with me; attainment of supernatural powers will be possible. Why do I say this? You see, I have explained it out of compassion, solely so that you may attain the bliss that I attain.
commentary: Vallalar asserts that his words are not his own; they are the direct words of God. He joyfully prepares to welcome a new manifestation of the divine, and he invites everyone to join him. Those who participate can receive divine boons and even extraordinary abilities (siddhi). He clarifies his motive is pure compassion, a desire for others to share in the bliss he himself experiences.

translit: kuṟitturaikkiṉ ṟēṉitaṉaik kēṇmiṉ iṅkē vammiṉ kōṇummaṉak kuraṅkālē nāṇukiṉṟa ulakīr veṟitta:ummāl orupayaṉum vēṇṭukilēṉ eṉatu meyyuraiyaip poyyuraiyāy vēṟuniṉai yātīr poṟittamatam camayamelām poypoyyē avaṟṟil pukutātīr civamoṉṟē poruḷeṉakkaṇ ṭaṟimiṉ ceṟittiṭuciṟ capainaṭattait terintututit tiṭumiṉ cittielām ittiṉamē cattiyamcērn tiṭumē.
translation: I state this with certainty. Listen! Come here, O people of the world, who are shamed by your crooked monkey-mind! I desire no benefit from you in your frenzy. Do not mistake my true words for false ones or think otherwise. The established religions and creeds are all false, utterly false. Do not enter them. See and realize that Sivam alone is the true substance. Know and praise the dance in the dense hall of consciousness. All perfections will truly be yours this very day.
commentary: With emphatic certainty, Vallalar rejects all established religions, declaring them utterly false. He asks people to abandon them and instead realize that Sivam, the ultimate auspicious reality, is the one true substance. The way to connect with this reality is to witness the divine dance within the cit sabai (the inner space of consciousness). This direct perception, he promises, is the key to attaining all perfection this very day.

translit: cērntiṭavē oruppaṭumiṉ camaracacaṉ mārkkat tiruneṟiyē peruneṟiyām cittielām peṟalām ōrntiṭumiṉ uṇṇutaṟkum uṟaṅkutaṟkum uṇarntīr ulakamelām kaṇṭiṭumōr uḷavaiaṟin tilirē vārntakaṭal ulakaṟiya maraṇamuṇṭē antō maraṇameṉṟāl caṭameṉumōr tiraṇamumcam matiyā cārntiṭumam maraṇamatait taṭuttiṭalām kaṇṭīr taṉittiṭuciṟ capainaṭattait taricaṉañcey vīrē.
translation: Agree to come together and join. The sacred path of Samarasa Sanmarkkam is the great path; all siddhis can be attained. Consider this: you have learned how to eat and sleep, but you have not perceived the one open secret the whole world can witness. Alas, the world surrounded by the vast ocean knows that death exists. At the mention of 'death', even a blade of grass, an inanimate thing, does not consent. See here, you can prevent that death from reaching you! Go and have the darshan of the dance in the unique Chit Sabhai.
commentary: The great path of Samarasa Sanmarkkam (the Path of Harmonious Truth) is the way to achieve all perfections. Vallalar points to an open secret: while everyone learns to eat and sleep, they ignore the universal reality of death, which even a blade of grass instinctively resists. He declares that this death can be prevented. The method is to have a darshan (sacred viewing) of the divine dance within the unique Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness).

translit: ceytālum tīmaielām poṟuttaruḷvāṉ potuvil tirunaṭañcey peruṅkaruṇait tiṟattāṉaṅ kavaṉai meytāva niṉaittiṭuka camaracacaṉ mārkkam mēvukaeṉ ṟuraikkiṉṟēṉ mētiṉiyīr eṉaittāṉ vaitālum vaitiṭumiṉ vāḻtteṉakkoṇ ṭiṭuvēṉ maṉaṅkōṇēṉ māṉamelām pōṉavaḻi viṭuttēṉ poytāṉōr ciṟiteṉiṉum pukalēṉcat tiyamē pukalkiṉṟēṉ nīvirelām puṉitamuṟum poruṭṭē.
translation: He will forgive all the wrongs you may have done. He is the possessor of great compassion who performs the sacred dance in the common space. Think of Him with sincere longing. O people of the world, I tell you to embrace Samarasa Sanmarkkam. Scold me if you will; I will take it as a blessing. My mind will not be troubled. I have abandoned all sense of honor, letting it go its own way. I do not speak even a trace of falsehood. I speak only the truth, so that all of you may become pure.
commentary: The Divine who performs this dance is defined by great compassion and will forgive any past wrongs. Vallalar frames his teaching as a selfless act, born from a desire for everyone's purification. He demonstrates the path through his own state, declaring he has abandoned personal honor and is indifferent to praise or blame, caring only that this truth is heard.

translit: poruṭṭalanum pōkamelām poyyāmiṅ kitunāṉ pukaluvateṉ nāṭoṟum puntiyiṟkaṇ ṭatuvē maruṭṭulakīr iruṭṭulakil maṭivataḻa kalavē maraṇamilāp peruvāḻvil vāḻavammiṉ iṅkē poruṭṭiṟañcēr cuttaciva caṉmārkka nilaiyil poruntumiṉciṟ capaiamutam aruntumiṉaṉ puṭaṉē aruṭṭiṟañcērn teṇṇiyavā ṟāṭumiṉō nummai aṭuppavarē aṉṟiniṉṟu taṭuppavarmaṟ ṟilaiyē.
translation: Your pleasures are worthless; they are false. Why do I say this? It is what I see daily in my own mind. O people of this deluding world, it is not beautiful to die in this world of darkness. Come here, live the great life without death. Settle into the state of Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, which is filled with substance. With love, drink the amritam of the Chit Sabhai. Filled with the power of Grace, rejoice just as you wish. There is no one to stop you; there are only those who will draw near you.
commentary: Worldly pleasures are an illusion leading only to death in a world of darkness. Vallalar offers a direct invitation to a "great life without death" through his path, which he here calls Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (the pure path of Siva). This life is attained by drinking the amritam (nectar of immortality) from the Chit Sabhai, an inner experience of Grace that brings absolute freedom and joy.

translit: maṟṟaṟivōm eṉacciṟitu tāḻttiruppīr āṉāl maraṇameṉum perumpāvi vantiṭumē antō caṟṟumatai nummālē taṭukkamuṭi yātē camaracacaṉ mārkkacaṅkat tavarkaḷallāl ataṉai eṟṟiniṉṟu taṭukkavallār evvulakil evarum illaikaṇṭīr cattiyamī teṉmoḻikoṇ ṭulakīr paṟṟiyapaṟ ṟaṉaittiṉaiyum paṟṟaṟaviṭ ṭaruḷam palappaṟṟē paṟṟumiṉō eṟṟumiṟa vīrē.
translation: If you hesitate even a little, thinking, "We can learn about this later," then alas, the great sinner called death will arrive. You will be utterly unable to stop it. Know this: apart from the members of the Samarasa Sanmarkka Sangam, there is no one in any world who has the power to stand, kick it away, and stop it. This is the truth. O people of the world, accept my words. Completely abandon all the attachments you hold. Cling only to the attachment of the Arul Ambalam. You will never die.
commentary: Procrastination is fatal, because death will come to anyone who hesitates. Vallalar states with absolute certainty that only those who follow his path, the Samarasa Sanmarkka Sangam (fellowship of universal harmony), can conquer death. The practice is to release all worldly attachments and cling to a single, supreme attachment: the experience of the Arul Ambalam, the Hall of Grace.

translit: iṟantavarai eṭuttiṭumpō taraṟṟukiṉṟīr ulakīr iṟavāta peruvaramnīr ēṉaṭaiya māṭṭīr maṟantiruntīr piṇimūppil cammatamō numakku maṟantumitai niṉaikkilnallōr maṉamnaṭuṅkum kaṇṭīr ciṟantiṭucaṉ mārkkamoṉṟē piṇimūppu maraṇam cērāmal tavirttiṭuṅkāṇ terintuvammiṉ iṅkē piṟantapiṟap pitiṟṟāṉē nittiyamey vāḻvu peṟṟiṭalām pēriṉpam uṟṟiṭalām viraintē.
translation: O people of the world, you cry and lament when you carry away the dead. Why do you not attain the great boon of deathlessness? You have forgotten. Do you consent to disease and old age? See here, if good people think of this even for a moment, their hearts will tremble. The excellent Sanmarkkam alone will prevent disease, old age, and death from reaching you. Realize this and come here. In this very birth, you can obtain eternal, true life; you can attain supreme bliss, quickly.
commentary: Vallalar points out a contradiction in human behavior: people grieve death but passively accept it, along with disease and old age, as inevitable. He asks directly why they do not choose the "great boon of deathlessness" instead. His path of Sanmarkkam is presented as the one way to prevent all three conditions: disease, old age, and death. It is possible to achieve an eternal, blissful, and true existence in this very body, in this very birth.

translit: uṟṟamoḻi uraikkiṉṟēṉ orumaiyiṉāl umakkē uṟavaṉaṉṟip pakaivaṉeṉa uṉṉātīr ulakīr kaṟṟavarum kallārum aḻintiṭakkāṇ kiṉṟīr karaṇamelām kalaṅkavarum maraṇamumcam matamō caṟṟumitaic cammatiyā teṉmaṉantāṉ umatu taṉmaṉantāṉ kaṉmaṉamō vaṉmaṉamō aṟiyēṉ iṟṟitaṉait taṭuttiṭalām eṉṉoṭumcērn tiṭumiṉ eṉmārkkam iṟappoḻikkum caṉmārkkan tāṉē.
translation: I speak these words to you out of a sense of oneness. O people of the world, do not think of me as an enemy rather than a relative. You see both the learned and the unlearned perish. Is death, which comes confounding all the inner faculties, acceptable? My mind does not consent to this in the slightest. I do not know if your minds are made of stone or are just hard. This can be prevented; join with me. My path is the Sanmarkkam, the very one that abolishes death.
commentary: The tone here is one of desperate, loving appeal. Vallalar asks people to see him as family, sharing a vital truth. He expresses his own deep inability to accept death, questioning how anyone can be at peace with it. His invitation to join him on the Sanmarkkam is presented as the one solution to what he sees as the greatest, unacceptable tragedy.

translit: caṉmārkkap peruṅkuṇattār tampatiyai eṉṉait tāṅkukiṉṟa perumpatiyait taṉittacapā patiyai naṉmārkkat teṉainaṭattic caṉmārkka caṅka naṭuvirukka aruḷamutam nalkiyanā yakaṉaip puṉmārkkark kaṟivaritām puṇṇiyaṉai ñāṉa pūraṇameyp poruḷākip poruntiyamā maruntai aṉmārkkam tavirttaruḷi ampalattē naṭañcey aruṭperuñcō tiyaiulakīr teruṭkoḷaccār vīrē.
translation: O people of the world, with clear understanding, you must approach the Vast Grace-Jothi who, having graciously averted the untrue path, dances in the sacred space. He is the Lord of those with the great qualities of Sanmarkkam; the great Lord who sustains me; the Lord of the unique hall of assembly; the Master who led me on the good path, bestowed the nectar of grace, and had me sit in the center of the Sanmarkkam Sangam; the holy one, difficult for those on wretched paths to know; the great medicine that is the true substance of perfect wisdom.
commentary: After the urgent warnings about death, Vallalar now points to the solution: God, whom he calls the Vast Grace-Jothi (ArutPerunJothi). He depicts the divine through its relationship with the devotee: a sustainer, a guide who placed him in the Sanmarkkam Sangam, and a healing medicine of pure wisdom. The instruction is simple: turn your whole attention to this divine light dancing in the sacred inner space (ambalam).

translit: cārulaka vātaṉaiyait tavirttavaruḷ ḷakattē cattiyamāy amarntaruḷum uttamacaṟ kuruvai nēruṟavē evarālum kaṇṭukoḷaṟ karitām nittiyavāṉ poruḷaielā nilaikaḷuntāṉ āki ēruṟavē viḷaṅkukiṉṟa iyaṟkaiuṇmai taṉṉai ellāmcey vallapattai eṉakkaḷitta patiyai ōruṟaveṉ ṟaṭaintulakīr pōṟṟimakiḻn tiṭumiṉ uḷḷamelām kaṉinturuki uḷḷapaṭi niṉaintē.
translation: O people of the world, with your hearts ripening and melting, contemplating him as he truly is, approach him as your one true relation, praise him, and rejoice. He is the supreme true guru who graciously abides as truth within the hearts of those who have given up worldly afflictions; the eternal heavenly substance, difficult for anyone to perceive directly; the natural truth that shines in beauty, having become all states; the Lord who granted me the all-doing power.
commentary: The path to God is through the heart. Vallalar urges the reader to approach the divine with a feeling of deep love, as if one's heart is ripening and melting. God is revealed here as the supreme true guru (satguru), who abides secretly within the hearts of those who renounce worldly desire. This inner presence is the source of all power, and the way to connect with it is to recognize it as your one and only true relation.
NOTES
Note 359

tamil: அகமறியீர் - முதற்பதிப்பு, பொ. சு., ச. மு. க.
translit: akamaṟiyīr — mutaṟpatippu, po. cu., ca. mu. ka.
translation: akamaṟiyīr — reading of the first edition, Po. Su., S. Mu. Ka.

glossary.def: The five divine functions: creation, preservation, dissolution, veiling and grace. Vallalar says these are done by deities under God, and that God granted them to him.
The Agamas, scriptures of temple worship and doctrine. Vallalar says their truth is known by grace, not by reading.
A Tamil verse form of long, flowing lines. The ArutPerunJothi Agaval, Vallalar's hymn of 1,596 lines, belongs to the Sixth Thirumurai and is published as a separate volume.
Ambalam: the hall or open stage where God dances. It is the hall at Chidambaram and, within, the space of consciousness where God is known.
Nectar, ambrosia. Vallalar's word for the sweetness of grace, tasted within, which brings deathless life.
Bliss, Ananda. The joy of union with God.
The root impurity of the ego, the "I-ness" that veils the soul. The first of the three impurities (malam).
Anma Neya Orumaipadu: the unity of all souls in love. Every living being shares the same essence, so every being is to be seen as one's own.
The universe, the macrocosm. Vallalar sees the same Light filling the countless universes (aṇṭam) and the human body (piṇṭam).
Traditionally a name for Brahmins. Vallalar gives it its root meaning: the gracious ones whose nature is coolness and compassion toward all life, whatever their birth.
Refuge. The cry "apayam, apayam" ("refuge, refuge") runs through the pathigam Apayam Iṭutal, the soul's plea to be held by God.
Virtue, righteous action. For Vallalar its heart is compassion: feeding the hungry and relieving the suffering of every living being.
A name for the Vedas.
The six "ends" (antam) or culminations of the philosophical traditions: Vedanta, Siddhanta, Bodhanta, Nadanta, Yoganta and Kalanta. Vallalar says God is beyond all six.
Grace. The living, compassionate power of God that frees the soul and transforms it. For Vallalar grace is received through compassion for all life.
ArutJothi, the Grace-Light: God as the Light of grace, seen and received within.

ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light: Vallalar's name for God in the Sixth Thirumurai. The one infinite Light of grace from which everything comes and in which everything is held, open to every living being.
The deathless education: the knowledge, given by grace, of the life that does not end in death.
The waking state, the first of the states of consciousness. Vallalar speaks of a higher waking beyond the usual states.
Salai, the hall or house. Here the Sathya Dharma Salai, the free kitchen at Vadalur.
Samarasam: perfect harmony, equality of all. Part of the full name of Vallalar's path, Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam.
Religion as an organized creed. In the Sixth Thirumurai Vallalar declares the religions, creeds and sects false, and calls people beyond them to the true path.
The conch, blown to announce victory and arrival. Vallalar has it blown to proclaim the coming of God.
Sanmarkkam, the true path. Vallalar's name for the way of grace, compassion and direct knowledge of God, open to every living being.
Satguru, the true teacher. Vallalar's name for God, who taught him directly from within.
Caste. Vallalar declares caste false, a darkness to be thrown away, and calls all people one family.
Sathya Gnana Sabai, the Hall of True Wisdom that Vallalar consecrated at Vadalur in 1872, a hall of light open to all, built for no religion.
Sathya Dharma Salai, the free kitchen Vallalar opened at Vadalur in 1867 so that no one would go hungry. Its fire has not been put out since.
Crest-jewel, the jewel worn at the top of a crown. Used for God as the highest of all.
Chit Sabhai, the Hall of Consciousness, where God dances. Both the hall at Chidambaram and the inner space of awareness.
Chitrambalam, the "small" or subtle hall: the hall of the dance at Chidambaram and the hall of consciousness within. Thiru Chitrambalam is "the sacred Chitrambalam".
Siddhanta, the Saiva philosophical tradition. One of the six "ends" (āṟantam) that Vallalar says God transcends.
Siddhar, a perfected one. Vallalar calls God the Siddhar who can do all things.
Siddhi, attainment or perfect power. Vallalar speaks above all of the Siddhi that can do all things, given by grace.
Sivakami, the Divine Mother, consort of the Lord who dances at Chidambaram.
Sivam, the Auspicious: the supreme Reality. In the Sixth Thirumurai Vallalar says that Sivam alone is the true substance.
Bliss, lasting well-being.
The bliss of simply being: the stillness beyond all effort and thought that Vallalar longs for in the second verse of the Sixth Thirumurai.
Suddha Sanmarkkam, the pure true path that Vallalar names and teaches in the Sixth Thirumurai: compassion for all life, the end of caste and creed, and union with ArutPerunJothi.
The seven levels. In the pathigam on the Hall of Pure Gold, the seven stages of the inner vision, each marked by a change of jewel and color.
Jeeva Karunyam, compassion for all living beings. For Vallalar the foundation of all spiritual life and the key to God's grace.
Jothi, Light. Vallalar's central name for God.
Husband. In the bridal songs the soul is the bride and God the husband, the closest union a human life knows.
Karma: the accumulated effect of one's actions. One of the three impurities (malam).
The evil eye: harm believed to come from an envious look.
The inner faculties: mind, intellect, will and ego. Vallalar asks that they be purified and ruled by grace.
Compassion, mercy. God's compassion toward all, and the compassion the soul must have for every living being.
Kollāmai, non-killing. For Vallalar the condition of the true path: those who kill and eat flesh stand outside it until they give up killing.
Death, personified as Yama, the god of death.
Mahamayai, the great māyai: the subtle, primal form of illusion.
Malam, impurity. The three impurities, ego (āṇavam), karma (kaṉmam) and illusion (māyai), veil the soul until grace removes them.
Manimanram, the Hall of Gems, where God dances.
Creed or doctrine; also pride or madness. Vallalar uses the double meaning: attachment to creed is a kind of madness.
Māyai, illusion: the power that makes the passing world seem the whole of reality. One of the three impurities.
Mettukuppam, the village near Vadalur where Vallalar lived his last years and where, on 30 January 1874, he entered his room and was not seen again.
Silence, the stillness beyond all words.
Mutti, liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
A unit of time of twenty-four minutes.
Gnana Sabai, the Hall of Wisdom: the hall of God's dance, and Vallalar's hall at Vadalur.
Gnanam, wisdom: direct knowledge of God, given by grace and not by study.
The medicine of wisdom: God as the remedy for every ill, above all for birth and death.
Dance. God's dance in the hall is the movement of grace that sustains all things.
Nadam, the primordial sound from which manifestation arises.
Nadanta, "the end of sound": the state beyond primordial sound. One of the six "ends" (āṟantam).
Nataraja, the King of Dance: God as the Dancer in the hall at Chidambaram and in the hall of consciousness.
The central channel, the subtle path at the center of the body in which, Vallalar says, God dances.
Justice. Vallalar speaks of the compassionate justice that rules in God's hall.
The sacred sound Om.
Parai, the supreme Power of God, worshipped as the Divine Mother.
Pati, Lord. God as the sovereign of all souls, as in Sivapati, "the Lord who is Siva".
Pathigam, a hymn, usually of ten verses. The Sixth Thirumurai is arranged in pathigams.
The body, the microcosm, set against aṇṭam, the universe.
Enjoyment. In the Sixth Thirumurai, the bliss of union with God.
The Golden Hall (Pon Sabhai) at Chidambaram, where God dances.
The common space, open to all. God dances in the common space so that all may see.
The heroine of the love songs. In Vallalar's bridal songs she is the soul, and her beloved is God.
Tandavam, the cosmic dance of God.
Tattva, a principle of existence. The tattvas are the levels from the elements to the subtlest powers. God is in them all and beyond them.
Tapas, spiritual discipline or penance.
Thillai, the old name of Chidambaram, the town of the Golden Hall where God dances.
Thirumurai, "sacred book". The Thiru Arutpa is arranged in six Thirumurai; this is the sixth and last.
Thiru Arutpa, "the Divine Songs of Grace": the collected poetry of Vallalar.
The sacred feet of God, the place of refuge and of grace.
The heroine's friend and confidant in the love songs, to whom the soul tells her experience of God.
The evil path, the way of cruelty and falsehood, as opposed to Sanmarkkam.
Turiyam, the "fourth" state of consciousness beyond waking, dreaming and deep sleep.
Turiyatitam, the state beyond the fourth.
The refrain of a traditional Tamil girls' game-song, also used by Manikkavasagar. Vallalar uses it to sing God's deeds as joyful play.
Latent tendencies left in the mind by past experience, which bind the soul until grace frees it.
"Come!" The refrain of the pathigam Ampalavāṇar Varukai, calling God to come.
Vadalur, the town in Tamil Nadu where Vallalar founded the Sathya Dharma Salai and the Sathya Gnana Sabai.
Space, the expanse. Vallalar speaks of many spaces, up to the Space of Siva (Siva veḷi).
Vedanta, the philosophy of the Upanishads. One of the six "ends" (āṟantam) that Vallalar says God transcends.
Open space, the boundless expanse of pure consciousness in which all things are seen to resolve.
Karma: the effect of past actions that binds the soul to birth.
